senses.en: lacking spirit or liveliness

examples.text: A languid afternoon heat settled over the town, and even the dogs refused to stir.

origin.ko: 라틴어 languidus '기운 없는'에서 왔고 langueō '맥이 빠지다'에서 나왔습니다.

senses.en: plausible but false

examples.text: This idea that we must see through what we have started is specious, however good it may sound.

senses.en: based on pretense; deceptively pleasing

examples.text: The brochure's specious glamour hid the shoddy construction of the resort.

origin.ko: 라틴어 speciōsus(보기 좋은)에서 왔습니다. 겉보기만 좋고 알맹이는 틀렸다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: Making or characterized by a noisy outcry; clamorous.

examples.text: Vociferous protesters filled the square, chanting demands until the council agreed to meet them.

senses.en: Vocally and forcefully opinionated.

examples.text: Not even the most vociferous advocates of reform were willing to go to such lengths.

origin.ko: 라틴어 vōcifer('소리를 실어 나르는')에 -ous를 붙였습니다. 목소리를 크게 내뱉는 것입니다.

senses.en: liveliness and eagerness

examples.text: The volunteers responded with alacrity, arriving at the shelter within an hour of the appeal.

origin.ko: 라틴어 alacritas(활기)에서 왔고 alacer(민첩한)에서 나왔습니다. 팔팔하게 기꺼이 움직이는 태도를 뜻합니다.

senses.en: (used with regard to idealized country life) idyllically rustic

examples.text: Weary of the city, he retired to a bucolic village of stone cottages and sheep meadows.

origin.ko: 그리스어 boukolikos('소 치는 사람의')를 라틴어를 거쳐 빌려 온 말입니다. 목동이 있는 전원 풍경을 가리킵니다.

senses.en: avoid and stay away from deliberately; stay clear of

examples.text: The monk eschewed all luxury and lived on bread and water.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑크어 *skiuhijan(두려워 피하다)에서 앵글로노르만어를 거쳐 왔습니다. 꺼려서 멀리한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: having only superficial plausibility

examples.text: The consultant offered glib assurances that the merger would cost no one a job.

senses.en: Having a ready flow of words but lacking thought or understanding; superficial; shallow.

examples.text: Critics dismissed his glib answers as clever phrases with no substance behind them.

origin.ko: '미끄러운'을 뜻하던 glibbery 또는 저지 독일어 glibberig의 줄임말입니다. 미끄러지듯 매끄러운 말솜씨라는 이미지입니다.

senses.en: repeated too often; overfamiliar through overuse

examples.text: The sermon was full of hackneyed phrases and platitudes.

origin.ko: hackney(임대 마차)에 -ed가 붙은 말입니다. 임대 마차처럼 너무 흔하게 쓰여 식상해졌다는 이미지입니다.

senses.en: incapable of being placated
senses.ko: 달랠 수 없는, 화해할 수 없는

examples.text: an implacable enemy

origin.ko: 라틴어 implācābilis '달랠 수 없는'에서 왔습니다. plācō(달래다)에 부정 접두사가 붙었습니다.

senses.en: concise and full of meaning

examples.text: welcomed her pithy comments

origin.ko: pith(알맹이)에 -y가 붙은 말로, 알맹이만 꽉 찬 간결한 표현입니다.

senses.en: temperamentally disinclined to talk

examples.text: The usually reticent scientist surprised everyone by speaking openly about her failed experiments.

senses.en: reluctant to draw attention to yourself

examples.text: Reticent about her achievements, she let her colleagues take most of the public credit.

origin.ko: 라틴어 reticēre('입을 다물다')의 현재분사에서 왔습니다. 말을 아끼는 과묵함입니다.

senses.en: having keenness and forcefulness and penetration in thought, expression, or intellect

examples.text: The review offered trenchant criticism of the film's script without ignoring its visual achievements.

senses.en: characterized by or full of force and vigor

examples.text: a trenchant argument

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 trenchier('자르다')의 현재분사에서 왔습니다. 칼처럼 베는 날카로움이 '예리한'입니다.

senses.en: powerfully persuasive

examples.text: The senator presented a cogent argument that swayed several undecided colleagues.

origin.ko: 라틴어 cōgēns에서 왔고, cōgō('함께 몰아붙이다, 강제하다')에서 갈라졌습니다. 상대를 몰아붙이는 설득력입니다.

senses.en: Excessively moralizing.

examples.text: The novel's didactic tone made readers feel they were being lectured rather than entertained.

senses.en: Instructive or intended to teach or demonstrate, especially with regard to morality.

examples.text: didactic poetry

origin.ko: 그리스어 didaktikós(가르치는 데 능한)에서 왔고 didáskō(가르치다)가 뿌리입니다.

senses.en: an amateur who engages in an activity without serious intentions and who pretends to have knowledge

examples.text: The dilettante sampled painting, pottery and poetry but never mastered any of them.

senses.en: showing frivolous or superficial interest; amateurish

examples.text: his dilettantish efforts at painting

origin.ko: 이탈리아어 dilettare(즐기다)의 현재분사에서 왔습니다. 즐기기 위해 하는 아마추어를 뜻합니다.

senses.en: stubbornly resistant to authority or control

examples.text: The fractious coalition struggled to agree on even the simplest points of policy.

senses.en: easily irritated or annoyed

examples.text: Tired and hungry, the fractious toddler screamed through the entire flight.

origin.ko: 옛 단어 fraction(불화)에 -ous가 붙었습니다. 불화를 일으키며 말을 듣지 않는다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: To abase oneself before another person.

examples.text: She refused to grovel in front of the bully, standing her ground.

senses.en: show submission or fear

examples.text: The defeated courtiers groveled before the new king, begging to keep their titles.

origin.ko: 고대 노르드어 á grufu '배를 땅에 대고'에서 왔습니다. 바닥에 엎드려 기는 모습이 '굽실거리다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: marked by a narrow focus on or display of learning especially its trivial aspects

examples.text: His pedantic insistence on citing every source slowed the discussion to a crawl.

senses.en: ostentatiously lofty in style

examples.text: The senator's turgid prose buried a simple proposal beneath layers of pretentious abstraction.

senses.en: abnormally distended especially by fluids or gas

examples.text: After days of rain the turgid river spilled over its banks and flooded the lower fields.

origin.ko: 라틴어 turgidus('부푼')에서 왔습니다. 바람 든 풍선처럼 부풀린 문체가 '과장된'입니다.

senses.en: regard with feelings of respect and reverence; consider hallowed or exalted or be in awe of

examples.text: Many villagers continue to venerate the ancient shrine as the home of their protecting spirits.

origin.ko: 라틴어 veneror('숭배하다')에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: Impulsive and unpredictable; determined by chance, impulse, or whim.

examples.text: The capricious ruler granted favors one day and withdrew them the next without any explanation.

origin.ko: 이탈리아어 capriccioso에서 왔고 caprice에 -ious가 붙은 말입니다. 변덕에 좌우되는 성질을 뜻합니다.

senses.en: not subject or susceptible to change or variation in form or quality or nature

examples.text: the immutable laws of nature

origin.ko: 라틴어 immūtābilis '변하지 않는'에서 왔습니다. 변할 수 없다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: Harmful in effect.

examples.text: Policies inimical to small businesses drove many shopkeepers out of the city center.

senses.en: not friendly

examples.text: The rival delegation adopted an inimical tone from the first day of the talks.

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 inimīcālis '적대적인'에서 왔습니다. 친구(amicus)가 아닌 적이라는 데서 '해로운'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: easily influenced

examples.text: Young children have malleable minds that readily absorb the attitudes of those around them.

senses.en: capable of being shaped or bent or drawn out

examples.text: malleable metals such as gold

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 malleābilis에서 왔고 malleus(망치)에서 나왔습니다. 망치질로 모양이 바뀌듯 쉽게 영향을 받습니다.

senses.en: liable to sudden unpredictable change

examples.text: Her mercurial temperament made her a thrilling but exhausting colleague.

senses.en: Having a lively or volatile character; animated, changeable, quick-witted.

examples.text: The mercurial editor praised a draft one day and rejected it the next.

origin.ko: 로마 신 메르쿠리우스(Mercury)와 관련됨을 뜻하는 라틴어 mercuriālis에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: a trite or obvious remark

examples.text: The senator's speech was little more than a string of platitudes about hard work and opportunity.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 platitude에서 왔고, plat는 '평평한'입니다. 밋밋하고 평범한 상투어를 뜻합니다.

senses.en: responsive to suggestions and influences

examples.text: The director was amenable to changes, provided that the central scene remained untouched.

senses.en: liable to answer to a higher authority
senses.ko: 책임을 져야 하는, 복종할 의무가 있는

examples.text: Officials are amenable to the courts, which can review any decision they make.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 amener(이끌어 오다)에서 왔습니다. 이끄는 대로 따라올 수 있다는 데서 '순응하는'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: attack someone physically or emotionally

examples.text: Our ears were assailed by her joyous efforts on her new saxophone.

senses.en: attack in speech or writing

examples.text: Opposition leaders assailed the budget as reckless and unfair to working families.

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 assalire(~를 향해 뛰어들다)에서 왔습니다. 달려들어 공격하는 모습입니다.

senses.en: disposed to venture or take risks

examples.text: It was an audacious thing for her to attempt, but boldness had often served her turn before.

senses.en: unrestrained by convention or propriety

examples.text: an audacious trick to pull

origin.ko: 라틴어 audax(대담한)에서 왔고 audere(감히 ~하다)에서 나왔습니다. 두려움 없이 덤비는 태도입니다.

senses.en: repeated too often; overfamiliar through overuse

examples.text: banal conversation

origin.ko: 프랑스어 banal(공동으로 쓰는)에서 왔습니다. 영주의 시설을 모두가 함께 쓰던 데서 흔해 빠진 '진부한'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: lacking self-confidence

examples.text: stood in the doorway diffident and abashed

senses.en: showing modest reserve

examples.text: she was diffident when offering a comment on the professor's lecture

origin.ko: 라틴어 diffīdere(믿지 못하다)의 현재분사에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: containing or implying a slight or showing prejudice

examples.text: Critics argued that ranking the schools by income created an invidious comparison between poor and rich districts.

senses.en: Causing ill will, envy, or offense.

examples.text: The manager faced the invidious task of choosing which of two equally loyal employees to dismiss.

origin.ko: 라틴어 invidia '질투'에서 왔습니다. '곁눈질로 보다'에서 '시샘하다'로 뜻이 변했습니다.

senses.en: Not easily excited to action or passion; calm; sluggish.

examples.text: The phlegmatic captain barely reacted as the storm battered the ship around him.

origin.ko: 그리스어 phlégma는 고대 의학에서 차분하고 굼뜬 성격을 만든다고 본 체액입니다. 여기서 무덤덤하고 침착하다는 뜻이 되었습니다.

senses.en: practicing great self-denial

examples.text: a desert nomad's austere life

senses.en: severely simple

examples.text: The interior of the church was as austere as the parishioners were dour.

senses.en: of a stern or strict bearing or demeanor; forbidding in aspect

examples.text: The headmistress was an austere old woman.

origin.ko: 그리스어 austēros(떫은, 혀를 마르게 하는)에서 왔습니다. 입안을 건조하게 하는 떫음에서 '엄격한'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: Stubbornly persistent, generally in wrongdoing; refusing to reform or repent.

examples.text: The obdurate chairman rejected every compromise, even as the company's losses mounted.

senses.en: Hardened against feeling; hard-hearted.

examples.text: Moved by no plea, the obdurate landlord evicted the family in midwinter.

origin.ko: 라틴어 obdūrō '단단히 굳히다'에서 왔습니다. 마음을 돌처럼 굳혀 뉘우치지 않는 고집입니다.

senses.en: conspicuously and outrageously bad or reprehensible

examples.text: The student has made egregious errors on the examination.

origin.ko: 라틴어 'e + grex(양 떼)', 곧 '무리에서 튀어나온'이 원뜻입니다. 원래는 칭찬이었으나 지금은 '지독하게 눈에 띄는 나쁜'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: A position that requires little to no work, or easy work, but still gives an ample payment; a cushy job.
senses.ko: 한직, 일은 적고 보수는 좋은 자리

examples.text: A lucrative sinecure in the Excise was bestowed on Ferguson.

origin.ko: 라틴어 sine cūrā(돌봄 없이)에서 왔습니다. 영혼을 돌볼 의무 없이 보수만 받는 성직이 한직이 되었습니다.

senses.en: Highest point or state; peak.

examples.text: Winning the continental championship was the zenith of my career.

senses.en: The point in the sky vertically above a given position or observer; the point in the celestial sphere opposite the nadir.

examples.text: At noon in the tropics, the sun stands almost at the zenith and casts hardly any shadow.

origin.ko: 아랍어 samt('방향')에서 왔고 samt ar-raʔs('머리 위의 방향')가 줄어든 말입니다. 머리 바로 위가 '정점'입니다.

senses.en: formally reject or disavow a formerly held belief, usually under pressure

examples.text: Under threat of imprisonment, the scholar was forced to abjure the theories he had championed for decades.

origin.ko: 라틴어 abiurare(맹세로 부인하다)에서 왔습니다. 맹세하며 이전 믿음을 내던지는 것입니다.

senses.en: lacking even the rudiments of courage; abjectly fearful

examples.text: the craven fellow turned and ran

senses.en: an abject coward

examples.text: Critics branded the senator a craven who abandoned his principles at the first sign of public pressure.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 cravanté(패배한)에서 온 것으로 봅니다. 패배한 자의 모습에서 '겁쟁이'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: very generous

examples.text: On the hill, where kites used to be flown, stood the fine college which Mr Laurence's munificent legacy had built.

origin.ko: 라틴어 mūnificentia '관대함'에서 거꾸로 만들어진 말입니다. 아낌없이 베푸는 모습을 뜻합니다.

senses.en: grow and flourish

examples.text: The city's technology sector began to burgeon once the university opened its research park.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 burjon('새싹')에서 왔습니다. 싹이 돋아 쑥쑥 자라는 이미지입니다.

senses.en: obvious to the eye or mind

examples.text: He was conspicuous by his absence.

senses.en: without any attempt at concealment; completely obvious

examples.text: The mayor showed conspicuous disregard for the rules he had himself written.

origin.ko: 라틴어 conspicuus('눈에 보이는, 두드러진')에서 왔고, cōnspicere(알아채다)에서 갈라졌습니다.

senses.en: difficult to penetrate; incomprehensible to one of ordinary understanding or knowledge

examples.text: The journal publishes recondite essays on medieval logic that few readers outside the field can follow.

senses.en: Little known; esoteric, secret.

examples.text: Her recondite knowledge of obscure dialects made her an invaluable consultant for linguists.

senses.en: native to or confined to a certain region

examples.text: Kangaroos are endemic to Australia.

senses.en: Prevalent in a particular area or region, persistent within a population.

examples.text: Malaria is endemic to the tropics.

origin.ko: 그리스어 en(안에)과 dêmos(사람들)가 합쳐졌습니다. 그 지역 사람들 속에 늘 있는 것이라 '고유의'라는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: found in the ordinary course of events

examples.text: The novelist found beauty in the mundane details of a commuter's daily routine.

senses.en: concerned with the world or worldly matters

examples.text: The monk tried to put aside mundane concerns such as money and reputation.

origin.ko: 라틴어 mundus '세계'에서 왔습니다. 이 속세의 평범한 일이라는 뜻으로 '일상적인'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: To criticize severely.

examples.text: The captain upbraided the crew for their carelessness after the cargo was left unsecured during the storm.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 upbreġdan으로, up과 braid('홱 잡아채다')의 결합입니다. 잘못을 들춰내 몰아세우는 것이 '질책하다'입니다.

senses.en: extreme greed for material wealth

examples.text: The novel portrays a banker whose avarice ultimately costs him his family and his friends.

origin.ko: 라틴어 avaritia(탐욕)에서 왔고 avere(갈망하다)와 이어집니다. 재물을 몹시 탐내는 마음입니다.

senses.en: To give a false representation of.
senses.ko: 잘못 전하다, 실제와 다르게 보이게 하다

examples.text: Her smooth complexion and dark hair belie her actual age.

senses.en: To contradict, to show (something) to be false.

examples.text: Her obvious nervousness belied what she said.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 belēogan(거짓으로 속이다)에서 왔습니다. 겉모습이 실제를 속여 다르게 보이게 한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: heedful of potential consequences

examples.text: Being aware of the danger of upsetting her audience, she was somewhat circumspect in her comments.

origin.ko: 라틴어 circumspectō('둘러보다')에서 왔습니다. 사방을 살펴 신중하게 행동한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: feeling or expressing pain or sorrow for sins or offenses

examples.text: The contrite executive issued a public apology and promised to repay the lost funds.

origin.ko: 라틴어 contrītus('산산이 갈린')에서 왔고 conterō(갈다, 짓이기다)에서 갈라졌습니다. 마음이 부서지도록 뉘우친다는 이미지입니다.

senses.en: Treating serious issues with (often deliberately) inappropriate humour; flippant.

examples.text: Robbie's joke about Heather's appearance was just him being facetious.

origin.ko: 라틴어 facētia(재치, 농담)에서 프랑스어를 거쳐 왔습니다. 진지한 자리에서 농담하는 태도를 뜻합니다.

senses.en: marked by quiet and caution and secrecy; taking pains to avoid being observed

examples.text: He cast a furtive glance over his shoulder before slipping the envelope into his coat.

origin.ko: 라틴어 fūrtīvus '훔친, 은밀한'에서 왔고, fūr(도둑)에서 나온 말입니다. 도둑처럼 몰래 하는 모습입니다.

senses.en: a dissolute person; usually a man who is morally unrestrained

examples.text: The novel's hero is a charming libertine who squanders his inheritance on gambling and seduction.

senses.en: unrestrained by convention or morality

examples.text: The court's libertine atmosphere scandalized visiting dignitaries.

origin.ko: 라틴어 libertinus '해방 노예'에서 왔습니다. 속박에서 풀려난 사람이 방종한 사람을 뜻하게 되었습니다.

senses.en: hasty and without attention to detail; not thorough

examples.text: The inspector gave the wiring a perfunctory glance and moved on to the next room.

senses.en: done or produced as a formality only

examples.text: The committee gave the proposal only a perfunctory review before approving it.

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 perfunctōrius '건성인'에서 왔고, perfungor는 '해치우다'입니다. 겨우 해치우듯 형식만 채운다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: Prone to causing disputes; inclined to causing the expression of opposing opinions, disputatious, contentious, edgy.

examples.text: Not only are all these allegations worded in an unnecessarily polemical style, they are also simply false

origin.ko: polemic에 -al이 붙은 말로, 그리스어 '전쟁'에서 나온 '논쟁을 벌이는'의 뜻입니다.

senses.en: a strong liking

examples.text: The editor's predilection for long, ornate sentences often frustrated her younger colleagues.

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 praedīlēctiō에서 왔습니다. 다른 것보다 먼저 골라 아끼는 마음을 뜻합니다.

senses.en: assign to a lower position; reduce in rank

examples.text: The once-celebrated director was relegated to making low-budget commercials after a string of failures.

senses.en: refer to another person for decision or judgment

examples.text: She likes to relegate difficult questions to her colleagues

origin.ko: 라틴어 relēgāre('쫓아 보내다, 추방하다')에서 왔습니다. 뒤로 밀어 보낸다는 데서 '강등시키다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: reject as untrue, unfounded, or unjust

examples.text: She repudiated the accusations

senses.en: refuse to acknowledge, ratify, or recognize as valid

examples.text: The woman repudiated the divorce settlement

senses.en: To refuse to have any relation to; to disown.

examples.text: The movement publicly repudiated its founder after he praised violent extremists.

origin.ko: 라틴어 repudiāre('내치다')에서 왔고 repudium('거부, 이혼')와 이어집니다. 받아들이지 않고 물리친다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: temporary cessation or suspension

examples.text: The merger plans were held in abeyance until regulators completed their review of the proposed deal.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 abeance에서 왔고 원래 '입을 벌리고 바라봄'이라는 뜻입니다. 기대하며 기다리는 상태에서 '보류'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: to make better

examples.text: New housing programs were designed to ameliorate conditions in the city's poorest neighborhoods.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 améliorer(개선하다)에서 왔고 라틴어 melior(더 좋은)에서 나왔습니다. 더 좋게 만든다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: provide physical relief, as from pain

examples.text: A cool compress can assuage the pain of a mild burn.

senses.en: cause to be more favorably inclined; gain the good will of

examples.text: The mayor tried to assuage residents' fears with a public briefing on the new safety measures.

senses.en: satisfy (thirst)

examples.text: A long drink from the mountain stream was enough to assuage her thirst.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 asuagier(달래다)에서 왔고 라틴어 suavis(달콤한)에서 나왔습니다. 고통을 달콤하게 어루만져 누그러뜨립니다.

senses.en: To join into a mass or whole.

examples.text: The droplets coalesced into a puddle.

origin.ko: 라틴어 coalēscō에서 왔고, co-(함께)와 alēscō(자라다)가 합쳐졌습니다. 함께 자라 하나가 된다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: show the form or outline of

examples.text: The sketch delineated the building's silhouette against the evening sky with a few bold lines.

senses.en: describe in vivid detail

examples.text: The report delineates the responsibilities of each department so that no duties are overlooked.

origin.ko: 라틴어 dēlīneāre(선으로 그려내다)에서 왔습니다. 선으로 윤곽을 그려 보인다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: To laugh at or mock (someone or something) harshly; to ridicule, to scorn.

examples.text: Critics derided the proposal as naive, but it later became the basis of national policy.

origin.ko: 라틴어 dērīdēre(비웃다)에서 왔습니다. 상대를 깔보며 웃는다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: An abusive, bitter verbal or written attack, criticism or denunciation.

examples.text: The senator was prone to diatribes which could go on for more than an hour.

origin.ko: 그리스어 diatribḗ(시간을 보냄, 강론)에서 왔습니다. 닳도록 오래 이어지는 연설이 '통렬한 비난'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: To bring into existence (a situation, quality, result etc.); to give rise to, cause, create.

examples.text: Years of broken promises engendered deep distrust of the government.

origin.ko: 라틴어 ingenerāre(안에 만들어 넣다)에서 고대 프랑스어를 거쳐 왔습니다. 무언가를 낳듯 만들어 낸다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: To free (someone) from accusation or blame.

examples.text: The investigation exonerated the pilot, concluding that mechanical failure had caused the crash.

senses.en: To free (someone) from an obligation, responsibility or task.

examples.text: The new contract exonerated the tenants from any liability for damage caused by the storm.

origin.ko: 라틴어 exonerāre(짐을 내려놓다)에서 왔습니다. 죄의 짐을 벗겨 준다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: giving careful attention to detail; hard to please; excessively concerned with cleanliness

examples.text: The fastidious editor rejected the manuscript twice because of minor inconsistencies in its footnotes.

origin.ko: 라틴어 fastīdiōsus(역겨워하는)에서 왔습니다. fastus(오만)와 taedium(싫증)이 합쳐진 말로, 쉽게 만족하지 않는 까다로움입니다.

senses.en: characterized by undue haste and lack of thought or deliberation

examples.text: His impetuous decision to quit without another job lined up left his family anxious about money.

senses.en: marked by violent force

examples.text: The impetuous current swept away the footbridge and carried debris miles downstream.

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 impetuōsus '격렬한'에서 왔고 impetus(공격, 돌진)가 뿌리입니다.

senses.en: lacking interest or significance or impact

examples.text: The critics dismissed the film as an insipid romance with flat characters and a predictable plot.

senses.en: lacking taste or flavor or tang

examples.text: The diners were disappointed with the plain, insipid soup they were served.

origin.ko: 프랑스어를 거쳐 라틴어 īnsipidus '맛없는'에서 왔습니다. 맛이 없다는 데서 '재미없는'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: abusive or venomous language used to express blame or censure or bitter deep-seated ill will

examples.text: The debate degenerated into personal invective, with each candidate hurling insults at the other.

origin.ko: 라틴어 invehō '쏟아붓다'에서 온 invectīvus에서 왔습니다. 욕설을 상대에게 퍼붓는다는 이미지입니다.

senses.en: brief and to the point; effectively cut short

examples.text: The senator's laconic reply, a single sentence, ended the press conference in seconds.

origin.ko: 그리스어 Lakōnikós '라코니아 사람의'에서 왔습니다. 스파르타인들이 말을 짧게 하기로 유명했던 데서 나왔습니다.

senses.en: A lightness of manner or speech, frivolity; flippancy; a lack of appropriate seriousness; an inclination to make a joke of serious matters.

examples.text: An attempt to inject a little levity into the proceedings.

origin.ko: 라틴어 levitās '가벼움, 경박함'에서 왔고 levis(가벼운)에서 나왔습니다.

senses.en: noble and generous in spirit

examples.text: The magnanimous victor praised his defeated opponent and refused to gloat over the result.

origin.ko: 라틴어 magnanimus에서 왔고 magnus(큰)와 animus(마음)가 합쳐졌습니다. 마음이 크니 '도량이 넓은'입니다.

senses.en: Sullen, gloomy; showing a brooding ill humour.

examples.text: He sat morose and silent at the table, ignoring every attempt to cheer him up.

origin.ko: 라틴어 mōrōsus에서 왔고, mōs는 '습관, 고집'입니다. 고집 세고 까탈스러운 기질이 뚱하고 침울한 상태로 이어졌습니다.

senses.en: lacking foresight or scope

examples.text: Cutting research funding to balance one year's budget is a myopic policy with lasting costs.

senses.en: unable to see distant objects clearly

examples.text: Corrective lenses compensate for the excessive positive diopters of the myopic eye.

origin.ko: 그리스어 myōps는 '눈을 가늘게 뜨는 사람', 즉 근시입니다. 멀리 보지 못한다는 뜻이 선견지명이 없다는 비유가 되었습니다.

senses.en: a person who is uninterested in intellectual pursuits
senses.ko: 교양 없는 속물, 문화에 무관심한 사람

examples.text: The director dismissed his critics as philistines who could not appreciate serious art.

senses.en: smug and ignorant and indifferent or hostile to artistic and cultural values

examples.text: The council's philistine decision to close the library angered local writers.

origin.ko: 독일어 Philister에서 영향을 받은 말로, 성경 속 블레셋 사람에서 나왔습니다. 대학 구성원이 아닌 교양 없는 사람, 문화에 무관심한 속물을 뜻하게 되었습니다.

senses.en: Having or showing pluck, courage or spirit in trying circumstances.

examples.text: The plucky underdog team held on through three rounds of brutal competition.

origin.ko: pluck(배짱, 끈기)에 -y가 붙은 말로, 어려운 상황에서도 담차다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: complete and confirmed integrity; having strong moral principles

examples.text: The judge's probity was so well known that even her critics never questioned her rulings.

origin.ko: 라틴어 probitās('올곧음')에서 왔으며 probus('훌륭한, 정직한')에서 나왔습니다.

senses.en: a natural inclination

examples.text: The young poet showed an early proclivity for melancholy themes.

origin.ko: 라틴어 prōclīvitās('앞으로 기울어짐')에서 왔습니다. 마음이 한쪽으로 기우는 성향입니다.

senses.en: recklessly wasteful

examples.text: Critics condemned the profligate spending that left the city deeply in debt.

senses.en: unrestrained by convention or morality

examples.text: The novel portrays a profligate aristocracy indifferent to the suffering around it.

origin.ko: 라틴어 prōflīgāre('때려눕히다')에서 왔습니다. 쓰러질 만큼 막 써 버리는 '방탕한'의 뜻으로 번졌습니다.

senses.en: lacking wit or imagination

examples.text: The film's prosaic dialogue failed to capture the drama of the story.

senses.en: not fanciful or imaginative

examples.text: I was simply making the prosaic point that we are running late.

origin.ko: 라틴어 prosa('산문')에서 왔고, prorsus('곧바로')는 pro-와 vertō('돌리다')에서 나왔습니다. 운율 없는 산문 같은 평범함입니다.

senses.en: displaying or suggesting a lack of maturity

examples.text: The senators' puerile name-calling embarrassed even their own supporters.

origin.ko: 라틴어 puerīlis('어린아이 같은')에서 왔고 puer('아이')에서 나왔습니다. 어른이 아이처럼 유치하다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: impatient especially under restriction or delay

examples.text: The restive crowd began to jeer as the speaker's remarks dragged on past midnight.

senses.en: Resistant to control; stubborn.

examples.text: The restive provinces repeatedly defied orders from the central government.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 restif('멈춰 서 있는')에서 왔고 라틴어 restāre('머물다')와 이어집니다. 명령을 안 듣고 버티던 말에서 '안달하는'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: characterized by extreme care and great effort

examples.text: The auditor's scrupulous review uncovered errors that three earlier checks had missed.

senses.en: having scruples; arising from a sense of right and wrong; principled

examples.text: She remained scrupulous in her dealings, refusing even small favors that might compromise her independence.

origin.ko: 라틴어 scrupulus(작고 뾰족한 돌)에서 왔습니다. 신발 속 작은 돌에도 신경 쓰듯 꼼꼼한 태도입니다.

senses.en: take the place or move into the position of

examples.text: Will online dictionaries ever supplant paper dictionaries?

origin.ko: 라틴어 supplantāre(발바닥 아래를 걸어 넘어뜨리다)에서 왔습니다. 발을 걸어 밀어내고 그 자리를 차지합니다.

senses.en: habitually reserved and uncommunicative

examples.text: The two sisters could hardly have been more different, one so boisterous and expressive, the other so taciturn and calm.

origin.ko: 라틴어 taciturnus(말없는)에서 왔고 tacitus(침묵한)에서 나왔습니다. 말수가 적고 과묵한 성격입니다.

senses.en: tastelessly showy

examples.text: It was all cheap and incredibly tawdry, from the festoons of paper roses on the walls to the flash of paste jewels in make-believe crowns.

senses.en: made of inferior workmanship and materials

examples.text: The tawdry souvenirs fell apart within a week of being bought.

origin.ko: 성 오드리(Audrey)의 장터에서 팔던 값싼 레이스 목걸이 'Saint Audrey lace'가 줄어든 말입니다. 싸구려라는 뜻이 되었습니다.

senses.en: markedly different from an accepted norm

examples.text: The researchers discarded the aberrant readings, which differed sharply from every other measurement in the data set.

origin.ko: 라틴어 aberrare(길을 잃다)에서 왔습니다. 정해진 길에서 벗어나 헤매는 모습이 '일탈적인'입니다.

senses.en: take to task

examples.text: The coach admonished the players for their careless play in the opening minutes.

senses.en: warn strongly; put on guard

examples.text: Doctors admonished the public to avoid unnecessary travel while the outbreak continued.

origin.ko: 라틴어 admonere(일깨우다, 경고하다)에서 왔습니다. 상기시켜 주는 데서 '꾸짖다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: diffusing warmth and friendliness

examples.text: The affable host greeted every guest by name and made even strangers feel welcome.

origin.ko: 라틴어 affabilis(말을 걸기 쉬운)에서 왔습니다. 누구든 말 붙이기 편한 사람이 '상냥한'입니다.

senses.en: a feeling of intense dislike

examples.text: The two scholars shared a long-standing antipathy that surfaced at every conference they attended.

origin.ko: 그리스어 antipatheia(반대되는 감정)에서 왔습니다. 마음이 거꾸로 향하는 강한 반감입니다.

senses.en: being of questionable authenticity

examples.text: Many scholars consider the stories of the monk Teilo to be apocryphal.

origin.ko: 그리스어 apokryphos(감춰진)에서 왔습니다. 출처를 숨겨 진위가 의심스러운 글을 가리킵니다.

senses.en: a disloyal person who betrays or deserts their cause or religion or political party or friend etc.

examples.text: Party loyalists branded him an apostate after he endorsed the rival coalition.

senses.en: not faithful to religion or party or cause

examples.text: We must punish this apostate priest.

origin.ko: 그리스어 apostates(반역자)에서 왔고 '떨어져 서다'가 문자 그대로의 뜻입니다. 신앙에서 등을 돌린 사람입니다.

senses.en: become weaker, in strength, value, or magnitude

examples.text: Over successive decades the party's influence began to attenuate as its core voters aged.

senses.en: To make thinner, as by physically reshaping, starving, or decaying.

examples.text: Lovell, wan and hollow-eyed, his arm in a sling, his once burly frame gaunt and attenuated with disease, nodded.

origin.ko: 라틴어 attenuare(얇게 만들다)에서 왔습니다. 가늘고 약해지는 것을 뜻합니다.

senses.en: make sense of; assign a meaning to

examples.text: Her silence was construed as agreement, though she had merely been thinking.

origin.ko: 라틴어 construo('함께 쌓다')에서 왔고, 후기 라틴어에서 '문법적으로 엮다'는 뜻이 되었습니다. construct와 같은 어원입니다.

senses.en: To discredit, or expose to ridicule the falsehood or the exaggerated claims of something; to refute.

examples.text: The physicist debunked the psychic's claims

origin.ko: de-(제거)에 bunk(헛소리)를 합친 1923년의 말입니다. 헛소리를 걷어내니 '허위를 폭로하다'입니다.

senses.en: Harmful, often in a subtle or unexpected way.

examples.text: deleterious to someone's health

origin.ko: 그리스어 dēlētḗrios(해로운)에서 왔습니다. 'delete'와는 관련이 없습니다.

senses.en: Happening by fortune or chance; accidental, coincidental.

examples.text: Their meeting on the train was entirely fortuitous, yet it led to a lifelong partnership.

senses.en: occurring by happy chance

examples.text: profits were enhanced by a fortuitous drop in the cost of raw materials

origin.ko: 라틴어 fortuītus(우연히 일어난)에서 왔고 fors(우연, 운)가 바탕입니다. 뜻하지 않게 닥친 우연입니다.

senses.en: instinctively or temperamentally seeking and enjoying the company of others

examples.text: Her gregarious nature made her the center of every party she attended.

senses.en: (of animals) tending to form a group with others of the same species

examples.text: gregarious bird species

origin.ko: 라틴어 gregārius '무리의'에서 왔습니다. greg는 '가축 떼, 무리'를 뜻하며 무리 짓기 좋아하는 성질입니다.

senses.en: idyllically calm and peaceful; suggesting happy tranquillity

examples.text: She recalled the halcyon summers of her childhood spent beside the quiet lake.

senses.en: marked by peace and prosperity

examples.text: the halcyon days of the clipper trade

origin.ko: 그리스어 alkyōn '물총새'에서 왔습니다. 물총새가 알을 품는 동안 바다가 잔잔했다는 전설에서 '평온한'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: Old or old-fashioned; trite.

examples.text: The comedian relied on hoary jokes that audiences had heard a hundred times before.

senses.en: showing characteristics of age, especially having grey or white hair

examples.text: The hoary old fisherman mended his nets on the dock each morning.

origin.ko: hoar(서리처럼 하얀)에 -y가 붙은 말로 봅니다. 백발이 된 늙음이 '케케묵은'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: impervious to pleas, persuasion, requests, reason

examples.text: The intransigent union leader rejected every compromise, and the strike entered its third month.

origin.ko: 스페인어를 거쳐 라틴어 trānsigō '합의를 보다'에서 왔습니다. 합의에 이르지 않으려는 완강함입니다.

senses.en: quickly aroused to anger

examples.text: The irascible editor berated reporters over the smallest typographical errors.

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 īrāscibilis에서 왔고 īrāscī '화내다'에서 나왔습니다. 화가 쉽게 나는 성미입니다.

senses.en: ridicule with satire

examples.text: The magazine lampooned the minister's proposal in a cartoon that quickly went viral.

senses.en: A written attack or other work ridiculing a person, group, or institution; especially, a satirical one.

examples.text: The magazine's weekly lampoon of the royal family drew both laughter and complaints.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 lampons '마시자'라는 풍자 노래의 후렴에서 왔습니다. 그런 노래 같은 풍자글이라는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: Stubbornly adhering to an opinion, purpose, or course, usually with implied unreasonableness; persistent.

examples.text: The obstinate negotiator refused to yield on a single point, prolonging the talks for months.

origin.ko: 라틴어 obstinō '마음을 굳게 먹다'에서 왔고, stare '서다'와 이어집니다. 한 자리에 버티고 서서 물러나지 않는 고집입니다.

senses.en: distinctive and stylish elegance

examples.text: The pianist performed the difficult concerto with remarkable panache.

origin.ko: 프랑스어로 '투구에 꽂은 깃털 장식'이라는 뜻입니다. 깃털을 꽂은 듯 멋과 기세가 있는 모습이 되었습니다.

senses.en: Childishly irritable.

examples.text: Lack of sleep is causing Dave's recent petulant behavior.

origin.ko: 라틴어 petulāns '건방진'에서 왔고, petō '요구하다'와 가까운 말입니다.

senses.en: not sensible about practical matters; idealistic and unrealistic

examples.text: Critics called his plan to end poverty in a year a quixotic and hopelessly naive crusade.

origin.ko: 세르반테스의 소설 주인공 돈키호테(Quixote)에서 왔습니다. 풍차에 덤비는 그의 이상주의에서 '비현실적인'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: confidently optimistic and cheerful

examples.text: I'm sanguine about the eventual success of the project.

senses.en: inclined to a healthy reddish color often associated with outdoor life

examples.text: The old sailor's sanguine complexion spoke of decades spent at sea in all weathers.

origin.ko: 라틴어 sanguis(피)에서 왔습니다. 중세 의학에서 피가 많으면 명랑하고 낙천적이라고 여겼습니다.

senses.en: marked by quiet and caution and secrecy; taking pains to avoid being observed

examples.text: He cast a surreptitious glance at the answers on his neighbor's desk.

origin.ko: 라틴어 surrēptīcius에서 왔고 surrepere(몰래 기어들다)와 이어집니다. 슬그머니 몰래 하는 일입니다.

senses.en: someone new to a field or activity

examples.text: Even a tyro at chess could see that the opening move left the king dangerously exposed.

origin.ko: 라틴어 tīrō('신병, 초심자')에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: a feeling of anger caused by being offended

examples.text: The ambassador took umbrage at the suggestion that his government had interfered in the election.

origin.ko: 라틴어 umbra('그늘')에서 왔습니다. 그늘이 드리우듯 마음에 어두운 불쾌감이 생긴 것이 '분개'입니다.

senses.en: not in keeping with accepted standards of what is right or proper in polite society

examples.text: He was drunk and made some very unseemly comments.

origin.ko: 중세 영어 unsemli로, 고대 노르드어 úsǽmiligr를 본뜬 말로 봅니다. un-과 seemly('어울리는')의 결합입니다.

senses.en: Noncontentious, blandly agreeable, unlikely to cause offence or debate.

examples.text: The candidate gave an anodyne speech that offended no one and inspired even fewer.

senses.en: capable of relieving pain

examples.text: Herbal teas were once valued for their mild anodyne properties.

origin.ko: 그리스어 anodynos(고통 없는)에서 왔습니다. 아픔을 주지 않는 데서 '무난한'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: practicing great self-denial

examples.text: This experience enables Nāgārjuna to recognize that desire is the root cause of suffering and motivates him to turn to a more ascetic lifestyle.

senses.en: someone who practices self denial as a spiritual discipline

examples.text: Female ascetics find shelter in a wide variety of establishments and vary greatly in the degree to which they travel.

origin.ko: 그리스어 askētēs(수행자)에서 왔고 askeō(훈련하다)에서 나왔습니다. 몸과 마음을 단련하는 금욕 수행을 뜻합니다.

senses.en: a crusty irascible cantankerous old person full of stubborn ideas

examples.text: The neighborhood curmudgeon complained about every new fence, every barking dog, and every loud birthday party.

senses.en: fool or hoax

examples.text: The immigrant was duped because he trusted everyone

senses.en: a person who is tricked or swindled

examples.text: It would vex me, indeed, to see you again the dupe of Miss Bingley's pretended regard.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 duper에서 왔고 huppe(후투티)의 변형으로 봅니다. 쉽게 속는 새에 빗댄 말입니다.

senses.en: joyously unrestrained

examples.text: Marina's oddly ebullient words seemed to come to her slow as balloons

origin.ko: 라틴어 ēbulliō(끓어오르다)에서 왔습니다. 기쁨이 보글보글 끓어오르는 이미지입니다.

senses.en: left unplowed and unseeded during a growing season

examples.text: Farmers let the field lie fallow for a year so that the soil could recover its nutrients.

senses.en: Inactive; undeveloped.

examples.text: After a fallow period in the middle of her career, the novelist produced her finest work.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 fealh(휴경지)에서 왔습니다. 갈아엎은 채 씨를 뿌리지 않고 놀리는 땅을 가리킵니다.

senses.en: gain favor with somebody by deliberate efforts

examples.text: The new intern tried to ingratiate himself with the director by praising every idea she proposed.

origin.ko: 라틴어 in grātiam '~의 호의를 얻으려고'에서 왔습니다. 남의 호감 속으로 파고든다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: Habitually travelling from place to place.

examples.text: an itinerant preacher or peddler

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 itinerantem '여행하는'에서 왔고 iter(길)에서 나왔습니다.

senses.en: a pauper who lives by begging

examples.text: A lone mendicant sat outside the cathedral, holding out a battered tin cup.

senses.en: practicing beggary

examples.text: The mendicant friars of the thirteenth century relied entirely on public charity for their food.

origin.ko: 라틴어 mendīcāns '구걸하는'에서 왔고 mendīcō '구걸하다'에서 나왔습니다.

senses.en: someone who dislikes people in general

examples.text: The reclusive author, a confirmed misanthrope, refused every invitation to public events.

origin.ko: 그리스어 miséō '미워하다'와 ánthrōpos '사람'이 합쳐졌습니다. 사람 자체를 싫어하는 사람입니다.

senses.en: excessively unwilling to spend

examples.text: The parsimonious heir counted every coin and refused to hire any household help.

senses.en: Using a minimal number of assumptions, steps, or conjectures.

examples.text: Scientists prefer the more parsimonious explanation when two theories fit the data equally well.

origin.ko: 라틴어 parsimonia '절약'에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: cause to be more favorably inclined; gain the good will of

examples.text: The mayor tried to placate angry residents by promising a full review of the zoning decision.

origin.ko: 라틴어 plācō '달래다'에서 왔고, 원래 '부드럽게 하다'라는 뜻입니다. please와 뿌리가 같습니다.

senses.en: done with very great haste and without due deliberation

examples.text: Critics warned that a precipitate withdrawal of troops would leave the region dangerously unstable.

senses.en: To make something happen suddenly and quickly.

examples.text: it precipitated their success

senses.en: To send violently into a certain state or condition.

examples.text: we were precipitated into a conflict

origin.ko: 라틴어 praeceps('머리부터 거꾸로')에서 왔습니다. 머리부터 내던지듯 서두르는 데서 '성급한'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: presenting favorable circumstances; likely to result in or show signs of success

examples.text: The calm weather made it a propitious moment to begin the voyage.

origin.ko: 라틴어 propitius('호의적인')에서 왔습니다. 신이 호의를 보여 형편이 유리하다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: correct or appropriate behavior

examples.text: The diplomat observed every rule of propriety during the formal state dinner.

origin.ko: 라틴어 proprietās('고유한 성질')에서 왔습니다. 자기 신분에 걸맞은 올바른 행동이라는 뜻이 되었습니다.

senses.en: inspiring fear

examples.text: The challenger faced a redoubtable opponent who had not lost a debate in ten years.

senses.en: worthy of respect or honor

examples.text: born of a redoubtable family

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 redoter('두려워하다')에 -able이 붙은 말입니다. 두려워할 만한 상대라는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: An excessive amount of something.

examples.text: A surfeit of wheat is driving down the price.

senses.en: To supply (someone) with something to excess; to disgust (someone) through overabundance.

examples.text: Constant exposure to cheap sensational news can surfeit readers until they stop caring.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 surfaire(지나치게 하다)의 과거분사에서 왔습니다. 도를 넘어 과잉이 된다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: a person who tries to please someone in order to gain a personal advantage

examples.text: Surrounded by sycophants, the chairman never heard a single honest criticism of his plans.

origin.ko: 그리스어 sykophantēs(밀고자, 사기꾼)에서 왔고 '무화과를 보여 주는 자'가 글자 뜻입니다. 이후 아첨꾼을 뜻하게 되었습니다.

senses.en: repeated too often; overfamiliar through overuse

examples.text: The graduation speech relied on trite advice about following your dreams and never giving up.

origin.ko: 라틴어 trītus('닳아빠진')에서 왔고 terō('문질러 닳게 하다')의 분사입니다. 너무 써서 닳은 표현이 '진부한'입니다.

senses.en: the highest level or degree attainable; the highest stage of development

examples.text: Many critics regard the symphony as the acme of the composer's creative career.

origin.ko: 그리스어 akmē(뾰족한 끝, 정점)를 그대로 빌려온 말입니다. 가장 높은 꼭대기를 뜻합니다.

senses.en: To criticize harshly.

examples.text: The Woodwalton signalman, Rose, who was severely censured in Captain Tyler's report, behaved with great negligence.

senses.en: harsh criticism or disapproval

examples.text: Both the censure and the praise were merited.

senses.en: Official reprimand.

examples.text: The legislature issued a formal censure of the minister after the audit revealed repeated misuse of public funds.

origin.ko: 라틴어 censūra('감찰관의 직무, 평가')에서 왔습니다. 평가해서 흠을 지적하는 일이 '비난'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: establish or strengthen as with new evidence or facts

examples.text: Two independent witnesses corroborated her account of what happened that night.

origin.ko: 라틴어 corrōborō('강하게 하다')에서 왔고, con-과 rōbur(힘)가 합쳐졌습니다. 증거를 더해 힘을 실어 준다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: Scarcity; a lack or short supply.

examples.text: A dearth of signalmen and the high cost of labour is hastening an elimination process that already was well under way before the second world war.

origin.ko: dear(귀한)에 -th가 붙은 말입니다. 물건이 귀해지는 것, 곧 '부족'을 뜻하게 되었습니다.

senses.en: propriety in manners and conduct

examples.text: The judge demanded decorum in the courtroom and warned the spectators against further outbursts.

origin.ko: 라틴어 decōrum(어울리는 것)에서 왔습니다. 상황에 맞는 행동이 '예의'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: not straightforward or candid; giving a false appearance of frankness

examples.text: a disingenuous excuse

senses.en: Asserting dogmas or beliefs in a superior or arrogant way; opinionated, dictatorial.

examples.text: The dogmatic professor refused to consider any theory that challenged his own long-held views.

senses.en: characterized by assertion of unproved or unprovable principles

examples.text: Her dogmatic claims rested on assumptions that no experiment had ever confirmed.

origin.ko: 그리스어 dógma(신조)에서 후기 라틴어 dogmaticus를 거쳐 왔습니다.

senses.en: tending to vanish like vapor

examples.text: The evanescent glow of the sunset faded from the hills within minutes.

origin.ko: 라틴어 ēvānēscere(사라져 가다)에서 왔습니다. vānus(텅 빈)가 되어 가는 모습이 '곧 사라지는'입니다.

senses.en: make worse

examples.text: The proposed shutdown would exacerbate unemployment problems.

origin.ko: 라틴어 exacerbāre(몹시 쓰게 하다, 자극하다)에서 왔습니다. 쓴맛을 더해 상황을 더 나쁘게 만든다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: Excessively or tiresomely talkative.

examples.text: The garrulous host kept his guests at the door for an hour with stories.

origin.ko: 라틴어 garrulus '수다스러운'에서 왔고, garriō(재잘거리다)에서 나온 말입니다.

senses.en: A tirade, harsh scolding or rant, whether spoken or written.

examples.text: She gave her son a harangue about the dangers of playing in the street.

senses.en: To give a forceful and lengthy lecture or criticism to someone.

examples.text: The angry motorist leapt from his car to harangue the other driver.

origin.ko: 이탈리아어 aringare '공개 집회에서 연설하다'에서 왔고, 고트어 계통 hriggs(집회, 둥근 모임)가 뿌리로 추정됩니다.

senses.en: someone who attacks cherished ideas or traditional institutions
senses.ko: 우상 파괴자, 기존 관습에 도전하는 사람

examples.text: The young architect was an iconoclast who rejected every convention of the classical tradition.

senses.en: a destroyer of images used in religious worship

examples.text: Medieval iconoclasts smashed the statues and defaced the paintings that filled the cathedral.

origin.ko: 중세 그리스어 eikonoklástēs '성상 파괴자'에서 왔습니다. 형상(icon)을 부수는(clast) 사람이 기존 관습에 맞서는 사람이 되었습니다.

senses.en: attack as false or wrong

examples.text: Critics sought to impugn the researcher's findings by questioning both his methods and his motives.

origin.ko: 라틴어 impugnō '맞서 싸우다'에서 왔고 pugnus(주먹)가 뿌리입니다. 주먹을 들고 덤비듯 반박합니다.

senses.en: only partly in existence; imperfectly formed
senses.ko: 막 시작된, 아직 형태가 갖춰지지 않은

examples.text: The inchoate plan had no budget, no timeline, and only a vague sense of purpose.

senses.en: Chaotic, disordered, confused; also, incoherent, rambling.

examples.text: His inchoate ramblings left the committee unsure what exactly he was proposing.

origin.ko: 라틴어 incohātus '막 시작된, 미완성의'에서 왔고 incohō(시작하다)가 뿌리입니다.

senses.en: fill quickly beyond capacity; as with a liquid

examples.text: The agency was inundated with phone calls.

senses.en: fill or cover completely, usually with water

examples.text: Heavy rains inundated the valley, forcing hundreds of families to leave their homes overnight.

origin.ko: 라틴어 inundō '범람하다'에서 왔고 unda(물결)에서 나왔습니다. 물결이 밀려드는 모습입니다.

senses.en: full of trivial conversation

examples.text: The loquacious host kept his guests at the table long after the meal was finished.

origin.ko: 라틴어 loquāx '말 많은'에서 왔고 loquor '말하다'에서 나왔습니다.

senses.en: Having or displaying ill will; wishing harm on others.

examples.text: The villain fixed the hero with a malevolent stare before slipping out of the room.

senses.en: having or exerting a malignant influence

examples.text: malevolent stars

origin.ko: 라틴어 male(나쁘게)과 volens(바라는)가 합쳐졌습니다. 남에게 나쁜 일을 바라는 마음입니다.

senses.en: The lowest point; time of greatest depression.

examples.text: The team's fortunes reached their nadir after a ninth consecutive defeat.

origin.ko: 아랍어 '천정(zenith)의 맞은편 지점'이라는 표현에서 왔습니다. 하늘 꼭대기의 정반대가 최저점입니다.

senses.en: Excessively eager and attentive to please or to obey instructions; fawning, subservient, servile.

examples.text: The obsequious aide laughed at every joke his employer made, however feeble.

origin.ko: 라틴어 obsequor '순순히 따르다'에서 왔습니다. 윗사람 뒤를 졸졸 따라다니며 비위를 맞추는 모습입니다.

senses.en: To anticipate and prevent or bypass (something which would otherwise have been necessary or required); to render (something) unnecessary.

examples.text: A reliable public transit system would obviate the need for most residents to own a car.

origin.ko: 라틴어 obviō '길을 막다, 방해하다'에서 왔습니다. 길목을 미리 막아 일이 필요 없게 만든다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: Offensively intrusive or interfering in offering advice and services.

examples.text: The officious receptionist insisted on reviewing every visitor's paperwork twice, though nobody had asked her to.

origin.ko: 라틴어 officiōsus '친절한'에서 왔고, officium은 '봉사'입니다. 원치 않는 봉사까지 하려 드는 데서 참견하는이 되었습니다.

senses.en: working or spreading in a hidden and usually injurious way

examples.text: Critics warned of the pernicious influence of misinformation on public trust.

senses.en: exceedingly harmful

examples.text: Poverty has a pernicious effect on children's long-term health.

origin.ko: 라틴어 perniciōsus '파멸적인'에서 왔고, perniciēs는 '파괴'입니다. nex는 '죽음'이라는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: recklessly wasteful

examples.text: The prodigal heir squandered the family fortune within a decade.

senses.en: Yielding profusely, lavish.

examples.text: How can he be so prodigal with money on such a tight budget?

senses.en: Returning or having returned, especially repentantly, after such an abandonment.

examples.text: Fans welcomed the prodigal star back to the club after three years abroad.

origin.ko: 라틴어 prōdigus('낭비하는')에서 왔고, prōd-('앞으로')와 agō('몰다')가 합쳐졌습니다. 재산을 마구 몰아 내버린다는 이미지입니다.

senses.en: Having a tendency to argue or fight; aggressive, combative.

examples.text: The pugnacious columnist seemed to relish every opportunity to provoke an argument.

origin.ko: 라틴어 pugnāx('싸우기 좋아하는')에서 왔고 pugnus('주먹')와 이어집니다. 주먹부터 나가는 호전적인 성격입니다.

senses.en: To criticize or rebuke (someone).

examples.text: She reproached herself for failing to notice the warning signs sooner.

senses.en: a mild rebuke or criticism

examples.text: words of reproach

senses.en: disgrace or shame

examples.text: he brought reproach upon his family

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 reprochier('나무라다')에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: marked by care and persistent effort

examples.text: Through sedulous practice, the young pianist mastered the difficult concerto in a matter of months.

origin.ko: 라틴어 sēdulus(부지런한)에서 왔습니다. '속임수 없이' 성실하게 한다는 뜻으로 보는 설이 있습니다.

senses.en: sleep inducing

examples.text: The professor delivered a soporific lecture.

senses.en: a drug that induces sleep

examples.text: The doctor prescribed a soporific to help the patient sleep.

origin.ko: 라틴어 sopor(깊은 잠)에서 왔습니다. 잠을 만들어내는 것입니다.

senses.en: inclined to anger or bad feelings with overtones of menace

examples.text: a surly waiter

origin.ko: sir(나리)에서 나온 sirly의 변형입니다. 나리처럼 거만하고 퉁명스럽다는 뜻이 되었습니다.

senses.en: Inherent baseness, depravity or wickedness; corruptness and evilness.

examples.text: The visa was denied because the applicant had been convicted of a crime of moral turpitude.

origin.ko: 라틴어 turpitūdō('추함, 수치')에서 왔고 turpis('더러운')와 이어집니다.

senses.en: occurring without motivation or provocation

examples.text: The report condemned the wanton destruction of the village by retreating troops.

senses.en: casual and unrestrained in sexual behavior

examples.text: The preacher denounced the wanton behavior of the court.

senses.en: spend wastefully

examples.text: The young man wantoned away his inheritance.

origin.ko: 중세 영어 wantoun으로, wan-('아닌')과 towen('가르침을 받은')의 결합입니다. 교육받지 못해 제멋대로라는 뜻이 '이유 없는'으로 이어졌습니다.

senses.en: polish and make shiny

examples.text: The silversmith burnished the bowl until it gleamed like a mirror.

senses.en: To make (someone or something) appear positive and highly respected.

examples.text: The charity gala helped the senator burnish his image after a damaging scandal.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 burnir('윤을 내다, 갈색으로 만들다')에서 왔습니다. 문질러 반들반들 빛내는 일입니다.

senses.en: a false accusation of an offense or a malicious misrepresentation of someone's words or actions

examples.text: The candidate denounced the rumors as calumny invented by rivals desperate to ruin his reputation.

origin.ko: 라틴어 calumnia('거짓 고발, 악의적 모함')에서 왔고, challenge와 같은 어원에서 갈라진 말입니다.

senses.en: cause to become widely known

examples.text: The values of the human rights movement have disseminated throughout the world.

origin.ko: 라틴어 dissēmināre(씨를 흩뿌리다)에서 왔습니다. 씨 뿌리듯 널리 퍼뜨린다는 이미지입니다.

senses.en: lasting a very short time

examples.text: the ephemeral joys of childhood

origin.ko: 그리스어 ephḗmeros(하루 동안 사는)에서 왔습니다. 하루살이처럼 짧게 지속된다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: Exceeding proper limits; excessive or unduly high; extravagant.

examples.text: You also have to pay exorbitant interest if you have credit card debt.

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 exorbitāre(바퀴 자국에서 벗어나다)에서 왔습니다. 정상 궤도를 벗어난 '터무니없는'이라는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: try to gain favor by cringing or flattering

examples.text: Aides fawned over the chairman, laughing at every joke and praising every mediocre idea.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 fagnian(기뻐하다)에서 왔습니다. 기뻐하는 척 굽실대는 데서 '아첨하다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: intellectually productive

examples.text: The fecund imagination of the young architect produced dozens of striking designs in a single year.

senses.en: capable of producing offspring or vegetation

examples.text: The river's fecund delta has supported dense farming populations for thousands of years.

origin.ko: 라틴어 fēcundus(열매 많은, 비옥한)에서 프랑스어를 거쳐 왔습니다. 땅이 비옥하듯 창의력이 풍부하다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: invulnerable to fear or intimidation

examples.text: The intrepid explorers crossed the frozen plateau with little more than sled dogs and a few supplies.

origin.ko: 라틴어 intrepidus에서 왔습니다. 불안해 떠는(trepidus) 일이 없으니 '두려움을 모르는'입니다.

senses.en: transmitting light; able to be seen through with clarity

examples.text: The limpid water of the mountain lake revealed every pebble on the bottom.

senses.en: (of language) transparently clear; easily understandable

examples.text: writes in a limpid style

origin.ko: 프랑스어 limpide에서 왔고 라틴어 limpidus '맑은'과 이어집니다.

senses.en: Gloomy, mournful or dismal, especially to an exaggerated degree.

examples.text: His client’s lugubrious expression tipped off the detective that something lurked beneath her optimistic words.

origin.ko: 라틴어 lūgubris '애도하는, 침울한'에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: To appease anger, pacify, gain the good will of.

examples.text: He tried to mollify the angry customer.

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 mollificō에서 왔고 mollis(부드러운)에서 나왔습니다. 부드럽게 만들어 달랜다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: not easily irritated

examples.text: Her placid temperament kept the team calm even when deadlines collapsed around them.

senses.en: calm and quiet; peaceful; tranquil

examples.text: a placid lake

origin.ko: 라틴어 placidus '평온한'에서 왔고, placeō는 '마음에 들다'입니다.

senses.en: having or revealing little emotion or sensibility; not easily aroused or excited

examples.text: The stolid juror listened to the emotional testimony without any visible reaction.

origin.ko: 라틴어 stolidus(둔한, 어리석은)에서 왔습니다. 감정 변화가 없어 둔해 보인다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: marked by a ready flow of speech

examples.text: The voluble taxi driver told us his whole life story before we had even left the airport.

origin.ko: 라틴어 volūbilis('구르는')에서 왔고 volvō('굴리다')와 이어집니다. 말이 굴러가듯 막힘없이 나옵니다.

senses.en: To punish or reprimand someone severely.

examples.text: The editorial castigated the board for ignoring safety warnings that might have prevented the disaster.

origin.ko: 라틴어 castīgō('꾸짖다')에서 왔고, castus(순결한)에서 갈라졌습니다. 순수하게 바로잡으려고 혹독하게 벌한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: highly complex or intricate and occasionally devious

examples.text: He gave a convoluted explanation that amounted to little more than a weak excuse for his absence.

senses.en: hide under a false appearance

examples.text: He masked his disappointment

senses.en: make believe with the intent to deceive

examples.text: He dissembled sleep so that the guards would not question him during the long night.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 dissembler에서 왔고 라틴어 dissimulō(숨기다)에 기원합니다. 겉모습을 다르게 꾸민다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: Insolent and shameless audacity.

examples.text: We even had the effrontery to suggest that he should leave the country.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 effronterie에서 왔고 effronté(철면피)에서 나왔습니다. 이마(front)가 두꺼워 부끄러움을 모르는 모습입니다.

senses.en: To draw out, bring out, bring forth (something latent); to obtain information from someone or something.

examples.text: Fred wished to elicit the time of the meeting from Jane.

origin.ko: 라틴어 ēlicere(끌어내다)에서 왔습니다. 숨은 것을 밖으로 끌어내는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: a behavioral attribute that is distinctive and peculiar to an individual

examples.text: Among the professor's idiosyncrasies was a habit of lecturing while standing on a chair.

origin.ko: 그리스어 idiosynkrasía '자기만의 기질'에서 왔습니다. 자기만의(idio) 것이 함께(syn) 섞인(cras) 기질이라는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: not easily perturbed or excited or upset; marked by extreme calm and composure

examples.text: The imperturbable pilot calmly guided the damaged aircraft through the storm while passengers panicked.

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 imperturbābilis에서 왔습니다. 완전히 흔들어 놓을 수 없을 만큼 침착하다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: not injurious to physical or mental health

examples.text: The mushrooms looked innocuous, but several of them were in fact mildly poisonous.

senses.en: not causing disapproval

examples.text: it was an innocuous remark

origin.ko: 라틴어 innocuus '해가 없는'에서 왔습니다. 해치지(noc) 않으니 무해합니다.

senses.en: a subtle difference in meaning or opinion or attitude

examples.text: Translators struggle to preserve every nuance of the poet's tone when rendering it into another language.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 nuance '색조, 농담'에서 왔습니다. 구름(라틴어 nūbēs)처럼 번지는 미묘한 색의 차이를 뜻합니다.

senses.en: model of excellence or perfection of a kind; one having no equal

examples.text: In the novel, Constanza is a paragon of virtue who would never compromise her reputation.

origin.ko: 이탈리아어 paragonare '시금석에 대어 시험하다'에서 왔습니다. 시금석에 대도 가장 뛰어난 본보기라는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: a strong liking

examples.text: He has a penchant for fine wine.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 pencher '기울다'의 현재분사입니다. 마음이 한쪽으로 기우는 강한 취향입니다.

senses.en: prove to be false or incorrect

examples.text: New archaeological evidence refuted the long-held theory that the settlement was abandoned suddenly.

origin.ko: 라틴어 refūtāre('물리치다, 반박하다')에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: determined by chance or impulse or whim rather than by necessity or reason

examples.text: The whimsical decisions of the new owner left employees unsure what to expect each week.

senses.en: Given to whimsy.

examples.text: The illustrator's whimsical drawings of talking teapots delighted young readers.

senses.en: enlarge or increase

examples.text: The money from renting out a spare room can augment a salary.

origin.ko: 라틴어 augmentum(증가)에서 왔고 augere(늘리다)에서 나왔습니다.

senses.en: Lacking the proper care or concern for something important, reckless, rash, high-handed.

examples.text: The executive's cavalier attitude toward safety complaints alarmed regulators and angered the workers.

senses.en: a gallant or courtly gentleman

examples.text: The old cavalier bowed deeply and kissed her hand before escorting her to the dance.

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 caballārius('기마병')에서 온 프랑스어를 거쳤고, 라틴어 caballus(말)가 뿌리입니다. 말 탄 기사의 거만함입니다.

senses.en: Chiefly followed by to, and sometimes by at or on: to object or be reluctant; to balk, to take exception.

examples.text: The personnel demurred at the management’s new scheme.

origin.ko: 라틴어 dēmorārī(지체하다)에서 왔습니다. 선뜻 응하지 않고 미적대다가 '이의를 제기하다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: Slow or tardy.

examples.text: The dilatory contractor missed every deadline and left the renovation unfinished for months.

senses.en: Intentionally delaying (someone or something), intended to cause delay, gain time, or adjourn decision.

examples.text: a dilatory strategy

origin.ko: 라틴어 dīlātōrius(미루는)에서 왔고 differō에서 나왔습니다. delay와는 어원이 다릅니다.

senses.en: confined to and understandable by only an enlightened inner circle

examples.text: The writing in this manual is very esoteric; I’d need a degree in engineering just to understand it!

origin.ko: 그리스어 esōterikós(안쪽 모임에 속한)에서 왔습니다. 원래 철학자들이 제자 내부에만 가르친 비밀 교리를 가리켰습니다.

senses.en: Characterized by very precise, conscientious attention to details.

examples.text: The archivist kept meticulous records of every manuscript that passed through the library.

origin.ko: 라틴어 meticulōsus '겁 많은'에서 왔고 metus '두려움'에서 나왔습니다. 프랑스어를 거치며 '세심한'이라는 뜻이 더해졌습니다.

senses.en: An inclination, disposition, tendency, preference, or attraction.

examples.text: He has a propensity for lengthy discussions of certain favorite topics.

origin.ko: 라틴어 propensus('기울어진')에서 나온 말입니다. 마음이 어느 쪽으로 기우는 성향입니다.

senses.en: acutely insightful and wise

examples.text: observant and thoughtful, he was given to asking sagacious questions

origin.ko: 라틴어 sagāx(날카로운 감각의)에서 왔습니다. 냄새를 잘 맡는 사냥개처럼 통찰력이 예리하다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: To swing indecisively from one course of action or opinion to another.

examples.text: Though it is vital to be alert for circumstances which require a change of plan, it is fatal to vacillate.

origin.ko: 라틴어 vacillō('흔들리다')에서 왔습니다. 이리저리 비틀거리듯 마음이 오가는 것이 '망설이다'입니다.

senses.en: the trait of lacking enthusiasm for or interest in things generally

examples.text: Widespread voter apathy left the municipal election decided by barely a fifth of eligible residents.

origin.ko: 그리스어 apatheia(고통받지 않음, 무감정)에서 왔습니다. 감정이 전혀 일지 않는 상태입니다.

senses.en: To appropriate or lay claim to something for oneself without right.

examples.text: The executive branch has steadily arrogated powers that the constitution reserves to the legislature.

origin.ko: 라틴어 arrogare(요구해 자기 것으로 삼다)에서 왔습니다. 권리 없이 제 것으로 요구하는 것입니다.

senses.en: find out, learn, or determine with certainty, usually by making an inquiry or other effort

examples.text: As soon as we ascertain what the situation is, we can plan how to proceed.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 acertener(확실하게 하다)에서 왔고 라틴어 certus(확실한)에서 나왔습니다. 확실한 쪽으로 가져가 알아내는 것입니다.

senses.en: fundamentally different or distinct in quality or kind

examples.text: such disparate attractions as grand opera and game fishing

origin.ko: 라틴어 disparātus(갈라 놓은)에서 왔습니다. 서로 나뉘어 이질적이라는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: Clear; easily understood.

examples.text: The professor's lucid explanation made a notoriously difficult theorem accessible to first-year students.

senses.en: having a clear mind

examples.text: a lucid moment in his madness

origin.ko: 라틴어 lucidus에서 왔고 lūceō '빛나다'에서 나왔습니다. 빛처럼 환히 맑다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: Of or pertaining to piety, exhibiting piety, devout, god-fearing.

examples.text: The pious villagers gathered each morning for prayer before beginning their work.

senses.en: Insisting on or making a show of one's own virtue, especially in comparison to others; sanctimonious, condescending, judgmental.

examples.text: His pious lectures about honesty irritated colleagues who knew his own record.

origin.ko: 라틴어 pīus '독실한, 의무를 다하는'에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: Unspoiled; still with its original purity; uncorrupted or unsullied.
senses.ko: 원래 상태 그대로의, 때 묻지 않은

examples.text: The beach back is in pristine condition after a council-led cleanup.

origin.ko: 라틴어 prīstinus('옛날의, 원래의')에서 왔습니다. 처음 상태 그대로 때 묻지 않았다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: so extremely old as seeming to belong to an earlier period

examples.text: The company's archaic filing system slowed every request for records.

origin.ko: 그리스어 arkhaikos(옛날식의)에서 왔고 arkhe(시작)에서 나왔습니다. 처음 시절의 것이라 '고풍의'입니다.

senses.en: characterized by great caution and wariness

examples.text: chary of the risks involved

senses.en: Not disposed to give freely; not lavish; frugal, sparing.

examples.text: The critic was chary of praise, awarding top marks to only a handful of films each decade.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 ċeariġ('조심스러운, 근심하는')에서 왔습니다. 걱정이 많아 몸을 사리는 모습입니다.

senses.en: extreme greed for material wealth

examples.text: The historian blamed the collapse of the colony on the cupidity of its merchant backers.

origin.ko: 라틴어 cupiditās(강한 욕망)에서 왔습니다. 사랑의 신 Cupid와 같은 어원 계열입니다.

senses.en: Selecting a mixture of what appears to be best of various doctrines, methods or styles.

examples.text: Though rooted in jazz, Byron's music is stylistically eclectic.

senses.en: Unrelated and unspecialized; heterogeneous.

examples.text: Her eclectic reading list ranged from medieval poetry to quantum physics and cookbooks.

origin.ko: 그리스어 eklektikós(골라 뽑는)에서 왔습니다. 여러 곳에서 좋은 것만 골라 쓴다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: strive to equal or match, especially by imitating

examples.text: He is emulating the skating skills of his older sister

origin.ko: 라틴어 aemulārī(겨루다, 따라잡으려 하다)에서 왔습니다. 경쟁 상대를 본받아 따라잡으려는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: hard or impossible to understand

examples.text: The contract's opaque language hid several costly obligations from the unwary buyer.

senses.en: Allowing little light to pass through, not translucent or transparent.

examples.text: The opaque glass shielded the room from the street.

origin.ko: 라틴어 opacus '그늘진, 어두운'에서 왔습니다. 빛이 통하지 않는다는 뜻이 이해하기 어렵다로 이어졌습니다.

senses.en: (of language) transparently clear; easily understandable

examples.text: Written in spare, pellucid prose, the book reads like a close-to-the-bone memoir.

senses.en: transmitting light; able to be seen through with clarity

examples.text: Divers admired the pellucid water of the mountain lake.

origin.ko: 라틴어 pellūcidus '속까지 환히 비치는'에서 왔습니다. 빛이 통과할 만큼 투명하게 명쾌하다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: be deliberately ambiguous or unclear in order to mislead or withhold information

examples.text: Pressed about the missing funds, the treasurer prevaricated and changed the subject.

origin.ko: 라틴어 praevāricārī('비뚤게 걷다')에서 왔습니다. 다리를 벌리고 비틀거리듯 말을 얼버무리게 되었습니다.

senses.en: habitually complaining

examples.text: The querulous patient found fault with the food, the bed, and the nurses.

origin.ko: 라틴어 querulus('불평하는')에서 왔고 queror('불평하다')에서 나왔습니다.

senses.en: official permission or approval

examples.text: The whalers had been operating in the contested waters off the island with sanction from the Japanese government.

senses.en: A penalty, punishment, or some coercive measure, intended to ensure compliance; especially one adopted by several nations, or by an international body.

examples.text: The United States enacted a new round of sanctions against the apartheid regime of South Africa.

senses.en: give authority or permission to

examples.text: The board refused to sanction the merger until regulators completed their review.

origin.ko: 라틴어 sānctiō(법령, 확정)에서 왔습니다. 법적으로 확정된 승인이라는 뜻이며 제재의 뜻도 갖게 되었습니다.

senses.en: practicing great self-denial

examples.text: I went on the retreat to the monastery, thinking I would be sleeping in a spartan cell, only to discover a simple but comfortable bedroom.

senses.en: resolute in the face of pain or danger or adversity

examples.text: The spartan legionaries vowed to fight to the death.

origin.ko: 고대 그리스 도시국가 스파르타 사람들이 검소하고 금욕적이었던 데서 나온 말입니다.

senses.en: Straightforward, open and sincere, whether people find either refreshing or distasteful.

examples.text: In a candid interview, the coach admitted that the team had played poorly all season.

senses.en: Impartial and free from prejudice.

examples.text: The committee asked for a candid assessment of the proposal from someone with no stake in the outcome.

origin.ko: 라틴어 candidus('하얀')에서 왔습니다. 속이 희고 깨끗해 숨길 것 없이 솔직하다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: To say something in contradiction to.

examples.text: No one could gainsay the evidence of the scientists' decade of careful measurements.

origin.ko: 중세영어 gainsayen에서 왔습니다. 상대의 말에 맞서(gain-) 말한다(say)는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: uncertain how to act or proceed

examples.text: Irresolute about the merger, the board postponed its vote for a third time.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 irrésolu에서 왔거나 ir-와 resolute(단호한)가 합쳐졌습니다. 마음을 정하지 못한 상태입니다.

senses.en: To reduce, lessen, or decrease and thereby to make less severe or easier to bear.

examples.text: Planting trees along the river bank helps mitigate the damage caused by seasonal flooding.

origin.ko: 라틴어 mītigō '부드럽게 하다, 달래다'에서 왔고 mītis(부드러운)에서 나왔습니다. 거친 정도를 누그러뜨린다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: To conciliate, appease, or make peace with someone, particularly a god or spirit.

examples.text: Villagers offered grain and wine to propitiate the angry river god.

origin.ko: 라틴어 propitiāre('호의를 얻다')에서 왔고 propitius('호의적인')와 이어집니다. 화난 신을 달래 호의를 얻는다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: a person addicted to luxury and pleasures of the senses

examples.text: The sybarite spent his afternoons in silk robes, sampling rare wines and ignoring his estates.

origin.ko: 이탈리아 남부의 그리스 도시 시바리스 주민에서 왔습니다. 부와 향락으로 유명했던 도시입니다.

senses.en: Imitative of the work of someone else.

examples.text: Reviewers dismissed the novel as derivative, a pale echo of the author's more inventive early work.

senses.en: Obtained by derivation; not radical, original, or fundamental.

examples.text: a derivative word

senses.en: a financial instrument whose value is based on another security

examples.text: Complex derivatives tied to subprime mortgages amplified losses across the global banking system.

origin.ko: 라틴어 dērīvāre(물을 끌어내다)에서 왔습니다. 남의 물줄기에서 가져온 것이라 '모방적인'입니다.

senses.en: Insignificantly small.

examples.text: He gave me only a nominal sum for my services.

senses.en: Existing in name only.

examples.text: a nominal difference

origin.ko: 라틴어 nōmen '이름'에서 왔습니다. 이름뿐이고 실질이 없다는 데서 '명목상의'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: To bear; endure; put up with; tolerate.

examples.text: I will not brook any disobedience.

senses.en: a natural stream of water smaller than a river (and often a tributary of a river)

examples.text: Children waded in the shallow brook behind the farmhouse all summer.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 brūcan('즐기다, 사용하다')에서 왔습니다. 받아들여 쓰다에서 '참고 견디다'로 바뀌었습니다.

senses.en: To reduce strength or energy; debilitate.

examples.text: After being laid off three times in a row, she felt too enervated to look for another job.

origin.ko: 라틴어 ēnervāre(힘줄을 뽑아내다)에서 왔습니다. 힘줄이 빠진 듯 힘이 약해진다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: To become (or cause to become) inflexible and rigid in habits or opinions.

examples.text: Before long, the entire organization ossifies.

senses.en: become bony

examples.text: The tissue ossified

origin.ko: 라틴어 os, ossis '뼈'에 -ify가 붙은 말입니다. 뼈처럼 굳어 융통성이 없어진다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: Meaningless language with an exaggerated style intended to impress.

examples.text: Voters grew tired of campaign rhetoric that promised sweeping change but offered no concrete plans.

senses.en: using language effectively to please or persuade

examples.text: Aristotle's treatise on rhetoric remains a foundation for the study of persuasion.

origin.ko: 그리스어 rhētorikē(연설가의 기술)에서 왔습니다. 말솜씨가 알맹이 없는 미사여구라는 뜻으로도 쓰입니다.

senses.en: concerning or characterized by an appreciation of beauty or good taste

examples.text: Planners argued that the new tower offered aesthetic value as well as practical office space.

senses.en: The set of artistic motifs defining a collection of things, especially works of art; more broadly, their aura or “vibe”.

examples.text: The studio's minimalist aesthetic runs through its posters, packaging, and even its office furniture.

origin.ko: 그리스어 aisthanomai(느끼다)에서 온 aisthētikos(감각의)가 어원입니다. 감각으로 아름다움을 느낀다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: Casually careless or indifferent; showing a lack of concern; nonchalant.

examples.text: She had a blithe disregard of cultures outside the United States.

senses.en: carefree and happy and lighthearted

examples.text: The blithe young poet sang as he walked along the river each morning.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 blīþe('기쁜, 온화한')에서 왔습니다. 걱정 없이 밝은 상태가 '무심한'이란 뜻으로 번졌습니다.

senses.en: To surrender on stipulated terms, end all resistance, give up, go along with or comply.

examples.text: He argued and hollered for so long that I finally capitulated just to make him stop.

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 capitulō('항목별로 정리하다, 협상하다')에서 왔고, capitulum(작은 머리, 장)에서 갈라졌습니다. 조건을 항목별로 적어 항복한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: censure severely

examples.text: My urban, academic friends chastise me for romanticizing rural life.

senses.en: To punish, especially by corporal punishment.

examples.text: In earlier centuries, schoolmasters routinely chastised disobedient pupils with a cane.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 chastier에서 왔고 라틴어 castīgō에서 갈라졌습니다. castigate와 같은 어원으로, 순수하게 바로잡는 꾸짖음입니다.

senses.en: an authoritative declaration

examples.text: The coach's dictum that practice makes perfect shaped how the whole team trained.

senses.en: A judicial opinion expressed by judges on points that do not necessarily arise in the case, and are not involved in it.

examples.text: The judge's dictum on press freedom was not binding but was widely quoted in later cases.

origin.ko: 라틴어 dictum(말해진 것, 격언)에서 왔고 dīcō(말하다)가 뿌리입니다.

senses.en: unaffected by strong emotion or prejudice

examples.text: a journalist should be a dispassionate reporter of fact

senses.en: producing or capable of producing an intended result or having a striking effect

examples.text: Researchers found the new antibiotic highly efficacious against drug-resistant infections.

origin.ko: 라틴어 efficāx(효과적인)에서 왔고 efficere(이루어내다)에서 나왔습니다.

senses.en: add details to

examples.text: The witness was accused of embellishing the story to make it sound more dramatic.

senses.en: To make more beautiful and attractive by adding ornamentation; to decorate.

examples.text: The old book cover was embellished with golden letters

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 embellir에서 왔습니다. bel(아름다운)을 더해 꾸민다는 뜻이어서 이야기를 윤색한다는 뜻이 되었습니다.

senses.en: lacking social polish

examples.text: It seemed gauche to the hostess that he asked the price of every painting on her walls.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 gauche '왼쪽의, 서투른'에서 왔습니다. 왼쪽을 어색하고 서투르다고 여긴 데서 나온 뜻입니다.

senses.en: improperly forward or bold

examples.text: The teacher scolded the boy for his impertinent reply to the visiting dignitary.

senses.en: not pertinent to the matter under consideration

examples.text: The lawyer objected that the question was impertinent to the central issue of the trial.

origin.ko: 라틴어 impertinēns에서 왔습니다. 맞는 자리에 속하지 않고 나선다는 데서 '무례한'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: In an initial stage; beginning, starting, coming into existence.

examples.text: After 500 years, incipient towns appeared.

origin.ko: 라틴어 incipiēns '시작하는'에서 왔고 incipiō(시작하다)가 뿌리입니다. 막 손을 대기 시작한다는 이미지입니다.

senses.en: impossible to deny or disprove
senses.ko: 논란의 여지가 없는, 반박할 수 없는

examples.text: incontrovertible evidence

origin.ko: controvert(반박하다)에 부정 접두사가 붙은 말입니다. 반대쪽으로 돌려세울 수 없으니 반박할 수 없다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: impervious to correction by punishment

examples.text: The incorrigible prankster ignored every detention and kept scheming new tricks to play on his teachers.

senses.en: difficult or impossible to manage or control

examples.text: The committee found the backlog incorrigible, since no reorganization had ever managed to tame it.

origin.ko: 라틴어 incorrigibilis '고칠 수 없는'에서 왔습니다. corrigere(바로잡다)에 부정 접두사가 붙었습니다.

senses.en: To let go or get rid of as being useless or defective.

examples.text: The new administration was quick to jettison its predecessor's most costly programs.

senses.en: To eject from a boat, submarine, aircraft, spaceship or hot-air balloon, so as to lighten the load.

examples.text: The ballooners had to jettison all of their sand bags to make it over the final hill.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 geter '던지다'에서 왔습니다. 배의 짐을 바다에 던져 버린다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: offensively self-assured or given to exercising usually unwarranted power

examples.text: The critic's magisterial tone suggested that no other reading of the poem could possibly be valid.

senses.en: Befitting the status or skill of a magister or master; authoritative, masterly.

examples.text: Her magisterial survey of the period remains the standard reference for graduate students.

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 magisterialis에서 왔고 라틴어 magisterium '스승의 직분'과 이어집니다. 스승 같은 권위를 내세우는 태도입니다.

senses.en: An incongruous mixture; a hodgepodge.

examples.text: The house failed to attract a buyer because the decor was a pastiche of Bohemian and Scandinavian styles.

senses.en: a work of art that imitates the style of some previous work

examples.text: The film is a loving pastiche of 1940s detective stories.

origin.ko: 이탈리아어 pasticcio '여러 재료를 섞은 파이'에서 왔습니다. 이것저것 섞은 짜깁기라는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: labored and dull

examples.text: a ponderous speech

senses.en: Clumsy, unwieldy, or slow, especially due to weight.

examples.text: The ponderous machinery groaned slowly into motion as the factory shift began.

origin.ko: 라틴어 ponderōsus('무게 있는')에서 왔습니다. 무겁고 둔한 느낌이 '둔하고 지루한'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: Distant from the lives and everyday concerns of ordinary people; esoteric, exclusive, select.

examples.text: This is one of the most sought-after models in the rarefied world of high-performance sports car collecting.

senses.en: Less dense than usual; thin.

examples.text: The air at high altitudes at the top of mountains is rarefied.

senses.en: showing a high degree of refinement and the assurance that comes from wide social experience

examples.text: The urbane ambassador charmed every guest at the dinner with his easy wit and impeccable manners.

origin.ko: 라틴어 urbānus('도시의')에서 왔습니다. 도시 사람처럼 세련됐다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: an indication that something has been present

examples.text: Only a few vestiges of the ancient forest survive among the housing developments.

senses.en: A vestigial organ; a non-functional organ or body part that was once functional in an evolutionary ancestor.

examples.text: The human appendix is often described as a vestige of a larger digestive organ in our ancestors.

origin.ko: 라틴어 vestīgium('발자국')에서 왔습니다. 지나간 발자국이 '자취, 흔적'입니다.

senses.en: speak, plead, or argue in favor of

examples.text: The report advocates stricter limits on emissions from coal-fired power stations.

senses.en: a person who pleads for a cause or propounds an idea

examples.text: As a lifelong advocate of public libraries, she donated her book collection to the town.

origin.ko: 라틴어 advocatus(도움을 청해 불려온 사람)에서 왔습니다. 곁에서 변호해 주는 사람이 '옹호하다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: surround so as to force to give up

examples.text: The Turks besieged Vienna

senses.en: harass, as with questions or requests

examples.text: The press photographers besieged the movie star

origin.ko: 중세 영어 besegen에서 왔고, be-(둘레에)에 siege(포위)가 붙은 말입니다. 성 둘레를 빙 둘러싸는 모습입니다.

senses.en: a deliberately misleading fabrication

examples.text: The claim that the dam was unsafe turned out to be a canard spread by its opponents.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 canard('오리, 거짓 소문')를 빌려 온 말입니다. 오리를 '반만 판다'는 옛 표현에서 왔다는 설이 있습니다.

senses.en: a very intense and uncontrolled fire

examples.text: A single spark from the warehouse ignited a conflagration that consumed the entire block.

origin.ko: 라틴어 cōnflagrātiō('완전히 불탐')에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: be confusing or perplexing to; cause to be unable to think clearly

examples.text: The unexpected results confounded researchers, who had predicted the opposite outcome.

senses.en: To defeat, to frustrate, to thwart.

examples.text: The champion confounded expectations by winning the title with a seriously injured shoulder.

origin.ko: 라틴어 cōnfundō('함께 붓다, 뒤섞다')에서 왔습니다. 모두 섞어 뒤죽박죽 만든다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: To criticize so as to besmirch; traduce, disparage or defame.

examples.text: Rival candidates tried to denigrate her record by distorting her votes on key bills.

senses.en: To treat as worthless; belittle, degrade or disparage.

examples.text: You have no right to denigrate people and things that you have no personal experience with.

origin.ko: 라틴어 dēnigrāre(검게 칠하다)에서 왔습니다. 남을 검게 칠해 평판을 더럽힌다는 이미지입니다.

senses.en: A mournful poem or piece of music composed or performed as a memorial to a deceased person.

examples.text: It was as if the night sang dirges with clenched teeth.

origin.ko: 라틴어 dirige(인도하소서)에서 왔습니다. 장례 기도문의 첫머리 말이 그대로 '장송곡'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: comical in an odd or whimsical manner

examples.text: a droll little man with a quiet tongue-in-cheek kind of humor

origin.ko: 프랑스어 drôle(익살꾼)에서 왔고 중세 네덜란드어 drol(작은 요괴)로 거슬러 올라갑니다. troll과 이중어입니다.

senses.en: specify individually

examples.text: She enumerated the many obstacles she had encountered

senses.en: determine the number or amount of

examples.text: Volunteers enumerated the migrating birds as they passed over the marsh.

origin.ko: 라틴어 ēnumerāre(하나하나 세다)에서 왔습니다. 하나씩 수를 세듯 나열한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: steadiness of mind under stress

examples.text: he accepted their problems with composure and she with equanimity

origin.ko: 라틴어 aequanimitās에서 왔습니다. '고른 마음'이라는 뜻으로, 흔들리지 않는 평정을 가리킵니다.

senses.en: containing or based on a fallacy

examples.text: The debate coach showed students how a fallacious argument can sound persuasive while proving nothing.

senses.en: involving deception

examples.text: Regulators fined the company for fallacious advertising that hid the true cost of the loan.

origin.ko: 라틴어 fallācia(속임)에서 고대 프랑스어를 거쳐 왔습니다. 속이는 듯한 잘못된 논리라는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: To incite or cause troublesome acts; to encourage; to instigate.

examples.text: Foreign governments have tried to foment unrest.

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 fōmentāre(따뜻한 찜질을 하다)에서 왔습니다. 불씨를 덥혀 키우듯 불화를 조장한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: marked by defiant disregard for danger or consequences

examples.text: It would be foolhardy to invest your entire savings in a single speculative venture.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 fol hardi(어리석게 용감한)에서 왔습니다. fool(어리석은)과 hardy(대담한)가 합쳐진 말입니다.

senses.en: To incite or provoke.

examples.text: Rivals goaded the young senator into making a speech he would later regret.

senses.en: a pointed instrument that is used to prod into a state of motion

examples.text: The drover used a sharpened goad to keep the oxen moving along the muddy road.

origin.ko: 고대영어 gād '찌르는 막대'에서 왔습니다. 소를 막대로 찔러 몰듯 사람을 몰아붙입니다.

senses.en: A collection containing a variety of miscellaneous things.

examples.text: His latest sculpture is a hodgepodge of kitchen clutter and scrap glued together.

origin.ko: 중세 네덜란드어 hutspot '고기를 잘게 썰어 한 솥에 끓인 요리'에서 왔습니다. 여러 재료를 섞은 솥이 '뒤죽박죽'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: tediously repetitious or lacking in variety

examples.text: After years of a humdrum office routine, she longed for a career with real variety.

origin.ko: 소리를 흉내 낸 말로, hum(웅얼거림)을 겹친 것으로 봅니다. 같은 소리가 계속되는 단조로움입니다.

senses.en: impervious to pleas, persuasion, requests, reason

examples.text: The inexorable negotiator ignored every plea for a compromise and held to his original terms.

senses.en: Impossible to prevent or stop; inevitable.
