examples.text: The inexorable advance of the glacier eventually buried the village under a wall of ice.

origin.ko: 라틴어 inexōrābilis에서 왔고 ōs(입)가 뿌리입니다. 간청해서 마음을 움직일 수 없다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: Difficult or impossible to comprehend, fathom, or interpret.

examples.text: The judge's inscrutable expression gave no hint of how she would rule on the motion.

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 īnscrūtābilis '살펴볼 수 없는'에서 왔습니다. 샅샅이 조사해도 알 수 없다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: Extravagantly or excessively sentimental; mawkish, self-pitying.

examples.text: The film slides into maudlin melodrama in its final act, lingering on every tearful farewell.

origin.ko: 중세 영어 Maudelen, 곧 마리아 막달레나의 방언형에서 왔습니다. 눈물짓는 모습으로 그려지던 데서 눈물 많은 감상이 되었습니다.

senses.en: suitable for or like a palace

examples.text: palatial furnishings

origin.ko: 라틴어 palātium '궁전'에서 왔고, 로마 팔라티누스 언덕에 황제의 궁전이 있었습니다.

senses.en: abnormally deficient in color as suggesting physical or emotional distress

examples.text: the pallid face of the invalid

senses.en: lacking in vitality or interest or effectiveness

examples.text: The sequel was a pallid imitation of the original film.

origin.ko: 라틴어 pallidus '창백한'에서 왔으며 pale과 같은 뿌리입니다.

senses.en: an insufficient quantity or number

examples.text: The study was criticized for the paucity of data supporting its conclusions.

origin.ko: 라틴어 paucitās '소수, 부족'에서 왔고, paucus는 '적은'입니다.

senses.en: spread or diffuse through

examples.text: An atmosphere of distrust has permeated this administration

senses.en: pass through

examples.text: Water permeates sand easily

origin.ko: 라틴어 permeō '통과하다'에서 왔습니다. 속속들이 지나가며 스며든다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: state of uncertainty or perplexity especially as requiring a choice between equally unfavorable options

examples.text: The mayor faced a quandary: raising taxes would anger voters, but cutting services would anger them more.

senses.en: being quiet or still or inactive

examples.text: The volcano had been quiescent for centuries before the sudden eruption.

origin.ko: 라틴어 quiēscēns('쉬고 있는')에서 왔습니다. 움직임 없이 조용히 쉬는 상태입니다.

senses.en: having excessive asymmetrical ornamentation

examples.text: The novelist's rococo prose, crowded with ornate clauses, wearied even her admirers.

senses.en: fanciful but graceful asymmetric ornamentation in art and architecture that originated in France in the 18th century

examples.text: They built a rococo aedicule that stands around the Tomb today.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 rococo를 빌려온 말로, 18세기의 화려한 장식 양식을 가리킵니다.

senses.en: excessively or hypocritically pious

examples.text: The sanctimonious columnist lectured readers on morality while quietly ignoring the rules himself.

origin.ko: 라틴어 sanctus(거룩한)에서 나온 말입니다. 거룩한 척하는 위선을 뜻합니다.

senses.en: disdainfully or ironically humorous; scornful and mocking

examples.text: He distances himself from people with his nasty, sardonic laughter.

origin.ko: 그리스어 sardonios에서 왔습니다. 사르데냐 식물을 먹으면 얼굴이 일그러져 비웃는 듯하다는 설이 있습니다.

senses.en: brilliantly clever

examples.text: a play full of scintillating dialogue

senses.en: having brief brilliant points or flashes of light

examples.text: On the scintillating water yellow and blue boats bobbed up and down.

origin.ko: 라틴어 scintilla(불꽃)에서 나온 scintillate의 현재분사입니다. 불꽃이 튀듯 재치가 반짝인다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: unpredictably excitable (especially of horses)

examples.text: The dog likes people he knows, but he is skittish around strangers.

origin.ko: '재빨리 움직이다'라는 뜻의 skite에 -ish가 붙은 것으로 봅니다. 갑자기 튀는 겁 많은 말의 모습입니다.

senses.en: Reckless boldness; foolish bravery.

examples.text: One day when he knew old Lobbs was out, Nathaniel Pipkin had the temerity to kiss his hand to Maria Lobbs.

senses.en: Effrontery; impudence.

examples.text: The intern had the temerity to correct the chief executive in front of the entire board.

origin.ko: 라틴어 temeritās(우연, 무모함)에서 왔고 temere(되는대로, 경솔히)와 이어집니다. 앞뒤 안 재는 무모한 용기입니다.

senses.en: inactivity resulting from lethargy and lack of vigor or energy

examples.text: A summer torpor settled over the town, and nobody seemed willing to start any work before evening.

senses.en: A state similar to hibernation characterised by energy-conserving, very deep sleep.

examples.text: Hummingbirds enter torpor on cold nights to conserve energy when food is scarce.

origin.ko: 라틴어 torpor('마비, 무감각')에서 왔습니다. 몸이 굳어 둔해진 상태가 '무기력'입니다.

senses.en: marked by repeated turns and bends

examples.text: A tortuous road climbed the mountain, doubling back on itself every few hundred meters.

senses.en: highly complex or intricate and occasionally devious

examples.text: The lawyer's tortuous reasoning left the jury unsure what she was actually asking them to conclude.

origin.ko: 라틴어 tortuōsus('꼬불꼬불한')에서 왔고 tortus('비틂')와 이어집니다. 비틀려 굽이진 길의 이미지입니다.

senses.en: using or containing too many words

examples.text: The report was so verbose that its single useful recommendation was buried on page forty.

origin.ko: 라틴어 verbōsus에서 왔고 verbum('말')에 '가득한' 뜻의 접미사가 붙었습니다. 말로 가득하다는 뜻이 '장황한'입니다.

senses.en: chronologically misplaced

examples.text: Critics called the dress code anachronistic, a leftover from an era when offices were all-male.

origin.ko: anachronism에서 파생된 말로, 그리스어 '시간을 잘못 잡음'에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: official approval

examples.text: The new curriculum went into effect only after receiving the board's formal approbation.

senses.en: The act of approving; an assenting to the propriety of a thing with some degree of pleasure or satisfaction; approval, sanction, commendation or official recognition.

examples.text: The young painter craved the approbation of the critics more than any prize.

origin.ko: 라틴어 approbatio에서 왔고 approbare(좋다고 인정하다)에서 나왔습니다. 공식적으로 승인하는 것입니다.

senses.en: attribute or credit to

examples.text: It is arguable as to whether we can truly ascribe this play to Shakespeare.

origin.ko: 라틴어 ascribere(~에 써넣다)에서 왔습니다. 이름이나 원인을 적어 넣어 '~의 탓으로 돌리다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: make stronger or defensible

examples.text: New archival evidence buttressed her argument that the treaty had been signed under pressure.

senses.en: a support usually of stone or brick; supports the wall of a building

examples.text: Stone buttresses along the sides of the cathedral keep its tall walls from bowing outward.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 'ars bouterez'(떠받치는 아치)에서 왔고, 어원은 '밀다'를 뜻하는 프랑크어입니다. 건물을 받치는 버팀벽입니다.

senses.en: occurring with or following as a consequence

examples.text: Rapid urban growth brings concomitant problems of congestion and pollution.

origin.ko: 라틴어 concomitor('함께 동행하다')에서 왔고, comes(동반자)가 뿌리입니다. 곁에 붙어 같이 따라오는 것입니다.

senses.en: make clear and (more) comprehensible

examples.text: The footnotes elucidate several obscure references in the poet's late work.

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 ēlūcidāre(밝게 하다)에서 왔습니다. 어둠에 빛을 비추듯 '명료하게 설명하다'입니다.

senses.en: artificial and inferior

examples.text: ersatz coffee

origin.ko: 독일어 Ersatz(대체품)를 그대로 빌려 왔습니다. ersetzen(대신하다)에서 나온 말로, 진짜를 대신하는 질 낮은 모조품을 가리킵니다.

senses.en: having or showing profound knowledge

examples.text: The professor gave an erudite lecture that impressed everyone in the audience.

origin.ko: 라틴어 ērudīre(거친 상태에서 벗어나게 가르치다)에서 왔습니다. 미숙함을 벗어난 '박식한' 사람입니다.

senses.en: choose and follow; as of theories, ideas, policies, strategies or plans

examples.text: The candidate espouses Republican ideals

senses.en: To marry.

examples.text: The prince espoused a foreign duchess to seal the alliance between the two kingdoms.

origin.ko: 라틴어 spōnsāre(약혼하다, 맹세하다)에서 고대 프랑스어를 거쳐 왔습니다. 배우자를 맞듯 사상을 받아들인다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: A critical explanation or interpretation of a text, especially a religious text.

examples.text: Her doctoral thesis offered a detailed exegesis of the book of Job.

origin.ko: 그리스어 exḗgēsis(설명, 해석)에서 왔습니다. 글의 뜻을 밖으로 이끌어 내는 일입니다.

senses.en: To infer by extending known information.

examples.text: Economists extrapolated from last year's figures to predict that growth would slow considerably.

senses.en: To estimate the value of a variable outside a known range from values within that range by assuming that the estimated value follows logically from the known ones

examples.text: The researchers extrapolated the trend line beyond the measured data to estimate future temperatures.

origin.ko: 라틴어 extrā(바깥에)와 interpolate의 -polate를 합쳐 만든 말입니다. 아는 범위 밖까지 미루어 추정한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: Frenzied and frantic, harried; having extreme enthusiasm or energy.

examples.text: After a week of working at a frenetic pace, she was ready for Saturday.

origin.ko: 그리스어 phrēn(마음)에서 온 phrenitis(정신착란)에서 왔습니다. 정신이 나간 듯 날뛰는 모습이 '광란의'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: relevant and appropriate

examples.text: The judge ruled that the defendant's past employment was not germane to the case.

origin.ko: german '같은 부모에게서 난, 혈연의'의 변형입니다. 햄릿의 용례에서 '관련 있는'이라는 뜻으로 쓰였습니다.

senses.en: Excessively dramatic or emotional, especially with the intention to draw attention.

examples.text: Her histrionic outburst over the minor delay embarrassed everyone at the table.

senses.en: characteristic of acting or a stage performance; often affected

examples.text: The old actor's histrionic gestures looked out of place in the intimate, naturalistic film.

origin.ko: 라틴어 histriōnicus '배우의, 연극의'에서 왔고 histriō(배우)가 뿌리입니다. 배우처럼 과장되게 감정을 드러내는 모습입니다.

senses.en: (used of conduct or character) deserving or bringing disgrace or shame

examples.text: The team suffered an ignominious defeat, losing by forty points to a squad of amateurs.

origin.ko: 라틴어 ignōminiōsus '수치스러운'에서 왔습니다. 이름(nōmen)과 명예를 잃었다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: Domineering, arrogant, or overbearing.

examples.text: The imperious director barked orders at his staff and never listened to their objections.

origin.ko: 라틴어 imperiōsus '강력한'에서 왔고 imperium(명령, 권력)이 뿌리입니다. 명령하는 태도가 '고압적인'입니다.

senses.en: lacking in harmony or compatibility or appropriateness

examples.text: The glass tower looked incongruous beside the centuries-old stone cottages of the village.

origin.ko: 라틴어 incongruus에서 왔습니다. congruus(함께 맞는)에 부정 접두사가 붙어 어울리지 않는다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: teach and impress by frequent repetitions or admonitions

examples.text: inculcate values into the young generation

origin.ko: 라틴어 inculcō '밟아 넣다, 강요하다'에서 왔고 calx(발뒤꿈치)가 뿌리입니다. 발로 꾹꾹 밟아 다지듯 되풀이해 새겨 넣는다는 이미지입니다.

senses.en: disinclined to work or exertion

examples.text: The indolent girl resisted doing her homework.

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 indolēns '아프지 않은'에서 왔습니다. 고통을 느끼지 않으니 애써 일하지 않는 나태함이 되었습니다.

senses.en: worthy of high praise

examples.text: Though the goal of cutting waste is laudable, the proposed method would harm essential services.

origin.ko: 라틴어 laudabilis에서 왔습니다. laud(칭찬하다)에 -able이 붙어 칭찬할 만하다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: A modest, small, or trifling amount.

examples.text: Unable to garner even a modicum of support for his plan, he conceded to follow the others.

origin.ko: 라틴어 modicum '조금'에서 왔고 modus(척도, 한도)에서 나왔습니다. 한도 안의 적은 양입니다.

senses.en: Having or showing a sharp or critical quality.

examples.text: The critic's mordant wit left few of the season's plays unscathed.

origin.ko: 라틴어 mordeō '물다'에서 왔습니다. 물어뜯는 듯 날카로운 말투가 신랄함이 되었습니다.

senses.en: A beginner; a person who is new to a subject, skill, or belief.

examples.text: The neophyte lawyer was nervous about cross-examining such an experienced witness.

origin.ko: 그리스어 neóphutos '새로 심은'에서 왔습니다. 갓 심은 어린 식물처럼 새로 입문한 초보자를 가리킵니다.

senses.en: intended to attract notice and impress others

examples.text: His ostentatious display of wealth, from the gold watch to the chauffeured car, alienated his colleagues.

origin.ko: 라틴어 ostentātus '내보이기'에서 왔습니다. 남의 눈앞에 자꾸 내미는 과시하는 태도입니다.

senses.en: To mollify, placate or soothe (someone or something).

examples.text: The manager offered a full refund to pacify the furious customer.

senses.en: fight violence and try to establish peace in (a location)

examples.text: The U.N. troops are working to pacify Bosnia

origin.ko: 중세 프랑스어 pacifier에서 왔고, 라틴어로 '평화(pāx)를 만들다'입니다.

senses.en: To treat condescendingly; to talk down to.

examples.text: Please don't patronize me; I understand the contract perfectly well.

senses.en: To act as a patron of; to defend, protect, or support.

examples.text: Wealthy merchants patronized the young painter and funded his studies in Rome.

senses.en: To be a customer of (an establishment), especially a regular customer.

examples.text: Locals still patronize the old bakery on the corner every morning.

origin.ko: patron(후원자)에 -ize가 붙은 말입니다. 후원자인 양 아랫사람 대하듯 한다는 데서 깔보는 뜻이 되었습니다.

senses.en: Disparaging, belittling or derogatory.

examples.text: Critics used the term in a pejorative sense to dismiss the whole movement.

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 peiōrāre '악화시키다'에서 왔고, peior는 '더 나쁜'입니다. 가치를 깎아내리는 말입니다.

senses.en: Constantly travelling.

examples.text: The peripatetic conductor spent most of the year touring orchestras on three continents.

origin.ko: 그리스어 peripatētikós '이리저리 걷기 좋아하는'에서 왔습니다. 두루 걸어 다닌다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: abundant or generous to the point of excess; copious; volubly expressed.

examples.text: The host offered profuse apologies for the delay and a second round of drinks.

origin.ko: 라틴어 profusus('쏟아져 나온')에서 왔습니다. 앞으로 콸콸 쏟아지듯 풍부하다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: To increase in number or spread rapidly; to multiply.

examples.text: The flowers proliferated rapidly all spring.

origin.ko: proliferation에서 거꾸로 만든 말로, 라틴어 proles('자손')와 ferre('낳다')에서 왔습니다. 자손이 불어나듯 급증합니다.

senses.en: lasting a very short time

examples.text: The poet mourned the transitory nature of beauty, which fades almost as soon as it is noticed.

origin.ko: 라틴어 trānsitōrius('지나가는')에서 왔습니다. 잠깐 지나가 버리는 '덧없는' 것입니다.

senses.en: to bring or combine together or with something else

examples.text: The two rival banks agreed to amalgamate in order to compete with larger international firms.

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 amalgamare(수은과 합금하다)에서 왔습니다. 서로 섞어 하나로 융합한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: marked by care and persistent effort

examples.text: her assiduous attempts to learn French

origin.ko: 라틴어 assiduus(곁에 붙어 앉아 있는)에서 왔습니다. 자리를 뜨지 않고 꾸준히 일하는 모습입니다.

senses.en: To persuade someone to do something which they are reluctant to do, especially by flattery or promises; to coax.

examples.text: She cajoled her reluctant brother into lending her the car by promising to pay for gas.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 cajoler에서 왔고, 어치(새)처럼 재잘대다와 새장으로 꾀어 들이다가 섞인 말로 봅니다. 달콤한 말로 새장에 꾀는 이미지입니다.

senses.en: the use of tricks to deceive someone (usually to extract money from them)

examples.text: The contractor won the bid through legal chicanery rather than the merit of his proposal.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 chicanerie('속임수')에서 왔고 chicaner(트집 잡다)에서 갈라졌습니다.

senses.en: rude and boorish

examples.text: It seemed churlish to refuse the invitation after the family had gone to such trouble.

senses.en: Stingy or grudging.

examples.text: The firm's churlish offer of severance angered the longtime employees.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 ċeorlisċ에서 왔고, churl(평민, 상것)에 -ish가 붙었습니다. 천한 사람처럼 무례하다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: corresponding in size or degree or extent

examples.text: The rewards will be commensurate with the efforts made.

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 commēnsūrātus에서 왔고, com-(함께)과 mēnsūrō(재다)가 합쳐졌습니다. 같은 척도로 재서 맞는다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: A gradual increase of anything, especially to a dramatic climax.

examples.text: Their fighting rose in a fearsome crescendo.

senses.en: grow louder

examples.text: The protests crescendoed through the summer until the government finally agreed to negotiate.

origin.ko: 이탈리아어 crescere(자라다, 커지다)의 현재분사에서 왔습니다. 소리가 점점 커지는 음악 용어였습니다.

senses.en: deserving of esteem and respect

examples.text: The estimable judge was widely respected for her fairness and integrity.

senses.en: may be computed or estimated
senses.ko: 추정할 수 있는, 어림잡을 수 있는

examples.text: The risk of failure is estimable from the historical data.

origin.ko: 라틴어 aestimābilis(값을 매길 수 있는)에서 왔습니다. 높이 평가할 만한 '훌륭한'이라는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: Urgent; pressing; needing immediate action.

examples.text: Doctors had to act quickly because of the exigent circumstances surrounding the patient's collapse.

senses.en: Demanding; requiring great effort.

examples.text: The exigent standards of the guild forced apprentices to practice for years before earning recognition.

origin.ko: 라틴어 exigere(요구하다)의 현재분사에서 왔습니다. 즉각적 행동을 요구하는 '긴급한'입니다.

senses.en: not pertinent to the matter under consideration

examples.text: The editor deleted several extraneous details that distracted readers from the central argument.

senses.en: Not essential or intrinsic.

examples.text: The architect stripped away every extraneous ornament, leaving a clean and functional facade.

origin.ko: 라틴어 extrāneus(바깥에서 온)에서 왔습니다. 문제 바깥에 있어 관련이 없다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: extremely silly or stupid

examples.text: The candidate's fatuous remark about the economy was quoted mockingly in newspapers for weeks.

origin.ko: 라틴어 fatuus(어리석은, 멍청한)를 그대로 가져왔습니다.

senses.en: completely lacking nobility in character or quality or purpose

examples.text: Historians condemned the general's ignoble decision to abandon his wounded troops.

senses.en: not of the nobility

examples.text: Though of ignoble birth, he rose through talent alone to become the king's chief minister.

origin.ko: 라틴어 ignōbilis '고귀하지 않은'에서 왔습니다. in-(아닌)과 nōbilis(고귀한)가 합쳐졌습니다.

senses.en: not disposed or willing to believe; unbelieving

examples.text: The jury listened with incredulous expressions as the defendant described his improbable alibi.

origin.ko: 라틴어 incrēdulus '믿지 않는'에서 왔습니다. 믿지(cred) 않는다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: Excessive patriotism or aggressive nationalism, especially with regards to foreign policy.

examples.text: Soviet reports today on the British victory in the Falkland Islands said a “new flare-up of jingoism” in Britain obscured the fact that the problem was far from solved.

senses.en: Humorous, amusing or joking.

examples.text: He was in a jocular mood all day.

origin.ko: 라틴어 iocularis에서 왔고 ioculus(작은 농담)와 iocus(농담)에서 나왔습니다.

senses.en: To place side by side, especially for contrast or comparison.

examples.text: The documentary effectively juxtaposes the lives of two rival politicians.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 juxtaposer에서 왔고 라틴어 iuxtā '가까이'와 pōnō '놓다'가 합쳐졌습니다. 바로 옆에 놓는다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: deficient in alertness or activity

examples.text: bullfrogs became lethargic with the first cold nights

origin.ko: 그리스어 lēthargikós에서 왔고 lḗthē(망각)와 argós(일하지 않는)가 합쳐졌습니다. 멍하니 잊은 듯 늘어진 상태입니다.

senses.en: One who has behaved badly, or illegally.

examples.text: The teacher sent the miscreants to see the school principal.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 mescreant '잘못 믿는 사람'에서 왔습니다. 이단자에서 악당으로 뜻이 변했습니다.

senses.en: A solution to all problems.

examples.text: A monorail will be a panacea for our traffic woes.

origin.ko: 그리스어 panákeia '모든 것을 고치는'에서 왔습니다. 모든 병과 문제를 해결하는 만병통치약입니다.

senses.en: a person who is rejected (from society or home)

examples.text: After the scandal, the once-admired banker became a social pariah.

origin.ko: 타밀어 paṟaiyar에서 왔고, 원래 북(paṟai)을 치던 낮은 신분의 사람들을 가리켰습니다. 여기서 사회에서 배척당하는 사람이 되었습니다.

senses.en: take as a given; assume as a postulate or axiom

examples.text: He posited three basic laws of nature

senses.en: To propose for consideration or study; to suggest.

examples.text: The researchers posit that sleep strengthens memory by replaying recent experience.

origin.ko: 라틴어 pōnō('놓다')의 과거분사 positus에서 왔습니다. 논의의 바탕에 어떤 전제를 놓는다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: To speak incessantly and in an inconsequential or childish manner; to babble.

examples.text: The guests prattled on about the weather while the real issues went undiscussed.

senses.en: idle or foolish and irrelevant talk

examples.text: The candidate dismissed her opponent's speech as empty prattle devoid of any real policy.

origin.ko: prate('수다 떨다')에 반복을 나타내는 -le가 붙은 말입니다. 쉴 새 없이 재잘거리는 모습입니다.

senses.en: found in the ordinary course of events

examples.text: The poet finds beauty in quotidian details like laundry, traffic, and morning coffee.

senses.en: Happening every day; daily.

examples.text: Her quotidian routine began with a long walk before sunrise.

origin.ko: 라틴어 quōtīdiānus('매일 일어나는')에서 왔습니다. '매일'이라는 뜻에서 '일상적인, 평범한'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: a quick reply to a question or remark (especially a witty or critical one)

examples.text: it brought a sharp rejoinder from the teacher

origin.ko: 프랑스어 rejoindre('다시 잇다')의 부정사를 명사로 쓴 말입니다. 상대 말에 되받아 이어 응답하는 것입니다.

senses.en: A person with low morals or principles.

examples.text: The village gossips called him a drunken reprobate who had squandered his family's fortune.

senses.en: deviating from what is considered moral or right or proper or good

examples.text: The preacher denounced the reprobate city and warned its citizens to mend their ways.

senses.en: express strong disapproval of

examples.text: Church leaders reprobated the spread of gambling dens near the harbor in a sharply worded letter.

origin.ko: 라틴어 reprobātus('인정받지 못한')에서 왔습니다. 시험에서 불합격해 버림받은 타락한 사람입니다.

senses.en: someone who spends money prodigally

examples.text: The heir proved a spendthrift and had exhausted the family fortune within a decade.

senses.en: recklessly wasteful

examples.text: Critics condemned the spendthrift government for ignoring the growing deficit.

origin.ko: spend(쓰다)와 thrift(저축, 재산)가 합쳐진 말입니다. 모은 재산을 써 버리는 사람입니다.

senses.en: hinder or prevent the progress or accomplishment of

examples.text: Legal disputes over ownership continued to stymie the redevelopment of the old harbor.

origin.ko: 골프에서 공이 홀로 가는 길을 막는 상황을 가리킨 말입니다. 스코틀랜드어 어원설이 있으나 확실하지 않습니다.

senses.en: Capable of being easily led, taught, or managed.

examples.text: The tractable young horse learned the commands within a week and rarely resisted its rider.

senses.en: Capable of being shaped; malleable.

examples.text: Soft copper is a tractable metal, easily drawn into wire or hammered into sheets.

origin.ko: 라틴어 tractābilis('다룰 수 있는')에서 왔습니다. 손으로 끌어 다룰 수 있어서 '다루기 쉬운'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: greatly exceeding bounds of reason or moderation

examples.text: The effective rate of interest was unconscionable, but not legally usurious.

senses.en: Not conscionable; unscrupulous and lacking principles or conscience.

examples.text: Critics called it unconscionable that the firm knowingly sold the defective product for years.

senses.en: the appearance of truth; the quality of seeming to be true

examples.text: The novelist added period slang and precise street names to lend her story verisimilitude.

origin.ko: 라틴어 vērī similitūdō('진실과의 닮음')에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: marked by skill in deception

examples.text: The wily negotiator extracted concessions from his rivals without ever raising his voice.

origin.ko: wile('꾀')에 -y를 붙인 말입니다. 꾀가 많아 '교활한'입니다.

senses.en: difficult to penetrate; incomprehensible to one of ordinary understanding or knowledge

examples.text: The physicist's abstruse argument left most of the audience nodding politely while understanding very little.

origin.ko: 라틴어 abstrusus(감춰진)에서 왔습니다. 깊숙이 밀어 넣어 숨긴 것이라 이해하기 어렵습니다.

senses.en: shrewdness shown by keen insight

examples.text: Her political acumen allowed her to anticipate the opposition's strategy months before it was announced.

origin.ko: 라틴어 acumen(날카로운 끝)에서 왔습니다. 바늘 끝처럼 날카로운 판단력을 뜻합니다.

senses.en: having no definite form or distinct shape

examples.text: Through the fog, the ship appeared as an amorphous gray mass on the horizon.

senses.en: Lacking organization or unity.

examples.text: The amorphous movement had no clear leader, no budget, and no agreed set of goals.

origin.ko: 그리스어 amorphos(형태 없는)에서 왔습니다. 모양이 갖춰지지 않은 상태입니다.

senses.en: deviating from the general or common order or type

examples.text: The anomalous results puzzled the team, since they contradicted every previous experiment.

origin.ko: 그리스어 anōmalos(고르지 않은)에서 왔습니다. 일반적인 질서에서 벗어난 상태입니다.

senses.en: Awe-inspiring, majestic, noble, venerable.

examples.text: an august patron of the arts

origin.ko: 라틴어 augustus(위엄 있는)에서 왔고 augere(늘리다)에서 나왔습니다. 로마 황제 칭호 Augustus와도 이어집니다.

senses.en: strong feelings of embarrassment

examples.text: To her chagrin, the error in her calculations was found by a first-year student.

senses.en: cause to feel shame; hurt the pride of

examples.text: The public rebuke chagrined the young director, who had expected nothing but praise for her film.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 chagrin('슬픔, 고통')에서 왔고 더 이전 기원은 불확실합니다.

senses.en: To lower in character, quality, or value; to degrade.

examples.text: Critics argued that constant sensationalism had debased the quality of public debate on television.

senses.en: To lower the value of (a currency) by reducing the amount of valuable metal in the coins.
senses.ko: (화폐의) 품위를 낮추다, 질 낮은 금속을 섞다

examples.text: Roman emperors repeatedly debased the silver denarius to pay for their costly military campaigns.

origin.ko: de-와 base(낮은)를 합친 말입니다. 질을 낮은 쪽으로 끌어내린다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: marked by lack of definite plan or regularity or purpose; jumping from one thing to another

examples.text: the desultory conversation characteristic of cocktail parties

origin.ko: 라틴어 dēsultor(달리는 말에서 다른 말로 뛰어 옮겨 타는 곡마사)에서 왔습니다. 이리저리 옮겨 다니니 '두서없는'입니다.

senses.en: Having no interest or stake in the outcome, and no conflicts of interest; free of bias, impartial.

examples.text: A disinterested mediator with no stake in the dispute is needed to settle the contract.

senses.en: Synonym of uninterested (“not interested; not concerned; indifferent”).

examples.text: Robin took to wandering again, to intermittent travel from which she came back hours, days later, disinterested.

origin.ko: dis-와 interested를 합친 말이거나 disinterest의 과거분사로 봅니다. 이해관계가 없다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: an inoffensive or indirect expression that is substituted for one that is considered offensive or too harsh

examples.text: "Passed away" is a common euphemism for "died" in polite conversation.

origin.ko: 그리스어 euphēmía(불길한 말을 피하고 좋은 말만 하기)에서 왔습니다. 거북한 말을 부드럽게 돌려 말하는 것입니다.

senses.en: severe and unremitting in making demands

examples.text: The conductor was an exacting taskmaster who made the orchestra repeat each passage dozens of times.

senses.en: requiring precise accuracy

examples.text: Restoring the fresco was an exacting task that demanded years of patient, precise work.

senses.en: Very unlucky; ill-fated.

examples.text: The hapless traveler arrived at the station just as the last train pulled away.

origin.ko: 옛말 hap(운)에 -less(없는)가 붙은 말입니다. 운이 없으니 '불운한'입니다.

senses.en: Unaffected or unable to be affected by something.

examples.text: The man was completely impervious to the deception we were trying.

senses.en: Preventive of any penetration; impenetrable, impermeable, particularly of water.

examples.text: Although patchworked and sagging, the roof proved impervious to the weather.

origin.ko: 라틴어 impervius '통과할 수 없는'에서 왔습니다. 길(via)이 통하지 않으니 영향이 스며들지 않는다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: angered at something unjust or wrong

examples.text: Indignant residents packed the town hall to protest the unfair closure of their school.

origin.ko: 라틴어 indignor '부당하다고 여기다'에서 왔고 dignus(합당한)가 뿌리입니다. 부당하다고 느끼니 분개하는 것입니다.

senses.en: A strict disciplinarian.

examples.text: The new principal proved a martinet who punished students for the smallest breach of the dress code.

origin.ko: 17세기 프랑스 군 장교 장 마르티네의 이름에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: The fact or condition of being untruthful; dishonesty.

examples.text: Critics condemned the mendacity of a campaign built on invented statistics.

senses.en: A deceit, falsehood, or lie.

examples.text: The memoir was riddled with small mendacities meant to flatter its author.

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 mendacitas에서 왔고 라틴어 mendāx '거짓말하는'에서 나왔습니다.

senses.en: not easily borne; wearing

examples.text: Small businesses complained that the new reporting requirements were onerous and costly to meet.

origin.ko: 라틴어 onerosus에서 왔고, onus는 '짐'입니다. 어깨에 얹힌 짐처럼 힘겹다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: Disgrace or bad reputation arising from exceedingly shameful behaviour; ignominy.

examples.text: The company faced public opprobrium after the memo revealing the cover-up was leaked.

senses.en: Scornful contempt or reproach; (countable) an instance of this.

examples.text: The senator's remarks drew widespread opprobrium from members of both parties.

origin.ko: 라틴어 opprobrium '비난, 치욕'에서 왔습니다. 상대 얼굴 앞에 치욕을 들이대는 모습입니다.

senses.en: tending to betray; especially having a treacherous character as attributed to the Carthaginians by the Romans

examples.text: The king, betrayed by his perfidious advisors, lost both his throne and his army.

origin.ko: 라틴어 perfidia '배신'에서 왔고, fidēs는 '믿음'입니다. 믿음을 저버리는 성향입니다.

senses.en: Characterized by exceptionally early development or maturity.

examples.text: The precocious child began reading the newspaper at age four.

origin.ko: 라틴어 praecox('일찍 익은')에서 왔습니다. 과일이 제철보다 먼저 익듯 일찍 성숙한 아이를 뜻합니다.

senses.en: Making unwarranted presumptions or assumptions, often out of arrogance or excessive self-confidence, and thus exceeding appropriate or rightful limits.

examples.text: It would be presumptuous of me to advise someone with so much more experience.

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 praesūmptuōsus에서 왔습니다. 자격도 없이 앞질러 취하려 드는 '주제넘은' 태도입니다.

senses.en: so great in size or force or extent as to elicit awe

examples.text: The young pianist displayed a prodigious memory, performing entire concertos without a score.

senses.en: of momentous or ominous significance

examples.text: a prodigious vision

origin.ko: 라틴어 prōdigium('전조, 경이로운 일')에서 왔습니다. 불가사의할 만큼 엄청나다는 뜻이 되었습니다.

senses.en: a person skilled in telling anecdotes

examples.text: The retired diplomat was a gifted raconteur who held dinner guests spellbound with tales of his postings abroad.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 raconteur('이야기하는 사람')를 그대로 빌려 왔습니다.

senses.en: stubbornly resistant to authority or control

examples.text: The refractory mule balked at every command and would not pull the cart up the hill.

senses.en: not responding to treatment

examples.text: Doctors tried three antibiotics before concluding the infection was refractory to standard treatment.

origin.ko: 라틴어 refractārius('고집 센')에서 왔고 refringere('부수다')와 이어집니다. 꺾이지 않고 버티는 고집입니다.

senses.en: (followed by ‘with’) deeply filled or permeated

examples.text: The memoir is replete with vivid details of life in a wartime village.

senses.en: filled to satisfaction with food or drink

examples.text: After the holiday feast, the guests lay replete and drowsy on the sofas.

origin.ko: 라틴어 repletus('가득 채워진')에서 왔습니다. 속이 꽉 찬 상태입니다.

senses.en: cancel officially

examples.text: The university rescinded its offer after discovering that the applicant had falsified her credentials.

origin.ko: 라틴어 rescindere('잘라 내다')에서 왔습니다. 이미 있는 것을 뒤로 잘라 없애 철회한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: humorously vulgar

examples.text: The comedian's ribald jokes delighted the late-night crowd but scandalized the more conservative members of the audience.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 ribaud(불량배, 건달)에서 왔습니다. 건달의 상스러운 농담이라는 이미지입니다.

senses.en: promoting health; healthful

examples.text: The doctor recommended the salubrious mountain air as a cure for the patient's chronic cough.

origin.ko: 라틴어 salūbris(건강한)에 -ous가 붙었습니다. 건강에 좋다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: showing hovering attentiveness

examples.text: solicitous about her health

senses.en: full of anxiety and concern

examples.text: solicitous parents

origin.ko: 라틴어 sollicitus(마음이 온통 흔들린)에서 왔습니다. 걱정하며 챙기는 마음입니다.

senses.en: wear off or die down

examples.text: The pain subsided

senses.en: sink to a lower level or form a depression

examples.text: the valleys subside

origin.ko: 라틴어 subsīdere(아래로 앉다)에서 왔습니다. 가라앉아 잦아든다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: implied by or inferred from actions or statements

examples.text: tacit consent

origin.ko: 라틴어 tacitus(말없이 넘어간)에서 왔고 tacere(침묵하다)와 이어집니다. 말하지 않아도 통하는 암묵적인 뜻입니다.

senses.en: A long, angry or violent speech.

examples.text: The coach launched into a tirade about the team's carelessness that lasted until the buses departed.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 tirade('긴 독백, 장광설')를 그대로 빌려 왔습니다.

senses.en: The quality of speaking or stating the truth; truthfulness.

examples.text: Of course if you don't accept Conway's story, it means that you doubt either his veracity or his sanity—one may as well be frank.

senses.en: Agreement with the facts; accordance with the truth; accuracy or precision.

examples.text: Fact-checkers spent days confirming the veracity of the leaked documents before publication.

origin.ko: 라틴어 vērāx('진실한')에서 온 중세 라틴어 vērācitās에서 왔습니다. 진실을 말하는 성질입니다.

senses.en: having a relatively high resistance to flow

examples.text: Cold temperatures made the motor oil so viscous that the engine struggled to start.

origin.ko: 라틴어 viscum('새 잡는 끈끈이')에서 나온 viscōsus에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: lean and wrinkled by shrinkage as from age or illness

examples.text: A wizened old fisherman sat mending his nets on the dock, his face creased by decades of sun.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 wisnian('시들다')에서 나온 wizen의 과거분사형입니다. 말라 쪼그라든 모습입니다.

senses.en: Simultaneously experiencing or expressing opposing or contradictory feelings, beliefs, motivations, or meanings.

examples.text: She felt ambivalent about the promotion, which promised higher pay but demanded constant travel.

origin.ko: 독일어 Ambivalenz에서 온 말입니다. 두 방향으로 동시에 강한 감정이 작용한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: requiring secret or mysterious knowledge

examples.text: The tax code is so arcane that even seasoned accountants disagree about its provisions.

origin.ko: 라틴어 arcanus(숨겨진)에서 왔고 '상자에 가둬 두다'와 연결됩니다. 닫혀 있어 비밀스럽다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: simple and natural; without cunning or deceit

examples.text: an artless manner

senses.en: showing lack of art

examples.text: an artless translation

origin.ko: art(기교)에 -less(없는)가 붙은 말입니다. 꾸밈이나 잔재주가 없어 순박하다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: immoderately desirous of acquiring e.g. wealth

examples.text: they are avaricious and will do anything for money

origin.ko: 라틴어 avaritia(탐욕)에서 왔고 avere(갈망하다)에서 나왔습니다.

senses.en: (logic) a proposition that is not susceptible of proof or disproof; its truth is assumed to be self-evident

examples.text: The theorem follows directly from three axioms that the authors take to be self-evident.

senses.en: a saying that is widely accepted on its own merits

examples.text: Any publicity, runs the axiom, is good publicity.

origin.ko: 그리스어 axioma(마땅하다고 여겨진 것)에서 왔고 axios(합당한)에서 나왔습니다. 증명 없이 인정되는 원리입니다.

senses.en: harsh or corrosive in tone

examples.text: The critic's caustic review dismissed the play as a tedious exercise in self-indulgence.

senses.en: of a substance, especially a strong acid; capable of destroying or eating away by chemical action

examples.text: Workers wore gloves and goggles when handling the caustic cleaning solution.

origin.ko: 라틴어 causticus와 그리스어 kaustikos('타는')에서 왔습니다. 불에 태우듯 부식시키는 날카로운 말투입니다.

senses.en: Great respect.

examples.text: The children treated their elders with deference.

senses.en: a disposition or tendency to yield to the will of others

examples.text: The young associate showed such deference to the partners that she rarely voiced her own opinions.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 déférence에서 왔고 defer(따르다)에 -ence가 붙은 말입니다.

senses.en: To free (someone) of a misconception or misapprehension; to unveil a falsehood held by (someone).

examples.text: If we had any hopes or illusions about the National Party before they came into office, we were disabused of them quickly.

origin.ko: dis-와 abuse를 합친 말로, 프랑스어 désabuser와 비교됩니다. 속은 것을 풀어 준다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: stubbornly insistent on theory without regard for practicality or suitability

examples.text: The minister's doctrinaire insistence on austerity ignored the evidence that the policy was deepening the recession.

senses.en: a stubborn person of arbitrary or arrogant opinions

examples.text: Critics called him a doctrinaire who would never bend his principles to fit the realities of governing.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 doctrinaire에서 왔고 doctrine에 -aire가 붙은 말입니다.

senses.en: To instruct or improve morally or intellectually.

examples.text: The museum aims to edify visitors as well as entertain them.

origin.ko: 라틴어 aedificāre(짓다)에서 왔습니다. 건물을 세우듯 마음과 지식을 쌓아 올려 '교화하다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: To deceive using a disguise; to beguile, dupe, mislead.

examples.text: The con artist hoodwinked investors into believing the company held vast gold reserves.

origin.ko: hood(두건)와 wink(눈 감다)가 합쳐진 말입니다. 두건으로 눈을 가려 놓고 속인다는 이미지입니다.

senses.en: narrowly restricted in outlook or scope

examples.text: The insular community distrusted outsiders and resisted every attempt to modernize its customs.

senses.en: relating to or characteristic of or situated on an island

examples.text: The insular climate of the archipelago keeps temperatures mild throughout the year.

origin.ko: 라틴어 īnsulāris '섬의'에서 왔습니다. 섬처럼 고립되어 시야가 좁다는 뜻이 되었습니다.

senses.en: lacking in insight or discernment

examples.text: too obtuse to grasp the implications of his behavior

senses.en: Blunt; not sharp, pointed, or acute in form.

examples.text: The tool's obtuse tip made it useless for fine carving.

origin.ko: 라틴어 obtūsus '무뎌진, 뭉툭한'에서 왔습니다. 계속 두들겨 날이 무뎌지듯 이해력이 둔하다는 뜻이 되었습니다.

senses.en: A formal speech publicly praising someone or something.

examples.text: The biography reads less like history than a long panegyric to the founder.

senses.en: formally expressing praise

examples.text: The critic's panegyric tone left no room for any real criticism.

origin.ko: 그리스어 panēgyrikos '대중 집회의'에서 왔습니다. 모두가 모인 자리에서 하는 칭송 연설입니다.

senses.en: narrowly restricted in outlook or scope

examples.text: little sympathy with parochial mentality

senses.en: relating to or supported by or located in a parish

examples.text: parochial schools

origin.ko: 그리스어 pároikos '이웃'에서 온 교구라는 말입니다. 한 교구의 좁은 범위에 갇혀 시야가 좁다는 뜻이 되었습니다.

senses.en: the food served and eaten at one time

examples.text: After the long journey, the travelers sat down to a modest but welcome repast.

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 repastus('식사')에서 왔고 repāscere('먹이다')와 이어집니다. 기운을 되찾게 해 주는 한 끼입니다.

senses.en: ostensibly valid, but not actually valid

examples.text: His argument was spurious and had no validity.

senses.en: False, not authentic, not genuine.

examples.text: a spurious work of art

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 spurius(사생아의, 가짜의)에서 왔습니다. 정통이 아닌 가짜라는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: more than is needed, desired, or required

examples.text: With a full rain suit, carrying an umbrella may be superfluous.

senses.en: serving no useful purpose; having no excuse for being

examples.text: The editor cut every superfluous adjective from the manuscript, and the prose improved at once.

origin.ko: 라틴어 superfluus(넘쳐흐르는)에서 왔습니다. 그릇을 넘어 흐를 만큼 지나쳐 불필요하다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: stubbornly unyielding

examples.text: The tenacious reporter pursued the story for three years despite threats and mounting legal costs.

senses.en: good at remembering

examples.text: Her tenacious memory allowed her to recite long passages of poetry she had read decades earlier.

senses.en: Clinging to an object or surface; adhesive.

examples.text: The tenacious mud clung to our boots and slowed the whole hike.

origin.ko: 라틴어 tenāx('꽉 붙잡는')에서 왔습니다. 한번 쥔 것을 놓지 않는 모습이 '끈질긴'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: Having a tendency, written or spoken, with a partisan, biased or prejudiced purpose, especially a controversial one; implicitly or explicitly slanted; biased.

examples.text: Critics dismissed the documentary as a tendentious account that ignored evidence contradicting its thesis.

origin.ko: tendency에 -ious를 붙이고 독일어 tendenziös를 본떠 만들었습니다. 한쪽으로 기우는 경향이 '편향된'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: defiantly aggressive

examples.text: The truculent defendant glared at the judge and refused to answer a single question.

senses.en: Violent; rude; scathing; savage; harsh.

examples.text: The columnist's truculent attack on the minister left even his supporters feeling uneasy.

origin.ko: 라틴어 truculentus('사납고 거친')에서 왔고 trux('사나운')와 이어집니다.

senses.en: To emphasize or draw attention to.

examples.text: I wish to underscore the importance of proper formatting.

origin.ko: under와 score('줄을 긋다')의 결합입니다. 밑줄을 그어 눈에 띄게 하는 것이 '강조하다'입니다.

senses.en: True; genuine.

examples.text: A fair is a veritable smorgasbord.

origin.ko: verity('진실')에 -able을 붙였고 고대 프랑스어 veritable을 거쳤습니다.

senses.en: choose not to consume

examples.text: Patients were advised to abstain from alcohol for the duration of the treatment.

senses.en: refrain from voting

examples.text: Three delegates chose to abstain, leaving the resolution just short of the votes it needed.

origin.ko: 라틴어 abstinere(스스로 붙잡아 두다)에서 왔습니다. 손을 뻗지 않고 자신을 붙드는 모습이 '삼가다'입니다.

senses.en: An omen or prediction; a foreboding; a prophecy.

examples.text: The sudden drop in orders was read by analysts as an augury of a coming downturn.

origin.ko: 라틴어 augurium(새점)에서 왔습니다. 고대 로마 점술가가 새의 움직임으로 앞일을 점친 데서 '전조'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: auguring favorable circumstances and good luck

examples.text: an auspicious beginning for the campaign

origin.ko: 라틴어 auspicium(새점)에서 왔고 auspex(새점 치는 사람)와 이어집니다. 새가 길조를 보인다는 데서 '상서로운'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: Shameless or impudent; shocking or audacious; brash.

examples.text: She was brazen enough to deny stealing the handbag even though she was caught on camera doing so.

senses.en: Generally followed by out or through: to carry through in a brazen manner; to act boldly despite embarrassment, risk, etc.

examples.text: Caught in the lie, the minister tried to brazen it out rather than apologize.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 bræsen('놋쇠로 된')에서 왔습니다. 놋쇠처럼 굳은 낯짝이라 부끄러움을 모르는 모습입니다.

senses.en: Emotionally hardened; unfeeling and indifferent to the suffering/feelings of others.

examples.text: She was so callous that she could criticise a cancer patient for wearing a wig.

origin.ko: 라틴어 callōsus('살갗이 굳은')에서 왔습니다. 굳은살처럼 마음이 무뎌진 상태입니다.

senses.en: large in number or quantity (especially of discourse)

examples.text: she took copious notes

origin.ko: 라틴어 copiosus에서 왔고, copia('풍부함')가 뿌리입니다.

senses.en: failing in what duty requires
senses.ko: 직무를 태만히 하는, 책임을 다하지 않는

examples.text: derelict (or delinquent) in his duty

senses.en: forsaken by owner or inhabitants

examples.text: The derelict mill, long since abandoned by its owners, slowly crumbled beside the silent canal.

origin.ko: 라틴어 dērelictus(완전히 버려진)에서 왔습니다. 맡은 의무를 버려둔 상태가 '직무 태만'입니다.

senses.en: To tax the patience of; irk, frustrate, vex, provoke, annoy; to make angry.

examples.text: The constant delays and contradictory instructions began to exasperate even the most patient members of the committee.

origin.ko: 라틴어 exasperāre(거칠게 만들다)에서 왔습니다. 신경을 거칠게 긁어 화나게 한다는 이미지입니다.

senses.en: Appropriate, apt, fitting.

examples.text: The novelist's felicitous phrasing captured the mood of the village in a single sentence.

senses.en: marked by good fortune

examples.text: The two companies agreed that the merger came at a felicitous moment for both of them.

origin.ko: felicity에 -ous가 붙었습니다. 복되게 잘 들어맞는 '적절한'이라는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: young and inexperienced

examples.text: The fledgling company struggled to compete against established industry giants.

senses.en: any new participant in some activity

examples.text: As a fledgling in the diplomatic corps, she spent months learning protocol.

origin.ko: fledge(날 준비를 하다)에 -ling이 붙었습니다. 막 날기 시작하는 어린 새라서 '풋내기'입니다.

senses.en: avoiding waste

examples.text: Raised during the Depression, she remained frugal and reused everything she could.

origin.ko: 라틴어 frūgālis '덕 있는, 알뜰한'에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: the dominance or leadership of one social group or nation over others

examples.text: Historians debate how Britain maintained naval hegemony throughout the nineteenth century.

origin.ko: 그리스어 hēgemonía '지도력, 최고 지휘'에서 왔고, hēgeisthai(이끌다)에서 나온 말입니다.

senses.en: be a hindrance or obstacle to

examples.text: Bureaucratic delays continued to impede the delivery of aid to the flooded region.

origin.ko: 라틴어 impediō '족쇄를 채우다'에서 왔고 pēs(발)가 뿌리입니다. 발을 묶어 못 가게 하는 이미지입니다.

senses.en: attribute (responsibility or fault) to a cause or source

examples.text: The teacher imputed the student's failure to his nervousness.

origin.ko: 라틴어 imputō '계산에 넣다, 책임을 지우다'에서 왔습니다. 남의 계산서에 잘못을 얹는 이미지입니다.

senses.en: characterized by an inability to mask your feelings; not devious

examples.text: The child's ingenuous admission that he had eaten the cake made the whole room laugh.

senses.en: Naive and trusting.

examples.text: Only an ingenuous investor would trust a stranger who promised guaranteed returns of fifty percent.

origin.ko: 라틴어 ingenuus '고귀한 성품의, 솔직한'에서 왔습니다. 타고난 그대로 꾸밈이 없다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: (used especially of ideas or principles) deeply rooted; firmly fixed or held

examples.text: Habits of obedience were so ingrained in the soldiers that they hesitated even when the order was clearly mistaken.

origin.ko: ingrain(깊이 스며들게 하다)에 -ed가 붙은 말입니다. 깊이 배어 뿌리 박힌 상태를 뜻합니다.

senses.en: cause to accept or become hardened to; habituate

examples.text: Years of covering war zones had inured the reporter to scenes that would horrify most people.

origin.ko: 중세 영어에서 in-과 ure(실행하다, 단련하다)가 합쳐졌습니다. 몸에 배도록 단련시킨다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: liberality in bestowing gifts; extremely liberal and generous of spirit

examples.text: The university's new library was built entirely through the largess of a single anonymous donor.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 largesse에서 왔고 large(넉넉한, 관대한)에서 나왔습니다.

senses.en: Emerging; just coming into existence.

examples.text: Regulators struggled to keep pace with the nascent industry of commercial drone delivery.

origin.ko: 라틴어 nāscēns '태어나는 중인'에서 왔습니다. 막 태어나는 단계라는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: An expert in a particular field, especially as called upon to provide comment or opinion in the media; a commentator, a critic.

examples.text: Television pundits disagreed sharply about what the election results meant for the party.

origin.ko: 힌디어 paṇḍit에서 빌려 왔고 산스크리트어 paṇḍita('학자')로 거슬러 갑니다. 박식한 사람이 전문가·평론가를 뜻하게 되었습니다.

senses.en: To criticise harshly; to reprove.

examples.text: The judge sharply rebuked the lawyer for repeatedly interrupting the witness during testimony.

senses.en: an act or expression of criticism and censure

examples.text: The senator's speech was a stinging rebuke of the administration's foreign policy.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 buchier('치다, 쪼개다')에 re-가 붙은 말입니다. 되받아 두들긴다는 데서 꾸짖는다는 뜻이 되었습니다.

senses.en: make reparations or amends for

examples.text: The government pledged to redress the injustices suffered by families displaced during the dam project.

senses.en: act of correcting an error or a fault or an evil

examples.text: Workers who were unfairly dismissed sought redress through the labor tribunal.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 redrecier('다시 세우다')에서 왔습니다. 쓰러진 것을 바로 세우듯 잘못을 바로잡고 보상한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: having a quality that thrusts itself into attention

examples.text: The report's most salient finding was that wages had stagnated for a decade.

senses.en: Worthy of note; pertinent or relevant.

examples.text: The article is not exhaustive, but it covers the salient points pretty well.

origin.ko: 라틴어 saliēns(뛰어오르는)에서 왔습니다. 튀어나와 눈에 띄는 데서 두드러진, 핵심적인 뜻이 되었습니다.

senses.en: Experiencing sensation, thought, or feeling.

examples.text: Consider fish, who are apparently sentient yet cognitively extremely primitive in comparison with humans.

origin.ko: 라틴어 sentiēns(느끼는)에서 왔습니다. 감각과 느낌을 지닌 존재를 뜻합니다.

senses.en: seeming unaffected by pleasure or pain; impassive

examples.text: stoic courage

senses.en: someone who is seemingly indifferent to emotions

examples.text: Even a Rolls-Royce owner, I began to feel, would be a stoic to travel across Europe by car when the "Rheingold" is on offer.

origin.ko: 그리스어 stoa(주랑)에서 왔습니다. 제논이 아테네의 채색 주랑에서 가르친 학파의 이름입니다.

senses.en: make dirty or spotty, as by exposure to air; also used metaphorically

examples.text: She tried to sully her rival’s reputation with a suggestive comment.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 sylian(더럽히다)에서 왔습니다. 진흙이나 때를 묻혀 더럽힌다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: having or showing arrogant superiority to and disdain of those one views as unworthy

examples.text: Now he was a sturdy, straw haired man of thirty with a rather hard mouth and a supercilious manner.

origin.ko: 라틴어 superciliōsus(거만한)에서 왔고 supercilium(눈썹)과 이어집니다. 눈썹을 치켜올리고 남을 내려다보는 모습입니다.

senses.en: cause to be more favorably inclined; gain the good will of

examples.text: The airline offered free upgrades to appease passengers whose flights had been canceled.

senses.en: overcome or allay

examples.text: A small snack was enough to appease his hunger until dinner.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 apeser(평화롭게 하다)에서 왔습니다. 화난 상대를 평화 쪽으로 이끄는 것입니다.

senses.en: characterized by effort to the point of exhaustion; especially physical effort

examples.text: The movement towards a peaceful settlement has been a long and arduous political struggle.

origin.ko: 라틴어 arduus(가파른, 높은, 힘든)에서 왔습니다. 가파른 비탈을 오르듯 힘겹다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: restrict or confine within limits

examples.text: New regulations circumscribe the powers of the agency, leaving it little room to act without legislative approval.

senses.en: draw a line around

examples.text: another circle is circumscribed about the square

origin.ko: 라틴어 circumscrībō에서 왔고, circum(둘레에)과 scrībō(쓰다)가 합쳐졌습니다. 둘레에 선을 그어 범위를 한정한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: conducted with or marked by hidden aims or methods

examples.text: clandestine military operations

origin.ko: 라틴어 clandestīnus('비밀의, 숨겨진')에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: contented to a fault with oneself or one's actions

examples.text: The company grew complacent after years of market dominance and ignored emerging competitors.

origin.ko: 라틴어 complacēns('매우 기쁘게 하는')에서 왔고, com-과 placēre(기쁘게 하다)가 합쳐졌습니다. 스스로 만족해 안주한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: difficult to handle or use especially because of size or weight

examples.text: a cumbersome piece of machinery

senses.en: not elegant or graceful in expression

examples.text: The memo's cumbersome phrasing buried its main point under layers of needless qualification.

origin.ko: 중세 영어 cumber(방해, 장애)에 -some이 붙은 말입니다. 방해가 되는 것이 '거추장스러운'입니다.

senses.en: Fluently persuasive and articulate.

examples.text: an eloquent writer

origin.ko: 라틴어 ēloquī(말을 쏟아내다)에서 왔습니다. 생각을 밖으로 막힘없이 말하는 '달변'입니다.

senses.en: something that baffles understanding and cannot be explained

examples.text: The motives of the reclusive painter remain an enigma to historians.

origin.ko: 그리스어 aínigma(수수께끼 같은 말)에서 라틴어를 거쳐 왔습니다. 돌려서 말하는 어두운 말이 '수수께끼'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: characterized by intense emotion

examples.text: The fervid debate continued late into the night as delegates argued over every clause.

origin.ko: 라틴어 fervidus(뜨거운)에서 왔고 fervēre(끓다)가 바탕입니다. 펄펄 끓는 듯한 열렬함입니다.

senses.en: not serious in content or attitude or behavior

examples.text: The council refused to waste public money on such a frivolous project.

senses.en: Of little weight or importance; not worth notice; slight; trivial.

examples.text: The judge dismissed the suit as frivolous and ordered the plaintiff to pay costs.

origin.ko: 라틴어 frīvolus '시시한, 하찮은'에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: criticize severely

examples.text: Editorial writers fulminated against the new tax, calling it an outrage against working families.

senses.en: cause to explode violently and with loud noise

examples.text: The unstable compound fulminated when the technician struck it with a hammer.

origin.ko: 라틴어 fulmen(번개)에서 온 fulminō '번개를 내리치다'에서 왔습니다. 번개 치듯 맹렬히 비난한다는 이미지입니다.

senses.en: regret strongly

examples.text: we lamented the loss of benefits

senses.en: express grief verbally

examples.text: we lamented the death of the child

senses.en: a cry of sorrow and grief

examples.text: their pitiful laments could be heard throughout the ward

origin.ko: 라틴어 lāmentor '통곡하다'에서 왔고 lāmentum '울부짖음'에서 나왔습니다. 소리를 흉내 낸 말로 보입니다.

senses.en: Not straightforward; indirect; by implication; (sometimes even) obscure, ambiguous, or confusing.

examples.text: The minister made only an oblique reference to the scandal and avoided naming anyone.

senses.en: Not erect or perpendicular; not parallel to, or at right angles from, the base.

examples.text: The oblique rays of the winter sun cast long shadows across the field.

origin.ko: 라틴어 oblīquus '비스듬한, 옆으로 기운'에서 왔습니다. 곧바르지 않다는 뜻이 에둘러 말하는 것을 가리키게 되었습니다.

senses.en: To obstruct, cover, or otherwise block (an opening, a portion of an image, etc.).

examples.text: His reflection is occluded by the mist on the mirror.

origin.ko: 라틴어 occlūdere '앞을 닫아 막다'에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: Elaborately ornamented, often to excess.

examples.text: The ornate ceiling of the opera house was covered in gilded carvings.

senses.en: marked by elaborate rhetoric and elaborated with decorative details

examples.text: The professor's ornate, adjective-laden style made even simple points sound grand.

origin.ko: 라틴어 ōrnātus '장식된'에서 왔고, ōrnō는 '갖추다, 꾸미다'입니다.

senses.en: marked by precise accordance with details

examples.text: The punctilious clerk checked every figure twice before signing the final report.

origin.ko: punctilio('사소한 격식')에 -ous가 붙은 말입니다. 라틴어 punctum('점')에서 나와, 작은 점 하나까지 따지는 태도입니다.

senses.en: Showing ignoble cowardice, or contemptible timidity.

examples.text: The soldier deserted his troop in a pusillanimous manner.

origin.ko: 라틴어 pusillanimis('마음이 작은')에서 왔습니다. 담이 작아 겁이 많다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: Basic; minimal; with less than, or only the minimum, necessary.

examples.text: I have only a rudimentary grasp of chemistry.

senses.en: being in the earliest stages of development

examples.text: rudimentary plans

senses.en: not fully developed in mature animals

examples.text: rudimentary wings

origin.ko: rudiment에 -ary가 붙은 말로, 아직 다듬어지지 않은 초보적인 상태를 뜻합니다.

senses.en: timid by nature or revealing timidity

examples.text: The timorous clerk never dared to question a decision made by his superiors.

origin.ko: 라틴어 timor('두려움')에서 온 중세 라틴어 timōrōsus에서 왔습니다. 두려움이 가득하다는 뜻에서 '겁 많은'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: To flaunt, to publicize/publicise; to boast or brag about; to promote.

examples.text: Mary has been touted as a potential successor to the current CEO.

senses.en: Someone advertising for customers in an aggressive way.

examples.text: Be careful of the ticket touts outside the arena; they are famed for selling counterfeits.

origin.ko: 중세 영어 touten('튀어나오다, 엿보다')에서 왔습니다. 손님을 엿보며 호객하던 데서 '크게 선전하다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: make imperfect

examples.text: Flawed sampling methods vitiate the study's conclusions and render its statistics meaningless.

senses.en: take away the legal force of or render ineffective

examples.text: Proof of fraud would vitiate the contract and free both parties from their obligations.

senses.en: corrupt morally or by intemperance or sensuality

examples.text: Moralists feared that easy wealth would vitiate the character of the young heir.

origin.ko: 라틴어 vitiō('손상시키다')에서 왔고 vitium('악덕, 흠')과 이어집니다. 흠집을 내 망치는 것입니다.

senses.en: corrupt, debase, or make impure by adding a foreign or inferior substance; often by replacing valuable ingredients with inferior ones

examples.text: Unscrupulous merchants were caught adulterating the spices with cheap powdered filler.

origin.ko: 라틴어 adulterare에서 왔고 '다른 것에 가까이 가다'가 문자 그대로의 뜻입니다. 다른 것을 섞어 질을 떨어뜨리게 되었습니다.

senses.en: support and strengthen

examples.text: Strong earnings reports helped bolster investor confidence after months of market uncertainty.

senses.en: A large cushion or pillow, usually cylindrical in shape.

examples.text: She propped the bolster behind her back and settled in to read.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 bolster('베개, 쿠션')에서 왔습니다. 베개로 받쳐 주듯 '떠받치다, 북돋우다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: highly complex or intricate and occasionally devious

examples.text: Applicants struggled with the byzantine rules governing permits, which changed from one office to the next.

origin.ko: 비잔티움(비잔틴 제국)에서 온 말입니다. 제국의 복잡한 관료 체제와 궁정 음모에서 '미로 같은'이란 뜻이 나왔습니다.

senses.en: inclined or showing an inclination to dispute or disagree, even to engage in law suits

examples.text: His contentious temperament turned every committee meeting into a prolonged argument.

senses.en: involving or likely to cause controversy

examples.text: The council voted on a contentious proposal to rezone the historic waterfront.

origin.ko: 라틴어 contentiōsus('다투기 좋아하는')에서 왔고, contendere(겨루다)에서 갈라졌습니다.

senses.en: irritable as if suffering from indigestion

examples.text: The dyspeptic critic greeted every new production with a weary scowl and a scathing review.

senses.en: suffering from dyspepsia

examples.text: The dyspeptic patient avoided fried food and rich sauces after every meal.

origin.ko: 그리스어 dúspeptos(소화가 어려운)에서 왔습니다. 소화불량으로 짜증 내는 사람에 빗댔습니다.

senses.en: be deliberately ambiguous or unclear in order to mislead or withhold information

examples.text: Pressed about the missing funds, the treasurer began to equivocate and change the subject.

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 aequivocāre(같은 이름으로 부르다)에서 왔습니다. 두 가지로 해석되는 말로 일부러 얼버무린다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: liable to sudden unpredictable change

examples.text: erratic behavior

origin.ko: 라틴어 errāticus(떠도는)에서 왔습니다. 예측 없이 이리저리 헤매는 듯 불규칙하다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: A pronunciation of letters and syllables which is pleasing to the ear.

examples.text: The poet chose each word for its euphony as much as its meaning.

origin.ko: 그리스어 euphōnía(좋은 소리)에서 프랑스어를 거쳐 왔습니다. 듣기 좋은 소리를 뜻합니다.

senses.en: pronounce not guilty of criminal charges

examples.text: New DNA evidence exculpated the defendant after he had spent twelve years in prison.

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 exculpāre에서 왔습니다. culpa(죄)를 밖으로 내보내 혐의를 벗긴다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: look angry or sullen, wrinkle one's forehead, as if to signal disapproval

examples.text: The coach glowered at the referee after the controversial call went against his team.

origin.ko: 스칸디나비아어 계통으로 보이며 glow(노려보다)에 -er이 붙은 말로 설명됩니다.

senses.en: Given to using language in a showy way by using an excessive number of difficult words to impress others; bombastic; turgid.

examples.text: The American people believe that they have a free country, and we are treated to grandiloquent speeches about our flag and our reputation for freedom and enlightenment.

origin.ko: 라틴어 grandiloquus에서 왔습니다. grandis(큰)와 loquor(말하다)가 합쳐져 거창하게 말한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: not having enough money to pay for necessities

examples.text: The impecunious young poet survived on borrowed money and the occasional generosity of friends.

origin.ko: 라틴어 pecūnia(돈)에서 온 pecunious의 반대말입니다. 돈이 없다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: Tearful, sorrowful, sad, pertaining to tears, weeping, causing tears or crying.

examples.text: The film's lachrymose finale left even the most skeptical critics reaching for tissues.

origin.ko: 라틴어 lacrimōsus에서 왔고 lacrima(눈물)에서 나왔습니다. 눈물이 가득하다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: One who is unconventional or does not abide by rules.

examples.text: Among historians he was a maverick because of his belief that history is meaningless.

senses.en: independent in behavior or thought

examples.text: The maverick senator frequently voted against her own party's leadership.

origin.ko: 소에 낙인을 찍지 않았던 텍사스 변호사 새뮤얼 매버릭의 이름에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: Offensive to the senses; disgusting, unpleasant, nauseous, especially having an undesirable smell.

examples.text: A noisome odor rose from the abandoned cellar, and the workers refused to enter.

senses.en: Hurtful or noxious to health; unwholesome, insalubrious.

examples.text: Residents blamed the noisome fumes from the tannery for the town's chronic respiratory illness.

origin.ko: annoy(괴롭히다)에서 앞부분이 떨어져 나간 noy에 -some이 붙은 말입니다. 성가시고 불쾌하다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: acutely insightful and wise

examples.text: much too perspicacious to be taken in by such a spurious argument

origin.ko: 라틴어 perspicāx '날카롭게 꿰뚫어 보는'에서 왔고, perspiciō는 '속까지 들여다보다'입니다.

senses.en: Dangerously insecure or unstable; perilous.

examples.text: The firm's finances remained precarious after two consecutive years of falling revenue.

origin.ko: 라틴어 precārius('간청해서 얻은')에서 왔습니다. 남의 호의에 달려 불안정하다는 뜻이 되었습니다.

senses.en: recurring in scattered and irregular or unpredictable instances

examples.text: a city subjected to sporadic bombing raids

origin.ko: 그리스어 sporas(흩어진)에서 왔고 '씨 뿌림'과 이어집니다. 씨앗이 흩어지듯 여기저기 드문드문 일어납니다.

senses.en: (used of the voice or sound) deep and resonant

examples.text: The drill sergeant's stentorian voice carried across the entire parade ground.

origin.ko: 호메로스의 일리아스에서 목소리가 컸던 전령 스텐토르의 이름에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: similar or equivalent in some respects though otherwise dissimilar

examples.text: The economist argued that the housing bubble was analogous to the tulip mania of the seventeenth century.

origin.ko: 그리스어 analogos(비례하는)에서 왔습니다. 서로 비율이 맞아 비슷하다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: deliver to an enemy by treachery

examples.text: The spy betrayed his country

senses.en: reveal unintentionally

examples.text: Her smile betrayed her true feelings

origin.ko: 중세 영어 betrayen('반역하다')에서 왔고, traitor(반역자), treason(반역)과 같은 계통입니다.

senses.en: composed of people from or at home in many parts of the world; especially not provincial in attitudes or interests

examples.text: Lisbon has grown into a cosmopolitan city, home to residents from dozens of countries.

senses.en: growing or occurring in many parts of the world

examples.text: a cosmopolitan herb

origin.ko: cosmopolite(세계 시민)에 -an이 붙은 말입니다. metropolitan(대도시의)과 비교됩니다.

senses.en: marked by prudence or modesty and wise self-restraint

examples.text: his trusted discreet aide

origin.ko: 라틴어 discrētus(가려낸)에서 왔습니다. 옳고 그름을 가려내는 분별에서 '신중한'이 되었습니다. discrete와 이중어입니다.

senses.en: fair to all parties as dictated by reason and conscience

examples.text: an equitable distribution of gifts among the children

origin.ko: 프랑스어 équitable에서 왔고, equity(공평)와 이어집니다. 모두에게 고르게 대한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: producing no result or effect

examples.text: Rescuers made a futile attempt to reach the trapped miners before the tunnel collapsed.

origin.ko: 중세 프랑스어를 거쳐 라틴어 fūtilis에서 들어온 말입니다.

senses.en: implied though not directly expressed; inherent in the nature of something

examples.text: an implicit agreement not to raise the subject

senses.en: being without doubt or reserve

examples.text: implicit trust

origin.ko: 라틴어 implicitus '얽혀 들어간'에서 왔습니다. 안에 접혀 들어 있어 겉으로 드러나지 않는다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: characterized by extravagance and profusion

examples.text: a lavish buffet

senses.en: very generous

examples.text: the critics were lavish in their praise

senses.en: To give out extremely generously; to squander.

examples.text: They lavished money on the dinner.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 lavasse '쏟아지는 소나기'에서 왔습니다. 퍼붓듯 넘치게 쓴다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: a crafty and involved plot to achieve your (usually sinister) ends

examples.text: Historians have traced the downfall of the minister to the political machinations of his rivals.

origin.ko: 프랑스어와 라틴어 māchinātiō에서 왔고 machinate(꾀하다)에서 나왔습니다.

senses.en: A precept; a succinct statement or observation of a rule of conduct or moral teaching.

examples.text: The old maxim that honesty is the best policy guided the merchant throughout his career.

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 maxima '공리'에서 왔고 라틴어 maximus '가장 큰'과 이어집니다.

senses.en: Stubbornly defiant; disobedient; resistant to authority or control (whether in a noisy manner or not).

examples.text: The obstreperous students ignored the teacher's repeated pleas for order.

senses.en: Attended by, or making, a loud and tumultuous noise; boisterous.

examples.text: An obstreperous crowd gathered outside the courthouse, chanting and banging on drums.

origin.ko: 라틴어 obstreperus에서 17세기에 들어온 말입니다. 시끄럽게 맞서며 말을 안 듣는다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: threatening or foreshadowing evil or tragic developments

examples.text: Ominous clouds gathered over the harbor as the fleet prepared to leave.

origin.ko: 라틴어 ōminōsus '징조로 가득한'에서 왔고, ōmen은 '전조'입니다. 나쁜 일이 올 징조라는 뜻이 불길함이 되었습니다.

senses.en: avoid or try to avoid fulfilling, answering, or performing (duties, questions, or issues)

examples.text: The minister parried every question about the budget deficit.

senses.en: To avoid, deflect, or ward off (an attack, a blow, an argument, etc.).

examples.text: She parried the blow with her forearm and stepped back.

origin.ko: 라틴어 parāre '막다, 준비하다'에서 중세 라틴어와 프랑스어를 거쳐 왔습니다. 공격을 막아 받아넘긴다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: spreading or spread throughout

examples.text: the pervasive odor of garlic

origin.ko: 라틴어 pervādō '구석구석 지나가다'에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: careful and sensible; marked by sound judgment

examples.text: It is prudent to consult a physician before beginning any new exercise regimen.

senses.en: Frugal; economical; not extravagant.

examples.text: Only prudent expenditure may provide quality within a restrictive budget.

origin.ko: 라틴어 prūdēns는 prōvidēns('미리 보는')가 줄어든 말입니다. 앞일을 내다보니 신중합니다.

senses.en: lasting a very short time

examples.text: a transient pleasure

senses.en: one who stays for only a short time

examples.text: The cheap hotel catered mostly to transients, who rarely stayed beyond a single night.

origin.ko: 라틴어 trānsīre('지나가다')의 현재분사에서 왔습니다. 스쳐 지나가는 것이 '일시적인'입니다.

senses.en: being present everywhere at once

examples.text: Smartphones have become ubiquitous, appearing in the hands of nearly every commuter on the train.

origin.ko: 라틴어 ubīque('어디에나')에서 온 ubiquity에 -ous를 붙였습니다. 어디에나 있다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: To make great or greater in power, rank, honor, or wealth (applied to persons, countries, etc.).

examples.text: The king used every conquest to aggrandize his family at the expense of neighboring states.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 agrandir(크게 하다)에서 왔습니다. 힘이나 지위를 더 크게 키운다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: a disparaging remark

examples.text: The candidate refused to cast aspersions on her opponent's character without evidence.

origin.ko: 라틴어 aspersio(뿌림)에서 왔습니다. 남에게 더러운 말을 끼얹는 모습이 '비방'입니다.

senses.en: Kind; gentle; mild.

examples.text: The benign old judge treated first-time offenders with patience rather than severity.

senses.en: not dangerous to health; not recurrent or progressive (especially of a tumor)

examples.text: The biopsy showed the tumor was benign, and no further treatment was needed.

senses.en: Of a climate or environment, mild and favorable.

examples.text: The benign climate of the valley allows farmers to harvest two crops each year.

origin.ko: 라틴어 benignus(친절한)에서 왔습니다. bene(좋은)와 genus(태생)가 합쳐져 '좋은 성품을 타고난'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: swell from or as if from internal pressure

examples.text: The distended bellies of the starving cows

senses.en: cause to expand as if by internal pressure

examples.text: The gas distended the animal's body

senses.en: open to doubt or suspicion

examples.text: After he made some dubious claims about the company, fewer people trusted him.

senses.en: not convinced

examples.text: they admitted the force of my argument but remained dubious

origin.ko: 라틴어 dubius(둘 사이에서 망설이는)에서 왔고 duo(둘)와 이어집니다. 두 갈래 사이에서 확신 못하는 상태입니다.

senses.en: dissenting (especially dissenting with the majority opinion)

examples.text: The factious assembly could not agree on a single policy, and reform stalled for years.

origin.ko: 라틴어 factiōsus(파당을 짓는)에서 왔습니다. 파벌을 만들어 분열을 일으킨다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: influence or urge by gentle urging, caressing, or flattering

examples.text: The salesman tried to inveigle the couple into buying a warranty they clearly did not need.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 '눈이 없는'에서 왔습니다. 눈을 멀게 해 속이고 꾄다는 데서 '감언으로 꾀다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: assign great social importance to

examples.text: The tenor was lionized in Vienna

origin.ko: lion(사자)에 '~로 만들다'를 뜻하는 -ize가 붙은 말입니다.

senses.en: Appearing or recurring again and again; recurrent.

examples.text: Change is a perennial theme in politics.

senses.en: lasting an indefinitely long time; suggesting self-renewal

examples.text: perennial happiness

senses.en: lasting three seasons or more

examples.text: the common buttercup is a popular perennial plant

origin.ko: 라틴어 perennis '해를 꿰뚫는'에서 왔습니다. 해마다 되풀이된다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: concerned with practical matters

examples.text: The senator took a pragmatic approach, accepting a modest compromise rather than risking the entire bill.

origin.ko: 그리스어 pragma('행해진 일')에서 왔습니다. 실제 일에 밝다는 뜻에서 '실용적인'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: inspiring awe

examples.text: sublime scenery

senses.en: of high moral or intellectual value; elevated in nature or style

examples.text: a sublime deed

senses.en: greatest or maximal in degree; extreme

examples.text: The sublime arrogance of the plan stunned even the project's staunchest supporters.

origin.ko: 라틴어 sublīmis(높이 들린)에서 왔습니다. 높이 솟아 경외감을 주는 숭고함입니다.

senses.en: harshness of manner

examples.text: The senator answered the reporter's question with unexpected asperity.

senses.en: something hard to endure

examples.text: the asperity of northern winters

origin.ko: 라틴어 asperitas(거칢)에서 왔고 asper(거친)에서 나왔습니다. 표면의 거칠함이 말투의 퉁명스러움으로 옮겨졌습니다.

senses.en: involving intelligence rather than emotions or instinct

examples.text: Certainly, “Capital” is a cerebral read and the dangers of the world Marx lived in are not all the same as ours.

senses.en: of or relating to the cerebrum or brain

examples.text: Doctors monitored cerebral activity throughout the procedure to detect any sign of damage.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 cérébral에서 왔고, 라틴어 cerebrum(뇌)에서 갈라졌습니다. 뇌를 쓰는 지적인 성질입니다.

senses.en: acting as or providing a complement (something that completes the whole)

examples.text: The two business partners had complementary abilities: one had excellent people skills, while the other had a head for figures.

origin.ko: complement(보충)에 -ary가 붙은 말입니다. complimentary와 같은 어원에서 갈라졌습니다.

senses.en: maintain or assert

examples.text: He contended that Communism had no future

senses.en: compete for something; engage in a contest; measure oneself against others

examples.text: Three teams are contending for the championship this season.

origin.ko: 라틴어 contendere('팽팽히 뻗다, 애쓰다')에서 왔습니다. 서로 팔을 뻗어 겨룬다는 뜻에서 '주장하다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: treat with excessive indulgence

examples.text: The car cossets its occupants in comfort.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 cotsǣta('오두막 사는 사람')에서 왔을 것으로 추정되며, 확실하지는 않습니다.

senses.en: To remove moisture from; to dry; (sometimes) to dry to an extreme degree.

examples.text: Months of relentless sun and wind desiccated the soil until it crumbled into dust.

senses.en: lacking vitality or spirit; lifeless

examples.text: The pianist gave a technically flawless but desiccate rendering, devoid of any warmth or feeling.

origin.ko: 라틴어 dēsiccāre(완전히 말리다)에서 왔고 siccus(마른)가 뿌리입니다.

senses.en: conspicuously or grossly unconventional or unusual

examples.text: The eccentric billionaire insisted on conducting every board meeting from the roof of his greenhouse.

senses.en: a person with an unusual or odd personality

examples.text: Neighbors regarded the retired professor as a harmless eccentric who talked to his tomato plants.

senses.en: Not at or in the centre; away from the centre.

examples.text: The wheel turned on an eccentric axle, producing a wobbling motion.

origin.ko: 그리스어 ékkentros '중심에서 벗어난'에서 왔습니다. 중심을 벗어난 모습이 '별난'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: Distinguished, important, noteworthy.

examples.text: In later years, the professor became known as an eminent historian.

origin.ko: 라틴어 ēminēre(튀어나오다)에서 왔습니다. 다른 사람보다 우뚝 솟은 '저명한' 사람입니다.

senses.en: derived from experiment and observation rather than theory

examples.text: an empirical basis for an ethical theory

origin.ko: 그리스어 empeiría(경험)에서 왔습니다. 이론이 아니라 직접 겪은 경험에 바탕을 둔다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: A small flaw or sin.

examples.text: Voters were willing to forgive the candidate's youthful peccadilloes but not his dishonesty about them.

origin.ko: 스페인어 pecadillo, 즉 pecado(죄)에 지소사가 붙은 말로 '작은 죄'입니다.

senses.en: excessively unwilling to spend

examples.text: The penurious landlord refused to repair the heating even in midwinter.

senses.en: not having enough money to pay for necessities

examples.text: A penurious student, he lived on bread and tea for most of the winter.

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 pēnūriōsus에서 왔고, 라틴어 penuria는 '결핍'입니다.

senses.en: To weaken or work against; to hinder, sabotage.

examples.text: The war efforts were undermined by the constant bickering between the allies.

senses.en: To erode the base or foundation of something, e.g. by the action of water.

examples.text: Floodwater slowly undermined the bridge piers until the whole span collapsed into the river.

senses.en: be earlier in time; go back further

examples.text: Cave paintings in the region antedate the earliest known written language by thousands of years.

origin.ko: 라틴어 ante(앞)와 date(날짜)가 합쳐진 말입니다. 날짜가 더 앞선다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: a downward slope or bend

examples.text: The path followed a steep declivity into the valley, where a stream wound between the trees.

origin.ko: 라틴어 dēclīvis(아래로 기운)에서 왔고 clīvus(비탈)가 뿌리입니다.

senses.en: clearly revealed to the mind or the senses or judgment

examples.text: The effects of the drought were manifest to anyone who saw the parched and cracked fields.

senses.en: To become manifest; to be revealed.

examples.text: His osteoporosis first manifested as pain in his hips.

senses.en: provide evidence for; stand as proof of; show by one's behavior, attitude, or external attributes

examples.text: The buildings in Rome manifest a high level of architectural sophistication

origin.ko: 라틴어 manifestus '손에 잡힐 듯한'에서 왔습니다. 손으로 만질 수 있을 만큼 분명하다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: Lacking worldly experience, wisdom, or judgement; unsophisticated.

examples.text: It was naive to assume that the rival firm would simply hand over its customers.

senses.en: Produced in a simple, childlike style, deliberately rejecting sophisticated techniques.

examples.text: The gallery devoted a wing to naive painting by self-taught artists from rural villages.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 naïve는 라틴어 nātīvus '타고난, 자연 그대로의'에서 왔습니다. 꾸밈없이 타고난 그대로라 순진하다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: lessen or to try to lessen the seriousness or extent of

examples.text: The company tried to palliate its mistake with a hasty apology.

senses.en: provide physical relief, as from pain

examples.text: The drug does not cure the disease but can palliate its worst symptoms.

origin.ko: 라틴어 palliō '망토로 덮다'에서 왔고, pallium은 '망토'입니다. 문제를 망토로 덮어 가볍게 보이게 한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: lacking wit or imagination

examples.text: a pedestrian movie plot

senses.en: a person who travels by foot

examples.text: The new law requires drivers to yield to every pedestrian at the crosswalk.

origin.ko: 라틴어 pedester '걸어서 가는'에서 왔고, ped는 '발'입니다. 걸어 다니는 보통 수준이라 평범하고 재미없다는 뜻이 되었습니다.

senses.en: An agent or substitute authorized to act for another person.

examples.text: Shareholders who cannot attend the meeting may appoint a proxy to vote on their behalf.

senses.en: A measurement of one physical quantity that is used as an indicator of the value of another.

examples.text: Researchers often use tree rings as a proxy for past climate conditions.

origin.ko: 중세 영어 procuracie('대리권')의 줄임말로, 라틴어 prōcūrāre('관리하다')에서 왔습니다. 남을 대신해 돌보는 사람입니다.

senses.en: a variation in circumstances or fortune at different times in your life or in the development of something

examples.text: The family firm survived the vicissitudes of two wars and a depression.

origin.ko: 라틴어 vicissitūdō('교대, 변화')에서 왔고 vicis('차례, 변화')와 이어집니다. 번갈아 바뀌는 운이 '변천'입니다.

senses.en: based on or subject to individual discretion or preference or sometimes impulse or caprice

examples.text: The decision to use 18 years as the legal age of adulthood was arbitrary, as both age 17 and 19 were reasonable alternatives.

senses.en: Determined by impulse rather than reason; often connoting heavy-handedness.

examples.text: the arbitrary rule of a dictator

origin.ko: 라틴어 arbitrarius에서 왔고 arbiter(심판)에서 나왔습니다. 심판 마음대로라는 데서 '제멋대로의'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: the property of being prompt and efficient

examples.text: We must act with dispatch in this matter.

senses.en: dispose of rapidly and without delay and efficiently

examples.text: He dispatched the task he was assigned

senses.en: send away towards a designated goal

examples.text: Scores of foreign journalists have been dispatched to Seoul to report on the growing tensions between the two Koreas and the possibility of war.

origin.ko: 스페인어 despachar나 이탈리아어 dispacciare에서 왔다고 보며, 자세한 기원은 불확실합니다.

senses.en: call forth (emotions, feelings, and responses)

examples.text: He kindled an enthusiasm for the project in his fellow workers.

senses.en: cause to start burning

examples.text: The setting sun kindled the sky with oranges and reds

origin.ko: 고대 노르드어 kynda '불을 붙이다'에서 왔습니다. 불을 붙이듯 감정을 일으킨다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: Difficult to understand; abstruse.

examples.text: The philosopher's obscure prose frustrated even specialists who tried to paraphrase it.

senses.en: Not well-known.

examples.text: The obscure poet died unnoticed, and her work was rediscovered only decades later.

senses.en: Unknown or uncertain; unclear.

examples.text: The etymological roots of the word "blizzard" are obscure and open to debate.

origin.ko: 라틴어 obscūrus '어두운, 희미한'에서 왔습니다. 어두워 잘 안 보인다는 뜻이 이해하기 어렵다로 이어졌습니다.

senses.en: Devoted to or biased in support of a party, group, or cause.

examples.text: partisan politics

senses.en: a fervent and even militant proponent of something

examples.text: The senator remained a fierce partisan of tax reform throughout her career.

origin.ko: 이탈리아어 partigiano '한 편의 옹호자'에서 왔고, parte는 '부분, 편'입니다.

senses.en: cause to become

examples.text: The shot rendered her immobile

senses.en: pass down

examples.text: render a verdict

senses.en: give an interpretation or rendition of

examples.text: The pianist rendered the Beethoven sonata beautifully

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 rendre('되돌려 주다')에서 왔고 라틴어 reddere에서 나왔습니다. 어떤 상태로 되돌려 놓는다는 데서 '~하게 만들다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: reluctant to draw attention to yourself

examples.text: The retiring young scholar avoided public lectures and preferred the quiet of the archive.

senses.en: of a person who has held and relinquished a position or office

examples.text: a retiring member of the board

senses.en: Never before seen, done, or experienced; without precedent.

examples.text: The pandemic forced governments into unprecedented spending on public health and economic relief.

origin.ko: un-과 precedent('앞서 간 선례')의 결합입니다. 앞선 사례가 없으니 '전례 없는'입니다.

senses.en: contrary to your interests or welfare

examples.text: The drug was withdrawn after patients reported adverse reactions, including severe headaches and dizziness.

origin.ko: 라틴어 adversus(~을 향해 돌린)에서 왔습니다. 나를 향해 맞서 있다는 데서 '불리한'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: Of fundamental importance; crucial, pivotal.

examples.text: Honesty is the cardinal virtue in science, since every result depends on trust in the data.

origin.ko: 라틴어 cardinālis('문 경첩에 관한')에서 왔습니다. 경첩에 문이 매달리듯 모든 것이 달린 '핵심'이라는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: Thorny; difficult to deal with, especially due to being complex or tricky.

examples.text: The task of proving Fermat’s “last” theorem remains nettlesome.

senses.en: causing irritation or annoyance

examples.text: The nettlesome delays at the border frustrated even the most patient travelers.

origin.ko: nettle(쐐기풀, 짜증 나게 하다)에 -some이 붙은 말로, 쐐기풀처럼 다루기 까다롭다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: An error in the use of language.

examples.text: Prepositions are also prone to particular solecisms and infelicities.

senses.en: a socially awkward or tactless act

examples.text: Arriving at the formal dinner in casual clothes was a solecism that the hosts politely ignored.

origin.ko: 그리스어 soloikismos에서 왔습니다. 소아시아 도시 솔로이 사람들의 어법이 아테네인 귀에 틀려 보인 데서 나왔습니다.

senses.en: marked by simplicity; having a humble opinion of yourself

examples.text: Despite winning the prize, the physicist remained modest about her contribution.

senses.en: relatively moderate, limited, or small

examples.text: Her latest novel was a modest success.

origin.ko: 프랑스어를 거쳐 라틴어 modestus에서 왔고 modus(척도)에서 나왔습니다. 분수를 지켜 지나치지 않는다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: yield to another's wish or opinion

examples.text: After weeks of protest, the administration finally acceded to the students' demands for lower fees.

senses.en: take on duties or office

examples.text: She acceded to the throne at the age of eighteen, following her father's sudden death.

origin.ko: 라틴어 accedere(다가가다)에서 왔습니다. 상대 쪽으로 다가서 양보하는 데서 '들어주다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: to agree or express agreement

examples.text: Though she doubted the plan, she acquiesced rather than prolong the argument with her partners.

origin.ko: 라틴어 acquiescere(~에서 쉬다)에서 왔습니다. 맞서지 않고 편히 내려놓는 모습이 '묵인하다'입니다.

senses.en: something located at a time when it could not have existed or occurred

examples.text: A wristwatch in the medieval battle scene was a glaring anachronism that the film's editors missed.
