origin.ko: 그리스어 anachronismos(시간을 잘못 잡음)에서 왔습니다. 시간을 거스르는 듯한 어긋남이 '시대착오'입니다.

senses.en: To choose or nominate somebody for a leading or otherwise important position, especially formally or officially, or as an intended successor.

examples.text: The retiring chairman anointed his deputy as his successor months before the board's formal vote.

senses.en: administer an oil or ointment to; often in a religious ceremony of blessing

examples.text: The priest anointed the new king with sacred oil during the coronation.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 enoindre(기름을 바르다)에서 왔습니다. 머리에 기름을 부어 선택된 자로 세우는 의식이 어원입니다.

senses.en: a short pithy instructive saying

examples.text: The essayist's best-known aphorism holds that every victory carries the seed of its own complacency.

origin.ko: 그리스어 aphorismos(경계를 짓기, 정의)에서 왔습니다. 핵심을 구분해 짧게 뽑아낸 말이 '격언'입니다.

senses.en: Sharp, caustic, severe.

examples.text: The critic's astringent review left the young playwright shaken.

senses.en: sour or bitter in taste

examples.text: The unripe persimmon left an astringent, puckering taste in her mouth.

senses.en: tending to draw together or constrict soft organic tissue

examples.text: astringent cosmetic lotions

origin.ko: 라틴어 adstringere(바싹 묶다)에서 왔습니다. 조이는 듯한 날카로움이 '신랄한'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: a large gathering of people of a particular type

examples.text: A bevy of reporters crowded around the senator as she left the hearing room.

origin.ko: 중세 영어 bevey에서 왔으나 정확한 기원은 불분명합니다. 앵글로노르만어에서 왔을 가능성이 있습니다.

senses.en: young and inexperienced

examples.text: The callow recruit had never seen real combat and trembled at the first distant explosion.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 calu('털 없는, 대머리의')에서 왔습니다. 아직 털도 안 난 새끼처럼 미숙하다는 뜻이 되었습니다.

senses.en: fanatical patriotism

examples.text: The politician's speeches mixed economic grievance with a crude chauvinism that appealed to nervous voters.

senses.en: Unwarranted bias, favoritism, or devotion to one's own particular group, cause, or idea.

examples.text: Feminists say that male chauvinism is still prevalent in cultures worldwide.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 chauvinisme에서 왔고, 지나치게 애국적이던 전설적 병사 Nicolas Chauvin의 이름에서 나왔습니다.

senses.en: being attentive to women like an ideal knight

examples.text: He made the chivalrous gesture of offering his coat to the stranger waiting in the cold.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 chevalerous에서 왔고 chivalry(기사도)와 같은 어원입니다. 말 탄 기사다운 정중함입니다.

senses.en: act in unison or agreement and in secret towards a deceitful or illegal purpose

examples.text: Regulators accused the airlines of colluding to keep ticket prices artificially high.

origin.ko: 라틴어 collūdere에서 왔고, con-(함께)과 lūdere(놀다)가 합쳐졌습니다. 짜고 함께 놀아난다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: an exclusive circle of people with a common purpose

examples.text: A tightly knit coterie of executive powerbrokers made all the real decisions in the company.

senses.en: a political leader who seeks support by appealing to popular passions and prejudices

examples.text: The demagogue stoked fears about immigrants to win votes rather than offering any workable policy.

origin.ko: 그리스어 dēmagōgós '민중의 지도자'에서 왔습니다. 민중을 이끄는 사람이 '선동가'로 변했습니다.

senses.en: (of e.g. speech and writing) tending to depart from the main point or cover a wide range of subjects

examples.text: a rambling discursive book

senses.en: proceeding to a conclusion by reason or argument rather than intuition

examples.text: Philosophy proceeds by discursive reasoning rather than by flashes of intuition or revelation.

origin.ko: 라틴어 discursus(이리저리 달림)에서 왔습니다. 이야기가 이곳저곳으로 뛰어다니는 모습입니다.

senses.en: extract by the process of distillation

examples.text: The editor distilled a sprawling report into a one-page summary of its central findings.

senses.en: remove impurities from, increase the concentration of, and separate through the process of distillation

examples.text: The plant distills seawater to produce drinking water for the island's residents.

senses.en: Intentional deceptiveness; double-dealing.

examples.text: The diplomat's duplicity came to light when leaked cables revealed his secret promises to both sides.

origin.ko: 라틴어 duplicare(두 겹으로 하다)에서 왔습니다. 말과 속마음이 두 겹인 '이중성'입니다.

senses.en: generally incompetent and ineffectual

examples.text: The feckless manager ignored every warning sign, and the company slid steadily toward bankruptcy.

senses.en: not fit to assume responsibility

examples.text: Her feckless brother borrowed money constantly and never bothered to repay any of it.

origin.ko: 스코틀랜드어 feckless에서 왔고 effect(효과)에 -less가 붙은 말입니다. 효과가 없는, 곧 무능하다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: someone who deliberately foments trouble

examples.text: The member of the college's Communist League was a firebrand who would launch a sit-in or protest march at a moment's notice.

origin.ko: fire(불)와 brand(타는 나뭇가지)가 합쳐졌습니다. 불붙은 나뭇가지처럼 분쟁에 불을 붙이는 사람입니다.

senses.en: marked by casual disrespect

examples.text: the student was kept in for impudent behavior

origin.ko: 라틴어 impudēns '부끄러움을 모르는'에서 왔습니다. 부끄러움이 없으니 뻔뻔합니다.

senses.en: showing sustained enthusiastic action with unflagging vitality

examples.text: an indefatigable advocate of equal rights

origin.ko: 라틴어 indēfatīgābilis '지치지 않는'에서 왔습니다. 완전히 지칠 수 없다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: marked by close acquaintance, association, or familiarity

examples.text: an intimate friend

senses.en: concerning things deeply private and personal

examples.text: The memoir reveals intimate details of the author's struggle with illness and her fear of failure.

origin.ko: 라틴어 intimus '가장 안쪽의'에서 왔습니다. 가장 안쪽까지 들어올 만큼 가까운 사이라는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: the ceremonial act of clothing someone in the insignia of an office; the formal promotion of a person to an office or rank

examples.text: The investiture of the new archbishop drew thousands of worshippers to the cathedral.

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 investīre '옷을 입히다'에서 왔습니다. 관직의 예복을 입혀 주는 의식입니다.

senses.en: having or demonstrating ability to recognize or draw fine distinctions

examples.text: A keen observer of local politics, she predicted the election result months in advance.

senses.en: Often with a prepositional phrase, or with to and an infinitive: showing a quick and ardent responsiveness or willingness; eager, enthusiastic, interested.

examples.text: I’m keen on computers.

senses.en: intense or sharp

examples.text: The explorers felt a keen disappointment when the summit was lost to the storm.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 cēne '용감한, 영리한'에서 왔습니다. 날카롭고 예리하다는 뜻으로 이어졌습니다.

senses.en: To live in miserable or disheartening conditions.

examples.text: He languished in prison for years.

senses.en: To be neglected; to make little progress, be unsuccessful.

examples.text: The case languished for years before coming to trial.

senses.en: lose vigor, health, or flesh, as through grief

examples.text: After the factory closed, the once-thriving town slowly languished into poverty.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 languir에서 왔고 라틴어 languēre '기운이 없다'와 이어집니다. 시들어 가는 상태입니다.

senses.en: Lacking energy, enthusiasm, or liveliness.

examples.text: After the long illness, she felt listless and uninterested in her usual hobbies.

origin.ko: 중세 영어 lystles에서 왔고 list(욕구)에 -less가 붙었습니다. 의욕이 없는 상태입니다.

senses.en: Appearing as such; being such in appearance; professed, supposed (rather than demonstrably true or real).

examples.text: The ostensible purpose of the meeting was to review the budget, but the real aim was to remove the director.

origin.ko: 라틴어 ostendō '앞에 내밀어 보이다'에서 왔습니다. 겉으로 내보이는 모습이라는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: Excessively nervous, excited, tense, angry, anxious, or upset; overemotional; very uneasy.

examples.text: Overwrought after days without sleep, she burst into tears at the slightest criticism.

senses.en: Elaborate; baroque; overdone.

examples.text: Reviewers found the novel's overwrought prose tiresome, with every sentence straining for effect.

origin.ko: overwork의 옛 과거분사로, 지나치게 혹사당해 신경이 곤두선 상태입니다.

senses.en: perform an act, usually with a negative connotation

examples.text: perpetrate a crime

origin.ko: 라틴어 perpetrāre '끝까지 해내다'에서 왔습니다. 일을 끝까지 해치운다는 뜻이 나쁜 짓을 저지른다로 쓰입니다.

senses.en: the choicest or most essential or most vital part of some idea or experience

examples.text: The pith of my idea is that people should choose their own work hours.

senses.en: soft spongelike central cylinder of the stems of most flowering plants

examples.text: Cut the stem open to see the white pith at its center.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 piþa '식물의 부드러운 속'에서 왔습니다. 겉이 아닌 알맹이라는 뜻에서 핵심이 되었습니다.

senses.en: Not cosmopolitan; limited in outlook; narrow; illiberal.

examples.text: Critics dismissed the mayor's views as provincial and blind to the wider world.

senses.en: of or associated with a province

examples.text: provincial government

origin.ko: 라틴어 prōvincia('속주')의 형용사형 prōvinciālis에서 왔습니다. 수도에서 먼 지방 사람처럼 시야가 좁다는 뜻이 되었습니다.

senses.en: stubbornly resistant to authority or control
senses.ko: 고집 세고 말을 안 듣는, 반항적인

examples.text: The recalcitrant board members refused to approve the merger despite weeks of persuasion.

origin.ko: 라틴어 recalcitrāre('뒤로 걷어차다')에서 왔고 calx('발뒤꿈치')가 어원입니다. 말이 뒷발질하듯 반항합니다.

senses.en: feeling or showing profound respect or veneration

examples.text: maintained a reverent silence

origin.ko: 라틴어 reverēns('공경하는')에서 왔으며 revere에 -ent가 붙은 말입니다. 깊은 경의를 품은 태도입니다.

senses.en: To make angry.

examples.text: Nothing riles an anti-mosque demonstrator more than being called a bigot.

senses.en: make turbid by stirring up the sediments of

examples.text: The heavy rains riled the normally clear stream, turning it the color of coffee.

origin.ko: roil의 방언 발음에서 나왔습니다. 물을 휘저어 흐리게 하듯 마음을 휘저어 화나게 한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: Having curves in alternate directions; meandering.

examples.text: We followed every bend of the sinuous river.

senses.en: gracefully thin and bending and moving with ease

examples.text: The dancer's sinuous movements held the audience spellbound for the entire performance.

origin.ko: 라틴어 sinuōsus(굽이진)에서 왔습니다. 뱀처럼 구불구불한 모양입니다.

senses.en: presenting a summary or general view of a whole

examples.text: a synoptic presentation of a physical theory

origin.ko: 그리스어 synoptikos(한눈에 보는)에서 왔습니다. 전체를 함께 한눈에 내려다보는 개관입니다.

senses.en: characterized by violent emotions or behavior

examples.text: After their tempestuous argument, they did not speak to each other for weeks.

senses.en: (of the elements) as if showing violent anger

examples.text: Sailors avoided the tempestuous waters off the cape during the winter months.

origin.ko: 라틴어 tempestuōsus(폭풍 같은)에서 왔고 tempestās(날씨, 폭풍)에서 나왔습니다. 폭풍처럼 격렬하다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: an exorbitant or unlawful rate of interest

examples.text: Medieval theologians condemned usury as a sin against the poor who were forced to borrow.

senses.en: The practice of lending money at such rates.

examples.text: Many cultures have historically outlawed usury, viewing profit from lending as morally suspect.

origin.ko: 라틴어 ūsūra('이자를 받고 빌려줌')에서 왔고 ūsus('사용')와 이어집니다. 돈을 쓰게 하고 받는 대가가 '고리'로 굳었습니다.

senses.en: devoid of significance or force

examples.text: The candidate's speech was full of vacuous slogans that said nothing about actual policy.

senses.en: devoid of intelligence or thought

examples.text: A vacuous smile spread across his face as the lecturer went on.

origin.ko: 라틴어 vacuus('텅 빈')에 -ous를 붙였습니다. 속이 비어 '내용 없는'입니다.

senses.en: lacking significance or liveliness or spirit or zest

examples.text: The talk show host's vapid chatter filled the hour without offering a single memorable idea.

senses.en: lacking taste or flavor or tang

examples.text: The vapid soup tasted of nothing but warm water and a hint of salt.

origin.ko: 라틴어 vapidus('김빠진')에서 왔습니다. 맛이 빠진 음료처럼 생기 없는 것입니다.

senses.en: assist or encourage, usually in some wrongdoing

examples.text: Prosecutors charged the accountant with abetting the fraud by deliberately falsifying the company's quarterly records.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 abeter(꾀다)에서 왔고, 사냥개를 몰아 물게 한다는 뜻이 어원에 있습니다. 나쁜 일을 부추기는 뜻이 되었습니다.

senses.en: find repugnant

examples.text: She abhorred cruelty of any kind and refused to support anyone who tolerated it.

origin.ko: 라틴어 abhorrēre에서 왔습니다. '몸서리치며 뒤로 물러나다'라는 뜻이 지금의 '혐오하다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: provoke the hostility of

examples.text: The company antagonized its workers by announcing layoffs just before the holiday season.

origin.ko: 그리스어 antagonizesthai(맞서 싸우다)에서 왔습니다. 상대를 적으로 돌려 맞서게 한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: sharply contrasted in character or purpose

examples.text: Her cautious temperament was antithetical to the reckless approach favored by the rest of the team.

origin.ko: 라틴어 antitheticus에서 왔고 antithesis(맞세워 놓음)와 같은 뿌리입니다. 서로 정반대로 놓인 상태입니다.

senses.en: a final climactic stage

examples.text: The cult of the chief executive reached its apogee in the nineteen-nineties, a period when C.E.O.s seemed not so much to serve their companies as to embody them.

origin.ko: 그리스어 apogeion(지구에서 먼)에서 왔습니다. 지구에서 가장 멀어진 지점이 '정점'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: The best moment or highest point in the development of something, for example of a life or career; the apex, culmination, or climax (of a development).

examples.text: The apotheosis of her career was her appointment as chairman.

senses.en: the elevation of a person (as to the status of a god)

examples.text: As a former mortal who underwent apotheosis, Hercules was important to the emperors.

origin.ko: 그리스어 apotheosis(신격화)에서 왔습니다. 인간이 신의 자리에 오른다는 데서 '극치'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: ostentatiously lofty in style

examples.text: The bombastic preface promised a revolution in physics but delivered only familiar ideas.

origin.ko: bombast(솜 채움)에 -ic가 붙은 말입니다. 속을 부풀린 과장된 말투를 가리킵니다.

senses.en: an event resulting in great loss and misfortune

examples.text: The First World War was a cataclysm that destroyed empires and reshaped the map of Europe.

senses.en: a sudden violent change in the earth's surface

examples.text: Geologists believe a cataclysm of volcanic eruptions reshaped the entire plateau millions of years ago.

origin.ko: 그리스어 kataklysmos('홍수')에서 왔습니다. 위에서 아래로 쏟아져 모든 것을 휩쓰는 대홍수의 이미지입니다.

senses.en: a flamboyant deceiver; one who attracts customers with tricks or jokes

examples.text: The so-called healer proved to be a charlatan who sold worthless tonics to desperate patients.

origin.ko: 이탈리아어 ciarlatano('돌팔이')에서 왔고, ciarlatore(수다쟁이)와 cerretano(약장수)가 섞인 말로 봅니다.

senses.en: Friendly or sociable.

examples.text: The congenial bartender makes the Hog’s Head an inviting place to hang out during the weekends.

senses.en: suitable to your needs

examples.text: The quiet library provided a congenial atmosphere for the long hours of reading.

origin.ko: con-(함께)에 genial(타고난 기질의)이 붙은 말입니다. 기질이 서로 맞는다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: render holy by means of religious rites

examples.text: The bishop consecrated the new cathedral in a ceremony attended by thousands.

senses.en: give entirely to a specific person, activity, or cause

examples.text: She consecrated her career to the cause of public health reform.

origin.ko: 라틴어 cōnsecrāre에서 왔고 중세 영어 consecraten으로 들어왔습니다. 제단과 교회를 신께 바친다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: occupied with or fond of the pleasures of good company

examples.text: a woman of convivial nature

origin.ko: 라틴어 convīvium('잔치')에서 왔고, con-(함께)과 vīvō(살다)가 합쳐졌습니다. 함께 먹고 사는 즐거움입니다.

senses.en: express strong disapproval of

examples.text: Environmental groups decried the decision to open the protected wetlands to commercial development.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 descrier(소리치다)에서 왔습니다. 외쳐서 가치를 깎아내리는 뜻으로 발전했습니다.

senses.en: To pay or discharge (a debt, expense etc.); to meet (the cost of something).

examples.text: A small grant from the foundation helped defray the cost of the students' research trip.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 défrayer에서 왔고 고대 프랑스어 fraier(쓰다)와 이어집니다. 비용을 대신 쓴다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: the final resolution of the main complication of a literary or dramatic work

examples.text: The film's denouement ties up every loose thread, revealing who was behind the theft.

senses.en: the outcome of a complex sequence of events

examples.text: The denouement of the long negotiations surprised even the diplomats who had arranged them.

senses.en: express a negative opinion of

examples.text: She disparaged her student's efforts

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 desparagier(신분이 맞지 않게 하다)에서 왔습니다. 동등한 지위(parage)에서 끌어내린다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: To combine or fit (things) together well.

examples.text: The parts of your essay should dovetail so that it is cohesive and coherent.

senses.en: a mortise joint formed by interlocking tenons and mortises

examples.text: The cabinetmaker joined the drawer with a hand-cut dovetail that has lasted over a century.

origin.ko: dove(비둘기)와 tail(꼬리)을 합친 말입니다. 비둘기 꼬리 모양으로 파서 맞물리는 짜맞춤 이음에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: give qualities or abilities to

examples.text: She was endowed with a beautiful voice.

senses.en: furnish with an endowment

examples.text: A wealthy alumnus endowed a chair in astronomy at the university.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 endouer에서 왔고, 라틴어 dōtāre(지참금을 주다)가 바탕입니다. 재산이나 재능을 안겨 준다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: the feeling of being bored by something tedious

examples.text: A deep ennui settled over the idle aristocrats during the long winter.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 enui(성가심)에서 왔고, 라틴어 in odiō(미움받는)가 바탕입니다. 성가시고 싫은 느낌이 '권태'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: open to two or more interpretations; or of uncertain nature or significance; or (often) intended to mislead

examples.text: an equivocal statement

senses.en: open to question

examples.text: The committee's equivocal conduct during the audit raised suspicions about its motives.

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 aequivocus(같은 이름으로 불리는)에서 왔습니다. 같은 말이 여러 뜻으로 들려 모호하다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: praise, glorify, or honor

examples.text: They exalted their queen.

senses.en: raise in rank, character, or status

examples.text: The man was exalted from a humble carpenter to a minister.

origin.ko: 라틴어 exaltāre(높이 들어 올리다)에서 고대 프랑스어를 거쳐 왔습니다. 높이 올려 칭송한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: partially excusing or justifying

examples.text: Because of extenuating circumstances, the committee agreed to accept the application after the deadline.

origin.ko: 라틴어 extenuāre(얇게 하다)의 현재분사형입니다. 사정을 참작해 책임을 줄여 준다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: superficially impressive, but lacking depth and attention to the true complexities of a subject

examples.text: Critics dismissed the senator's facile explanation of the crisis as a slogan rather than an analysis.

senses.en: performing adroitly and without effort

examples.text: Her writing was facile and articulate.

origin.ko: 라틴어 facilis(하기 쉬운)에서 왔습니다. 너무 쉽게 해치운 듯 깊이 없는 '안이한'이라는 뜻이 되었습니다.

senses.en: likely to fail or make errors
senses.ko: 틀리기 쉬운, 오류를 범할 수 있는

examples.text: Even the most careful scientists are fallible, which is why independent replication matters.

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 fallibilis에서 왔고 fallere(속이다, 틀리게 하다)가 바탕입니다. 틀리기 쉬운 상태를 뜻합니다.

senses.en: showing inappropriate levity

examples.text: Her flippant reply to a serious question offended the grieving family.

origin.ko: 북부 영어 방언 flip(재잘대다)의 현재분사에서 왔습니다. 진지한 일에 재잘거리며 가볍게 구는 태도입니다.

senses.en: elaborately or excessively ornamented

examples.text: the senator's florid speech

senses.en: inclined to a healthy reddish color often associated with outdoor life

examples.text: The old sailor's florid face bore the marks of decades spent at sea.

origin.ko: 라틴어 floridus(꽃이 핀)에서 프랑스어를 거쳐 왔습니다. 꽃이 만발한 듯 지나치게 화려하다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: keep from happening or arising; make impossible

examples.text: The central bank cut interest rates to forestall a deeper recession.

senses.en: act in advance of; deal with ahead of time

examples.text: She forestalled her rivals' objections by addressing every weakness in her proposal at the outset.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 foresteall(앞에 서서 가로막음, 매복)에서 왔습니다. 앞질러 막아 미리 방지한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: noisy quarrel

examples.text: Police were called to break up the fracas that erupted outside the stadium after the match.

origin.ko: 이탈리아어 fracassare(박살 내다)에서 프랑스어를 거쳐 왔습니다. 물건이 부서지는 소리 같은 소란스러운 난투입니다.

senses.en: A sequence of gradual, successive stages; a systematic progression.

examples.text: The report traces the gradation from small village markets to a fully integrated regional economy over two centuries.

senses.en: A passing by small degrees from one tone or shade, as of color, to another.
senses.ko: 미묘한 농담 차이, 단계적 색조 변화

examples.text: The painter achieved depth through subtle gradations of blue across the canvas.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 gradation에서 왔고 grade(단계)에 -ation이 붙은 말입니다. 한 걸음씩 단계를 밟는 변화입니다.

senses.en: completely sealed; completely airtight

examples.text: The specimens were kept in hermetic containers to prevent any contamination from outside air.

senses.en: Isolated, away from outside influence.

examples.text: The monastery's hermetic community had little contact with the changing world beyond its walls.

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 hermeticus로, 연금술사 헤르메스 트리스메기스토스에서 왔습니다. 그가 보물 상자를 마법으로 완전히 봉인했다는 전설에서 '밀폐된'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: To act according to, to conform to; usually construed with to.

examples.text: Few men measured up to his standard of righteousness; he hewed to the line.

senses.en: make or shape as with an axe

examples.text: The settlers hewed a rough path through the dense forest to reach the river.

origin.ko: 고대영어 hēawan '도끼로 찍어 베다'에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: characterized by attack on established beliefs or institutions

examples.text: Many of Thomas Hardy's works were considered iconoclastic in his day.

origin.ko: iconoclast(성상 파괴자)의 형용사형입니다. 형상을 깨뜨리듯 기존 통념을 부순다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: To instill or inspire (someone) with a certain quality, feeling, or idea.

examples.text: The entire text is imbued with the sense of melancholy and hopelessness.

origin.ko: 라틴어 imbuō '적시다'에서 왔습니다. 물이 스며들듯 감정이나 사상을 불어넣는다는 이미지입니다.

senses.en: preventing especially liquids to pass or diffuse through

examples.text: The clay layer beneath the soil is impermeable, so rainwater collects in shallow pools on the surface.

origin.ko: 라틴어 impermeābilis에서 왔습니다. 통과해(per) 지나갈(me) 수 없다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: defying expression or description
senses.ko: 말로 표현할 수 없는, 형언할 수 없는

examples.text: Standing before the vast canyon at dawn, she felt an ineffable calm that no words could capture.

origin.ko: 라틴어 ineffābilis에서 왔습니다. 밖으로(ex) 말해 낼(fa) 수 없다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: give to understand

examples.text: She insinuated that her friends had betrayed her.

senses.en: introduce or insert (oneself) in a subtle manner

examples.text: He insinuated himself into the conversation of the people at the nearby table

origin.ko: 라틴어 īnsinuō '파고들다, 슬며시 들어가다'에서 왔습니다. 굽이진 틈으로 슬쩍 스며들듯 넌지시 비친다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: the sound of a bell rung slowly to announce a death or a funeral or the end of something

examples.text: The merger sounded the knell for the small, family-owned shops on the street.

senses.en: To ring a bell slowly, especially for a funeral; to toll.

examples.text: The church bells knelled the peaceful ending of the day, while the purple shades of night descended sadly and majestically on the low chain of neighbouring hills.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 cnyllan '치다, 두드리다'에서 왔습니다. 종을 천천히 치는 소리를 가리킵니다.

senses.en: openly distrustful and unwilling to confide

examples.text: Since he was bitten by a dog when he was young, he has always been leery of animals.

origin.ko: leer(곁눈질)에 -y가 붙은 것으로 추정되지만 불확실합니다.

senses.en: Misconduct or wrongdoing, especially by a public official and causing damage.

examples.text: By then, Mr. Altman had gathered more allies. Mr. Nadella, now confident that Mr. Altman was not guilty of malfeasance, threw Microsoft’s weight behind him.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 malfaire '악행을 하다'에서 왔고 라틴어 malefaciō와 이어집니다. 나쁜 짓을 한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: great merriment

examples.text: The old tavern rang with mirth as the travelers traded jokes late into the night.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 myrgþ '기쁨'에서 왔고 merry에 -th가 붙은 꼴입니다.

senses.en: A person who hoards money rather than spending it; one who is cheap or extremely parsimonious.

examples.text: Scrooge was a typical miser: spending nothing he could save, nor enjoying his wealth.

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 miser '비참한, 불쌍한'에서 왔습니다. 돈을 쌓아 두고 궁색하게 사는 사람을 가리키게 되었습니다.

senses.en: A written message; a letter, note or memo.

examples.text: The ambassador's carefully worded missive reached the capital within a week.

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 missīvus에서 왔고 mittō '보내다'에서 나왔습니다. 보내는 글, 곧 편지입니다.

senses.en: cast off hair, skin, horn, or feathers

examples.text: Birds typically molt once a year, replacing worn feathers with fresh plumage.

origin.ko: 중세 영어 melten '녹다'의 옛 활용형에서 나왔습니다.

senses.en: Approaching death; about to die; dying; expiring.

examples.text: The moribund patient was moved to a quiet room where his family could stay beside him.

senses.en: not growing or changing; without force or vitality

examples.text: The moribund steel industry could no longer support the town's dwindling population.

origin.ko: 라틴어 moribundus '죽어 가는'에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: A conference, especially one between enemies.

examples.text: The two commanders met under a white flag for a brief parley.

senses.en: discuss, as between enemies

examples.text: The rebels agreed to parley with government envoys before the deadline.

origin.ko: 옛 프랑스어 parler '말하다'에서 왔습니다. 적과 마주 앉아 말로 풀어 보는 회담입니다.

senses.en: Biased in favor of a person, side, or point of view, especially when dealing with a competition or dispute.

examples.text: God is not partial; he does not play favorites.

senses.en: Existing as a part or portion; incomplete.

examples.text: So far, I have only pieced together a partial account of the incident.

senses.en: Having a predilection for something.

examples.text: not partial to an ostentatious display

origin.ko: 라틴어 pars '부분'에서 왔습니다. 전체가 아닌 한쪽 부분만 편드는 데서 '편파적인'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: clearly revealed to the mind or the senses or judgment

examples.text: It was patent to everyone in the room that the witness was lying.

senses.en: a document granting an inventor sole rights to an invention

examples.text: The firm filed a patent for its new battery design.

origin.ko: 라틴어 patēns '열린, 명백한'에서 왔고, pateō는 '열려 있다'입니다. 활짝 열려 누구 눈에나 분명하다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: feeling or expressing remorse for misdeeds

examples.text: The penitent thief returned the stolen money and begged for forgiveness.

origin.ko: 라틴어 paenitēns '후회하는'에서 왔고, paeniteō는 '뉘우치다'입니다.

senses.en: Of little consequence; small and of little importance; petty, trivial.

examples.text: The committee wasted hours arguing over picayune details of the wording.

origin.ko: 남프랑스 오크어 picaioun '값싼 작은 동전'에서 왔습니다. 동전처럼 하찮다는 뜻이 되었습니다.

senses.en: Common, particularly (derogatory) vulgar, crude, coarse, uncultured.

examples.text: The critic dismissed the novel as plebeian entertainment unworthy of serious attention.

senses.en: of or associated with the great masses of people

examples.text: the common people in those days suffered greatly

origin.ko: 라틴어 plēbēius '평민의'에서 왔고, plēbēs는 '평민'입니다. 고상하지 않고 저속하다는 뜻으로도 쓰입니다.

senses.en: Progressing slowly and laboriously.

examples.text: The film's plodding pace left the audience restless long before the final act.

senses.en: A strong verbal or written attack on someone or something.

examples.text: Her essay was less a balanced analysis than a fierce polemic against the new curriculum.

senses.en: of or involving dispute or controversy

examples.text: The journal's polemic tone discouraged careful readers from trusting its conclusions.

origin.ko: 그리스어 polemikos('전쟁의')에서 왔습니다. 말로 벌이는 전쟁, 곧 격렬한 논쟁이 되었습니다.

senses.en: One who has mastered (especially when able to speak) several languages.

examples.text: A true polyglot, the interpreter moved easily between six languages during the summit.

senses.en: having a command of or composed in many languages
senses.ko: 여러 언어를 구사하는, 여러 언어로 된

examples.text: a polyglot traveler

origin.ko: 그리스어 polyglōttos('많은 언어를 말하는')에서 왔습니다. '많은'과 '혀'가 합쳐진 말입니다.

senses.en: dangerously steep

examples.text: The trail follows a precipitous ridge with a long drop on either side.

senses.en: Hasty; rash; quick; sudden

examples.text: […]humans have been responsible for a precipitous decline of elephants, from perhaps 300,000 in the early 1970s to some 10,000 today.

origin.ko: 라틴어 praeceps('머리부터 거꾸로')에서 왔습니다. 머리부터 곤두박질칠 만큼 가파르다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: formally reject or disavow a formerly held belief, usually under pressure

examples.text: Under threat of imprisonment, the astronomer was forced to recant his claim that the earth moved.

origin.ko: 라틴어 recantāre('다시 노래하다, 취소하다')에서 왔습니다. 이미 부른 노래를 거꾸로 부르듯 앞말을 철회합니다.

senses.en: failing in what duty requires

examples.text: It would be remiss of the committee to ignore the warnings raised by the auditors.

origin.ko: 라틴어 remissus('느슨해진, 게으른')에서 왔고 remittere('늦추다')의 과거분사입니다. 조여 둘 의무가 느슨해진 상태입니다.

senses.en: tear or be torn violently

examples.text: The violent storm threatened to rend the old sail into ribbons before the ship reached harbor.

senses.en: To violently disturb the peace of; to throw into chaos.

examples.text: A bitter dispute over succession threatened to rend the royal family apart.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 rendan('찢다')에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: rising again as to new life and vigor

examples.text: resurgent nationalism

senses.en: Beyond alteration, criticism, or interference, especially due to religious sanction; inviolable.

examples.text: After decades of being considered politically sacrosanct, why are homeowner mortgage write-offs suddenly on the chopping block?

origin.ko: 라틴어 sacrōsānctus에서 왔습니다. '의식으로 신성하게 된' 것이라 건드릴 수 없다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: A shallow or superficial knowledge of a subject.

examples.text: She knows a smattering of Greek, but not enough to carry on a conversation.

senses.en: a small number or amount

examples.text: Only a smattering of spectators braved the rain to watch the match.

origin.ko: smatter(어설프게 말하다)에 -ing이 붙은 말입니다. 겉핥기로 아는 얕은 지식입니다.

senses.en: reject with contempt

examples.text: She spurned his advances

origin.ko: 고대 영어 spurnan(걷어차다)에서 왔습니다. 발로 걷어차듯 경멸하며 거절한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: foul and run-down and repulsive

examples.text: a squalid overcrowded apartment in the poorest part of town

senses.en: Showing or characterized by a contemptible lack of moral standards.

examples.text: a squalid attempt to buy votes

origin.ko: 라틴어 squālēre(거칠고 더럽다)에서 온 squalidus에서 왔습니다. 더럽고 누추한 모습입니다.

senses.en: characterized by dignity and propriety

examples.text: The staid accounting firm was startled by the new partner's flamboyant approach to client meetings.

origin.ko: stay의 과거분사 stayed의 옛 철자에서 왔습니다. 흔들리지 않고 자리를 지키는 점잖은 태도입니다.

senses.en: capable of being maintained or justified; well-founded

examples.text: Back in the 1800s, many did not consider Darwin's theory of evolution to be tenable at all.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 tenir(붙잡다)에서 나온 tenable에서 왔습니다. 붙들고 지킬 만한 타당한 주장입니다.

senses.en: To defeat (someone); to overcome.

examples.text: After years of struggle, the young champion finally vanquished her long-time rival in the final match.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 veincre에서 왔고 라틴어 vincō('이기다')와 이어집니다.

senses.en: To say defamatory things about someone or something; to speak ill of.

examples.text: Opponents tried to vilify the whistleblower as a liar in order to discredit her report.

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 vīlificāre에서 왔습니다. 남을 vile('천한')하게 만든다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: harsh or corrosive in tone

examples.text: The critic's vitriolic review accused the director of laziness and called the film an insult to viewers.

origin.ko: vitriol('황산')에 -ic를 붙였습니다. 산처럼 쓰라린 말투가 '신랄한'입니다.

senses.en: make keen or more acute

examples.text: The brief preview was enough to whet the public's appetite for the full documentary.

senses.en: sharpen by rubbing, as on a whetstone

examples.text: The old blacksmith would whet his knife on a stone before carving the roast.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 hwettan('날을 갈다')에서 왔습니다. 칼을 갈듯 식욕과 흥미를 날카롭게 하는 것입니다.

senses.en: Charming, engaging, winning; inspiring approval and trust, especially if in an innocent manner.

examples.text: Her winsome smile put the nervous interviewee at ease within seconds.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 wynsum('즐거운')에서 왔고 winne('기쁨')에 -some을 붙인 형태입니다. 기쁨을 주는 '매력적인' 모습입니다.

senses.en: become less in amount or intensity

examples.text: The storm abated

senses.en: To lessen (something) in force or intensity; to moderate.

examples.text: Officials hoped that a public apology would abate the anger of residents living near the plant.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 abatre(때려 눕히다)에서 왔습니다. 세게 눕혀 기세를 꺾는다는 데서 '약해지다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: give up, such as power, as of monarchs and emperors, or duties and obligations

examples.text: Critics argued that the board had abdicated its responsibility by ignoring repeated warnings about the company's finances.

origin.ko: 라틴어 abdicare(거부하다)에서 왔습니다. 자리를 '멀리 선언해 버린다'는 뜻에서 '퇴위하다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: harsh or corrosive in tone

examples.text: The columnist was known for her acerbic wit, which spared neither politicians nor fellow journalists.

origin.ko: 라틴어 acerbus(시고 쓴)에서 왔습니다. 혀를 찌르는 신맛이 말투의 '신랄함'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: quick or skillful or adept in action or thought

examples.text: An adroit negotiator, she turned the hostile meeting into an agreement acceptable to both sides.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 à droit(바르게)에서 왔습니다. 오른쪽(droit)처럼 곧게 잘 다루는 데서 '노련한'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: a deliberate pretense or exaggerated display

examples.text: His fake British accent was an affectation that fooled no one who knew him well.

origin.ko: 라틴어 affectare(~인 체하다)에서 왔습니다. 일부러 꾸며 보이는 태도가 '허식'입니다.

senses.en: A feeling of enmity, animosity or ill will.

examples.text: The judge found no evidence of personal animus behind the prosecutor's decision to bring charges.

origin.ko: 라틴어 animus(마음, 정신, 격정)를 그대로 빌려왔으며 '숨 쉬다'에서 나왔습니다. 마음속 적의를 뜻하게 되었습니다.

senses.en: of an appropriate or pertinent nature

examples.text: The quotation from Orwell seemed particularly apropos given the week's headlines.

senses.en: Regarding, concerning, in regard to, on the subject of.

examples.text: Apropos the budget, the committee has yet to reach a decision.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 à propos(그 주제에 대해)에서 왔습니다. 화제에 딱 맞는다는 데서 '적절한'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: refuse to comply

examples.text: balked at paying a day's wages for a pencil; he said he would buy her one, but when he saw the price, he balked

senses.en: something immaterial that interferes with or delays action or progress

examples.text: Bureaucratic delays proved a serious balk to the construction of the new bridge.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 balca(두둑, 칸막이)에서 왔습니다. 앞을 가로막는 장애물 때문에 멈칫하는 이미지입니다.

senses.en: ill-mannered and coarse and contemptible in behavior or appearance

examples.text: His boorish behavior at the dinner embarrassed his hosts and offended the other guests.

senses.en: a trite or obvious remark

examples.text: We hoped the speech would include reassurances, but instead it was merely one bromide after another.

origin.ko: 화학 물질 브롬화물(bromide)에서 왔습니다. 진정제로 쓰이던 물질이라, 마음을 달래는 식상한 말을 가리키게 되었습니다.

senses.en: overly sweet

examples.text: The frosting was so cloying that most guests left half of their slices untouched.

senses.en: Unpleasantly excessive.

examples.text: The cloying fondness she displayed was what, in the end, drove me away.

origin.ko: cloy(물리게 하다)에 -ing가 붙은 말입니다.

senses.en: To reach a climax; to come to a decisive point, especially an end or conclusion.

examples.text: Their messy breakup culminated in a restraining order.

origin.ko: 라틴어 culmen(꼭대기, 정점)에서 왔습니다. 정점에 오르니 '절정에 달하다'입니다.

senses.en: do something that one considers to be below one's dignity

examples.text: He didn’t even deign to give us a nod of the head; he thought us that far beneath him.

origin.ko: 라틴어 dignāre(~할 만하다고 여기다)에서 왔습니다. 자기 품위에 맞는다고 여겨 '황송하게 ~해 주다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: To remove (a leader) from (high) office without killing (them).

examples.text: A deposed monarch may go into exile as pretender to the lost throne, hoping to be restored in a subsequent revolution.

senses.en: make a deposition; declare under oath

examples.text: The engineer was deposed by the plaintiff's lawyers three months before the trial began.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 deposer에서 왔습니다. 높은 자리에서 아래로 내려놓으니 '폐위하다'입니다.

senses.en: a cruel and oppressive dictator

examples.text: The despot silenced his critics, jailed journalists, and ruled the country for three decades.

origin.ko: 그리스어 despótēs(주인, 주군)에서 왔습니다. 집안의 주인이 절대 권력자인 '폭군'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: discontented as toward authority

examples.text: Disaffected voters stayed home, convinced that neither party would address their concerns.

senses.en: deprive of voting rights

examples.text: Strict identification laws could disenfranchise elderly voters who no longer hold a valid driver's license.

senses.en: of or belonging to or active during the day

examples.text: Most birds are diurnal.

senses.en: having a daily cycle or occurring every day

examples.text: diurnal rotation of the heavens

origin.ko: 라틴어 diurnālis에서 왔고 diēs(날)가 뿌리입니다. journal과 이중어입니다.

senses.en: a mournful poem; a lament for the dead

examples.text: The poet composed an elegy for his friend who died at sea.

origin.ko: 그리스어 elegeía(애도의 노래)에서 라틴어와 프랑스어를 거쳐 왔습니다. 죽은 이를 기리는 슬픈 시를 가리킵니다.

senses.en: ask for or request earnestly

examples.text: The mother entreated the guards to let her see her imprisoned son.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 entraiter(상대를 어떤 식으로 대하다, 협상하다)에서 왔습니다. 상대를 설득하며 간절히 부탁한다는 뜻이 되었습니다.

senses.en: praise, glorify, or honor

examples.text: Reviewers extolled the novel's elegant prose and its unflinching portrait of rural poverty.

origin.ko: 라틴어 extollere(높이 들어 올리다)에서 왔습니다. 높이 들어 올려 칭송한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: offensively malodorous

examples.text: I caught the fetid odor of dirty socks.

origin.ko: 라틴어 fētidus(악취 나는)에서 왔고 fēteō(악취를 풍기다)가 바탕입니다.

senses.en: treat with contemptuous disregard

examples.text: flout the rules

senses.en: laugh at with contempt and derision

examples.text: Hecklers flouted the candidate throughout his speech, mocking every promise he made.

senses.en: a socially awkward or tactless act

examples.text: The candidate's gaffe about rural voters dominated the news for an entire week.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 gaffe '실수'에서 왔고, 옛 오크어 gaf(걸쇠, 갈고리)가 어원입니다.

senses.en: to stimulate to action

examples.text: The shocking report galvanized residents into demanding cleaner drinking water.

senses.en: cover with zinc

examples.text: Workers galvanize the steel beams to protect them from rust.

origin.ko: 이탈리아 생리학자 갈바니(Galvani)의 이름에서 왔습니다. 전기 자극을 주듯 사람을 자극해 움직이게 한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: diffusing warmth and friendliness

examples.text: The genial innkeeper greeted every traveler as though he were an old friend.

senses.en: Pleasantly mild and warm.

examples.text: The valley's genial climate allows farmers to grow citrus fruit well into November.

origin.ko: 라틴어 geniālis '혼례의, 축제의'에서 왔고 genius(수호신)에서 나왔습니다. 잔치처럼 즐겁고 따뜻한 분위기가 '상냥한'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: obtain by coercion or intimidation

examples.text: Some merchants gouged desperate residents by tripling the price of bottled water after the flood.

senses.en: make a groove in

examples.text: The glacier gouged deep valleys into the bedrock as it advanced.

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 gubia '둥근 끌'에서 고대 프랑스어를 거쳐 왔습니다. 끌로 파내듯 돈을 뜯어낸다는 이미지입니다.

senses.en: shrewdness as demonstrated by being skilled in deception

examples.text: The negotiator relied on guile rather than force, slowly steering the talks toward his own terms.

origin.ko: 프랑크어 *wīl '계략'에서 고대 프랑스어를 거쳐 왔습니다. wile(꾀)과 같은 뿌리입니다.

senses.en: having or showing arrogant superiority to and disdain of those one views as unworthy

examples.text: The haughty maître d' looked past the couple as though they were not worth his attention.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 haut '높은'에서 왔습니다. 스스로를 높이 두는 태도가 '오만한'입니다.

senses.en: receive into the mind and retain

examples.text: As a young apprentice, she imbibed the principles of careful research from her demanding mentor.

senses.en: To drink (used frequently of alcoholic beverages).

examples.text: The guests imbibed freely throughout the evening, and the party grew louder by the hour.

origin.ko: 라틴어 imbibō '들이마시다'에서 왔습니다. 안으로(in-) 마신다(bib)는 뜻에서 지식을 빨아들이는 뜻이 되었습니다.

senses.en: defying imitation; matchless

examples.text: an inimitable style

origin.ko: 프랑스어를 거쳐 라틴어 inimitabilis에서 왔습니다. 흉내 낼 수 없으니 '독보적인'입니다.

senses.en: morally objectionable behavior

examples.text: The preacher warned that the iniquity of the city's rulers would eventually bring about its downfall.

senses.en: an unjust act

examples.text: The seizure of the farmers' land without payment was widely denounced as an iniquity.

origin.ko: 라틴어 inīquitās '불평등, 불공정'에서 왔습니다. 고르지 않고 공정하지 못한 것이 '부도덕'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: marked by casual disrespect

examples.text: The insolent clerk rolled his eyes and refused to answer the customer's polite question.

origin.ko: 라틴어 īnsolēns '익숙하지 않은, 오만한'에서 왔습니다. 관례를 따르지 않아 무례해졌습니다.

senses.en: Having had a habit (usually a bad habit) for a long time.

examples.text: An inveterate gambler, he lost his savings again and again despite repeated promises to stop.

origin.ko: 라틴어 inveterātus '오래된, 만성이 된'에서 왔습니다. 오래 묵어 굳은 습관을 뜻합니다.

senses.en: Marked by irritation or annoyance; disagreeable; troublesome by reason of long continuance or repetition

examples.text: He has this irksome habit of racing up to red lights, so he has to brake heavily.

origin.ko: irk(짜증나게 하다)에 -some이 붙은 말입니다. 지치고 귀찮게 하는 성질입니다.

senses.en: Having, characterized by, or done with good judgment or sound thinking.

examples.text: A judicious use of the budget allowed the department to avoid layoffs during the downturn.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 judicieux에서 왔고 라틴어 iudico '판단하다'에서 나왔습니다. 판단을 잘하는 분별력을 뜻합니다.

senses.en: The trait of being willing to donate money, resources, or time; generosity, liberality.

examples.text: The museum survives chiefly on the largesse of wealthy patrons.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 largesce에서 왔고 large(넉넉한, 관대한)에서 나왔습니다. 넉넉히 베푸는 마음입니다.

senses.en: Averse, disinclined; reluctant, unwilling. Always followed by a verbal phrase.

examples.text: I was loath to return to the office without the Henderson file.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 lāð '악의적인, 혐오스러운'에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: A chaotic or turbulent situation.

examples.text: He escaped at last, dizzy from the maelstrom of conflicting emotions that had caught and whirled him.

senses.en: a powerful circular current of water (usually the result of conflicting tides)

examples.text: Sailors in the strait feared the maelstrom that formed whenever opposing tides collided.

origin.ko: 네덜란드어 malen '빙빙 돌다'와 stroom '물살'이 합쳐졌습니다. 노르웨이 앞바다의 거대한 소용돌이 이름에서 '대혼란'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: to move or cause to move in a sinuous, spiral, or circular course

examples.text: The stream meandered through the valley.

senses.en: To be intricate.

examples.text: His speech meandered through various topics.

origin.ko: 소아시아의 강 Maeander에서 왔습니다. 구불구불 흐르기로 유명한 강 이름이 '굽이쳐 가다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: (used of persons or behavior) characterized by or indicative of lack of generosity

examples.text: The miserly landlord refused to repair the heating even in the coldest weeks of winter.

origin.ko: miser(구두쇠)에 -ly가 붙은 말로 1540년대부터 쓰였습니다.

senses.en: an incorrect or unsuitable name

examples.text: The name Chinese checkers is a misnomer since the game has nothing to do with China.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 mesnomer '이름을 잘못 부르다'에서 왔습니다. mes-(잘못)와 nommer(이름 붙이다)가 합쳐졌습니다.

senses.en: cause annoyance in; disturb, especially by minor irritations

examples.text: The senator was visibly nettled by the reporter's repeated questions about his donors.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 netele '쐐기풀'에서 왔습니다. 쐐기풀에 쏘인 듯 따끔하고 짜증 나게 한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: Indifferent; unconcerned; behaving as if detached.

examples.text: He is far too nonchalant about such a serious matter.

origin.ko: 옛 프랑스어 nonchaloir '마음 쓰지 않다'에서 왔습니다. 마음이 달아오르지 않는 태연한 태도입니다.

senses.en: To deliberately make more confusing in order to conceal the truth.

examples.text: obfuscate facts

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 obfuscō '어둡게 하다'에서 왔습니다. 일부러 어둡게 가려 진실을 흐린다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: To express an opinion; to state as an opinion; to suppose, consider (that).

examples.text: I opined that matters would soon become considerably worse.

origin.ko: 라틴어 opīnor '의견을 갖다'에서 왔습니다. 자기 생각을 밝힌다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: To exceed or surpass (someone or something).

examples.text: This year’s production has already outstripped last year’s.

senses.en: To move more quickly than (someone or something) so as to outrun or leave it behind.

examples.text: We quickly outstripped the amateur runners.

origin.ko: out(넘어서)에 옛말 strip('재빨리 지나가다')을 붙인 말로, 상대를 앞질러 지나친다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: a complete and impressive array

examples.text: The festival offered a dazzling panoply of music, dance, and street food.

senses.en: Something that covers and protects.

examples.text: A panoply of legal safeguards protects whistleblowers from retaliation.

origin.ko: 그리스어 panoplía '갑옷 한 벌'에서 왔습니다. 완전히 갖춘 장비 일체라는 뜻이 화려한 총집합으로 이어졌습니다.

senses.en: examine or consider with attention and in detail

examples.text: Please peruse this report at your leisure

origin.ko: per-(철저히)와 use(쓰다)를 합친 말로, 원래 '다 써서 닳게 하다'였습니다. 속속들이 꼼꼼히 살핀다는 뜻만 남았습니다.

senses.en: To cause a group to be divided into extremes.

examples.text: The proposed tax reform polarized the electorate and left little room for compromise.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 polariser에서 왔으며, polar(극의)에 -ize가 붙은 말입니다. 양 극단으로 갈라놓는다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: perceiving the significance of events before they occur

examples.text: The report proved prescient, warning of the housing collapse years before it happened.

origin.ko: 라틴어 praesciēns('미리 아는')에서 왔습니다. prae-('앞')와 sciō('알다')가 합쳐진 말입니다.

senses.en: argue over petty things

examples.text: They are constantly quibbling over insignificant details.

senses.en: an evasion of the point of an argument by raising irrelevant distinctions or objections

examples.text: Her only quibble with the proposal concerned the wording of a single footnote.

senses.en: witty remark

examples.text: The senator defused the tense hearing with a well-timed quip about the committee's coffee.

senses.en: fail to fulfill a promise or obligation

examples.text: she reneged on her promise

origin.ko: 라틴어 renegāre('부인하다')에서 왔습니다. 했던 약속을 부인하고 어긴다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: freedom from activity (work or strain or responsibility)

examples.text: took his repose by the swimming pool

senses.en: a disposition free from stress or emotion

examples.text: Even in the middle of the crisis, the old judge maintained an air of calm repose.

senses.en: lean in a comfortable resting position

examples.text: He was reposing on the couch

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 reposer('쉬다')에서 왔고 후기 라틴어 repausāre('쉬게 하다')와 이어집니다. 몸을 내려놓고 쉬는 안식입니다.

senses.en: To satisfy to excess. To fill to satiety.

examples.text: The lavish banquet satiated the guests so thoroughly that none could manage dessert.

senses.en: To fill to satisfaction; to satisfy.

examples.text: Nothing seemed to satiate her desire for knowledge.

origin.ko: 라틴어 satis(충분한)에서 온 satiāre에서 왔습니다. 충분을 넘도록 채운다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: A person of learning, especially one who is versed in literature or science.

examples.text: The young savant astonished the faculty with his command of ancient languages and modern physics.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 savant(아는 사람)에서 왔고, 라틴어 sapere에서 나왔습니다. 많이 아는 학자를 뜻합니다.

senses.en: full and loud and deep

examples.text: He was selected to give the opening speech thanks to his imposing, sonorous voice.

origin.ko: 라틴어 sonor(소리)에서 온 sonōrus에서 왔습니다. 소리가 풍부하고 깊게 울린다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: given to merry frolicking

examples.text: The sportive lambs leapt and chased one another across the spring meadow all afternoon.

origin.ko: sport(놀이)에 -ive가 붙은 말입니다. 신나게 뛰놀며 장난친다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: spend thoughtlessly; throw away

examples.text: You squandered the opportunity to get an advanced degree

origin.ko: 16세기 말 처음 보이며 어원은 불확실합니다. scatter와 wander의 혼합일 수 있다고 봅니다.

senses.en: suppress or crush completely

examples.text: Even the king's announcement could not squelch the rumors.

senses.en: To make a sucking, splashing noise as when walking on muddy ground.

examples.text: The mud squelched underfoot; it had been raining all night.

origin.ko: 어원은 알려져 있지 않고, 철벅 눌러 으깨는 소리를 흉내 낸 말로 보입니다.

senses.en: people having the same social, economic, or educational status

examples.text: The policy disproportionately benefited the wealthiest stratum of society.

senses.en: One of several parallel horizontal layers of material arranged one on top of another.

examples.text: It is built of alternate strata of brick and clay, and the sides correspond to the direction of the meridians and parallels.

origin.ko: 라틴어 strātum(펼쳐 놓은 것, 이불)에서 왔습니다. 켜켜이 깔린 층에서 사회 계층이라는 뜻이 되었습니다.

senses.en: An indirect or deceptive device or stratagem; a blind. Refers especially to war and diplomatics.

examples.text: How’s the spy hunt going? Uncovered any subterfuge?

origin.ko: 라틴어 subterfugere(몰래 달아나다)에서 왔습니다. 책임을 슬쩍 피하는 핑계와 속임수입니다.

senses.en: take the place or move into the position of

examples.text: Those older products have been superseded by our new range.

origin.ko: 라틴어 supersedēre(위에 앉다)에서 왔습니다. 남의 자리 위에 앉아 대신한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: the relation between two different species of organisms that are interdependent; each gains benefits from the other

examples.text: Bees and flowers display symbiosis. The bees get nectar and the flowers get pollinated.

senses.en: The state of people of different types, races, cultures, communities, etc., living together.

examples.text: The newspaper and the city's politicians lived in an uneasy symbiosis, each needing the other.

origin.ko: 그리스어 symbiōsis(함께 삶)에서 왔습니다. 서로 의지하며 함께 사는 공생입니다.

senses.en: brief and to the point; effectively cut short

examples.text: The memo was terse, listing three decisions and the names of those responsible for each.

senses.en: Of manner or speech: abruptly or brusquely short; curt.

examples.text: His terse reply, a single word, made it clear that the conversation was over.

origin.ko: 라틴어 tersus('깨끗이 닦인')에서 왔습니다. 군더더기를 닦아낸 듯 깔끔한 표현이 '간결한'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: not worth considering

examples.text: The company dismissed the complaint as a trifling matter, but the regulators saw a pattern.

senses.en: Frivolous.

examples.text: The headmaster scolded the boys for their trifling attitude toward the serious examination.

origin.ko: trifle('하찮은 것')에 -ing를 붙인 말입니다. 대수롭지 않은 '사소한' 것을 뜻합니다.

senses.en: beyond doubt or reproach
senses.ko: 의심할 여지 없는, 흠잡을 데 없는

examples.text: an unimpeachable source

senses.en: Unfavourable, adverse, or disadvantageous.

examples.text: No untoward effects were reported; however, this was not a blinded or controlled study.

senses.en: not in keeping with accepted standards of what is right or proper in polite society

examples.text: Auditors found nothing untoward in the accounts, though they continued to review them carefully.

origin.ko: un-과 toward의 결합입니다. '순조롭게 향하지 않는' 데서 '불리한'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: Abundant in verdure; lush with vegetation.

examples.text: A serene sky and verdant fields filled me with ecstasy.

senses.en: Inexperienced.

examples.text: The verdant recruit made every mistake a rookie could make during his first week on the job.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 vert('초록')에서 나온 verdoier에서 왔고 라틴어 viridis와 이어집니다.

senses.en: a healthy capacity for vigorous activity

examples.text: The coach was amazed by the vim of the new recruits during the first morning drill.

origin.ko: 라틴어 vīs('힘')의 대격 vim에서 왔다는 설이 있습니다. 확실하지는 않습니다.

senses.en: Full of longing or yearning.

examples.text: His eyes grew wistful as he recalled his university days.

origin.ko: whist('조용한')에 -ful을 붙인 말로 추정합니다. 말없이 그리워하는 모습입니다.

senses.en: to stress, single out as important

examples.text: The report accentuates the need for stronger oversight of the banking sector.

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 accentuare에서 왔으며 accent(악센트)에서 나왔습니다. 소리를 두드러지게 하는 데서 '강조하다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: an increase by natural growth or addition

examples.text: The delta formed through the slow accretion of silt carried down the river over millennia.

origin.ko: 라틴어 accrescere(더해져 자라다)에서 왔습니다. 조금씩 덧붙어 커지는 현상을 뜻합니다.

senses.en: the lofty nest of a bird of prey (such as a hawk or eagle)

examples.text: An eagle's aerie clung to the cliff face, far beyond the reach of any climber.

senses.en: any habitation at a high altitude

examples.text: From her mountaintop aerie, the novelist looked down on the village lights each evening.

senses.en: diffusing warmth and friendliness

examples.text: The amiable innkeeper chatted with every traveler and remembered each regular's favorite dish.

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 amicabilis(우호적인)에서 왔고 amicus(친구)에서 나왔습니다. 친구처럼 다정한 사람입니다.

senses.en: a person who argues to defend or justify some policy or institution

examples.text: The senator was widely criticized as an apologist for the industry he was supposed to regulate.

origin.ko: 그리스어 apologia(변론)에서 왔습니다. 말로 변호하는 사람입니다.

senses.en: to declare or affirm solemnly and formally as true

examples.text: The defendant continued to aver that he had never seen the document before the trial.

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 advērare에서 왔고 라틴어 verus(참된)에서 나왔습니다. 참이라고 확언한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: doing or producing good

examples.text: The beneficent donor quietly funded scholarships for hundreds of students in the region.

origin.ko: 라틴어 bene(잘)와 facere(하다)에서 온 말입니다. 좋은 일을 하는 사람이라는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: lacking enlightenment or knowledge or culture

examples.text: The reformer regarded the village's superstitions as the habits of a benighted and fearful age.

origin.ko: benight(밤이 덮치다)에 -ed가 붙은 말입니다. 어둠에 덮여 앞이 안 보이는 데서 '무지몽매한'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: Deprived of, stripped of, robbed of.

examples.text: The proposal was bereft of any evidence, and the committee rejected it within minutes.

senses.en: Pained by the loss of someone.

examples.text: I was utterly bereft in the months following my wife's death.

origin.ko: 중세 영어 bireven(빼앗다)의 과거분사에서 왔습니다. 소중한 것을 빼앗긴 상태입니다.

senses.en: anger or take offense

examples.text: She bridled at his suggestion to elope

senses.en: To check, restrain, or control with, or as if with, a bridle; as in bridle your tongue.

examples.text: The new law was meant to bridle the power of the largest banks.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 brīdel('고삐')에서 왔습니다. braid(엮다)에 -le가 붙은, 엮은 끈이라는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: emotionally purging

examples.text: Writing the letter, though she never mailed it, proved a cathartic way to process her grief.

origin.ko: 그리스어 kathartikos('깨끗이 하는')에서 왔습니다. 마음속 감정을 씻어 내는 정화입니다.

senses.en: A supply or store of money, often belonging to an organization.

examples.text: The new tax was intended to replenish the depleted coffers of the municipal government.

senses.en: a chest especially for storing valuables

examples.text: The merchant locked the gold coins in an iron coffer beneath his bed.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 cofre('상자')에서 왔고, 그리스어 kophinos(바구니)까지 거슬러 갑니다. coffin과 같은 어원입니다.

senses.en: to feel or express sympathy or compassion

examples.text: Colleagues gathered to commiserate with her after the grant proposal was rejected.

origin.ko: 라틴어 commiseror에서 왔고, '함께 불쌍히 여기다'는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: intended to placate

examples.text: The minister struck a conciliatory tone in her address to the striking workers.

senses.en: come up with (an idea, plan, explanation, theory, or principle) after a mental effort

examples.text: The engineers contrived a clever system for recycling water on the remote research station.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 controver에서 왔고 trover('찾다')에서 갈라졌습니다. 방법을 찾아내 고안한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: wish, long, or crave for (something, especially the property of another person)

examples.text: Rival museums coveted the rare manuscript and made repeated offers to its owner.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 covoitier(욕망)에서 왔으며 라틴어 cupiditas(강한 욕망)와 관련됩니다.

senses.en: Sad because of a disappointment.

examples.text: The crestfallen candidate watched the returns come in and knew the election was lost.

origin.ko: crest(볏, 머리장식)와 fallen의 합성어입니다. 패배한 말이 목을 떨구거나 수탉이 볏을 늘어뜨린 모습에서 '풀 죽은'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: pass on or delegate to another

examples.text: Many legislative powers devolved to the new Scottish parliament in 1999.

senses.en: grow progressively worse

examples.text: A discussion about politics may devolve into a shouting match.

senses.en: be inherited by

examples.text: On the earl's death, the estate devolved upon his nephew, who sold the land within a year.

origin.ko: 라틴어 dēvolvō(굴려 내리다)에서 왔습니다. 책임이 아래로 굴러 내려가는 데서 '이양하다'입니다.

senses.en: characteristic of or peculiar to a woman

examples.text: They inherit Plantagenet blood by direct descent, and Tudor on the distaff side.

senses.en: the sphere of work by women

examples.text: Historians once treated the distaff as a footnote, though women's labor sustained the household economy.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 distæf에서 왔고 '아마 다발'과 stæf(막대)의 합성입니다. 실 잣는 일이 여자의 몫이라 '여성의'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: A dummy or other crude representation of a person, group or object that is hated.

examples.text: Protesters burned an effigy of the minister outside the parliament building.

senses.en: a representation of a person (especially in the form of sculpture)

examples.text: the coin bears an effigy of Lincoln

origin.ko: 라틴어 effigiēs(초상, 형상)에서 왔고 effingō(본떠 만들다)가 뿌리입니다.

senses.en: escape, either physically or mentally

examples.text: The thief eluded the police

senses.en: be incomprehensible to; escape understanding by

examples.text: I get algebra, but calculus eludes me.

origin.ko: 라틴어 ēlūdere(놀리며 빠져나가다)에서 왔습니다. 상대를 속이며 슬쩍 벗어나는 이미지입니다.

senses.en: give instructions to or direct somebody to do something with authority

examples.text: The charter enjoins every member to attend the annual assembly.

senses.en: To prohibit or restrain by a judicial order or decree; to put an injunction on.

examples.text: The court enjoined the company from selling the disputed product pending trial.

origin.ko: 라틴어 iniungere(붙이다, 부과하다)에서 왔습니다. 의무를 덧붙여 지운다는 데서 '명령하다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: To urge; to advise earnestly.

examples.text: The coach exhorted his exhausted players to give everything they had in the final quarter.

origin.ko: 라틴어 exhortārī(격려하다)에서 왔습니다. 곁에서 힘껏 부추겨 행동을 권한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: Affording short-term benefit, often at the expense of the long-term.

examples.text: The council chose the expedient solution of borrowing more money rather than reforming the budget.

senses.en: Suitable to effect some desired end or the purpose intended.

examples.text: Most people, faced with a decision, will choose the most expedient option.

senses.en: a means to an end; not necessarily a principled or ethical one

examples.text: Critics called the tax cut a political expedient designed to win votes before the election.

origin.ko: 라틴어 expedīre(발을 풀어 앞으로 내보내다)에서 왔습니다. 거치적거림이 없어 당장 유리하다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: dependent upon or characterized by chance

examples.text: The library's haphazard arrangement of books made finding any particular title a matter of luck.

senses.en: marked by great carelessness

examples.text: a most haphazard system of record keeping

origin.ko: 옛말 hap(우연, 운)과 hazard(우연, 위험)가 합쳐진 말입니다. 우연에 맡긴다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: based on or having the nature of an illusion

examples.text: The apparent stability of the market proved illusory once the banks began to fail.

origin.ko: 라틴어 illūsōrius '조롱하는'에서 왔습니다. 눈을 속여 놀리는 듯한 착각이라는 뜻으로 이어졌습니다.

senses.en: happening by chance or unexpectedly or unintentionally

examples.text: We check everything because an inadvertent error could be disastrous.

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 inadvertēns에서 왔습니다. 마음을 그쪽으로 돌리지(advert) 않은 채 하는 행동이 '무심코 한'입니다.

senses.en: having or demonstrating ability to recognize or draw fine distinctions

examples.text: The critic's incisive analysis exposed the flaw at the heart of the policy within a single paragraph.

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 incīsīvus '자르는'에서 왔고 incīdō(안으로 베다)가 뿌리입니다. 칼처럼 깊이 베어 들어가는 날카로운 통찰입니다.

senses.en: (of weather or climate) severe

examples.text: The marathon was postponed because of inclement weather that made the course dangerously slick.

senses.en: used of persons or behavior; showing no clemency or mercy

examples.text: The inclement judge handed down the harshest sentence the law allowed.

origin.ko: 라틴어 inclēmēns '인정사정없는, 거친'에서 왔습니다. clēmēns(온화한)에 부정 접두사가 붙어 궂은 날씨를 뜻하게 되었습니다.

senses.en: characterized by hard work and perseverance

examples.text: He was a very industrious student at school.

origin.ko: 라틴어 industria '부지런함'에서 후기 라틴어 industriōsus와 프랑스어를 거쳐 왔습니다.

senses.en: the time between two reigns, governments, etc.

examples.text: Several rival nobles competed for power during the long interregnum that followed the king's sudden death.

origin.ko: 라틴어 interrēgnum에서 왔습니다. 두 왕(reign) 사이의 공백기라는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: A set of moral norms or customs derived from generally accepted practices rather than written laws.

examples.text: The country's traditional mores have sparked recent ideological battles, as well as a few national embarrassments.

origin.ko: 라틴어 mōrēs '방식, 성품, 도덕'의 복수형입니다. 한 사회가 따르는 관습과 도덕 규범을 뜻합니다.

senses.en: Arousing or meriting strong dislike, aversion, or intense displeasure.

examples.text: Critics found the regime's treatment of dissidents odious and called for sanctions.

origin.ko: 라틴어 odiōsus '미움을 사는'에서 왔고, odium은 '증오'입니다.

senses.en: engagingly stimulating or provocative

examples.text: a piquant wit

senses.en: having an agreeably pungent taste

examples.text: The chef served the fish with a piquant sauce of capers and lemon.

origin.ko: 중세 프랑스어 piquant '찌르는 듯한'에서 왔습니다. 혀나 마음을 톡 쏘듯 자극하는 맛과 흥미를 뜻합니다.

senses.en: capable of being bent or flexed or twisted without breaking

examples.text: a pliant young tree

senses.en: Easily influenced; tractable.

examples.text: The pliant committee approved every proposal the chairman put before it.

origin.ko: 옛 프랑스어 ploiant '구부러지는'에서 왔고, ploiier는 '접다'입니다.

senses.en: Shrewd, prudent and expedient; showing policy.

examples.text: It would be politic to postpone the announcement until after the negotiations conclude.

senses.en: Discreet and diplomatic.

examples.text: Her politic reply avoided offending either faction in the dispute.

origin.ko: 그리스어 politēs('시민')에서 나온 politikos('시민의')가 어원입니다. 시민 사회에서 요령 있게 처신하는 데서 '현명한'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: a member of the working class (not necessarily employed)

examples.text: Marx predicted that the proletarian would eventually overthrow the capitalist order.

senses.en: belonging to or characteristic of the proletariat

examples.text: The writer cultivated a proletarian image despite his comfortable upbringing.

origin.ko: 라틴어 proletarius에서 왔고 proles('자손')와 관련됩니다. 자식 말고는 재산이 없는 가난한 시민을 가리키던 말입니다.

senses.en: reflect deeply on a subject

examples.text: She would ruminate for days over a single decision, weighing every possible consequence.

senses.en: chew the cuds

examples.text: cows ruminate

origin.ko: 라틴어 rūminor(되새김질하다)에서 왔습니다. 소가 되새김하듯 생각을 되씹는 이미지입니다.

senses.en: A sudden increase or rush of something; a flood, an outburst, an outpouring.

examples.text: A spate of resignations followed the announcement of the merger.

senses.en: the occurrence of a water flow resulting from sudden rain or melting snow

examples.text: The river rose in a spate after three days of heavy rain in the hills.

origin.ko: 중세 영어 spate(홍수)에서 왔습니다. 갑자기 불어난 물이 쇄도하는 이미지입니다.

senses.en: specify as a condition or requirement in a contract or agreement; make an express demand or provision in an agreement

examples.text: The contract stipulates the dates of the payments

senses.en: To acknowledge the truth of; not to challenge.

examples.text: The defense stipulates that the witness has identified my client.

origin.ko: 라틴어 stipulor(정식 약속을 요구하다)에서 왔습니다. 계약에 조건을 못 박는다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: establish or strengthen as with new evidence or facts

examples.text: The investigators could not substantiate the allegations with any documentary evidence.

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 substantiare(실체를 주다)에서 왔습니다. 증거로 실체를 부여해 입증한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: (of liquids) clouded as with sediment

examples.text: Spring floods left the river turbid, so that nothing below the surface could be seen.

senses.en: Unclear; confused; obscure.

examples.text: Those turbid emotions swirled inside him again—part frustration, part anxiety.

origin.ko: 라틴어 turbidus('휘저어진')에서 왔고 turba('소란, 군중')와 이어집니다. 휘저어 흐려진 물이 '탁한'입니다.

senses.en: To progressively lose its splendor, value, ardor, power, intensity etc.; to decline.

examples.text: Public enthusiasm for the project began to wane once the costs became clear.

senses.en: decrease in phase

examples.text: The moon is waning, so the nights will grow darker this week.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 wanian('줄어들다')에서 왔고 '부족, 결핍'을 뜻하는 말과 이어집니다. 달이 이지러지는 모습이 '쇠퇴하다'입니다.

senses.en: being up to particular standard or level especially in being up to date in knowledge

examples.text: Good journalists keep abreast of developments in the fields they cover.

origin.ko: a-(~에)와 breast(가슴)가 합쳐진 말입니다. 가슴을 나란히 맞춘 모습에서 '뒤처지지 않고 나란히 알고 있는'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: revoke formally

examples.text: The government threatened to abrogate the treaty if its neighbor continued to violate the border agreement.

origin.ko: 라틴어 abrogare(법안을 철회하다)에서 왔습니다. 제안된 법을 물리쳐 '폐지하다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: run away; usually includes taking something or somebody along

examples.text: The treasurer absconded with the club's savings, leaving members unable to pay the rent.

origin.ko: 라틴어 abscondere(숨기다)에서 왔습니다. 멀리 가서 몸을 숨기는 데서 '몰래 달아나다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: Extremely bad; terrible.

examples.text: The team's abysmal performance in the second half cost it the championship.

senses.en: resembling an abyss in depth; so deep as to be unmeasurable

examples.text: Explorers peered into the abysmal darkness of the trench, unable to see where it ended.

origin.ko: abysm(심연)에 -al이 붙은 말입니다. 바닥 모를 심연처럼 한없이 나쁘다는 뜻이 되었습니다.

senses.en: being of striking appropriateness and pertinence

examples.text: the successful copywriter is a master of apposite and evocative verbal images

origin.ko: 라틴어 appositus(곁에 놓인)에서 왔습니다. 딱 알맞은 자리에 놓였다는 데서 '적절한'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: give or assign a resource to a particular person or cause

examples.text: Congress appropriated additional funds for rural broadband expansion.

senses.en: To take to oneself; to claim or use, especially as by an exclusive right.

examples.text: Critics accused the designer of appropriating motifs from indigenous artists without credit.

senses.en: suitable for a particular person or place or condition etc

examples.text: a book not appropriate for children

origin.ko: 라틴어 appropriare(자기 것으로 만들다)에서 왔습니다. 몫으로 따로 배정한다는 뜻이 되었습니다.

senses.en: the state that exists when one person or group has power over another

examples.text: The Tory hard right is in the ascendancy, and a fascist street movement – led by convicted fraudster Tommy Robinson – represents a growing threat.

origin.ko: ascend(오르다)에서 나왔습니다. 남보다 위로 올라서 있는 상태가 '우위'입니다.

senses.en: with suspicion or disapproval

examples.text: he looked askance at the offer

senses.en: with a side or oblique glance

examples.text: I glanced askance at this strange creature, and found him watching me with his queer, restless eyes.

senses.en: threatening or foreshadowing evil or tragic developments

examples.text: a baleful look

senses.en: deadly or sinister

examples.text: The baleful influence of the corrupt administration lingered long after its fall.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 bealuful에서 왔고 bale(재앙)에 -ful(가득한)이 붙은 말입니다. 재앙이 가득한 듯 불길하다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: not adhering to ethical or moral principles

examples.text: base and unpatriotic motives

senses.en: (used of metals) consisting of or alloyed with inferior metal

examples.text: a base metal

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 bas(낮은)에서 왔고 후기 라틴어 bassus(낮은)에서 나왔습니다. 지위나 도덕이 낮다는 데서 '비열한'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: cheat somebody out of what is due, especially money

examples.text: The contractor bilked dozens of homeowners out of their deposits and then vanished.

senses.en: hinder or prevent (the efforts, plans, or desires) of

examples.text: A sudden injury bilked the sprinter of her chance to defend her title.

origin.ko: 기원이 불확실하며 balk의 변형일 수 있다고 합니다.

senses.en: a crude uncouth ill-bred person lacking culture or refinement

examples.text: The boor interrupted the speaker twice and then loudly answered his phone during the toast.

origin.ko: 네덜란드어 boer('농부')를 빌려 온 말입니다. 농사꾼을 투박한 사람으로 깔보던 데서 '무례한 사람'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: All-embracing.

examples.text: Her catholic taste in music ranged from medieval chants to modern jazz and folk songs.

origin.ko: 그리스어 katholikos('보편적인')에서 왔고, kata(~에 걸쳐)와 holos(전체)가 합쳐졌습니다. 전체를 아우른다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: relinquish possession or control over

examples.text: Edward decided to cede the province.

senses.en: To give way.

examples.text: The senator refused to cede the floor until she had finished presenting her argument.

origin.ko: 라틴어 cēdō('양보하다, 물러나다')에서 왔습니다. 한 발 물러서 넘겨준다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: marked by changeable fortune

examples.text: The former mayor had a checkered career, marked by early triumphs, a corruption scandal, and a late comeback.

senses.en: patterned with alternating squares of color

examples.text: That is a checkered tablecloth.

origin.ko: 체스판(chequer)에서 온 말입니다. 격자무늬처럼 밝고 어두운 칸이 번갈아 나타나듯 기복이 많다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: an expert able to appreciate a field; especially in the fine arts

examples.text: As a connoisseur of early jazz, he owned thousands of rare recordings.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 connoisseur에서 왔고 connoître('알다')에서 갈라졌습니다. 1700년대 초에 영어로 들어왔습니다.

senses.en: excessively fat

examples.text: The corpulent innkeeper wheezed as he climbed the narrow stairs with our luggage.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 corpulent를 거친 라틴어 corpulentus(몸집이 큰)에서 왔습니다. corpus(몸)가 뿌리입니다.

senses.en: consent to, give permission; permit

examples.text: The university will not countenance any form of plagiarism among its students.

senses.en: the appearance conveyed by a person's face

examples.text: Her calm countenance gave no hint of the anxiety she felt before the verdict.

origin.ko: 앵글로노르만어 countenance에서 왔고, contenir(함께 지니다)와 후기 라틴어 continentia에서 갈라졌습니다. 표정을 받아들이듯 허용한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: hasty and without attention to detail; not thorough

examples.text: A cursory view of the report revealed his egregious errors.

origin.ko: 라틴어 cursorius(달리기의, 급한)에서 왔습니다. 달리듯 훑어보니 '대충 하는'입니다.

senses.en: skillful in physical movements; especially of the hands

examples.text: With a few deft strokes of the brush, the artist captured the old man's weary expression.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 dæfte(온화한, 알맞은)에서 왔습니다. '적절한'에서 '솜씨 좋은'으로 의미가 이동했습니다.

senses.en: act nervously; be undecided; be uncertain

examples.text: While the committee dithered over the budget, the deadline for funding quietly passed.

senses.en: an excited state of agitation

examples.text: he was in a dither

origin.ko: 중세 영어 dideren(떨다)에서 온 didder의 변형입니다. 떨듯 우물쭈물한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: make known to the public information that was previously known only to a few people or that was meant to be kept a secret

examples.text: I will never divulge that secret to anyone.

origin.ko: 라틴어 dīvulgō(널리 알리다)에서 왔고 vulgus(대중)가 뿌리입니다.

senses.en: willing to be taught or led or supervised or directed

examples.text: the docile masses of an enslaved nation

origin.ko: 라틴어 docilis(가르치기 쉬운)에서 왔고 docēre(가르치다)가 뿌리입니다.

senses.en: A level or rank in an organization, profession, or society.

examples.text: Few women had reached the upper echelons of the company before the reforms of the 1990s.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 échelon(사다리 가로대)에서 왔고 échelle(사다리)에 축소 접미사가 붙었습니다. 사다리 단에서 '등급'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: straying from the right course or from accepted standards

examples.text: The coach disciplined the errant player for missing practice twice in one week.

senses.en: Roving around; wandering.

examples.text: The errant knight traveled from kingdom to kingdom seeking adventure.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 errer(떠돌다)의 현재분사에서 왔습니다. 길을 벗어나 방황하는 모습입니다.

senses.en: belonging to some prior time

examples.text: erstwhile friend

origin.ko: 옛 영어 erst(이전에)와 while(동안)이 합쳐졌습니다. '예전 한때의'라는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: One who expounds, represents or advocates.

examples.text: She was a leading exponent of free trade throughout her long political career.

senses.en: a mathematical notation indicating the number of times a quantity is multiplied by itself

examples.text: In the expression five cubed, the exponent tells you to multiply five by itself three times.

origin.ko: 라틴어 expōnere(밖에 내놓다, 설명하다)에서 왔습니다. 주장을 밖에 내세워 설명하는 사람입니다.

senses.en: To edit out (incorrect, offensive, or otherwise undesirable information) from a book or other publication; to cleanse; to purge.

examples.text: The publisher decided to expurgate the love scene from the book, to make it more child-friendly.

origin.ko: 라틴어 expurgāre(깨끗이 씻어 내다)에서 왔습니다. 글에서 불온한 부분을 씻어 낸다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: droop, sink, or settle from or as if from pressure or loss of tautness

examples.text: As the marathon dragged on, the runners' enthusiasm began to flag in the afternoon heat.

senses.en: become less intense

examples.text: Public interest in the reform plan flagged once the initial controversy faded from the headlines.

senses.en: emblem usually consisting of a rectangular piece of cloth of distinctive design

examples.text: The flag of France has three vertical stripes.

senses.en: cross a river where it's shallow

examples.text: The pioneers forded the swollen creek with their wagons, losing only a few barrels.

senses.en: a shallow area in a stream that can be forded

examples.text: The old road led down to a ford where travelers could cross without a bridge.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 ford(얕은 건널목)에서 왔습니다. 강을 걸어서 건너는 얕은 곳입니다.

senses.en: To abandon, to give up, to leave (permanently), to renounce (someone or something).

examples.text: He forsook a lucrative career in banking to devote his life to teaching.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 forsacan(거부하다, 포기하다)에서 왔습니다. 완전히 등을 돌려 버린다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: unnecessary and unwarranted

examples.text: Critics complained that the film's gratuitous violence added nothing to the story.

senses.en: Given freely; unearned.

examples.text: The hotel offered gratuitous breakfast to guests who had endured the delayed check-in.

origin.ko: 라틴어 grātuītus '공짜의'에서 왔고 grātia(호의)가 뿌리입니다. 대가나 이유 없이 주어진다는 데서 '정당한 이유 없는'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: overbearing pride or presumption

examples.text: Antitrust prosecutors target big companies that exude hubris.

origin.ko: 그리스어 hýbris '오만, 방자함'에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: extravagant exaggeration

examples.text: Calling the mild drizzle a deluge was pure hyperbole, but the audience laughed all the same.

origin.ko: 그리스어 hyperbolḗ '지나침, 과장'에서 왔습니다. hypér(넘어서)와 bállō(던지다)가 합쳐져 표적 너머로 던진다는 이미지입니다.

senses.en: lock up or confine, in or as in a jail

examples.text: The recluse immured himself in his study for weeks, refusing all visitors and correspondence.

origin.ko: 라틴어 immūrō에서 왔습니다. in(안에)과 mūrus(벽)가 합쳐져 벽 안에 가둔다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: make worse or less effective

examples.text: Chronic sleep deprivation can seriously impair memory and the ability to concentrate on complex tasks.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 empeirier에서 왔고 후기 라틴어 peiōrāre(악화시키다)가 뿌리입니다. 더 나쁘게 만든다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: lacking piety or reverence for a god

examples.text: The preacher denounced the impious crowd for laughing during the solemn funeral service.

origin.ko: 라틴어 impius '경건하지 않은'에서 왔습니다. pius(경건한)에 부정 접두사가 붙은 말입니다.

senses.en: lacking worth or importance

examples.text: The error was inconsequential and had no effect on the final results of the experiment.

senses.en: not following logically as a consequence
senses.ko: 논리적 귀결이 아닌, 앞뒤가 맞지 않는

examples.text: His conclusion was inconsequential, since it did not follow from any of the premises he had listed.

origin.ko: consequential(결과가 따르는, 중요한)에 부정 접두사가 붙은 말입니다. 따라오는 결과가 없을 만큼 하찮다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: not tractable; difficult to manage or mold

examples.text: The intractable mule refused to move, no matter how hard the farmer pulled on the rope.

senses.en: Difficult to deal with, solve, or manage. (of a problem)

examples.text: Decades of negotiation failed to resolve the intractable conflict over the disputed border region.

origin.ko: in-(아닌)과 tractable(끌어 다룰 수 있는)이 합쳐졌습니다. 끌어당겨 다룰 수 없을 만큼 고집이 셉니다.

senses.en: lacking moral discipline; especially sexually unrestrained

examples.text: Moralists condemned the licentious behavior of the court as a sign of national decay.

senses.en: Disregarding accepted rules.

examples.text: The licentious use of quotation in the article made the argument impossible to verify.

origin.ko: 라틴어 licentiōsus에서 왔고 licentia '허가, 자유'에서 나왔습니다. 제멋대로 허락된 듯 구는 방종입니다.

senses.en: shockingly repellent; inspiring horror

examples.text: The museum's macabre exhibit of medieval torture devices left many visitors visibly shaken.

senses.en: Obsessed with death or the gruesome.

examples.text: The novelist's macabre fascination with funerals shaped every chapter of her debut.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 danse macabre '죽음의 무도'에서 왔다고 하며, 정확한 어원은 불확실합니다.

senses.en: in the current fashion or style

examples.text: The boutique stocked only modish clothing aimed at the city's younger professionals.

origin.ko: mode(유행)에 -ish가 붙은 말입니다.

senses.en: Having great diversity or variety; of various kinds; made up of many differing parts.

examples.text: The mayor faced multifarious problems, from crumbling bridges to a shrinking tax base.

origin.ko: 라틴어 multifārius에서 왔으며, 여러 갈래로 가지각색이라는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: Unsure how to act or respond; bewildered, perplexed.

examples.text: The candidate looked nonplussed when the moderator quoted his own earlier speech back to him.

senses.en: Unaffected, unfazed; unimpressed.

examples.text: Surprisingly nonplussed by the uproar, the veteran diplomat calmly continued his remarks.

origin.ko: 라틴어 nōn plūs '더 이상 없다'에서 나온 nonplus의 과거분사형입니다. 말문이 막혀 더 나아가지 못하는 상태입니다.

senses.en: Harmful; injurious.

examples.text: Regulators ordered the plant to stop releasing noxious fumes near the residential district.

senses.en: Morally corrupting.

examples.text: Moralists condemned the pamphlet as a noxious influence on impressionable young readers.

origin.ko: 라틴어 noxius '해를 끼치는'에서 왔고, nocēre는 '해치다'입니다.

senses.en: seemingly contradictory but nonetheless possibly true

examples.text: it is paradoxical that standing is more tiring than walking

origin.ko: paradox(통념에서 벗어난 의견)에 -ical이 붙은 말입니다.

senses.en: not allowing contradiction or refusal

examples.text: spoke in peremptory tones

senses.en: offensively self-assured or given to exercising usually unwarranted power

examples.text: The new supervisor's peremptory manner quickly alienated the whole team.

origin.ko: 라틴어 peremptōrius '결정적인'에서 왔고, perimō는 '없애다'입니다. 토론의 여지를 아예 없애 버리는 단호함입니다.

senses.en: A large group of people, animals or things, compact or closely massed, or tightly knit and united in common purpose.

examples.text: A phalanx of reporters blocked the courthouse steps as the defendant arrived.

senses.en: a body of troops in close array

examples.text: The Macedonian phalanx advanced with long spears lowered.

origin.ko: 그리스어 phálanx '전투 대형'에서 왔습니다. 방패를 맞대고 빽빽이 선 대열을 가리킵니다.

senses.en: a sketchy summary of the main points of an argument or theory

examples.text: Each student submitted a one-page precis of the article before the seminar began.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 précis('간결한')에서 온 말입니다. 군더더기를 잘라 낸 요약문을 뜻합니다.

senses.en: the power to foresee the future

examples.text: Her essay showed remarkable prescience about the effects of social media on public debate.

origin.ko: 라틴어 praescientia('미리 앎')에서 왔습니다. 일이 벌어지기 전에 아는 능력입니다.

senses.en: surpassing the ordinary or normal

examples.text: The old sailor had a preternatural ability to sense a storm hours before it arrived.

origin.ko: 라틴어 praeter nātūram('자연을 넘어서')에서 왔습니다. 보통 자연의 범위를 넘는 이상함입니다.

senses.en: The state or condition of being prime or first, as in time, place, rank, preference etc.

examples.text: The report stresses the primacy of evidence over personal opinion in policy decisions.

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 primatia에서 왔으며 prime에 -acy가 붙은 말입니다. 첫째 자리에 있는 상태입니다.

senses.en: peculiarly fortunate or appropriate; as if by divine intervention

examples.text: A providential rainstorm arrived just in time to save the withering crops.
