origin.ko: 라틴어 prōvidentia('미리 내다봄, 섭리')에 -al이 붙은 말입니다. 신의 섭리처럼 운 좋게 들어맞는다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: strong and sharp

examples.text: The pungent smell of vinegar filled the kitchen as the pickles simmered.

senses.en: capable of wounding

examples.text: The critic gave a pungent review.

origin.ko: 라틴어 pungere('찌르다')의 현재분사에서 왔습니다. 코와 혀를 찌르듯 톡 쏩니다.

senses.en: especially fine or decorative clothing

examples.text: The king appeared in ceremonial raiment embroidered with gold thread and sewn with pearls.

origin.ko: 중세 영어 arayment에서 앞소리가 떨어져 나온 말로 array('차려입히다')와 이어집니다. 잘 갖춰 입은 옷을 뜻합니다.

senses.en: one who lives in solitude

examples.text: After her husband died, the once-sociable author became a recluse and refused all interviews.

senses.en: withdrawn from society; seeking solitude

examples.text: lived an unsocial reclusive life

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 reclus('가둬진')에서 왔고 라틴어 reclūdere에서 나왔습니다. 문을 닫아걸고 홀로 사는 사람입니다.

senses.en: Offensive or repulsive; arousing disgust or aversion.

examples.text: Most citizens found the regime's treatment of prisoners morally repugnant.

senses.en: Opposed or in conflict.

examples.text: a repugnant condition

origin.ko: 라틴어 repugnāre('맞서 싸우다')의 현재분사에서 왔습니다. 마음이 맞서 싸울 만큼 불쾌하다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: a tiny or scarcely detectable amount

examples.text: a scintilla of hope

origin.ko: 라틴어 scintilla(불꽃)에서 왔습니다. 작은 불똥 같은 극소량을 뜻합니다.

senses.en: A familiar name for a person or thing; a nickname (sometimes assumed by the person, but often given by others) that is descriptive.

examples.text: “The Bard” is a sobriquet of English playwright William Shakespeare.

origin.ko: 프랑스어에서 왔고 원래 '턱 밑을 톡 치는 것'을 뜻했습니다. 가볍고 친근한 별명이 되었습니다.

senses.en: a deliberately invalid argument displaying ingenuity in reasoning in the hope of deceiving someone

examples.text: The lawyer's sophistry made a weak case sound convincing, but the judge saw through it.

origin.ko: 그리스어 sophistēs(지혜로운 사람, 소피스트)에서 왔습니다. 그럴듯하게 꾸민 궤변이라는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: dependable

examples.text: a stalwart supporter of the UN

senses.en: having rugged physical strength; inured to fatigue or hardships

examples.text: proud of her tall stalwart son

senses.en: One who firmly supports a cause.

examples.text: The party's stalwarts gathered at headquarters to defend the leader after the scandal broke.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 stǣlwierþe(제 구실을 하는, 쓸모 있는)에서 왔습니다. 굳건히 제자리를 지키는 믿음직한 사람입니다.

senses.en: To stunt, inhibit (progress, ideas, etc.) or make dull and uninteresting, especially through routine that is overly restrictive or limiting.

examples.text: Bureaucracy and over-regulation have stultified the economy.

senses.en: cause to appear foolish

examples.text: He stultified himself by contradicting himself and being inconsistent

origin.ko: 라틴어 stultus(어리석은)에 -ify가 붙었습니다. 어리석고 둔하게 만든다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: being essentially equal to something

examples.text: his statement was tantamount to an admission of guilt

origin.ko: 이탈리아어 tanto montare(그만큼에 이르다)에서 왔다고 봅니다. 그만큼의 값에 해당해 마찬가지라는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: To compromise, damage, soil, or sully.

examples.text: He is afraid that she will tarnish his reputation if he disagrees with her.

senses.en: To oxidize or discolor due to oxidation.

examples.text: Careful storage of silver will prevent it from tarnishing.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 ternir(흐리게 하다)에서 왔습니다. 광택이 흐려져 얼룩진다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: a person who tries to please someone in order to gain a personal advantage

examples.text: The senator was surrounded by toadies who laughed at every joke and never questioned his policies.

senses.en: try to gain favor by cringing or flattering

examples.text: Ambitious aides toady to the director, laughing at his jokes and echoing every opinion he offers.

origin.ko: toadeater('두꺼비 먹는 사람')를 줄인 말입니다. 비위를 맞추려 역겨운 것도 삼키는 사람의 이미지입니다.

senses.en: the act of transgressing; the violation of a law or a duty or moral principle

examples.text: The council punished even minor transgressions of the code of conduct with public censure.

senses.en: the action of going beyond or overstepping some boundary or limit

examples.text: Every transgression of the border was recorded and reported to the regional commander.

origin.ko: 라틴어 trānsgredior('건너가다')에서 왔습니다. 선을 넘어가는 행위가 '위반, 죄'입니다.

senses.en: lying beyond what is openly revealed or avowed (especially being kept in the background or deliberately concealed)

examples.text: Her generous offer made him suspect an ulterior motive, perhaps a bid to win his vote.

senses.en: beyond or outside an area of immediate interest; remote

examples.text: The committee confined itself to the immediate question and set aside every ulterior issue.

origin.ko: 라틴어 ulterior('더 먼 쪽의')에서 왔습니다. 겉 너머 저편에 숨은 속셈을 뜻합니다.

senses.en: admitting of no doubt or misunderstanding; having only one meaning or interpretation and leading to only one conclusion

examples.text: The ministry issued an unequivocal denial, leaving no room for speculation about its involvement.

origin.ko: '똑같이 불릴 수 있는' 두 뜻이 아니라 하나뿐이라는 말입니다. 그래서 '명백한'입니다.

senses.en: cause annoyance in; disturb, especially by minor irritations

examples.text: Billy's professor was vexed by his continued failure to improve his grades.

senses.en: be a mystery or bewildering to

examples.text: The question of how the manuscript vanished has vexed historians for more than a century.

origin.ko: 라틴어 vexāre('흔들다, 괴롭히다')에서 왔습니다. 마음을 뒤흔드는 짜증을 뜻합니다.

senses.en: someone who is dazzlingly skilled in any field

examples.text: The young violinist was hailed as a virtuoso after her flawless debut at the concert hall.

senses.en: having or revealing supreme mastery or skill

examples.text: The pianist gave a virtuoso performance that left even the critics speechless.

origin.ko: 이탈리아어 virtuoso('뛰어난')에서 왔고 라틴어 virtus('탁월함')와 이어집니다. 기량이 탁월한 사람이 '거장'입니다.

senses.en: extremely poisonous or injurious; producing venom

examples.text: A virulent strain of the fungus wiped out most of the region's banana crop.

senses.en: Extremely hostile or malicious; intensely acrimonious.

examples.text: The politicians were virulent in their hatred of the president.

origin.ko: 라틴어 vīrulentus('독이 있는')에서 왔고 vīrus('독')와 이어집니다.

senses.en: abusive or venomous language used to express blame or censure or bitter deep-seated ill will

examples.text: The online comments section was filled with vitriol directed at anyone who disagreed with the author.

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 vitriolum('황산')에서 왔고 vitrum('유리')과 이어집니다. 유리처럼 반짝이는 부식성 물질에서 '독설'로 비유되었습니다.

senses.en: To attack (someone or something) with abusive language; to revile, to vilify.

examples.text: The editorial continued to vituperate the minister for weeks, calling him a coward and a fraud.

origin.ko: 라틴어 vituperō('꾸짖다')에서 왔고 vitium('흠')과 이어집니다. 흠을 들춰 비난하는 것입니다.

senses.en: a slight wind (usually refreshing)

examples.text: A cool zephyr drifted off the lake and rustled the pages on the porch table.

origin.ko: 그리스어 Zéphuros('서풍')에서 라틴어를 거쳐 왔습니다. 서쪽에서 불어오는 부드러운 바람이 '산들바람'입니다.

senses.en: arouse hostility or indifference in where there had formerly been love, affection, or friendliness

examples.text: The senator's blunt remarks alienated many longtime supporters who had once defended him.

senses.en: transfer property or ownership

examples.text: Under the old law, the heir could not alienate the estate without the consent of the family.

origin.ko: 라틴어 alienare(남으로 만들다)에서 왔습니다. 가까운 사이를 남처럼 멀어지게 한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: Either physically or emotionally remote: distant, standoffish.

examples.text: The professor remained aloof from campus politics, rarely attending meetings or voicing an opinion.

origin.ko: 뱃사람 용어로 '바람 불어오는 쪽으로 뱃머리를 돌려 멀리 피하라'는 명령에서 왔습니다. 그래서 '거리를 두는'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: characterized by friendship and good will

examples.text: The partners reached an amicable settlement and avoided a long and costly trial.

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 amicabilis(우호적인)에서 왔고 amicus(친구)에서 나왔습니다. 친구 사이 같은 원만함입니다.

senses.en: An original model of which all other similar concepts, objects, or persons are merely copied, derivative, emulated, or patterned.

examples.text: Critics often cite Hamlet as the archetype of the indecisive, brooding hero.

senses.en: An ideal example of something; a quintessence.

examples.text: She was the archetype of the self-made entrepreneur.

origin.ko: 그리스어 arkhetypon(처음 찍어낸 틀)에서 왔습니다. 모든 복제의 원본이 '원형'입니다.

senses.en: Blessed, blissful, heavenly.

examples.text: The monk wore a beatific expression as he listened to the choir fill the ancient cathedral.

senses.en: marked by utter benignity; resembling or befitting an angel or saint

examples.text: A beatific smile spread across her face when she saw her grandchildren at the door.

origin.ko: 라틴어 beatificus(행복하게 만드는)에서 왔습니다. beatus(복된)와 facere(만들다)가 합쳐진 말입니다.

senses.en: To deceive or delude (using guile).

examples.text: The swindler beguiled retirees into investing their savings in a company that did not exist.

senses.en: To charm, delight or captivate.

examples.text: The storyteller beguiled the children with tales of dragons and hidden treasure.

origin.ko: 중세 영어 begilen에서 왔고 be-와 guile(꾀)이 합쳐진 말입니다. 꾀로 홀려 속인다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: Aggressively hostile, eager to fight.

examples.text: The belligerent customer shouted at the staff and refused to leave until he got a refund.

senses.en: engaged in war

examples.text: The council urged the belligerent nations to open talks before the conflict spread further.

origin.ko: 라틴어 belligerans(전쟁을 수행하는)에서 왔습니다. bellum(전쟁)과 gerere(수행하다)가 합쳐진 말입니다.

senses.en: Peevishly ill-humored, irritable or bad tempered; irascible.

examples.text: The bilious critic dismissed the entire exhibition in a single sneering paragraph.

senses.en: suffering from or suggesting a liver disorder or gastric distress

examples.text: After the heavy banquet he felt bilious and retired early to his room.

origin.ko: 라틴어 bīliōsus('담즙이 가득한')에서 왔습니다. 담즙이 넘치면 성미가 까칠해진다고 보았습니다.

senses.en: a clique (often secret) that seeks power usually through intrigue

examples.text: A cabal of senior officials quietly worked to remove the director before the audit became public.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 cabale에서 왔고, 히브리어 qabbalah('전수받은 것', 유대 신비주의)까지 거슬러 갑니다. 소수만 아는 비밀 모임의 이미지입니다.

senses.en: having or revealing supreme mastery or skill

examples.text: a consummate artist

senses.en: make perfect; bring to perfection

examples.text: The treaty consummated years of delicate negotiation between the two rival nations.

origin.ko: 라틴어 cōnsummātus('다 합쳐 완성한')에서 왔고, summa(합계)에서 갈라졌습니다. 모든 것을 더해 끝까지 완성했다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: a difficult problem

examples.text: How to expand access without raising costs remains the central conundrum of the reform.

origin.ko: 기원 불명의 말로, 스콜라 철학식 라틴어를 흉내 낸 장난스러운 신조어에서 인기를 얻었습니다.

senses.en: characterized by propriety and dignity and good taste in manners and conduct

examples.text: The guests maintained a decorous silence throughout the long and solemn ceremony.

origin.ko: 라틴어 decōrus(어울리는, 알맞은)에서 왔고 decor(품위)가 뿌리입니다.

senses.en: so thin as to transmit light

examples.text: The bride's diaphanous veil floated in the breeze, barely hiding her face.

origin.ko: 그리스어 diaphanḗs '투과해 보이는'에서 왔습니다. 빛이 통과해 비치는 얇은 천의 이미지입니다.

senses.en: a conflict of people's opinions or actions or characters

examples.text: Cognitive dissonance exists when a person possesses two cognitions, one of which is contradictory to the other

senses.en: A harsh, discordant combination of sounds.

examples.text: The orchestra's deliberate dissonance unsettled listeners accustomed to more melodic compositions.

origin.ko: 라틴어 dissonantia에서 왔습니다. 소리가 어울리지 않는다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: stubbornly unyielding

examples.text: dogged persistence

origin.ko: dog에 -ed가 붙은 말입니다. 개처럼 끈질기게 물고 늘어진다는 이미지입니다.

senses.en: compulsory force or threat

examples.text: confessed under duress

origin.ko: 라틴어 dūritia(단단함, 가혹함)에서 왔고 dūrus(단단한)가 뿌리입니다.

senses.en: exultantly proud and joyful; in high spirits

examples.text: She was elated with her new car.

origin.ko: 라틴어 ēlātus(들어 올려진)에서 왔습니다. 마음이 위로 들떠 오른 상태가 '의기양양'입니다.

senses.en: a state of deep-seated ill-will

examples.text: Generations of enmity between the two families made any reconciliation unlikely.

origin.ko: 라틴어 inimīcus(적)에서 왔습니다. '친구(amicus)가 아닌 사람'이라는 뜻에서 적의가 되었습니다.

senses.en: a formal expression of praise for someone who has died recently

examples.text: Her son delivered a moving eulogy at the funeral.

senses.en: a formal expression of praise

examples.text: The review was a long eulogy to the architect's lifetime of work.

origin.ko: 그리스어 eulogía(좋은 말, 칭찬)에서 라틴어를 거쳐 왔습니다. 고인에 대한 좋은 말이 '추도사'입니다.

senses.en: deliberately vague or ambiguous

examples.text: The spokesman gave evasive answers whenever reporters asked about the company's falling profits.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 évasif에서 왔고, 라틴어 ēvādere(빠져나가다)가 바탕입니다. 질문을 슬쩍 피하는 태도입니다.

senses.en: with little or no preparation or forethought

examples.text: The senator abandoned her script and gave a moving extemporaneous speech to the crowd.

origin.ko: 라틴어 ex tempore(그때그때)에서 후기 라틴어를 거쳐 왔습니다. 준비 없이 그 순간에 즉흥으로 한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: not based on fact; existing only in the imagination

examples.text: The explorer's fanciful tales of golden cities were soon dismissed by serious geographers.

senses.en: indulging in or influenced by fancy

examples.text: The children's fanciful drawings showed castles floating among clouds and dragons wearing top hats.

origin.ko: fancy(상상)에 -ful이 붙었습니다. 상상으로 가득해 현실과 거리가 있다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: characterized by intense emotion

examples.text: The candidate's fervent speech about education reform moved even her harshest critics in the audience.

origin.ko: 라틴어 fervēre(끓다, 뜨겁다)의 현재분사에서 왔습니다. 끓어오르는 듯한 열정을 뜻합니다.

senses.en: hinder or prevent (the efforts, plans, or desires) of

examples.text: Bad weather frustrated the expedition's attempts to reach the summit before winter.

senses.en: To disappoint or defeat; to vex by depriving of something expected or desired.

examples.text: It frustrates me to do all this work and then lose it all.

origin.ko: 라틴어 frūstrō '속이다'에서 왔습니다. 기대를 속여 헛되게 만든다는 뜻에서 '좌절시키다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: someone motivated by desires for sensual pleasures

examples.text: The novel's hero is a hedonist who spends his inheritance on lavish parties and travel.

origin.ko: 그리스어 hēdonḗ(쾌락)에 -ist가 붙은 말입니다. 쾌락을 좇는 사람입니다.

senses.en: a situation in which no progress can be made or no advancement is possible

examples.text: reached an impasse on the negotiations

origin.ko: 프랑스어 impasse '지나갈 수 없는 길'에서 왔습니다. 길이 막혀 더 못 가는 상황이 '교착 상태'입니다.

senses.en: uninterrupted in time and indefinitely long continuing

examples.text: The dog's incessant barking kept the girl awake all night.

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 incessāns '멈추지 않는'에서 왔습니다. 멈추지 않고 이어지는 상태입니다.

senses.en: incapable of failure or error

examples.text: No scientific method is infallible, which is why findings must be replicated by independent teams.

senses.en: Certain to produce the intended effect; sure.

examples.text: Try this infallible cure for hiccups.

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 īnfallibilis에서 왔습니다. fallibilis(틀릴 수 있는)에 부정 접두사가 붙었습니다.

senses.en: a person who shows no gratitude

examples.text: After all the help he had received, he proved an ingrate who never once thanked his benefactors.

origin.ko: 라틴어 ingrātus '달갑지 않은'에서 왔습니다. 고마움(grat)을 모르는 사람이라는 뜻이 되었습니다.

senses.en: A critical moment in time.

examples.text: We're at a crucial juncture in our relationship.

senses.en: A place where things join, a junction.

examples.text: Cracks had formed at the juncture where the old wing met the new construction.

origin.ko: 라틴어 iūnctūra '이음, 접합'에서 왔습니다. 두 상황이 이어지는 지점에서 '중대한 시점'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: a very wealthy or powerful businessperson

examples.text: The shipping magnate donated millions to the new maritime museum.

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 magnātēs에서 왔고 magnus(큰)에서 나왔습니다. 큰 인물, 곧 거물입니다.

senses.en: having unnatural mannerisms

examples.text: The actor's mannered delivery made every line sound rehearsed and oddly lifeless.

origin.ko: manner(태도)에 -ed가 붙은 말입니다.

senses.en: A word or phrase which has recently been coined; a new word or phrase.

examples.text: Critics dismissed the term as a mere neologism, though it soon entered everyday speech.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 néologisme에서 왔고, 그리스어 '새로운(néos) + 말(lógos)'이 바탕입니다.

senses.en: an act of deliberate betrayal

examples.text: The ally's perfidy, revealed only after the treaty was signed, shocked the entire nation.

origin.ko: 라틴어 perfidia '신의를 저버림'에서 왔고, fidēs는 '믿음'입니다. fidelity와 같은 뿌리입니다.

senses.en: To remove the possibility of; to rule out; to prevent or exclude; to render impossible.

examples.text: It has been raining for days, but that doesn’t preclude the skies clearing by this afternoon!

origin.ko: 라틴어 praeclūdere('앞을 닫다')에서 왔습니다. 미리 문을 닫아 가능성을 막는다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: convert to another faith or religion

examples.text: Missionaries were forbidden to proselytize among the local population.

senses.en: To advertise a non-religious belief, way of living, cause, point of view, (scientific) hypothesis, social or other position, political party, or other organization; to convince someone to join such a cause or organization or support such a position; to recruit someone.

examples.text: He has strong political views, and an annoying habit of proselytizing at parties.

origin.ko: 그리스어 prosēlytos('새로 온 사람, 개종자')에서 왔습니다. 남을 자기 종교로 끌어들이는 일입니다.

senses.en: Dashingly, carelessly, or sportingly unconventional or stylish; jaunty; characterized by a devil-may-care unconventionality; having a somewhat disreputable quality or appearance.

examples.text: a hat worn at a rakish angle

senses.en: Like a rake; dissolute; profligate.

examples.text: The novel follows a rakish aristocrat who squanders his inheritance on gambling and extravagant parties.

origin.ko: rake('방탕한 남자')에 -ish가 붙은 말입니다. 약간 방탕하지만 멋을 부린 태도를 뜻합니다.

senses.en: marked by harshly abusive criticism

examples.text: The critic's scathing review dismissed the film as shallow, derivative, and tediously long.

senses.en: division of a group into opposing factions

examples.text: A schism broke the organization into two rivals.

senses.en: the formal separation of a church into two churches or the withdrawal of one group over doctrinal differences

examples.text: The schism between Sunnis and Shias happened quite early in Islamic history.

origin.ko: 그리스어 skhizō(쪼개다)에서 온 skhisma에서 왔습니다. 집단이 둘로 쪼개지는 분열입니다.

senses.en: Organized incitement of rebellion or civil disorder against authority or the state, usually by speech or writing.

examples.text: The pamphleteer was jailed for sedition after urging soldiers to lay down their arms.

origin.ko: 라틴어 sēditiō에서 왔고 '따로 떨어져 나가는 것'을 뜻합니다. 권위에서 갈라서는 반란 선동이 되었습니다.

senses.en: To satisfy (thirst, or other desires).

examples.text: It could not slake mine ire nor ease my heart.

senses.en: make less active or intense

examples.text: A cool evening breeze did little to slake the oppressive heat of the long summer day.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 sleacian에서 왔고 slack(느슨한)에서 나왔습니다. 갈증을 느슨하게 가라앉힌다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: morally degraded

examples.text: The trial exposed the sordid details of the senator's bribery scheme.

senses.en: foul and run-down and repulsive

examples.text: They rented a sordid apartment together.

senses.en: meanly avaricious and mercenary

examples.text: The heir's sordid greed drove him to quarrel with his siblings over every trinket in the estate.

origin.ko: 라틴어 sordidus(더러운)에서 왔습니다. 몸이 더러운 데서 도덕적으로 추잡하다는 뜻이 되었습니다.

senses.en: inactivity resulting from a static balance between opposing forces

examples.text: His company was sized for growth, not stasis.

senses.en: an abnormal state in which the normal flow of a liquid (such as blood) is slowed or stopped

examples.text: Venous stasis in the legs can lead to dangerous clots after a long flight.

origin.ko: 그리스어 stasis(멈춰 서 있음)에서 왔습니다. 움직임 없이 멈춘 정체 상태입니다.

senses.en: severe criticism

examples.text: The review was a harsh stricture on the director's careless handling of historical fact.

senses.en: A rule restricting behaviour or action.

examples.text: Even venerable print publications seem to accept that old strictures no longer apply when they move online.

origin.ko: 라틴어 strictūra에서 왔고 '죄는 것'이 원뜻입니다. 옥죄는 듯한 혹평이 되었습니다.

senses.en: consider (an instance of something) as part of a general rule or principle

examples.text: The theory subsumes several earlier hypotheses under a single, more general principle.

senses.en: contain or include

examples.text: This new system subsumes the old one

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 subsūmere(아래에 취하다)에서 왔습니다. 더 큰 범주 아래로 포함시킨다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: lacking substance or significance

examples.text: His argument was not convincing in the debate, considering how tenuous it was.

senses.en: Thin in substance or consistency.

examples.text: A tenuous mist hung over the valley, thinning as the sun climbed higher.

origin.ko: 라틴어 tenuis('얇은')에 -ous를 붙였습니다. 실처럼 가늘어 끊어질 듯한 근거가 '빈약한'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: An absurd, grotesque, misrepresentative or grossly inferior likeness or imitation.

examples.text: A battlefield trial is a travesty of justice.

senses.en: a composition that imitates or misrepresents somebody's style, usually in a humorous way

examples.text: The comedian's travesty of the epic poem had audiences laughing at every solemn line.

origin.ko: 이탈리아어 travestire('옷을 바꿔 입히다, 변장시키다')에서 왔습니다. 엉터리로 변장시킨 모방이 '왜곡된 모방'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: (of theories etc.) incapable of being defended or justified
senses.ko: 옹호할 수 없는, 지지될 수 없는

examples.text: The theory of cold fusion was untenable.

senses.en: a malevolent or haunting spirit

examples.text: Villagers claimed a pale wraith drifted across the marsh each night before the first frost.

senses.en: marked by active interest and enthusiasm

examples.text: The zealous young lawyer worked through the night to prepare her client's defense.

origin.ko: zeal에 -ous를 붙인 말이고 jealous와 짝을 이루는 말입니다. 열성이 가득해 '열렬한'입니다.

senses.en: fearful expectation or anticipation

examples.text: the student looked around the examination room with apprehension

senses.en: the cognitive condition of someone who understands

examples.text: The child's apprehension of moral rules develops long before she can articulate them.

senses.en: the act of apprehending (especially apprehending a criminal)

examples.text: The warrant had been issued for his apprehension on the charge of rioting.

origin.ko: 라틴어 apprehensio(붙잡음)에서 왔습니다. 마음을 움켜쥔 두려움이 '불안'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: inform (somebody) of something

examples.text: Have the students been apprised of the tuition hike?

origin.ko: 프랑스어 apprendre(배우다, 가르치다)의 과거분사에서 왔습니다. 잡아서 이해시킨다는 뜻에서 '알리다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: ban from a place of residence, as for punishment

examples.text: He was banished from the kingdom for his crimes.

senses.en: drive away

examples.text: banish bad thoughts

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 banir(공표하다, 금지하다)에서 왔고 게르만어 어원입니다. 공식적으로 금지를 선포해 내쫓는다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: having an unpleasant sound

examples.text: The cacophonous traffic outside made it impossible to hear the lecture in the old hall.

origin.ko: 그리스어 kakophōnos('나쁜 소리의')에서 왔습니다. kakos(나쁜)와 phōnē(소리)가 합쳐졌습니다.

senses.en: declare (a dead person) to be a saint

examples.text: After he was shown to have performed a miracle, the priest was canonized

senses.en: To regard (an artistic or written work or its creator) as one of a group that are representative of a particular field.

examples.text: Critics canonized the novel soon after its release, and schools placed it on every reading list.

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 canōnizāre에서 왔고, 그리스어 kanōn(기준)에서 갈라졌습니다. 성인의 공식 목록에 올린다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: avoid or try to avoid fulfilling, answering, or performing (duties, questions, or issues)

examples.text: The company used offshore accounts to circumvent the tax regulations.

senses.en: beat through cleverness and wit

examples.text: She circumvented her rivals by securing the contract before they had even submitted a bid.

origin.ko: 라틴어 circumveniō('둘러 오다, 에워싸다')에서 왔습니다. 정면 대신 빙 둘러 피해 간다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: showing marked and often playful or irritating evasiveness or reluctance to make a definite or committing statement

examples.text: a politician coy about his intentions

senses.en: affectedly modest or shy especially in a playful or provocative way

examples.text: She gave a coy smile and refused to reveal who had sent the flowers.

origin.ko: 라틴어 quiētus(조용한, 쉬는)에서 고대 프랑스어 coi를 거쳐 왔습니다. 조용히 빼는 태도에서 '내숭 떠는'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: Acceptance of a belief or claim as true, especially on the basis of evidence.

examples.text: Based on the scientific data, I give credence to this hypothesis.

origin.ko: 라틴어 crēdō(믿다)에서 중세 라틴어 crēdentia(믿음)로 이어졌습니다.

senses.en: poor enough to need help from others

examples.text: The war left thousands of families destitute and dependent on charity for food.

senses.en: completely wanting or lacking

examples.text: young recruits destitute of experience

origin.ko: 라틴어 dēstitūtus(버려진, 남겨진)에서 왔습니다. 의지할 것 없이 내버려진 상태가 '극빈'입니다.

senses.en: being twofold; a classification into two opposed parts or subclasses

examples.text: the dichotomy between eastern and western culture

origin.ko: 그리스어 dikhotomía에서 왔습니다. 둘로 자른다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: very small

examples.text: diminutive in stature

origin.ko: 라틴어 dīminuere(줄이다)에서 고대 프랑스어를 거쳐 왔습니다.

senses.en: showing or indicating careful judgment and discernment especially in matters of taste

examples.text: The restaurant attracts discriminating customers who expect high-quality ingredients.

senses.en: favoring social equality

examples.text: The founders envisioned an egalitarian community in which land and labor were shared equally.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 égalitaire에 영어 -ian이 붙은 말입니다. '평등'을 뜻하는 égal에서 나왔습니다.

senses.en: marked by erratic changeableness in affections or attachments

examples.text: Voters proved fickle, abandoning the popular governor as soon as the economy began to weaken.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 ficol(교활한, 믿을 수 없는)에서 왔습니다. 속이기 쉽고 마음이 자주 변하는 성질을 뜻합니다.

senses.en: (used of the meanings of words or text) not literal; using figures of speech

examples.text: When the poet calls grief an ocean, she is using figurative language, not describing water.

senses.en: Representing forms recognisable in life and clearly derived from real object sources, in contrast to abstract art.

examples.text: After years of abstraction, the painter returned to figurative work, portraying her neighbors in quiet domestic scenes.

origin.ko: 중세 프랑스어 figuratif에서 왔고 figure(모양, 표현)가 바탕입니다. 글자 그대로가 아니라 비유적 표현을 쓴다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: strength of mind that enables one to endure adversity with courage

examples.text: She faced her long illness with remarkable fortitude and never complained.

origin.ko: 라틴어 fortitūdō(용기, 강함)에서 왔습니다. 역경을 견디는 마음의 강함입니다.

senses.en: filled with or attended with

examples.text: The negotiations were fraught with difficulties from the very first day.

senses.en: marked by distress

examples.text: a fraught mother-daughter relationship

origin.ko: 중세 네덜란드어 vracht(화물, 뱃짐)에서 왔습니다. 짐을 가득 실은 배처럼 무언가로 가득 차 있다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: lacking grace in movement or posture

examples.text: The gawky teenager grew into an elegant dancer within a few years.

senses.en: consisting of elements that are not of the same kind or nature

examples.text: the population of the United States is vast and heterogeneous

origin.ko: 그리스어 heterogenḗs '서로 다른 종류의'에서 왔습니다. héteros(다른)와 génos(종류)가 합쳐졌습니다.

senses.en: A period of success, popularity, or power; prime.

examples.text: The early twentieth century was the heyday of the steam locomotive.

origin.ko: 16세기 감탄사 heyda에서 왔고, 뒤에 day(날, 시기)로 풀이되어 '전성기'라는 뜻이 되었습니다.

senses.en: an intricate and confusing interpersonal or political situation

examples.text: The diplomatic imbroglio over fishing rights dragged on for months and strained relations between the two neighbors.

origin.ko: 이탈리아어 imbroglio '뒤엉킴'에서 왔고, 프랑스어 embrouiller(뒤섞다)와 같은 뿌리입니다.

senses.en: arousing to action or rebellion

examples.text: The senator's incendiary speech provoked angry protests outside the capitol within hours of its broadcast.

senses.en: involving deliberate burning of property

examples.text: Investigators concluded the warehouse blaze was caused by an incendiary device left near the loading dock.

origin.ko: 라틴어 incendiārius '불을 지르는'에서 왔고 incendō(불붙이다)가 뿌리입니다. 불을 붙이듯 사람들을 부추기는 선동적인 말이 되었습니다.

senses.en: Not violated; free from violation or hurt of any kind; secure against violation or impairment.

examples.text: The remote valley remained inviolate, untouched by roads, mines, or the settlers who had spread elsewhere.

origin.ko: 라틴어 inviolātus에서 왔습니다. 침범당하지 않아 온전한 상태입니다.

senses.en: make calm or still

examples.text: The gentle rocking of the train lulled the exhausted children to sleep.

senses.en: calm by deception

examples.text: Don't let yourself be lulled into a false state of security

senses.en: a pause during which things are calm or activities are diminished

examples.text: there was a lull in the storm

origin.ko: 중세 영어 lullen에서 왔고, 아이를 달랠 때 내던 la-la 같은 소리에서 나왔다고 봅니다.

senses.en: Excessively or falsely sentimental; showing a sickly excess of sentiment.

examples.text: The greeting card's mawkish verse made even its intended recipient wince.

senses.en: of communal life sequestered from the world under religious vows

examples.text: He led a nearly monastic life, devoting his days to study and silence.

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 monasticus에서 중세 프랑스어를 거쳐 들어온 말로, 세상과 떨어진 수도 생활을 가리킵니다.

senses.en: Unduly confident; (sometimes also) arrogant.

examples.text: overweening pride

senses.en: Exaggerated, excessive.

examples.text: The film's overweening ambition collapsed under the weight of its own bloated plot.

origin.ko: 중세 영어 overweninge에서 왔습니다. 자신을 지나치게 높게 생각한다는 데서 자만하는이 되었습니다.

senses.en: Tolerable, acceptable.

examples.text: The agreement was palatable to both of them.

senses.en: Pleasing to the taste, tasty.

examples.text: The hospital tried to make its meals more palatable for patients.

senses.en: A powerful leader; a monarch; a ruler.

examples.text: The visiting potentate arrived with a retinue of two hundred courtiers and servants.

origin.ko: 라틴어 potēns('힘 있는')에서 나온 potentātus('통치')를 거쳤습니다. 힘을 쥔 통치자를 뜻합니다.

senses.en: cause to become widely known

examples.text: Partisan websites propagate rumors faster than fact-checkers can correct them.

senses.en: multiply sexually or asexually

examples.text: Gardeners can propagate the shrub easily by taking cuttings in late summer.

senses.en: travel through the air

examples.text: sound and light propagate in this medium

origin.ko: 라틴어 prōpāgāre('번식시키다')에서 왔습니다. 식물을 가지치기로 퍼뜨리듯 널리 퍼뜨린다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: draw back, as with fear or pain

examples.text: The witness quailed under the prosecutor's fierce and relentless cross-examination.

origin.ko: 중세 네덜란드어 queilen('괴로워하다')에서 온 동사입니다. 고통에 움츠러드는 데서 '겁먹다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: A prick of the conscience; a moral scruple, a pang of guilt.

examples.text: This lawyer has no qualms about saving people who are on the wrong side of the law.

senses.en: a mild state of nausea

examples.text: A sudden qualm of seasickness forced her to leave the dinner table.

senses.en: tending or intended to rectify or improve

examples.text: a remedial reading course

senses.en: tending to cure or restore to health

examples.text: The spa advertised the remedial properties of its mineral springs.

origin.ko: 라틴어 remediālis에서 왔으며 remedy('치료')에 -al이 붙은 말입니다. 부족한 것을 고쳐 주는 교육 등에 씁니다.

senses.en: Not full, large, or plentiful; scarcely sufficient; scanty; meager.

examples.text: The report offered scant evidence that the new policy had any measurable effect on unemployment.

senses.en: To limit in amount or share; to stint.

examples.text: The company scanted safety training in order to cut costs, with tragic results.

origin.ko: 고대 노르드어 skamt(짧은)에서 왔습니다. 길이가 짧듯 양도 모자란다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: Followed by of: the outward appearance of a person or thing which is different from what the person or thing actually is; also, an outward appearance of a thing which does not actually exist.

examples.text: The regime maintained a semblance of democracy while jailing every serious opponent.

senses.en: The outward appearance or form of a person or thing.

examples.text: After the storm, the village slowly regained some semblance of normal life.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 sembler(~처럼 보이다)에서 왔습니다. 실제와 다르게 '그렇게 보이는' 겉모습입니다.

senses.en: stop the flow of a liquid

examples.text: A small amount of cotton can be stuffed into the nose to stanch the flow of blood if necessary.

senses.en: To check or stop, or deter (an action).

examples.text: Beijing devotes immense resources to restricting access for and stanching scrutiny from international groups and reporters.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 estanchier(흐름을 막다)에서 왔습니다. 피나 물이 흐르는 것을 멈춘다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: marked by firm determination or resolution; not shakable

examples.text: Despite years of setbacks, she remained steadfast in her commitment to the research.

senses.en: Firmly loyal or constant; unswerving.

examples.text: steadfast support

origin.ko: 고대 영어 stedefæst에서 왔고 stead(자리)와 fast(단단한)가 합쳐졌습니다. 제자리에 단단히 박혀 흔들리지 않습니다.

senses.en: consideration in dealing with others and avoiding giving offense

examples.text: By the use of tact, she was able to calm her jealous husband.

origin.ko: 라틴어 tāctus(만짐)에서 왔습니다. 섬세한 촉감처럼 남의 마음을 건드리지 않는 눈치가 되었습니다.

senses.en: the trait of avoiding excesses

examples.text: The philosopher praised temperance as the virtue that keeps appetite from overruling reason.

senses.en: Moderation in the use of intoxicating substances; sobriety; specifically, complete abstinence from alcoholic beverages; teetotalism.

examples.text: The temperance movement of the nineteenth century campaigned for abstinence from alcohol across much of the country.

origin.ko: 라틴어 temperantia(절제)에서 왔습니다. 지나치지 않게 조절하는 태도입니다.

senses.en: without scruples or principles

examples.text: Unscrupulous landlords exploited the shortage by charging desperate tenants far more than the law allowed.

senses.en: easily excused or forgiven

examples.text: The editor treated the occasional typo as a venial error, not worth a reprimand.

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 veniālis('용서할 만한')에서 왔고 venia('용서')와 이어집니다.

senses.en: liquidate gradually

examples.text: The firm plans to amortize the loan over twenty years through fixed monthly payments.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 amortir(죽게 하다)에서 왔습니다. 빚을 조금씩 '죽여' 없애는 데서 '분할 상환하다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: a feeling of ill will arousing active hostility

examples.text: Years of border disputes had bred deep animosity between the two neighboring villages.

origin.ko: 라틴어 animositas(기세, 격정)에서 왔고 animus(마음)에서 나왔습니다. 마음속 격한 감정이 '적개심'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: Something that impedes development or growth, or spoils any other aspect of life.

examples.text: Chronic unemployment has been a blight on the town for more than a generation.

senses.en: any plant disease resulting in withering without rotting

examples.text: A fungal blight swept through the potato fields and destroyed most of the harvest.

senses.en: To impede the development or growth of (an aspect of life); to damage, to ruin, to spoil.

examples.text: Those obscene tattoos are going to blight your job prospects.

origin.ko: 정확한 기원은 불확실합니다. '창백해지다, 빛나다'를 뜻하던 옛말과 관련 있다는 설이 있습니다.

senses.en: a disposition to be friendly and approachable (easy to talk to)

examples.text: The host's easy bonhomie put nervous guests at ease within minutes of their arrival.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 bonhomme('착한 사람', bon 좋은 + homme 사람)에서 왔습니다. 좋은 사람다운 붙임성을 뜻합니다.

senses.en: quickly aroused to anger

examples.text: The choleric general lashed out at his officers whenever the slightest detail went wrong.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 colerique에서 왔고, choler(담즙)에 -ic가 붙었습니다. 담즙이 넘치면 화를 잘 낸다고 보았습니다.

senses.en: excuse, overlook, or make allowances for; be lenient with

examples.text: The school does not condone cheating under any circumstances.

origin.ko: 라틴어 condōnāre('용서하다')를 학술적으로 빌려 온 말입니다. 잘못을 선물처럼 넘겨 준다는 이미지입니다.

senses.en: tending to bring about; being partly responsible for

examples.text: A small, dark kitchen is not conducive to elaborate cooking.

origin.ko: 라틴어 condūcere('함께 이끌다')에서 온 conduce에 -ive가 붙은 말입니다. 좋은 결과로 이끈다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: To grant as a possession; to bestow.

examples.text: The college has conferred an honorary degree upon the visiting Prime Minister.

senses.en: have a conference in order to talk something over

examples.text: We conferred about a plan of action

origin.ko: 라틴어 cōnferō('함께 가져오다')에서 왔습니다. 모아서 건네준다는 뜻에서 '수여하다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: cancel officially

examples.text: The general countermanded the order to advance after learning of the approaching storm.

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 contramandō에서 왔습니다. 앞선 명령에 '반대되는 명령'을 내리니 '취소하다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: having a secret or hidden meaning

examples.text: cryptic writings

senses.en: having a puzzling terseness

examples.text: a cryptic note

origin.ko: 그리스어 krúptō(숨기다)에서 kruptós(숨은)를 거쳐 왔습니다. 숨겨진 뜻이 있다는 말입니다.

senses.en: To make (something) deviate from its original path or position.

examples.text: A thin metal shield deflected the blast away from the control room.

senses.en: To avoid addressing (questions, criticism, etc.).

examples.text: The Prime Minister deflected some increasingly pointed questions by claiming he had an appointment.

origin.ko: 라틴어 deflectō에서 왔습니다. 가던 길에서 휘어 벗어나게 한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: To regard as being like a deity; to treat as worthy of worship; to exalt.

examples.text: Admirers deified the founder, treating his every casual remark as sacred wisdom.

origin.ko: 라틴어 deus(신)에서 deificāre를 거쳐 왔습니다. 신으로 만든다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: Warm praise, especially a formal expression of such praise; a tribute.

examples.text: The ceremony opened with a lavish encomium to the retiring headmaster.

origin.ko: 그리스어 enkṓmion(승리자를 기리는 송가)에서 왔습니다. kômos는 '축제, 흥겨운 행렬'입니다.

senses.en: a person devoted to refined sensuous enjoyment (especially good food and drink)

examples.text: The epicure traveled across Europe sampling regional cheeses and rare vintages.

origin.ko: 고대 그리스 철학자 에피쿠로스의 이름에서 왔습니다. 그가 즐거움을 추구하는 삶을 가르쳤다 해서, 음식을 즐기는 미식가를 가리키게 되었습니다.

senses.en: not produced by natural forces

examples.text: brokers created a factitious demand for stocks

origin.ko: 라틴어 factītius(인공의)에서 왔고 facere(만들다)가 바탕입니다. 사람이 만든 것이라 자연스럽지 않다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: play boisterously

examples.text: Lambs gambol across the meadow each spring while their mothers graze nearby.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 gambade '껑충 뛰어오름'에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: The main idea or substance, or the most essential part, of a longer or more complicated matter; the crux, the heart, the pith.

examples.text: Skim the abstract first so that you grasp the gist of the paper before reading it closely.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 gist '(소송이) 놓여 있다'에서 왔고 gesir(눕다)에서 나왔습니다. 사건이 바탕을 두는 핵심이라는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: Serious, grave, dire, or dangerous.

examples.text: As for the captain, his wounds were grievous indeed, but not dangerous.

senses.en: causing or marked by grief or anguish

examples.text: The sudden closure of the mill was a grievous blow to the small town.

senses.en: shockingly brutal or cruel

examples.text: The tribunal condemned the grievous crimes committed against civilians during the siege.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 grever에서 왔고, 라틴어 gravō(짐 지우다)가 뿌리입니다. 무겁게 짓누른다는 데서 '심각한'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: all of the same or similar kind or nature

examples.text: a close-knit homogeneous group

origin.ko: 그리스어 homogenḗs '같은 종류의'에서 왔습니다. homós(같은)와 génos(종류)가 합쳐졌습니다.

senses.en: working or spreading in a hidden and usually injurious way

examples.text: glaucoma is an insidious disease

senses.en: Intending to entrap; alluring but harmful.

examples.text: Hansel and Gretel were lured by the witch’s insidious gingerbread house.

origin.ko: 라틴어 īnsidiae '매복'에서 왔고 insideō '그 위에 앉다'에서 나왔습니다. 숨어서 기다리다 덮친다는 이미지입니다.

senses.en: organized opposition to authority; a conflict in which one faction tries to wrest control from another

examples.text: The army crushed the insurrection within a week, but unrest simmered in the capital for months.

origin.ko: 라틴어 īnsurrēctiō '봉기'에서 왔고 īnsurgō '일어나다'에서 나왔습니다.

senses.en: specialized technical terminology characteristic of a particular subject

examples.text: Legal jargon often makes contracts nearly impenetrable to ordinary readers.

senses.en: Speech or language that is incomprehensible or unintelligible; gibberish.

examples.text: Cut the jargon and get to your point.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 jargon '재잘거림, 말'에서 왔습니다. 남들은 알아듣기 힘든 그들만의 말이라는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: Emitting light; glowing brightly; shining.

examples.text: The luminous dial of the old clock glowed faintly in the dark bedroom.

senses.en: Clear; enlightening; easy to understand.

examples.text: a luminous explanation

origin.ko: 프랑스어를 거쳐 라틴어 lūminōsus에서 왔고 lūmen(빛)에서 나왔습니다.

senses.en: done or made using whatever is available

examples.text: They used the ledge and a few branches for a makeshift shelter.

origin.ko: make shift(임시변통하다)에서 나온 말입니다.

senses.en: having an unpleasant smell

examples.text: There were malodorous garbage bags aplenty outside her house.

origin.ko: mal-(나쁜), odor(냄새), -ous가 합쳐진 말입니다.

senses.en: open to argument or debate

examples.text: Whether the policy actually reduced crime remains a moot question among economists.

senses.en: Having no practical consequence or relevance.

examples.text: That point may make for a good discussion, but it is moot.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 mōt는 '모임'이었습니다. 모임에서 토론하던 문제라는 데서 '논란의 여지가 있는'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: cause to continue or prevail

examples.text: perpetuate a myth

origin.ko: 라틴어 perpetuō '끊임없이 이어지게 하다'에서 왔고, perpetuus '영원한'이 원형입니다.

senses.en: an incidental benefit awarded for certain types of employment (especially if it is regarded as a right)

examples.text: The perquisites of this job include health insurance and a performance bonus.

senses.en: a right reserved exclusively by a particular person or group (especially a hereditary or official right)

examples.text: Private jets and motor yachts are perquisites of the rich.

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 perquīsītum '이익을 보고 얻은 것'에서 왔습니다. 본 급여 외에 따로 얻는 부수입을 뜻합니다.

senses.en: An excessive amount or number; an abundance.

examples.text: The menu offers a plethora of cuisines from around the world.

origin.ko: 그리스어 plēthṓra '가득함'에서 후기 라틴어를 거쳐 왔습니다. 넘치도록 가득한 과잉을 뜻합니다.

senses.en: A tactic, strategy, or scheme.

examples.text: The free T-shirt is really a ploy to get you inside to see their sales pitch.

origin.ko: employ나 deploy가 줄어든 말이거나, 라틴어 plicāre '접다'에서 왔다는 두 가지 설이 있습니다.

senses.en: making claim to or creating an appearance of (often undeserved) importance or distinction

examples.text: Reviewers found the novel pretentious, its dense allusions serving to impress rather than illuminate.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 prétentieux에서 왔고 라틴어 praetendere('앞에 내세우다')와 닿습니다. 중요한 척 내세우는 모습입니다.

senses.en: foretelling events as if by supernatural intervention

examples.text: Her warnings about the bank's collapse now seem almost prophetic.

origin.ko: 그리스어 prophētikos에서 왔으며 pro('앞')와 phēmi('말하다')에서 나왔습니다. 앞일을 미리 말한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: To forbid or prohibit.

examples.text: The law proscribes driving a car while intoxicated.

senses.en: To banish or exclude.

examples.text: Many Roman citizens were proscribed for taking part in rebellions.

origin.ko: 라틴어 prōscrībere('공포하다, 추방하다')에서 왔습니다. 이름을 공개 명단에 써서 내친다는 뜻에서 '금지하다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: powerful or influential

examples.text: The puissant monarch commanded armies that no rival dared to confront.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 pooir('할 수 있다')의 현재분사에서 왔고 라틴어 posse에서 나왔습니다. 할 수 있는 힘이 있다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: To drink or imbibe with vigour or relish; to drink copiously; to swallow in large draughts.

examples.text: The weary travelers quaffed cold ale and traded stories by the fire.

senses.en: give up, such as power, as of monarchs and emperors, or duties and obligations

examples.text: The prince renounced his claim to the throne in order to marry a commoner.

senses.en: cast off

examples.text: She renounced her husband

origin.ko: 라틴어 renūntiāre('거절을 알리다')에서 왔습니다. 가진 권리를 내려놓겠다고 공식으로 알리는 것입니다.

senses.en: having a sweet nature befitting an angel or cherub

examples.text: The child wore a seraphic smile as she slept, untroubled by the noise around her.

origin.ko: 히브리어 seraph(불타는 천사, 세라핌)에 -ic이 붙었습니다. 천사 같다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: Intending to subvert, overturn, undermine or debase.

examples.text: subversive influence

senses.en: A radical supporter of political or social revolution.

examples.text: The regime jailed anyone it labeled a subversive, including several respected novelists.

origin.ko: subvert에 -ive가 붙은 말입니다. 아래에서부터 뒤집어엎으려는 성질을 뜻합니다.

senses.en: A large or scholarly book.

examples.text: The professor pulled a dusty old tome from the bookshelf.

origin.ko: 그리스어 tómos('잘라 낸 한 부분, 두루마리')에서 왔습니다. 큰 저작의 한 권이 '두꺼운 책'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: To cajole or attempt to persuade by flattery.

examples.text: The child tried to wheedle an extra dessert out of his grandmother with sweet compliments.

senses.en: be abundant or plentiful; exist in large quantities

examples.text: Rumors abounded after the CEO's sudden departure, though the company offered no explanation.

origin.ko: 라틴어 abundare(넘쳐흐르다)에서 왔고 unda(파도)와 연결됩니다. 파도처럼 넘쳐나는 데서 '풍부하다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: sparing in consumption of especially food and drink

examples.text: Though he could afford lavish banquets, the philosopher led an abstemious life of bread, water, and study.

origin.ko: 라틴어 abstemius(술을 삼가는)에서 왔습니다. 독한 술에서 멀리 떨어진다는 뜻이 '절제하는'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: characterized by intense emotion

examples.text: an ardent lover

origin.ko: 라틴어 ardere(타다)의 현재분사에서 왔습니다. 불타는 듯한 열정이 '열렬한'입니다.

senses.en: a feeling of intense dislike

examples.text: Due to her aversion to the outdoors she complained throughout the entire camping trip.

origin.ko: 라틴어 aversio(외면함)에서 왔습니다. 얼굴을 돌려 피하는 마음이 '혐오'입니다.

senses.en: A cause of misery or ruin.

examples.text: the bane of one’s existence

origin.ko: 고대 영어 bana(살인자, 죽음을 부르는 것)에서 왔습니다. 파멸의 원인이라는 뜻이 '골칫거리, 화근'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: intending or showing kindness

examples.text: The benevolent headmaster often paid the fees of students whose families could not afford them.

origin.ko: 라틴어 benevolens(호의를 가진)에서 왔습니다. 남이 잘되기를 바라는 마음입니다.

senses.en: split or divide into two

examples.text: The debate began to bifurcate into two camps, one favoring reform and the other resisting it.

senses.en: resembling a fork; divided or separated into two branches

examples.text: The bifurcate river split around the island before rejoining downstream.

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 bifurcātus에서 왔습니다. '두 갈래(포크 모양)로 나뉜'이라는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: very thin especially from disease or hunger or cold

examples.text: After months in the prison camp, the cadaverous survivors could barely stand without help.

origin.ko: 라틴어 cadāverōsus에서 왔습니다. 시체(cadaver)처럼 핼쑥하고 말랐다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: cause to be more favorably inclined; gain the good will of

examples.text: The mayor tried to conciliate angry residents by promising to reopen the community center.

origin.ko: 라틴어 conciliō('하나로 합치다')에서 왔고 concilium(회의, 모임)에서 갈라졌습니다.

senses.en: be a sign or indication of

examples.text: The yellow blazes denote the trail.

senses.en: have as a meaning

examples.text: The prefix pre- denotes "before", as in preview.

origin.ko: 라틴어 denotare(표시하다)에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: lacking conciseness

examples.text: a diffuse historical novel

senses.en: To spread (something) over or through as in air, water, or other matter, especially by fluid motion or passive means.

examples.text: Ideas are easily diffused with the help of technology.

senses.en: spread out; not concentrated in one place

examples.text: a large diffuse organization

origin.ko: 라틴어 diffundere(사방으로 쏟다)에서 왔습니다. 퍼져 흩어져서 '장황한'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: An inconsistency between facts or sentiments.

examples.text: They found a discrepancy between the first set of test results and the second, and they're still trying to figure out why.

origin.ko: 라틴어 discrepantia에서 왔고 discrepō(소리가 어긋나다)가 뿌리입니다. 소리가 맞지 않는 데서 '불일치'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: lack of respect accompanied by a feeling of intense dislike

examples.text: The cat viewed the cheap supermarket catfood with disdain and stalked away.

senses.en: reject with contempt

examples.text: The critic disdained popular fiction, refusing even to review novels he considered beneath serious attention.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 desdeignier(가치 없다고 여기다)에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: move away from each other

examples.text: The crowds dispersed

senses.en: to cause to separate and go in different directions

examples.text: Police used loudspeakers to disperse the protesters before the evening curfew began.

senses.en: To disseminate.

examples.text: Volunteers helped disperse leaflets about the new vaccination program across the rural district.

origin.ko: 라틴어 dispergō(흩뿌리다)에서 왔고 spargō(뿌리다)가 뿌리입니다.

senses.en: To cause (someone) to be drawn into or involved in a difficult situation or state of contention.

examples.text: Avoid him. He will embroil you in his fights.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 embrouiller(뒤얽히게 하다)에서 왔습니다. 헝클어진 상황 속으로 끌어들인다는 이미지입니다.

senses.en: restrict (someone or something) so as to make free movement difficult

examples.text: Heavy packs encumbered the soldiers as they crossed the muddy field.

senses.en: To burden with a legal claim or other obligation.

examples.text: The estate was encumbered with debts that left little for the heirs.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 encombrer(방해하다)에서 왔습니다. 짐을 얹어 움직임을 방해한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: To hold spellbound.

examples.text: The magician's final illusion enthralled even the most skeptical members of the audience.

origin.ko: en-에 thrall(노예)이 붙었습니다. 노예처럼 마음을 사로잡는다는 이미지입니다.

senses.en: established firmly and securely

examples.text: the entrenched power of the nobility

senses.en: destroy completely, as if down to the roots

examples.text: Smallpox was globally eradicated in 1980.

origin.ko: 라틴어 ērādīcāre(뿌리째 뽑다)에서 왔습니다. 풀을 뿌리째 뽑듯 완전히 없앤다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: The character or fundamental values of a person, people, culture, or movement.

examples.text: The company's ethos of collaboration shaped how every team approached its work.

origin.ko: 그리스어 êthos(성격, 관습)를 그대로 가져왔습니다. 한 집단의 관습과 가치관을 가리키게 되었습니다.

senses.en: performed comprehensively and completely; not superficial or partial

examples.text: The committee conducted an exhaustive review of the agency's records before issuing its findings.

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 exhaustīvus에서 왔습니다. 속을 남김없이 퍼내듯 빠짐없이 다룬다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: come to understand

examples.text: Investigators struggled to fathom why the experienced pilot had ignored every warning on the instrument panel.

senses.en: measure the depth of (a body of water) with a sounding line

examples.text: Sailors used weighted ropes to fathom the harbor before guiding the large ship inside.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 fæþm(두 팔을 벌린 길이)에서 왔습니다. 두 팔로 깊이를 재듯 속을 헤아린다는 뜻이 되었습니다.

senses.en: prevent the progress or free movement of

examples.text: He was hampered in his efforts by the bad weather

senses.en: widely known and esteemed

examples.text: The university boasts an illustrious roster of alumni, including three Nobel laureates.

origin.ko: 라틴어 illūstris '빛나는, 저명한'에서 왔습니다. 환히 비춘다는 이미지가 이름이 널리 빛나는 '저명한'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: not of prime or central importance

examples.text: That character, though colorful, is incidental to the overall plot.

senses.en: occurring with or following as a consequence

examples.text: Injuries are incidental to contact sports: they're going to happen.

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어에서 왔고 라틴어 incidere(우연히 떨어지다)가 뿌리입니다. 우연히 곁들여 일어난다는 데서 '부수적인'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: impossible to avoid or evade

examples.text: Historians debate whether the empire's collapse was an ineluctable outcome of its economic decline.

origin.ko: 라틴어 inēlūctābilis에서 왔습니다. 몸부림쳐 빠져나올(ēluctor) 수 없다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: a feeling of lack of interest or energy

examples.text: A deep lassitude settled over the staff after months of fruitless negotiations.

origin.ko: 프랑스어를 거쳐 라틴어 lassitūdō '피로, 나른함'에서 왔습니다. 기운이 빠진 상태입니다.

senses.en: potentially existing but not presently evident or realized

examples.text: The program is designed to uncover latent talent among students from overlooked schools.

origin.ko: 라틴어 latēns '숨어 있는'에서 왔고 lateō '숨어 있다'에서 나왔습니다.

senses.en: Sleight of hand; "magic" trickery.

examples.text: The magician's legerdemain fooled even the skeptics sitting in the front row.

senses.en: A show of skill or deceitful ability.

examples.text: Through accounting legerdemain, the firm concealed millions in losses from its auditors.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 léger de main '손이 가벼운'에서 왔습니다. 가벼운 손재주로 속이는 마술입니다.

senses.en: Intention to harm or deprive in an illegal or immoral way. Desire to take pleasure in another's misfortune.

examples.text: Your voice positively drips malice.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어를 거쳐 라틴어 malitia '못됨, 악의'에서 왔고 malus(나쁜)에서 나왔습니다.

senses.en: Careless or inattentive.

examples.text: The inspector was negligent in checking the bridge, and the cracks went unreported for years.

origin.ko: 라틴어 neglegere '소홀히 하다'에서 왔습니다. 신경 쓰지 않는 태도가 태만함이 되었습니다.

senses.en: Open and not concealed or secret.

examples.text: The report found no overt discrimination, though subtler biases persisted in hiring.

origin.ko: 옛 프랑스어 overt '열린'에서 왔고, 라틴어 aperīre '열다'가 원형입니다. 열려서 숨김없다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: Evoking strong mental sensation, to the point of distress; emotionally moving.

examples.text: Flipping through his high school yearbook evoked many a poignant memory of yesteryear.

senses.en: Incisive; penetrating; piercing.

examples.text: His comments were poignant and witty.

origin.ko: 옛 프랑스어 poindre '찌르다'에서 왔고, 라틴어 pungō가 원형입니다. 가슴을 콕 찌르는 듯 애절하다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: tediously prolonged or tending to speak or write at great length

examples.text: The judge grew impatient with the lawyer's prolix and repetitive closing argument.

origin.ko: 라틴어 prōlixus('길게 뻗은')에서 왔습니다. 길게 늘어져 장황하다는 뜻이 되었습니다.

senses.en: Skillfulness or extraordinary ability in a particular area of expertise; dexterity, mastery, or proficiency.

examples.text: The young chef's culinary prowess earned her a Michelin star within three years.

senses.en: Distinguished bravery or courage, especially in battle; heroism.

examples.text: The knight was celebrated throughout the kingdom for his prowess in battle.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 proesce('용맹, 훌륭함')에서 왔습니다. 전투에서의 용맹이 뛰어난 기량이 되었습니다.

senses.en: gnaw into; make resentful or angry

examples.text: The injustice rankled her

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 rancler('곪다')에서 왔고 라틴어 dracunculus('작은 뱀')로 거슬러 갑니다. 곪은 상처처럼 마음을 쑤신다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: act of turning to for assistance

examples.text: have recourse to the courts

senses.en: something or someone turned to for assistance or security

examples.text: his only recourse was the police

origin.ko: 라틴어 recursus('되달려옴')에서 왔습니다. 도움을 구해 되돌아가 달려간다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: the act of paying for goods or services or to recompense for losses

examples.text: adequate remuneration for his work

origin.ko: 라틴어 remūnerātiō에서 왔습니다. munus('선물, 의무')를 되돌려 갚는다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: make repayment for or return something

examples.text: He hoped one day to requite the kindness of the neighbors who had sheltered his family.

origin.ko: re-에 중세 영어 quiten('갚다')이 붙은 말입니다. 받은 것을 되돌려 갚는다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: showing a brooding ill humor

examples.text: The saturnine professor rarely smiled and answered most questions with a weary grunt.

origin.ko: 로마 신 사투르누스(토성)에서 왔습니다. 토성의 영향을 받은 사람은 음울하다고 믿었습니다.

senses.en: not agitated; without losing self-possession

examples.text: Even amid the uproar, the old judge remained serene.

senses.en: completely clear and fine

examples.text: serene skies and a bright blue sea

origin.ko: 라틴어 serēnus(맑고 구름 없는)에서 왔습니다. 구름 없는 맑은 하늘처럼 고요한 마음입니다.

senses.en: (often followed by ‘of’) a large number or amount or extent

examples.text: The new law drew a slew of lawsuits from businesses across the country.

senses.en: turn sharply; change direction abruptly

examples.text: The truck slewed across the icy lane before the driver regained control.

senses.en: inclined to or marked by drowsiness

examples.text: The somnolent village seemed to doze through the long, hot afternoon.

origin.ko: 라틴어 somnus(잠)에서 온 somnolentus에서 왔습니다. 잠이 오는 상태입니다.

senses.en: ask humbly (for something)

examples.text: He supplicated the King for clemency

origin.ko: 라틴어 supplicāre(무릎을 굽혀 빌다)에서 왔습니다. 몸을 낮춰 간청한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: Deceitful; inclined to betray.

examples.text: The treacherous adviser sold the king's secrets to the enemy for a modest sum.

senses.en: dangerously unstable and unpredictable

examples.text: treacherous winding roads

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 trecheros('속이는')에서 왔고 treacher('배신자')에 -ous를 붙인 형태입니다.

senses.en: cause to feel shame; hurt the pride of

examples.text: The senator seemed determined to abase his rival by publicly questioning his honesty before the entire committee.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 abaissier(낮추다)에서 왔습니다. 남을 아래로 끌어내리는 모습에서 '굴욕을 주다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: Counterfeit or fake; not genuine.

examples.text: He was arrested for trying to cash a bogus check at the bank.

origin.ko: 위조 주화를 만드는 기계를 가리키던 미국 은어에서 시작됐고, 정확한 기원은 모릅니다.

senses.en: agreement on a secret plot

examples.text: The inquiry found evidence of collusion between the contractors to rig the bidding process.

origin.ko: 라틴어 collusio('공모 행위')에서 온 고대 프랑스어 collusion에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: Appearing to be difficult; challenging.

examples.text: It was a daunting task, but it was accomplished with some forward planning.

origin.ko: daunt(기를 꺾다)에 -ing가 붙은 말입니다.

senses.en: To strongly condemn or criticize.

examples.text: The editorial excoriated the minister for ignoring repeated warnings about the unsafe bridge.

senses.en: tear or wear off the skin or make sore by abrading

examples.text: The rough harness excoriated the horse's flanks after a long day of hauling.

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 excoriāre(가죽을 벗기다)에서 왔습니다. 껍질을 벗기듯 통렬하게 비난한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: unrestrained, especially with regard to feelings

examples.text: The advertisement made extravagant claims about the supplement's ability to cure every known illness.

senses.en: recklessly wasteful

examples.text: The heir's extravagant spending soon exhausted the fortune his grandfather had spent decades building.

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 extravagārī(범위 밖을 헤매다)에서 왔습니다. 적정선을 벗어나 떠돈다는 데서 '과도한'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: a minor flaw or shortcoming in character or behavior.

examples.text: The students admired their teacher despite his foibles.

senses.en: a behavioral attribute that is distinctive and peculiar to an individual

examples.text: Try to look past his foibles and see the friendly fellow underneath.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 foible(약한)에서 왔고 feeble과 같은 뿌리입니다. 사소한 약점이라는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: free from undue bias or preconceived opinions

examples.text: A judge must remain impartial and decide each case solely on the evidence presented in court.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 impartial에서 왔고 partial(한쪽으로 치우친)에 부정 접두사가 붙은 말입니다.

senses.en: lacking propriety and good taste in manners and conduct

examples.text: The guest's indecorous remarks at the funeral shocked the grieving family.

origin.ko: 라틴어 indecōrus에서 왔습니다. decorous(품위 있는)에 부정 접두사가 붙었습니다.

senses.en: stopping and starting at irregular intervals

examples.text: intermittent rain showers

origin.ko: 라틴어 intermittens '중간에 보내는'에서 왔습니다. 사이사이 끊어 내보내니 '간헐적인'입니다.

senses.en: cause to be interested or curious

examples.text: The strange symbols carved on the wall intrigued the archaeologists, who spent weeks trying to decipher them.

senses.en: a crafty and involved plot to achieve your (usually sinister) ends

examples.text: The novel follows a web of political intrigue at the royal court, where every courtier plots against a rival.

origin.ko: 이탈리아어를 거쳐 라틴어 intrīcō '얽히게 하다'에서 왔습니다. 얽힌 음모에서 호기심을 끄는 뜻이 되었습니다.

senses.en: characterized by motion

examples.text: modern dance has been called kinetic pantomime

senses.en: relating to the motion of material bodies and the forces associated therewith

examples.text: kinetic energy

origin.ko: 그리스어 kinētikós '움직이게 하는'에서 왔고 kinéō '움직이다'에서 나왔습니다.

senses.en: A curse.

examples.text: The exiled prince hurled a bitter malediction at the court that had betrayed him.

origin.ko: 라틴어 maledictiō에서 왔고 malus(나쁜)와 dictiō(말)가 합쳐졌습니다. 나쁜 말을 퍼붓는 '저주'입니다.

senses.en: based on pretense; deceptively pleasing

examples.text: The film's earnest message was undercut by a meretricious plot built on cheap spectacle.

senses.en: tastelessly showy

examples.text: The hotel lobby was a meretricious display of gilt and marble.

origin.ko: 라틴어 meretrīcius에서 왔고 meretrīx '창녀'에서 나왔습니다. 겉만 화려하게 꾸며 유혹한다는 뜻으로 번졌습니다.

senses.en: have force or influence; bring about an effect or change

examples.text: Trade sanctions militate against international cooperation.

origin.ko: 라틴어 mīlitō '군인으로 복무하다'에서 왔습니다. 맞서 싸우듯 어떤 쪽으로 작용한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: caused by or evidencing a mentally disturbed condition

examples.text: a pathological liar

senses.en: caused by or altered by or manifesting disease or pathology

examples.text: The biopsy revealed pathological changes in the liver tissue.

origin.ko: 그리스어 páskhō '겪다'와 -logía '학문'에서 나온 말로, 병을 다루는 학문에서 병적인 상태를 가리키게 되었습니다.

senses.en: having precise or logical relevance to the matter at hand

examples.text: a list of articles pertinent to the discussion

origin.ko: 라틴어 pertinēns '~에 닿는, 속하는'에서 왔습니다. 어떤 일에 닿아 있다는 데서 관련 있다는 뜻이 되었습니다.

senses.en: the entire range of skills or aptitudes or devices used in a particular field or occupation

examples.text: The negotiator's repertoire of tactics ranged from patient listening to calculated silence.

senses.en: a collection of works (plays, songs, operas, ballets) that an artist or company can perform and do perform for short intervals on a regular schedule

examples.text: The opera company's repertoire includes works by Mozart and Verdi.

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 repertōrium('목록, 재고')에서 온 프랑스어를 빌려 왔습니다. 공연할 수 있는 작품 목록을 뜻합니다.

senses.en: characteristic of rural life

examples.text: The inn's rustic charm, with its stone walls and wooden beams, drew tourists from the city.

senses.en: awkwardly simple and provincial

examples.text: The city snobs mocked his rustic manners, though he was far shrewder than he appeared.

origin.ko: 라틴어 rūsticus(시골의)에서 왔습니다. 시골의 소박한 모습을 가리킵니다.

senses.en: demanding strict attention to rules and procedures

examples.text: They have stringent quality requirements outlining what is acceptable.

origin.ko: 라틴어 stringēns(팽팽히 조이는)에서 왔습니다. 바짝 조이듯 엄격한 규칙을 뜻합니다.

senses.en: provide physical relief, as from pain

examples.text: The new medication helped alleviate the patient's chronic pain without serious side effects.

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 alleviare(가볍게 하다)에서 왔습니다. 짐을 가볍게 덜어준다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: deviation from the normal or common order or form or rule

examples.text: The unusually warm week in January was an anomaly in an otherwise bitterly cold winter.

origin.ko: 그리스어 anōmalia(고르지 않음)에서 왔습니다. homalos(평평한)를 부정해 '울퉁불퉁한 예외'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: expressing yourself easily or characterized by clear expressive language

examples.text: She’s a bright, articulate young woman.

senses.en: put into words or an expression

examples.text: I like this painting, but I can’t articulate why.

senses.en: unite by forming a joint or joints

examples.text: The lower jaw articulates with the skull at the temporomandibular joint.

origin.ko: 라틴어 articulatus(마디가 있는)에서 왔습니다. 말을 마디마디 또렷이 끊어 낸다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: a reappearance of an earlier characteristic

examples.text: The recurrence of tribal rivalries in the region struck the historian as a kind of political atavism.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 atavisme에서 왔고 라틴어 atavus(고조부, 조상)에서 나왔습니다. 조상의 특징이 다시 나타나는 현상입니다.

senses.en: marked by active interest and enthusiasm

examples.text: an avid sports fan

senses.en: (often followed by ‘for’) ardently or excessively desirous

examples.text: avid for adventure

origin.ko: 라틴어 avidus(탐하는, 열망하는)에서 왔고 aveo(갈망하다)에서 나왔습니다.

senses.en: without any attempt at concealment; completely obvious

examples.text: The company showed a blatant disregard for safety rules, ignoring repeated warnings from inspectors.

senses.en: conspicuously and offensively loud; given to vehement outcry

examples.text: The blatant music from the street fair kept the whole neighborhood awake until dawn.

origin.ko: 1596년 스펜서가 시에서 'blatant beast'라는 말로 처음 썼습니다. bleat(메에 울다)에서 왔다고 추정됩니다.

senses.en: A good thing; a thing to be thankful for or to appreciate duly.

examples.text: Finding the dry cave was a boon to the weary travellers.

senses.en: very close and convivial

examples.text: The two old sailors remained boon companions long after they retired from the sea.

origin.ko: 고대 노르드어 bón('기도, 청원')에서 왔고, '좋은'을 뜻하는 boon의 영향으로 '고마운 혜택'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: To admit or agree to be true; to acknowledge

examples.text: The author concedes that her sample size was small but insists the trend is real.

senses.en: acknowledge defeat

examples.text: The candidate conceded after enough votes had come in to show that he would lose

origin.ko: 라틴어 concēdō('양보하다')에서 왔고, con-(완전히)과 cēdō(물러나다)가 합쳐졌습니다.

senses.en: secret or hidden; not openly practiced or engaged in or shown or avowed

examples.text: covert operations

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 covert(덮인)에서 왔고 cover의 과거분사입니다. 덮여 있어 '은밀한' 뜻이 되었습니다.

senses.en: Temperament, temperamental makeup or habitual mood.

examples.text: She has a sunny disposition.

senses.en: an attitude of mind especially one that favors one alternative over others

examples.text: Salt has a disposition to dissolve in water.

senses.en: Final decision or settlement.

examples.text: The disposition of the case will be announced tomorrow.

origin.ko: 라틴어 dispositiō(배치)에서 왔습니다. 마음이 놓인 상태가 '기질'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: assemble or get together

examples.text: The survey team garnered data from more than two thousand households across the region.

senses.en: acquire or deserve by one's efforts or actions

examples.text: The young director garnered widespread praise for her debut film.

origin.ko: 라틴어 grānārium '곡물 창고'에서 왔고 granary와 같은 말에서 갈라진 쌍둥이입니다. 곡식을 창고에 거두어들이는 이미지입니다.

senses.en: Corruption in official life.

examples.text: The investigation uncovered years of graft in the city's construction contracts.

senses.en: cause to grow together parts from different plants

examples.text: graft the cherry tree branch onto the plum tree

senses.en: pay close attention to; give heed to

examples.text: Heed the advice of the old men

origin.ko: 고대영어 hēdan '주의하다, 지키다'에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: belonging to a thing by its very nature

examples.text: the intrinsic value of gold or silver

origin.ko: 라틴어 intrīnsecus '안쪽에서'에서 왔습니다. 안에 속해 있으니 '본질적인'입니다.

senses.en: lacking in rigor or strictness

examples.text: such lax and slipshod ways are no longer acceptable

senses.en: lacking in firmness or tension; not taut

examples.text: a lax rope

origin.ko: 라틴어 laxus '넓은, 느슨한'에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: (used with regard to idealized country life) idyllically rustic

examples.text: The painter's pastoral landscapes show sheep grazing beside quiet streams.

senses.en: a literary work idealizing the rural life (especially the life of shepherds)

examples.text: Virgil's pastoral poems helped establish a lasting literary tradition.

origin.ko: 라틴어 pāstōrālis '목자의'에서 왔고, pāstor는 '양치기'입니다. 양치기가 있는 목가적 전원을 가리킵니다.

senses.en: make (one thing) compatible with (another)

examples.text: It is hard to reconcile the company's green slogans with its record of polluting nearby rivers.

senses.en: To restore a friendly relationship; to bring back or return to harmony.

examples.text: to reconcile people who have quarrelled

senses.en: accept as inevitable

examples.text: After years of appeals, she finally reconciled herself to the loss of the family farm.

origin.ko: 라틴어 reconciliāre('다시 화해시키다')에서 왔습니다. 어긋난 것을 다시 맞춘다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: abounding in or given to pompous or aphoristic moralizing

examples.text: His sententious remarks quickly bored the audience.

senses.en: concise and full of meaning

examples.text: The editor admired her sententious prose, in which every sentence carried a complete thought.

origin.ko: 라틴어 sententia(의견, 격언)에서 왔습니다. 격언을 늘어놓으며 훈계하는 말투입니다.

senses.en: effusively or insincerely emotional

examples.text: The film's sentimental ending, with its swelling strings and tearful reunion, felt manipulative.

senses.en: Derived from emotion rather than logical reason.

examples.text: She kept the broken watch for sentimental reasons, though it had no practical value.

origin.ko: sentiment(감정)에 -al이 붙었습니다. 감정에 치우친 상태를 뜻합니다.

senses.en: having more than one possible meaning

examples.text: The ambiguous wording of the contract allowed each side to claim victory in the dispute.

origin.ko: 라틴어 ambiguus(이리저리 오락가락하는)에서 왔습니다. 양쪽으로 흔들려 뜻이 정해지지 않은 상태입니다.

senses.en: showing a cheerful willingness to do favors for others

examples.text: The complaisant host agreed to every request his guests made, however inconvenient.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 complaisant('기꺼이 비위를 맞추는')에서 왔고, 라틴어 complacēre(잘 기쁘게 하다)가 뿌리입니다.

senses.en: Skeptical of the integrity, sincerity, or motives of others.

examples.text: Years of covering city politics had made the reporter cynical about every promise a candidate made.

origin.ko: 그리스어 kunikós(개 같은)에서 왔습니다. 견유학파(Cynic)를 가리키던 말이 '냉소적인'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: constituting a separate entity or part

examples.text: a government with three discrete divisions

origin.ko: 라틴어 discrētus(갈라진)에서 왔습니다. discreet와 이중어입니다.

senses.en: be of different opinions

examples.text: Several Republicans dissented

senses.en: Disagreement with the ideas, doctrines, decrees, etc. of a political party, government or religion.

examples.text: A system that suppresses dissent is fault-intolerant, ignorant and fragile.

origin.ko: 라틴어 dissentīre(다르게 느끼다)에서 왔습니다. 생각이 서로 달라 '반대하다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: separation into component parts

examples.text: The dissolution of the empire left dozens of newly independent states in its wake.

senses.en: The termination of an organized body or legislative assembly, especially a formal dismissal.

examples.text: The dissolution of parliament triggered a snap election within six weeks.

senses.en: The quality of being dissolute.

examples.text: He led a life of dissolution, drinking and gambling almost daily.

origin.ko: 라틴어 dissolūtiō(풀어 해체함)에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: failing to provide for the future; reckless

examples.text: His improvident spending left the family with no savings when the factory unexpectedly closed.

origin.ko: 라틴어 improvidens에서 왔습니다. 앞(pro)을 내다보지(vid) 않는다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: full of or showing high-spirited merriment

examples.text: The jocund crowd sang late into the night after the harvest festival.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어를 거쳐 라틴어 iūcundus '즐거운, 유쾌한'에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: scope for freedom of e.g. action or thought; freedom from restriction

examples.text: His parents gave him a great deal of latitude.

senses.en: an imaginary line around the Earth parallel to the equator

examples.text: snow showers in the northerly latitudes

origin.ko: 라틴어 lātitūdō '넓이, 폭'에서 왔고 lātus(넓은)에서 나왔습니다. 폭이 넓어 여유가 있다는 데서 '재량'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: A counterintuitive conclusion or outcome.

examples.text: It is an interesting paradox that drinking a lot of water can often make you feel thirsty.

senses.en: A person or thing having contradictory properties.

examples.text: He is a paradox; you would not expect him in that political party.

origin.ko: 그리스어 parádoxos '예상 밖의'에서 왔습니다. 통념에서 벗어난 의견이라는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: Physical beauty.

examples.text: The painter was renowned for portraits that captured the pulchritude of her aristocratic subjects.

origin.ko: 라틴어 pulchritūdō에서 왔으며 pulcher('아름다운')에서 나왔습니다.

senses.en: supply sparingly and with restricted quantities

examples.text: The next party you throw, don't stint on the beer.

senses.en: A period of time spent doing or being something; a spell.

examples.text: He had a stint in jail.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 styntan(무디게 하다, 짧게 하다)에서 왔습니다. 양을 줄여 아낀다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: obstreperous and defiant aggressiveness

examples.text: The striker's truculence toward referees earned him a reputation as the league's most disruptive player.

origin.ko: 라틴어 truculentia에서 왔고 trux('사나운')와 이어집니다.

senses.en: habitually speaking the truth

examples.text: a veracious witness

senses.en: precisely accurate

examples.text: The historian was praised for a veracious account that avoided both myth and propaganda.

origin.ko: 라틴어 vērāx('진실한')에 -acious를 붙였고 vērus('참된')와 이어집니다.

senses.en: marked by keen caution and watchful prudence

examples.text: He is wary of dogs.

senses.en: openly distrustful and unwilling to confide

examples.text: After being cheated once, the investors grew wary of any proposal that promised quick returns.

origin.ko: 형용사 ware('조심하는')에 -y를 붙인 말입니다. '경계하는'이라는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: being of striking appropriateness and pertinence

examples.text: an apt metaphor

senses.en: (usually followed by ‘to’) naturally disposed toward

examples.text: This tree, if unprotected, is apt to be stripped of its leaves by a leaf-cutting ant.

senses.en: mentally quick and resourceful

examples.text: an apt pupil

origin.ko: 라틴어 aptus(알맞은, 들어맞는)에서 왔습니다. 서로 꼭 맞게 붙는다는 이미지입니다.

senses.en: lack of respect accompanied by a feeling of intense dislike

examples.text: She regarded the empty promises of politicians with open contempt.

senses.en: a willful disobedience to or disrespect for the authority of a court or legislative body

examples.text: The witness was held in contempt of court after repeatedly refusing to answer.

origin.ko: 라틴어 contemptus('경멸')에서 왔고, contemnō(경멸하다)에서 갈라졌습니다.

senses.en: characterized by a firm and humorless belief in the validity of your opinions

examples.text: both sides were deeply in earnest, even passionate

senses.en: Strenuous; diligent.

examples.text: earnest efforts

senses.en: A sum of money paid in advance as a deposit; hence, a pledge, a guarantee, an indication of something to come.

examples.text: The firm paid a small sum as earnest money to show it intended to complete the purchase.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 eornest(진지함, 열의)에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: capable of being done with means at hand and circumstances as they are

examples.text: Engineers concluded that building the tunnel was feasible only if the government agreed to fund it.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 faisable(할 수 있는)에서 왔고 라틴어 facere(하다)가 바탕입니다. 해낼 수 있어 '실행 가능한'입니다.

senses.en: be a mystery or bewildering to

examples.text: The complexity of the tax code flummoxed even experienced accountants.

senses.en: To avoid verbal commitment.

examples.text: He carefully hedged his statements with weasel words.

senses.en: minimize loss or risk

examples.text: Many investors buy gold to hedge against inflation and currency swings.

senses.en: a fence formed by a row of closely planted shrubs or bushes

examples.text: A tall hedge of boxwood screened the garden from the road.

origin.ko: 고대영어 heċġ '울타리'에서 왔습니다. 울타리를 쳐 두듯 확답을 피하고 빠져나갈 구석을 남깁니다.

senses.en: close in time; about to occur

examples.text: Forecasters warned that a major storm was imminent and urged coastal residents to evacuate immediately.

origin.ko: 라틴어 imminēre '위로 드리워지다'에서 왔습니다. 머리 위에 걸려 곧 떨어질 듯한 이미지가 '임박한'입니다.

senses.en: The act of imprecating, or invoking evil upon someone; a prayer that a curse or calamity may befall someone.

examples.text: The defeated tyrant hurled bitter imprecations at the crowd as soldiers led him from the palace.

origin.ko: 라틴어 imprecātiō '저주를 부름'에서 왔고 imprecor(불러 청하다)가 뿌리입니다. 누군가에게 재앙을 빌어 청하는 기도입니다.

senses.en: make flesh-colored

examples.text: The setting sun seemed to incarnadine the clouds, turning the whole western sky a deep blood red.

origin.ko: 이탈리아어 incarnadino '살빛'에서 왔고 라틴어 carō(살)가 뿌리입니다. 살빛에서 핏빛 붉은색으로 물들이는 뜻이 되었습니다.

senses.en: no longer in use

examples.text: Digital cameras made film-based photography nearly obsolete within a single decade.

origin.ko: 라틴어 obsolētus '닳아 없어진, 쓰이지 않게 된'에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: related to the key issue but not of central importance

examples.text: energy is far from a peripheral issue in the economy

senses.en: on or near an edge or constituting an outer boundary; the outer area

examples.text: peripheral suburbs

origin.ko: 그리스어 periphéreia '둘레'에서 왔습니다. 중심이 아니라 가장자리에 있어 부수적이라는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: a symbol of disgrace or infamy

examples.text: Hence, the stigma attached to mental disorders in general forms the basis of the stigma towards women with mental health problems. […]

origin.ko: 그리스어 stigma(노예나 죄인에게 찍던 표시)에서 왔고 stizō(찍다)와 이어집니다. 살갗에 찍은 낙인이 오명이 되었습니다.

senses.en: tending to vary often or widely

examples.text: Investors avoided the volatile market, where prices swung wildly from one day to the next.

senses.en: liable to lead to sudden change or violence

examples.text: Troops were sent to keep order in the volatile border region after the disputed election.

senses.en: evaporating readily at normal temperatures and pressures

examples.text: Volatile solvents such as acetone must be stored in sealed containers to prevent evaporation.

origin.ko: 라틴어 volātilis('날아다니는')에서 왔고 volō('날다')와 이어집니다. 날아가 버리듯 불안정한 것입니다.

senses.en: tending to find and call attention to faults

examples.text: The captious reviewer seized on every small error and ignored the book's real achievements.

origin.ko: 라틴어 captiōsus(말로 함정에 빠뜨리는)에서 왔습니다. 꼬투리를 잡으려 드는 성격입니다.

senses.en: Something that encourages progress or change.

examples.text: Economic development and integration are working as a catalyst for peace.

senses.en: (chemistry) a substance that initiates or accelerates a chemical reaction without itself being affected

examples.text: Platinum serves as a catalyst in the converter, speeding up the breakdown of harmful exhaust gases.

origin.ko: 그리스어 katalysis('풀어 헤침')에서 왔습니다. 굳은 상태를 풀어 변화를 일으키는 것이라는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: wilfully obstinate; stubbornly disobedient

examples.text: The contumacious witness ignored the court's summons for the third time.

origin.ko: 라틴어 contumāx('고집 센, 완강한')에 -ious가 붙은 말입니다.

senses.en: capable of being believed

examples.text: The defense offered no credible explanation for why the documents had been shredded.

senses.en: Dependable, trustworthy, or reliable.

examples.text: credible sources

origin.ko: 라틴어 crēdibilis(믿을 만한)에서 왔고, crēdō(믿다)에서 나온 말입니다.

senses.en: characterized by conscious design or purpose

examples.text: a deliberate attempt to cover up his crime

senses.en: unhurried and with care and dignity

examples.text: with all deliberate speed

senses.en: think about carefully; weigh

examples.text: The jury deliberated for two days before reaching a unanimous verdict.

origin.ko: 라틴어 dēlīberāre(저울질하다)에서 왔습니다. 저울에 달 듯 따져보고 한 일이라 '고의적인'입니다.

senses.en: To embarrass (someone) greatly; to confuse; to perplex; to disconcert.

examples.text: The reporter's blunt question visibly discomfited the minister, who fumbled for an answer.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 desconfit(패배한)에서 왔습니다. 원래 '무너뜨리다'였고 discomfort와 혼동되어 '당황시키다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: be greater in significance than

examples.text: The young pianist's brilliance soon eclipsed the fame of her more celebrated teacher.

senses.en: Obscurity, decline, downfall.

examples.text: The once-powerful dynasty fell into eclipse after losing its last overseas colonies.

senses.en: one celestial body obscures another

examples.text: Crowds gathered on the plain to watch the total eclipse of the sun.

origin.ko: 그리스어 ekleípō(버리고 떠나다, 사라지다)에서 왔습니다. 해나 달이 사라지는 '식'에서 '가리다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: find repugnant

examples.text: Many citizens execrated the dictator long before his regime finally collapsed.

senses.en: To declare to be hateful or abhorrent; to denounce.

examples.text: The crowd gathered outside the courthouse to execrate the officials who had approved the scheme.

origin.ko: 라틴어 execrārī(저주하다)에서 왔습니다. 대상을 저주받은 것으로 선언한다는 데서 몹시 혐오한다는 뜻이 되었습니다.

senses.en: To write or speak at length; to be copious in argument or discussion.
