examples.text: The professor expatiated on the causes of the war for nearly an hour without notes.

origin.ko: 라틴어 expatiārī(널리 거닐다)에서 왔습니다. 말이 넓게 돌아다니듯 길게 늘어놓는다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: A group of people, especially within a political organization, which expresses a shared belief or opinion different from people who are not part of the group.

examples.text: A radical faction within the party threatened to withdraw its support unless the leadership changed course.

senses.en: Strife; discord.

examples.text: Years of faction and distrust left the young republic unable to agree on even basic laws.

origin.ko: 라틴어 factiō(함께 행동하는 무리)에서 왔습니다. 같은 일을 하는 한 패가 '파벌'입니다.

senses.en: hinder or prevent (the efforts, plans, or desires) of

examples.text: Alert security officers foiled the attempted robbery before the thieves could reach the vault.

senses.en: anything that serves by contrast to call attention to another thing's good qualities

examples.text: In the novel, the cynical sidekick serves as a foil to the idealistic hero.

origin.ko: 중세 영어 foilen(냄새 자취를 밟아 흐리게 하다)에서 왔습니다. 사냥감의 흔적을 밟아 지워 추적을 막는 데서 '좌절시키다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: existing as an essential constituent or characteristic

examples.text: Some risk is inherent in any investment, however carefully the portfolio is diversified.

origin.ko: 라틴어 inhaerēre '~에 딱 붙어 있다'에서 왔습니다. 안에 붙어 떨어지지 않으니 '본질적인'입니다.

senses.en: gracefully thin and bending and moving with ease

examples.text: The lissome dancer crossed the stage in three effortless leaps.

origin.ko: lissom의 변형입니다.

senses.en: To feign illness, injury, or incapacitation in order to avoid work, obligation, or perilous risk.

examples.text: It is not uncommon on exam days for several students to malinger rather than prepare themselves.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 malingre '허약한'에서 온 malingrer에서 왔습니다. 허약한 척한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: Of speech or writing: bombastic, pompous.

examples.text: The senator's orotund oratory filled the chamber but said remarkably little.

senses.en: (of sounds) full and rich

examples.text: orotund tones

origin.ko: 라틴어 ōre rotundō, 즉 '둥근 입으로'에서 왔습니다. 입을 크게 둥글려 말하는 데서 과장되고 거창한 말투가 되었습니다.

senses.en: radiating or as if radiating light

examples.text: The refulgent dome of the cathedral glowed in the late afternoon sun.

origin.ko: 라틴어 refulgēre('되비쳐 빛나다')의 현재분사에서 왔습니다. 눈부시게 빛을 내뿜는 모습입니다.

senses.en: taking place within the mind and modified by individual bias

examples.text: a subjective judgment

origin.ko: 라틴어 subiectīvus에서 왔고 subject에 -ive가 붙었습니다. 개인의 마음 아래에 놓인 주관적인 것을 뜻합니다.

senses.en: make more temperate, acceptable, or suitable by adding something else

examples.text: The editor tempered her harsh critique with genuine praise for the author's vivid characters.

senses.en: A tendency to become angry.

examples.text: He has quite a temper when dealing with salespeople.

senses.en: To strengthen or toughen a material, especially metal, by heat treatment; anneal.

examples.text: The blacksmith tempered the blade in oil so that it would hold an edge without becoming brittle.

origin.ko: 라틴어 temperāre(알맞게 섞다, 조절하다)에서 왔습니다. 강한 것을 누그러뜨려 균형을 맞춘다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: Sharp; caustic.

examples.text: The critic's acidulous review left the playwright wounded and the cast quietly furious.

senses.en: being sour to the taste

examples.text: The acidulous sauce balanced the richness of the roasted duck.

origin.ko: 라틴어 acidulus(약간 신)에서 왔습니다. 약간 시큼한 맛이 톡 쏘는 말투를 뜻하게 되었습니다.

senses.en: (of political bodies) not controlled by outside forces

examples.text: an autonomous judiciary

senses.en: (of persons) free from external control and constraint in e.g. action and judgment

examples.text: Teachers argue that autonomous students learn more than those who simply follow instructions.

origin.ko: 그리스어 autonomos(자기 법을 따르는)에서 왔습니다. 스스로 정한 법으로 사는 상태입니다.

senses.en: the outside boundary or surface of something

examples.text: Small farms survive only on the fringe of the expanding suburbs.

senses.en: a social group holding marginal or extreme views

examples.text: Ideas once confined to the political fringe have gradually entered mainstream debate.

origin.ko: 라틴어 fimbriae(술, 가장자리 실)에서 왔습니다. 천 가장자리의 술에서 '가장자리, 주변부'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: Having a tendency, preference, likelihood, or disposition.

examples.text: I am inclined to believe you.

senses.en: At an angle to the horizontal; slanted or sloped.

examples.text: The take-off ramp was inclined at 20 degrees.

origin.ko: incline(기울다)에서 온 말입니다. 마음이 어떤 쪽으로 기울어 있어 '~하는 경향이 있는'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: Adhering to whatever is customary, traditional, or generally accepted.

examples.text: The orthodox view among economists held that lower taxes would raise growth, but the data disagreed.

senses.en: Conforming to the accepted, established, or traditional doctrines of a given faith, religion, or ideology.

examples.text: The orthodox clergy condemned the new interpretation as a departure from sacred doctrine.

origin.ko: 그리스어 orthodoxos, 즉 '바른(orthós) 의견(dóxa)'에서 왔습니다. 정통이라 인정받는 견해를 따른다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: stubbornly unyielding

examples.text: The pertinacious reporter pursued the story despite repeated threats from officials.

origin.ko: 라틴어 pertinax '아주 꽉 붙잡고 놓지 않는'에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: showing intellectual penetration or emotional depth

examples.text: a profound insight

senses.en: far-reaching and thoroughgoing in effect especially on the nature of something

examples.text: The invention of printing had a profound effect on the spread of literacy across Europe.

origin.ko: 라틴어 profundus('깊은')에서 왔고, pro('앞으로')와 fundus('바닥')가 합쳐졌습니다. 바닥까지 닿는 깊이입니다.

senses.en: Likely or expected to happen or become.

examples.text: Prospective students are those who have already applied to the university, but have yet to be admitted.

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 prospectivus에서 왔습니다. 앞을 내다본다는 뜻에서 '장래의'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: strong enough to withstand or overcome intellectual challenges or adversity

examples.text: the experiment yielded robust results

senses.en: sturdy and strong in form, constitution, or construction

examples.text: He was a robust man of six feet four.

origin.ko: 라틴어 rōbustus(참나무처럼 단단한)에서 왔습니다. 굳센 참나무가 튼튼함의 이미지입니다.

senses.en: go up or advance

examples.text: The company's fortunes waxed as demand for its software soared.

senses.en: increase in phase

examples.text: As the moon waxes toward full, the tides along the coast grow stronger.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 weaxan('자라다')에서 왔습니다. 달이 차오르듯 커지는 것이 '커지다'입니다.

senses.en: An inclination or talent.

examples.text: He had a natural bent for painting.

senses.en: Determined or insistent; inclined, set.

examples.text: They were bent on mischief.

origin.ko: bend(구부리다)에 -t가 붙은 말입니다. 마음이 한쪽으로 기운 데서 '성향, 소질'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: tending to persuade by forcefulness of argument

examples.text: He made a compelling argument.

senses.en: very interesting; able to capture and hold one's attention

examples.text: The novel was so compelling that I couldn't put it down.

origin.ko: compel(강요하다)에 -ing가 붙은 말입니다. 마음을 몰아붙이는 설득력입니다.

senses.en: precisely and clearly expressed or readily observable; leaving nothing to implication

examples.text: I gave explicit instructions for him to stay here, but he followed me, anyway.

origin.ko: 라틴어 explicitus(펼쳐진, 풀린)에서 프랑스어를 거쳐 왔습니다. 접힌 곳 없이 활짝 펼쳐 분명하다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: avoid or try to avoid fulfilling, answering, or performing (duties, questions, or issues)

examples.text: The minister skirted the question of tax increases throughout the entire interview.

senses.en: pass around or about; move along the border

examples.text: The boat skirted the coast

origin.ko: 고대 노르드어 skyrta(셔츠, 앞치마)에서 왔고 '짧게 자른 것'과 이어집니다. 가장자리를 돌아 피해 간다는 뜻이 나왔습니다.

senses.en: To imbue with something; to immerse deeply in.

examples.text: a town steeped in history

senses.en: greatly exceeding bounds of reason or moderation

examples.text: Many residents found the new rents too steep to afford and began leaving the neighborhood.

senses.en: having a sharp inclination

examples.text: steep cliffs

origin.ko: 동사 steep은 고대 노르드어 steypa(쏟다, 담그다)에서 왔습니다. 액체에 푹 담가 스며들게 한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: capable of being done with means at hand and circumstances as they are

examples.text: Engineers concluded that solar power was a viable option for the remote island's electricity needs.

senses.en: capable of life or normal growth and development

examples.text: Only a fraction of the seeds stored in the old vault were still viable after decades.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 viable에서 왔고 라틴어 vīta('삶')와 이어집니다. 살아갈 수 있다는 뜻이 '실행 가능한'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: lie adjacent to another or share a boundary

examples.text: The new library abuts the old courthouse, sharing a wall along its entire eastern side.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 abuter(끝이 닿다)에서 왔습니다. 한쪽 끝이 다른 것에 맞닿는다는 뜻에서 '인접하다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: marked by strong resentment or cynicism

examples.text: The acrimonious divorce dragged on for years, with each side accusing the other of deceit.

origin.ko: 라틴어 acrimonia(매서움)에서 왔고 acer(날카로운)와 연결됩니다. 맛이 맵고 쓰듯 말이 험악하다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: put on trial or hear a case and sit as the judge at the trial of

examples.text: A special tribunal was created to adjudicate disputes between the two trading partners.

origin.ko: 라틴어 adiudicare(판결을 내리다)에서 왔습니다. ad와 iudicare(재판하다)가 합쳐진 말입니다.

senses.en: declare invalid

examples.text: The high court moved to annul the election results after finding evidence of widespread fraud.

origin.ko: 라틴어 annullare(없는 것으로 만들다)에서 왔습니다. 효력을 0으로 되돌린다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: evident without proof or argument

examples.text: It is axiomatic that the "physical entry of the home is the chief evil against which the wording of the Fourth Amendment is directed."

origin.ko: 그리스어 axiomatikos(공리의)에서 왔고 axioma(자명한 원리)에서 나왔습니다.

senses.en: discuss lightly

examples.text: to have one's name bandied about (or around)

senses.en: To give and receive reciprocally; to exchange.

examples.text: to bandy words (with somebody)

origin.ko: 프랑스어 bander(테니스에서 공을 주고받다)에서 왔습니다. 공을 이리저리 주고받듯 말을 오가게 한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: Confused or perplexed.

examples.text: The befuddled tourists studied the subway map for several minutes before finding the right line.

senses.en: leave or give by will after one's death

examples.text: My aunt bequeathed me all her jewelry

senses.en: To hand down; to transmit.

examples.text: The ancient empire bequeathed to later generations a legal tradition that still shapes modern law.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 becweþan(말하다, 유언으로 남기다)에서 왔습니다. 말로 남긴다는 뜻이 '유증하다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: turn pale, as if in fear

examples.text: His cheek blanched with fear.

senses.en: To take the color out of, and make white; to bleach.

examples.text: Age has blanched his hair.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 blanc(흰)에서 온 blanchir('하얗게 만들다')가 어원입니다. 핏기가 가셔 얼굴이 하얘지는 모습입니다.

senses.en: a clear seasoned broth

examples.text: The chef simmered beef bones overnight to make a rich bouillon for the soup.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 bouillir('끓다')에서 왔고, 라틴어 bulla(거품)까지 거슬러 올라갑니다. 보글보글 끓인 국물입니다.

senses.en: an injury that doesn't break the skin but results in some discoloration

examples.text: The fall left a large contusion on his thigh but no broken bones.

origin.ko: 중세 프랑스어 contusion에서 왔고, 라틴어 contundō('두들기다')가 뿌리입니다. 세게 두들겨 생긴 멍입니다.

senses.en: To crouch or cringe, or to avoid or shy away from something, in fear.

examples.text: The villagers cowered in their cellars while the storm tore roofs from the houses.

origin.ko: 중세 저지 독일어 kûren(웅크리고 숨어 기다리다) 등에서 왔다고 봅니다. 몸을 구부린 자세가 '움츠러들다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: worthy of often limited commendation

examples.text: the student's effort on the essay — though not outstanding — was creditable

senses.en: A young woman who makes her first formal appearance in society.

examples.text: The debutante curtsied to the guests at the ball her family had hosted in her honor.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 débutante에서 왔고 debut(첫 등장)에 -ante가 붙은 말입니다.

senses.en: marked by high spirits or excitement

examples.text: Her effervescent personality made her the center of every gathering.

senses.en: Giving off bubbles; fizzy.

examples.text: The effervescent mineral water tingled on her tongue.

origin.ko: 라틴어 effervescere(끓어 넘치다)에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: Gushy; unrestrained, extravagant or excessive (in emotional expression).

examples.text: effusive praise

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 effūsīvus에서 왔습니다. 감정을 물처럼 쏟아낸다는 이미지입니다.

senses.en: marked by complexity and richness of detail

examples.text: an elaborate lace pattern

senses.en: add details, as to an account or idea; clarify the meaning of and discourse in a learned way, usually in writing

examples.text: She elaborated on the main ideas in her dissertation

origin.ko: 라틴어 ēlabōrāre(공들여 만들어 내다)에서 왔습니다. 많은 노동을 들인 결과가 '정교한'입니다.

senses.en: being of such surpassing excellence as to suggest inspiration by the gods

examples.text: They spent an elysian week on the quiet island, free of every worry.

senses.en: (philosophy) the doctrine that knowledge derives from experience

examples.text: Hume's empiricism held that all knowledge ultimately rests on sensory experience.

origin.ko: 그리스어 empeiría(경험)에 -ismós가 붙었습니다. 지식은 경험에서 나온다는 입장입니다.

senses.en: To intrude unrightfully on someone else’s rights or territory.

examples.text: Developers continued to encroach on land the tribe had held for centuries.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 encrochier(붙잡다)에서 왔고, croc(갈고리)가 바탕입니다. 갈고리로 남의 것을 낚아채듯 침범한다는 이미지입니다.

senses.en: To set out the meaning of; to explain or discuss at length.

examples.text: Today I'll expound at length the theory propounded last week.

origin.ko: 라틴어 expōnere(밖에 내놓다)에서 고대 프랑스어를 거쳐 왔습니다. 뜻을 늘어놓아 설명한다는 이미지입니다.

senses.en: any distracting or deceptive maneuver (as a mock attack)

examples.text: The general ordered a feint along the coast to draw the enemy away from the real landing site.

senses.en: deceive by a mock action

examples.text: The fencer feinted left to lure her opponent off balance before striking from the right.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 feinte(속임)에서 왔고 라틴어 fingere(꾸며내다)가 바탕입니다. 공격하는 척하는 속임 동작입니다.

senses.en: exacting especially about details

examples.text: The finicky chef sent the dish back twice because the sauce was a degree too warm.

origin.ko: finick(사소한 일에 공들이다)에 -y가 붙었습니다. 세세한 것에 지나치게 신경 쓰는 모습입니다.

senses.en: To wave or swing vigorously

examples.text: He stopped in his tracks – then, flailing his arms wildly in the air, began to stagger backwards.

senses.en: give a thrashing to; beat hard

examples.text: The angry crowd flailed at the fallen statue with sticks and iron bars.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 fligel(도리깨)에서 왔습니다. 곡식을 터는 도리깨를 휘두르듯 팔을 마구 휘두른다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: To lash or whip.

examples.text: Critics flayed the minister in the press for his handling of the crisis.

senses.en: strip the skin off

examples.text: The hunters flayed the deer and stretched its hide to dry in the sun.

senses.en: Despondent; moody; sullen.

examples.text: The players sat glum and silent in the locker room after the defeat.

origin.ko: 중세 저지 독일어 glum '침울한'에서 왔을 것으로 봅니다. gloom(우울)과 같은 계통입니다.

senses.en: extremely difficult; requiring the strength of a Hercules

examples.text: Rebuilding the flooded town in a single season was a herculean task for the small crew.

senses.en: displaying superhuman strength or power

examples.text: With a herculean effort, the climber hauled his injured partner over the ledge.

origin.ko: 그리스 신화의 힘센 영웅 Hercules에서 온 말입니다. 헤라클레스만큼의 힘이 필요할 정도로 엄청나다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: Plain and homely; unsophisticated and unpretentious.

examples.text: The senator's homespun charm and folksy anecdotes won over skeptical rural voters.

origin.ko: home(집)과 spun(실을 자은)이 합쳐진 말입니다. 집에서 손수 짠 천처럼 소박하고 꾸밈없다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: loud confused noise from many sources

examples.text: The hubbub of the crowded market made it impossible to hold a quiet conversation.

origin.ko: 아일랜드어의 전투 함성에서 왔을 가능성이 있으며 확실하지는 않습니다.

senses.en: invade in great numbers

examples.text: the roaches infested our kitchen

origin.ko: 라틴어 īnfestus '적대적인'에서 고대 프랑스어 infester를 거쳐 왔습니다. 해로운 것이 떼로 들이닥쳐 괴롭힌다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: give character or essence to

examples.text: His sense of religion informs everything he writes.

senses.en: act as an informer

examples.text: She had informed on her own parents for years

senses.en: impart knowledge of some fact, state of affairs, or event to

examples.text: I informed him of his rights

origin.ko: 라틴어 īnfōrmō '형태를 만들다, 가르치다'에서 왔습니다. 안에 모양(form)을 새겨 특징을 부여한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: a small storeroom for storing foods or wines

examples.text: The farmhouse larder was stocked with preserves, smoked ham, and sacks of flour for the winter.

origin.ko: 앵글로노르만어를 거쳐 라틴어 lardārium에서 왔습니다. lard(돼지기름)를 보관하던 곳입니다.

senses.en: driven by lust; preoccupied with or exhibiting lustful desires

examples.text: The senator's lascivious remarks at the dinner prompted an immediate ethics inquiry.

origin.ko: 라틴어 lascīviōsus에서 왔고 lascīvia '장난기, 음탕함'에서 나왔습니다.

senses.en: A song for a small number of unaccompanied voices; from 13th century Italy.

examples.text: The choir opened its Renaissance program with a madrigal sung without any instrumental accompaniment.

origin.ko: 이탈리아어 madrigale에서 왔고 라틴어 mātrīcālis와 이어집니다.

senses.en: Any ailment or disease of the body; especially, a lingering or deep-seated disorder.

examples.text: The village doctor could not identify the strange malady that had weakened so many residents.

senses.en: any unwholesome or desperate condition

examples.text: Economists often cite corruption as the chief malady of the fragile young democracy.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 maladie '병'에서 왔고 라틴어 male habitus '상태가 나쁜'과 이어집니다.

senses.en: Of, relating to, or suggestive of war; warlike.

examples.text: The parade's martial music and marching columns stirred a fierce patriotic mood in the crowd.

origin.ko: 라틴어 Mārtiālis '전쟁의 신 마르스의'에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: Rule by merit and talent.

examples.text: As a small nation without natural resources, Singapore relies on education and meritocracy to develop its economy.

origin.ko: merit(능력)에 -cracy(지배)가 붙은 말입니다. 1956년 사회학자 앨런 폭스가 만들었습니다.

senses.en: Of or pertaining to currency, especially to coins.

examples.text: The museum's numismatic collection includes rare coins minted under the Roman Empire.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 numismatique에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: a musical composition for voices and orchestra based on a religious text

examples.text: The choir spent the winter rehearsing Handel's oratorio for the spring concert.

origin.ko: 이탈리아어 oratorio에서 왔고, 라틴어 ōrātōrius가 원형입니다.

senses.en: To decree.

examples.text: The council ordained that no new buildings be raised within the old city walls.

senses.en: To predestine.

examples.text: Believing that fate had ordained their meeting, the two refused to part.

senses.en: To admit into the ministry, for example as a priest, bishop, minister or Buddhist monk, or to authorize as a rabbi.

examples.text: She was ordained as a minister after four years of seminary training.

origin.ko: 라틴어 ordinare '질서를 세우다'에서 왔고, ordo는 '질서'입니다. 질서를 세워 법으로 정한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: out of fashion

examples.text: Critics claimed that the grand narrative style had become passe by the 1980s.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 passé '지나간'에서 왔습니다. 시대가 지나간 한물간 것이라는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: relating to or involving money

examples.text: He chose the degree for pecuniary reasons, but had no real interest in it.

origin.ko: 라틴어 pecūnia '돈'에서 왔고, 가축(pecū)이 곧 재산이었던 데서 나왔습니다.

senses.en: expressing sorrow

examples.text: The plaintive cry of the lost child echoed across the empty station.

origin.ko: 옛 프랑스어 pleintif '한탄하는'에서 왔고, plainte는 '탄식'입니다.

senses.en: talk in a dogmatic and pompous manner

examples.text: The new professor always pontificates

origin.ko: 라틴어 pontifex('다리를 만드는 사람', 대제사장)에서 왔습니다. 교황처럼 독단적으로 말한다는 뜻이 되었습니다.

senses.en: the property of being extremely abundant

examples.text: Wildflowers grew in profusion along the roadside after the spring rains.

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 profusio에서 왔습니다. 쏟아져 넘치는 풍부함입니다.

senses.en: to gather something into small wrinkles or folds

examples.text: The child puckered her face at the sour taste of the lemon.

senses.en: a feeling of deep and bitter anger and ill-will

examples.text: Years after the lawsuit, rancor still poisoned relations between the two branches of the family.

origin.ko: 라틴어 rancor('썩은 냄새, 원한')에서 왔고 rancid('썩은')와 같은 뿌리입니다. 마음속에서 썩어 가는 원한입니다.

senses.en: giving or marked by complete attention to

examples.text: The audience listened in rapt silence as the survivor described her ordeal.

senses.en: feeling great rapture or delight

examples.text: The child wore a rapt expression as the fireworks lit the night sky.

origin.ko: 라틴어 raptus('낚아채인')에서 왔습니다. 마음을 빼앗겨 넋을 잃고 몰두한 상태입니다.

senses.en: tear down so as to make flat with the ground

examples.text: The old factory district was razed to make room for a public park.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 raser('깎다, 밀다')에서 왔습니다. 땅과 평평하게 밀어 버린다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: a puzzle where you decode a message consisting of pictures representing syllables and words

examples.text: The children solved the rebus by recognizing that a picture of an eye and a sea meant 'I see'.

origin.ko: 라틴어 rēbus('사물들로')에서 온 프랑스어에서 왔습니다. 글자 대신 사물 그림으로 말을 나타내는 수수께끼입니다.

senses.en: To give in or be swayed; to become less hard, harsh, or cruel; to show clemency.

examples.text: After weeks of protest, the mayor finally relented and agreed to reopen the community pool.

senses.en: To slacken; to abate.

examples.text: We waited for the storm to relent before we ventured outside.

origin.ko: 라틴어 lentus('부드러운, 유연한')에서 나온 말입니다. 굳은 마음이 다시 부드러워져 누그러진다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: unrestrained merrymaking

examples.text: Sounds of revelry drifted from the square long after midnight on the eve of the festival.

origin.ko: revel('흥청대다')에 -ry가 붙은 말입니다. 떠들썩하게 놀며 즐기는 일입니다.

senses.en: a sheath for a sword or dagger or bayonet

examples.text: The knight drew his sword from its leather scabbard and faced the approaching riders.

origin.ko: 게르만어 '칼날 보호'라는 뜻의 말에서 왔다고 봅니다. 칼날을 지키는 덮개, 곧 칼집입니다.

senses.en: a frozen dessert made primarily of fruit juice and sugar, but also containing milk or egg-white or gelatin

examples.text: After the heavy meal, the waiter brought a small dish of lemon sherbet to cleanse the palate.

origin.ko: 아랍어 sharba(마실 것)가 페르시아어와 튀르크어를 거쳐 들어왔습니다. 달콤한 과즙 음료가 얼음과자가 되었습니다.

senses.en: The act of a character speaking to themselves so as to reveal their thoughts to the audience.

examples.text: At the end of the second act the main villain gave a soliloquy detailing his plans to attack the protagonist.

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 sōliloquium에서 왔고 '혼자 말하기'를 뜻합니다. 아우구스티누스의 책 제목에서 퍼졌습니다.

senses.en: make subservient; force to submit or subdue

examples.text: The empire sought to subjugate neighboring tribes and force them to pay tribute.

senses.en: put down by force or intimidation

examples.text: The occupying army moved quickly to subjugate the rebellious provinces.

origin.ko: 라틴어 subiugāre(멍에 아래 두다)에서 왔습니다. 소에게 멍에를 씌우듯 복종시킵니다.

senses.en: difficult to detect or grasp by the mind or analyze

examples.text: The difference between the tones is subtle, but you can hear it if you listen carefully.

senses.en: able to make fine distinctions

examples.text: a subtle mind

senses.en: working or spreading in a hidden and usually injurious way

examples.text: a subtle poison

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 subtil에서 왔고 라틴어 subtīlis(가늘게 짠)와 이어집니다. 올이 가늘어 포착하기 어렵다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: Arduous or painful exertion; excessive labor, suffering, hardship.

examples.text: The memoir recounts the travail of immigrants who crossed an ocean in search of work.

senses.en: work hard

examples.text: She travailed for years over the translation before it finally reached publication.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 travail('고통')에서 왔고 라틴어 tripālium('고문 도구')까지 거슬러 올라갑니다. 고문 같은 고통이 '고역'입니다.

senses.en: Any group of three joint rulers.

examples.text: After the dictator's death, a triumvirate of generals governed the country for two uneasy years.

origin.ko: 라틴어 triumvir('세 사람 중 한 명')에서 왔습니다. 세 사람이 함께 다스리는 체제입니다.

senses.en: The condition of agreement by all parties, the state of being unanimous.

examples.text: The board reached unanimity on the merger after a single afternoon of discussion.

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 ūnanimitās('한마음')에서 왔습니다. 모두가 한마음이라서 '만장일치'입니다.

senses.en: immune to attack; incapable of being tampered with

examples.text: The hilltop fortress seemed unassailable, protected on three sides by sheer cliffs.

senses.en: Undeniable, incontestable or incontrovertible.

examples.text: She won the debate with her unassailable logic.

senses.en: lacking refinement or cultivation or taste

examples.text: I don't want to associate with uncouth people.

senses.en: Clumsy, awkward.

examples.text: The uncouth young waiter fumbled with the tray and spilled soup across the tablecloth.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 uncūþ('모르는, 낯선')에서 왔습니다. 익숙지 않아 낯설다는 뜻이 '교양 없는'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: guarantee financial support of

examples.text: A philanthropic foundation agreed to underwrite the cost of the new research wing.

senses.en: protect by insurance

examples.text: The company underwrites policies for shipping firms operating in some of the world's riskiest waters.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 underwrītan('아래에 쓰다, 서명하다')에서 왔습니다. 문서 아래에 서명해 책임진다는 뜻이 '보증하다'입니다.

senses.en: clear of accusation, blame, suspicion, or doubt with supporting proof

examples.text: New DNA evidence vindicated the prisoner after he had spent twelve years behind bars.

senses.en: show to be right by providing justification or proof

examples.text: The successful trial vindicated the scientist's long-ridiculed theory.

origin.ko: 라틴어 vindicō('권리를 주장하다, 해방하다')에서 왔습니다. 결백을 주장해 입증한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: a confused multitude of things

examples.text: They use these words to express a welter of opinions on what they think is good or bad, right or wrong, and all too readily wail ‘It's not fair!’.

senses.en: toss, roll, or rise and fall in an uncontrolled way

examples.text: The wrecked boat weltered in the heavy swell until the rescuers arrived.

origin.ko: 중세 영어 welteren('구르다')에서 왔습니다. 이리저리 뒹구는 모습이 '혼란, 뒤죽박죽'입니다.

senses.en: a fervent and even militant proponent of something

examples.text: The zealot rejected every compromise, insisting that only total victory would satisfy his cause.

origin.ko: 그리스어 zēlōtḗs('열렬한 추종자')에서 왔고 zêlos('열성')와 이어집니다.

senses.en: An attendant, assistant, or follower.

examples.text: The famous chef arrived at the market followed by a small group of eager acolytes.

origin.ko: 그리스어 akolouthos(따르는 사람, 시종)에서 왔습니다. 뒤따르며 시중드는 사람이 '추종자'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: servile flattery; exaggerated and hypocritical praise

examples.text: The young actor, unused to such adulation, struggled to keep his sense of perspective.

origin.ko: 라틴어 adulatio(아첨)에서 왔습니다. 꼬리 치며 비위를 맞추는 모습이 어원 이미지입니다.

senses.en: cause great unhappiness for; distress

examples.text: Chronic uncertainty afflicted the village for years after the factory closed.

origin.ko: 라틴어 affligere(내리치다)에서 왔습니다. 계속 얻어맞는 듯한 고통이 '괴롭히다'입니다.

senses.en: struck with fear, dread, or consternation

examples.text: Residents stood aghast as the flood swept away the footbridge they had crossed for decades.

origin.ko: 중세 영어 agasten(겁먹게 하다)에서 왔습니다. 공포로 그 자리에 얼어붙은 모습이 '질겁한'입니다.

senses.en: try to stir up public opinion

examples.text: Reformers agitated for years to win the vote for women in the province.

senses.en: cause to be agitated, excited, or roused

examples.text: The unexpected news agitated the crowd, and murmurs spread quickly through the hall.

origin.ko: 라틴어 agitare(계속 몰아대다)에서 왔습니다. 사람들을 흔들어 움직이게 하는 데서 '선동하다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: a small recess opening off a larger room
senses.ko: 알코브, 방에 딸린 움푹 들어간 공간

examples.text: A narrow bed sat in an alcove beside the fireplace, hidden from the main hall.

origin.ko: 아랍어 al-qubba(둥근 천장의 방)에서 스페인어를 거쳐 왔습니다.

senses.en: sufficiently; more than adequately

examples.text: The generous grant amply covered the costs of the expedition, leaving funds for a second season.

origin.ko: 라틴어 amplus(넓은, 풍부한)에서 온 ample에 -ly가 붙은 말입니다. 넉넉하고 풍부하다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: absence of the sense of pain without loss of consciousness

examples.text: The patient received epidural analgesia during labor and remained fully awake throughout.

origin.ko: 그리스어 analgesia(고통을 못 느낌)에서 왔습니다. an-(없는)과 algos(고통)가 합쳐진 말입니다.

senses.en: great coolness and composure under strain

examples.text: The diplomat answered the hostile questions with remarkable aplomb.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 aplomb(다림줄처럼 수직)를 그대로 빌려온 말입니다. 추처럼 흔들리지 않는 침착함을 뜻합니다.

senses.en: add to the very end

examples.text: He appended a glossary to his novel where he used an invented language

origin.ko: 라틴어 appendere(~에 매달다)에서 왔습니다. 뒤에 덧달아 붙인다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: To make a judgment (on a dispute) as an arbitrator or arbiter

examples.text: to arbitrate a disputed case

origin.ko: 라틴어 arbitrari(심판 노릇을 하다)에서 왔습니다. 제3자가 판정을 내린다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: Crafty deception.

examples.text: The notion that consequence can be as easily managed as PR is the ultimate artifice and the ultimate delusion.

senses.en: a deceptive maneuver (especially to avoid capture)

examples.text: The spy escaped across the border through an elaborate artifice involving forged papers.

origin.ko: 라틴어 artificium(솜씨로 만든 것)에서 왔습니다. 재주를 부린 꾸밈이 '교활한 속임수'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: with care and persistence

examples.text: she worked assiduously on the senior thesis

origin.ko: assiduous(부지런한)에 -ly가 붙은 말입니다. 라틴어 '곁에 앉아 있는'에서 나왔습니다.

senses.en: into parts or pieces

examples.text: The bitter dispute threatened to tear the coalition asunder.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 on sundur(따로, 떨어져)에서 왔습니다. 서로 갈라져 따로 떨어진 모습입니다.

senses.en: a trite or obvious remark

examples.text: The keynote speech was a string of banalities about innovation and the future of work.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 banalité에서 왔고 banal(진부한)에 -ity가 붙은 말입니다.

senses.en: humorously vulgar

examples.text: bawdy songs

senses.en: To grudge about or over; be envious or covetous.

examples.text: No one begrudged the veteran actor his award after decades of overlooked performances.

senses.en: To give reluctantly.

examples.text: The landlord begrudged every dollar he spent on repairs to the aging building.

origin.ko: 중세 영어 bigrucchen(~에 대해 투덜대다)에서 왔습니다. be-(~에 대해)와 grudge(불평)가 합쳐진 말입니다.

senses.en: a bell tower; usually stands alone unattached to a building

examples.text: Pigeons nested in the belfry, and the old bell rang only on holidays.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 berfroi(방어용 탑)에서 왔습니다. 종(bell)과 혼동되어 bel-로 바뀌어 '종탑'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: perplexed and bewildered

examples.text: The bemused audience wondered whether the strange ending was a joke or a mistake.

senses.en: deeply absorbed in thought

examples.text: The professor stood bemused at the window, lost in thought about an unsolved proof.

origin.ko: bemuse(어리둥절하게 하다)에 -ed가 붙은 말입니다. 생각에 빠져 멍한 상태입니다.

senses.en: censure severely or angrily

examples.text: The coach berated his players in the locker room after they squandered a ten-point lead.

origin.ko: be-와 rate(꾸짖다)가 합쳐진 말입니다. 몹시 호되게 나무란다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: vain and empty boasting

examples.text: Behind the senator's bluster lay a weak argument that collapsed under the first serious question.

senses.en: To speak or protest loudly.

examples.text: When confronted by opposition his reaction was to bluster, which often cowed the meek.

origin.ko: 중세 저지 독일어 blüstren('거세게 불다')의 영향을 받았습니다. 바람이 거칠게 몰아치듯 큰소리를 치는 모습입니다.

senses.en: (of a female body) healthily plump and vigorous

examples.text: The painter favored buxom, rosy-cheeked figures that celebrated rural health and abundance.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 bōcsum('구부리기 쉬운, 순종적인')에서 왔습니다. 말랑하고 유연하다는 뜻에서 포동포동한 몸을 가리키게 되었습니다.

senses.en: A mix of discordant sounds; dissonance.

examples.text: A cacophony of car horns and shouting vendors greeted travelers stepping off the train.

origin.ko: 그리스어 kakophōnia에서 왔고, kakos(나쁜)와 phōnē(소리)가 합쳐진 말입니다. 거슬리는 소리의 뒤섞임입니다.

senses.en: a person who makes maps

examples.text: The cartographer spent two years surveying the coastline before completing an accurate chart of the bay.

origin.ko: cartography에서 파생된 말로, 프랑스어 carte(지도)에 그리스어 graphō(쓰다)가 합쳐진 형태입니다.

senses.en: an extreme bellicose nationalist

examples.text: The chauvinist insisted that his country's culture was superior to every other and refused to hear criticism.

senses.en: a person with a prejudiced belief in the superiority of his or her own kind

examples.text: The manager was a chauvinist who assumed that his female colleagues could not handle technical work.

origin.ko: chauvinism에서 파생된 말로, 병사 Nicolas Chauvin의 이름에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: subject to limits or subjected to limits

examples.text: Under the old regime, the role of the press was narrowly circumscribed by censorship laws.

senses.en: loud and persistent outcry from many people

examples.text: he ignored the clamor of the crowd

senses.en: make loud demands

examples.text: Anyone who tastes our food seems to clamor for more.

senses.en: a loud harsh or strident noise

examples.text: The clamor of the construction site made conversation on the street nearly impossible.

origin.ko: 라틴어 clāmor('외침')에서 왔고, clāmō(외치다)에서 갈라졌습니다.

senses.en: having the same ancestral language

examples.text: cognate languages

senses.en: a word is cognate with another if both derive from the same word in an ancestral language

examples.text: The English word night and the German word Nacht are cognates descended from a common ancestor.

origin.ko: 라틴어 cognātus('혈연으로 이어진')에서 왔고, co-(함께)와 gnātus(태어난)가 합쳐졌습니다. 같은 뿌리에서 난 말입니다.

senses.en: careful examination and comparison to note points of disagreement

examples.text: The editor's collation of the three manuscripts revealed dozens of discrepancies in the text.

senses.en: a light informal meal

examples.text: A cold collation of bread, cheese, and fruit was laid out for the guests.

origin.ko: 라틴어 collatiō에서 왔고 cōnferō('함께 가져오다')의 분사 어간이 뿌리입니다. 가져와 나란히 비교한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: To fail to properly distinguish or keep separate (things); to mistakenly treat (them) as equivalent.

examples.text: Critics warn against conflating correlation with causation when interpreting the survey results.

senses.en: mix together different elements

examples.text: The film conflates two historical figures into a single character.

origin.ko: 라틴어 cōnflō('함께 불다, 녹여 합치다')에서 왔습니다. 풀무로 불어 두 쇳덩이를 하나로 녹여 붙이는 이미지입니다.

senses.en: acting together in secret toward a fraudulent or illegal end

examples.text: The conniving advisor quietly steered the young king toward decisions that benefited only himself.

senses.en: expressing extreme contempt

examples.text: Sir George burst into a loud fit of contemptuous laughter.

origin.ko: 라틴어 contemptus(경멸)에 -ous가 붙은 말입니다.

senses.en: The state of being contrite; sincere penitence or remorse.

examples.text: Kremlin officials have shown no signs of contrition.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 contriciun에서 왔고 라틴어 contrītiō가 뿌리입니다. contrite와 같은 계통으로 마음이 부서지는 뉘우침입니다.

senses.en: returning to health after illness or debility

examples.text: She stayed in a convalescent hospital for two weeks before returning home.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 convalescent에서 왔고 라틴어 convalēscere('강해지기 시작하다')가 뿌리입니다.

senses.en: (usually followed by ‘with’) well informed about or knowing thoroughly

examples.text: She is equally conversant with Shakespeare and the laws of physics.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 conversant(converser의 현재분사)에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: the property of being extremely abundant

examples.text: The open-air market offered a cornucopia of fruits, spices, and handmade crafts.

senses.en: a goat's horn filled with grain and flowers and fruit symbolizing prosperity

examples.text: The harvest festival poster showed a cornucopia spilling over with grapes and wheat.

origin.ko: 라틴어 cornūcōpia('풍요의 뿔')를 빌려 온 말입니다. 과일과 곡식이 쏟아지는 뿔 모양 장식입니다.

senses.en: having material or physical form or substance

examples.text: The ghost in the story had no corporeal form and passed easily through walls.

senses.en: affecting or characteristic of the body as opposed to the mind or spirit

examples.text: The monk renounced corporeal pleasures in pursuit of spiritual discipline.

origin.ko: 중세 영어 corporealle에서 왔고, 라틴어 corporeus와 corpus(몸)가 뿌리입니다.

senses.en: A narrow crack or fissure, as in a rock or wall.

examples.text: Lichen clung to every crevice of the cliff face, surviving on rainwater and wind-blown dust.

origin.ko: 라틴어 crepō(갈라지다, 터지다)에서 고대 프랑스어 crevace를 거쳐 왔습니다.

senses.en: An ugly, evil-looking, or frightening old woman; a hag.

examples.text: In the fairy tale, a toothless crone offers the lost children a poisoned apple.

origin.ko: 앵글로노르만어 carogne(썩은 고기, 늙은 암양)에서 왔습니다. 시체에 빗댄 욕설이 '추한 노파'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: a platform raised above the surrounding level to give prominence to the person on it

examples.text: The guest of honor climbed onto the dais and waited for the applause to fade.

origin.ko: 라틴어 discus(원반, 쟁반)에서 고대 프랑스어 deis로 이어졌습니다. 쟁반이나 식탁처럼 높이 놓인 대가 '연단'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: Respectful and considerate; showing deference.

examples.text: The deferential intern spoke only when invited and thanked everyone for their time.

origin.ko: deference에 -al이 붙은 말로, 월터 스콧이 만들었다고 합니다.

senses.en: reduce in worth or character, usually verbally

examples.text: A good teacher never demeans a student for asking a question, however basic it may seem.

origin.ko: de-와 mean(천한)을 합친 1595년의 말입니다. 품위를 낮은 데로 끌어내린다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: capable of being demonstrated or proved

examples.text: It is easily demonstrable that water extinguishes fire.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어에서 왔고 라틴어 mōnstrāre(보여주다)가 뿌리입니다. 보여줄 수 있어 '입증 가능한'입니다.

senses.en: given to or marked by the open expression of emotion

examples.text: an affectionate and demonstrative family

senses.en: serving to demonstrate

examples.text: demonstrative evidence

origin.ko: 라틴어 dēmōnstrātīvus에서 왔습니다. 감정을 겉으로 드러내 보인다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: Modest, quiet, reserved, or serious.

examples.text: She is a demure young lady.

senses.en: affectedly modest or shy especially in a playful or provocative way

examples.text: Behind her demure smile lay a sharp wit that she deployed only when the moment was right.

origin.ko: 앵글로노르만어 de mure port '성숙한 태도로'에서 왔다고 봅니다. 차분하고 얌전한 태도를 가리킵니다.

senses.en: abusing vocally; expressing contempt or ridicule

examples.text: derisive laughter

origin.ko: 라틴어 dērīdeō(비웃다)의 어간에 -ive가 붙은 말입니다.

senses.en: thoroughly dried out

examples.text: old boxes of desiccated Cuban cigars

senses.en: lacking vitality or spirit; lifeless

examples.text: The professor's desiccated lectures drained all the excitement from what should have been a vivid subject.

senses.en: characteristic of an absolute ruler or absolute rule; having absolute sovereignty

examples.text: The despotic ruler abolished the parliament and imprisoned anyone who questioned his decrees.

origin.ko: 그리스어 despotikós에서 왔고 despot(절대 군주)에 -ic이 붙은 말입니다.

senses.en: An ornamental headband worn as a badge of royalty.

examples.text: The Apollon wing of the Louvre has a set of historic crowns, diadems and sovereign jewellery.

senses.en: Regal power; sovereignty; empire—considered as symbolized by the crown.

examples.text: The young prince was too eager to inherit the diadem and the burdens that came with it.

origin.ko: 그리스어 diádēma(머리에 두르는 띠)에서 왔고 diadéō(둘러 묶다)가 뿌리입니다.

senses.en: To become wider or larger; to expand.

examples.text: The eye doctor put drops in my eye to dilate the pupil so he could see the nerve better.

senses.en: add details, as to an account or idea; clarify the meaning of and discourse in a learned way, usually in writing

examples.text: The author declined to dilate on her methods, saying the appendix covered them thoroughly enough.

origin.ko: 라틴어 dīlātāre(넓게 펼치다)에서 왔고 lātus(넓은)가 뿌리입니다.

senses.en: not in agreement or harmony

examples.text: views discordant with present-day ideas

senses.en: lacking in harmony

examples.text: The discordant notes of the out-of-tune piano echoed through the empty hall.

origin.ko: 라틴어 discordāre(마음이 안 맞다)의 현재분사에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: To free or deprive of illusion; to disenchant.
senses.ko: 환상에서 깨어나게 하다, 환멸을 느끼게 하다

examples.text: Years of bureaucratic delay began to disillusion the once-idealistic young volunteers.

origin.ko: dis-와 illusion을 합친 말로, 환상을 걷어낸다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: perceive intuitively or through some inexplicable perceptive powers

examples.text: She could divine her employer's mood from the way he closed the office door.

senses.en: emanating from God

examples.text: divine guidance

senses.en: being of such surpassing excellence as to suggest inspiration by the gods

examples.text: her pies were simply divine

origin.ko: 라틴어 dīvīnus(신의)에서 왔고 divus(신)가 뿌리입니다. 신의 영감으로 알아챈다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: lacking in smartness or taste

examples.text: a dowdy grey outfit

senses.en: The worst and lowest part of something.

examples.text: the dregs of society

senses.en: sediment that has settled at the bottom of a liquid

examples.text: He drained the cup and grimaced at the bitter dregs of coffee clinging to the bottom.

senses.en: marked by deliberate deceptiveness especially by pretending one set of feelings and acting under the influence of another

examples.text: The duplicitous adviser praised the plan in public while quietly working to sabotage it.

senses.en: willingly obedient out of a sense of duty and respect

examples.text: Ralph was a dutiful child, and took the trash out without being told.

origin.ko: duty(의무)에 -ful이 붙은 말입니다.

senses.en: enlightening or uplifting so as to encourage intellectual or moral improvement

examples.text: The documentary was an edifying look at how ordinary citizens resisted the regime.

senses.en: Chiefly in the form eke out: to add to, to augment; to increase; to lengthen.

examples.text: She took a night job to eke out her meager income from teaching.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 ēaca(증가, 보탬)에서 왔습니다. 모자란 것에 조금씩 보태서 '겨우 꾸려 간다'는 뜻이 되었습니다.

senses.en: expressing sorrow often for something past

examples.text: The film's elegiac tone mourned a vanished way of rural life.

origin.ko: 그리스어 elegeiakós에서 라틴어와 프랑스어를 거쳐 왔습니다. 애가(elegy)의 분위기를 띤다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: omission or suppression of parts of words or sentences

examples.text: The writer's use of ellipsis forced readers to infer what the characters left unsaid.

origin.ko: 그리스어 élleipsis(빠뜨림, 생략)에서 왔습니다. 말의 일부가 빠진 것을 가리킵니다.

senses.en: hold spellbound

examples.text: The storyteller enchanted the children with tales of dragons and hidden kingdoms.

senses.en: cast a spell over someone or something; put a hex on someone or something

examples.text: In the legend, a sorceress enchanted the castle so no visitor could ever leave.

origin.ko: 라틴어 incantāre(주문을 노래하다)에서 고대 프랑스어를 거쳐 왔습니다. 노래 같은 주문으로 홀린다는 이미지입니다.

senses.en: comprehensive in scope or content (as an encyclopedia)

examples.text: encyclopedic knowledge

origin.ko: 그리스어 enkúklios paideíā(원을 이루는 교육, 전반적 교육)에서 encyclopedia가 나왔고 여기에 -ic이 붙었습니다. 모든 분야를 아우른다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: profound scholarly knowledge

examples.text: Her erudition in medieval history made her the department's most sought-after adviser.

origin.ko: 라틴어 ērudītiō(가르침)에서 왔습니다. 거친 상태를 벗겨 내는 가르침이 '학식'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: To drive out (an evil spirit) from a person, place or thing, especially by an incantation or prayer.

examples.text: The priest attempted to exorcise the evil spirit from the house.

origin.ko: 그리스어 exorkízō(맹세로 묶다, 악령을 쫓다)에서 왔습니다. 맹세의 힘으로 악령을 밖으로 몰아낸다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: make believe with the intent to deceive

examples.text: The pupil feigned sickness on the day of his exam.

origin.ko: 라틴어 fingere(빚다, 꾸며내다)에서 고대 프랑스어를 거쳐 왔습니다. 없는 모습을 빚어내는 데서 '~인 체하다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: Debris floating in a river or sea, in particular fragments from a shipwreck.

examples.text: After the storm, flotsam from the wrecked trawler washed up along the beach for miles.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 flotaison(떠다님)에서 왔고 float(뜨다)와 이어집니다. 난파 후 바다 위에 떠다니는 잔해입니다.

senses.en: indicate, as with a sign or an omen

examples.text: The early chapters subtly foreshadow the tragedy that overtakes the family at the novel's end.

origin.ko: fore(미리)에 shadow(그림자)가 붙었습니다. 일이 오기 전에 먼저 드리우는 그림자 같은 조짐입니다.

senses.en: tastelessly showy

examples.text: The casino's garish neon signs lit up the street long after midnight.

senses.en: look with amazement; look stupidly

examples.text: Tourists stopped to gawk at the film star as she stepped out of the limousine.

senses.en: an awkward stupid person

examples.text: The boy, a tall and shy gawk, tripped over his own feet on the way to the stage.

senses.en: marked by refinement in taste and manners

examples.text: The genteel tea room was filled with elderly ladies in lace collars.

senses.en: Affectedly proper or refined; somewhat prudish refinement; excessively polite.

examples.text: Their genteel horror at the slightest coarse word seemed more theater than sincere feeling.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 gentil에서 왔고 라틴어 gēns(씨족, 가문)가 뿌리입니다. 좋은 가문다운 품위가 '점잖은'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: characterized by unusual lightness and delicacy

examples.text: The dancer's gossamer costume floated behind her like morning mist.

senses.en: filaments from a web that was spun by a spider

examples.text: Gossamer glistened with dew between the branches of the hedge at dawn.

origin.ko: 중세영어 gossomer로, goose(거위)와 summer(여름)의 합성에서 왔다는 설이 유력합니다. 늦가을 맑은 날 떠다니는 거미줄을 가리키던 말입니다.

senses.en: a storehouse for threshed grain or animal feed

examples.text: The village granary was rebuilt on stilts to keep the harvest safe from floods and rats.

origin.ko: 라틴어 grānārium '곡물 창고'에서 왔습니다. grain(곡식)에 장소를 뜻하는 -ary가 붙은 모양입니다.

senses.en: Unwilling or with reluctance.

examples.text: The senator offered grudging praise for the opposition's budget proposal.

senses.en: petty or reluctant in giving or spending

examples.text: The grudging host gave each departing guest a single biscuit and a cold farewell.

senses.en: a thin porridge (usually oatmeal or cornmeal)

examples.text: The orphans were fed little more than watery gruel twice a day.

senses.en: Something that lacks substance.

examples.text: Critics dismissed the committee's final report as thin gruel after months of anticipation.

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 grutum '곡식 가루'에서 고대 프랑스어 gruel을 거쳐 왔습니다. 곡식 가루를 끓인 묽은 죽입니다.

senses.en: Boldness of enterprise; aggressiveness or initiative.

examples.text: It took real gumption for the intern to challenge the director's forecast in front of the board.

senses.en: sound practical judgment

examples.text: She had the gumption to read the contract carefully before signing anything.

origin.ko: 스코틀랜드어 gumption '상식, 추진력'에서 들어온 말이며, 그 이전 어원은 확실하지 않습니다.

senses.en: blowing in puffs or short intermittent blasts

examples.text: Gusty winds forced the airline to cancel several afternoon flights along the coast.

senses.en: Stressed, rushed, panicked, overly busy or preoccupied.

examples.text: The entire place teemed with harried executives who had no time to talk to one another.

senses.en: hamper the action or progress of

examples.text: The chairman was hobbled by the all-powerful dean

senses.en: walk impeded by some physical limitation or injury

examples.text: The old woman hobbles down to the store every day

origin.ko: 중세영어 hoblen에서 왔고 네덜란드어 hobbelen과 같은 계통입니다. 절뚝거리며 걷는 이미지에서 '방해하다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: A moralizing lecture.

examples.text: The teacher followed the prank with a long homily on responsibility and respect.

senses.en: A sermon, especially concerning a practical matter.

examples.text: The pastor's Sunday homily focused on forgiveness within families.

origin.ko: 그리스어 homilía '군중과의 모임, 강론'에서 왔습니다. hómilos(군중)에서 나온 말로 군중 앞에서 하는 설교가 '훈계'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: urge or force (a person) to an action; constrain or motivate

examples.text: A deep sense of injustice impelled her to leave her career and become an advocate for refugees.

origin.ko: 라틴어 impellō '몰아붙이다'에서 왔습니다. ~를 향해(in-) 밀어붙인다(pel)는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: immune to attack; incapable of being tampered with

examples.text: an impregnable fortress

senses.en: incapable of being overcome, challenged or refuted

examples.text: impregnable self-confidence

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 imprenable '잡을 수 없는'에서 왔습니다. 잡거나 빼앗을 수 없으니 '난공불락'입니다.

senses.en: Innate; possessed by an organism at birth.

examples.text: inborn talent

origin.ko: in(안)과 born(태어난)의 합성어입니다. 태어날 때부터 몸 안에 갖고 있다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: secure against future loss, damage, or liability; give security for

examples.text: The contract indemnifies the landlord against any claims arising from damage caused by tenants.

senses.en: To compensate or reimburse someone for some expense or injury.

examples.text: The insurer agreed to indemnify the family for the full cost of rebuilding their flooded home.

origin.ko: indemn(다치지 않은)에 -ify가 붙은 말입니다. 손해를 입지 않은 상태로 되돌려 놓는다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: originating where it is found

examples.text: That style of pottery is indigenous to that region.

senses.en: Innate, inborn.

examples.text: Her indigenous talent for languages let her pick up new tongues with almost no formal study.

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 indigenus '그 땅에서 태어난'에서 왔습니다. 안에서(indi) 태어난(gen) 토착의 존재입니다.

senses.en: injustice by virtue of not conforming with rules or standards

examples.text: The report highlights the inequity in funding between wealthy and poor school districts.

origin.ko: in-(않는)에 equity(공평)가 붙은 말입니다. 공평하지 않은 상태입니다.

senses.en: place in a grave or tomb

examples.text: The fallen soldiers were interred with full honors in the cemetery overlooking the valley.

origin.ko: 속라틴어 *interrāre '흙 속에 넣다'에서 왔습니다. 땅속에 묻는다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: a person who takes part in a conversation

examples.text: The diplomat was a patient interlocutor, listening carefully before answering each of the journalist's questions.

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 interlocūtor에서 왔습니다. 서로 사이에서 말을 주고받는 사람입니다.

senses.en: tiresomely long; seemingly without end

examples.text: The interminable meeting dragged on for hours while the audience quietly checked their watches.

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 interminābilis에서 왔습니다. 끝낼 수 없으니 '끝없는'입니다.

senses.en: irritate or vex

examples.text: It irks me doing all this work and have someone wreck it.

origin.ko: 고대 노르드어 '일하다'에서 온 중세 영어 irken '지치다'에서 왔습니다. 지치게 한다는 데서 '짜증나게 하다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: be compatible, similar or consistent; coincide in their characteristics

examples.text: That explanation doesn’t jibe with the facts.

senses.en: A facetious or insulting remark; a jeer, a taunt.

examples.text: He flung subtle jibes at her until she couldn’t bear to work with him any longer.

senses.en: joyful and proud especially because of triumph or success

examples.text: The jubilant fans poured into the streets after the team clinched its first title in decades.

origin.ko: 라틴어 iubilans '기뻐 소리치는'에서 왔습니다. 환호성을 지르는 모습입니다.

senses.en: praise, glorify, or honor

examples.text: Critics lauded the novel for its unflinching honesty and lyrical prose.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어를 거쳐 라틴어 laudāre에서 왔고 laus '칭찬, 명성'에서 나왔습니다.

senses.en: a celebrity who is an inspiration to others

examples.text: he was host to a large gathering of luminaries

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 lūminārium '빛을 내는 것'에서 왔고 lūmen(빛)에서 나왔습니다. 빛나는 별처럼 뛰어난 명사입니다.

senses.en: To make defamatory statements about; to slander or traduce.

examples.text: The senator accused the press of maligning him with unsubstantiated rumors.

senses.en: evil or harmful in nature or influence

examples.text: prompted by malign motives

origin.ko: 라틴어 malignus에서 왔고 malus(나쁜)와 genus(종류)가 합쳐졌습니다. 성질이 나쁘다는 데서 남을 헐뜯는 뜻이 되었습니다.

senses.en: make imperfect

examples.text: A series of petty disputes marred what should have been a triumphant conference.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 mierran '망치다, 방해하다'에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: relegate to a lower or outer edge, as of specific groups of people

examples.text: We must not marginalize the poor in our society

origin.ko: margin(가장자리)에 -ize가 붙은 말입니다. 가장자리로 밀어낸다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: Anything that entraps or makes progress difficult.

examples.text: The merger bogged down in a morass of regulatory paperwork.

senses.en: a soft wet area of low-lying land that sinks underfoot

examples.text: The army's wagons sank into the morass after three days of heavy rain.

origin.ko: 네덜란드어 moeras '습지, 늪'에서 왔습니다. 발이 빠져 나오기 힘든 늪이 헤어나기 힘든 곤경이 되었습니다.

senses.en: A small particle; a speck.

examples.text: Dust motes drifted lazily through the beam of afternoon light in the attic.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 mot '모래알, 티끌'에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: A person who accepts or champions nihilism.

examples.text: The protagonist, a committed nihilist, scoffs at every moral principle his friends hold dear.

origin.ko: 라틴어 nihil '아무것도 없음'에 -ist가 붙은 말로, 허무주의를 따르는 사람입니다.

senses.en: showing a cheerful willingness to do favors for others

examples.text: The obliging clerk stayed late to help us find the missing documents.

senses.en: Without planning or thinking ahead.

examples.text: She gave an offhand speech.

senses.en: Careless; without sufficient thought or consideration.

examples.text: He doesn't realise how hurtful his offhand remarks can be.

senses.en: Curt, abrupt, unfriendly.

examples.text: She was quite offhand with me yesterday.

origin.ko: 영어에서 off(떨어진)와 hand(손)를 합친 말로, 미리 손쓰지 않고 그 자리에서 곧바로 한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: A formal, often ceremonial speech.

examples.text: a funeral oration; an impassioned oration; to make / deliver / pronounce an oration

origin.ko: 라틴어 ōrātiō '말하기, 연설'에서 왔고, ōrō는 '연설하다'입니다.

senses.en: To vacillate between conflicting opinions, etc.

examples.text: The mood for change oscillated from day to day.

senses.en: To swing back and forth, especially if with a regular rhythm.

examples.text: A pendulum oscillates slower as it gets longer.

origin.ko: 라틴어 ōscillō '흔들리다'에서 왔고, ōscillum은 '그네'입니다. 그네처럼 이쪽저쪽 흔들린다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: An enthusiastic expression of praise.

examples.text: The review was a paean to the novelist's gift for capturing everyday life.

origin.ko: 그리스어 Paián은 의술의 신 아폴론에게 바치던 승전 찬가였습니다. 여기서 열렬한 찬사를 뜻하게 되었습니다.

senses.en: Preference, bias in favor of, tendency.

examples.text: The judge's partiality towards the defendant caused him to be replaced, with someone who was apparently more neutral.

senses.en: a predisposition to like something

examples.text: The old professor had a well-known partiality for strong black tea.

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 partiālitās에서 왔으며, 부분(한쪽)만 편드는 성향을 뜻합니다.

senses.en: belonging to or characteristic of the nobility or aristocracy

examples.text: Her patrician bearing and clipped accent marked her as old money.

senses.en: a member of the aristocracy

examples.text: The emperor elevated several loyal families to the status of patricians.

origin.ko: 라틴어 patricius에서 왔고, 로마 원로원 의원 '아버지들(patrēs)'에서 나온 말입니다. 로마 귀족 계층을 가리킵니다.

senses.en: deeply or seriously thoughtful

examples.text: He sat in pensive silence, weighing his options carefully.

senses.en: showing pensive sadness

examples.text: Her pensive gaze followed the departing train long after it vanished.

origin.ko: 옛 프랑스어 pensif '생각에 잠긴'에서 왔고, 라틴어 pēnsō는 '무게를 달다, 곰곰이 따지다'입니다.

senses.en: characterized by a lightly pert and exuberant quality

examples.text: The pert young waitress answered every complaint with a cheeky remark.

origin.ko: 중세 영어 apert '열린, 숨김없는'의 앞부분이 떨어져 나간 말입니다. 거침없이 나서는 당돌함이 되었습니다.

senses.en: To bind the arms of someone, so as to deprive him of their use; to disable by so binding.

examples.text: Guards pinioned the prisoner's arms behind his back before leading him away.

senses.en: wing of a bird

examples.text: The hawk spread its pinions and rose over the valley.

origin.ko: 옛 프랑스어 pignon, 라틴어 penna '깃털, 날개'에서 왔습니다. 날개를 묶어 날지 못하게 하듯 팔을 결박한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: A meagre allowance of money or wages.

examples.text: Dad was forced to claim benefit money from the government. It was a pittance, barely enough to live on.

origin.ko: 라틴어 pietās '경건'에서 중세 라틴어와 옛 프랑스어를 거쳐 왔습니다. 경건의 뜻으로 베푸는 소액 몫에서 쥐꼬리만 한 보수가 되었습니다.

senses.en: To assume as a truthful or accurate premise or axiom, especially as a basis of an argument.

examples.text: Early astronomers postulated the existence of an unseen planet to explain the irregular orbit.

senses.en: maintain or assert

examples.text: The author postulates that economic decline, not invasion, ended the ancient empire.

senses.en: (logic) a proposition that is accepted as true in order to provide a basis for logical reasoning

examples.text: The proof rests on a single postulate that the authors never bother to justify.

origin.ko: 라틴어 postulāre('요구하다')에서 왔습니다. 증명 없이 인정해 달라고 요구하는 전제를 세운다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: A rule or principle, especially one governing personal conduct.

examples.text: Precept guides, but example draws.

origin.ko: 라틴어 praecipere('미리 가르치다', prae + capere)에서 왔습니다. 앞서 쥐여 주는 가르침이 교훈입니다.

senses.en: To prevent or beat to the punch, to forestall an expected occurrence by acting first.

examples.text: By his statement, the Secretary-General had effectively preempted the usual frustrating debates over questions of fact and law.

senses.en: take the place of or have precedence over

examples.text: Breaking news coverage preempted the regular evening programming for several hours.

origin.ko: preemption에서 거꾸로 만든 말입니다. 라틴어 '먼저 사다'에서 남보다 앞서 차지한다는 뜻이 나왔습니다.

senses.en: A person who is or tries to be excessively proper, especially one who is easily offended by matters of a sexual nature.
senses.ko: 점잔 빼는 사람, 지나치게 도덕적인 사람

examples.text: Her brother teased her as a prude whenever the conversation turned to romance.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 prude('훌륭한 여자')에서 왔습니다. 처신이 훌륭하다는 칭찬이 지나치게 점잔 빼는 사람이라는 뜻으로 변했습니다.

senses.en: have the often specious appearance of being, intending, or claiming

examples.text: The letter purports to express people's opinion

senses.en: the intended meaning of a communication

examples.text: My practice, you say, refutes my doubts. But you mistake the purport of my question.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 purporter('나르다, 담고 있다')에서 왔습니다. 겉으로 어떤 뜻을 담은 듯 내세운다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: To modify, limit, restrict or moderate something; especially to add conditions or requirements for an assertion to be true.

examples.text: The author qualifies her claim by noting that the data cover only urban areas.

senses.en: prove capable or fit; meet requirements

examples.text: Applicants must hold a graduate degree to qualify for the fellowship.

senses.en: describe or portray the character or the qualities or peculiarities of

examples.text: Historians qualify the early republic as a fragile experiment rather than a settled democracy.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 qualifier에서 왔고 quality('성질')에 -fy가 붙었습니다. 성질에 제한을 두어 한정한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: excessively greedy and grasping

examples.text: Rapacious landlords raised rents sharply, forcing long-time tenants out of the neighborhood.

senses.en: living by preying on other animals especially by catching living prey

examples.text: The rapacious hawk circled above the field, scanning for mice in the tall grass.

origin.ko: 라틴어 rapāx('낚아채는, 탐욕스러운')에서 왔고 rapere('움켜쥐다')와 이어집니다.

senses.en: the reestablishing of cordial relations

examples.text: The two rival nations pursued a cautious rapprochement after decades of mutual hostility.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 rapprocher('다시 가까이 가져가다')에서 온 말을 그대로 빌려 왔습니다. 멀어진 사이를 다시 가깝게 한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: (philosophy) the doctrine that knowledge is acquired by reason without resort to experience

examples.text: Descartes is often cited as the founder of modern rationalism, which prizes deduction over observation.

senses.en: the doctrine that reason is the right basis for regulating conduct

examples.text: Enlightenment rationalism encouraged thinkers to question tradition and judge beliefs by reasoned argument.

origin.ko: rational에 -ism이 붙은 말입니다. 이성으로 지식을 얻는다고 보는 입장입니다.

senses.en: cause extensive destruction or ruin utterly

examples.text: Floods ravaged the countryside, destroying crops and leaving thousands of families without homes.

senses.en: (usually plural) a destructive action

examples.text: the ravages of time

origin.ko: 프랑스어 ravir('낚아채 가다')에서 왔고 라틴어 rapere('움켜쥐다')로 거슬러 갑니다. 모조리 휩쓸어 황폐하게 한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: prove to be false or incorrect

examples.text: The defense attorney rebutted the prosecution's claims with documents showing her client was abroad that night.

senses.en: To deny the truth of something, especially by presenting arguments that disprove it.

examples.text: The company issued a statement rebutting allegations that it had concealed safety data.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 reboter('되밀치다')에서 왔고 butt('들이받다')와 이어집니다. 상대 주장을 되받아 밀쳐 냅니다.

senses.en: go back to a previous state

examples.text: Under stress, the toddler began to regress, refusing to walk and demanding to be carried.

senses.en: returning to a former state

examples.text: Critics saw the new policy as a regress to the discredited practices of an earlier era.

origin.ko: 라틴어 regredī('되돌아가다')에서 왔습니다. 뒤로 걸어 이전 상태로 간다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: reach a decision

examples.text: he resolved never to drink again

senses.en: bring to an end; settle conclusively

examples.text: The mediator helped resolve the long dispute between the neighboring towns.

senses.en: the trait of being resolute

examples.text: his resoluteness carried him through the battle

origin.ko: 라틴어 resolvere('풀다, 녹이다')에서 왔습니다. 문제를 풀어 결론에 이르러 결심한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: the group following and attending to some important person

examples.text: The ambassador arrived with a large retinue of aides, bodyguards, and translators.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 retenue('붙들어 둠')에서 왔고 retenir('붙들다')와 이어집니다. 높은 사람이 곁에 붙들어 두는 수행원입니다.

senses.en: absentminded dreaming while awake

examples.text: The teacher's question broke into the student's reverie about the summer holidays.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 rêverie('몽상')에서 왔고 고대 프랑스어 resver('꿈꾸다, 헛소리하다')와 이어집니다.

senses.en: Effecting or designed to effect an improvement; remedial.

examples.text: salutary advice

origin.ko: 라틴어 salus(건강)에서 온 salutaris에서 왔습니다. 건강을 되찾게 하는 이로운 효과를 뜻합니다.

senses.en: of or relating to a tailor or to tailoring

examples.text: His sartorial rebellions were slight: he wore jeans, for example, when giving tutorials.

origin.ko: 라틴어 sartor(재단사)에서 왔고, sarcire(깁다)에서 나왔습니다. 재단과 옷차림에 관한 뜻입니다.

senses.en: fill to satisfaction

examples.text: At last he stopped, his hunger and thirst sated.

origin.ko: 옛 영어 sade(물리다)에서 왔고, satiate 같은 말의 영향을 받아 모양이 바뀌었습니다. 배불리 채운다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: infuse or fill completely

examples.text: Modern television is saturated with violence.

senses.en: To cause to become completely permeated with, or soaked (especially with a liquid).

examples.text: Rain saturated their clothes.

origin.ko: 라틴어 satur(가득 찬)에서 온 saturāre에서 왔습니다. 빈틈없이 가득 채워 흠뻑 적신다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: delight in another person's misfortune

examples.text: Rivals could not hide their schadenfreude when the celebrated chef's restaurant lost its third star.

origin.ko: 독일어에서 그대로 빌려온 말로, Schaden(해, 불행)과 Freude(기쁨)가 합쳐졌습니다. 남의 불행에서 느끼는 기쁨입니다.

senses.en: lacking substance or significance

examples.text: slight evidence

senses.en: To treat (someone or something) with disdain or neglect, usually out of prejudice, hatred, or jealousy; to ignore disrespectfully; to skimp on one's duties toward.

examples.text: The composer felt slighted when the orchestra failed to invite him to the opening night.

senses.en: a deliberate discourteous act (usually as an expression of anger or disapproval)

examples.text: He took the omission of his name from the list as a deliberate slight.

senses.en: being of delicate or slender build

examples.text: a slight but graceful woman

origin.ko: 고대 영어 sliht(매끄러운, 평평한)에서 왔습니다. 매끈하고 가는 데서 보잘것없다는 뜻이 되었습니다.

senses.en: conduit that carries a rapid flow of water controlled by a sluicegate

examples.text: Engineers opened the sluice to release water from the reservoir into the irrigation canals.

senses.en: To wash (down or out).

examples.text: And now men with a hose have come and are sluicing out the streets.

origin.ko: 라틴어 exclūdere(막아 내다)에서 온 말입니다. 물을 막고 여닫는 수문을 뜻합니다.

senses.en: Disparaging or derisive in an insinuative way.

examples.text: Don't make snide remarks to me.

origin.ko: '날카롭고 베는 듯한'이라는 뜻의 방언 snithe에서 왔을 것으로 봅니다. 찌르듯 비꼬는 말투입니다.

senses.en: Easily shocked, sickened or frightened; tending to be nauseated or nervous; oversensitive.

examples.text: He might have made a good doctor, had he not been so squeamish at the sight of blood.

senses.en: Averse or reluctant.

examples.text: Regulators were squeamish about confronting the powerful bank, so the abuses continued.

origin.ko: 어원이 분명하지 않습니다. 현기증과 메스꺼움을 뜻하는 방언 말과 섞였다고 봅니다.

senses.en: artificially formal

examples.text: He gave a stilted bow and left.

origin.ko: stilt(죽마)에 -ed가 붙은 말입니다. 죽마를 타고 걷듯 부자연스럽고 딱딱하다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: an elaborate or deceitful scheme contrived to deceive or evade

examples.text: The general's clever stratagem lured the enemy forces away from the undefended pass.

origin.ko: 그리스어 stratēgēma(장군의 책략)에서 왔습니다. 군을 이끄는 장군의 계략이라는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: a hypothesis that is taken for granted

examples.text: The whole argument rests on the supposition that human behavior is basically rational.

senses.en: a message expressing an opinion based on incomplete evidence

examples.text: The supposition that Geoffrey had been chloroformed was a reasonable hypothesis at that stage of the disclosure.

origin.ko: 라틴어 suppositiō에서 왔습니다. 논의의 밑에 놓아둔 전제, 곧 가정입니다.

senses.en: be about a place without any apparent purpose

examples.text: The travelers tarried in the village square, reluctant to leave before sunset.

senses.en: To delay; to be late or tardy in beginning or doing anything.

examples.text: For the vision is yet for an appointed time, but at the end it shall speak, and not lie: though it tarry, wait for it; because it will surely come, it will not tarry.

origin.ko: 중세 영어 tarien(지연시키다, 괴롭히다)에서 왔습니다. 가지 않고 머뭇거린다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: repeated too often; overfamiliar through overuse

examples.text: The candidate's threadbare slogans failed to stir an audience that had heard them every election.

senses.en: having the nap worn away so that the threads show through

examples.text: The student wore a threadbare coat that had clearly seen many winters.

origin.ko: thread('실')와 bare('드러난')의 합성어입니다. 올이 다 드러나도록 닳은 옷이 '진부한' 표현으로 비유되었습니다.

senses.en: extremely hot and dry

examples.text: the torrid heat of the noonday sun

senses.en: characterized by intense emotion

examples.text: The novelist's torrid romance with a married diplomat scandalized polite society for a decade.

origin.ko: 라틴어 torridus는 torreō('바싹 말리다, 태우다')에서 왔습니다. 땅이 타듯 뜨거운 날씨를 가리킵니다.

senses.en: lacking grace in movement or posture

examples.text: The ungainly heron lurched into the air, its long legs trailing awkwardly behind.

senses.en: difficult to handle or manage especially because of shape

examples.text: Movers struggled to carry the ungainly sofa up the narrow staircase.

origin.ko: un-과 gainly('우아한')의 결합이고 gain은 고대 노르드어 gegn('알맞은')에서 왔습니다. 맵시가 없다는 뜻이 '볼품없는'입니다.

senses.en: not diminished or moderated in intensity or severity; sometimes used as an intensifier

examples.text: Their handling of the recent diplomatic crisis was an unmitigated disaster.

senses.en: Streaked, spotted, or otherwise marked with a variety of color.

examples.text: The garden was bordered by variegated leaves splashed with cream and green.

senses.en: Varied, heterogeneous, motley

examples.text: The city's variegated population includes immigrants from dozens of countries.

senses.en: marked by extreme intensity of emotions or convictions; inclined to react violently; fervid

examples.text: The senator issued a vehement denial of the corruption charges during the televised hearing.

origin.ko: 라틴어 vehemēns는 '정신이 모자란'에서 온 것으로 추정합니다. 이성을 잃을 만큼 '격렬한' 것입니다.

senses.en: of or characteristic of or occurring in spring

examples.text: the vernal equinox

senses.en: suggestive of youth; vigorous and fresh

examples.text: The poet praised the vernal energy of the young dancers as they leaped across the stage.

origin.ko: 라틴어 vēr('봄')에서 나온 vernālis에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: Experienced or gained by taking in another person’s experience rather than through first-hand experience, such as through watching or reading.

examples.text: People experience vicarious pleasures through watching television.

senses.en: suffered or done by one person as a substitute for another

examples.text: Many religions teach that a martyr's vicarious suffering can redeem the sins of others.

origin.ko: 라틴어 vicārius('대리의')에 -ous를 붙였습니다. 남을 대신해 겪는 '간접 체험'입니다.

senses.en: provide adequate grounds to justify (a certain course of action)

examples.text: The minor delay hardly warrants such an angry complaint to the airline.

senses.en: a writ from a court commanding police to perform specified acts

examples.text: an arrest warrant issued by the court

senses.en: stand behind and guarantee the quality, accuracy, or condition of

examples.text: The manufacturer warrants every part of the engine for five years.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 warant('보호자, 보증')에서 왔고 프랑크어 '막다'에서 나왔습니다. 보증해 준다는 뜻이 '정당화하다'입니다.

senses.en: a round shape formed by a series of concentric circles (as formed by leaves or flower petals)

examples.text: The detective pointed to the distinct whorl pattern in the fingerprint on the glass.

origin.ko: whirl('빙글 돌다')이 변한 말입니다.

senses.en: to quarrel noisily, angrily or disruptively

examples.text: The heirs wrangled for years over who should inherit the family estate.

senses.en: an angry dispute

examples.text: A bitter wrangle over funding delayed the construction of the new library.

origin.ko: 중세 네덜란드어와 저지 독일어에서 온 말로 '비틀다, 싸우다'와 이어집니다. 서로 비틀며 다투는 모습이 '말다툼하다'입니다.

senses.en: give in, as to influence or pressure

examples.text: After hours of pressure, the committee finally yielded to the protesters' demands.

senses.en: give or supply

examples.text: This year's crop yielded 1,000 bushels of corn

senses.en: the income or profit arising from such transactions as the sale of land or other property

examples.text: Government bonds offered a modest yield compared with the riskier stocks.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 ġieldan('지불하다')에서 왔습니다. 값을 내준다는 뜻이 '굴복하다, 양보하다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: a rough and bitter manner

examples.text: The negotiations ended in acrimony, with neither delegation willing to shake hands.

origin.ko: 라틴어 acrimonia(날카로움, 매운맛)에서 왔습니다. 혀가 얼얼한 매서움이 '독설'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: lessen the intensity of or calm

examples.text: The company released safety data to allay public fears about the new vaccine.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 āleċġan(내려놓다)에서 왔습니다. 두려움을 눕혀 가라앉힌다는 이미지입니다.

senses.en: Anything delightfully sweet and pleasing.
senses.ko: 맛과 향이 뛰어난 음식, 감미로운 것

examples.text: After days of dry rations, the ripe peaches tasted like ambrosia to the exhausted hikers.

senses.en: (classical mythology) the food and drink of the gods; mortals who ate it became immortal

examples.text: In Greek myth, the gods preserved their immortality by feasting on ambrosia.

origin.ko: 그리스어 ambrosia(불사)에서 왔습니다. 신들이 먹어 죽지 않게 해 준다는 음식이 '감미로운 것'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: capable of relieving pain

examples.text: The cream has a mild analgesic effect that eases sore muscles after exercise.

senses.en: a medicine used to relieve pain

examples.text: Doctors recommended a simple analgesic rather than a stronger prescription drug.

origin.ko: analgesia(고통 없음)에 -ic이 붙은 말입니다. 그리스어 algos(고통)가 바탕입니다.

senses.en: suggesting human characteristics for animals or inanimate things

examples.text: The children's book gave the fox an anthropomorphic personality, complete with spectacles and a pocket watch.

origin.ko: 그리스어 anthropos(인간)와 morphe(형태)가 합쳐진 말입니다. 인간의 모습을 입힌다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: a ludicrous or grotesque act done for fun and amusement

examples.text: The comedian's wild antics on stage kept the audience laughing for the entire evening.

origin.ko: 이탈리아어 antico(고대의)에서 왔고, 고대 벽화의 기괴한 그림을 가리키던 말입니다. 우스꽝스러운 행동으로 뜻이 옮겨졌습니다.

senses.en: a feeling of strong eagerness (usually in favor of a person or cause)

examples.text: they were imbued with a revolutionary ardor

origin.ko: 라틴어 ardor(불타오름)에서 왔고 ardere(타다)에서 나왔습니다. 마음속에서 타오르는 열정입니다.

senses.en: cheap showy jewelry or ornament on clothing

examples.text: The market stall was crowded with glittering baubles aimed at tourists.

senses.en: Anything trivial and worthless.

examples.text: She dismissed the title as a mere bauble that carried no real authority.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 babel(장신구, 아이 장난감)에서 왔습니다. 예쁘다는 뜻의 bel이 겹쳐진 말로 보입니다.

senses.en: having or showing a ready disposition to fight

examples.text: You don't have to be so bellicose, and we can work out a peaceful solution.

origin.ko: 라틴어 bellicosus(전쟁을 좋아하는)에서 왔고 bellum(전쟁)에서 나왔습니다.

senses.en: To moan or complain about (something).

examples.text: He bemoaned the drought but went on watering his lawn.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 bemǣnan(한탄하다)에서 왔습니다. 어떤 일을 두고 신음하며 슬퍼한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: ask for or request earnestly

examples.text: The villagers besought the governor to send food before the winter closed the mountain roads.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 sēċan(찾다)에 be-가 붙은 말입니다. 간절히 찾아가 청한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: Infatuated.

examples.text: He was so besotted with the young singer that he attended every one of her concerts.

senses.en: very drunk

examples.text: The besotted sailors stumbled back to the ship long after midnight, singing loudly.

senses.en: pompous or pretentious talk or writing

examples.text: The candidate's speech was all bombast, with soaring phrases but not a single concrete proposal.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 bombace('목화솜')에서 왔습니다. 옷에 솜을 채워 부풀리듯 속 빈 말을 부풀린다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: react in an offended or angry manner

examples.text: He bristled at her suggestion that he should teach her how to use the program

senses.en: To abound, to be covered with, or to have an abundance of, something, especially something jutting out.

examples.text: The harbor bristled with masts, and cranes lined the docks as far as the eye could see.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 bristl('뻣뻣한 털')에서 왔습니다. 화가 나면 털이 곤두서듯 발끈한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: having a difficult and contrary disposition

examples.text: The cantankerous old neighbor complained about every noise and refused to speak to anyone on the street.

origin.ko: 옛말 contenkerous에서 왔고, contentious(다투기 좋아하는)와 rancorous(원한 깊은)가 섞였다고 추정합니다.

senses.en: the dead and rotting body of an animal; unfit for human food

examples.text: Vultures feed on carrion.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 charoigne에서 왔고 라틴어 caro('살')가 뿌리입니다. 썩어 가는 살덩이를 뜻합니다.

senses.en: the making of maps and charts

examples.text: Advances in satellite imaging transformed cartography, making detailed maps of remote regions cheap to produce.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 cartographie에서 왔고, carte(지도)와 그리스어 graphō(쓰다)가 합쳐졌습니다. 지도를 그리는 일입니다.

senses.en: Of or pertaining to a cataclysm; causing great destruction or upheaval; catastrophic.

examples.text: It is believed that a cataclysmic impact caused the extinction of the dinosaurs.

senses.en: Any excess or unwanted material, resource, or person; anything worthless.

examples.text: The editor's job is to separate the wheat from the chaff and publish only the strongest submissions.

senses.en: material consisting of seed coverings and small pieces of stem or leaves that have been separated from the seeds

examples.text: To separate out the chaff, early cultures tossed baskets of grain into the air and let the wind blow away the lighter chaff.

senses.en: To make fun of; to turn into ridicule by addressing in ironical or bantering language.

examples.text: His friends chaffed him good-naturedly about his terrible singing throughout the dinner.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 ċeaf('겨')에서 왔습니다. 곡식을 털고 남은 쓸모없는 껍질입니다.

senses.en: fanatically patriotic

examples.text: It would be smallmindedly chauvinistic to pretend that Scotland was other than a strong participant in the furthering of British Imperial ambitions.

senses.en: of or relating to persons convinced of the superiority of their own gender or kind

examples.text: The senator's chauvinistic remarks about working mothers drew sharp criticism from both parties.

senses.en: A conclusion (of a statement or event, for example), final portion, tail end.

examples.text: The memoir ends with a brief coda reflecting on how the town has changed since.

senses.en: the closing section of a musical composition

examples.text: The symphony builds to a thundering coda that leaves the audience breathless.

origin.ko: 이탈리아어 coda('꼬리')에서 왔고 라틴어 cauda와 같은 어원입니다. 곡의 꼬리 부분이 '끝맺음'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: treat with excessive indulgence

examples.text: Critics argue that universities coddle students instead of preparing them for professional criticism.

origin.ko: 아마 caudle에서 왔을 것으로 추정되며, 확실하지는 않습니다.

senses.en: of or relating to marriage or to the relationship between a wife and husband

examples.text: The prison eventually allowed conjugal visits for inmates serving long sentences.

origin.ko: 라틴어 coniugālis에서 왔고, con-(함께)과 iugum(멍에)이 합쳐졌습니다. 한 멍에를 함께 멘 부부의 이미지입니다.

senses.en: squeeze or press together

examples.text: Cold temperatures cause blood vessels near the skin to constrict.

origin.ko: 라틴어 cōnstrictus('압축된')에서 왔고, cōnstringō(함께 묶다, 조이다)에서 갈라졌습니다.

senses.en: go against, as of rules and laws

examples.text: The company's dumping of waste contravenes several environmental regulations.

origin.ko: 라틴어 contraveniō('맞서 오다')에서 온 중세 프랑스어 contravenir에서 왔습니다. 규칙과 정면으로 부딪친다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: a practical consequence that follows naturally

examples.text: blind jealousy is a frequent corollary of passionate love

senses.en: (logic) an inference that follows directly from the proof of another proposition

examples.text: The second theorem has an immediate corollary that every such set is finite.

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 corōllārium('화환 값, 덤')에서 왔고, corōlla(작은 화관)가 뿌리입니다. 덤으로 따라오는 결론이라는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: contrary to what common sense would suggest

examples.text: It seems counterintuitive, but resting after a mild injury can slow recovery more than gentle exercise.

origin.ko: counter-와 intuitive를 합친 말로, 1955년 노엄 촘스키가 처음 만들어 썼습니다.

senses.en: tendency to believe readily

examples.text: a tall story that strains credulity

origin.ko: 라틴어 crēdulitās에서 왔고 credulous에 -ity가 붙은 형태입니다.

senses.en: disposed to believe on little evidence

examples.text: the gimmick would convince none but the most credulous

origin.ko: 라틴어 crēdulus(쉽게 믿는)에서 왔고 crēdō(나는 믿는다)에서 나온 말입니다.

senses.en: To give a definite or precise form to (something).

examples.text: After some thought, I crystallized my ideas for the paper.

senses.en: To take a definite form.

examples.text: My ideas crystallized overnight.

origin.ko: crystal에 -ize가 붙은 말입니다. 그리스어 krústallos(얼음, 수정)에서 왔고, 흐릿한 것이 결정처럼 뚜렷해진다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: having a sophisticated charm

examples.text: The debonair host greeted each guest by name and kept every conversation effortlessly alive.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 de bon aire '좋은 혈통의'에서 왔습니다. 품위 있는 사람의 태도가 '세련된'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: The killing or destruction of any large portion of a population.

examples.text: The plague caused the decimation of villages across the valley within a single winter.

origin.ko: 라틴어 decimātiō에서 왔습니다. 로마군이 열 명 중 한 명을 처형한 벌에서 '대량 살상'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: mar or spoil the appearance of

examples.text: Vandals defaced the memorial overnight, spraying slogans across its marble base.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 desfacier(훼손하다)에서 왔습니다. 얼굴(face)을 지워 버린다는 이미지입니다.

senses.en: To profane or violate the sacredness or sanctity of something.

examples.text: Vandals desecrated the ancient cemetery, overturning headstones and scrawling slogans across the chapel walls.

origin.ko: de-와 consecrate(봉헌하다)의 어간을 합친 말입니다. 신성함을 벗겨낸다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: An aside, an act of straying from the main subject in speech or writing.

examples.text: The lectures included lengthy digressions on topics ranging from the professor's dog to the meaning of life.

origin.ko: 라틴어 dīgressiō에서 왔습니다. 주제에서 옆으로 걸어 나간다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: interchangeable with ‘means’ in the expression ‘by means of’

examples.text: By dint of sheer persistence, she finished the marathon despite a severe injury.
