origin.ko: 고대 영어 dynt(타격, 일격)에서 왔습니다. 일격으로 이뤄낸 힘에서 'by dint of'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: go ashore

examples.text: The passengers disembarked at Southampton

senses.en: free from involvement or entanglement

examples.text: How can I disentangle myself from her personal affairs?

senses.en: To unravel; to separate into discrete components or units.

examples.text: This overlapping is reflective of hybrid languages, where certain features (phonetic, orthographic, semantic, syntactic) are also difficult to disentangle.

senses.en: made less hopeful or enthusiastic

examples.text: felt discouraged by the magnitude of the problem

origin.ko: 동사 hearten(용기를 북돋우다)에서 온 말입니다. 용기를 잃은 상태를 뜻합니다.

senses.en: causing mental discomfort

examples.text: the disquieting sounds of nearby gunfire

senses.en: a gabled extension built out from a sloping roof to accommodate a vertical window

examples.text: Sunlight streamed through the dormer into the cramped attic bedroom under the sloping roof.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 dormoir(침실)에서 왔습니다. 다락 침실에 낸 창에서 '지붕창'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: An exit or way out.

examples.text: The window provides an egress in the event of an emergency.

senses.en: The process of exiting or leaving.

examples.text: Barricades blocked the egress of protesters from the square.

origin.ko: 라틴어 ēgressus(밖으로 나감)에서 왔습니다. 밖으로 걸어 나가는 길이 '출구'입니다.

senses.en: the quality of extreme wickedness

examples.text: Not until the war ended and journalists were able to enter Cambodia did the world really become aware of the enormity of Pol Pot’s oppression.

senses.en: vastness of size or extent

examples.text: universities recognized the enormity of their task

origin.ko: 라틴어 ēnōrmis(규범에서 벗어난)에서 왔습니다. 기준을 벗어난 괴물 같은 악행이라는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: written in the form of or carried on by letters or correspondence

examples.text: the epistolatory novel

origin.ko: 그리스어 epistolḗ(보낸 글, 편지)에서 라틴어 epistola를 거쳐 왔습니다. 편지로 이루어진 글이라는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: Something fit to be imitated; an ideal, a worthy model or role model: a desirable example.

examples.text: Michelangelo's "David" is an exemplar of Renaissance sculpture.

senses.en: Something typical or representative; an example that typifies its class.

examples.text: The novel is often cited as an exemplar of the nineteenth-century social realism that followed.

origin.ko: 라틴어 exemplar(본보기)에서 왔습니다. 여러 가지 중 뽑아 놓은 견본이라 모범이 됩니다.

senses.en: clarify by giving an example of

examples.text: The professor used a famous court case to exemplify how precedent shapes legal reasoning.

senses.en: be typical of

examples.text: Her quiet generosity exemplifies the community spirit that the town is known for.

origin.ko: 라틴어 exemplum(본보기)에서 중세 프랑스어를 거쳐 왔습니다. 본보기를 들어 보인다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: remove by erasing or crossing out or as if by drawing a line

examples.text: The judge ordered the juvenile conviction expunged from the defendant's permanent record.

senses.en: To eliminate completely; to annihilate.

examples.text: The new regime tried to expunge every trace of the old order from public memory.

origin.ko: 라틴어 expungere(점을 찍어 지우다)에서 왔습니다. 고대에 지울 글자 아래 점을 찍어 표시한 데서 온 말입니다.

senses.en: attempting to win favor from influential people by flattery

examples.text: The fawning courtiers competed to praise the king's every decision, however foolish.

senses.en: To celebrate (a person or event).

examples.text: Danielle Salamon was also four when she was feted as a musical genius in 1953.

senses.en: an elaborate party (often outdoors)

examples.text: The village held an annual summer fete with music, games and stalls selling homemade jam.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 fête(축제)에서 왔고 feast, fiesta와 같은 뿌리입니다. 축제처럼 성대히 대접한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: promote the growth of

examples.text: Our company fosters an appreciation for the arts.

senses.en: providing or receiving nurture or parental care though not related by blood or legal ties

examples.text: The foster family welcomed three siblings into their home during the long winter.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 fōstor(음식, 양육)에서 왔습니다. 먹여 키운다는 데서 '육성하다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: the state of being weak in health or body (especially from old age)

examples.text: Despite his frailty, the old professor insisted on delivering the lecture himself.

senses.en: moral weakness

examples.text: The novelist treats human frailty with sympathy rather than condemnation.

origin.ko: 라틴어 fragilitās(깨지기 쉬움)에서 고대 프랑스어를 거쳐 왔습니다. 쉽게 부서질 듯한 허약함입니다.

senses.en: a worker who holds or is invested with an office

examples.text: A minor party functionary stamped the documents without even glancing at their contents.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 fonctionnaire에서 왔습니다. function(직무)을 수행하는 사람이라는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: To gather (something, now chiefly something intangible such as experience or information) in small amounts over a period of time, often with some difficulty; to scrape together.

examples.text: Historians have gleaned much of what we know about daily life from merchants' account books.

senses.en: gather, as of natural products

examples.text: Poor villagers were allowed to glean the leftover grain once the fields had been harvested.

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 glenāre '모으다'에서 고대 프랑스어를 거쳐 왔습니다. 추수 뒤 떨어진 이삭을 줍는 데서 '조금씩 모으다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: make happy or satisfied

examples.text: It gratified the author to learn that her old novel had been reissued to critical praise.

senses.en: yield (to); give satisfaction to

examples.text: The company's advertising seeks to gratify consumers' every passing whim rather than meet genuine needs.

origin.ko: 라틴어 grātificō '호의를 베풀다'에서 왔습니다. grātus(기쁜)와 faciō(만들다)가 합쳐져 기쁘게 해 준다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: shockingly repellent; inspiring horror

examples.text: The photographs of the killings depict a grisly scene.

origin.ko: 고대영어 grīsan '공포에 떨다'에 -lic이 붙은 grisliċ에서 왔습니다. 몸서리쳐지는 모습이라는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: To argue for a better deal, especially over prices between a buyer and seller.

examples.text: I haggled for a better price because the original price was too high.

origin.ko: 중세영어 haggen '마구 베다'에서 왔고 hack(난도질하다)과 같은 계통입니다. 값을 깎아 잘라낸다는 이미지입니다.

senses.en: an excessive and often ineffectual display of concern or distress

examples.text: After all the public hand-wringing, the council quietly approved the budget cuts without any alternative plan.

senses.en: excessively quick

examples.text: The company's headlong expansion into new markets left it with dangerously thin cash reserves.

senses.en: in a hasty and foolhardy manner

examples.text: he fell headlong in love with his cousin

origin.ko: 중세영어 hedling '머리부터'가 long처럼 바뀐 말입니다. 머리부터 곧장 뛰어드는 성급함입니다.

senses.en: habitually disposed to disobedience and opposition

examples.text: The headstrong young prince ignored every warning from his advisers and marched into the mountains.

origin.ko: head(머리)와 strong(강한)의 합성어입니다. 머릿속 생각이 너무 세서 고집이 셉니다.

senses.en: listen; used mostly in the imperative

examples.text: The villagers gathered to hearken to the elder's account of the long-forgotten flood.

origin.ko: 고대영어 hercnian '귀 기울이다'에서 왔고 hark에 -en이 붙은 모양입니다.

senses.en: characterized by departure from accepted beliefs or standards

examples.text: Most Christian denominations consider each other heterodox.

origin.ko: 그리스어 heteródoxos로, héteros(다른)와 dóxa(의견)가 합쳐졌습니다. 남과 다른 의견이라 '이단적인'입니다.

senses.en: a state of dishonor

examples.text: The disgraced minister retired in ignominy after the fraud was exposed.

origin.ko: 라틴어 ignōminia '불명예'에서 왔습니다. in-(없는)과 nomen(이름, 명성)이 합쳐져 명성을 잃은 상태입니다.

senses.en: having or revealing little emotion or sensibility; not easily aroused or excited

examples.text: The defendant remained impassive as the jury read out the verdict, betraying neither relief nor fear.

origin.ko: in-(않는)에 passive가 붙은 말입니다. 겪어도 감정이 움직이지 않아 '무표정한'입니다.

senses.en: To collapse or burst inward violently.

examples.text: The submarine imploded as it sank below its crush depth.

senses.en: To suddenly lose support in all areas of a campaign simultaneously.

examples.text: Ragusa's campaign imploded after she confused coal mining with oil drilling during a speech.

origin.ko: implosion에서 거꾸로 만든 말입니다. 안쪽(in)으로 터지는(plode) 모습입니다.

senses.en: not prudent or wise

examples.text: It was imprudent of the company to expand so quickly without securing adequate funding.

origin.ko: 라틴어 imprūdens '미리 내다보지 못하는'에서 왔습니다. 분별이 없으니 '경솔한'입니다.

senses.en: without or deprived of the use of speech or words
senses.ko: 말을 못 하는, 분명하게 표현하지 못하는

examples.text: Overwhelmed by grief, the witness became inarticulate and could only shake his head when questioned.

origin.ko: 라틴어 inarticulātus에서 왔습니다. 말을 마디마디 또렷이 나누지 못해 분명히 표현하지 못합니다.

senses.en: poor enough to need help from others

examples.text: The clinic provides free care to indigent patients who cannot afford insurance.

origin.ko: 라틴어 indigēns '필요로 하는'에서 왔고 indigeō(부족하다)가 뿌리입니다. 필요한 것이 없는 가난한 상태입니다.

senses.en: beyond normal limits

examples.text: The project consumed an inordinate amount of time and money without producing any usable results.

origin.ko: 라틴어 inōrdinātus '정리되지 않은, 무질서한'에서 왔습니다. 질서의 한계를 벗어나 '지나친'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: the trait of being rude and impertinent; inclined to take liberties

examples.text: The captain punished the sailor's insolence by taking away his shore leave for a month.

origin.ko: 라틴어 īnsolentia에서 왔습니다. 관례(익숙함)에 따르지 않는 건방진 태도입니다.

senses.en: command against

examples.text: The council moved to interdict the sale of the drug until further safety tests were completed.

senses.en: a court order prohibiting a party from doing a certain activity

examples.text: The court issued an interdict barring the factory from dumping waste into the river.

origin.ko: 라틴어 interdīcō '금지하다'에서 왔습니다. 사이에 끼어들어 말로 막는다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: (of conflict) within a group or organization

examples.text: Internecine disputes among the party's factions weakened it far more than any opposition attack.

senses.en: Mutually destructive; most often applied to warfare.

examples.text: The internecine struggle left both armies exhausted and the countryside in ruins.

origin.ko: 라틴어 internecīnus '치명적인'에서 왔고 원래는 '대학살'과 관련됩니다. 영어에서 inter-(사이)로 재해석되어 '내부 갈등'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: spin, wind, or twist together

examples.text: intertwine the ribbons

senses.en: To become mutually involved.

examples.text: The economies of the two nations have become so intertwined that a crisis in one affects the other.

origin.ko: inter-(서로)와 twine(꼬다)이 합쳐진 말입니다. 서로 꼬여 얽히는 모습입니다.

senses.en: give life or energy to

examples.text: The cold water invigorated him

origin.ko: 새 라틴어 invigōrō에서 왔고 in-과 vigor(활력)가 합쳐졌습니다. 몸속에 힘을 불어넣는다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: not capable of being violated or infringed

examples.text: The constitution declares freedom of conscience an inviolable right that no government may override.

origin.ko: 라틴어 inviolābilis '건드릴 수 없는'에서 왔습니다. 범할 수 없으니 '불가침의'입니다.

senses.en: without flaws or loopholes

examples.text: The suspect had an ironclad alibi for his whereabouts on the night of the crime.

senses.en: inflexibly entrenched and unchangeable

examples.text: The party's ironclad traditions left no room for reform-minded newcomers.

origin.ko: iron(쇠)과 clad(입은)가 합쳐진 말입니다. 철갑을 두른 듯 빈틈이 없다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: impossible to deny or disprove

examples.text: The recovered documents provided irrefutable proof that the company had falsified its safety reports.

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 irrefūtābilis에서 왔습니다. 되받아 물리칠 수 없다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: distort adversely

examples.text: Jealousy had jaundiced his judgment

senses.en: A feeling of bitterness, resentment or jealousy.

examples.text: Years of rejection left the critic with a jaundice that colored every review.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 jaunisse에서 왔고 jaune(노란색)에서 나왔습니다. 노란 눈으로 보듯 시각이 비뚤어진다는 뜻으로 번졌습니다.

senses.en: Cheerful and good-humoured; jolly, merry.

examples.text: The jovial host greeted every guest with a warm handshake and a joke.

origin.ko: 이탈리아어와 프랑스어를 거쳐 로마 신 유피테르(Iovis)에서 왔습니다. 목성 아래 태어난 사람이 쾌활하다고 믿던 데서 나왔습니다.

senses.en: a trip taken by an official at public expense

examples.text: Watchdog groups criticized the committee's overseas junket as a taxpayer-funded vacation.

senses.en: A feast or banquet.

examples.text: The village held a lavish junket after the harvest was safely gathered in.

origin.ko: 중세 영어 jonket '골풀 바구니'에서 왔습니다. 바구니에 담은 잔치 음식, 소풍, 공비로 가는 놀이 여행으로 뜻이 넓어졌습니다.

senses.en: One who is not intimately familiar with a given subject or activity.

examples.text: The book was written for professionals, but an intelligent layperson could understand most of it.

senses.en: someone who is not a clergyman or a professional person

examples.text: The council includes both clergy and laypersons from each parish.

origin.ko: lay(성직자가 아닌)와 person이 합쳐졌습니다. layman을 본뜬 말로 비전문가를 가리킵니다.

senses.en: the words of an opera or musical play

examples.text: The composer rewrote the libretto twice before the opera finally reached the stage.

origin.ko: 이탈리아어 libro(책)에 축소 접미사가 붙은 말입니다. 오페라의 작은 책, 곧 대본입니다.

senses.en: A rich source of supply.

examples.text: The archive proved a rich lode of material for historians of the period.

senses.en: a deposit of valuable ore occurring within definite boundaries separating it from surrounding rocks

examples.text: Prospectors struck a lode of silver high in the canyon wall.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 lād '길, 여정'에서 왔습니다. 광업 용어로 굳어 '광맥'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: glaringly vivid and graphic; marked by sensationalism

examples.text: lurid details of the accident

senses.en: shining with an unnatural red glow as of fire seen through smoke

examples.text: a lurid sunset

origin.ko: 라틴어 lūridus '창백한 노란색의'에서 왔습니다. 병든 듯한 섬뜩한 빛깔이 선정적인 뜻으로 번졌습니다.

senses.en: produced or growing in extreme abundance

examples.text: Luxuriant vines covered the ruined walls of the abandoned monastery.

senses.en: marked by complexity and richness of detail

examples.text: The poet's luxuriant imagery occasionally overwhelmed the simple story beneath it.

origin.ko: 라틴어 lūxuriāns에서 왔고 lūxuria '사치, 넘침'에서 나왔습니다. 넘치도록 무성하다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: A female leader of a family, a tribe or an ethnic or religious group.

examples.text: The family matriarch presided over every holiday dinner and settled all disputes with a glance.

origin.ko: 라틴어 māter(어머니)와 그리스어 -arkhēs(우두머리)가 합쳐졌습니다. 어머니가 이끄는 집안의 지도자입니다.

senses.en: A mixture of different things; a disordered mixture.

examples.text: The room was a melange of comic books and posters.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 mélange에서 왔고 mêler(섞다)와 라틴어 misceō에서 나왔습니다.

senses.en: Like a meteor in speed, brilliance, or ephemeralness.

examples.text: Her meteoric rise to power was followed by a slow, lackluster career at the top.

origin.ko: meteor(유성)에 -ic이 붙은 말입니다. 유성처럼 빠르고 눈부시다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: A quality of courage and endurance.

examples.text: The harsh winter tested the mettle of every member of the expedition.

origin.ko: metal(금속)의 비유적 쓰임에서 나왔습니다. 쇠처럼 단단한 기개라는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: dignified manner or conduct

examples.text: The retired general kept a calm, authoritative mien even in the middle of the crisis.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 mine '외모'에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: affectedly dainty or refined

examples.text: He crossed the room with mincing steps, wary of scuffing his polished shoes.

senses.en: Tedium as a result of repetition or a lack of variety.

examples.text: Long voyages at sea were broken only rarely from the monotony of endless grey water.

origin.ko: 그리스어 monotonía '한 가지 음조'에서 프랑스어를 거쳐 왔습니다. 변화 없는 한 가지 소리가 지루함이 되었습니다.

senses.en: Smart and fashionable.

examples.text: The natty gentleman arrived in a pressed linen suit and a bright silk pocket square.

senses.en: Vague or ill-defined.

examples.text: The committee's nebulous guidelines left applicants unsure what evidence would actually satisfy the review board.

origin.ko: 라틴어 nebula '안개, 구름'에서 왔습니다. 안개가 낀 듯 흐릿해서 모호하다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: The view that all endeavours are devoid of objective meaning.

examples.text: The novel's bleak nihilism leaves its characters with no belief in morality or purpose.

senses.en: complete denial of all established authority and institutions

examples.text: The movement's political nihilism rejected every institution, from parliament to the church.

origin.ko: 라틴어 nihil '무(無)'에서 나온 말입니다. 모든 것이 무의미하다고 보는 입장입니다.

senses.en: Not obvious or easy to prove; not self-evident.

examples.text: Extending the theorem to higher dimensions is a nontrivial problem that took mathematicians decades.

senses.en: An ineffective but favorite remedy for a problem, usually involving political action.

examples.text: Economists warned that tax cuts alone were a political nostrum, not a cure for stagnation.

senses.en: patent medicine whose efficacy is questionable

examples.text: Peddlers sold bottled nostrums at county fairs, promising to cure everything from baldness to grief.

origin.ko: 라틴어 nostrum '우리의 것'에서 왔습니다. '우리만의 비방'이라며 내세우는 만병통치약 같은 처방을 가리킵니다.

senses.en: Having total knowledge.

examples.text: The story was narrated from an omniscient point of view.

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 omnisciens '모든 것을 아는'에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: wealth as evidenced by sumptuous living

examples.text: Visitors were stunned by the opulence of the palace, with its gilded ceilings and marble floors.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 opulence에서 왔고, 라틴어 opulentia가 원형입니다. 재물이 넘치는 호화로움을 뜻합니다.

senses.en: be greater in significance than

examples.text: The scandal overshadowed the company's record profits and dominated the news for weeks.

senses.en: To obscure something by casting a shadow.

examples.text: Tall pines overshadowed the cottage and kept its garden in perpetual gloom.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 ofersceadwian '그늘로 덮다'에서 왔습니다. 큰 그림자가 덮어 빛을 잃게 한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: A partially shaded area around the edges of a shadow, especially an eclipse.

examples.text: The other places see the penumbra of the moon's shadow fall on the earth, so the eclipse is partial, and part of the sun's disc is still visible.

senses.en: An area of uncertainty or intermediacy between two mutually exclusive states or categories.

examples.text: The new technology operates in a legal penumbra that regulators have yet to address.

origin.ko: 신라틴어 pēnumbra에서 왔으며, paene(거의) + umbra(그림자)로 '거의 그림자'라는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: A person of low rank or importance.

examples.text: He is well dressed in cheap clothing. Like an office peon whose wife works in a laundry.

senses.en: a laborer who is obliged to do menial work

examples.text: Landowners once kept entire families as peons, bound to the estate by debt.

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 pedōnem '보행자'에서 왔습니다. 걸어 다니는 하인이라는 데서 말단 인물을 가리키게 되었습니다.

senses.en: The humanistic study of texts and their languages, especially ancient or classical languages.

examples.text: Her training in philology allowed her to date the manuscript from its spelling alone.

origin.ko: 그리스어 philología '말과 학문에 대한 사랑'에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: a quality that arouses emotions (especially pity or sorrow)

examples.text: The poignancy of the soldier's last letter moved even the most hardened readers.

senses.en: Pompous, dignified or dogmatic.

examples.text: His pontifical manner made even simple suggestions sound like decrees from on high.

senses.en: Of or pertaining to a pope; papal.

examples.text: The pontifical decree was read aloud to the assembled bishops.

origin.ko: 라틴어 pontifex('대제사장')의 형용사형입니다. 교황 같은 권위를 부리는 태도에서 '거만한'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: A short, private conference.

examples.text: The coaches held a quick powwow on the sideline before changing the team's strategy.

origin.ko: 북미 원주민 알곤킨어 계통에서 온 말로, 원래 주술사나 주술 의식을 가리켰습니다. 모임·협의를 뜻하게 되었습니다.

senses.en: Alternative spelling of preempt.

examples.text: The company moved to pre-empt criticism by publishing its own audit before regulators could.

origin.ko: 라틴어 prae-('먼저')와 emere('사다')가 합쳐진 말입니다. 남보다 먼저 사서 차지한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: To make known or make public.

examples.text: Missionaries worked for decades to promulgate the new doctrine across the region.

senses.en: put a law into effect by formal declaration

examples.text: The ministry promulgated new safety regulations that take effect next year.

origin.ko: 라틴어 prōmulgāre('공표하다')에서 왔습니다. 법령을 앞으로 내놓아 널리 알린다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: providing carefully for the future

examples.text: A provident family, they saved a portion of every paycheck for emergencies.

origin.ko: 라틴어 prōvidēre('미리 보다')의 현재분사에서 왔습니다. 앞일을 미리 보고 대비합니다.

senses.en: To hit or strike heavily and repeatedly.

examples.text: Rain pummeled the roof.

senses.en: To scornfully criticize someone or something.

examples.text: The politician was pummeled by the media for his controversial statements.

origin.ko: pommel('칼자루 머리')의 변형입니다. 칼자루 머리로 두들기던 데서 마구 때린다는 뜻이 되었습니다.

senses.en: of or relating to or resembling Pyrrhus or his exploits (especially his sustaining staggering losses in order to defeat the Romans)
senses.ko: 피로스의 승리 같은, 희생이 너무 커서 득이 없는

examples.text: The company won the lawsuit, but legal fees made it a Pyrrhic victory.

origin.ko: 그리스어 purrhichē('전쟁 춤')에서 온 말로, 로마와 싸워 이기고도 큰 손실을 본 왕 피로스에서 '희생이 큰 승리'라는 뜻이 되었습니다.

senses.en: A perilous, mixed up and troubled situation; a hopeless tangle.

examples.text: The paperwork got lost in a quagmire of bureaucracy.

senses.en: a soft wet area of low-lying land that sinks underfoot

examples.text: Heavy rain turned the battlefield into a quagmire that swallowed boots and wagon wheels.

origin.ko: quag('늪')와 mire('진창')가 합쳐진 말입니다. 발이 빠지는 수렁에서 헤어나기 힘든 상황이라는 뜻이 되었습니다.

senses.en: declare invalid

examples.text: The appeals court quashed the conviction after new evidence cast doubt on the verdict.

senses.en: put down by force or intimidation

examples.text: The army quashed the rebellion.

origin.ko: 라틴어 quassāre('흔들다, 부수다')와 cassāre('무효로 하다')의 영향을 받은 고대 프랑스어에서 왔습니다. 판결을 부숴 무효로 한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: tangle or complicate

examples.text: a ravelled story

senses.en: disentangle

examples.text: can you unravel the mystery?

origin.ko: 네덜란드어 ravelen('엉키다, 풀리다')을 빌려 온 말입니다. 실이 엉키는 모습에서 얽히게 한다는 뜻이 되었습니다.

senses.en: a chemical substance that is present at the start of a chemical reaction

examples.text: In the experiment, the students measured how quickly each reactant was consumed as the temperature rose.

senses.en: serving to bring to mind

examples.text: The film's soft colors and jazz score are redolent of postwar Paris.

senses.en: (used with ‘of’ or ‘with’) noticeably odorous

examples.text: the hall was redolent of floor wax

origin.ko: 라틴어 redolēre('냄새를 풍기다')의 현재분사에서 왔습니다. 냄새가 기억을 불러내듯 무언가를 연상시킵니다.

senses.en: a communal dining-hall (usually in a monastery)

examples.text: The monks gathered in the refectory each evening for a silent meal.

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 refectorium에서 왔고 reficere('다시 만들다')에서 나왔습니다. 먹고 기운을 되찾는 식당입니다.

senses.en: a remote or indirect consequence of some action

examples.text: his declaration had unforeseen repercussions

origin.ko: 라틴어 repercutere('되튀게 하다')에서 왔습니다. 쳤을 때 되돌아오는 반향이 '간접적 영향'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: intense aversion

examples.text: Readers expressed revulsion at the detailed descriptions of cruelty in the report.

origin.ko: 라틴어 revulsio에서 왔습니다. 몸을 '뒤로 확 잡아당기는' 반응이 강한 혐오감이 되었습니다.

senses.en: A title of a category or a class.

examples.text: That would fall under the rubric of things we can ignore for now.

senses.en: an authoritative rule of conduct or procedure

examples.text: Under the university's rubric, any plagiarized assignment must be reported to the dean.

senses.en: A set of scoring criteria for evaluating student work and for giving feedback.

examples.text: We refer to the rubric when marking oral examinations.

origin.ko: 라틴어 rubrica(붉은 흙)에서 왔습니다. 붉은 글씨로 쓴 제목이 항목, 분류명이 되었습니다.

senses.en: a long piece of writing

examples.text: I see it's three o'clock in the morning and I've written whole screeds when I only intended to write a short note!

senses.en: a long monotonous harangue

examples.text: The senator delivered a screed against the proposed tax, ignoring the clock and the weary chamber.

origin.ko: 중세 영어 screde(조각, 긴 띠)에서 왔고 shred와 같은 계열입니다. 길게 잘라낸 조각 같은 장황한 글입니다.

senses.en: of the most contemptible kind

examples.text: The captain denounced the scurvy trick that had cost his crew their wages.

senses.en: a condition caused by deficiency of ascorbic acid (vitamin C)

examples.text: Sailors on long voyages once suffered terribly from scurvy until citrus fruit became part of their rations.

origin.ko: scurf(피부에 생기는 비늘, 딱지)에 -y가 붙어 '딱지투성이의'라는 뜻이었다가 비열하다는 뜻이 되었습니다.

senses.en: generate and separate from cells or bodily fluids

examples.text: Many tumors secrete two or more different hormones.

senses.en: place out of sight; keep secret

examples.text: The smuggler secreted the jewels in the lining of his coat before approaching the border.

origin.ko: 라틴어 sēcernere(분리하다)에서 왔습니다. 혈액 등에서 물질을 따로 가려내 내보낸다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: lucky in making unexpected and fortunate discoveries

examples.text: Their serendipitous meeting in a small bookshop led to a decade-long collaboration.

origin.ko: serendipity에서 나온 형용사로, 18세기 월폴이 만든 말입니다. 우연한 행운을 얻는다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: good luck in making unexpected and fortunate discoveries

examples.text: By pure serendipity, the researcher noticed the mold that would lead her to a new antibiotic.

origin.ko: 호러스 월폴이 1754년 동화 '세렌딥의 세 왕자'에서 지었습니다. 왕자들이 우연히 귀한 것을 발견하는 이야기입니다.

senses.en: A navigational device for deriving angular distances between objects so as to determine latitude and longitude.

examples.text: Before satellites, sailors fixed their position at sea with a sextant and a chronometer.

origin.ko: 라틴어 sextāns(6분의 1)에서 왔습니다. 원의 6분의 1 호를 가진 도구입니다.

senses.en: avoid (one's assigned duties)

examples.text: The derelict soldier shirked his duties

origin.ko: 1633년경 처음 보이며 어원이 불확실합니다. shark나 독일어 Schurke(악당)와 연관된다는 설이 있습니다.

senses.en: adroitness in using the hands

examples.text: The magician's sleight of hand was so smooth that no one in the audience saw the coin vanish.

senses.en: An artful trick; sly artifice; a feat so dexterous that the manner of performance escapes observation.

examples.text: The accountant's sleight with the figures concealed the missing funds for several years.

origin.ko: 고대 노르드어 slœgð(교활함)에서 왔고 sly와 같은 뿌리입니다. 능란하고 교묘한 손재주입니다.

senses.en: Filthiness and degradation, as from neglect or poverty

examples.text: The heterogenous indigent multitude, everywhere wearing nearly the same aspect of squalor.

origin.ko: 라틴어 squālor(더러움)에서 왔습니다. 방치되어 불결하고 초라한 상태입니다.

senses.en: showing a brooding ill humor

examples.text: And sullen I forsook the imperfect feast.

senses.en: Gloomy; dismal; foreboding.

examples.text: a sullen atmosphere

origin.ko: 앵글로노르만어 soleyn(혼자인)에서 왔고 라틴어 sōlus(혼자)와 이어집니다. 혼자 틀어박혀 시무룩하다는 뜻이 되었습니다.

senses.en: imagine to be the case or true or probable

examples.text: If, as I surmise, you see the ladies this evening, you might mention my intended visit.

senses.en: Thought, imagination, or conjecture, which may be based upon feeble or scanty evidence; suspicion; guess.

examples.text: This opinion, however, is merely a surmise, which may or may not be the case.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 surmettre(위에 얹다, 고발하다)의 과거분사에서 왔습니다. 증거 위에 얹은 짐작을 뜻합니다.

senses.en: deprive of by deceit

examples.text: The two men swindled the company out of $160,000.

senses.en: the act of swindling by some fraudulent scheme

examples.text: Investigators uncovered a pension swindle that had cost retirees millions of dollars.

origin.ko: 독일어 Schwindler(사기꾼)에서 역성된 말로, schwindeln(어지럽다, 속이다)에서 나왔습니다.

senses.en: stressing a normally weak beat

examples.text: The drummer's syncopated rhythm gave the old folk tune an unexpected jazz-like energy.

senses.en: of superficial relevance if any

examples.text: That subject is tangential to our discussion, and we cannot let it distract us.

senses.en: of or relating to or acting along or in the direction of a tangent

examples.text: tangential forces

origin.ko: tangent(접선)에 -ial이 붙은 말입니다. 살짝 스치기만 하는 정도의 관련성입니다.

senses.en: arousing desire or expectation for something unattainable or mockingly out of reach

examples.text: a tantalizing taste of success

senses.en: very pleasantly inviting

examples.text: a tantalizing aroma

origin.ko: 그리스 신화 탄탈로스에서 왔습니다. 물과 과일이 눈앞에 있어도 닿지 못하는 벌을 받았습니다.

senses.en: feeling or showing little interest or enthusiasm

examples.text: He gave me a tepid response to the proposal.

senses.en: moderately warm

examples.text: The bath had gone tepid by the time she finally climbed in.

origin.ko: 라틴어 tepidus('미지근한')에서 왔습니다. 뜨겁지도 차갑지도 않은 물처럼 열의가 없다는 뜻이 되었습니다.

senses.en: Any adversity; a trying period or event.

examples.text: The family endured years of tribulation after the factory closed and the town lost its main employer.

origin.ko: 라틴어 tribulāre('짓누르다')에서 왔고 곡식 타작 도구 trībulum과 이어집니다. 짓눌리는 고통이 '시련'입니다.

senses.en: a state of commotion and noise and confusion

examples.text: The announcement threw the trading floor into tumult as brokers shouted orders over one another.

senses.en: violent agitation

examples.text: She tried to calm the tumult of her emotions before facing the jury.

origin.ko: 라틴어 tumultus('소동, 소란')에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: To uncover or find; to bring out from concealment.

examples.text: Investigative reporters unearthed documents showing that the contractor had falsified its safety records.

senses.en: recover through digging

examples.text: Archaeologists unearthed a cache of bronze tools beneath the floor of the ancient house.

origin.ko: un-과 earth('땅')의 결합입니다. 땅에서 파내는 모습이 '발굴하다'입니다.

senses.en: Not viable: not capable of independent life; not practicable.

examples.text: With rising costs and falling demand, the business model had become financially unviable.

senses.en: The final result, or outcome of something.

examples.text: The upshot of the long negotiations was a modest agreement that satisfied neither side completely.

origin.ko: 양궁 시합의 마지막 한 발에서 나온 말로 추정합니다. 마지막 결과라는 뜻이 되었습니다.

senses.en: seize and take control without authority and possibly with force; take as one's right or possession

examples.text: The general plotted to usurp the throne while the young king was abroad.

senses.en: take the place of

examples.text: Streaming services have gradually usurped traditional television as the main way audiences watch films.

origin.ko: 라틴어 ūsūrpō('사용하려고 차지하다')에서 왔습니다. 남의 자리를 빼앗아 '찬탈하다'입니다.

senses.en: capable of being corrupted

examples.text: The venal inspector overlooked every safety violation in exchange for a steady stream of cash.

senses.en: Of a position, privilege etc.: available for purchase rather than assigned on merit.

examples.text: In the old regime, judicial offices were venal and went to the highest bidder.

origin.ko: 라틴어 vēnālis('팔려고 내놓은')에서 왔고 vēnum('판매물')과 이어집니다. 돈에 팔릴 수 있어 '매수당하기 쉬운'입니다.

senses.en: Lively and animated; full of life and energy.

examples.text: The vivacious hostess moved through the crowd, drawing even the shyest guests into conversation.

origin.ko: 라틴어 vīvāx('활기찬')에서 왔고 vīvere('살다')와 이어집니다.

senses.en: of very poor quality or condition

examples.text: The team's woeful defense allowed more goals than any other squad in the league.

senses.en: affected by or full of grief or woe

examples.text: The woeful widow stood silently at the graveside long after the others had left.

origin.ko: woe('비통')와 -ful의 결합입니다. 비통함이 가득하다는 뜻에서 '형편없는'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: in former times was free and cultivated their own land

examples.text: The English yeoman, owning his own modest farm, formed the backbone of the rural economy.

senses.en: A dependable, diligent, or loyal worker or someone who does a great service.

examples.text: She did yeoman work organizing the volunteers, and the festival ran smoothly because of her.

senses.en: a tangible symbol signifying approval or distinction

examples.text: The architect received many accolades for the museum, including the profession's highest prize.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 accolade(포옹)에서 왔고 라틴어 collum(목)에서 나왔습니다. 기사 서임 때 목을 껴안던 의식에서 '영예의 표시'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: eager to acquire and possess things especially material possessions or ideas

examples.text: The acquisitive young banker spent his weekends hunting for rare paintings to add to his collection.

origin.ko: 라틴어 acquisitus(얻은)에서 왔습니다. 계속 얻으려는 성향이 '탐욕스러운'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: Something which is vehemently disliked by somebody.

examples.text: Censorship was anathema to the editor, who had fought all his life for a free press.

senses.en: a formal ecclesiastical curse accompanied by excommunication

examples.text: The council pronounced an anathema upon the heretic and expelled him from the church.

origin.ko: 그리스어 anathema(바쳐진 것)에서 왔습니다. 저주받아 바쳐진 것이라는 뜻이 '극도로 혐오하는 대상'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: lacking vigor or energy

examples.text: Despite heavy promotion, the film's anemic box-office returns disappointed its producers.

origin.ko: 그리스어 an-(없는)과 haima(피)에서 온 anemia(빈혈)에서 나왔습니다. 피가 부족해 기운 없는 모습입니다.

senses.en: marked by a lack of interest

examples.text: an apathetic audience

origin.ko: apathy(무감정)에서 나온 형용사입니다. 감정이 일어나지 않는 상태입니다.

senses.en: enough to be estimated or measured

examples.text: appreciable amounts of noxious wastes are dumped into the harbor

origin.ko: 프랑스어 appréciable에서 왔습니다. 값을 매길 만큼 눈에 띈다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: free of or using methods to keep free of pathological microorganisms

examples.text: Pharmaceuticals are packaged using aseptic techniques.

origin.ko: 그리스어 a-(없는)와 septikos(썩게 하는)에서 왔습니다. 부패나 세균이 없는 상태입니다.

senses.en: moderate or restrain; lessen the force of

examples.text: He bated his breath when talking about this affair

origin.ko: abate(약해지다)의 앞 글자 a가 떨어져 나간 형태입니다. 기세를 눌러 줄인다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: Ruined, spoiled.

examples.text: Residents of the blighted neighborhood waited decades for new investment that never arrived.

senses.en: To move or swing a weapon back and forth, particularly if demonstrating anger, threat or skill.

examples.text: He brandished his sword at the pirates.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 brandir('칼을 휘두르다')에서 왔고, 프랑크어 brand(불붙은 나무토막, 검)에서 유래했습니다.

senses.en: a swaggering show of courage

examples.text: The angry customer stood in the middle of the showroom and voiced his complaints with loud bravado.

origin.ko: 이탈리아어 bravata(허세)를 거쳐 프랑스어 bravade에서 왔고, bravare(자랑하다)와 bravo에서 갈라졌습니다.

senses.en: Physical strength; muscularity.

examples.text: The builders at the site had more brawn than brain.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 braon('살점, 근육 있는 부위')에서 왔습니다. 고기가 붙은 살덩이에서 '근력'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: A defense or safeguard.

examples.text: An independent press is a bulwark against abuse of power in any democracy.

senses.en: an embankment built around a space for defensive purposes

examples.text: Soldiers stood along the bulwark of the old fortress, watching the road below.

origin.ko: 중세 네덜란드어 bolwerk에서 왔고, bole(나무 줄기)와 work가 합쳐졌습니다. 통나무로 쌓은 방벽입니다.

senses.en: Acting in a confused or ineffectual way; incompetent or inept; showing little or no skill.

examples.text: The bumbling detective in the comedy solves every case by accident rather than skill.

senses.en: well in the past; former

examples.text: The museum recreates the daily life of a bygone era with remarkable care.

origin.ko: by(옆을 지나)와 gone(가 버린)이 합쳐진 말로, 곁을 지나가 버린 과거를 뜻합니다.

senses.en: a major division of a long poem

examples.text: In the third canto of the epic, the hero descends into the underworld.

origin.ko: 이탈리아어 canto('노래')에서 왔고 chant와 같은 어원입니다. 긴 시를 노래의 한 대목처럼 나눈 단위입니다.

senses.en: censure severely or angrily

examples.text: The mother scolded the child for entering a stranger's car

origin.ko: 고대 영어 ċīdan('꾸짖다, 다투다')에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: climb awkwardly, as if by scrambling

examples.text: The children clambered over the jungle gym.

origin.ko: 중세 영어 clambren('기어오르다')에서 왔습니다. 정확한 기원은 불확실합니다.

senses.en: an elaborate poetic image or a far-fetched comparison of very dissimilar things

examples.text: Donne's famous conceit compares two separated lovers to the legs of a drawing compass.

senses.en: feelings of excessive pride

examples.text: His conceit was so great that he never asked anyone for advice.

origin.ko: 중세 영어 conceyte에서 왔고 conceyven(생각해 내다)에서 만들어졌습니다. concept와 같은 어원으로, 머릿속에 붙든 기발한 생각입니다.

senses.en: engage in plotting or enter into a conspiracy, swear together

examples.text: They conspired to overthrow the government

senses.en: To work together to bring about.

examples.text: Rain and sweat conspired to smudge her mascara.

origin.ko: 라틴어 conspīrō('함께 숨쉬다')에서 왔습니다. 숨결을 맞춰 몰래 뜻을 합친다는 이미지입니다.

senses.en: To place something or someone in a particular context.

examples.text: The curator added panels to contextualize the artifacts within the broader history of the region.

senses.en: any system of principles or beliefs

examples.text: The company's credo, printed on every wall, insisted that employees put customers before profit.

origin.ko: 라틴어 crēdō '나는 믿는다'를 그대로 가져왔습니다. 신앙 고백의 첫 말이 '신조'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: sing softly

examples.text: She crooned a lullaby to the baby until his eyelids finally drooped and closed.

origin.ko: 중세 네덜란드어 crônen(신음하다, 한탄하다)에서 왔다고 봅니다. 낮게 웅얼대는 소리가 '나직이 노래하다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: a state of guilt

examples.text: The investigation established his culpability in the fraud.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 culpabilité에서 왔고 라틴어 culpa(잘못)에서 나온 말입니다.

senses.en: A wasting of time in idleness or trifles.

examples.text: Any further dalliance over the budget would push the project past its funding deadline.

senses.en: Playful flirtation; amorous play.

examples.text: The novel recounts the duchess's brief dalliance with a young painter at court.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 dalier(수다 떨다)에서 중세 영어를 거쳐 왔고, dally에 -ance가 붙은 말입니다.

senses.en: To destroy the morale of; to dishearten.

examples.text: Constant layoffs and unclear leadership demoralized the staff and drove the best engineers away.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 démoraliser에서 왔습니다. 사기(morale)를 없앤다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: the easing of tensions or strained relations (especially between nations)

examples.text: The two superpowers entered a period of detente that reduced the risk of open conflict.

senses.en: lose clarity or turn aside especially from the main subject of attention or course of argument in writing, thinking, or speaking

examples.text: She always digresses when telling a story

origin.ko: 라틴어 digredi(따로 걸어가다)에서 왔습니다. 본래 길에서 옆으로 빠지는 이미지입니다.

senses.en: Shabby, squalid, uncared-for.

examples.text: The dingy apartment smelled of damp and its walls were stained from years of neglect.

senses.en: Dark, dull.

examples.text: The dingy light of a winter afternoon made the office feel even more oppressive.

origin.ko: 켄트 방언 dingy(더러운)에서 왔다고 보며, 확실하지 않습니다. dung(똥)에서 왔을 가능성이 있습니다.

senses.en: extend in a different direction

examples.text: Their interests diverged

senses.en: be at variance with; be out of line with

examples.text: The software is pretty good, except for a few cases where its behavior diverges from user expectations.

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 dīvergō(다른 쪽으로 꺾다)에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: shower with love; show excessive affection for

examples.text: Grandmother dotes on the twins

senses.en: be foolish or senile due to old age

examples.text: The old king began to dote, signing decrees he could no longer understand.

origin.ko: 중세 저지 독일어 doten(어리석다)에서 왔다고 봅니다. 어리석을 만큼 애정을 쏟는다는 뜻이 되었습니다.

senses.en: Bold; brave, courageous.

examples.text: The doughty old general led the final charge despite his age and several wounds.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 dohtiġ(유능한, 용감한)에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: someone sent on a mission to represent the interests of someone else

examples.text: The king dispatched an emissary to negotiate a truce with the rebel leaders.

origin.ko: 라틴어 ēmissārius(내보내진 사람, 밀사)에서 왔습니다. 임무를 띠고 밖으로 보내진 사람입니다.

senses.en: the branch of zoology that studies insects

examples.text: Her fascination with beetles led her to a career in entomology.

origin.ko: 그리스어 éntomon(곤충)에 -logía(학문)가 붙었습니다. éntomon은 몸이 마디로 '잘려 있다'는 데서 나온 말입니다.

senses.en: a witty saying

examples.text: Wilde's epigrams still sparkle with irony more than a century after they were written.

origin.ko: 그리스어 epígramma(비문, 새겨 쓴 글)에서 왔습니다. 짧게 새긴 글이 '경구'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: arouse hostility or indifference in where there had formerly been love, affection, or friendliness

examples.text: A bitter inheritance dispute served to estrange the two brothers for decades.

origin.ko: 라틴어 extrāneus(외부인)에서 고대 프랑스어 estranger를 거쳐 왔습니다. 가깝던 사람을 낯선 사람으로 대한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: obtain by coercion or intimidation

examples.text: They extorted money from the executive by threatening to reveal his past to the company boss

origin.ko: 라틴어 extorquēre(비틀어 짜내다)에서 왔습니다. 상대를 비틀어 억지로 빼앗아 내는 이미지입니다.

senses.en: be unsure or weak

examples.text: Their enthusiasm is faltering

senses.en: speak haltingly

examples.text: The speaker faltered when he saw his opponent enter the room

senses.en: To worsen, especially due to lack of attention.

examples.text: Deal with the problem immediately; do not let it fester.

senses.en: ripen and generate pus

examples.text: her wounds are festering

origin.ko: 라틴어 fistula(관, 고름이 나는 상처)에서 고대 프랑스어를 거쳐 왔습니다. 방치된 상처가 곪아 악화되는 이미지입니다.

senses.en: a long narrow cleft

examples.text: Steam escaped from a fissure in the volcano's side, warning scientists of a possible eruption.

senses.en: A state of incompatibility or disagreement.

examples.text: The scandal opened a deep fissure within the party that no compromise could fully repair.

origin.ko: 라틴어 fissūra(갈라진 틈)에서 왔고 findere(쪼개다)가 바탕입니다.

senses.en: intermittently stopping and starting

examples.text: Troubled by her unfinished work, she fell into a fitful sleep.

origin.ko: fit(발작, 갑작스러운 움직임)에 -ful이 붙었습니다. 발작처럼 멈췄다 시작했다 하는 불규칙함입니다.

senses.en: To act clumsily or confused; to struggle or be flustered.

examples.text: He gave a good speech, but floundered when audience members asked questions he could not answer well.

senses.en: walk with great difficulty

examples.text: The hikers floundered through waist-deep snow toward the distant cabin.

senses.en: a feeling of evil to come

examples.text: a steadily escalating sense of foreboding

senses.en: ominously prophetic

examples.text: Dark clouds gathered over the valley, lending the afternoon a foreboding stillness.

origin.ko: fore(미리)에 bode(전조가 되다)와 -ing이 붙었습니다. 나쁜 일을 미리 알리는 불길한 예감입니다.

senses.en: Pitifully sad, wretched, miserable; lonely, especially from feeling abandoned, deserted, forsaken.

examples.text: The forlorn child waited alone at the station long after the last train had left.

senses.en: marked by or showing hopelessness

examples.text: the last forlorn attempt

origin.ko: 고대 영어 forloren(잃어버린)에서 왔고 forlēosan(잃다)의 과거분사입니다. 버려져 잃어버린 듯 쓸쓸한 상태입니다.

senses.en: characterized by directness in manner or speech; without subtlety or evasion

examples.text: The witness was considered eminently credible thanks to her forthright answers.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 forþriht(곧장 앞으로)에서 왔습니다. forth(앞으로)와 right(곧은)로, 돌려 말하지 않는 직설입니다.

senses.en: an architectural ornament consisting of a horizontal sculptured band between the architrave and the cornice

examples.text: A marble frieze depicting a battle procession runs along the upper walls of the temple.

senses.en: A crux or pivot; a central point.

examples.text: The mediator became the fulcrum on which the entire peace negotiation turned.

senses.en: the pivot about which a lever turns

examples.text: Place the plank across a rock so the rock serves as the fulcrum of the lever.

origin.ko: 라틴어 fulcrum '침대 기둥'에서 왔고 fulciō(떠받치다)에서 나왔습니다. 받쳐 주는 지점이 '중심점'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: Able to be substituted for something of equal value or utility.

examples.text: Grain of a given grade is fungible, so one bushel can stand in for another.

origin.ko: 라틴어 fungor(수행하다, 대신하다)에서 왔습니다. 로마법에서 서로 대체할 수 있는 물건을 가리킨 법률 용어입니다.

senses.en: To prepare (oneself) for an action.

examples.text: The senator girded herself for a bruising confirmation battle.

senses.en: To encircle with, or as if with a belt.

examples.text: A broad moat girded the ancient fortress on three sides.

origin.ko: 고대영어 gyrdan '허리띠를 두르다'에서 왔습니다. 띠를 졸라매고 일할 채비를 하는 모습입니다.

senses.en: An excess, too much.

examples.text: A glut of cheap imports drove local steel producers out of business.

senses.en: supply with an excess of

examples.text: Foreign producers glutted the market with cheap grain, causing prices to collapse.

origin.ko: 라틴어 gluttīre '삼키다'에서 고대 프랑스어 gloter를 거쳐 왔습니다. 게걸스레 삼킨 듯 넘쳐나는 상태가 '과잉'입니다.

senses.en: complain

examples.text: Commuters gripe constantly about the delays, yet few have switched to other routes.

senses.en: A complaint, often a petty or trivial one.

examples.text: My only gripe about the new apartment is the thin walls between units.

origin.ko: 고대영어 grīpan '움켜쥐다'에서 왔습니다. grip과 같은 계통입니다.

senses.en: The excessive admiration of somebody or something.

examples.text: The public's idolatry of the young tycoon blinded many to the warning signs in his company's accounts.

senses.en: the worship of idols; the worship of physical objects or images as gods

examples.text: The reformers condemned the veneration of statues as idolatry.

origin.ko: 그리스어 eidōlolatríā '우상 숭배'에서 왔습니다. eídōlon(우상)과 látris(숭배자)가 합쳐졌습니다.

senses.en: To show to be connected or involved in an unfavorable or criminal way.

examples.text: The evidence implicates involvement of top management in the scheme.

senses.en: To imply, to have as a necessary consequence or accompaniment.

examples.text: Any serious tax reform will implicate difficult trade-offs between growth and fairness.

origin.ko: 라틴어 implicō '얽어 넣다'에서 왔습니다. 안으로(in) 접어 넣어(plic) 얽히게 한다는 이미지입니다.

senses.en: the quality of disagreeing; being unsuitable and inappropriate

examples.text: The incongruity of a marble fountain in the middle of the desert amused every passing tourist.

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 incongruitās에서 왔습니다. 서로 함께 맞아떨어지지 않는 상태입니다.

senses.en: unbearably arrogant or conceited

examples.text: After winning the award he became insufferable, boasting about it to anyone who would listen.

senses.en: too extreme to bear

examples.text: The insufferable heat of the crowded train car left passengers gasping and desperate for the next station.

origin.ko: in-(아닌)과 sufferable(견딜 수 있는)이 합쳐진 말입니다. 참고 견딜 수 없을 정도라는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: capable of being apprehended or understood

examples.text: Italian and Spanish are partially mutually intelligible languages.

origin.ko: 라틴어 intelligibilis에서 왔습니다. 사이에서 골라 읽어 낼 수 있어 '이해할 수 있는'입니다.

senses.en: an indirect suggestion

examples.text: The minister gave no intimation that a resignation was being considered until the announcement itself.

origin.ko: 라틴어 intimatio에서 왔고 intimate(안으로 넣다)와 이어집니다. 속뜻을 슬쩍 알려 주는 '암시'입니다.

senses.en: Accustomed to something, especially something unpleasant.

examples.text: By now she is inured to their inanities.

origin.ko: inure에 -ed가 붙은 말입니다. 단련되어 몸에 밴 상태입니다.

senses.en: showing lack of due respect or veneration

examples.text: The comedian's irreverent take on national politics delighted students and infuriated officials.

origin.ko: 라틴어 irreverēns에서 왔고 ir-와 reverent(경건한)가 합쳐졌습니다. 공경심이 없다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: Unable to be retracted or reversed; final.
senses.ko: 취소할 수 없는, 돌이킬 수 없는

examples.text: Once the trust is signed, the transfer of assets is irrevocable.

origin.ko: 라틴어 irrevocabilis에서 왔습니다. 뒤로 불러 되돌릴 수 없다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: try to gain favor by cringing or flattering

examples.text: He is always kowtowing to his boss

origin.ko: 중국어 叩頭(kòutóu)에서 왔습니다. 글자 그대로 '머리를 두드리다', 곧 머리를 땅에 조아리는 절입니다.

senses.en: characterized by effort to the point of exhaustion; especially physical effort

examples.text: Compiling the dictionary by hand was a laborious process that took the editors nearly two decades.

senses.en: Mentally difficult; painstaking.

examples.text: The laborious analysis of thousands of archival records finally yielded a clear pattern.

origin.ko: 라틴어 laboriosus에서 왔고 labor(노동)에서 나왔습니다. 수고가 많이 드는 일이라는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: An ambiguous feeling of mental or moral depression.

examples.text: A deep malaise settled over the company after the third round of layoffs.

senses.en: A feeling of general bodily discomfort, fatigue or unpleasantness, often at the onset of illness.

examples.text: She felt a vague malaise all morning before the fever finally set in.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 malaise에서 왔고 mal-(나쁜)과 aise(편안함)가 합쳐졌습니다. 편치 않은 기분입니다.

senses.en: A smaller system which is seen as representative of a larger one.

examples.text: With a few actors at his disposition he created a microcosm of life.

origin.ko: 그리스어 mikrós(작은)와 kósmos(우주)가 합쳐졌습니다. 작은 우주라는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: entangled or hindered as if e.g. in mire

examples.text: The negotiations remained mired in procedural disputes for months.

origin.ko: mire(진창)에 -ed가 붙은 말입니다. 진창에 빠져 꼼짝 못 하는 상태입니다.

senses.en: hating mankind in general

examples.text: His misanthropic outlook grew darker with every betrayal he suffered.

origin.ko: misanthrope(인간 혐오자)에서 나온 형용사입니다. 그리스어 miséō(미워하다)와 ánthrōpos(사람)에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: undistorted by emotion or personal bias; based on observable phenomena

examples.text: an objective appraisal

senses.en: the goal intended to be attained (and which is believed to be attainable)

examples.text: The study's primary objective is to measure how sleep affects memory in teenagers.

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 obiectīvus에서 왔고, '앞에 던져진 대상'이 바탕입니다. 내 감정과 별개로 눈앞에 놓인 사실에 근거한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: Someone who attempts to impede the progress of legislation.

examples.text: Party leaders branded the dissenting senators obstructionists for blocking every proposed budget.

senses.en: Someone who systematically obstructs the actions of others.

examples.text: The mayor accused the council of acting as obstructionists to any reform of city services.

origin.ko: obstruct(앞을 막아 세우다)에 -ist가 붙은 말로, 의사 진행을 가로막는 사람을 가리킵니다.

senses.en: To get hold of; to gain possession of, to procure; to acquire, in any way.

examples.text: obtain permission

senses.en: To exist or be the case; to hold true, be in force.

examples.text: The rules that obtained during the war no longer apply, and the old arrangements have lapsed.

origin.ko: 라틴어 obtinēre '손에 넣다'에서 왔고, tenēre는 '잡다'입니다.

senses.en: Being everywhere simultaneously.

examples.text: Smartphones have become omnipresent, shaping how people work, travel, and even sleep.

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 omnipraesēns에서 왔습니다. 모든 곳에 존재한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: loud and confused and empty talk

examples.text: The senator's speech was mostly palaver, offering no concrete plan for reform.

senses.en: influence or urge by gentle urging, caressing, or flattering

examples.text: He palavered her into going along

senses.en: Mentally draining activity, either physical or fuss.

examples.text: What a palaver!

origin.ko: 포르투갈어 palavra '말'에서 왔고, 라틴어 parabola '비유'가 원형입니다. 선원 은어로 쓰이다가 쓸데없는 수다를 뜻하게 되었습니다.

senses.en: of or relating to a typical example

examples.text: Her career is paradigmatic of the struggles facing first-generation immigrants.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 paradigmatique에서 왔고, 그리스어 '본보기'가 원형입니다.

senses.en: To reduce, diminish or trim gradually something as if by cutting off.

examples.text: Albert had to pare his options down by disregarding anything beyond his meager budget.

senses.en: remove the skin from

examples.text: Victor pared some apples in preparation to make a tart.

origin.ko: 옛 프랑스어 parer '다듬다'에서 왔고, 라틴어 parō '준비하다'가 원형입니다. 겉을 깎아 다듬는 데서 점차 줄이다가 되었습니다.

senses.en: (used of behavior or attitude) characteristic of those who treat others with condescension

examples.text: Her patronizing tone made the junior engineers feel their ideas were worthless.

senses.en: sell or offer for sale from place to place

examples.text: Street vendors peddle cheap souvenirs to tourists near the cathedral.

senses.en: To spread or cause to spread.

examples.text: Christine walked a dangerous line, peddling gossip about her detested son-in-law.

origin.ko: pedlar(행상인)에서 거꾸로 만든 말로, burglar에서 burgle이 나온 것과 같은 방식입니다.

senses.en: spread or diffuse through

examples.text: Cruel wars pervade history.

origin.ko: 라틴어 pervādō '구석구석 지나가다'에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: To loot or plunder by force, especially in time of war.

examples.text: Invading armies pillaged the countryside and left the villages in ruins.

senses.en: the act of stealing valuable things from a place

examples.text: The pillage of the abbey left its treasury empty and its library in ashes.

origin.ko: 옛 프랑스어 piller '약탈하다'에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: a political system governed by the wealthy people

examples.text: Critics warned that unlimited campaign donations were turning the republic into a plutocracy.

origin.ko: 그리스어 ploutokratía, 즉 '부(ploûtos)로 다스림'에서 왔습니다. 부자들이 지배하는 정치 체제입니다.

senses.en: A person with extraordinarily broad and comprehensive knowledge.

examples.text: A bit of a polymath, he was crucial in the early development of the railways in this country.

origin.ko: 그리스어 polymathēs('많이 배운')에서 왔습니다. 많이 배운 사람이 곧 박학다식한 사람입니다.

senses.en: made susceptible

examples.text: Some people are genetically predisposed to heart disease regardless of their diet.

origin.ko: pre-('미리')에 dispose('배치하다')의 과거분사가 붙은 말입니다. 미리 어느 쪽으로 기울어 놓였다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: designed or having the power to deter or prevent an anticipated situation or occurrence

examples.text: The government launched a preemptive campaign to calm investors before the announcement.

origin.ko: preempt에 -ive가 붙은 말입니다. 먼저 선수를 쳐서 막는다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: To spend time making oneself attractive and admiring one's appearance, e.g. in front of a mirror.

examples.text: The actor preened in front of the mirror before stepping onto the red carpet.

senses.en: pride or congratulate (oneself) for an achievement

examples.text: The minister preened over the modest gains as though they were a historic triumph.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 prēon('핀')에서 온 말로, 새가 부리로 깃털을 다듬는 모습과 prune의 영향을 받았습니다. 몸치장하는 뜻이 되었습니다.

senses.en: Based on presumption or conjecture; inferred, likely, presumed.

examples.text: By late May, he was already considered his party’s presumptive nominee.

senses.en: affording reasonable grounds for belief or acceptance

examples.text: presumptive evidence

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 praesumptivus에서 왔습니다. 먼저 그렇다고 취해 놓은 '추정상의'라는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: Deep intellect or insight.

examples.text: Unfortunately, Andrew's colossal ego means people miss his profundity.

origin.ko: 라틴어 profunditās('깊음')에서 왔습니다. 바닥까지 닿는 깊이가 지적 깊이가 되었습니다.

senses.en: An ancestral form of a species.

examples.text: The wolf is widely regarded as the progenitor of all domestic dog breeds.

senses.en: A predecessor of something, especially if also a precursor or model.

examples.text: ARPANET was the progenitor of the Internet.

origin.ko: 라틴어 prōgenitor('앞서 낳은 사람')에서 왔습니다. 후손보다 앞선 조상을 뜻합니다.

senses.en: Exceedingly variable; readily assuming different shapes or forms.

examples.text: The actor's protean talent allowed him to play a villain, a saint, and a clown in one season.

origin.ko: 그리스 신화의 바다 신 프로테우스(Proteus)에서 왔습니다. 모습을 마음대로 바꿨다는 데서 '변화무쌍한'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: characterized by lust

examples.text: The tabloid fed a prurient public appetite for details of the scandal.

senses.en: Curious, especially inappropriately so.

examples.text: Neighbors showed a prurient interest in the details of the couple's divorce.

origin.ko: 라틴어 prūriēns('가려워하는')에서 왔습니다. 근질거리는 욕망에서 '음탕한'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: A defensive structure; a protective barrier; a bulwark.

examples.text: A free press is often described as the last rampart against abuse of government power.

senses.en: an embankment built around a space for defensive purposes

examples.text: they stormed the ramparts of the city

origin.ko: 프랑스어 rempart에서 왔고 remparer('방어하다')에서 나왔습니다. 성을 다시 단단히 준비해 지키는 방벽입니다.

senses.en: unpleasantly loud and harsh

examples.text: A raucous cry from the crows echoed across the empty field at dawn.

senses.en: disturbing the public peace; loud and rough

examples.text: a raucous party

origin.ko: 라틴어 raucus('목쉰, 거친')에서 왔습니다. 쉰 목소리처럼 시끄럽고 거칠다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: extremely hungry

examples.text: After hiking all day, the ravenous campers devoured every scrap of dinner.

senses.en: Greedy, characterized by strong desires.

examples.text: The ravenous appetite of the young firm for new markets worried its cautious investors.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 ravineus에서 왔으며 ravin('약탈')에 -ous가 붙은 말입니다. 먹이를 낚아채는 맹수처럼 몹시 굶주린 상태입니다.

senses.en: the act of adjusting again (to changed circumstances)

examples.text: Returning veterans faced a difficult readjustment to civilian life after years of service overseas.

senses.en: a summary at the end that repeats the substance of a longer discussion

examples.text: The final chapter offers a brief recapitulation of the book's central claims for hurried readers.

senses.en: (music) the section of a composition or movement (especially in sonata form) in which musical themes that were introduced earlier are repeated

examples.text: In the recapitulation, the opening theme returns in the home key after a stormy development section.

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 recapitulatio('요약')에서 왔습니다. 요점을 다시 짚어 되풀이하는 일입니다.

senses.en: mutual accusations

examples.text: The peace talks collapsed amid bitter recriminations over who had broken the ceasefire.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 récrimination에서 왔습니다. 비난을 되받아 되돌려 서로 맞고발하는 일입니다.

senses.en: good at remembering

examples.text: a retentive mind

senses.en: having the power, capacity, or quality of retaining water

examples.text: soils retentive of moisture

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 retentivus에서 왔고 라틴어 retentus('붙들린')와 이어집니다. 머릿속에 꽉 붙들어 두는 기억력입니다.

senses.en: laugh at with contempt and derision

examples.text: Skeptics scoffed at the inventor's claims until the prototype flew across the field.

senses.en: treat with contemptuous disregard

examples.text: The reckless driver scoffed at every warning sign along the mountain road.

origin.ko: 북유럽어에서 온 것으로 보이는 중세 영어 scof(조롱)에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: to look at critically or searchingly, or in minute detail

examples.text: Investigators scrutinized every page of the contract for signs of hidden clauses.

origin.ko: 라틴어 scrūtārī(샅샅이 뒤지다)에서 나온 scrutiny에 -ize가 붙었습니다. 낱낱이 살핀다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: be in an agitated emotional state

examples.text: The customer was seething with anger

senses.en: boil vigorously

examples.text: Below the bridge the river seethed over the rocks after a week of heavy rain.

senses.en: be noisy with activity

examples.text: The marketplace seethed with merchants, shoppers, and pickpockets from dawn until dusk.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 sēoþan(끓이다)에서 왔습니다. 냄비가 끓듯 속이 부글부글 끓는다는 이미지입니다.

senses.en: Having an untidy appearance; unkempt.

examples.text: Which would you sooner employ, a boy who was plainly, yet neatly clad, or one who had a slovenly appearance, though dressed in fine clothes?

senses.en: Careless or negligent; sloppy.

examples.text: The editor rejected the manuscript for its slovenly prose and its many factual errors.

senses.en: be the leader of

examples.text: She spearheaded the effort to find a cure for the disease

senses.en: someone who leads or initiates an activity (attack or campaign etc.)

examples.text: The young economist became the intellectual spearhead of the reform movement.

origin.ko: 중세 영어 spere-hed(창의 끝)에서 왔습니다. 창끝처럼 맨 앞에서 이끈다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: to accuse or condemn or openly or formally or brand as disgraceful

examples.text: She was stigmatized by society because she had a child out of wedlock

origin.ko: 그리스어 stigma(낙인)에 동사 접미사 -ize가 붙었습니다. 낙인을 찍는다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: so great in size or force or extent as to elicit awe

examples.text: One cannot appreciate how stupendous the Matterhorn is without seeing it.

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 stupendus(어리둥절하게 하는)에서 왔고 stupeo(멍해지다)와 이어집니다. 어안이 벙벙할 만큼 엄청나다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: inferior in rank or status

examples.text: Historians increasingly study the subaltern voices excluded from official colonial records.

senses.en: A subordinate.

examples.text: As a subaltern of 24, Neave was captured in the defence of Calais in May 1940.

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 subalternus에서 왔습니다. 다른 사람 '아래의' 하급자라는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: abjectly submissive; characteristic of a slave or servant

examples.text: The subservient aides never dared to contradict the dictator, whatever his mistakes.

senses.en: serving or acting as a means or aid

examples.text: Local institutions played a subservient role, existing mainly to carry out the ministry's directives.

origin.ko: 라틴어 subservire(아래에서 섬기다)에서 왔습니다. 굽실거리며 섬기는 모습입니다.

senses.en: get on top of; deal with successfully

examples.text: She had to surmount enormous obstacles to become the first in her family to attend college.

senses.en: be on top of

examples.text: A bronze statue of an eagle surmounted the stone gateway of the old courthouse.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 surmonter(위로 오르다)에서 왔습니다. 장애물 위로 올라서서 이겨낸다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: The state of being under the control of another person.

examples.text: Today's kids are in thrall to their phones.

senses.en: someone held in bondage

examples.text: In the old saga, the farmer's thrall tended the sheep and was never allowed to leave the estate.

origin.ko: 고대 노르드어 þræll('노예')에서 왔고 원래 '달리는 심부름꾼'을 뜻하는 말에서 나왔습니다. 노예 상태가 '속박'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: a large gathering of people

examples.text: A throng of commuters pushed through the station gates as the evening trains arrived.

senses.en: To crowd into a place, especially to fill it.

examples.text: Thousands thronged the plaza to hear the president's first address after the election.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 þrang('군중, 밀집')에서 왔습니다. 서로 밀어붙이며 모인 사람들이 '인파'입니다.

senses.en: change or alter in form, appearance, or nature

examples.text: The alchemists tried to transmute base metals to gold.

origin.ko: 라틴어 trānsmūtāre('건너서 바꾸다')에서 왔습니다. 한 상태에서 다른 상태로 바꾸는 것이 '변형시키다'입니다.

senses.en: make shorter as if by cutting off

examples.text: The script was truncated to leave time for commercials.

origin.ko: 라틴어 truncō('줄기만 남기고 자르다')에서 왔습니다. 가지를 쳐 짧게 만드는 모습입니다.

senses.en: Instruction; teaching; guidance; being a tutor.

examples.text: Under the tutelage of an exacting mentor, the young chemist mastered laboratory technique within two years.

senses.en: The act of guarding, protecting, or guiding.

examples.text: The orphaned prince remained under the tutelage of his uncle until he reached adulthood.

origin.ko: 라틴어 tūtēla('보호, 후견')에서 왔고 tuērī('지켜보다')와 이어집니다. 지켜보며 이끄는 일이 '지도'입니다.

senses.en: Modest and having no pretensions or ostentation.

examples.text: The unassuming scientist rarely mentioned that she had won the field's most prestigious prize.

senses.en: the human face (‘kisser’ and ‘smiler’ and ‘mug’ are informal terms for ‘face’ and ‘phiz’ is British)

examples.text: The old soldier's stern visage softened when his granddaughter ran into the room.

origin.ko: 라틴어 vidēre('보다')에서 나온 vīsus('모습')에서 왔습니다. 눈에 보이는 모습이 '얼굴'입니다.

senses.en: Having a great appetite for anything; eager.

examples.text: a voracious reader

senses.en: devouring or craving food in great quantities

examples.text: After days in the mountains, the voracious hikers emptied every dish on the table.

origin.ko: 라틴어 vorāx('게걸스러운')에 -acious를 붙였습니다. 먹을 것에 달려드는 식탐이 '탐욕스러운'입니다.

senses.en: cover up a misdemeanor, fault, or error

examples.text: Critics said the official inquiry was an attempt to whitewash the agency's role in the disaster.

senses.en: a specious or deceptive clearing that attempts to gloss over failings and defects

examples.text: The investigation proved to be a whitewash that cleared every executive without questioning a single witness.

origin.ko: white와 wash의 합성어입니다. 흰 칠로 더러운 곳을 덮는 모습이 '잘못을 덮어 감추다'입니다.

senses.en: To reduce or gradually eliminate something (such as a debt).

examples.text: Months of steady payments slowly whittled the debt down to a manageable sum.

senses.en: cut small bits or pare shavings from

examples.text: whittle a piece of wood

origin.ko: 중세 영어 thwiten('깎다')에서 나온 '큰 칼'이라는 명사에서 왔습니다. 칼로 조금씩 깎아 내는 것이 '점차 줄이다'입니다.

senses.en: the spirit of the time; the spirit characteristic of an age or generation

examples.text: The film captured the zeitgeist of the late sixties, when protest and idealism filled the streets.

origin.ko: 독일어 Zeitgeist('시대의 정신')를 그대로 빌려 왔습니다.

senses.en: give an incentive for action

examples.text: Investigators wanted to know what motive had actuated the clerk to destroy the records.

senses.en: put in motion or move to act

examples.text: Pressing the lever actuates a valve that releases steam into the turbine.

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 actuare에서 왔으며 라틴어 agere(행하다)에서 나왔습니다. 행동하게 만든다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: An old saying which has obtained credit by long use.

examples.text: The old adage that haste makes waste proved true when the rushed project collapsed.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 adage를 거쳐 라틴어에서 온 말로, 오래 전해 내려온 격언을 뜻합니다.

senses.en: a deliberately offensive act or something producing the effect of deliberate disrespect

examples.text: The delegation regarded the late invitation as an affront to their country's dignity.

senses.en: treat, mention, or speak to rudely

examples.text: The remark so affronted the committee that several members left the room.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 afronter(이마를 치다)에서 왔습니다. 얼굴을 정면으로 때리는 듯한 무례가 '모욕'입니다.

senses.en: the quality of unselfish concern for the welfare of others

examples.text: The donor's altruism was evident when she gave away most of her fortune and asked for no recognition.

origin.ko: 1830년 콩트가 프랑스어 autrui(타인)와 -isme로 만든 말이고 라틴어 alter(다른)에서 나왔습니다. 남을 위하는 마음입니다.

senses.en: showing unselfish concern for the welfare of others

examples.text: Biologists debate whether truly altruistic behavior exists in animals or merely serves hidden self-interest.

origin.ko: altruist에 -ic이 붙은 말로, 라틴어 alter(다른 사람)에서 나왔습니다.

senses.en: a combination or blend of diverse things

examples.text: The city's cuisine is an amalgam of Portuguese, African, and Indian traditions.

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 amalgama(수은 합금)에서 왔고 그리스어 '부드럽게 하다'와 연결됩니다. 여러 물질이 섞인 혼합물이 되었습니다.

senses.en: wildly; without self-control

examples.text: Without strict supervision, the project ran amuck, with costs doubling and deadlines ignored.

origin.ko: 말레이어 amok(광란하며 덤벼드는)에서 왔다고 알려져 있습니다.

senses.en: marked by skill in achieving a desired end especially with cunning or craft

examples.text: an artful choice of metaphors

senses.en: not straightforward or candid; giving a false appearance of frankness

examples.text: His artful display of humility fooled no one who knew his ambitions.

origin.ko: art(기술)에 -ful(가득한)이 붙은 말입니다. 재주가 가득해 교묘하다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: characteristic of an absolute ruler or absolute rule; having absolute sovereignty

examples.text: In recent years, the prime minister has become increasingly autocratic.

senses.en: offensively self-assured or given to exercising usually unwarranted power

examples.text: Despite his lack of actual authority, his autocratic demeanour annoyed many of his colleagues.

origin.ko: autocrat(독재자)에 -ic이 붙은 말입니다. 그리스어 '스스로 통치하는'에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: be appropriate or necessary

examples.text: It behooves us to reflect on this matter

origin.ko: 고대 영어 behofian(필요하다)에서 왔습니다. 필요하니 마땅히 해야 한다는 뜻이 되었습니다.

senses.en: To disparage, depreciate, or minimize the importance, value, merit, or significance of someone or something.

examples.text: Critics belittled the young architect's design until the finished building won an international prize.

origin.ko: be-와 little을 합쳐 1782년 제퍼슨이 만든 말입니다. 남을 작게 만든다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: pledged to be married

examples.text: The betrothed couple announced that their wedding would take place in the spring.

senses.en: One who is betrothed, i.e. a fiancé or fiancée.

examples.text: She introduced him as her betrothed.

origin.ko: 중세 영어 betroth(약혼시키다)에 과거분사형 -ed가 붙은 형태입니다.

senses.en: Having tunnel vision, being unable to see what is happening around one: uncircumspect, narrow-minded, or both.

examples.text: The minister's blinkered view of the crisis ignored the warnings of his own advisers.

senses.en: noisy and lacking in restraint or discipline

examples.text: A boisterous crowd of fans filled the street outside the stadium long after the final whistle.

senses.en: violently agitated and turbulent

examples.text: Boisterous winds tore at the sails and forced the fishing fleet back to harbor.

origin.ko: 중세 영어 boistous('거칠고 투박한')가 바뀐 말입니다. 기원은 불확실하며 거칠고 소란스럽다는 뜻으로 이어졌습니다.

senses.en: a speech of violent denunciation

examples.text: The columnist launched a broadside against the council, accusing it of waste and incompetence.

origin.ko: broad(넓은)와 side(옆)가 합쳐진 말입니다.

senses.en: Knowing, shrewd, astute.

examples.text: The canny lawyer knew just how to get what he wanted.

senses.en: Careful, prudent, cautious.

examples.text: A canny investor, she kept most of her savings in cash until the market settled.

origin.ko: 북부 영어 방언에서 온 말로, can('알다')에 -y가 붙었습니다. 아는 게 많아 약삭빠르다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: An impulsive, seemingly unmotivated action, change of mind, or notion.

examples.text: On a sudden caprice, the heiress canceled her wedding and sailed for Europe.

origin.ko: 이탈리아어 capriccio에서 왔고, caporiccio('소름, 갑작스러운 놀람')에서 갈라졌습니다. 갑작스런 충동이 '변덕'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: Absolute; having no exception.

examples.text: The spokesman gave a categorical denial, insisting that no such meeting had ever taken place.

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 catēgoricus에서 왔고 category에 -ical이 붙은 말입니다. 범주에 딱 잘라 넣는 단정적인 태도입니다.

senses.en: a grotesque product of the imagination

examples.text: Although now considered a pseudo-science, the 'Abbasids were also fascinated by alchemy and the chimera of transforming base metals into gold for their treasury.

senses.en: Anything composed of very disparate parts.

examples.text: He built his car one piece at a time, producing a chimera with the head of a Volkswagen, the body of a Geely, and the tail of an aftermarket Porsche.

origin.ko: 그리스어 Khimaira('불을 뿜는 괴물', 원래는 암염소)에서 왔습니다. 사자, 염소, 뱀이 섞인 괴물이 '기괴한 환상'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: laugh quietly or with restraint

examples.text: The old fellow chortled as he recalled his youthful adventures.

senses.en: a soft partly suppressed laugh

examples.text: He frequently interrupted himself with chortles while he told us his favorite joke.

origin.ko: 루이스 캐럴이 'Jabberwocky'에서 chuckle(킬킬)과 snort(코웃음)를 섞어 만든 말입니다.

senses.en: loud and clear

examples.text: a clarion call

senses.en: a medieval brass instrument with a clear shrill tone

examples.text: At dawn a clarion sounded from the castle wall to summon the garrison.

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 clāriō('나팔')에서 왔고, 라틴어 clārus(또렷한, 큰 소리의)에서 갈라졌습니다. 맑고 날카로운 나팔 소리입니다.

senses.en: come or be in close contact with; stick or hold together and resist separation

examples.text: Despite mounting evidence, the committee continued to cleave to its original theory.

senses.en: separate or cut with a tool, such as a sharp instrument

examples.text: With one blow the woodsman cleaved the log in two.

origin.ko: 뜻이 반대인 '쪼개다'와 '들러붙다'는 서로 다른 고대 영어 동사에서 왔습니다. 이 뜻은 '들러붙다'(clifian, clīfan) 쪽입니다.

senses.en: a state or atmosphere of harmony or mutual civility and respect

examples.text: Despite sharp disagreements, the two parties preserved a measure of comity in the chamber.

origin.ko: 라틴어 cōmitās(공손함, 호의)에서 왔고 후기 중세 영어 comite로 들어왔습니다.

senses.en: To be in agreement (with); to be of an accord.

examples.text: The new rules did not seem to comport with the spirit of the club.

senses.en: To behave (in a given manner).

examples.text: She comported herself with grace.

origin.ko: 라틴어 comportare('함께 가져오다')에서 왔습니다. 함께 가져와 맞춘다는 뜻에서 '부합하다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: an idea that is implied or suggested

examples.text: The word cheap carries a negative connotation that thrifty does not.

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 connotātiō에서 왔고, con-(함께)과 notō(표시하다)가 합쳐졌습니다. 본뜻 옆에 덧붙여 표시된 의미입니다.

senses.en: deserving blame or censure as being wrong or evil or injurious

examples.text: The board was culpable for ignoring repeated warnings about the faulty safety valves.

origin.ko: 라틴어 culpābilis(비난받을 만한)에서 왔고, culpa(잘못, 죄)가 뿌리입니다.

senses.en: Stylishly dressed, neatly dressed, spiffy.

examples.text: The dapper gentleman in the pinstriped suit tipped his hat to every passerby.

origin.ko: 중세 네덜란드어 dapper(씩씩한, 재빠른)에서 왔습니다. '기운찬'이 '말쑥한' 쪽으로 바뀌었습니다.

senses.en: the state of being degenerate in mental or moral qualities

examples.text: Historians often cite the decadence of the late empire as a cause of its eventual fall.

senses.en: With a positive connotation: the quality of being luxuriously enjoyable or self-indulgent, especially of food; luxuriousness, richness.

examples.text: the decadence of a five-star hotel

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 decadentia에서 왔고 '아래로 떨어짐'이 어원입니다. 쇠퇴하는 상태가 '퇴폐'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: Bearing; manner of presenting oneself.

examples.text: Her deportment impressed her interviewers.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 déportement에서 왔고 deport(처신하다)에 -ment가 붙은 말입니다.

senses.en: moral perversion; impairment of virtue and moral principles

examples.text: The trial exposed the depravity of a regime that tortured its own citizens.

senses.en: expecting unquestioning obedience

examples.text: The manager's dictatorial style left no room for questions or dissent among his staff.

senses.en: characteristic of an absolute ruler or absolute rule; having absolute sovereignty

examples.text: The dictatorial ruler silenced the press and jailed every opponent who questioned his decrees.

senses.en: sad beyond comforting; incapable of being consoled
senses.ko: 위로할 수 없을 만큼 슬픈, 실의에 빠진

examples.text: For weeks after the death of her cat she was disconsolate.

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 discōnsōlātus(위로받지 못한)에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: lacking orderly continuity

examples.text: The witness gave a disjointed account that jumped between events without clear order.

senses.en: an exemption from some rule or obligation

examples.text: The school granted her a special dispensation to submit the thesis after the usual deadline.

senses.en: the act of dispensing (giving out in portions)

examples.text: a fair dispensation of money

origin.ko: 라틴어 dispēnsātiō에서 왔습니다. 저울에 달아 나누어 주는 데서 '면제, 특별 허가'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: spend frivolously and unwisely

examples.text: The heir dissipated his inheritance on gambling and lavish parties within a few short years.

senses.en: move away from each other

examples.text: By noon the morning fog had dissipated and the valley was bright with sunlight.

origin.ko: 라틴어 dissipō(흩어버리다)에서 왔습니다. 흩뿌려 없애는 데서 '탕진하다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: take away possessions from someone

examples.text: He was divested of his rights and his title

senses.en: reduce or dispose of; cease to hold (an investment)

examples.text: Glasgow will become the first university in Europe to divest from fossil fuels.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 desvestir(옷을 벗기다)에서 왔습니다. 옷을 벗기듯 소유물을 빼앗는다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: to take off from the body or head

examples.text: He doffed his hat

senses.en: To cast aside or get rid of (something), to throw off.

examples.text: Doff that stupid idea: it will never work.

origin.ko: do off가 줄어든 말입니다. '벗다'라는 뜻이며, don(do on)의 반대입니다.

senses.en: Very severe, cruel, or harsh.

examples.text: The mayor announced draconian budget cuts today.

origin.ko: 기원전 7세기 아테네의 입법자 드라콘(Draco)에서 왔습니다. 그가 만든 법이 지나치게 가혹해 '가혹한'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: pleasing to the ear

examples.text: the dulcet tones of the cello

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 doucet에서 왔고 라틴어 dulcis(달콤한)에 축소 접미사가 붙었습니다.

senses.en: A building; a structure; an architectural fabric, especially a large and spectacular one.

examples.text: The marble edifice dominated the skyline of the old financial district.

senses.en: An abstract structure, such as a school of thought, an argument, a theoretical position, etc.

examples.text: The new evidence threatened to topple the entire edifice of the economist's theory.

origin.ko: 라틴어 aedificium(건물)에서 왔습니다. 집을 짓는다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: Vivacity.

examples.text: The host's effervescence kept the dinner party lively until well past midnight.

senses.en: The escape of gas from solution in a liquid, especially the escape of carbon dioxide from a carbonated drink.

examples.text: The effervescence of the tablet in water released a stream of tiny bubbles.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 effervescence에서 왔습니다. 거품이 보글보글 일어나는 모습이 '활기'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: deprived of vigor and the ability to be effective

examples.text: Critics dismissed the aging regime as an effete institution unable to meet any real challenge.

senses.en: affected, overrefined, and effeminate

examples.text: He mocked the critics as effete snobs who had never worked a day outdoors.

origin.ko: 라틴어 effētus '새끼를 다 낳아 지친'에서 왔습니다. 기력이 소진된 상태가 '무기력한'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: having a softening or soothing effect especially to the skin

examples.text: The emollient cream relieved the dryness of her hands in winter.

senses.en: Soothing or mollifying.

examples.text: The minister adopted an emollient tone to calm the angry delegates.

origin.ko: 라틴어 ēmolliēns(부드럽게 하는)에서 왔습니다. mollis는 '부드러운'이라는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: showing empathy or ready comprehension of others' states

examples.text: a sensitive and empathetic school counselor

origin.ko: empathic에서 sympathetic과 소리를 맞추려고 바꾼 말입니다. 남의 감정 속으로 들어가 느낀다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: attract; cause to be enamored

examples.text: The young poet was soon enamored of the city's cafes and crowded bookshops.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 enamorer에서 왔습니다. 사랑(amor) 속에 빠뜨려 반하게 한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: An intrusion upon another's possessions or rights; infringement.

examples.text: Residents protested the steady encroachment of commercial development on the wetlands.

senses.en: To occur afterwards, as a result or effect.

examples.text: Give three freshmen six bottles of wine, and hilarity will ensue.

origin.ko: 라틴어 īnsequī(바싹 뒤따르다)에서 고대 프랑스어를 거쳐 왔습니다. 어떤 일의 뒤를 바로 따라 일어난다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: pertaining to or causing improvement in the offspring produced

examples.text: Early twentieth-century eugenic policies sought to control who was permitted to have children.

origin.ko: 그리스어 eu(좋은)와 -genēs(태생의)가 합쳐졌습니다. 좋은 태생, 곧 우량한 자손을 뜻합니다.

senses.en: exaggerated feeling of well-being or elation

examples.text: Fans were euphoric after their team won the championship for the first time in decades.

origin.ko: 그리스어 eúphoros(잘 견디는)에서 왔습니다. euphoria의 형용사형으로 '행복감에 찬'이라는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: greatly annoyed; out of patience

examples.text: Exasperated by the third cancelled flight, she demanded to speak with the airline's manager.

senses.en: use of physical or mental energy; hard work

examples.text: The climb required such exertion that several members of the group had to turn back.

senses.en: a person who is voluntarily absent from home or country

examples.text: Many expatriates in the city gather weekly to share news and meals from home.

senses.en: expel from a country

examples.text: The regime expatriated several prominent writers who had criticized the government in print.

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 expatriāre(조국 밖으로 내보내다)에서 왔습니다. 조국(patria)을 떠나 사는 사람입니다.

senses.en: In the nature of exploitation; acting to exploit someone or something

examples.text: We are protesting the company's exploitative policies.

senses.en: concoct something artificial or untrue

examples.text: The witness admitted that he had fabricated the entire story to protect his brother.

senses.en: put together out of artificial or natural components or parts

examples.text: the company fabricates plastic chairs

origin.ko: 라틴어 fabricāre(만들다)에서 왔고 fabrica는 '공방'입니다. 없는 것을 만들어 내는 데서 '날조하다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: a fleet of small craft

examples.text: Toward the horizon a flotilla of fishing-boats showed immutable, pink-lacquered by the evening sun.

origin.ko: 스페인어 flota(함대)의 지소형입니다. 작은 배들의 무리를 가리킵니다.

senses.en: thrown into a state of agitated confusion; (‘rattled’ is an informal term)

examples.text: The speaker became quite flustered when she dropped all her notes.

senses.en: to force onto another

examples.text: Senior partners often foist unpleasant tasks on the newest associates in the firm.

senses.en: insert surreptitiously or without warrant

examples.text: Lobbyists tried to foist a controversial clause into the bill at the last minute.

origin.ko: 옛 네덜란드어 vuisten(손에 쥐다)에서 왔다고 추정됩니다. 슬쩍 손에 쥐여 남에게 떠넘긴다는 이미지입니다.

senses.en: make strong or stronger
