examples.text: Regular exercise and a balanced diet fortify the body against seasonal illness.

senses.en: To support (one's or someone's opinion, statement, etc.) by producing evidence, etc.; to confirm, to corroborate.

examples.text: New archaeological findings fortified the historian's argument that the city had been settled earlier.

senses.en: enclose by or as if by a fortification

examples.text: The townspeople fortified the hilltop with stone walls and watchtowers against the coming invasion.

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 fortificāre(강하게 하다)에서 왔습니다. fortis(강한)를 더해 튼튼하게 만든다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: A person who upsets the status quo by posing novel or upsetting questions, or attempts to stimulate innovation by being an irritant.
senses.ko: 기존 질서에 도전하는 비판자, 귀찮게 구는 사람

examples.text: Socrates, the Athenian gadfly, tormented the city's leaders with relentless questions about justice.

senses.en: a persistently annoying person

examples.text: The reporter became a gadfly, pestering the mayor at every public appearance.

origin.ko: 소를 모는 뾰족한 막대(gad)처럼 소를 물어 괴롭히는 파리(fly)입니다. 가만있는 사람을 쿡쿡 찌르는 비판자가 되었습니다.

senses.en: very thin especially from disease or hunger or cold

examples.text: After months in the wilderness, the explorers returned gaunt and exhausted.

senses.en: Of a place or thing: bleak, desolate.

examples.text: The gaunt ruins of the abandoned factory loomed over the empty, windswept valley.

senses.en: divide unfairly and to one's advantage; of voting districts

examples.text: The ruling party was accused of gerrymandering districts to guarantee itself a legislative majority.

origin.ko: 1812년 매사추세츠 주지사 Gerry와 salamander(도롱뇽)의 합성어입니다. 새 선거구 모양이 도롱뇽 같다고 비꼰 데서 나왔습니다.

senses.en: To behave dramatically or showily to impress an audience or observers; to pander to a crowd.
senses.ko: 관중에게 잘 보이려고 과시하다, 인기를 끌려 하다

examples.text: Many politicians prefer to grandstand on hot-button issues rather than enact tough policy changes.

origin.ko: grand와 stand의 합성어입니다. 큰 관람석(grandstand)의 관중에게 잘 보이려 과시하는 이미지입니다.

senses.en: costing nothing

examples.text: The museum offers gratis admission to students on the first Sunday of every month.

senses.en: without charge

examples.text: I'll give you this gratis

origin.ko: 라틴어 grātīs '호의로'에서 왔습니다. 대가 없이 호의로 주는 것이라 '무료'입니다.

senses.en: something that precedes and indicates the approach of something or someone

examples.text: Early crocuses are often seen as the harbinger of spring after a long winter.

senses.en: foreshadow or presage

examples.text: The sudden drop in orders harbingered a much deeper slump in manufacturing.

origin.ko: 원래 숙소를 미리 마련하러 먼저 보내던 사람입니다. 앞서 와서 다음을 알리는 존재가 '전조, 선구자'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: Intoxicating or stupefying.

examples.text: The cocktail was a heady mixture of spirits.

senses.en: Exhilarating or exciting; producing a feeling of high energy or confidence

examples.text: The rock concert was a heady mixture of their greatest hits.

senses.en: marked by defiant disregard for danger or consequences

examples.text: The heady young trader gambled the firm's capital on a single volatile stock.

origin.ko: 중세영어 hedi로 head(머리)에 -y가 붙은 말입니다. 머리로 훅 올라오는 취기가 '도취시키는'입니다.

senses.en: characterized by departure from accepted beliefs or standards

examples.text: Her heretical claim that the old theory was flawed provoked outrage among senior colleagues.

origin.ko: heretic(이단자)에 -al이 붙은 말입니다. 그리스어 hairéō(고르다)에서 나왔습니다.

senses.en: A place of seclusion.

examples.text: The novelist treated her remote cabin as a hermitage where she could write without interruption.

senses.en: the abode of a hermit

examples.text: The pilgrims climbed the cliff to reach the hermitage carved into the rock.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 ermitage로, hermit(은둔자)에 -age가 붙은 말입니다. 그리스어 erēmítēs(외딴 곳에 사는 사람)가 뿌리입니다.

senses.en: in a heated manner

examples.text: the children were arguing hotly

origin.ko: 고대영어 hātlīce '열렬히'에서 왔습니다. hot(뜨거운)에 -ly가 붙은 말입니다.

senses.en: use cautiously and frugally

examples.text: Hikers must husband their water carefully during the long crossing of the desert.

origin.ko: 고대영어 hūsbonda로, hūs(집)와 bonda(주인)가 합쳐진 말입니다. 집을 건사하는 사람이라 살림을 아껴 쓰는 뜻이 나왔습니다.

senses.en: The prudent management or conservation of resources.

examples.text: Careful husbandry of the city's water supply carried residents through three years of drought.

senses.en: the practice of cultivating the land or raising stock

examples.text: Advances in animal husbandry dramatically increased milk yields during the nineteenth century.

origin.ko: 중세영어 husbondrye '살림 관리'에서 왔고 husband(집 주인)에서 나왔습니다. 집안 살림을 알뜰히 꾸리는 일이 '자원의 신중한 관리'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: peculiar to the individual

examples.text: The critic praised the film's idiosyncratic visual style, unlike anything else in current cinema.

origin.ko: idiosyncrasy(특이한 기질)에 -ic이 붙은 형용사입니다. 그리스어 idios(자기 자신의)가 핵심입니다.

senses.en: Engaging in excessive attachment or reverence; inordinately or profanely devoted.

examples.text: Fans gave the retired striker an almost idolatrous devotion, hanging his portrait in their homes.

senses.en: relating to or practicing idolatry

examples.text: The prophet denounced the idolatrous rites that had spread through the kingdom.

origin.ko: idolatry(우상 숭배)에서 나온 형용사입니다. 우상(idol)을 숭배한다(latr)는 뜻에서 맹목적으로 떠받드는 모습을 가리킵니다.

senses.en: not pertinent to the matter under consideration

examples.text: Objection, your Honour! The defendant’s criminal record is immaterial to this case.

senses.en: without material form or substance

examples.text: Some believe that because ghosts are immaterial, they can pass through walls.

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 immāteriālis '물질이 아닌'에서 왔습니다. 물질적 실체가 없으니 중요하지 않다는 뜻으로 이어졌습니다.

senses.en: having a quality that provokes disbelief

examples.text: gave the teacher an implausible excuse

origin.ko: plausible(그럴듯한)에 부정 접두사가 붙은 말입니다. plausible은 라틴어 plaudere(박수치다)에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: In like degree; in like manner; to the same or similar degree; likewise.

examples.text: The argument is persuasive inasmuch as it rests on evidence that independent researchers have repeatedly confirmed.

origin.ko: in, as, much가 하나로 합쳐진 말입니다. '그만큼의 정도로'라는 뜻에서 '~인 점에서'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: not precisely determined or established; not fixed or known in advance

examples.text: of indeterminate age

senses.en: of uncertain or ambiguous nature

examples.text: The painting's indeterminate shapes could be read as either clouds or waves, depending on the viewer.

origin.ko: determinate(경계가 정해진)에 부정 접두사가 붙은 말입니다. 경계(terminus)가 확정되지 않은 상태입니다.

senses.en: accuse formally of a crime

examples.text: his former manager was indicted for fraud

senses.en: To accuse of wrongdoing; charge.

examples.text: a book that indicts modern values

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 enditer '받아 적게 하다'에서 왔고 라틴어 dicere(말하다)가 뿌리입니다. 죄를 공식적으로 말해 선언하는 것이 '기소하다'입니다.

senses.en: easily ignited

examples.text: Workers were warned to keep inflammable solvents away from the heaters in the storage room.

senses.en: Easily excited; set off by the slightest excuse; easily enraged or inflamed.

examples.text: With tempers already inflammable after the long strike, a single insult was enough to spark a brawl.

origin.ko: 라틴어 īnflammāre '불을 붙이다'에서 왔습니다. 불꽃(flamma)이 붙을 수 있다는 뜻으로, in-은 부정이 아니라 '안으로'입니다.

senses.en: an artless innocent young girl (especially as portrayed on the stage)
senses.ko: 순진한 젊은 여자, 순진한 아가씨 역

examples.text: The director cast her as the wide-eyed ingenue who is gradually drawn into the city's corrupt politics.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 ingénu(순진한)의 여성형이고, 라틴어 ingenuus에서 왔습니다. 무대의 순진한 아가씨 역을 가리킵니다.

senses.en: a slight suggestion or vague understanding

examples.text: he had no inkling what was about to happen

origin.ko: 중세 영어에서 '암시, 귀띔'을 뜻하던 말에서 왔다고 하며, 정확한 경로는 불확실합니다.

senses.en: unaware of or indifferent to

examples.text: The CEO seemed insensible to the growing anger among employees over the sudden layoffs.

senses.en: barely able to be perceived

examples.text: The change in the river's course was so gradual as to be almost insensible.

senses.en: incapable of physical sensation

examples.text: insensible to pain

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 īnsēnsibilis에서 왔습니다. 느낄 수 없는 상태, 곧 의식하지 못함을 뜻합니다.

senses.en: unable to meet or discharge financial obligations

examples.text: an insolvent debtor

origin.ko: in-(아닌)과 solvent(빚을 갚을 수 있는)가 합쳐진 말입니다. 빚을 풀어낼 수 없는 상태입니다.

senses.en: The act or form of calling for the assistance or presence of some superior being, especially prayer offered to a divine being.

examples.text: The ceremony opened with an invocation asking for guidance and blessing on the gathering.

senses.en: An act of invoking or claiming a legal right.

examples.text: The senator's invocation of executive privilege delayed the inquiry for several months.

origin.ko: 라틴어 invocātiō에서 왔고 invoke(부르다)에서 나왔습니다. 신을 불러 도움을 청하는 기도입니다.

senses.en: a small natural hill

examples.text: Sheep grazed on the grassy knoll overlooking the valley.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 cnoll '꼭대기'에서 왔고 '덩어리'를 뜻하는 게르만어 뿌리와 이어집니다. 봉긋한 작은 언덕을 가리킵니다.

senses.en: the act of taking something from someone unlawfully

examples.text: That young man already has four assaults, a DUI, and a larceny on his record.

origin.ko: 앵글로노르만어 larcin '절도'에서 왔고 라틴어 latrocinium '강도질'과 이어집니다.

senses.en: given or giving freely

examples.text: He was liberal with his compliments.

senses.en: showing or characterized by broad-mindedness

examples.text: Her parents had liberal ideas about child-rearing.

senses.en: not literal

examples.text: The translator took a liberal approach, preserving the poem's spirit rather than its exact words.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어를 거쳐 라틴어 līberālis '자유인에게 어울리는'에서 왔습니다. 자유인답게 아낌없이 베푼다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: any long and tedious address or recital

examples.text: a litany of failures

senses.en: A ritual liturgical prayer in which a series of prayers recited by a leader are alternated with responses from the congregation.

examples.text: The congregation answered each line of the litany with a murmured refrain.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어와 라틴어를 거쳐 그리스어 litaneía '기도'에서 왔습니다. 끝없이 이어 외는 기도문처럼 장황한 나열입니다.

senses.en: an awkward stupid person

examples.text: The clumsy lout knocked over the display and then stood there gaping.

senses.en: A troublemaker, often violent; a rude violent person; a yob.

examples.text: A gang of drunken louts wrecked the bus shelter on their way home.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 lūtan '몸을 숙이다'와 이어진 중세 영어에서 왔다고 보입니다. 구부정한 촌뜨기의 이미지입니다.

senses.en: A person who is not satisfied with current conditions; a discontented person, a rebel.

examples.text: The regime tried to silence every malcontent who dared to criticize its economic policies.

senses.en: discontented as toward authority

examples.text: A malcontent faction within the party plotted to unseat its leader.

origin.ko: 중세 프랑스어 malcontent에서 왔고 mal-과 content(만족한)가 합쳐졌습니다. 만족하지 못하는 사람입니다.

senses.en: To savage; to cause serious physical wounds.

examples.text: The bear mauled him in a terrible way.

senses.en: To criticise harshly.

examples.text: The latest film by the Cohen brothers was mauled by the press, and was a box-office flop to boot.

origin.ko: 중세 영어 malle '철퇴'에서 왔고 라틴어 malleus '망치'와 이어집니다. 망치로 내리치듯 심하게 상처 입힌다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: Sweet, smooth and musical; pleasant to hear (generally used of a person's voice, tone or writing style).

examples.text: The radio host's mellifluous voice made even the weather report sound like poetry.

origin.ko: 라틴어 mellifluus '꿀처럼 흐르는'에서 왔습니다. 꿀처럼 달고 매끄러운 소리입니다.

senses.en: Lying, untruthful or dishonest.

examples.text: He was dismissed as a mendacious witness.

senses.en: intentionally untrue

examples.text: The campaign relied on mendacious claims that were debunked within hours of their release.

origin.ko: 프랑스어와 라틴어 mendāx '거짓말하는'에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: Marked by mettle or bravery; courageous.

examples.text: The mettlesome young pilot volunteered for the most dangerous missions of the war.

origin.ko: mettle(기개)에 -some이 붙은 말입니다.

senses.en: A social environment or setting.

examples.text: The novelist grew up in a literary milieu where debate and publishing were part of daily life.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 milieu에서 왔고 고대 프랑스어 mi(가운데)와 lieu(장소)가 합쳐졌습니다. 한가운데 놓인 주위 환경입니다.

senses.en: infinitely or immeasurably small

examples.text: The report detected minute traces of lead in the water supply.

senses.en: characterized by painstaking care and detailed examination

examples.text: Investigators carried out a minute inspection of the wreckage before drawing any conclusions.

origin.ko: 라틴어 minūtus '작은'에서 왔고 minuō '작게 하다'에서 나왔습니다.

senses.en: One who professes misogyny; a hater of women.

examples.text: The columnist was denounced as a misogynist after his dismissive remarks about female scientists.

origin.ko: 그리스어 miséō '미워하다'와 gunḗ '여자'가 합쳐졌습니다. 여성을 싫어하는 사람입니다.

senses.en: tediously repetitious or lacking in variety

examples.text: The assembly-line work was so monotonous that employees struggled to stay alert through the shift.

senses.en: Having an unvarying pitch or tone.

examples.text: The lecturer's monotonous delivery put half the room to sleep.

origin.ko: 그리스어 monotonos, 즉 '한 가지 음조'에서 왔습니다. 늘 같은 가락이라 단조롭고 지루하다는 뜻이 되었습니다.

senses.en: original and of a kind not seen before

examples.text: the computer produced a completely novel proof of a well-known theorem

origin.ko: 라틴어 novus '새로운'의 지소형 novellus에서 왔습니다. 새롭고 신선하다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: To make legally invalid.

examples.text: The court moved to nullify the contract after discovering that the signatures had been forged.

senses.en: To make of no use or value; to cancel out.

examples.text: Rising inflation threatened to nullify the benefits of the wage increase.

origin.ko: 라틴어 nullus '아무것도 아닌'에 -ify가 붙은 말로, 효력을 없는 것으로 만든다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: bending the head or body or knee as a sign of reverence or submission or shame or greeting

examples.text: The courtiers made deep obeisance as the queen entered the great hall.

senses.en: An obedient attitude.

examples.text: The regime demanded constant obeisance from officials, who flattered the leader in every speech.

origin.ko: 옛 프랑스어 obeïr '복종하다'에서 왔고, 라틴어로는 '~에게 귀 기울이다'입니다. 복종의 뜻으로 몸을 숙이는 절을 가리킵니다.

senses.en: To keep down by unjust force.

examples.text: The rural poor were oppressed by the land-owners.

senses.en: To make sad or gloomy.

examples.text: We were oppressed by the constant grey skies.

origin.ko: 라틴어 opprimere '위에서 짓누르다'에서 왔습니다. 힘으로 눌러서 꼼짝 못 하게 한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: ostentatiously rich and superior in quality

examples.text: The opulent hotel lobby glittered with crystal chandeliers and gold leaf.

origin.ko: 라틴어 opulentus에서 왔고, ops는 '부, 힘, 자원'입니다.

senses.en: remove from a position or office

examples.text: The chairman was ousted after he misappropriated funds

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 oster '치우다'에서 왔고, 라틴어 obstāre '앞을 가로막다'가 원형입니다. 방해되는 것을 치운다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: Overly bossy, domineering, arrogant, forceful, intense, or annoying.

examples.text: Her overbearing manager second-guessed every decision and rarely let anyone finish a sentence.

origin.ko: overbear '위에서 짓누르다'에 -ing이 붙은 말로, 상대를 위에서 누르듯 고압적이라는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: characterized by extreme care and great effort

examples.text: The restorers did painstaking work to repair the fragile frescoes.

origin.ko: pains(수고)와 taking(들이다)을 합친 말로, 수고를 아끼지 않는다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: a manuscript (usually written on papyrus or parchment) on which more than one text has been written with the earlier writing incompletely erased and still visible

examples.text: Scholars used ultraviolet light to read the original prayer book beneath the medieval palimpsest.

senses.en: Something bearing the traces of an earlier, erased form.

examples.text: The old city is a palimpsest, with Roman walls still visible beneath its medieval streets.

origin.ko: 그리스어 palímpsēstos '다시 긁어낸'에서 왔습니다. 쓴 글을 긁어내고 다시 쓴 양피지입니다.

senses.en: lose strength or effectiveness; become or appear boring, insipid, or tiresome (to)

examples.text: the course palled on her

senses.en: Something that covers or surrounds like a cloak; in particular, a cloud of dust, smoke, etc., or a feeling of fear, gloom, or suspicion.

examples.text: The early election results cast a pall over what was supposed to be a celebration.

origin.ko: appall(맥이 빠지게 하다)이 줄어든 말로 보입니다. 힘이 빠져 시들해지고 싫증난다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: qualifying or explaining; placed or as if placed in parentheses

examples.text: The author's parenthetical remarks often contain the sharpest insights in the essay.

origin.ko: 그리스어 parénthetos '곁에 끼워 넣은'에서 왔습니다. 문장 안에 덧붙여 넣은 설명이라는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: Hanging from, or as if from, a support.

examples.text: Pendulous clusters of wisteria hung from the garden pergola.

origin.ko: 라틴어 pendulus '매달린'에서 왔고, pendeō는 '매달리다'입니다.

senses.en: a state of extreme poverty or destitution

examples.text: The poet died in penury, his work unrecognized until decades later.

origin.ko: 라틴어 pēnūria '결핍, 궁핍'에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: To travel from place to place, or from one country to another, especially on foot; hence, to sojourn in foreign countries.

examples.text: As a young scholar, he peregrinated across Europe, studying in a dozen universities.

origin.ko: 라틴어 peregrīnārī '외국에서 살거나 여행하다'에서 왔습니다. 땅을 가로질러 두루 다닌다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: To steal in small quantities, or articles of small value; to practise petty theft.

examples.text: The clerk was fired for pilfering small amounts of cash from the register.

origin.ko: 옛 프랑스어 pelfre '약탈품'에서 왔습니다. 작은 물건을 슬쩍 가져간다는 뜻이 되었습니다.

senses.en: To subject to humiliation, scorn, ridicule or abuse.

examples.text: The governor was pilloried in the press for his handling of the crisis.

senses.en: a wooden instrument of punishment on a post with holes for the wrists and neck; offenders were locked in and so exposed to public scorn

examples.text: Petty thieves were once locked in the village pillory as a public lesson.

origin.ko: 옛 프랑스어 pilori에서 왔고, 죄인을 세워 구경거리로 만들던 형틀을 뜻했습니다. 그래서 공개적으로 망신 준다는 뜻이 되었습니다.

senses.en: To excite (someone) to action, especially by causing jealousy, resentment, etc.; also, to stimulate (an emotion or feeling, especially curiosity or interest).

examples.text: I believe this will pique your interest.

senses.en: cause to feel resentment or indignation

examples.text: The senator was piqued by the suggestion that she had ignored her constituents.

senses.en: a sudden outburst of anger

examples.text: In a fit of pique, he stormed out of the meeting without a word.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 piquer '찌르다'에서 왔습니다. 바늘로 콕 찌르듯 호기심이나 감정을 건드린다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: capable of being influenced or formed

examples.text: Neuroscientists stress that the adolescent brain remains remarkably plastic and responsive to new experience.

senses.en: capable of being molded or modeled (especially of earth or clay or other soft material)

examples.text: plastic substances such as wax or clay

origin.ko: 그리스어 plastikós '빚을 수 있는'에서 왔고, plássō는 '빚어 만들다'입니다. 모양을 쉽게 만들 수 있다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: To think about or explore in depth, to get to the bottom of.

examples.text: The novel plumbs the depths of grief without ever slipping into sentimentality.

senses.en: To determine the depth, generally of a liquid; to sound.

examples.text: Sailors plumbed the channel before guiding the heavy ship toward the harbor.

senses.en: exactly vertical

examples.text: The mason checked that the new wall was plumb before laying the next course of bricks.

origin.ko: 라틴어 plumbum '납'에서 왔습니다. 납추를 늘어뜨려 깊이를 재는 데서 깊이 파고들다가 되었습니다.

senses.en: To drop swiftly, in a direct manner; to fall quickly.

examples.text: After its ascent, the arrow plummeted to earth.

origin.ko: 옛 프랑스어 plommet '납 추'에서 왔고, 라틴어 plumbum '납'이 원형입니다. 납추처럼 곤두박질친다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: Organizational structure and governance, especially of a state or a religion.

examples.text: Church polity was a topic of fierce dispute in 17th-century Britain.

senses.en: A politically organized unit, especially a nation of people, a class or ingroup that governs it, or the state ruled thereby.

examples.text: New polities emerged in Europe after the fall of the Roman Empire.

origin.ko: 그리스어 politeia('시민의 국가, 통치 방식')가 라틴어와 프랑스어를 거쳐 들어왔습니다.

senses.en: ceremonial elegance and splendor

examples.text: The coronation was carried out with all the pomp and pageantry the monarchy could muster.

senses.en: cheap or pretentious or vain display

examples.text: Behind the pomp of the ministry's announcement lay a surprisingly modest set of reforms.

origin.ko: 그리스어 pompē('보냄, 엄숙한 행렬')가 라틴어와 프랑스어를 거쳐 들어왔습니다. 행렬의 화려함이 '장엄함'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: To serve as a warning or omen of.

examples.text: Dark clouds and a sudden drop in pressure portended a violent storm.

origin.ko: 라틴어 portendere('예고하다')에서 왔습니다. 앞쪽으로 뻗어 보여 주는 것이 곧 전조입니다.

senses.en: of momentous or ominous significance

examples.text: A portentous silence settled over the chamber before the verdict was announced.

senses.en: puffed up with vanity

examples.text: The director's portentous narration made an ordinary documentary feel absurdly self-important.

origin.ko: 라틴어 portentum('전조, 괴이한 일')에서 왔습니다. 불길하고 중대한 징조를 가진 것을 가리킵니다.

senses.en: A short preliminary statement or remark, especially an explanatory introduction to a formal document or statute.

examples.text: The preamble to the treaty states its purpose before listing any binding obligations.

senses.en: A precursor.

examples.text: High winds are often a preamble to a winter storm.

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 praeambulum('앞서 걷다')에서 왔습니다. 본문 앞에 먼저 걸어가는 글이 서문입니다.

senses.en: Costly to the extreme; beyond budget.

examples.text: I'd like to visit Europe someday, but the cost is prohibitive right now.

senses.en: Tending to prohibit, preclude, or disallow.

examples.text: Prohibitive regulations discouraged small firms from entering the market.

origin.ko: 라틴어 prohibēre('막다')에서 왔습니다. 가격이 너무 높아 아예 접근을 막는 정도라는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: Made without careful choice; indiscriminate.

examples.text: The senator was criticized for his promiscuous acceptance of donations from any interested party.

senses.en: Made up of various disparate elements mixed together; of disorderly composition.

examples.text: A promiscuous crowd of merchants, soldiers, and pilgrims filled the market square.

origin.ko: 라틴어 prōmiscuus('뒤섞인')에서 왔습니다. 구별 없이 마구 섞인다는 뜻에서 '무분별한'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: someone who fights with their fists for sport

examples.text: The retired pugilist now trains young boxers at a gym downtown.

origin.ko: 라틴어 pugil('주먹싸움꾼')에 -ist가 붙은 말입니다. 주먹으로 싸우는 사람입니다.

senses.en: approve and express assent, responsibility, or obligation

examples.text: All parties ratified the peace treaty

origin.ko: 라틴어 ratus('헤아려 정해진')에서 온 중세 라틴어 ratificare에서 왔습니다. 확정된 것으로 만든다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: To recur, or break out anew after a quiescence or dormant period.

examples.text: Old tensions between the two communities recrudesced after the election, ending years of calm.

origin.ko: 라틴어 recrūdēscere('다시 날것이 되다')의 영향을 받은 말입니다. 아물던 상처가 다시 도지듯 재발한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: An act of retaliation.

examples.text: Villagers feared reprisals if they cooperated with the investigators, so few agreed to testify.

origin.ko: 고대 이탈리아어 ripresaglia에서 왔고 riprendere('되찾아 가다')와 이어집니다. 당한 만큼 되가져오는 보복입니다.

senses.en: a quick reply to a question or remark (especially a witty or critical one)

examples.text: Her witty retort to the heckler drew laughter and applause from the whole audience.

senses.en: answer back

examples.text: When accused of laziness, she retorted that nobody else had worked on the weekend.

origin.ko: 라틴어 retorquēre('뒤로 비틀다')에서 왔습니다. 상대 말을 되비틀어 받아치는 응수입니다.

senses.en: having or emitting a high-pitched and sharp tone or tones

examples.text: The woods rang with shrill cries of the birds.

senses.en: being sharply insistent on being heard

examples.text: Her shrill criticism of the plan alienated even those who shared her concerns.

origin.ko: 중세 영어 shrille에서 왔고 소리를 흉내 낸 의성어에서 나온 것으로 봅니다. 날카롭게 높은 소리입니다.

senses.en: A thing which has the appearance or form of another thing, but not its true qualities; a thing which simulates another thing; an imitation; a semblance.

examples.text: The theme park offered a simulacrum of a medieval village, complete with costumed actors and plastic stone walls.

senses.en: a representation of a person (especially in the form of sculpture)

examples.text: The museum displayed a marble simulacrum of the emperor, carved soon after his death.

origin.ko: 라틴어 simulācrum(형상, 닮은 것)에서 왔습니다. 진짜를 닮았지만 알맹이가 없는 모조품입니다.

senses.en: someone who habitually doubts accepted beliefs

examples.text: As a lifelong skeptic, he demanded independent evidence before accepting any of the company's bold claims.

origin.ko: 그리스어 skeptikos(살펴보는 사람)에서 왔습니다. 쉽게 믿지 않고 따져 보는 사람입니다.

senses.en: To slight, ignore or behave coldly toward someone.

examples.text: The senator snubbed his rival by refusing to shake hands at the ceremony.

senses.en: A deliberate affront or slight.

examples.text: I hope the people we couldn't invite don't see it as a snub.

origin.ko: 고대 노르드어 snubba(꾸짖다)에서 왔고 '잘라내다'라는 뜻이었습니다. 쌀쌀맞게 잘라 내치는 이미지입니다.

senses.en: affecting or characteristic of the body as opposed to the mind or spirit

examples.text: Anxiety often produces somatic symptoms such as headaches, a racing heart, and stomach pain.

origin.ko: 그리스어 sōma(몸)에서 온 sōmatikos에서 왔습니다. 정신과 대비되는 신체의 뜻입니다.

senses.en: exercising or showing good judgment

examples.text: The advisor gave sound counsel, urging the board to delay the acquisition until the figures were clearer.

senses.en: logically valid

examples.text: a sound argument

senses.en: financially secure and safe

examples.text: a sound economy

senses.en: in good condition; free from defect or damage or decay

examples.text: the wall is sound

origin.ko: 형용사 sound는 고대 영어 sund(건강한, 온전한)에서 왔습니다. 온전하고 건강해 믿을 만하다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: cause the downfall of; of rulers

examples.text: subvert the ruling class

senses.en: destroy property or hinder normal operations

examples.text: The oppressive regime stays in power only as long as they manage to subvert the will of the people.

senses.en: corrupt morally or by intemperance or sensuality

examples.text: Critics charged that the lavish gifts were meant to subvert the integrity of the judges.

origin.ko: 라틴어 subvertere(아래에서 뒤집다)에서 왔습니다. 밑에서부터 뒤집어 무너뜨린다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: briefly giving the gist of something

examples.text: You should give clear, succinct information to the clients.

origin.ko: 라틴어 succīnctus(허리띠로 걷어 올린)에서 왔습니다. 옷자락을 띠로 졸라맨 듯 간결하다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: assistance in time of difficulty

examples.text: Aid workers brought food and succor to villagers cut off by the flood.

senses.en: help in a difficult situation

examples.text: The monastery had long succored travelers caught in the mountain storms.

senses.en: (used of persons' bodies) capable of moving or bending freely

examples.text: supple joints

senses.en: (used of e.g. personality traits) readily adaptable

examples.text: a supple mind

senses.en: Compliant; yielding to the will of others.

examples.text: a supple horse

origin.ko: 라틴어 supplex(무릎 꿇은, 순종하는)에서 온 프랑스어 souple에서 왔습니다. 몸을 굽히듯 유연하다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: turn sharply; change direction abruptly

examples.text: The driver had to swerve sharply to avoid a fallen branch in the road.

senses.en: To wander from any line prescribed, or from a rule or duty; to depart from what is established by law, duty, custom, or the like; to deviate.

examples.text: They swerve from the strict letter of the law.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 sweorfan(문지르다, 돌아서다)에서 왔습니다. 옆으로 휙 틀어 비낀다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: deductive reasoning in which a conclusion is derived from two premises

examples.text: All humans are mortal; Socrates is human; therefore Socrates is mortal is the classic syllogism.

origin.ko: 그리스어 syllogismos(추론)에서 왔습니다. 전제들을 함께 모아 결론을 셈해 내는 논법입니다.

senses.en: To be prolific; to abound; to be rife.

examples.text: Fish teem in this pond.

senses.en: To pour (especially with rain)

examples.text: By evening the rain was teeming down, and the streets emptied of pedestrians.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 tēman(새끼를 낳다)에서 온 말이 유력합니다. 번식해 우글거린다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: Revealing something, especially something not intended to be known.

examples.text: A telltale blush crept into her cheeks as he approached.

senses.en: someone who gossips indiscreetly

examples.text: Nobody trusted the office telltale, who repeated every private remark to the manager within the hour.

origin.ko: tell(말하다)과 tale(이야기)이 합쳐진 말입니다. 비밀을 이야기해 버리듯 드러내 보입니다.

senses.en: a person who makes a will

examples.text: The court ruled that the testator had been of sound mind when she signed the will.

origin.ko: 라틴어 testari('증언하다, 유언하다')에서 온 말입니다. 유언으로 뜻을 증언하는 사람을 가리킵니다.

senses.en: Showing thrift; economical; frugal.

examples.text: Raised by thrifty parents, she saved a third of every paycheck from her very first job.

origin.ko: 중세 영어 thrift에 -y를 붙인 말입니다. 아끼며 살림을 불리는 모습이 '검소한'입니다.

senses.en: Something which gives the appearance of something.

examples.text: The president enjoyed the trappings of power, including a motorcade and a staff of two hundred.

origin.ko: trap('말 장식')에서 나온 trapping의 복수형으로 보입니다. 이 사전 정보만으로는 확실히 말하기 어렵습니다.

senses.en: a solemn pledge of fidelity

examples.text: The knight plighted his troth to the king and swore never to abandon the realm.

senses.en: a mutual promise to marry

examples.text: In the old ballad the couple plight their troth beneath an oak tree on midsummer's eve.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 trēowþ('충실, 약속')에서 왔고 true에 -th를 붙인 형태입니다. 진실을 걸고 한 약속이 '서약'입니다.

senses.en: not easily perturbed or excited or upset; marked by extreme calm and composure

examples.text: The unflappable pilot calmly guided the damaged aircraft to a safe landing.

origin.ko: un-, flap('동요시키다'), -able의 결합입니다. 허둥대며 파닥이지 않는다는 뜻이 '침착한'입니다.

senses.en: not forbearing; ruthless

examples.text: The critic was unsparing in her review, listing every flaw in the production without mercy.

senses.en: very generous

examples.text: The patron was unsparing in his support, funding the orchestra's tours year after year.

senses.en: a person holding a fief; a person who owes allegiance and service to a feudal lord

examples.text: Each vassal swore loyalty to the duke and pledged knights for his wars in exchange for land.

senses.en: Any subordinate bound by similar close ties.

examples.text: The smaller nation was little more than a vassal of its powerful neighbor.

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 vassallus('하인')에서 왔고 켈트어 계통의 '젊은이, 종'에서 나왔습니다. 주군을 섬기는 '봉신'입니다.

senses.en: Enthusiasm, rapture, spirit, or vigour, especially of imagination such as that which animates an artist, musician, or writer, in composing or performing.

examples.text: The young pianist played with such verve that the audience forgot the cold of the hall.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 verve에서 왔고 후기 라틴어 verva, 즉 verba('말')와 이어집니다. 말에 실린 기운이 '열정'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: a noisy or scolding or domineering woman

examples.text: The playwright cast the landlady as a loud virago who terrorized her tenants.

origin.ko: 라틴어 virāgō('남자 같은 여자')에서 왔고 vir('남자')와 이어집니다.

senses.en: To sing like a bird, especially with trills.

examples.text: A thrush warbled from the top of the hedge as the sun rose over the meadow.

senses.en: a raised mark on the skin (as produced by the blow of a whip); characteristic of many allergic reactions

examples.text: The mosquito bites left itchy red welts along his arm.

origin.ko: 원래 구두 제작 용어였고, 1800년경 '피부에 솟은 자국'의 뜻이 생겼습니다. 어원은 불확실합니다.

senses.en: To cause harm; to afflict; to inflict; to harm or injure; to let out harm.

examples.text: The earthquake wreaked havoc in the city.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 wrecan('몰아내다, 복수하다')에서 왔습니다. 복수로 해를 가하는 것이 '(피해를) 입히다'입니다.

senses.en: humorously sarcastic or mocking

examples.text: With a wry smile, the veteran reporter remarked that the politician's promises were nothing new.

senses.en: bent to one side

examples.text: He made a wry face as he swallowed the bitter medicine.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 wrīġian('비틀다, 휘다')에서 왔습니다. 입을 비튼 표정에서 '비꼬는'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: a state or condition markedly different from the norm

examples.text: Analysts described the sudden drop in sales as an aberration rather than the start of a lasting decline.

origin.ko: 라틴어 aberrare(길을 벗어나 헤매다)에서 왔습니다. 정상 경로에서 벗어난 상태를 뜻합니다.

senses.en: most unfortunate or miserable

examples.text: Thousands of families lived in abject poverty, without clean water or reliable shelter.

senses.en: showing humiliation or submissiveness

examples.text: The minister issued an abject apology, begging the public to forgive his remarks.

origin.ko: 라틴어 abiectus(내던져진)에서 왔습니다. 버려져 내팽개쳐진 처지가 '비참한'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: associated by chance and not an integral part

examples.text: The theory dismissed the similarities between the two languages as adventitious rather than evidence of a common origin.

origin.ko: 라틴어 adventicius(외부에서 온)에서 왔습니다. 밖에서 우연히 도착한 것이라 '외래의'라는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: characterized by indirect references

examples.text: The poem is dense and allusive, echoing classical myths without ever naming them.

origin.ko: 라틴어 alludere(농담하듯 건드리다)에서 왔습니다. 직접 말하지 않고 슬쩍 건드려 암시합니다.

senses.en: a trinket or piece of jewelry usually hung about the neck and thought to be a magical protection against evil or disease

examples.text: The traveler wore a small stone amulet around his neck to ward off misfortune.

origin.ko: 프랑스어를 거쳐 라틴어 amuletum(부적)에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: exact opposite

examples.text: The quiet librarian was the antithesis of the flamboyant showman who had preceded him.

senses.en: the juxtaposition of contrasting words or ideas to give a feeling of balance

examples.text: “To err is human; to forgive, divine” is a classic antithesis that balances two opposed ideas.

origin.ko: 그리스어 antithesis(맞세워 놓음)에서 왔습니다. 서로 반대편에 놓인 것이 '정반대'입니다.

senses.en: someone with the power to settle matters at will

examples.text: she was the final arbiter on all matters of fashion

senses.en: someone chosen to judge and decide a disputed issue

examples.text: The two firms agreed to accept the ruling of a neutral arbiter.

origin.ko: 라틴어 arbiter(증인, 심판)에서 왔고 '보러 가는 사람'이 원뜻입니다. 직접 보고 판결하는 사람입니다.

senses.en: to agree or express agreement

examples.text: The princess assented to all that was suggested.

senses.en: agreement with a statement or proposal to do something

examples.text: He lowered his head in assent.

origin.ko: 라틴어 assentire(~에 같은 느낌을 갖다)에서 왔습니다. 마음이 같아 동의한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: adjust or accustom to; bring into harmony with

examples.text: By meditating, I try to attune myself to the greater cosmos.

origin.ko: ad-(~쪽으로)와 tune(곡조)이 합쳐진 말입니다. 음을 맞추듯 조화시킨다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: To tarnish something, especially someone's reputation.

examples.text: The newspaper was on a campaign to besmirch the actor.

origin.ko: 중세 영어 besmorchen에서 왔고, be-에 smirch(얼룩지게 하다)가 붙은 말입니다. 명예에 얼룩을 묻히는 이미지입니다.

senses.en: give as a gift

examples.text: Medals were bestowed on the winning team.

origin.ko: 중세 영어 bestowen에서 왔습니다. '짐을 싣듯 자리에 놓아 두다'에서 '아낌없이 내려 주다'로 발전했습니다.

senses.en: a decorative pin worn by women

examples.text: She fastened a silver brooch to her coat before leaving for the ceremony.

origin.ko: broach(뾰족한 핀)의 변형입니다.

senses.en: characterized by liveliness and lightheartedness

examples.text: Despite the long delay, the team stayed buoyant and joked all the way to the airport.

senses.en: tending to float on a liquid or rise in air or gas

examples.text: Cork is buoyant enough to support a heavy fishing net on the surface of the water.

senses.en: complaining excessively.

examples.text: Ignoring the carping critics, the chef kept the menu exactly as she had designed it.

senses.en: persistent petty and unjustified criticism

examples.text: Constant carping from the audience made it hard for the speaker to finish his argument.

senses.en: a rate that is rapid

examples.text: The committee acted with remarkable celerity, approving the emergency budget within a single afternoon.

origin.ko: 라틴어 celeritas에서 왔고 celer('빠른')가 뿌리입니다.

senses.en: leniency and compassion shown toward offenders by a person or agency charged with administering justice

examples.text: The defendant pleaded for clemency, citing her cooperation and her lack of any prior offenses.

senses.en: A pardon, commutation, or similar reduction, removal, or postponement of legal penalties by an executive officer of a state.

examples.text: The governor granted clemency to the prisoner hours before the scheduled execution.

origin.ko: 라틴어 clēmentia('온화함, 관대함')에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: influence or urge by gentle urging, caressing, or flattering

examples.text: He coaxed the horse gently into the trailer.

origin.ko: 1586년 은어 'make a coax of'(바보 취급하다)에서 시작됐고 기원은 불분명합니다.

senses.en: have internal elements or parts logically connected so that aesthetic consistency results

examples.text: The essay's scattered observations fail to cohere into a persuasive overall argument.

senses.en: come or be in close contact with; stick or hold together and resist separation

examples.text: Wet sand coheres far better than dry sand, which is why sandcastles need water.

origin.ko: 라틴어 cohaereō('함께 달라붙다, 일관되다')에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: the arrangement of the hair (especially a woman's hair)

examples.text: Her elaborate coiffure required nearly two hours of work by a team of stylists.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 coiffure를 그대로 빌려 온 말입니다.

senses.en: a concise but comprehensive summary of a larger work

examples.text: The handbook serves as a compendium of the field's major findings over the past century.

senses.en: a publication containing a variety of works

examples.text: The compendium gathers essays, poems, and letters from dozens of nineteenth-century writers.

origin.ko: 라틴어 compendium('함께 달아 본 것, 절약, 축약')에서 왔습니다. 많은 내용을 달아 추려 낸 요약본입니다.

senses.en: based primarily on surmise rather than adequate evidence

examples.text: Any account of the city's earliest years remains largely conjectural because few records survive.

senses.en: To signify beyond its literal or principal meaning.

examples.text: The word "hearth" often connotes coziness and warmth.

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 connotō('덧붙여 표시하다')에서 왔습니다. 글자 뜻 너머를 함께 가리킨다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: being of equal extent or scope or duration

examples.text: The county's borders are coterminous with those of the old medieval parish.

origin.ko: 라틴어 conterminus에서 왔고, con-(함께)과 terminus(경계)가 합쳐졌습니다. 경계를 함께 한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: tending to hinder the achievement of a goal

examples.text: Punishing students for asking questions is counterproductive and discourages genuine curiosity.

senses.en: terminate or abbreviate before its intended or proper end or its full extent

examples.text: When the audience grew restless, the speaker curtailed her speech.

senses.en: place restrictions on

examples.text: The authoritarian government moved quickly to curtail press freedom during the unrest.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 court(짧은, 라틴어 curtus)에서 왔습니다. 꼬리를 짧게 자른 말에서 '줄이다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: To discourage, intimidate.

examples.text: Failing the first exam did not daunt her; she simply studied harder for the retake.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 danter(길들이다)에서 왔고 라틴어 domāre(길들이다)가 뿌리입니다. 길들이듯 기를 꺾는다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: To spend time idly and unfruitfully; to waste time.

examples.text: If we dawdle over breakfast any longer, we will miss the train to the airport.

senses.en: marked by excessive self-indulgence and moral decay

examples.text: a decadent life of excessive money and no sense of responsibility

senses.en: luxuriously self-indulgent

examples.text: I spent a decadent day at a spa

origin.ko: 라틴어 dēcadere(아래로 떨어지다)에서 왔습니다. 몰락해 가는 상태를 가리킵니다.

senses.en: To reach (a conclusion) by applying rules of logic or other forms of reasoning to given premises or known facts.

examples.text: From the muddy footprints, the detective deduced that the intruder had entered through the garden.

origin.ko: 라틴어 dēdūcere(끌어내다)에서 왔습니다. 전제에서 결론을 끌어내니 '추론하다'입니다.

senses.en: set, mark, or draw the boundaries of something

examples.text: The treaty delimited the border between the two nations along the course of the river.

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 dēlīmitō(경계를 표시하다)에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: set, mark, or draw the boundaries of something

examples.text: Low stone walls demarcate the monastery's land from the neighboring farms.

origin.ko: demarcation에서 만들어진 말입니다. 경계를 표시한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: extremely evil or cruel; expressive of cruelty or befitting hell

examples.text: The dictator's diabolical regime tortured dissidents and starved entire provinces into submission.

senses.en: showing the cunning or ingenuity or wickedness typical of a devil

examples.text: The villain devised a diabolical scheme that fooled even the most seasoned detectives.

origin.ko: 그리스어 diábolos(악마)에서 왔고 '이간질하며 중상하는 자'라는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: Having fallen into a state of disrepair or deterioration, especially through neglect.

examples.text: The dilapidated farmhouse had sagging beams and windows that had not been repaired in decades.

senses.en: perceptible by the senses or intellect

examples.text: the newspaper reports no discernible progress in the negotiations

origin.ko: discern에 -ible이 붙은 말로, 가려낼 수 있다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: having or revealing keen insight and good judgment

examples.text: a discerning critic

senses.en: fall away or decline

examples.text: The patient's strength ebbed away

senses.en: a gradual decline (in size or strength or power or number)

examples.text: Painting was then at its lowest ebb.

senses.en: flow back or recede

examples.text: the tides ebbed at noon

origin.ko: 고대 영어 ebba(썰물)에서 왔습니다. 물이 빠지듯 점차 줄어든다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: deeply involved especially in something complicated

examples.text: The senator became embroiled in a lengthy dispute over campaign funding.

senses.en: An agent that induces vomiting.

examples.text: Physicians once prescribed an emetic to rid the patient of suspected poison.

origin.ko: 그리스어 émetos(구토)에서 프랑스어를 거쳐 왔습니다. 토하게 하는 약을 가리킵니다.

senses.en: become ground down or deteriorate

examples.text: Her confidence eroded

senses.en: remove soil or rock

examples.text: Rain eroded the terraces

origin.ko: 라틴어 ērōdere(갉아 먹다)에서 프랑스어를 거쳐 왔습니다. 조금씩 갉아 없애는 이미지입니다.

senses.en: unequivocally detestable

examples.text: Historians condemned the regime for its execrable treatment of political prisoners.

senses.en: of very poor quality or condition

examples.text: The critics agreed that the restaurant's service was execrable and its food barely edible.

origin.ko: 라틴어 execrābilis에서 왔습니다. 신성한 곳에서 저주받아 쫓겨날 만한 '혐오스러운'이라는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: speed up the progress of; facilitate

examples.text: He expedited the search by alphabetizing the papers.

origin.ko: 라틴어 expedīre(발의 족쇄를 풀다)에서 왔습니다. 걸림돌을 치워 일을 빠르게 진행시킨다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: Able to be explained.

examples.text: The strange readings were perfectly explicable once the technicians discovered the faulty sensor.

origin.ko: 라틴어 explicāre(펼치다)에서 왔습니다. 접힌 것을 펼쳐 보일 수 있으니 '설명할 수 있는'입니다.

senses.en: joyously unrestrained

examples.text: The exuberant crowd poured into the streets to celebrate the team's first championship in decades.

senses.en: produced or growing in extreme abundance

examples.text: Exuberant vines covered the walls of the abandoned house and crept across its collapsed roof.

origin.ko: 라틴어 exūberāre(넘쳐흐르다)에서 왔습니다. uber는 젖통을 뜻해 젖이 넘치듯 활기가 넘친다는 이미지입니다.

senses.en: marked by excessive enthusiasm for and intense devotion to a cause or idea

examples.text: His fanatical devotion to the cause led him to reject every compromise offered by moderates.

senses.en: search and discover through persistent investigation

examples.text: She ferreted out the truth

origin.ko: 속라틴어 *furittum(족제비)에서 고대 프랑스어를 거쳐 왔고, 라틴어 fūr(도둑)의 지소형입니다. 작은 도둑 같은 동물이 굴을 뒤져 찾아내는 이미지입니다.

senses.en: feelings of great warmth and intensity

examples.text: The coach trains his water polo team with fervor.

origin.ko: 라틴어 fervor(끓는 열기)에서 왔습니다. 물이 끓듯 달아오른 열정을 뜻합니다.

senses.en: To illegally take possession of (something, especially items of low value); to pilfer, to steal.

examples.text: Hey, someone filched my wallet!

senses.en: conspicuously and outrageously bad or reprehensible

examples.text: The judge condemned the company's flagrant violation of environmental regulations.

origin.ko: 라틴어 flagrāre(활활 타다)의 현재분사에서 왔습니다. 불타듯 눈에 확 띄는 노골적인 잘못입니다.

senses.en: refrain from doing

examples.text: Though deeply provoked, the senator forbore from answering his critics in public.

senses.en: a person from whom you are descended

examples.text: Her forbears emigrated from Ireland during the great famine of the 1840s.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 forberan(참다, 삼가다)에서 왔습니다. 하고 싶은 것을 견디며 참는다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: elegance by virtue of fineness of manner and expression

examples.text: Despite her family's lost fortune, she maintained an air of quiet gentility.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 gentilité에서 왔습니다. 좋은 가문 출신다운 고상한 상태를 뜻합니다.

senses.en: The process of development of a plan or idea.

examples.text: The treaty had a long gestation, with draft proposals circulating for nearly a decade.

senses.en: the period during which an embryo develops (about 266 days in humans)

examples.text: The gestation of a horse lasts about eleven months.

origin.ko: 라틴어 gestātiō에서 왔습니다. 배 속에 품고 나르는 기간이 '임신 기간, 구상 단계'입니다.

senses.en: laugh at with contempt and derision

examples.text: Rival fans gibed at the visiting team's goalkeeper after every missed save.

senses.en: an aggressive remark directed at a person like a missile and intended to have a telling effect

examples.text: The columnist ended his article with a pointed gibe at the minister's economic record.

senses.en: be compatible, similar or consistent; coincide in their characteristics

examples.text: The suspect's alibi did not gibe with the timeline recorded by the security cameras.

senses.en: small bumps on the skin caused by cold, fear, or strong emotion

examples.text: The choir's final chord gave the whole audience goosebumps.

senses.en: a burst of deep loud hearty laughter

examples.text: His joke drew a guffaw from the back of the room that startled the speaker.

senses.en: To laugh boisterously.

examples.text: Peter, on the contrary, threw back his head and guffawed thunderously.

origin.ko: 18세기 초 스코틀랜드어에서 처음 나타났고, 웃음소리를 흉내 낸 말로 봅니다.

senses.en: Of, or relating to, the sense of taste.

examples.text: The festival offered a gustatory tour of regional cheeses, wines, and pastries.

origin.ko: 라틴어 gustō '맛보다'에서 온 gustātus에 -ory가 붙은 말입니다. 맛보는 감각과 관련됩니다.

senses.en: vigorous and enthusiastic enjoyment

examples.text: He sang with more gusto than talent.

origin.ko: 이탈리아어 gusto에서 왔고 라틴어 gustus '맛'이 뿌리입니다. 맛보는 즐거움이 '열정, 신나는 기분'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: Prone to pauses or breaks; hesitant; broken.

examples.text: After a halting start, the negotiations gradually gathered pace and produced a framework agreement.

senses.en: a person who holds unorthodox opinions in any field (not merely religion)

examples.text: Early proponents of continental drift were dismissed as heretics by the geological establishment.

senses.en: Someone whose beliefs are contrary to the fundamental tenets of a religion they claim to belong to.

examples.text: The council condemned the priest as a heretic for denying the doctrine of the Trinity.

origin.ko: 그리스어 hairetikos '선택할 수 있는'에서 왔고 hairéō(고르다)가 뿌리입니다. 정통 대신 자기 믿음을 골라 택한 사람이 '이단자'입니다.

senses.en: To move rapidly, violently, or without control, especially in a noisy manner.

examples.text: The car hurtled down the hill at 90 miles per hour.

origin.ko: 중세영어 hurtelen '던지다, 부딪치다'에서 왔고 hurt에 반복을 뜻하는 -el이 붙은 말입니다. 부딪칠 듯 맹렬히 돌진하는 모습입니다.

senses.en: Extremely happy, peaceful, or picturesque.

examples.text: They spent an idyllic summer in a stone cottage overlooking the lake.

origin.ko: 그리스어 eidýllion '짧은 전원시'에서 왔습니다. 전원시가 그리던 평화로운 풍경이 '목가적인'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: perform without preparation

examples.text: He had no speech prepared, so he improvised.

senses.en: manage in a makeshift way; do with whatever is at hand

examples.text: They improvised a simple shelter with branches and the rope they were carrying.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 improviser에서 왔고 라틴어 improvisus '예견 못 한'이 뿌리입니다. 미리 보지(prepare) 못한 채 즉석에서 한다는 뜻입니다. improve와는 무관합니다.

senses.en: characterized by ardent emotion or intensity or brilliance

examples.text: The incandescent performance enraptured the audience.

senses.en: Emitting light as a result of being heated.

examples.text: The incandescent filament glowed steadily inside the glass bulb once the current reached it.

senses.en: Extremely angry; furious.

examples.text: She is incandescent with rage because someone stole her wallet.

origin.ko: 라틴어 incandescō '달아오르다'에서 왔고 candidus(하얀)가 뿌리입니다. 하얗게 달아올라 빛나는 모습입니다.

senses.en: failing to make or recognize distinctions

examples.text: The indiscriminate use of antibiotics has contributed to the rise of drug-resistant bacteria.

origin.ko: discriminate(구별하다)에 부정 접두사가 붙은 말입니다. 가려내지 않고 닥치는 대로 한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: characterized by iniquity; wicked because it is believed to be a sin

examples.text: iniquitous deeds

senses.en: Grossly unfair or unjust.

examples.text: Critics condemned the iniquitous tax, which fell hardest on the poorest families in the district.

origin.ko: iniquity에 -ous가 붙은 말입니다. 공평하지 않음(inīquus)이 사악함의 뜻으로 번졌습니다.

senses.en: showing curiosity

examples.text: The inquisitive child took apart the old radio to see how it worked.

senses.en: Too curious; overly interested; nosy.

examples.text: Her inquisitive neighbors asked endless questions about who visited the house and why.

origin.ko: 라틴어 inquirere '묻다, 조사하다'에서 왔습니다. 안을 파고들어 캐묻는 성격입니다.

senses.en: insert words into texts, often falsifying it thereby

examples.text: Later copyists interpolated several passages into the manuscript, obscuring the author's original argument.

senses.en: estimate the value of something based on known values

examples.text: Analysts interpolate missing temperature readings from the values recorded at nearby weather stations.

origin.ko: 라틴어 interpolō의 분사 interpolātus에서 왔습니다. 글 사이에 끼워 넣는다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: a massive inexorable force that seems to crush everything in its way

examples.text: The marketing juggernaut flattened smaller competitors across every regional market it entered.

origin.ko: 산스크리트어 jagannātha '세계의 주'에서 왔습니다. 인도 푸리의 축제에서 거대한 수레가 사람들에게 끌려가는 광경에서 '막을 수 없는 힘'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: lacking brilliance or vitality

examples.text: The actor gave a lackluster performance in his latest film.

origin.ko: lack(부족)과 luster(광택)가 합쳐진 말입니다. 윤기가 없으니 '생기 없는'입니다.

senses.en: someone who takes more time than necessary; someone who lags behind

examples.text: Regulators warned that industry laggards would face fines if they missed the compliance deadline.

senses.en: wasting time

examples.text: Laggard progress on the bridge frustrated commuters and city officials alike.

origin.ko: lag(뒤처지다)에 -ard가 붙은 말입니다. 뒤처지는 사람을 뜻합니다.

senses.en: Of a piece of writing or a writing style: characteristic of or suitable for an inscription; embodying the precision and refinement of inscriptions on monuments; concise and stately.

examples.text: The obituary was a model of lapidary prose, every word chosen with care.

senses.en: an expert on precious stones and the art of cutting and engraving them

examples.text: The lapidary spent weeks cutting the rough sapphire into a flawless oval.

origin.ko: 라틴어 lapidārius '돌의, 석공'에서 왔고 lapis(돌)에서 나왔습니다. 돌에 새긴 비문처럼 간결한 문체를 뜻합니다.

senses.en: furiously angry

examples.text: willful stupidity makes him absolutely livid

senses.en: anemic looking from illness or emotion

examples.text: Livid with fear, the witness gripped the rail and could barely speak.

senses.en: discolored by coagulation of blood beneath the skin

examples.text: livid bruises

origin.ko: 라틴어 līvidus '푸르죽죽한'에서 왔습니다. 멍든 빛이 분노로 새파래진 얼굴로 번졌습니다.

senses.en: To speak in a disorganized or desultory manner; to babble or prattle.

examples.text: What are you maundering about? He's going out from here a free man and whole—he's not going to die.

senses.en: To wander or walk aimlessly.

examples.text: He maundered through the empty streets for hours, unable to decide where to go.

origin.ko: maund '구걸하다'에서 나온 말입니다.

senses.en: deserving reward or praise

examples.text: The soldier received a medal for meritorious service during the long campaign.

origin.ko: 라틴어 meritōrius에서 왔고 mereō '얻다, 자격이 있다'에서 나왔습니다.

senses.en: To spellbind; to enthrall.

examples.text: She mesmerized the audience with her tricks

senses.en: induce hypnosis in

examples.text: The stage performer claimed he could mesmerize any volunteer within seconds.

origin.ko: mesmerism(최면술)에서 거꾸로 만들어진 말에 -ize가 붙은 것입니다. 1829년에 처음 쓰였습니다.

senses.en: a striking change in appearance or character or circumstances

examples.text: The sleepy fishing village underwent a rapid metamorphosis into a bustling tourist resort.

senses.en: the marked and rapid transformation of a larva into an adult that occurs in some animals

examples.text: The metamorphosis of a tadpole into a frog takes several weeks.

origin.ko: 그리스어 metamórphōsis에서 왔고 metá(변화)와 morphḗ(모양)가 합쳐졌습니다. 모양이 바뀐다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: interpret in the wrong way

examples.text: It’s easy to misconstrue her silence as agreement.

origin.ko: 중세 영어에서 mis-(잘못)와 construe(해석하다)가 합쳐졌습니다. 뜻을 잘못 엮어 이해한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: One who shows extreme love and admiration for themself.

examples.text: The CEO, a notorious narcissist, took credit for every success and blamed others for failures.

origin.ko: 그리스 신화에서 자기 물에 비친 모습에 반한 나르키소스에 -ist가 붙은 말입니다.

senses.en: extremely wicked

examples.text: nefarious schemes

origin.ko: 라틴어 nefās '신의 법에 어긋나는 일'에서 왔습니다. 하늘의 법을 어기는 극악한 짓이라는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: make ineffective by counterbalancing the effect of

examples.text: Progress on the study has been negated by the lack of funds.

senses.en: To deny the existence, evidence, or truth of; to contradict.

examples.text: The new data negate the earlier claim that the drug reduces symptoms in older patients.

origin.ko: 라틴어 negō '부인하다, 거부하다'에서 왔습니다. 부정하여 효력을 없앤다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: Evoking a sense of the mystical, sublime, or transcendent; awe-inspiring.

examples.text: Hikers described the silent, mist-filled valley at dawn as a numinous place.

senses.en: evincing the presence of a deity

examples.text: a numinous wood

origin.ko: 라틴어 nūmen '신의 뜻, 신성'에서 왔습니다. 고개를 끄덕이는 신의 뜻이라는 데서 신비로운 기운을 가리킵니다.

senses.en: Hatred; dislike.

examples.text: His conduct brought him into odium, or, brought odium upon him.

senses.en: state of disgrace resulting from detestable behavior

examples.text: The governor bore the odium of the failed policy long after leaving office.

origin.ko: 라틴어 odium '증오'를 그대로 가져온 학술 차용어입니다.

senses.en: Miscellaneous items, especially the set of equipment required for a particular activity.

examples.text: He has an impressive collection of bicycling paraphernalia, but he doesn't ride very often anymore.

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어로 아내가 지참금 외에 가져오는 개인 재산을 가리켰습니다. 여기서 이런저런 개인 용품 일체가 되었습니다.

senses.en: able to cause disease

examples.text: While the environment is teeming with bacteria and fungi, most are not pathogenic.

origin.ko: patho-(병)와 -genic(~을 낳는)을 합친 말로, 병을 일으킨다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: A pedant; one who by teaching has become overly formal or pedantic in his or her ways; one who has the manner of a teacher.
senses.ko: 현학적인 교사, 훈장 티를 내는 사람

examples.text: The old pedagogue corrected every grammatical slip at the dinner table.

senses.en: someone who educates young people

examples.text: A gifted pedagogue, she made even difficult proofs seem approachable to beginners.

origin.ko: 그리스어 paidagōgós '아이를 이끄는 사람'에서 왔습니다. 아이를 이끌던 인도자가 지나치게 딱딱한 훈장 같은 교사를 뜻하게 되었습니다.

senses.en: great coolness and composure under strain

examples.text: The young diplomat answered the hostile questions with remarkable poise.

senses.en: To keep (something) in equilibrium; to hold suspended or balanced.

examples.text: The rock was poised precariously on the edge of the cliff.

origin.ko: 옛 프랑스어 pois '무게'에서 왔고, 라틴어 pendere '무게를 달다'가 원형입니다. 저울이 균형을 이루듯 침착하다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: The quality of being pompous; self-importance.

examples.text: With their super-formal tone and heavy use of jargon, legal documents are renowned for their pomposity.

origin.ko: 라틴어 pompōsitās에서 왔으며 pomp에 '~한 성질'이 붙은 말입니다. 행렬처럼 거창하게 구는 태도를 뜻합니다.

senses.en: occurring or coming into existence after a person's death

examples.text: a posthumous award

origin.ko: 라틴어 postumus('가장 나중의')에서 왔습니다. 아버지가 죽은 뒤에 태어난 아이를 가리키던 말입니다.

senses.en: pretending with intention to deceive

examples.text: She dropped the pretense of friendliness as soon as the cameras were turned off.

senses.en: a false or unsupportable quality

examples.text: She was a plain-speaking woman without a hint of pretense.

origin.ko: 라틴어 praetendere('앞에 펼치다')에서 왔습니다. 진짜 앞에 가면을 펼쳐 놓는 것이 가식입니다.

senses.en: strongly adhering to, or heedful of, guiding beliefs or moral rules

examples.text: The principled senator resigned rather than endorse a policy she considered unjust.

origin.ko: principle에 -ed가 붙은 말입니다. 라틴어 principium('첫 시작, 근본')에서 나온 원칙을 지닌 사람입니다.

senses.en: suppress or crush completely

examples.text: Riot police moved in to quell the disturbance before it spread to other districts.

senses.en: overcome or allay

examples.text: The company's swift response did little to quell public fears about the product.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 cwellan('죽이다')에서 왔습니다. 완전히 죽이듯 억눌러 진압한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: someone who collaborates with an enemy occupying force

examples.text: After the war, villagers shunned anyone suspected of being a quisling who had aided the occupiers.

origin.ko: 2차 대전 중 나치에 협력한 노르웨이 정치인 비드쿤 크비슬링의 이름에서 왔습니다. 1940년에 처음 쓰였습니다.

senses.en: fill something that had previously been emptied

examples.text: The charity worked to replenish the food bank's shelves before the winter holidays.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 replenir('다시 채우다')에서 왔고 라틴어 plenus('가득한')가 어원입니다.

senses.en: bringing or deserving severe rebuke or censure

examples.text: The council condemned the contractor's reprehensible decision to ignore basic safety rules.

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 reprehensibilis에서 왔고 reprehendere('붙잡아 꾸짖다')와 이어집니다. 꾸짖어 마땅하다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: A repetition of a phrase, a return to an earlier theme, or a second rendition or version of a song in a programme or musical.

examples.text: The film ends with a quiet reprise of the melody that opened the first scene.

senses.en: A recurrence or resumption of an action.

examples.text: The senator's speech was a reprise of arguments she had made throughout the campaign.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 reprendre('다시 잡다')에서 왔습니다. 앞의 주제를 다시 집어 드는 반복입니다.

senses.en: formally reject or disavow a formerly held belief, usually under pressure

examples.text: He retracted his earlier statements about his religion

senses.en: pull inward or towards a center

examples.text: The snail slowly retracted its horns into its shell when the child touched the leaf.

origin.ko: 라틴어 retrahere('뒤로 끌다')에서 왔습니다. 내놓은 말을 도로 끌어당겨 철회한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: An exaggeratedly enthusiastic or exalted expression of feeling in speech or writing.

examples.text: Her review was a rhapsody of praise for the restored cathedral and its luminous windows.

senses.en: (music) a free instrumental composition in one extended movement; typically emotional or exuberant in character

examples.text: The orchestra closed the evening with a lush rhapsody built on folk melodies.

origin.ko: 그리스어 rhapsōidia(서사시 낭송)에서 왔고, '노래를 꿰매 잇다'라는 이미지가 열광적 표현으로 바뀌었습니다.

senses.en: derive or receive pleasure from; get enjoyment from; take pleasure in

examples.text: After years of hard work, she paused to savor her victory.

senses.en: have flavor; taste of something

examples.text: His praise savored of condescension, leaving the young writer more insulted than flattered.

origin.ko: 라틴어 sapor(맛)에서 온 말로 알려져 있습니다. 맛을 음미한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: according with custom or propriety

examples.text: His behavior was seemly, as befits a gentleman.

origin.ko: 고대 노르드어 sœmiligr(어울리는)에서 왔습니다. 상황에 어울려 단정하다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: a broken piece of a brittle artifact

examples.text: Archaeologists pieced together the ancient vase from hundreds of pottery shards found at the site.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 sċeard(깨진 조각)에서 왔고 '벤 자국, 홈'과 이어집니다. 깨져 나간 날카로운 조각입니다.

senses.en: Characterized by a hissing or hushing sound such as the s or sh in sack or shack.

examples.text: The sibilant whisper of the audience grew louder as the lights dimmed on the stage.

origin.ko: 라틴어 sībilāre(쉿 소리를 내다)에서 왔습니다. 쉭쉭 하는 소리입니다.

senses.en: marked by great carelessness

examples.text: The slapdash renovation left the new kitchen with crooked cabinets and a leaking sink.

origin.ko: slap(철썩)과 dash(내던지다)가 합쳐진 말입니다. 철썩 내던지듯 대충 한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: suppress or constrain so as to lessen in intensity

examples.text: The army stifled the rebellion.

senses.en: impair the respiration of or obstruct the air passage of

examples.text: The heat was stifling the children.

origin.ko: 중세 영어 stuflen(숨이 막히다)에서 왔고 더 이전 어원은 불확실합니다. 숨통을 막아 억누른다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: unwilling to spend (money, time, resources, etc.)

examples.text: she practices economy without being stingy

senses.en: deficient in amount or quality or extent

examples.text: The stingy portions left the guests hungry, and the budget hotel offered only meager breakfasts.

origin.ko: sting의 방언형에서 온 것으로 추정되며 확실하지 않습니다.

senses.en: a sum of money allotted on a regular basis; usually for some specific purpose

examples.text: My stipend for doing public service is barely enough to cover living expenses.

origin.ko: 라틴어 stīpendium(병사의 급료)에서 왔습니다. 동전을 달아 지급하던 데서 정기 수당이 되었습니다.

senses.en: direct energy or urges into useful activities

examples.text: The poet sublimated her grief into a series of luminous elegies.

senses.en: make more subtle or refined

examples.text: Years of study helped sublimate his crude ambitions into a genuine scholarly vocation.

senses.en: change or cause to change directly from a solid into a vapor without first melting

examples.text: some salts sublime when heated

origin.ko: 라틴어 sublīmāre(들어 올리다)에서 왔습니다. 충동을 높은 활동으로 끌어올린다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: characterized by oppressive heat and humidity

examples.text: The battlefield—an undulating, parched, and dusty expanse—is lying under the sultry sun of a July afternoon.

senses.en: sexually exciting or gratifying

examples.text: a sultry look

origin.ko: swelter(찌는 듯이 덥다)의 옛 변형 sulter에 -y가 붙은 말입니다. 푹푹 찌는 무더위입니다.

senses.en: occurring or existing at the same time or having the same period or phase

examples.text: a synchronous set of clocks

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 synchronus에서 왔고 그리스어로 '시간을 함께하는'을 뜻합니다. 같은 때에 일어난다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: work hard

examples.text: Farmers toiled from dawn to dusk to bring in the harvest before the rains arrived.

senses.en: Labour, work, especially of a grueling nature.

examples.text: Years of unrelenting toil in the mines left him with scarcely any savings and failing health.

origin.ko: 앵글로노르만어 toiller('휘젓다')와 영어 tilyen('일하다')이 뒤섞인 것으로 보입니다. 휘젓듯 몸을 써서 일하는 모습이 '고생하다'입니다.

senses.en: cut short in duration

examples.text: Because of the storm, the festival ran a truncated schedule, with several performances cancelled outright.

senses.en: terminating abruptly by having or as if having an end or point cut off

examples.text: Erosion left the volcano with a truncated summit, flat where the peak once rose.

origin.ko: 라틴어 truncō('줄기만 남기고 자르다')에서 온 truncate의 분사형입니다.

senses.en: free from admixture

examples.text: The news of her recovery filled the family with unalloyed joy, untroubled by any lingering worry.

senses.en: smug self-serving earnestness

examples.text: The candidate delivered his promises with such oily unction that few voters believed a word.

senses.en: A religious or ceremonial anointing.

examples.text: The monarch's unction with sacred oil formed the central moment of the coronation.

senses.en: unpleasantly and excessively suave or ingratiating in manner or speech

examples.text: The unctuous salesman praised every detail of the client's taste while quietly raising the price.

senses.en: Having fat or oil present; fatty, greasy, oily.

examples.text: The unctuous broth coated the spoon and left a rich film on the lips.

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 ūnctuōsus('기름진')에서 왔고 unguō('기름을 바르다')와 이어집니다. 기름 바른 듯 번지르르한 태도가 '느끼하게 공손한'입니다.

senses.en: Practical and functional, present for use, not just for show.

examples.text: The architect favored a utilitarian design, with no ornament that did not serve a purpose.

senses.en: Pertaining to utilitarianism.

examples.text: A utilitarian approach to ethics judges actions by whether they maximize overall happiness.

origin.ko: utility에 -arian을 붙여 철학자 벤담이 만든 말입니다. 쓸모를 따진다는 뜻이 '실용적인'입니다.

senses.en: the psychological state of being irritated or annoyed

examples.text: She threw down her pen in vexation when the printer jammed for the third time.

senses.en: something or someone that causes anxiety; a source of unhappiness

examples.text: The endless paperwork was a constant vexation for the small business owner.

origin.ko: 라틴어 vexātiō('흔들어 괴롭힘')에서 왔고 vex에서 나온 말입니다.

senses.en: disposed to seek revenge or intended for revenge

examples.text: The vindictive manager fired anyone who had ever questioned his decisions.

origin.ko: 라틴어 vindicta('복수')에 -ive를 붙였습니다.

senses.en: someone who makes wine

examples.text: The local vintner opened his cellar to visitors every autumn after the grape harvest.

senses.en: someone who sells wine

examples.text: The vintner recommended a crisp white to go with the fish.

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 vīnētārius('포도주 상인')에서 왔고 vīnum('포도주')과 이어집니다.

senses.en: reduce in scope while retaining essential elements

examples.text: The publisher chose to abridge the nineteenth-century novel so that modern readers could finish it in a weekend.

senses.en: lessen, diminish, or curtail

examples.text: The court ruled that the new statute unlawfully abridged citizens' freedom of assembly.

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 abbreviare(짧게 만들다)에서 왔습니다. 글을 짧게 줄인다는 뜻으로 abbreviate와 같은 뿌리입니다.

senses.en: one who professes great sensitivity to the beauty of art and nature

examples.text: The aesthete declined the invitation, claiming that the ugly furniture would spoil his evening.

origin.ko: 그리스어 aisthētēs(지각하는 사람)에서 왔습니다. 아름다움을 예민하게 느끼는 사람입니다.

senses.en: The process of amalgamating; a mixture, merger or consolidation.

examples.text: The amalgamation of the three small colleges created the region's largest university.

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 amalgamatio에서 왔고 amalgam(합금)과 같은 뿌리입니다. 섞어 하나로 만드는 과정입니다.

senses.en: so extremely old as seeming to belong to an earlier period

examples.text: The agency still relied on antiquated computers that frequently failed during busy periods.

origin.ko: antiquate에 -ed가 붙은 말로, 라틴어 antiquus(옛날의)에서 나왔습니다. 낡아서 시대에 뒤떨어졌다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: a large fleet

examples.text: An armada of fishing boats set out at dawn to protest the new quotas.

origin.ko: 스페인어 armada(무장한 선단)에서 왔고 라틴어 armare(무장하다)에서 나왔습니다. army와 같은 뿌리입니다.

senses.en: Complete; downright; utter.

examples.text: The pundit dismissed the proposal as arrant nonsense.

origin.ko: errant(떠돌아다니는)의 변형입니다. '떠돌이 악당'처럼 나쁜 말과 어울려 '순전한'이라는 강조어가 되었습니다.

senses.en: marked by practical hardheaded intelligence

examples.text: an astute tenant always reads the small print in a lease

origin.ko: 라틴어 astutus(교활한, 약삭빠른)에서 왔고 astus(꾀)에서 나왔습니다.

senses.en: make automatic or control or operate automatically

examples.text: We saved time and money by automating the process.

origin.ko: automation(자동화)에서 거꾸로 만들어진 말입니다. 그리스어 automatos(스스로 움직이는)가 바탕입니다.

senses.en: prevent the occurrence of; prevent from happening; to protect from or to keep away anything undesirable; to ward off

examples.text: How can the danger be averted?

senses.en: turn away or aside

examples.text: I averted my eyes while my friend typed in her password.

origin.ko: 라틴어 avertere(돌려 버리다)에서 왔습니다. 눈이나 사건을 딴 쪽으로 돌려 피한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: an auxiliary activity

examples.text: Gardening is a wholesome avocation that encourages appreciation for nature and concern for the preservation and enhancement of our environment.

origin.ko: 라틴어 avocatio(딴 데로 불러냄)에서 왔습니다. 본업에서 불려 나와 하는 일이 '취미, 부업'입니다.

senses.en: discourage or frighten with threats or a domineering manner; intimidate

examples.text: The manager browbeat his staff into working weekends without any extra pay.

origin.ko: brow(이마, 눈썹)와 beat(치다)가 합쳐진 말입니다. 매서운 눈초리로 상대를 짓누르는 모습입니다.

senses.en: To lurch or sway violently from side to side.

examples.text: The overloaded cart careened down the muddy hill, shedding crates at every bend.

senses.en: To move swiftly and in an uncontrolled way.

examples.text: The runaway truck careened through the intersection before crashing into a wall.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 carène('배의 용골')에서 왔고 라틴어 carīna(용골)까지 거슬러 갑니다. 배를 한쪽으로 기울이던 데서 '기우뚱거리다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: conspicuously and offensively loud; given to vehement outcry

examples.text: a clamorous fire alarm

senses.en: Insistently expressing a desire for something.

examples.text: Clamorous voters demanded that the council reverse its decision before the next election.

origin.ko: clamor에 -ous가 붙은 말이고, 라틴어 clāmōrōsus와 비교됩니다. 아우성이 가득하다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: change from a liquid to a thickened or solid state

examples.text: In cheese making, milk coagulates into curds that become cheese.

origin.ko: 라틴어 coāgulō('응고시키다')에서 왔고, cōgō(함께 몰아넣다)와 관련됩니다. 흩어진 것을 한데 몰아 굳히는 이미지입니다.

senses.en: An addition or supplement that explains, modifies, or revokes a will or part of one.

examples.text: She added a codicil to her will leaving the family cottage to her nephew.

origin.ko: 라틴어 cōdicillus에서 왔고, cōdex(책)의 지소형입니다. 유언장에 덧붙이는 '작은 서판'입니다.

senses.en: worthy of high praise

examples.text: The volunteers showed commendable restraint while working through the long, exhausting night.

origin.ko: 라틴어 commendabilis에서 왔고, commendare는 manus(손)와 dare(주다)에서 갈라졌습니다. 손에 맡길 만큼 믿음직하다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: A convergence or combination of forces, people, or things.

examples.text: The confluence of our skills resulted in a successful home renovation project.

senses.en: a place where things merge or flow together (especially rivers)

examples.text: Pittsburgh is located at the confluence of the Allegheny and Monongahela rivers

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 cōnfluentia('함께 흐름')에서 왔습니다. 강물이 합쳐지는 모습입니다.

senses.en: summon into action or bring into existence, often as if by magic

examples.text: The smell of fresh bread conjured memories of her grandmother's kitchen.

senses.en: ask for or request earnestly

examples.text: The old priest conjured the villagers to forgive one another before the winter began.

origin.ko: 라틴어 coniūrō('함께 맹세하다, 공모하다')에서 왔습니다. 주문으로 영혼을 불러내는 뜻으로 이어졌습니다.

senses.en: Unnatural, forced; artificial, or unrealistic.

examples.text: Critics found the plot contrived, with coincidences piling up to force a happy ending.

senses.en: diffusing warmth and friendliness

examples.text: Since then, though, discussions have become more collaborative and cordial.

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 cordiālis('심장의')에서 왔습니다. 마음에서 우러난 따뜻함입니다.

senses.en: Any similar contrasting element in a work of art.

examples.text: The comic scenes serve as a counterpoint to the play's otherwise grim tone.

senses.en: a musical form involving the simultaneous sound of two or more melodies

examples.text: Bach's mastery of counterpoint allows several independent melodies to weave together seamlessly.

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 contrāpūnctum에서 왔습니다. 음표(점) 맞은편에 다른 음표를 대응시킨다는 데서 '대조 요소'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: To read text that is almost illegible or obscure.

examples.text: The archivist spent weeks trying to decipher the faded handwriting in the soldier's letters.

senses.en: To convert a code or cipher to plain text.

examples.text: Wartime analysts worked around the clock to decipher the enemy's intercepted radio messages.

origin.ko: de-와 cipher(암호)를 합친 말입니다. 암호를 풀어 '판독하다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: To search thoroughly and carefully for information, research, dig into, penetrate, fathom, trace out

examples.text: The biographer delved into decades of letters to understand the poet's troubled final years.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 delfan(땅을 파다)에서 왔습니다. 땅을 파듯 깊이 파고든다는 이미지입니다.

senses.en: To express disapproval of, protest or plead against.

examples.text: She deprecated any action which might disturb the peace.

senses.en: To belittle, depreciate.

examples.text: He deprecates any praise of his own merits.

origin.ko: 라틴어 dēprecor(재앙을 막아 달라고 빌다)에서 왔습니다. 악을 물리쳐 달라 비는 데서 '반대하다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: To fall outside of, or part from, some norm; to stray.

examples.text: His exhibition of nude paintings deviated from the norm.

senses.en: turn aside; turn away from

examples.text: The pilot deviated from the planned route to avoid a line of thunderstorms.

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 dēviāre(길에서 벗어나다)에서 왔습니다. 정해진 길을 벗어난다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: administer or bestow, as in small portions

examples.text: He is delighted to dispense a share of it to all the company.

senses.en: grant a dispensation; grant an exemption

examples.text: I was dispensed from this terrible task

origin.ko: 라틴어 dispendere(달아서 나누다)에서 왔습니다. 무게를 달아 조금씩 나누어 준다는 이미지입니다.

senses.en: a person who dissents from some established policy

examples.text: The exiled dissident continued to publish essays criticizing the government from abroad.

senses.en: disagreeing, especially with a majority

examples.text: The dissident faction within the party voted against the leadership's proposal.

origin.ko: 라틴어 dissideō(떨어져 앉다)에서 왔습니다. 다수와 따로 앉은 사람이 '반체제 인사'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: make false by mutilation or addition; as of a message or story

examples.text: In their articles, journalists sometimes distort the truth.

senses.en: twist and press out of shape

examples.text: The old glass distorted the reflection, stretching faces into strange, wavering shapes.

origin.ko: 라틴어 distorquēre(비틀다)에서 왔습니다. 비틀어 모양을 일그러뜨린다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: filled with or evoking sadness

examples.text: The doleful peal of the bell indicated another funeral was being held.

origin.ko: 중세 영어 dole(슬픔)에 -ful이 붙은 말입니다.

senses.en: mental infirmity as a consequence of old age; sometimes shown by foolish infatuations

examples.text: In his dotage the once-formidable judge could scarcely remember the names of his own grandchildren.

senses.en: Fondness or attentiveness, especially to an excessive degree.

examples.text: His dotage on his youngest daughter blinded him to her obvious faults.

origin.ko: 중세 영어 doten(멍청해지다)에 -age가 붙은 말입니다. 늙어 정신이 흐려진 상태를 뜻합니다.

senses.en: declining; growing less

examples.text: There is dwindling support for New Labour.

senses.en: a formal or authoritative proclamation

examples.text: The emperor's edict banned all public gatherings in the capital.

origin.ko: 라틴어 ēdictum(공포된 것)에서 왔습니다. 밖으로 말해 선포한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: a conceited and self-centered person

examples.text: The egotist dominated every conversation, steering it back to his own achievements.

origin.ko: 영어 ego(나)에 -ist가 붙었습니다. 늘 '나'만 내세우는 사람이라는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: someone who believes in rule by an elite group

examples.text: Opponents branded him an elitist who distrusted the judgment of ordinary voters.

origin.ko: elite(엘리트)에 그리스어 계열 접미사 -ist가 붙었습니다. 엘리트가 다스려야 한다고 믿는 사람입니다.

senses.en: not clear to the understanding

examples.text: prophetic texts so enigmatic that their meaning has been disputed for centuries

origin.ko: 그리스어 ainigmatikós에서 왔습니다. enigma(수수께끼)처럼 알 수 없다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: To lure; to attract by arousing desire or hope.

examples.text: I enticed the little bear into the trap with a pot of honey.

origin.ko: 속라틴어 *intitiāre(불을 붙이다)에서 고대 프랑스어를 거쳐 왔습니다. 욕망에 불을 붙여 꾄다는 이미지입니다.

senses.en: extremely painful
senses.ko: 극심한 고통을 주는, 견딜 수 없는

examples.text: After the accident he endured weeks of excruciating pain before the surgery finally brought relief.

origin.ko: 라틴어 excruciāre(고문하다)에서 왔고, cruc은 '십자가'입니다. 십자가형 같은 고통이라는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: making lively and cheerful

examples.text: Hiking to the summit at dawn was an exhilarating experience that none of us will forget.

origin.ko: 라틴어 hilaris(즐거운)에서 온 exhilarate에 -ing이 붙었습니다. 기분을 확 들뜨게 한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: marked by ostentation but often tasteless

examples.text: The singer was known for his flamboyant costumes and theatrical stage presence.

senses.en: elaborately or excessively ornamented

examples.text: The orator's flamboyant prose, crowded with metaphors and flourishes, exhausted his readers.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 flamboyer(불타오르다)에서 왔습니다. 불꽃처럼 눈에 띄게 화려하다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: a stroke of luck

examples.text: We've classified by a fluke; actually, the first goal was just a total fluke.

senses.en: collect or look around for (food)

examples.text: Bears forage for berries and roots throughout the autumn to build up their fat reserves.

senses.en: bulky food like grass or hay for browsing or grazing horses or cattle

examples.text: A dry summer left the ranchers short of forage for their herds.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 fourage(마소의 먹이)에서 왔습니다. 먹이를 구하러 다니는 데서 '뒤지고 찾아다니다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: a person from whom you are descended

examples.text: The museum preserves letters written by the family's forebears more than two centuries ago.

origin.ko: fore(앞의)와 beer(~로 존재하는 사람)가 합쳐졌습니다. 먼저 존재했던 사람, 곧 조상입니다.

senses.en: a mural done with watercolors on wet plaster

examples.text: Restorers spent years cleaning the Renaissance fresco that covers the chapel's entire ceiling.

origin.ko: 이탈리아어 fresco에서 왔고 영어 fresh와 뿌리가 같은 말입니다. 게르만어 '신선한'이 어원입니다.

senses.en: give something useful or necessary to

examples.text: The witness furnished investigators with documents that proved the company had falsified its records.

senses.en: provide or equip with furniture

examples.text: They furnished the apartment with secondhand tables and a few threadbare rugs.

origin.ko: 프랑크어 *frumjan '완수하다'에서 고대 프랑스어 furnir를 거쳐 왔습니다. 필요한 것을 마련해 준다는 뜻으로 이어졌습니다.

senses.en: Any ploy or stratagem.

examples.text: Their promise to lower taxes is clearly an election-year gambit.

senses.en: an opening remark intended to secure an advantage for the speaker

examples.text: She began the negotiation with a bold gambit, offering to waive the penalty clause.

origin.ko: 이탈리아어 gambetto '다리 걸기'에서 왔고 gamba(다리)에서 나왔습니다. 상대를 넘어뜨리는 수가 '책략'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: To ponder and intensely evaluate a problem; to struggle to deal with.

examples.text: Economists continue to grapple with the question of why wages have stagnated despite rising productivity.

senses.en: to grip or seize, as in a wrestling match

examples.text: the two men grappled with each other for several minutes

origin.ko: 중세영어 '붙잡다'에서 왔고 grab에 -le이 붙은 모양입니다. 움켜쥐고 맞붙어 씨름하는 이미지입니다.

senses.en: unpleasantly harsh or grating in sound

examples.text: His grating laugh echoed through the quiet library and drew annoyed glances from every table.

senses.en: a barrier that has parallel or crossed bars blocking a passage but admitting air

examples.text: A rusted grating covered the drain at the bottom of the narrow alley.

senses.en: a complaint about a (real or imaginary) wrong that causes resentment and is grounds for action

examples.text: Workers presented a list of grievances about unpaid overtime to the management.

senses.en: a resentment strong enough to justify retaliation

examples.text: He nursed a bitter grievance against his former partner for years.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 grever '괴롭히다'에서 왔고, 라틴어 gravō(짐 지우다)가 뿌리입니다. 마음을 짓누르는 부담이 '불만'입니다.

senses.en: To complain or grumble.

examples.text: Employees grouse about the new parking rules but rarely take their concerns to management.

senses.en: Free from guile; honest but naive.

examples.text: Her guileless questions exposed the flaws in the plan that experts had overlooked.

origin.ko: guile(간계)에 -less(없는)가 붙은 말입니다. 속임수가 없으니 순진하고 꾸밈없습니다.

senses.en: naive and easily deceived or tricked

examples.text: Scammers target gullible retirees with promises of guaranteed investment returns.

origin.ko: gull(속이다)에 -ible이 붙은 말로 봅니다. 중세영어 gull(깃털 안 난 새끼 새, 바보)에서 왔다는 설도 있습니다.
