senses.en: To traumatize or disturb; to torment, distress or vex.

examples.text: The memory of the shipwreck continued to harrow the survivors long after they returned home.

senses.en: draw a harrow over (land)

examples.text: The farmers harrow the field in early spring before sowing the seed.

origin.ko: 중세영어 harwe '써레(땅 긁는 농기구)'에서 왔습니다. 써레로 땅을 긁듯 마음을 헤집는 데서 '괴롭히다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: extremely painful

examples.text: The documentary offers a harrowing account of the family's escape across the war-torn border.

origin.ko: harrow(괴롭히다)에 -ing가 붙은 말입니다. 마음을 갈가리 긁어 놓을 만큼 고통스럽다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: cause to feel shame; hurt the pride of

examples.text: He humiliated his colleague by criticising him in front of the boss

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 humiliō '낮추다'에서 왔고 humus(땅)가 뿌리입니다. 땅바닥으로 끌어내리듯 창피를 줍니다.

senses.en: bestow a quality on

examples.text: The sun imparts warmth.

senses.en: To make known; to show (by speech, writing etc.).

examples.text: The veteran teacher worked tirelessly to impart her knowledge of history to a new generation of students.

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 impartiō에서 왔습니다. 안으로(in) 나누어(part) 준다는 데서 성질을 '부여하다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: The lack of respect for a god or something sacred.

examples.text: Villagers condemned the playwright's impiety after his satire mocked the most sacred rituals of the church.

origin.ko: 라틴어 impietas에서 왔습니다. in-(없는)과 pietas(경건함)가 합쳐져 경건함이 없는 상태입니다.

senses.en: total lack of meaning or ideas

examples.text: The inanity of the talk show's banter left viewers wondering why they had bothered to tune in at all.

senses.en: Something that is inane.

examples.text: Working in any bureaucracy means being bedeviled by inanities daily.

origin.ko: 라틴어 inānitās '텅 빈 상태'에서 프랑스어를 거쳐 왔습니다. 속이 텅 비어 '무의미함'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: slow and apathetic

examples.text: After the heavy meal, the guests lay inert on the sofas, too sleepy to continue the conversation.

senses.en: having only a limited ability to react chemically; chemically inactive

examples.text: Argon is an inert gas, so it is often used to protect metals during welding.

senses.en: unable to move or resist motion

examples.text: The inert body of the fallen tree blocked the narrow mountain road for two days.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 inerte를 거쳐 라틴어 iners '활동하지 않는'에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: reciprocal action and reaction

examples.text: The novel explores the subtle interplay between memory and identity across three generations of one family.

origin.ko: inter-(서로)와 play(작용)가 합쳐진 말입니다. 서로 주고받는 작용을 뜻합니다.

senses.en: To put in jeopardy, to threaten.

examples.text: This mission is too important for me to allow you to jeopardize it.

senses.en: a surgical knife with a pointed double-edged blade; used for punctures and small incisions

examples.text: The surgeon opened the abscess with a single quick stroke of the lancet.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 lancete에서 왔고 lance(창)에 작음을 뜻하는 -et이 붙었습니다. 작은 창 같은 수술칼입니다.

senses.en: The art or craft of compiling, writing, and editing dictionaries.

examples.text: Modern lexicography relies on vast digital corpora to track how words actually change in use.

origin.ko: lexico-(단어)와 -graphy(기록)가 합쳐진 말입니다. 단어를 적어 사전을 만드는 일입니다.

senses.en: find repugnant

examples.text: I absolutely loathe this place.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 lāþian에서 왔고 loath와 같은 뿌리입니다. 혐오스럽게 여긴다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: act between parties with a view to reconciling differences

examples.text: Negotiators managed to mediate a ceasefire.

senses.en: To act as an intermediary causal or communicative agent; to convey.

examples.text: Hormones mediate the body's response to stress by carrying signals between distant organs.

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 mediō '가운데 있다'에서 왔고 medius(가운데)에서 나왔습니다. 양쪽 사이 가운데에 선다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: expressing one thing in terms normally denoting another

examples.text: The poet's storm is metaphorical, standing for the turmoil in the speaker's marriage.

origin.ko: 그리스어 metaphorá(metaphor)에서 파생된 말입니다. 한 사물의 뜻을 다른 것으로 옮겨 나른다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: a slight but appreciable amount

examples.text: The sauce needs a mite more salt before it is ready to serve.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 mīte '작은 벌레'에서 왔습니다. 아주 작은 것이라는 데서 '소량'을 뜻하게 되었습니다.

senses.en: lasting for a markedly brief time

examples.text: A momentary lapse in concentration cost the pianist the final bars of the piece.

origin.ko: 라틴어 mōmentum은 '아주 짧은 시간, 순간'이라는 뜻이고, 여기서 '순간적인'이 나왔습니다.

senses.en: A suspension of an ongoing activity.

examples.text: Canada may put a moratorium on cloning for research.

senses.en: a legally authorized postponement before some obligation must be discharged

examples.text: The government declared a moratorium on student loan payments during the economic emergency.

origin.ko: 라틴어 mora '지체'에서 나온 말로, 어떤 일을 미루어 잠시 멈춘다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: To undergo dramatic change in a seamless and barely noticeable fashion.

examples.text: The small neighborhood bakery gradually morphed into a nationwide chain.

origin.ko: 동사 metamorphose(변신하다)가 줄어든 말입니다. 그리스어 morphḗ는 '모양'입니다.

senses.en: make ineffective by counterbalancing the effect of

examples.text: Her optimism neutralizes his gloom

senses.en: make politically neutral and thus inoffensive

examples.text: The treaty neutralized the small republic

origin.ko: 프랑스어 neutraliser에서 왔습니다. neutral에 -ize가 붙어 어느 쪽에도 기울지 않게 만든다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: Quick and light in movement or action.

examples.text: He was too nimble for the assailant and easily escaped his grasp.

senses.en: Quickwitted and alert.

examples.text: He has a nimble mind and can improvise in any situation.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 niman '잡다'에서 왔습니다. 재빨리 붙잡고 반응하는 데서 '민첩한'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: Attempting to establish or prescribe a norm.

examples.text: normative grammar

senses.en: Conforming to a norm or norms.

examples.text: normative behaviour

origin.ko: 라틴어 norma '기준'에 -ative가 붙은 말로, 표준을 정해 제시한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: Greatly different from common experience; bizarre, outrageous, strange.

examples.text: The rock star wore black with outlandish pink and green spiked hair.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 ūtlendisc '외국의'에서 왔습니다. 자기 땅 바깥 것이라는 뜻에서 낯설고 기이하다가 되었습니다.

senses.en: someone opposed to violence as a means of settling disputes

examples.text: As a committed pacifist, she refused to join the army even when conscription was introduced.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 pacifiste에서 왔으며, pacific(평화로운)에 -ist가 붙었습니다.

senses.en: A short narrative illustrating a lesson (usually religious/moral) by comparison or analogy.

examples.text: The teacher used a parable about a lost sheep to illustrate forgiveness.

origin.ko: 그리스어 parabolḗ '비교'에서 왔습니다. 두 가지를 나란히 놓고 견주어 교훈을 주는 이야기입니다.

senses.en: of or relating to pedagogy

examples.text: The school adopted a new pedagogical approach that emphasizes discussion over lectures.

origin.ko: pedagogy(교육학)에 -ical이 붙은 말로, 그리스어 '아이를 이끄는' 일에서 나왔습니다.

senses.en: Constantly complaining, especially in a childish way due to insignificant matters; fretful, whiny.

examples.text: Due to the long wait, there were several peevish patients in the doctor’s waiting room.

senses.en: disturb in mind or make uneasy or cause to be worried or alarmed

examples.text: She was rather perturbed by the news that her father was seriously ill

senses.en: throw into great confusion or disorder

examples.text: Fundamentalists threaten to perturb the social order

origin.ko: 라틴어 perturbāre '완전히 어지럽히다'에서 왔고, turbō는 '휘젓다'입니다. 마음을 휘저어 불안하게 한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: someone who makes charitable donations intended to increase human well-being

examples.text: The philanthropist donated millions to build a new children's hospital.

origin.ko: philanthropy에 -ist가 붙은 말로, 인류를 사랑하는 마음으로 베푸는 사람입니다.

senses.en: An abundance; a full supply.

examples.text: Mankind's old greatness was created in scarcity. But what may we expect from plenitude?

origin.ko: 라틴어 plēnitūdō '가득 참'에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: a statement made about the future

examples.text: The economist's gloomy prognostication proved far too pessimistic once exports began to recover.

senses.en: a sign of something about to happen

examples.text: The fever death-rate in May and June was abnormally high, a sure prognostication of the coming storm.

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 prognosticatio에서 왔습니다. 그리스어 '미리 앎'에서 나온 말로, 미래에 대한 예측을 뜻합니다.

senses.en: a person who pleads for a cause or propounds an idea

examples.text: She was an early proponent of renewable energy long before it became fashionable.

origin.ko: 라틴어 prōpōnere('앞에 내놓다')의 현재분사에서 왔습니다. 주장을 앞에 내놓고 지지하는 사람입니다.

senses.en: power to influence or coerce

examples.text: The ancient empire's puissance made neighboring kingdoms reluctant to challenge it.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 puissant('힘 있는')에서 왔습니다. 라틴어 posse('할 수 있다')와 이어지며 힘을 뜻합니다.

senses.en: a development that complicates a situation

examples.text: the court's decision had many unforeseen ramifications

senses.en: the act of branching out or dividing into branches

examples.text: Botanists studied the ramification of the root system across several soil types.

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 rāmificātiō에서 왔고 rāmus('가지')와 '만들다'가 합쳐졌습니다. 나뭇가지처럼 갈라진 복잡한 결과입니다.

senses.en: Full of rancor; bitter; unforgiving.

examples.text: rancorous speech

origin.ko: rancor('깊은 원한')에 -ous가 붙은 말입니다. 라틴어 rancor는 '썩음'에서 '원한'이 된 말입니다.

senses.en: summarize briefly

examples.text: Before taking questions, the lecturer recapitulated the main arguments of the previous three sessions.

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 recapitulāre에서 왔습니다. capitulum('머리, 요점')을 다시 짚는다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: to say, state, or perform again

examples.text: The spokesman reiterated that the government would not negotiate with the kidnappers under any circumstances.

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 reiterāre('되풀이하다')에서 왔고 iterum('다시')에서 나왔습니다. 같은 말을 다시 한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: part with a possession or right

examples.text: The aging founder was reluctant to relinquish control of the company to his younger daughter.

senses.en: release, as from one's grip

examples.text: The climber slowly relinquished his grip on the rope as the rescuers took his weight.

origin.ko: 라틴어 relinquere('뒤에 남기고 떠나다')에서 왔습니다. 가진 것을 두고 떠나 포기한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: firm in purpose or belief; characterized by firmness and determination

examples.text: stood resolute against the enemy

origin.ko: 라틴어 resolūtus('풀려난')에서 왔고 resolvere('풀다')의 과거분사입니다. 의문이 풀려 결심이 굳은 상태입니다.

senses.en: serving to bring to mind

examples.text: The poem's simple images are resonant with memories of the poet's childhood.

senses.en: characterized by resonance

examples.text: a resonant voice

origin.ko: 라틴어 resonāre('다시 울리다')의 현재분사에서 왔습니다. 마음에 메아리처럼 되울려 떠올리게 합니다.

senses.en: a fee charged in advance to retain the services of someone

examples.text: The firm paid the consultant a monthly retainer to remain available for urgent questions.

senses.en: a person working in the service of another (especially in the household)

examples.text: The old retainer had served the family faithfully for more than forty years.

origin.ko: retain('붙들어 두다')에 -er가 붙은 말입니다. 전문가를 계속 붙들어 두려고 미리 내는 선임료입니다.

senses.en: take revenge for a perceived wrong

examples.text: The country threatened to retaliate with tariffs if the trade restrictions were not lifted.

origin.ko: 라틴어 retāliāre('똑같이 갚다')에서 왔습니다. 당한 만큼 되돌려 갚는다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: regard with feelings of respect and reverence; consider hallowed or exalted or be in awe of

examples.text: Students revered the old professor, treating his every comment as a pearl of wisdom.

origin.ko: 라틴어 revereor('경외하다')에서 온 프랑스어 révérer에서 왔습니다. 두려울 만큼 높여 숭배한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: Widespread, common, prevalent, current (mainly of unpleasant or harmful things).

examples.text: Rumors were rife that the factory was about to shut down.

senses.en: Full of (mostly unpleasant or harmful things).

examples.text: Many post-colonial governments were rife with lawlessness and corruption.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 rīfe(풍부한, 흔한)에서 왔습니다. 풍부함이 점점 나쁜 것의 만연이라는 뜻으로 굳었습니다.

senses.en: the quality of being valid and rigorous

examples.text: Reviewers praised the study for its methodological rigor and its careful handling of confounding variables.

senses.en: excessive sternness

examples.text: The rigor of the new regime left the prisoners with little hope of leniency.

senses.en: something hard to endure

examples.text: The explorers were unprepared for the rigors of an Arctic winter.

origin.ko: 라틴어 rigor(뻣뻣함, 혹독함)에서 왔습니다. 뻣뻣하게 물러서지 않는 태도가 엄밀함이 되었습니다.

senses.en: Rosy; optimistic.

examples.text: Nothing could have seemed more assured and roseate than her professional future.

senses.en: Like the rose flower; pink; rosy.

examples.text: The mountains glowed a roseate hue in the first light of dawn.

origin.ko: 장미(rose)에 -ate가 붙어 '장밋빛의'가 되었고, 거기서 낙관적이라는 뜻이 나왔습니다.

senses.en: an overwhelming defeat

examples.text: The election became a rout, with the incumbent party losing nearly every contested seat.

senses.en: defeat disastrously

examples.text: The home team routed its rivals in the final, winning by more than thirty points.

senses.en: cause to flee

examples.text: rout out the fighters from their caves

origin.ko: 라틴어 rumpere(부수다)에서 온 프랑스어 route(패주)에서 왔습니다. 진영이 깨져 흩어지는 완패입니다.

senses.en: lack of respect accompanied by a feeling of intense dislike

examples.text: He was held in contempt by colleagues, who treated his proposals with open scorn.

senses.en: To reject, turn down with disdain.

examples.text: He scorned her romantic advances.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 escharnir(조롱하다)에서 왔습니다. 정확한 어원은 불확실합니다.

senses.en: cut off from a whole

examples.text: The storm severed the power lines, leaving the town without electricity for three days.

senses.en: set or keep apart

examples.text: After he graduated, he severed all links to his family.

origin.ko: 라틴어 separāre(분리하다)에서 왔습니다. 따로 떼어 잘라낸다는 뜻이며 separate와 같은 뿌리입니다.

senses.en: Special or pronounced concern or attention.

examples.text: The nurse treated the elderly patient with a solicitude that touched the whole family.

senses.en: a feeling of excessive concern

examples.text: Her constant solicitude about his health began to feel smothering rather than kind.

origin.ko: 라틴어 sollicitūdō(불안)에서 왔습니다. 마음이 쓰이는 상태에서 세심한 배려가 되었습니다.

senses.en: a laborer who loads and unloads vessels in a port

examples.text: The stevedores worked through the night to unload the grain freighter before the storm arrived.

origin.ko: 스페인어 estibador(짐을 싣는 사람)에서 왔고 '빽빽이 채워 넣다'라는 뜻의 라틴어와 이어집니다. 배에 짐을 채워 넣는 인부입니다.

senses.en: mark with striae or striations

examples.text: Glaciers striate the bedrock as they drag stones slowly across it.

senses.en: marked with stria or striations

examples.text: The striate muscle fibers appeared as fine parallel bands under the microscope.

origin.ko: 라틴어 strio(홈을 파다)에서 왔습니다. 줄무늬를 낸다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: old; no longer valid or fashionable

examples.text: The superannuated regulations had not been revised since the telegraph era.

senses.en: too old to be useful

examples.text: The factory kept a few superannuated machines running long after they should have been scrapped.

origin.ko: 라틴어 superannuatus(한 해 넘은)에서 왔습니다. 나이가 차서 낡고 구식이 되었다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: To cause to fail; to frustrate, to prevent.

examples.text: The police thwarted the would-be assassin.

origin.ko: 고대 노르드어 þvert('가로지르는')에서 왔습니다. 앞길을 가로막는다는 이미지에서 '좌절시키다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: Free from emotional or mental disturbance.

examples.text: After the retreat she returned to work with a tranquil mind and a clearer sense of her priorities.

senses.en: (of a body of water) free from disturbance by heavy waves

examples.text: At dawn the tranquil lake reflected the surrounding hills without a single ripple.

origin.ko: 라틴어 tranquillus에서 왔고 quiēs('휴식, 고요')와 이어집니다. 마음이 고요히 쉬는 상태가 '평온한'입니다.

senses.en: To pass beyond the limits of something.

examples.text: We cannot transcend what we refuse to face.

senses.en: To surpass, as in intensity or power; to excel.

examples.text: Her final performance transcended anything the critics had expected from so young a pianist.

origin.ko: 라틴어 transcendō('넘어 올라가다')에서 왔습니다. 벽을 타고 넘는 이미지가 '초월하다'입니다.

senses.en: characterized by unrest or disorder or insubordination

examples.text: The tumultuous decade saw three governments fall and the currency lose most of its value.

senses.en: Characterized by loud, confused noise.

examples.text: The winning goal drew a tumultuous roar from the stadium crowd.

origin.ko: 라틴어 tumultuōsus('소란스러운')에서 왔고 tumultus에 '~이 가득한' 뜻의 접미사가 붙었습니다.

senses.en: large deep serving dish with a cover; for serving soups and stews

examples.text: The hostess ladled steaming bisque from a silver tureen into each guest's bowl.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 terrine에서 온 terrene이 변한 말입니다. 원래 흙으로 빚은 그릇이라는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: Inflexible and unwilling to negotiate or make concessions.

examples.text: The union took an uncompromising stance, rejecting every proposal that cut pensions even slightly.

origin.ko: un-과 compromising('타협하는')의 결합입니다. 타협하지 않으니 '완고한'입니다.

senses.en: To undermine.

examples.text: The mayor's own remarks undercut the credibility of the report his office had commissioned.

senses.en: To sell (something) at a lower price, or to work for lower wages, than a competitor.

examples.text: Foreign manufacturers undercut local producers by selling the same goods at half the price.

origin.ko: under와 cut의 합성어입니다. 밑을 잘라내 지탱을 약하게 만드는 모습입니다.

senses.en: Restrained and unpretentious.

examples.text: The hotel's understated elegance appealed to guests who disliked gaudy displays of wealth.

senses.en: disturb the composure of

examples.text: The sudden silence in the courtroom unnerved the young attorney in the middle of her argument.

senses.en: unwilling to submit to authority

examples.text: The substitute teacher struggled to control an unruly class that ignored every instruction.

senses.en: noisy and lacking in restraint or discipline

examples.text: Police gathered to contain the unruly mob outside the stadium after the match.

origin.ko: 중세 영어 unruly('불안한')로, un-과 rule, -ly의 결합입니다. 규칙을 따르지 않아 '다루기 힘든'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: cancel officially

examples.text: The appeals court vacated the earlier ruling after finding that the trial judge had misapplied the law.

senses.en: leave behind empty; move out of

examples.text: You must vacate your office by tonight

senses.en: To leave an office or position.

examples.text: He vacated his coaching position because of the corruption scandal.

origin.ko: 라틴어 vacō('비어 있다')에서 왔습니다. 법에서 '무효로 하다'로 쓰이다가 '비우다'로 이어졌습니다.

senses.en: Possessing excessive vanity or unwarranted pride.

examples.text: The vainglorious king commissioned a hundred statues of himself to celebrate a minor victory.

origin.ko: 라틴어 vānus('빈')와 glōriōsus('영광스러운')의 결합입니다. 알맹이 없는 영광을 뽐내는 것입니다.

senses.en: An attractive appearance that covers or disguises one's true nature or feelings, the veneer of culture.

examples.text: Beneath the veneer of politeness, the two rivals despised each other.

senses.en: coating consisting of a thin layer of superior wood glued to a base of inferior wood

examples.text: The cheap cabinet was finished with a walnut veneer to resemble solid wood.

origin.ko: 독일어 Furnier('얇은 판을 덧씌움')에서 왔습니다. 겉에만 얇게 덧씌운 판이 '허울'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: A robe, gown, or other article of clothing worn as an indication of office.

examples.text: The priest wore a white vestment during the ceremony.

origin.ko: 라틴어 vestīmentum('의복')에서 왔고 vest('옷')와 -ment의 결합입니다.

senses.en: resistant to guidance or discipline

examples.text: The wayward teenager ignored every curfew his parents set.

origin.ko: away와 -ward가 줄어든 말입니다. 길에서 벗어나 제멋대로 가는 것이 '제멋대로인'입니다.

senses.en: habitually disposed to disobedience and opposition

examples.text: The willful child refused every suggestion simply because it came from an adult.

senses.en: done by design

examples.text: The company was fined for willful violations of the safety code.

senses.en: select desirable parts from a group or list

examples.text: They winnowed the field to twelve.

senses.en: separate the chaff from grain by using air currents

examples.text: Farmers once winnowed the harvested wheat by tossing it into the breeze to blow away the chaff.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 windwian('바람에 까부르다')에서 왔고 wind('바람')와 이어집니다. 바람으로 쭉정이를 날려 곡식을 가리는 것이 '추려내다'입니다.

senses.en: a fear of foreigners or strangers

examples.text: The United States is not the only country where xenophobia pays dividends for politicians.

origin.ko: 그리스어 xénos('낯선 사람')와 phobía('공포')를 합친 말입니다.

senses.en: suffering from xenophobia; having abnormal fear or hatred of the strange or foreign

examples.text: The xenophobic rhetoric of the campaign alarmed immigrant communities across the country.

origin.ko: 그리스어 xénos('낯선')와 phóbos('공포')를 합친 말입니다.

senses.en: an oppressive power

examples.text: they threw off the yoke of domination

senses.en: link with or as with a yoke

examples.text: The treaty yoked the two economies together, making each dependent on the other.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 ġeoc('멍에')에서 왔고 '잇다'는 어근과 이어집니다. 소의 목을 묶는 멍에가 '속박'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: Being rough and coarse in manner or disposition; overly aggressive and causing irritation.

examples.text: His abrasive management style alienated colleagues who might otherwise have supported his reforms.

senses.en: causing abrasion

examples.text: Workers wore gloves because the abrasive surface of the stone could quickly scrape the skin.

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 abrasivus에서 왔습니다. 표면을 긁어내는 성질이 거슬리는 태도를 뜻하게 되었습니다.

senses.en: The causing of any sort of mysterious sudden transmutation.

examples.text: Through some alchemy of timing and talent, the unknown band became a national sensation overnight.

senses.en: a pseudoscientific forerunner of chemistry in medieval times

examples.text: Medieval practitioners of alchemy sought a method for turning lead into gold.

origin.ko: 아랍어 al-kīmiyāʔ에서 왔고 그리스어로 '금속을 합금하는 기술'입니다. 물질을 신비롭게 바꾸는 이미지로 이어졌습니다.

senses.en: report or maintain

examples.text: Prosecutors allege that the executive concealed losses from investors for several years.

origin.ko: 라틴어 allegare(사절로 보내다, 진술하다)에서 왔습니다. 근거를 내세워 말한다는 뜻에서 '주장하다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: aggressively self-assured

examples.text: an energetic assertive boy who was always ready to argue

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 assertivus에서 왔고 assert(단언하다)와 같은 뿌리입니다.

senses.en: Protection or patronage.

examples.text: The project took place under the auspices of the local church.

origin.ko: 라틴어 auspicium(새를 보고 치는 점)에서 왔습니다. 길조를 내려주는 보호라는 뜻이 되었습니다.

senses.en: resembling an uncle in kindness or indulgence

examples.text: The avuncular professor put nervous first-year students at ease with gentle jokes.

origin.ko: 라틴어 avunculus(외삼촌)에서 왔습니다. 삼촌처럼 너그럽다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: In a brusque manner; abruptly; rudely.

examples.text: The clerk answered the question brusquely and turned back to his paperwork.

senses.en: gold or silver in bars or ingots

examples.text: The central bank stores its bullion in vaults deep beneath the city.

origin.ko: 앵글로노르만어 bullion에서 왔고 기원은 불분명합니다. 녹이다를 뜻하는 프랑스어 bouillon과 관련이 있을 수 있습니다.

senses.en: a representation of a person that is exaggerated for comic effect

examples.text: The newspaper ran a caricature of the mayor with an enormous nose and tiny feet.

senses.en: A grotesque misrepresentation.

examples.text: Critics said the film offered a caricature of rural life, reducing farmers to simple-minded stereotypes.

origin.ko: 이탈리아어 caricatura에서 왔고, 라틴어 carrus(수레)에서 갈라졌습니다. character와는 관계가 없는 말입니다.

senses.en: involved with others in an activity that is unlawful or morally wrong

examples.text: Officials who looked the other way were seen as complicit in the fraud.

origin.ko: complicity에서 거꾸로 만들어진 말이며, explicit 같은 단어의 영향을 받았다고 봅니다.

senses.en: be in accord; be in agreement

examples.text: I do not concur that this is the best way forward.

senses.en: happen simultaneously

examples.text: The drought and the economic downturn concurred, making the crisis far harder to manage.

origin.ko: 라틴어 concurro('함께 달리다, 의견이 일치하다')에서 왔습니다. 같은 방향으로 달려 만난다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: To change from a liquid to solid state, perhaps due to cold; called to freeze in nontechnical usage.

examples.text: The gravy congealed on the plate while the guests lingered over their conversation.

senses.en: To make rigid or immobile.

examples.text: We must act before opposition to our plans congeals.

origin.ko: 라틴어 congelare에서 왔고 프랑스어를 거쳤습니다. 완전히 얼어 굳는다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: characterized by extreme care and great effort

examples.text: A conscientious editor, she checked every citation twice before the book went to print.

senses.en: guided by or in accordance with conscience or sense of right and wrong

examples.text: As a conscientious objector, he refused to take part in the war on moral grounds.

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 cōnscientiōsus에서 왔고 conscience(양심)와 같은 계통입니다. 양심에 비추어 꼼꼼하다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: an awkward clash

examples.text: A minor contretemps over seating arrangements delayed the start of the state dinner.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 contretemps를 그대로 빌려 온 말입니다.

senses.en: move or draw together at a certain location

examples.text: The crowd converged on the movie star

origin.ko: 라틴어 convergere에서 왔고, con-(함께)과 vergere(기울다)가 합쳐졌습니다. 한 점을 향해 함께 기운다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: to bear a reciprocal or mutual relation

examples.text: Doctrine and worship correlate as theory and practice.

origin.ko: cor-(함께)에 relate(관련짓다)가 붙은 말입니다. 서로를 함께 연결해 가져온다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: marked by skill in deception

examples.text: The crafty negotiator concealed his true aims until the other side had already conceded the key points.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 cræftiġ에서 왔고 craft(힘, 기술)에 -y가 붙었습니다. 원래 '힘센, 재주 있는'이었다가 '교활한'으로 기울었습니다.

senses.en: a sudden and violent collapse

examples.text: The merger turned into a financial debacle that cost thousands of employees their jobs.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 débâcler(빗장을 풀다)에서 왔습니다. 막아둔 것이 풀려 쏟아지듯 '총체적 붕괴'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: impairing the strength and vitality

examples.text: She suffered from a debilitating illness that left her too weak to climb stairs.

senses.en: Tact and propriety; the need for such tact.

examples.text: The ambassador handled the diplomatic crisis with great delicacy, avoiding any word that might offend.

senses.en: Something appealing, usually a pleasing food, especially a choice dish of a certain culture suggesting rarity and refinement.

examples.text: a Chinese delicacy

senses.en: Frailty of health or fitness.

examples.text: The delicacy of the premature infant's lungs required constant monitoring in the hospital.

origin.ko: 중세 영어 delicat(섬세한)에서 왔고 delicate에 -acy가 붙은 말입니다.

senses.en: to accuse or condemn or openly or formally or brand as disgraceful

examples.text: He denounced the government action

senses.en: To announce the termination of; especially a treaty or armistice.

examples.text: The new government threatened to denounce the trade agreement unless its terms were renegotiated.

origin.ko: 라틴어 dēnūntiō(알리다, 위협하다)에서 왔고 nūntius(전령)가 뿌리입니다. 공공연히 알리며 규탄하는 뜻이 되었습니다.

senses.en: an act of plundering and pillaging and marauding

examples.text: Coastal villages suffered repeated depredations at the hands of pirates throughout the century.

senses.en: (usually plural) a destructive action

examples.text: the depredations of age and disease

origin.ko: 라틴어 depraedatio에서 왔고 praeda(약탈품)가 뿌리입니다.

senses.en: lack of self-confidence

examples.text: Her diffidence kept her from speaking up, even when she knew the answer.

origin.ko: 라틴어 diffīdere(믿지 못하다)에서 왔습니다. 처음엔 남을 불신한다는 뜻이었고, 1650년대에 '자신을 못 믿는' 뜻이 되었습니다.

senses.en: characterized by care and perseverance in carrying out tasks

examples.text: a diligent search of the files

origin.ko: 라틴어 dīligō(아끼다, 문자대로 '골라내다')에서 왔습니다. 골라 아끼는 마음으로 정성을 들이는 모습입니다.

senses.en: To perceive, recognize, or comprehend with the mind; to descry.

examples.text: Critics could discern a hint of irony beneath the author's earnest prose.

senses.en: To distinguish something as being different from something else; to differentiate or discriminate.

examples.text: He was too young to discern right from wrong.

origin.ko: 라틴어 discernere(갈라 구별하다)에서 왔습니다. 체로 걸러 따로 나누는 이미지입니다.

senses.en: To vomit or spew, to discharge.

examples.text: The train disgorged hundreds of commuters onto the crowded platform.

senses.en: To surrender (stolen goods or money, for example) unwillingly.

examples.text: Regulators forced the firm to disgorge the profits it had made through insider trading.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 desgorger에서 왔습니다. 목구멍(gorge)에서 쏟아낸다는 이미지입니다.

senses.en: a comic verse of irregular measure

examples.text: he had heard some silly doggerel that kept running through his mind

senses.en: Any writing of crude composition.

examples.text: The campaign speeches devolved into patriotic doggerel that impressed few thoughtful listeners.

origin.ko: dog에 경멸 접미사 -rel이 붙은 것으로 봅니다. 개 수준의 시라는 느낌입니다.

senses.en: in an early stage of development

examples.text: an embryonic nation, not yet self-governing

origin.ko: 신라틴어 embryonicus에서 왔습니다. 배아(embryo)처럼 아직 초기 단계라는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: make improvements or corrections to

examples.text: The editor emended several misprints in the manuscript before it went to press.

origin.ko: 라틴어 ēmendāre(흠을 없애다)에서 왔습니다. mendum은 '흠, 오류'이며, 글의 오류를 고친다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: Payment for employment or an office; compensation for a job, which is usually monetary.

examples.text: The emoluments of the post included a house and a modest annual stipend.

origin.ko: 라틴어 ēmolumentum에서 고대 프랑스어를 거쳐 왔습니다. 일한 대가로 받는 보수를 뜻합니다.

senses.en: A political, cultural or social entity or part thereof that is completely surrounded by another.

examples.text: The Republic of San Marino is an enclave of Italy.

origin.ko: 속라틴어 *inclāvāre(안에 잠그다)에서 프랑스어를 거쳐 왔습니다. 다른 영토 안에 갇힌 땅을 뜻합니다.

senses.en: An illuminating realization or discovery, often resulting in a personal feeling of elation, awe, or wonder.

examples.text: It came to her in an epiphany what her life's work was to be.

origin.ko: 그리스어 epipháneia(나타남, 현현)에서 왔습니다. 진실이 갑자기 눈앞에 나타나는 순간을 뜻합니다.

senses.en: containing or characterized by error

examples.text: erroneous conclusions

origin.ko: 라틴어 erroneus(떠도는, 잘못된)에서 프랑스어를 거쳐 왔습니다. 옳은 길에서 벗어난 오류라는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: Having become a stranger, of one who formerly was close, as a relative, friend, lover, or spouse.

examples.text: He managed to become estranged from all of his friends.

senses.en: characterized by lightness and insubstantiality; as impalpable or intangible as air
senses.ko: 가볍고 섬세한, 이 세상 것 같지 않은

examples.text: The singer's ethereal voice seemed to float above the hushed cathedral.

senses.en: of heaven or the spirit

examples.text: The painter sought to capture an ethereal light descending from the heavens.

origin.ko: 그리스어 aithérios(높은 하늘의)에서 라틴어를 거쳐 왔습니다. 하늘의 에테르처럼 가볍고 실체가 없는 느낌입니다.

senses.en: a feeling of great (usually exaggerated) elation

examples.text: The euphoria of victory faded quickly once the hard work of governing began.

origin.ko: 그리스어 euphoríā(잘 견딤, 순조로움)에서 왔습니다. 몸이 잘 버티는 기분 좋은 상태가 '희열'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: Fair and impartial; unbiased; just.

examples.text: The questioners are not evenhanded in dealing with the candidates.

origin.ko: even(고른)과 handed(손을 쓰는)가 합쳐졌습니다. 양쪽에 고르게 손을 쓰는 데서 '공평한'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: a sudden unforeseen crisis (usually involving danger) that requires immediate action

examples.text: The mayor invoked special powers to deal with the exigency created by the flood.

senses.en: that which is required in a particular situation — usually used in plural.

examples.text: The trench maps used in the Great War resulted from the exigencies of war.

origin.ko: 라틴어 exigere(요구하다)에서 왔습니다. 당장 대처를 요구하는 긴급 상황입니다.

senses.en: To explain meticulously or in great detail.

examples.text: My homework is to explicate a poem.

origin.ko: 라틴어 explicāre(펼치다)에서 왔습니다. 접혀 있던 뜻을 하나하나 펼쳐 설명한다는 이미지입니다.

senses.en: still in existence; not extinct or destroyed or lost

examples.text: There are many narrow-gauge systems still extant.

origin.ko: 라틴어 extāre(밖으로 서 있다, 존재하다)에서 왔습니다. 사라지지 않고 우뚝 남아 있다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: a misconception resulting from incorrect reasoning

examples.text: It is a common fallacy that correlation between two events proves one caused the other.

origin.ko: 라틴어 fallācia(속임, 기만)에서 고대 프랑스어를 거쳐 왔습니다. fallere(속이다)가 바탕입니다.

senses.en: A show of ceremony or celebration.

examples.text: The town opened the new library with fanfare and a speech from the mayor.

senses.en: A flourish of trumpets or horns as to announce; a short and lively air performed on hunting horns during the chase.

examples.text: They played a short fanfare to announce the arrival of the king.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 fanfare(트럼펫 소리)를 그대로 빌려 왔습니다. 요란한 나팔 소리가 떠들썩한 환영의 뜻이 되었습니다.

senses.en: pathetically lacking in force or effectiveness

examples.text: The minister's feeble defense of the policy did little to calm an angry public.

senses.en: lacking bodily or muscular strength or vitality

examples.text: Though she appeared old and feeble, she could still throw a ball.

origin.ko: 라틴어 flēbilis(눈물 날 만한, 애처로운)에서 왔습니다. 눈물 나게 가련한 약함이 '힘없는'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: achieve something by means of trickery or devious methods

examples.text: He finagled a seat on the sold-out flight by charming the gate agent with a made-up story.

senses.en: subtly skillful handling of a situation

examples.text: The negotiator handled the tense talks with such finesse that both sides left satisfied.

senses.en: To handle or manage carefully or skilfully; to manipulate in a crafty way.

examples.text: The mayor finessed the budget dispute by promising each faction a small concession.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 finesse(섬세함)에서 왔고, fin(고운, 얇은)이 바탕입니다. 섬세하고 능란하게 다루는 솜씨를 뜻합니다.

senses.en: affecting extreme elegance in dress and manner

examples.text: The foppish courtier spent hours arranging his lace cuffs and powdered wig each morning.

senses.en: People of education and good breeding.

examples.text: The landed gentry of the county gathered at the manor each autumn for the hunt.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 genterie '귀족'에서 왔고, gent(좋은 가문 출신)에서 나온 말입니다.

senses.en: make ineffective or powerless

examples.text: The teachers were hamstrung by the overly rigid schedules

origin.ko: ham(오금)과 string(힘줄)의 합성어입니다. 오금 힘줄을 끊어 다리를 못 쓰게 한다는 뜻에서 '무력하게 만들다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: a person who works only for money

examples.text: The candidate dismissed his critics as hirelings of the industry lobby, paid to spread doubt.

origin.ko: 고대영어 hȳrling으로 hire(고용)에 -ling이 붙은 말입니다. 돈에 고용된 사람을 얕잡아 부릅니다.

senses.en: a vast multitude

examples.text: We were beset by a horde of street vendors who thought we were tourists and would buy their cheap souvenirs.

origin.ko: 튀르크어 ordu '군대 주둔지'에서 폴란드어, 독일어, 프랑스어를 거쳐 들어왔습니다. 유목 군대 무리에서 '큰 떼'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: Perfect, without faults, flaws or errors

examples.text: He grew up in Norway, but he writes impeccable English.

origin.ko: 라틴어 impeccabilis '죄를 짓지 않는'에서 왔습니다. 잘못할 수 없으니 '흠잡을 데 없는'입니다.

senses.en: Not in accordance with good policy.

examples.text: It would be impolitic for the senator to criticize his own party's leadership so close to the election.

origin.ko: in-(않는)에 politic(현명한, 정책에 맞는)이 붙은 말입니다. 좋은 정책에 맞지 않는다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: An unwelcome burden, presence, or obligation.

examples.text: She hated to ask for a ride, fearing it would be an imposition on her busy neighbor.

senses.en: the act of imposing something (as a tax or an embargo)

examples.text: The imposition of new tariffs angered farmers who relied heavily on exports to overseas markets.

origin.ko: 라틴어 impositio에서 왔습니다. 남의 위에 짐을 얹는 일이 '부담, 강요'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: the power of creative imagination

examples.text: The pyramids demonstrate the ingenuity of the ancient Egyptians.

origin.ko: 라틴어 ingenuitās에서 왔고 genius(타고난 재능)와 가까운 말입니다.

senses.en: an inquiry into the cause of an unexpected death

examples.text: The coroner opened an inquest to determine how the hiker had died on the remote mountain trail.

senses.en: An inquiry, typically into an undesired outcome

examples.text: After the humiliating defeat, the party held a bitter inquest into what had gone wrong.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 enqueste에서 왔고 라틴어 '묻다, 조사하다'와 이어집니다. 안을 파고들어 조사한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: Carelessness, heedlessness, indifference, or casual unconcern.

examples.text: He faced the angry board with an insouciance that only made its members angrier.

origin.ko: 프랑스어에서 왔고 in-(아닌)과 souciant(걱정하는)가 합쳐졌습니다. 걱정이 없는 태연함입니다.

senses.en: a person who takes part in an armed rebellion against the constituted authority (especially in the hope of improving conditions)

examples.text: Government troops pushed the insurgents out of the northern provinces after months of fighting.

senses.en: Rebellious, opposing authority.

examples.text: The insurgent provinces.

origin.ko: 라틴어 īnsurgō '~에 맞서 일어나다'에서 왔습니다. 권력에 맞서 일어서는 사람입니다.

senses.en: Great anger; wrath; keen resentment.

examples.text: The senator's remarks drew the ire of voters across the district.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어를 거쳐 라틴어 īra '분노'에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: A route or proposed route of a journey.

examples.text: The senator's itinerary includes stops in six cities over the course of a single week.

origin.ko: 라틴어 itinerārium '여행 기록, 길 안내서'에서 왔고 iter(길)에서 나왔습니다.

senses.en: censure severely or angrily

examples.text: Editorial writers lambasted the mayor for ignoring warnings about the crumbling bridge.

origin.ko: lambaste와 같은 말로, lam(때리다)과 baste(때리다)가 합쳐졌다고 추정됩니다.

senses.en: grant freedom to; free from confinement

examples.text: Allied troops liberated the town after months of occupation.

senses.en: release (gas or energy) as a result of a chemical reaction or physical decomposition

examples.text: Since the reaction liberates a large amount of chlorine gas, a powerful ventilation system is recommended.

origin.ko: 라틴어 līberātus에서 왔고 līberō '자유롭게 하다'에서 나왔습니다.

senses.en: a noisy riotous fight

examples.text: The protest degenerated into a melee as police and demonstrators clashed in the square.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 mêlée에서 왔고 라틴어 misceō '섞다'에서 나왔습니다. 뒤엉켜 싸우는 난투입니다.

senses.en: highly abstract and overly theoretical

examples.text: The seminar drifted into metaphysical debates that had little bearing on the actual experiment.

senses.en: transcending physical matter or the laws of nature

examples.text: Many ancient philosophers sought metaphysical truths beyond the reach of the senses.

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 metaphysicālis에서 왔고 meta-와 physical이 합쳐졌습니다. 자연(물리)을 넘어선 추상의 영역입니다.

senses.en: cause to feel shame; hurt the pride of

examples.text: The senator was mortified when his offhand remark was broadcast to millions of viewers.

senses.en: To discipline (one's body, appetites etc.) by suppressing desires; to practise abstinence on.

examples.text: Some people seek sainthood by mortifying the body.

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 mortificō '죽게 하다'에서 왔습니다. 자존심을 죽이는 듯한 일이 굴욕감을 주다가 되었습니다.

senses.en: An unimportant or insignificant person or thing.

examples.text: Once a political nonentity, she rose within a decade to lead the party.

senses.en: the state of being known for some unfavorable act or quality

examples.text: The senator gained notoriety for his habit of abruptly reversing his positions.

origin.ko: 라틴어 nōtus '알려진'에서 나온 말입니다. 널리 알려졌다는 뜻이 나쁜 쪽으로 알려진 악명이 되었습니다.

senses.en: expel from a community or group

examples.text: The village ostracized anyone who refused to follow its strict customs.

origin.ko: 고대 그리스에서 추방할 사람의 이름을 도자기 조각(óstrakon)에 적어 투표한 데서 왔습니다. 그래서 따돌리고 추방한다는 뜻이 되었습니다.

senses.en: clearly revealed to the mind or the senses or judgment

examples.text: There was a palpable sense of relief in the room after the verdict.

senses.en: Capable of being touched, felt or handled; touchable, tangible.

examples.text: Osric: A hit, a very palpable hit.

origin.ko: 라틴어 palpābilis에서 왔고, palpō는 '부드럽게 만지다'입니다. 손으로 만질 수 있을 만큼 뚜렷하다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: fraught with danger

examples.text: a perilous voyage across the Atlantic in a small boat

origin.ko: 옛 프랑스어 perilleus에서 왔고, peril(위험)에 -ous가 붙은 말입니다.

senses.en: The belief of something based upon reasonable evidence, or upon something known to be true.

examples.text: The presumption is that an event has taken place.

senses.en: audacious (even arrogant) behavior that you have no right to

examples.text: He had the presumption to correct the professor in front of the entire lecture hall.

origin.ko: 라틴어 praesūmptiō에서 왔습니다. 증거를 다 보기 전에 먼저 취해 놓는 '추정'입니다.

senses.en: an unusually gifted or intelligent (young) person; someone whose talents excite wonder and admiration

examples.text: At nine, the chess prodigy was already defeating seasoned grandmasters in public exhibitions.

senses.en: a sign of something about to happen

examples.text: Ancient chroniclers recorded the comet as a prodigy foretelling the king's death.

origin.ko: 라틴어 prōdigium('전조, 불가사의')에서 왔습니다. 놀라운 일이라는 뜻에서 놀라운 재능을 지닌 아이가 되었습니다.

senses.en: A speech or section used as an introduction, especially to a play or novel.

examples.text: The novel opens with a brief prologue set several centuries before the main events.

origin.ko: 그리스어 prologos('앞의 말')에서 왔습니다. 본 이야기에 앞서 하는 말입니다.

senses.en: opposed to political or social liberalism or reform

examples.text: The reactionary government banned unions and censored newspapers to block any demand for reform.

senses.en: an extreme conservative; an opponent of progress or liberalism

examples.text: Progressives accused the reactionaries in parliament of trying to restore the privileges of the old aristocracy.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 réactionnaire에서 왔습니다. 프랑스 혁명에 맞서 반작용을 일으키려던 사람을 가리켰습니다.

senses.en: an abatement in intensity or degree (as in the manifestations of a disease)

examples.text: his cancer is in remission

senses.en: A pardon of a sin; (chiefly historical, also figuratively) the forgiveness of an offence, or relinquishment of a (legal) claim or a debt.

examples.text: The ancient ritual promised remission of sins to all who made the pilgrimage.

origin.ko: 라틴어 remissiō에서 왔고 remittere('늦추어 보내다')와 이어집니다. 병세를 풀어 늦춘다는 '완화'입니다.

senses.en: argue in protest or opposition

examples.text: Parents gathered at the school to remonstrate with the board over the planned closure.

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 remōnstrāre에서 왔습니다. 잘못을 되받아 지적해 보여 주며 항의한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: a disloyal person who betrays or deserts their cause or religion or political party or friend etc.

examples.text: The party denounced him as a renegade after he voted with the opposition on every key issue.

senses.en: Unconventional, unorthodox.

examples.text: The renegade physicist published theories that defied nearly every assumption of his field.

origin.ko: 스페인어 renegado에서 왔고 라틴어 renegāre('부인하다')에서 나왔습니다. 믿음을 저버린 배신자입니다.

senses.en: A brief interval of rest or relief.

examples.text: The rain brought a brief respite from the heat that had gripped the city for weeks.

senses.en: the act of reprieving; postponing or remitting punishment

examples.text: The governor granted the prisoner a respite hours before the scheduled execution.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 respit('휴식')에서 왔고 라틴어 respectus('뒤돌아봄')와 이어집니다. 잠시 멈추어 돌아보는 쉼입니다.

senses.en: tighten one's belt; use resources carefully

examples.text: Facing falling revenue, the university was forced to retrench and freeze all new hiring.

senses.en: make a reduction, as in one's workforce

examples.text: The company had to retrench

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 retranchier('잘라 내다')에서 왔습니다. 비용을 잘라 내 긴축한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: To improve, renew, renovate, or revise (something).

examples.text: The airline plans to revamp its loyalty program to attract more frequent business travelers.

origin.ko: re-('다시')에 vamp('수선하다')를 붙인 말입니다. 낡은 것을 다시 손봐 새롭게 한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: To annoy; to make angry; to throw into discord.

examples.text: The controversial ruling continued to roil the political establishment for weeks.

senses.en: be agitated

examples.text: The harbor began to roil as the storm front moved in from the west.

senses.en: To render turbid by stirring up the dregs or sediment of.

examples.text: to roil a spring

origin.ko: 어원이 확실하지 않으나 프랑스어 '녹, 진흙'과 관련된다고 봅니다. 진흙탕을 휘저어 흐리게 한다는 이미지입니다.

senses.en: An action intended to deceive; a trick.

examples.text: The charity call was merely a ruse to obtain the elderly woman's bank details.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어에서 온 말로, 쫓기는 짐승이 사냥꾼을 따돌리려 이리저리 피하는 동작을 뜻했습니다. 거기서 속임수가 나왔습니다.

senses.en: Delighting in or feeling pleasure from the pain or humiliation of others.

examples.text: The sadistic warden seemed to take real pleasure in devising new humiliations for the inmates.

origin.ko: 어원 정보가 없습니다. 일반적으로 프랑스 작가 사드(Sade) 후작의 이름에서 나온 말로 알려져 있습니다.

senses.en: To smile in a foolish, frivolous, self-conscious, coy, obsequious, or smug manner.
senses.ko: 어리석게 히죽 웃다, 아양 떨며 웃다

examples.text: a whimpering, simpering child

origin.ko: 기원이 불확실하며 덴마크어 simper(수줍은)와 비교됩니다. 점잔 빼며 웃는 모습입니다.

senses.en: verbal misrepresentation intended to take advantage of you in some way

examples.text: The inquiry uncovered political skullduggery involving forged ballots and secret payments to officials.

senses.en: slow and apathetic

examples.text: a sluggish worker

senses.en: (of business) not active or brisk

examples.text: Inflation has been rising despite a sluggish economy.

senses.en: firm and dependable especially in loyalty

examples.text: a staunch defender of free speech

senses.en: stop the flow of a liquid

examples.text: staunch the blood flow

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 estanche(물이 새지 않는, 견고한)에서 왔습니다. 물 샐 틈 없이 단단하다는 데서 충실하다는 뜻이 나왔습니다.

senses.en: to walk with a lofty proud gait, often in an attempt to impress others

examples.text: He struts around like a rooster in a hen house

senses.en: brace consisting of a bar or rod used to resist longitudinal compression

examples.text: Engineers added a steel strut to reinforce the aging bridge.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 strūtian(뻣뻣하게 튀어나오다)에서 왔습니다. 가슴을 부풀려 뻣뻣하게 으스대며 걷는 모습입니다.

senses.en: A course suddenly and unexpectedly divergent from one which was previously being followed (especially one embarked on before reaching the end of the previous course).

examples.text: I believe we went off onto a tangent when we started talking about monkeys on unicycles at his retirement party.

senses.en: a straight line or plane that touches a curve or curved surface at a point but does not intersect it at that point

examples.text: A tangent to a circle meets the circle at exactly one point.

origin.ko: 라틴어 tangēns(닿는)에서 왔습니다. 곡선에 살짝 닿고 비껴 나가는 선이라 화제 이탈이라는 뜻이 되었습니다.

senses.en: performed comprehensively and completely; not superficial or partial

examples.text: The new director ordered a thoroughgoing overhaul of the museum's cataloguing system.

senses.en: without qualification; used informally as (often pejorative) intensifiers

examples.text: The critic dismissed the pamphlet as the work of a thoroughgoing charlatan.

origin.ko: thorough에 going을 붙인 합성어입니다. 끝까지 밀고 나간다는 뜻에서 '철저한'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: marked by firm determination or resolution; not shakable

examples.text: Through months of setbacks, the coach kept an unfaltering belief that the young team would improve.

senses.en: Unimpressive or unremarkable; dull and ordinary; nondescript.

examples.text: The unprepossessing little restaurant turned out to serve the finest meal of our entire trip.

senses.en: Generous and tireless with one's contributions of money, time, etc.

examples.text: We thank her for her unstinting support of our new hospital.

origin.ko: un-과 stint('인색하게 굴다')의 결합입니다. 아끼지 않으니 '아낌없는'입니다.

senses.en: the qualities of a hero or heroine; exceptional or heroic courage when facing danger (especially in battle)

examples.text: he received a medal for valor

senses.en: The fact or state of being for sale, especially with reference to bribes or corruption.

examples.text: Reformers blamed the city's decline on the venality of officials who sold permits to the highest bidder.

origin.ko: venal에 -ity를 붙였습니다. 팔릴 수 있는 상태가 '매수되기 쉬움'입니다.

senses.en: To relinquish (a right etc.); to give up claim to; to forgo.

examples.text: If you waive the right to be silent, anything you say can be used against you in a court of law.

origin.ko: 앵글로노르만어 weyver('버리다')에서 왔습니다. 권리를 버려 둔다는 뜻이 '포기하다'입니다.

senses.en: without concealment or deception; honest

examples.text: The council insisted that every contract be awarded through an open and aboveboard bidding process.

senses.en: praise vociferously

examples.text: Critics acclaimed the debut novel as the most original work of the decade.

senses.en: enthusiastic approval

examples.text: The film earned widespread critical acclaim, though audiences were slower to warm to it.

origin.ko: 라틴어 acclamare(소리 질러 환호하다)에서 왔습니다. 큰 소리로 외쳐 칭송하는 모습입니다.

senses.en: Firm; unshakeable; unyielding; determined.

examples.text: The mayor remained adamant that the bridge would be rebuilt, despite mounting criticism of its cost.

origin.ko: 그리스어 adamas(정복할 수 없는)에서 왔고 diamond와 같은 뿌리입니다. 꺾이지 않는 단단함이 '요지부동'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: Well skilled; completely versed; thoroughly proficient.

examples.text: She was adept at translating dense legal language into plain terms that clients could understand.

origin.ko: 라틴어 adeptus(성취한 사람)에서 왔습니다. 기술을 몸에 익혀 얻어낸 사람이 '능숙한'입니다.

senses.en: curved down like an eagle's beak

examples.text: Frank's aquiline nose jutted out from underneath his glasses.

origin.ko: 라틴어 aquilinus(독수리 같은)에서 왔고 aquila(독수리)에서 나왔습니다. 독수리 부리처럼 굽은 코를 뜻합니다.

senses.en: a quantitative or qualitative test of a substance (especially an ore or a drug) to determine its components; frequently used to test for the presence or concentration of infectious agents or antibodies etc.

examples.text: The laboratory ran an assay to measure the concentration of the compound in each sample.

senses.en: make an effort or attempt

examples.text: Chemists tried to assay the ore sample to see how much silver it contained.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 essai(시도, 시험)에서 왔고 essay와 같은 말에서 갈라졌습니다.

senses.en: aggressive boldness or unmitigated effrontery

examples.text: he had the audacity to question my decision

senses.en: fearless daring

examples.text: The explorers' audacity carried them across the uncharted ice cap in midwinter.

origin.ko: 라틴어 audax(대담한)에서 왔습니다. 대담함이 지나쳐 '뻔뻔함'의 뜻이 되었습니다.

senses.en: Overly and needlessly complicated.

examples.text: baroque bookkeeping in pursuit of tax dodges

senses.en: having elaborate symmetrical ornamentation

examples.text: The theater's baroque ceiling was crowded with gilded angels and plaster garlands.

origin.ko: 포르투갈어 barroco(일그러진 진주)에서 프랑스어를 거쳐 왔습니다. 찌그러진 진주처럼 과하게 꾸민 양식을 가리키게 되었습니다.

senses.en: According to recognised or orthodox rules.

examples.text: The men played golf in the most canonical way, with no local rules.

senses.en: Present in a canon, religious or otherwise.

examples.text: The Gospel of Luke is a canonical New Testament book.

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 canōnicālis에서 왔고, canon(규범)에 -ical이 붙은 말입니다.

senses.en: settle conclusively

examples.text: I already planned to buy the car, but the color was what really clinched it for me.

senses.en: To fasten securely or permanently.

examples.text: The carpenter clinched the boards together so that no storm could pull them apart.

senses.en: hold in a tight grasp

examples.text: Nervous in the storm, she clinched the steering wheel with both hands.

origin.ko: 16세기에 clench(꽉 죄다)가 바뀐 말입니다. 못 끝을 꽉 구부려 확실히 고정한다는 이미지입니다.

senses.en: Actual or threatened force for the purpose of compelling action by another person; the act of coercing.

examples.text: The confession was thrown out because the court found it had been obtained through coercion.

origin.ko: 라틴어 coërcitiō에서 왔고, coërceō는 co-와 arceō(가두다)가 합쳐졌습니다. 울타리에 가두듯 억누르는 힘입니다.

senses.en: cohering or tending to cohere; well integrated

examples.text: a team welded into a cohesive unit

origin.ko: 라틴어 cohaesus(cohaereō의 과거분사)에 -ive가 붙은 말입니다. 서로 달라붙어 결속된다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: force somebody to do something

examples.text: New regulations compel companies to disclose the chemicals used in their products.

senses.en: necessitate or exact

examples.text: The severe water shortage compels strict conservation measures across the region.

origin.ko: 라틴어 compellere에서 왔고, com-(함께)과 pellere(몰다)가 합쳐졌습니다. 가축을 한데 몰듯 강제한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: forming an end or termination; especially putting an end to doubt or question

examples.text: conclusive evidence

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 conclusivus에서 왔고, concludere(닫아 끝내다)에서 갈라졌습니다. 문을 닫아 의문을 끝낸다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: a schoolhouse with special facilities for fine arts

examples.text: She trained at a famous conservatory before joining the national symphony orchestra.

senses.en: a greenhouse in which plants are arranged in a pleasing manner

examples.text: Tropical orchids bloomed year-round in the glass conservatory behind the manor.

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 cōnservātōrium에서 왔고, cōnservāre(보존하다)에서 갈라졌습니다. 재능을 보존해 가르치는 곳입니다.

senses.en: Something that constrains; a restriction.

examples.text: Budget constraints forced the museum to postpone its planned expansion.

senses.en: The repression of one's feelings.

examples.text: There was a noticeable constraint between the two old friends after their quarrel.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 constreinte(constreindre의 과거분사)에서 왔고, 라틴어 cōnstringō(묶다)가 뿌리입니다.

senses.en: get over an illness or shock

examples.text: The patient convalesced for six months after his stroke.

origin.ko: 라틴어 convalēscere에서 왔고, valēscere('강해지기 시작하다')에서 갈라졌습니다. 다시 튼튼해지는 과정입니다.

senses.en: To hold in belief or estimation; to adjudge as a conclusion; to regard as being; to evaluate according to one's beliefs; to account.

examples.text: She deemed his efforts insufficient.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 dēman(판단하다, 선고하다)에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: To lower in value or social position.

examples.text: Fred degrades himself by his behaviour.

senses.en: To reduce in quality or purity.

examples.text: The DNA sample has degraded.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 dégrader에서 왔습니다. 단계를 아래로 내린다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: Something that deters.

examples.text: Along with trial by ordeal, hanging was the most effective deterrent that could be devised in an age without police or prisons.

senses.en: tending to deter

examples.text: the deterrent effects of high prices

origin.ko: 라틴어 dēterrēns(겁주어 막는)에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: having or using the ability to act or decide according to your own discretion or judgment

examples.text: The commission has discretionary power to award extra funds

origin.ko: discretion(분별, 재량)에 -ary가 붙은 말입니다.

senses.en: showing sorrow

examples.text: The dolorous strains of the funeral march drifted slowly across the silent village square.

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 dolōrōsus(고통스러운)에서 왔고 dolor(고통)가 뿌리입니다.

senses.en: raise in a relief

examples.text: embossed stationery

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 embocer에서 왔고, boce(혹, 부풀음)가 바탕입니다. 표면을 부풀려 도드라지게 새긴다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: increase in extent or intensity

examples.text: Violence escalated during the election.

origin.ko: escalator(에스컬레이터)에서 거꾸로 만들어진 말입니다. 계단이 오르듯 규모가 점점 커진다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: call forth (emotions, feelings, and responses)

examples.text: The documentary evoked deep sympathy among viewers who had never heard of the region.

senses.en: call to mind

examples.text: Being here evokes long forgotten memories.

origin.ko: 라틴어 ēvocāre(불러내다)에서 프랑스어를 거쳐 왔습니다. 감정이나 기억을 밖으로 불러낸다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: To cut out; to remove.

examples.text: Military censors have excised some details from the photographs for security reasons.

senses.en: A tax charged on goods produced within the country (as opposed to customs duties, charged on goods from outside the country).

examples.text: The government raised the excise on tobacco and alcohol to help close the budget deficit.

origin.ko: 라틴어 excīdere(잘라 내다)에서 프랑스어를 거쳐 왔습니다. 도려내듯 잘라 삭제한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: make amends for

examples.text: He spent the rest of his life working in hospitals to expiate the guilt of his youth.

origin.ko: 라틴어 expiāre(속죄하다)에서 왔습니다. 잘못을 갚아 죄를 씻는다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: A phenomenon that becomes popular for a very short time.

examples.text: Critics predicted that the diet would prove a passing fad, forgotten within a single season.

senses.en: A sudden or unexpected failure.

examples.text: His speech was a fiasco that left the audience confused.

origin.ko: 이탈리아어 fiasco(병)에서 왔습니다. 극장 속어 'far fiasco(병을 만들다)'가 실패를 뜻하게 되었으나 정확한 유래는 불분명합니다.

senses.en: lasting for a markedly brief time

examples.text: a fleeting glance

origin.ko: 고대 영어 flēotan(떠다니다, 흘러가다)에서 왔습니다. 물에 떠 흘러가듯 순식간에 지나간다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: capable of being anticipated

examples.text: This project will not be finished in the foreseeable future.

origin.ko: foresee(미리 보다)에 -able이 붙었습니다. 미리 내다볼 수 있다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: lose (something) or lose the right to (something) by some error, offense, or crime

examples.text: Anyone convicted of the offense forfeits the right to hold public office for ten years.

senses.en: something that is lost or surrendered as a penalty

examples.text: The deposit was the forfeit he paid for cancelling the contract so late.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 forfait(범죄)에서 왔습니다. '선을 넘어 저지른 일'이 벌로서 무언가를 잃는다는 뜻이 되었습니다.

senses.en: wear away by rubbing

examples.text: The constant friction frayed the rope until it finally snapped under the load.

senses.en: Of a person's mental strength, nerves, temper, etc.: to become exhausted or worn out.

examples.text: The hectic day ended in her nerves frayed.

senses.en: a noisy fight

examples.text: The mayor declined to enter the fray over the controversial zoning proposal.

senses.en: worry unnecessarily or excessively

examples.text: Parents often fret over their children's grades long after the exams are over.

senses.en: To gnaw; to consume, to eat away.

examples.text: Years of saltwater spray had fretted the iron railings until they crumbled at a touch.

origin.ko: 고대영어 fretan '먹어 치우다'에서 왔습니다. 무언가가 속을 갉아먹듯 괴롭히는 모습에서 '안달하다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: Being productive in any sense; yielding benefits.

examples.text: The two laboratories began a fruitful collaboration that produced several landmark papers.

origin.ko: 중세영어에서 fruit(열매)에 -ful(가득한)이 붙은 말입니다. 열매가 가득하니 '결실 있는'입니다.

senses.en: the trait of being rude and impertinent; inclined to take liberties

examples.text: He had the gall to ask for a raise right after losing the firm's biggest client.

senses.en: become or make sore by or as if by rubbing

examples.text: It galled her that colleagues with less experience were promoted ahead of her.

senses.en: a feeling of deep and bitter anger and ill-will

examples.text: Years of rejection filled the poet with gall that bled into every line he wrote.

origin.ko: 고대영어 gealla '쓸개즙'에서 왔습니다. 쓸개즙이 성격과 연결된다던 옛 체액설 때문에 '뻔뻔함'이라는 뜻이 생겼습니다.

senses.en: To corrupt; to make unreadable, incomprehensible, or unintelligible.
senses.ko: (내용을) 왜곡하다, 뒤섞어 알아볼 수 없게 하다

examples.text: A poor phone connection garbled the message so badly that no one understood the instructions.

senses.en: make false by mutilation or addition; as of a message or story

examples.text: The tabloid garbled the senator's remarks to make them sound far more inflammatory.

origin.ko: 아랍어 ḡarbala '체로 치다'에서 중세 라틴어와 앵글로노르만어를 거쳐 왔습니다. 체로 쳐 뒤섞는다는 이미지가 '왜곡하다'로 이어졌습니다.

senses.en: To develop an idea.

examples.text: The novelist let the plot gestate for years before writing a single page.

senses.en: be pregnant with

examples.text: Elephants gestate their young for nearly two years, longer than any other land mammal.

origin.ko: gestation에서 거꾸로 만든 말입니다. 아이를 배 속에 품듯 아이디어를 마음속에 품고 키운다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: Uncritically reverent; adulating.

examples.text: Reviewers faulted the hagiographic biography for ignoring the statesman's well-documented failures.

origin.ko: 그리스어 hagios(성스러운)와 graphia(쓰기)가 합쳐져 성인전을 쓰는 글을 뜻합니다. 성인을 기리듯 무비판적으로 찬양한다는 뜻으로 번졌습니다.

senses.en: overbearing pride evidenced by a superior manner toward inferiors

examples.text: She addressed the junior staff with a hauteur that quickly made her unpopular.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 haut '높은'에서 나온 말입니다. 자신을 높이 두고 남을 내려다보는 태도입니다.

senses.en: Anything that impels; a stimulating factor.

examples.text: The outbreak of World War II in 1939 gave a new impetus to receiver development.

origin.ko: 라틴어 impetus '덮쳐 달려듦, 공격'에서 왔습니다. 앞으로 몰아가는 힘이 '추진력'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: difficult or impossible to evaluate with precision

examples.text: Investors struggled to predict the outcome because of the imponderable effects of political instability.

senses.en: a factor whose effects cannot be accurately assessed

examples.text: human behavior depends on many imponderables

origin.ko: 라틴어 pondus(무게)에서 온 말입니다. 무게를 달 수 없으니 가늠하기 어렵다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: pretending to be another person

examples.text: The imposture was exposed when the supposed professor could not answer a basic question in his field.

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 impostura에서 왔고 라틴어 imponere(얹다, 속여 씌우다)와 연결됩니다.

senses.en: make furious

examples.text: The company's decision to cut pensions without warning incensed employees across the country.

senses.en: a substance that produces a fragrant odor when burned

examples.text: The monks lit incense at dawn, and its sweet smoke drifted slowly through the stone hall.

origin.ko: 라틴어 incendō '불을 붙이다'에서 왔습니다. 마음에 불을 붙이듯 몹시 화나게 한다는 이미지입니다.

senses.en: the trait of lacking enthusiasm for or interest in things generally

examples.text: Voter indifference was blamed for the record-low turnout in the local election.

senses.en: unbiased impartial unconcern

examples.text: The arbiter's indifference between the two parties reassured both sides that the ruling would be fair.

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 indifferentia에서 왔습니다. 둘 사이에 차이를 두지 않아 어느 쪽에도 마음이 가지 않는 상태입니다.

senses.en: not to be dispensed with; essential

examples.text: foods indispensable to good nutrition

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 indispensābilis에서 왔습니다. 빼고 나눠 줄 수 없을 만큼 꼭 있어야 한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: showing inventiveness and skill

examples.text: That is an ingenious model of the atom.

origin.ko: 라틴어 ingenium '타고난 재능'에서 왔습니다. 몸 안에 타고난 재능이 있다는 데서 '독창적인'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: limit, block, or decrease the action or function of

examples.text: inhibit the action of the enzyme

senses.en: make (someone) self-conscious and as a result unable to act naturally

examples.text: Having the teacher watch from the back of the room inhibited the shy students from speaking.

origin.ko: 라틴어 inhibēre '붙들어 두다, 억제하다'에서 왔습니다. 안에 붙잡아 움직이지 못하게 한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: capable of replacing or changing places with something else; permitting mutual substitution without loss of function or suitability
senses.ko: 교환 가능한, 서로 바꿔 쓸 수 있는

examples.text: The two terms are often treated as interchangeable, though careful writers distinguish between them.

origin.ko: inter-(서로)와 change(바꾸다), -able이 합쳐진 말입니다. 서로 바꿔 쓸 수 있다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: cite as an authority; resort to

examples.text: He invoked the law that would save him

senses.en: summon into action or bring into existence, often as if by magic

examples.text: The candidate invoked the memory of past recessions to frighten voters away from her opponent.

senses.en: request earnestly (something from somebody); ask for aid or protection

examples.text: The villagers invoked the gods for rain after a third summer of failed crops.

origin.ko: 라틴어 invocāre '불러서 청하다'에서 왔습니다. 권위나 법을 불러내 근거로 삼는다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: a group of military officers who rule a country after seizing power

examples.text: The junta suspended the constitution and banned all opposition parties within days of the coup.

origin.ko: 스페인어 junta '모인 것'에서 왔고 라틴어 iungō '잇다'와 이어집니다. 모여 결합한 집단이라는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: a special way of doing something

examples.text: he had a special knack for getting into trouble

origin.ko: '날카로운 소리'를 뜻하는 중세 영어 knakke에서 왔을 가능성이 있습니다. 의성어로 보이며 '재주'로 뜻이 바뀐 경로는 불확실합니다.

senses.en: cut or tear irregularly

examples.text: Broken glass lacerated his palm as he reached into the wreckage.

senses.en: deeply hurt the feelings of; distress

examples.text: Her lacerating remarks left the young actor shaken for weeks.

origin.ko: 라틴어 lacerō '찢다'에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: To scold, reprimand or criticize harshly.

examples.text: Her first novel was well and truly lambasted by the critics.

origin.ko: lam(때리다)과 baste(때리다)가 합쳐졌다고 추정됩니다. 매질하듯 호되게 꾸짖는다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: the characteristic parts of a person's face: eyes and nose and mouth and chin

examples.text: his lineaments were very regular

senses.en: a characteristic property that defines the apparent individual nature of something

examples.text: Biographers trace the lineaments of the author's later style to his years in exile.

origin.ko: 프랑스어를 거쳐 라틴어 lineamentum에서 왔고 linea(선)에서 나왔습니다. 얼굴을 이루는 선, 곧 윤곽입니다.

senses.en: of high moral or intellectual value; elevated in nature or style

examples.text: The founders' lofty ideals of equality were rarely matched by their actual policies.

senses.en: Extremely proud; arrogant; haughty.

examples.text: The critic dismissed the debut with a lofty wave of his hand.

senses.en: Idealistic, implying over-optimism.

examples.text: a lofty goal

origin.ko: 중세 영어 loft(하늘, 위층)에 -y가 붙은 말입니다. 높이 솟아 고귀하다는 뜻이 되었습니다.

senses.en: Not adroit; awkward, clumsy, inept.

examples.text: His maladroit handling of the negotiations alienated both allies and opponents.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 maladroit에서 왔고 mal-(나쁘게)과 adroit(솜씨 좋은)가 합쳐졌습니다. 솜씨가 서투르다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: Motivated by personal gain.

examples.text: Her mercenary attitude toward friendship left her isolated once her fortune vanished.

senses.en: a person hired to fight for another country than their own

examples.text: The besieged king hired mercenaries from across the border to defend the capital.

origin.ko: 라틴어 mercēnārius '돈을 받고 일하는'에서 왔고 mercēs(보수)에서 나왔습니다.

senses.en: suggesting an unhealthy mental state

examples.text: Her morbid curiosity about disasters led her to collect old newspaper accounts of shipwrecks.

senses.en: caused by or altered by or manifesting disease or pathology

examples.text: The surgeon removed a morbid growth from the patient's lung.

origin.ko: 라틴어 morbidus '병든'에서 왔고, morbus는 '병'입니다. 병든 듯한 음울한 상태를 뜻합니다.

senses.en: One who sells by deception; a con artist.

examples.text: The traveling mountebank promised that his bottled tonic could cure every ailment known to man.

origin.ko: 이탈리아어 monta-in-banco, 즉 '벤치 위에 올라서'에서 왔습니다. 벤치에 올라 약을 팔던 돌팔이를 가리킵니다.

senses.en: An organized rebellion against a legally constituted authority, especially by seamen against their officers.

examples.text: The crew of the Bounty mutinied because of the harsh discipline of Captain Bligh.

origin.ko: 중세 프랑스어 mutiner에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: A small detail or distinction.

examples.text: The lawyers argued over legal niceties while the central question went unanswered.

origin.ko: 옛 프랑스어 niceté '단순함, 어리석음'에서 왔습니다. 뜻이 바뀌어 섬세하고 미묘한 구별을 가리키게 되었습니다.

senses.en: Lacking awareness; unmindful; unaware, unconscious of.

examples.text: Your grandmother is completely oblivious to her surroundings.

senses.en: Forgetful.

examples.text: He's hopelessly oblivious, always forgetting his appointments.

origin.ko: 라틴어 oblīviōsus '잘 잊는'에서 왔으며, oblīvīscor는 '잊다'입니다.

senses.en: Secret; hidden from general knowledge; undetected.

examples.text: occult blood loss; occult cancer

senses.en: having an import not apparent to the senses nor obvious to the intelligence; beyond ordinary understanding

examples.text: The scholar spent decades deciphering the occult symbols carved into the temple walls.

senses.en: supernatural practices and techniques

examples.text: He built a career writing popular histories of the occult in medieval Europe.

origin.ko: 라틴어 occultus '숨겨진, 비밀의'에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: the male head of family or tribe

examples.text: The family patriarch, aged ninety, still presided over every holiday dinner.

senses.en: A founder of a political or religious movement, an organization or an enterprise.

examples.text: He is regarded as the patriarch of modern environmental policy.

origin.ko: 그리스어 patriárkhēs '씨족의 창시자'에서 왔습니다. 아버지 같은 가문의 우두머리라는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: pass from physical life and lose all bodily attributes and functions necessary to sustain life

examples.text: The children perished in the fire

senses.en: To decay in such a way that it cannot be used for its original purpose

examples.text: The difficulty is that fresh foods perish due to the multiplication in them of harmful bacteria.

origin.ko: 라틴어 perīre '지나가 버리다'에서 왔고, per(통해) + īre(가다)로 이루어졌습니다. 사라져 가는 데서 죽다가 되었습니다.

senses.en: persistent determination

examples.text: Years of perseverance finally paid off when the team published its landmark study.

origin.ko: 라틴어 persevērantia '꿋꿋함'에서 왔습니다. 끝까지 엄격하게 버티는 끈기입니다.

senses.en: Acute discernment or understanding; insight.

examples.text: The investor's perspicacity allowed her to foresee the market crash months in advance.

origin.ko: 라틴어 perspicācitās '날카롭게 꿰뚫어 봄'에서 왔고, perspiciō는 '속까지 들여다보다'입니다.

senses.en: voluntary promotion of human welfare

examples.text: The university's new science wing was made possible by a lifetime of quiet philanthropy.

origin.ko: 그리스어 philanthrōpía '인류에 대한 사랑'에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: fraudulent; having a misleading appearance

examples.text: A good jeweler should be able to tell a real stone from a phony one.

senses.en: A person who professes beliefs or opinions that they do not hold.

examples.text: He's such a phony, he doesn't believe half of what he says.

senses.en: An unfortunate or trying position or condition.

examples.text: Stranded without money or a passport, the traveler found herself in a serious predicament.

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 praedicāmentum('단정된 것, 범주')에서 왔습니다. '처한 상태'라는 뜻을 거쳐 '곤경'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: having or showing knowledge and skill and aptitude

examples.text: After two years abroad, she became proficient in three languages.

origin.ko: 라틴어 proficere('앞으로 나아가다')에서 왔습니다. 계속 진전해 숙달되었다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: improve or perfect by pruning or polishing

examples.text: refine one's style of writing

senses.en: reduce to a fine, unmixed, or pure state; separate from extraneous matter or cleanse from impurities

examples.text: refine sugar

senses.en: derive or receive pleasure from; get enjoyment from; take pleasure in

examples.text: She relished her fame and basked in her glory

senses.en: vigorous and enthusiastic enjoyment

examples.text: The debater attacked her opponent's argument with obvious relish, delighting the crowd.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 reles('남은 것')에서 나온 release('냄새, 맛')의 변형입니다. 맛을 음미한다는 데서 '즐기다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: words falsely spoken that damage the reputation of another

examples.text: She sued her former employer for slander after he falsely told colleagues that she had stolen from the firm.

senses.en: charge falsely or with malicious intent; attack the good name and reputation of someone

examples.text: Rivals slandered the candidate in pamphlets that accused him of crimes he never committed.

origin.ko: 라틴어 scandalum(걸림돌, 유혹)에서 온 고대 프랑스어에서 왔고 scandal과 같은 뿌리입니다. 남을 넘어뜨리는 험담입니다.

senses.en: To kill; to murder.

examples.text: The knight slew the dragon.

senses.en: To eradicate or stamp out.

examples.text: You must slay these thoughts.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 slēan(때리다, 죽이다)에서 왔습니다. 쳐서 죽인다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: marked by excessive complacency or self-satisfaction

examples.text: Kate looked extremely smug this morning.

origin.ko: 저지 독일어 smuk(말끔한)에서 왔습니다. 말끔히 차려입고 우쭐대는 모습입니다.

senses.en: weep convulsively

examples.text: He was sobbing inconsolably

senses.en: convulsive gasp made while weeping

examples.text: A single sob escaped her as she read the letter announcing the news.

origin.ko: 중세 영어 sobben에서 왔습니다. 흐느끼는 소리를 흉내 낸 말로 보입니다.

senses.en: adornment consisting of a small piece of shiny material used to decorate clothing

examples.text: The dancer's gown was covered in silver spangles that caught the stage lights with every turn.

senses.en: To flash, glitter, or sparkle.

examples.text: Frost began to spangle the fields as the first light of morning crossed the valley.

origin.ko: 중세 영어 spang(작은 장신구)에 작다는 뜻의 -el이 붙은 말입니다. 작은 반짝이 조각을 뜻합니다.

senses.en: A brief argument, falling out, quarrel.

examples.text: get into a trivial spat over punctuality

senses.en: engage in a brief and petty quarrel

examples.text: The two senators spat openly over the budget before the cameras this week.

origin.ko: 어원이 불확실합니다. 침 뱉는 듯한 spit와 관련 있을 수 있습니다.

senses.en: a writ issued by court authority to compel the attendance of a witness at a judicial proceeding; disobedience may be punishable as a contempt of court

examples.text: The committee issued a subpoena demanding that the executive appear and produce the company's records.

senses.en: serve or summon with a subpoena

examples.text: The witness and her records were subpoenaed

origin.ko: 라틴어 sub poena(벌을 받는 조건으로)에서 왔습니다. 소환장 첫머리의 문구에서 이름이 되었습니다.

senses.en: not extreme in behavior

examples.text: Her temperate response to the insult surprised colleagues who expected an angry outburst.

senses.en: (of weather or climate) free from extremes; mild; or characteristic of such weather or climate

examples.text: These trees can only grow in temperate climates.

origin.ko: 라틴어 temperātus(알맞게 조절된)에서 왔습니다. 극단으로 치우치지 않고 온건하다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: slow and apathetic

examples.text: After the heavy lunch, the torpid committee could barely keep its eyes open during the budget review.

senses.en: in a condition of biological rest or suspended animation

examples.text: Through the winter the frogs lie torpid in the mud at the bottom of the pond.

origin.ko: 라틴어 torpidus('마비된, 지친')에서 왔습니다. 감각이 무뎌진 상태가 '무기력한'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: free of artificiality; sincere and genuine

examples.text: Despite her fame, she remained warm and unaffected, chatting with stagehands as easily as with directors.

senses.en: Not affected or changed.

examples.text: Since I work from home, I was unaffected by the office move.

origin.ko: un-과 affected('꾸민')의 결합입니다. 꾸밈이 없으니 '진솔한'이 됩니다.

senses.en: Strange, and mysteriously unsettling (as if supernatural); weird.

examples.text: He bore an uncanny resemblance to the dead sailor.

senses.en: surpassing the ordinary or normal

examples.text: The veteran trader had an uncanny knack for sensing a market reversal days before it happened.

origin.ko: un-과 canny의 결합으로, 낯익은 지식 바깥에 있다는 뜻입니다. 프로이트의 독일어 unheimlich를 옮긴 말이기도 합니다.

senses.en: not confined or limited

examples.text: The young poet wrote with untrammeled imagination, ignoring every convention of form.

origin.ko: trammel('물고기 그물, 족쇄')에서 온 말입니다. 그물과 족쇄에 묶이지 않았다는 뜻이 '구속받지 않는'입니다.

senses.en: Commanding respect because of age, dignity, character or position.

examples.text: The venerable professor, still teaching at ninety, was greeted by a standing ovation.

senses.en: Ancient, antiquated or archaic.

examples.text: The venerable oak at the center of the village has stood for nearly six hundred years.

origin.ko: 라틴어 venerabilis('존경할 만한')에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: compete for something; engage in a contest; measure oneself against others

examples.text: Three firms will vie for the contract to build the new stadium.

origin.ko: envy를 줄인 말이고 라틴어 invītō('초대하다, 도전하다')까지 거슬러 갑니다. 서로 도전하는 것이 '경쟁하다'입니다.

senses.en: carefully observant or attentive; on the lookout for possible danger

examples.text: Be vigilant for signs of disease in your garden.

origin.ko: 라틴어 vigilare('깨어 있다')에서 왔습니다. 잠들지 않고 지키는 모습이 '경계하는'입니다.

senses.en: To be indecisive about something; to dither, to vacillate, to waver.

examples.text: The governor continued to waffle on the tax bill, pleasing neither supporters nor critics.

senses.en: To speak or write evasively or vaguely.

examples.text: He waffled on for much of the earnings call without addressing the fall in share price.

origin.ko: 스코틀랜드어 waffle('흔들리다, 펄럭이다')에서 온 동사입니다. 이리저리 흔들리는 모습이 '우유부단하게 굴다'입니다.

senses.en: a feeling of strong eagerness (usually in favor of a person or cause)

examples.text: She extols the virtues of veganism with missionary zeal.

origin.ko: 그리스어 zêlos('열성, 질투')에서 후기 라틴어와 고대 프랑스어를 거쳐 왔습니다. jealous와 같은 뿌리입니다.

senses.en: the act of cutting something off

examples.text: Autumn leaves fall through abscission, in which the tree seals off the stem before releasing the leaf.

origin.ko: 라틴어 abscindere(잘라내다)에서 왔습니다. 떼어 잘라내는 행위를 뜻합니다.

senses.en: a bottomless gulf or pit; any unfathomable (or apparently unfathomable) cavity or chasm or void extending below (often used figuratively)

examples.text: After the scandal, the once-admired firm seemed to teeter on the edge of an abyss.

origin.ko: 그리스어 abyssos(바닥 없는)에서 왔습니다. 바닥이 없는 구렁이라는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: having an abundant supply of money or possessions of value

examples.text: The affluent suburbs funded their schools generously while neighboring districts struggled.

senses.en: a branch that flows into the main stream

examples.text: The river swelled as each affluent carried meltwater down from the mountains.

origin.ko: 라틴어 affluere(~로 흘러들다)에서 왔습니다. 재물이 풍부하게 흘러드는 모습이 '부유한'입니다.

senses.en: terse and witty and like a maxim

examples.text: Her aphoristic style made the lectures easy to quote but hard to summarize.

origin.ko: 그리스어 aphoristikos에서 왔고 aphorism(격언)과 같은 뿌리입니다. 격언처럼 간결하다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: an elaborate song for solo voice

examples.text: The soprano's final aria drew a standing ovation from the audience.

origin.ko: 이탈리아어 aria(공기, 노래 곡조)에서 왔고 그리스어 aēr(공기)와 연결됩니다.

senses.en: a man-made object taken as a whole

examples.text: The dig produced many Roman artifacts.

senses.en: A finding or structure in an experiment or investigation that is not a true feature of the object under observation, but is a result of external action, the test arrangement, or an experimental error.

examples.text: The spot on his lung turned out to be an artifact of the X-ray process.

origin.ko: 라틴어 arte(솜씨로)와 factum(만든 것)이 합쳐진 말입니다. 솜씨로 만든 물건이 '인공물'입니다.

senses.en: frivolous banter

examples.text: The ministers traded badinage across the table before the formal talks began.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 badiner(농담하다)에서 왔고 옛 프로방스어 badar(입을 벌리다)와 이어집니다. 입을 헤벌리고 가볍게 장난치는 모습입니다.

senses.en: the rapid and continuous delivery of linguistic communication (spoken or written)

examples.text: a barrage of questions

senses.en: the heavy fire of artillery to saturate an area rather than hit a specific target

examples.text: they laid down a barrage in front of the advancing troops

origin.ko: 프랑스어 barrage(장벽, 차단)를 그대로 빌려온 말입니다. 포격으로 길을 막는 데서 '쇄도'로 뜻이 넓어졌습니다.

senses.en: completely wanting or lacking

examples.text: writing barren of insight

senses.en: providing no shelter or sustenance

examples.text: barren mountain tracts

senses.en: Unproductive, fruitless, unprofitable; empty, hollow, vain.

examples.text: brilliant but barren reveries

origin.ko: 앵글로노르만어 baraigne(불모의)에서 왔고 더 앞의 어원은 확실치 않습니다. 아무것도 자라지 않는 땅의 이미지입니다.

senses.en: offering little or no hope

examples.text: Economists painted a bleak picture of the coming year, predicting layoffs and falling wages.

senses.en: Desolate and exposed; swept by cold winds.

examples.text: The expedition crossed a bleak plateau where nothing grew and the wind never stopped.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 blǣc('창백한')와 고대 노르드어 bleikr(희끄무레한)에서 왔습니다. 핏기 없고 음울한 느낌입니다.

senses.en: To review for, and if necessary to remove or suppress, content from books, films, correspondence, and other media which is regarded as objectionable (for example, obscene, likely to incite violence, or sensitive).

examples.text: Occupying powers typically censor anything reeking of resistance

senses.en: An official responsible for the removal or suppression of objectionable material (for example, if obscene or likely to incite violence) or sensitive content in books, films, correspondence, and other media.

examples.text: The headmaster was an even stricter censor of his boarding pupils’ correspondence than the enemy censors had been of his own when the country was occupied.

senses.en: someone who censures or condemns

examples.text: As a harsh censor of her colleagues' work, she rarely offered praise without a long list of faults.

origin.ko: 라틴어 cēnsor('판정하는 관리')에서 왔고, cēnseō(판단하다)에서 갈라졌습니다. 로마에서 시민의 품행을 평가하던 관리입니다.

senses.en: relating to or arranged according to temporal order
