examples.text: The live report lists all the events in chronological order.

origin.ko: 그리스어 khronos(시간)와 -logia에서 온 chronology에 -ical이 붙은 말입니다. 시간 순서대로 나열한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: a style that involves indirect ways of expressing things

examples.text: The spokesman answered the reporter's blunt question with so much circumlocution that no one learned anything.

senses.en: an indirect way of expressing something

examples.text: Lacking the technical term, she resorted to a circumlocution to describe the missing tool.

origin.ko: 라틴어 circumlocūtiō('돌려 말하기')에서 왔습니다. 핵심 둘레를 빙빙 돌며 말한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: An accomplice; abettor; associate.

examples.text: He was able to plea down his sentence by revealing the names of three of his cohorts, as well as the source of the information.

senses.en: a group of people having approximately the same age

examples.text: Researchers followed a cohort of children born in 1990 to study long-term health outcomes.

origin.ko: 라틴어 cohors에서 왔고 court와 같은 어원입니다. 로마 군대의 한 부대에서 '동료 무리'로 이어졌습니다.

senses.en: so great in size or force or extent as to elicit awe

examples.text: The project proved a colossal waste of public money and years of planning.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 colossal에서 왔고, 라틴어 colossus를 거쳐 그리스어 kolossos('거대한 조각상')가 뿌리입니다.

senses.en: inclined to comply

examples.text: The suspect was compliant when arrested.

senses.en: lacking spontaneity; not natural

examples.text: a constrained smile

senses.en: Forced; compelled.

examples.text: Constrained by a tight budget, the committee had to cancel several planned events.

senses.en: call together

examples.text: The president convoked an emergency session of the council to discuss the crisis.

origin.ko: 라틴어 convocare에서 왔고, con-(함께)과 vocō(부르다)가 합쳐졌습니다. 사람들을 한데 불러 모은다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: speak against in an impassioned manner

examples.text: he declaimed against the wasteful ways of modern society

senses.en: recite in elocution

examples.text: The actor declaimed the famous soliloquy to a hushed and attentive theater.

origin.ko: 라틴어 dēclāmō(큰 소리로 연설하다)에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: a mistaken or unfounded opinion or idea

examples.text: he has delusions of competence

origin.ko: 라틴어 dēlūsiō(속임)에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: To plunder; to pillage; take spoil from.

examples.text: Invading armies despoiled the countryside, carrying off grain, livestock, and church treasures.

origin.ko: 라틴어 dēspoliāre에서 왔고 spolium(벗긴 가죽, 전리품)이 뿌리입니다. 빼앗아 벗긴다는 이미지입니다.

senses.en: To upset the composure of; to startle.

examples.text: The embrace disconcerted the daughter-in-law somewhat, as the caresses of old gentlemen unshorn and perfumed with tobacco might well do.

senses.en: To frustrate, discomfit.

examples.text: The emperor disconcerted the plans of his enemy.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 desconcerter에서 왔습니다. 맞춰진 조화를 흩뜨려 당황하게 한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: To cause (an idea or piece of evidence) to seem false or unreliable.

examples.text: The evidence would tend to discredit such a theory.

senses.en: damage the reputation of

examples.text: This newspaper story discredits the politicians

origin.ko: dis-와 credit(신용)을 합친 말입니다. 믿음을 없앤다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: A lengthy, formal discourse that analyses or explains some topic; (loosely) a dissertation or treatise.

examples.text: The professor's disquisition on medieval trade routes ran well past the end of the seminar.

origin.ko: 라틴어 disquīsītiō(탐구)에서 왔고 disquīrō(샅샅이 조사하다)가 뿌리입니다.

senses.en: diverging from another or from a standard

examples.text: a divergent opinion

senses.en: tending to move apart in different directions

examples.text: The two research teams followed divergent paths and reached very different conclusions about the data.

origin.ko: 라틴어 dis-와 vergere(향하다)에 -ent가 붙은 말입니다.

senses.en: having variety of character or form or components; or having increased variety

examples.text: diversified farming

senses.en: turn aside; turn away from

examples.text: The workers diverted the stream away from the road.

senses.en: occupy in an agreeable, entertaining or pleasant fashion

examples.text: Street musicians diverted the waiting passengers during the long delay at the station.

senses.en: withdraw (money) and move into a different location, often secretly and with dishonest intentions

examples.text: Investigators found that the manager had diverted charity funds into his own personal accounts.

origin.ko: 라틴어 divertere(갈라져 돌아서다)에서 왔습니다. 방향을 돌린다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: inactive but capable of becoming active

examples.text: her feelings of affection are dormant but easily awakened

senses.en: in a condition of biological rest or suspended animation

examples.text: Grass goes dormant during the winter, waiting for spring before it grows again.

origin.ko: 라틴어 dormiō(자다)의 현재분사에서 왔습니다. 잠든 듯 쉬다가 깨어날 수 있다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: raise in rank or condition

examples.text: The scandal-free decade elevated the small party from obscurity to national prominence.

senses.en: To make (something or someone) more worthy or of greater value.

examples.text: A talented chef can elevate everyday ingredients into gourmet delights.

origin.ko: 라틴어 ēlevāre(들어 올리다)에서 왔습니다. 가볍게 해서 위로 올리는 이미지입니다.

senses.en: lacking energy or vitality

examples.text: The summer heat left the marchers enervated and unable to continue.

senses.en: the name derived from a person (real or imaginary)

examples.text: Alexandria is an eponym derived from the name of Alexander the Great.

senses.en: the person for whom something is named

examples.text: Constantine I is the eponym for Constantinople

origin.ko: 그리스어 epṓnumos(이름을 따서 붙인)에서 왔습니다. 사람 이름 위에 얹어 붙인 명칭이라는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: not easily irritated

examples.text: an equable temper

senses.en: not varying

examples.text: The island's equable climate means temperatures rarely change much through the year.

origin.ko: 라틴어 aequābilis(고른, 한결같은)에서 왔습니다. aequus는 '평평한'이라는 뜻이며, 감정이 고르게 유지된다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: to make a mistake or be incorrect

examples.text: He erred in his calculations, and made many mistakes.

senses.en: wander from a direct course or at random

examples.text: The hikers erred from the marked trail and wandered for hours in the fog.

origin.ko: 라틴어 errāre(헤매다, 길을 벗어나다)에서 고대 프랑스어를 거쳐 왔습니다. 길을 잃고 헤매는 데서 '잘못하다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: avoid or try to avoid fulfilling, answering, or performing (duties, questions, or issues)

examples.text: The senator evaded every direct question about the budget during the lengthy television interview.

senses.en: escape, either physically or mentally

examples.text: The robbers evaded the police.

origin.ko: 라틴어 ēvādere(빠져나가다)에서 프랑스어를 거쳐 왔습니다. 밖으로 슬쩍 걸어 나가 피한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: put to use

examples.text: He considered exerting his influence on John to gain an advantage for himself.

senses.en: make a great effort at a mental or physical task

examples.text: She exerted herself to finish the manuscript before the publisher's deadline.

origin.ko: 라틴어 exserere(밖으로 내밀다)에서 왔습니다. 힘을 밖으로 밀어내 쓰는 데서 '행사하다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: Talkative and sociable.

examples.text: After a glass of wine the usually reserved host grew expansive and told stories for hours.

senses.en: Comprehensive in scope or extent.

examples.text: The historian's expansive study traces trade routes across three continents over a thousand years.

origin.ko: 라틴어 expandere(펼치다)에서 왔습니다. 마음을 활짝 펼친 듯 개방적이고 말이 많다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: pleasing and appropriate manner or style (especially manner or style of expression)

examples.text: The translator rendered the difficult verse with remarkable felicity, preserving both its meaning and its music.

senses.en: state of well-being characterized by emotions ranging from contentment to intense joy

examples.text: The couple spoke of the quiet felicity of their first years together on the farm.

origin.ko: 라틴어 fēlīcitās(행복, 행운)에서 왔습니다. 행복이라는 뜻에서 표현이 알맞고 절묘하다는 뜻이 나왔습니다.

senses.en: To con or trick (someone) out of money.
senses.ko: 사기 쳐서 돈을 빼앗다, 바가지 씌우다

examples.text: Unscrupulous contractors fleeced elderly homeowners by charging for repairs that were never made.

senses.en: the wool of a sheep or similar animal

examples.text: The shepherd sheared the fleece from each sheep before the summer heat arrived.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 flēos(양털)에서 왔습니다. 양털을 깎듯 돈을 털어 간다는 뜻이 되었습니다.

senses.en: devoid of warmth and cordiality; expressive of unfriendliness or disdain

examples.text: She greeted her former rival with a glacial smile and a curt nod.

senses.en: Very slow.

examples.text: Progress on the new bridge has been glacial, with only a few girders in place after two years.

senses.en: extremely cold

examples.text: The hikers endured glacial winds that cut through even their heaviest jackets.

origin.ko: 라틴어 glaciālis '얼음의'에서 왔고 glaciēs(얼음)가 뿌리입니다. 얼음처럼 차가운 태도가 '냉랭한'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: a distinctive characteristic or attribute of someone or something

examples.text: Careful attention to detail is the hallmark of her scholarship.

origin.ko: hall과 mark의 합성어입니다. 런던 금세공사 회관(Goldsmiths' Hall)에서 순도를 보증해 찍던 도장이 '특징, 품질 보증'으로 번졌습니다.

senses.en: To make difficult to accomplish; to act as an obstacle; to frustrate.

examples.text: A drought hinders the growth of plants.

origin.ko: 고대영어 hindrian에서 왔고 hinder(뒤)와 연결됩니다. 뒤로 잡아당겨 앞으로 못 가게 하는 이미지입니다.

senses.en: pursue or chase relentlessly

examples.text: the detectives hounded the suspect until they found him

origin.ko: 고대영어 hund '개'에서 왔습니다. 사냥개가 짐승을 끈질기게 쫓듯 괴롭힌다는 뜻이 되었습니다.

senses.en: a small natural hill

examples.text: Hikers crossed the marsh by stepping from one grassy hummock to the next.

senses.en: contrary to or forbidden by law

examples.text: Customs officers seized a large shipment of illicit tobacco hidden in the cargo hold.

senses.en: contrary to accepted morality (especially sexual morality) or convention

examples.text: The scandal erupted when letters revealed the senator's illicit affair.

origin.ko: 라틴어 illicitus '허용되지 않은'에서 왔습니다. licet(허용된다)에 부정 접두사가 붙어 '금지된'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: completely neat and clean

examples.text: The hotel room was immaculate, with freshly pressed linens and not a speck of dust anywhere.

senses.en: without fault or error

examples.text: The pianist gave an immaculate performance, hitting every note with precision and restraint.

origin.ko: 라틴어 immaculātus '얼룩 없는'에서 왔습니다. in-(없는)과 macula(얼룩, 흠)가 합쳐져 티 하나 없다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: persistent to the point of annoying

examples.text: The importunate salesman kept calling the office, ignoring every polite request to stop.

origin.ko: 라틴어 importūnus '항구가 없는, 곤란한'에서 왔습니다. 쉴 항구 없이 계속 조르는 성가심입니다.

senses.en: the quality of being changeable and variable

examples.text: The inconstancy of public opinion made it nearly impossible for pollsters to predict the election's outcome.

senses.en: unfaithfulness by virtue of being unreliable or treacherous

examples.text: His inconstancy in friendship left former allies unwilling to trust him again.

origin.ko: in-(않는)에 constancy(꾸준함)가 붙은 말입니다. 한자리에 굳게 서 있지 못하는 변덕을 뜻합니다.

senses.en: showing no care or concern in attitude or action

examples.text: indifferent to the sufferings of others

senses.en: fairly poor to not very good

examples.text: has an indifferent singing voice

origin.ko: 라틴어 indifferēns에서 왔습니다. 차이(different)를 두지 않아 어느 쪽에도 마음이 쏠리지 않는다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: a state of extreme poverty or destitution

examples.text: Having lost his business, he lived out his final years in indigence, relying on charity for meals.

origin.ko: 라틴어 indigentia에서 왔고 indigēre(필요로 하다)가 뿌리입니다. 필요한 것이 모자란 극심한 가난입니다.

senses.en: displaying or suggesting a lack of maturity

examples.text: Critics dismissed the novel as a jejune exercise in adolescent angst.

senses.en: lacking interest or significance or impact

examples.text: The lecture was so jejune that half the audience left before it ended.

origin.ko: 라틴어 iēiūnus '굶주린, 단식하는'에서 왔습니다. 영양이 부족하다는 데서 '내용이 빈약한, 유치한'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: the financial means whereby one lives

examples.text: The new dam threatened the livelihood of thousands of fishing families downstream.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 līflād '삶의 길'에서 왔습니다. līf(삶)와 lād(길)가 합쳐졌습니다.

senses.en: a manifest indication of the existence or presence or nature of some person or thing

examples.text: a manifestation of disease

senses.en: The embodiment of an intangible, or variable thing.

examples.text: This particular manifestation resembled a young girl crying.

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 manifestātiō에서 왔고 manifest에 -ation이 붙었습니다. 겉으로 분명히 드러냄을 뜻합니다.

senses.en: characterized by or causing or expressing sadness

examples.text: The melancholy melody of the cello filled the empty hall at dusk.

senses.en: Great sadness or depression, especially of a thoughtful or introspective nature.

examples.text: A quiet melancholy settled over the poet as autumn deepened.

origin.ko: 그리스어 melankholía에서 왔고 mélas(검은)와 kholḗ(담즙)가 합쳐졌습니다. 검은 담즙이 우울을 일으킨다고 믿던 데서 나왔습니다.

senses.en: gather or bring together

examples.text: I couldn't muster the courage to tell him.

senses.en: To collect, call or assemble together, such as troops or a group for inspection, orders, display etc.

examples.text: The general mustered his troops on the parade ground before dawn.

origin.ko: 라틴어 mōnstrō '보여 주다'에서 왔습니다. 병사들을 모아 점검받게 하던 데서 '모으다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: Not expressed strongly or openly; subdued and understated

examples.text: The government offered only muted criticism of its ally's decision.

senses.en: being or made softer or less loud or clear

examples.text: Through the thick walls, the music was only a muted thump.

senses.en: so small as to be meaningless; insignificant

examples.text: The difference between the two groups was negligible, so the researchers drew no firm conclusions.

origin.ko: neglect에 해당하는 라틴어 neglegō에 -ible이 붙은 말입니다. 신경 쓰지 않아도 될 만큼 작다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: Equality; comparability of strength or intensity.

examples.text: Women's groups are demanding pay parity with their male colleagues.

origin.ko: 라틴어 pār '같은, 동등한'에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: a person who has suddenly risen to a higher economic status but has not gained social acceptance of others in that class

examples.text: Old-money families looked down on the parvenu who had bought the estate.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 parvenir '도달하다'의 과거분사로, 라틴어 perveniō '이르다'가 원형입니다. 갑자기 높은 자리에 올라선 사람입니다.

senses.en: someone who advocates the rights of the common people over those of the elite

examples.text: The populist promised to dismantle the privileges of a distant and self-serving political elite.

senses.en: Put forward just because it would be popular.

examples.text: Economists criticized the subsidy as a populist measure with no long-term plan behind it.

origin.ko: 라틴어 populus('민중')에 -ist가 붙은 말로, 민중 편에 서는 사람을 뜻합니다.

senses.en: something that precedes and indicates the approach of something or someone

examples.text: Economists treated the sharp drop in orders as a precursor of the coming recession.

origin.ko: 라틴어 praecursor('앞서 달리는 사람')에서 왔습니다. 먼저 달려와 뒤에 올 것을 알리는 선구자입니다.

senses.en: a feeling of evil to come

examples.text: She had a vague presentiment that the meeting would end badly.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 pressentiment에서 왔습니다. 일이 일어나기 전에 미리 느끼는 예감입니다.

senses.en: Food, especially for livestock.

examples.text: The farmers stored enough provender in the barn to feed the herd through the winter.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 provendre('지급분')에서 왔고 라틴어 praebenda('지급액')로 거슬러 갑니다. 가축에게 주는 사료입니다.

senses.en: serving or tending to provoke, excite, or stimulate; stimulating discussion or exciting controversy

examples.text: The professor's provocative lecture sparked a heated debate that lasted well past the hour.

origin.ko: 라틴어 prōvocāre('불러내다')에서 왔습니다. 상대를 앞으로 불러내 반응을 끌어내는 성질입니다.

senses.en: To furnish or provide.

examples.text: Those who sell their own products are distinguished from purveyors, who purvey what others produce.

origin.ko: 라틴어 prōvidēre('미리 보다, 마련하다')에서 온 고대 프랑스어에서 왔습니다. provide의 쌍둥이 말입니다.

senses.en: severe disapproval

examples.text: The editorial met the minister's remarks with open reprobation and called for his resignation.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 réprobation 또는 라틴어 reprobatio에서 왔으며 reprobate에 -ion이 붙은 말입니다. 인정하지 않고 내치는 강한 비난입니다.

senses.en: marked by avoidance of extravagance or extremes

examples.text: The prime minister gave a restrained response to the insult, avoiding any hint of anger.

senses.en: not showy or obtrusive

examples.text: The restrained decor of the hotel, in muted grays and creams, put guests instantly at ease.

senses.en: A small spreading change, impact, or effect produced by a larger or more consequential action.

examples.text: The central bank's surprise decision sent a ripple of anxiety through global financial markets.

senses.en: To propagate like a moving wave.

examples.text: These problems were complicated by a foreign exchange crunch which rippled through the economy in 1961-1962, […]

origin.ko: 중세 영어 동사에서 나온 말로, 잔물결이 퍼지듯 작은 영향이 번지는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: exposing human folly to ridicule

examples.text: a persistent campaign of mockery by the satirical fortnightly magazine

origin.ko: satire에 -ical이 붙은 말로, 풍자하는 성질을 뜻합니다.

senses.en: of or relating to meaning or the study of meaning

examples.text: The dispute turned on a semantic distinction between the words "permit" and "authorize."

senses.en: Petty or trivial; (of a person or statement) quibbling, niggling.

examples.text: Critics dismissed the objection as merely semantic, a quibble over words rather than substance.

origin.ko: 그리스어 sēmantikos(의미를 나타내는)에서 왔습니다. 기호가 가리키는 의미에 관한 것을 뜻합니다.

senses.en: a person employed to keep watch for some anticipated event

examples.text: A lone sentinel paced the castle wall through the night, watching the dark road for riders.

origin.ko: 이탈리아어 sentinella(보초)에서 왔고, sentire(감지하다)와 이어집니다. 주변을 살피며 감지하는 사람입니다.

senses.en: capable of meeting financial obligations

examples.text: Despite a difficult year, the company remained solvent and paid all its suppliers on time.

senses.en: a liquid substance capable of dissolving other substances

examples.text: Water is often called the universal solvent because it dissolves so many different substances.

origin.ko: 라틴어 solvens(풀어내는)에서 왔습니다. 빚을 '풀어 갚을' 수 있다는 데서 지불 능력이 있다는 뜻이 나왔습니다.

senses.en: not dense

examples.text: trees were sparse

origin.ko: 라틴어 sparsus(흩뿌려진)에서 왔습니다. 여기저기 드문드문 흩어진 모습입니다.

senses.en: bitter conflict; heated often violent dissension

examples.text: Years of ethnic strife left the region's economy in ruins.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 estrif(다툼)에서 왔고 strive와 같은 계열입니다. 서로 겨루는 격한 불화입니다.

senses.en: The right or chance to vote, express an opinion, or participate in a decision, especially in a democratic election.

examples.text: The movement campaigned for universal suffrage regardless of property or sex.

origin.ko: 라틴어 suffrāgium(지지, 투표권)에서 왔습니다. 의견을 지지하는 한 표를 뜻합니다.

senses.en: someone who takes the place of another person

examples.text: A mixture of horseradish and mustard often serves as a surrogate for wasabi.

senses.en: providing or receiving nurture or parental care though not related by blood or legal ties

examples.text: The old nurse became a surrogate mother to the orphaned children.

origin.ko: 라틴어 surrogāre(대신 뽑다)에서 왔습니다. 다른 사람 대신 선택된 대리인입니다.

senses.en: not easily borne; wearing

examples.text: a taxing problem

senses.en: A formal, usually lengthy, systematic discourse on some subject.

examples.text: Locke's treatise on government shaped the political thinking of generations of revolutionaries.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 traitis('논고')에서 왔고 traitier('다루다')와 이어집니다. 한 주제를 다룬 글이 '논문'입니다.

senses.en: not practical or realizable; speculative

examples.text: Critics dismissed the plan to colonize the ocean floor as a visionary scheme with no budget behind it.

senses.en: a person with unusual powers of foresight

examples.text: The founder was a true visionary who imagined the modern city long before it was built.

origin.ko: vision에 -ary를 붙인 말입니다. 눈에 보이는 환상을 좇는다는 뜻이 '공상적인'입니다.

senses.en: a healthy capacity for vigorous activity

examples.text: The city's vitality showed in its crowded cafes, packed theaters, and ever-changing skyline.

senses.en: the property of being able to survive and grow

examples.text: Scientists tested the vitality of the ancient seed by planting it in warm soil.

origin.ko: 라틴어 vitalitas('생명력')에서 왔고 vīta('삶')와 이어집니다.

senses.en: To lie in wait for and attack from ambush.

examples.text: Bandits waylaid the merchant's caravan in a narrow canyon and made off with the goods.

senses.en: To accost or intercept unexpectedly.

examples.text: Reporters waylaid the senator in the corridor and demanded an answer about the scandal.

origin.ko: way('길')와 lay('놓다')의 결합이고 중세 네덜란드어 wegelagen을 본뜬 것으로 봅니다. 길목에 숨어 기다리는 것이 '매복 습격하다'입니다.

senses.en: make reference to

examples.text: In his closing remarks, the senator adverted briefly to the budget crisis he had faced earlier.

senses.en: give heed (to)

examples.text: Readers should advert to the footnotes, where the author qualifies many of her boldest claims.

origin.ko: 라틴어 advertere(~쪽으로 돌리다)에서 왔습니다. 주의를 그쪽으로 돌린다는 뜻에서 '언급하다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: make amendments to

examples.text: Lawmakers voted to amend the constitution so that elections could be held every four years.

senses.en: set straight or right

examples.text: He tried to amend his earlier carelessness by working extra hours through the winter.

origin.ko: 라틴어 emendare(결점을 없애다)에서 왔습니다. 잘못을 걷어내 고친다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: a state of lawlessness and disorder (usually resulting from a failure of government)

examples.text: After the dictator fell, the capital descended into anarchy as rival militias fought for control.

origin.ko: 그리스어 anarchia(지배자 없음)에서 왔습니다. 다스리는 이가 없는 무질서 상태입니다.

senses.en: an inclination to evaluate reality exclusively in terms of human values

examples.text: Environmental philosophers criticize anthropocentrism for treating nature as valuable only when it serves human needs.

origin.ko: 20세기 초에 anthropocentric에 -ism을 붙여 만든 말입니다. 인간을 세계의 중심에 두는 입장입니다.

senses.en: an ardent early supporter of a cause or reform

examples.text: an apostle of revolution

origin.ko: 그리스어 apostolos(파견된 사람)에서 왔습니다. 사명을 띠고 보내진 사람이 '열렬한 주창자'로 이어졌습니다.

senses.en: commanding attention

examples.text: an arresting drawing of people turning into animals

origin.ko: arrest(멈추게 하다)에서 나온 말입니다. 발길을 붙잡을 만큼 눈길을 끈다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: annoy persistently

examples.text: He kept badgering her about her bad habits.

origin.ko: 동물 오소리를 뜻하는 말로, 이마의 배지(badge) 같은 흰 줄무늬에서 이름이 붙었다고 합니다. 끈질기게 괴롭히는 동사 뜻은 여기서 파생되었습니다.

senses.en: light teasing repartee

examples.text: The easy banter between the two anchors made the evening news feel almost like a conversation.

senses.en: an act that debases or corrupts

examples.text: Purists condemned the remake as a bastardization of the original novel's quiet moral force.

senses.en: lacking stimulating characteristics; uninteresting

examples.text: The film's bland script offered no surprises and little reason to care about its characters.

senses.en: lacking taste or flavor or tang

examples.text: The patient was put on a bland diet of rice, toast, and plain broth.

origin.ko: 라틴어 blandus('상냥한, 부드러운')를 빌려 온 말입니다. 자극 없이 순한 맛이라는 뜻으로 이어졌습니다.

senses.en: To brag; to talk loudly in praise of oneself.

examples.text: The young executive boasted constantly about his promotions, which tired his colleagues quickly.

senses.en: To possess (a special and desirable quality).

examples.text: The hotel boasts one of the best views of the sea.

origin.ko: 중세 영어 bost('자랑, 소란')에서 왔고, 게르만어 '부풀어 오른, 우쭐한'에서 유래한 것으로 봅니다.

senses.en: any organization in which action is obstructed by insistence on unnecessary procedures and red tape

examples.text: Entrepreneurs complained that bureaucracy delayed every permit by months and discouraged new investment.

senses.en: The body of officers and administrators, especially of a government.

examples.text: The federal bureaucracy grew rapidly during the war, adding thousands of clerks and several new agencies.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 bureaucratie에서 왔고, bureau(사무소)와 -cratie(지배)가 합쳐졌습니다. 책상 앞 관리들의 지배입니다.

senses.en: A single very brief appearance, especially by a prominent celebrity in a movie or song.

examples.text: The famous director made a brief cameo as a taxi driver in his own film.

senses.en: engraving or carving in low relief on a stone (as in a brooch or ring)

examples.text: Her grandmother's cameo, carved from shell, showed a delicate profile of a young woman.

origin.ko: 이탈리아어 cammeo(양각 보석 장식)에서 왔고 기원은 불명입니다. 브로치 속 얼굴처럼 눈에 띄는 짧은 출연이 연상됩니다.

senses.en: be fond of; be attached to

examples.text: I cherish your friendship.

senses.en: To treat with affection, care, and tenderness; to nurture or protect with care.

examples.text: For decades she cherished the hope that her missing brother would one day return home.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 cherir에서 왔고, cher(소중한)는 라틴어 cārus(사랑하는)에서 갈라졌습니다.

senses.en: work together on a common enterprise or project

examples.text: Physicists and biologists increasingly collaborate on problems that span both disciplines.

senses.en: cooperate as a traitor

examples.text: After the war, officials who had collaborated with the occupiers were put on trial.

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 collabōrāre('함께 일하다')에서 왔고 collaborator에서 거꾸로 만들어진 말입니다.

senses.en: make firm or secure; strengthen

examples.text: The new government moved quickly to consolidate its power after the election.

senses.en: bring together into a single whole or system

examples.text: The town and county schools are being consolidated

origin.ko: 라틴어 consolidō에서 왔고, solidus(단단한)에서 갈라졌습니다. 흩어진 것을 한데 단단히 굳힌다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: with the terms of the relation reversed

examples.text: Higher taxes can reduce spending; conversely, tax cuts often stimulate it.

senses.en: cheat or trick

examples.text: The charlatan cozened the widow out of her life savings with promises of a miracle cure.

senses.en: Bad-tempered or cantankerous.

examples.text: The crabbed old librarian scowled at every student who dared to whisper between the stacks.

senses.en: Crowded together and difficult to read.

examples.text: Her crabbed handwriting forced the archivist to spend hours deciphering a single page of the diary.

origin.ko: crab(게)에 -ed가 붙은 말입니다. 게처럼 까칠한 성미를 가리킵니다.

senses.en: marked by skill in deception

examples.text: cunning men often pass for wise

senses.en: shrewdness as demonstrated by being skilled in deception

examples.text: The spy escaped through sheer cunning, persuading the guards that he was a visiting inspector.

senses.en: showing inventiveness and skill

examples.text: the cunning maneuvers leading to his success

origin.ko: 고대 영어 cunnan(~할 줄 알다)의 현재분사에서 왔습니다. '아는 것이 많은'이 '교활한'으로 변했습니다.

senses.en: To obtain or receive (something) from something else.

examples.text: Reading books is the best way to derive knowledge.

senses.en: To originate or stem (from).

examples.text: Her excellent organisation skills derive from her time as a secretary in the army.

origin.ko: 라틴어 dērīvō '물을 끌어내다'에서 왔고 rīvus(시내)가 뿌리입니다. 물줄기를 끌어오듯 '얻다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: Something that is wished for, or considered desirable, particularly when thought to be essential.

examples.text: For the committee, transparency was the chief desideratum in any new funding procedure.

origin.ko: 라틴어 dēsīderātum '바라던 것'에서 왔습니다. 별(sīdus)에서 왔다는 설이 있지만 불확실합니다.

senses.en: turn away from by persuasion

examples.text: The steep entry fee was enough to deter most casual visitors from attending the exhibition.

senses.en: To prevent something from happening.

examples.text: Heavy fines are intended to deter companies from dumping waste into the river.

origin.ko: 라틴어 dēterreō(겁주어 쫓다)에서 왔습니다. 겁을 줘서 하려던 일을 단념시킨다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: Causing damage or harm.

examples.text: Smoking tobacco can be detrimental to your health.

origin.ko: 라틴어 dētrīmentum(손해)에서 왔고 dēterō(닳게 문지르다)가 뿌리입니다. 닳아 없어지는 이미지입니다.

senses.en: An act or expression of condemnation or disapproval, especially on moral grounds.

examples.text: The council's disapprobation of the plan was evident in the stony silence that followed.

senses.en: lack of agreement or harmony

examples.text: Discord among the coalition partners threatened to bring down the government before the budget vote.

senses.en: a harsh mixture of sounds

examples.text: The untuned instruments produced a painful discord that made the audience wince.

origin.ko: 라틴어 discors(마음이 갈라진)에서 왔습니다. 마음(cor)이 따로따로이니 '불화'입니다.

senses.en: To make distinctions.

examples.text: Since he was color blind he was unable to discriminate between the blue and green bottles.

senses.en: To make decisions harmful to (a person or group) based on prejudice.

examples.text: The law prohibits discriminating against people based on their skin color.

origin.ko: 라틴어 discrīmināre(갈라 구별하다)에서 왔고 discernō(가려내다)와 이어집니다.

senses.en: remove completely from recognition or memory

examples.text: Decades of peace could not efface the memory of the siege from the town's collective mind.

senses.en: make inconspicuous
senses.ko: 눈에 띄지 않게 하다, 자신을 낮추다

examples.text: She tended to efface herself in meetings, letting louder colleagues claim the credit.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 effacer에서 왔습니다. 얼굴(face)을 지워 없앤다는 이미지입니다.

senses.en: A gaseous or vaporous emission, especially a foul-smelling one.

examples.text: A foul effluvium rose from the stagnant canal on hot afternoons.

origin.ko: 라틴어 effluvium(흘러 나감)에서 왔습니다. 밖으로 흘러나오는 냄새를 뜻합니다.

senses.en: A state of being bright and radiant, splendor, brilliance.

examples.text: The effulgence of the setting sun turned the whole valley gold.

origin.ko: 라틴어 fulgere(빛나다)에서 왔습니다. 밖으로 뿜어져 나오는 빛이 '눈부신 광채'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: difficult to detect or grasp by the mind or analyze

examples.text: A precise definition of diarrhea is elusive

senses.en: skillful at eluding capture

examples.text: The elusive criminal was arrested

origin.ko: 라틴어 ēlūdere(피하다, 속이다)의 분사 ēlūsus에서 왔습니다. 자꾸 빠져나가 잡기 어렵다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: right granted by law or contract (especially a right to benefits)

examples.text: entitlements make up the major part of the federal budget

senses.en: A person's perceived but unjustified right to something; a tendency to claim what one does not deserve.

examples.text: A sense of entitlement made the young heir resent ordinary rules.

senses.en: the quality of being faithful

examples.text: The general was admired for his unwavering fidelity to the crown, even in defeat.

senses.en: Accuracy, or exact correspondence, to some given fact or quality; exactness.

examples.text: The translation is praised for its fidelity to the original text, down to the smallest nuance.

origin.ko: 라틴어 fidēlitās(충실)에서 고대 프랑스어를 거쳐 왔습니다. fidēs(믿음)가 바탕입니다.

senses.en: a natural talent

examples.text: he has a flair for mathematics

senses.en: distinctive and stylish elegance

examples.text: The chef presented even the simplest dishes with remarkable flair.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 flair(냄새)에서 왔습니다. 냄새로 알아채는 감각이 '타고난 재능'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: grow vigorously

examples.text: The barley flourished in the warm weather.

senses.en: a showy gesture

examples.text: With many flourishes of the captured banner, they marched down the avenue.

senses.en: move or swing back and forth

examples.text: They flourished the banner as they stormed the palace.

origin.ko: 라틴어 flōrēre(꽃피다)에서 고대 프랑스어를 거쳐 왔습니다. 꽃이 피듯 무성하게 번성한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: marked by excessive or uncontrollable emotion

examples.text: The hysterical crowd surged toward the stage as the band appeared.

senses.en: Provoking uncontrollable laughter.

examples.text: The comedian's impression of the mayor was so hysterical that the audience could barely breathe.

origin.ko: 그리스어 hysterikós '자궁이 아픈'에서 왔고 hystérā(자궁)가 뿌리입니다. 예전에 감정 폭발을 자궁의 병으로 여긴 데서 나왔습니다.

senses.en: close in time; about to occur

examples.text: I have no time right now because of an impending paper submission deadline.

origin.ko: impend(임박하다)에 -ing이 붙은 말입니다. 위에 매달려 곧 떨어질 듯하다는 이미지입니다.

senses.en: not established by conditioning or learning

examples.text: Linguists debate whether humans possess an innate capacity for grammar or acquire it purely through experience.

origin.ko: 라틴어 innātus '타고난'에서 왔습니다. 안에 지닌 채 태어났다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: without compunction or human feeling

examples.text: The insensate tyrant ordered the village burned without a second thought for the families inside.

senses.en: devoid of feeling and consciousness and animation

examples.text: The sculptor spoke to the insensate stone as though it could answer her.

senses.en: Senseless; foolish; irrational; thoughtless.

examples.text: The mob's insensate fury destroyed the very market that fed the town.

origin.ko: 라틴어 īnsēnsātus에서 왔습니다. 느낌(sens)이 없으니 '무감각한'입니다.

senses.en: an expression of approval and commendation

examples.text: The young researcher earned kudos from colleagues for her meticulous, groundbreaking study.

origin.ko: 그리스어 kûdos '찬사, 명성'에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: To imitate, especially in order to ridicule.

examples.text: The comedian could mimic the senator's drawl so precisely that the audience howled.

senses.en: To take on the appearance of another, for protection or camouflage.

examples.text: Several harmless butterfly species mimic the markings of poisonous ones to deter predators.

origin.ko: 라틴어 mīmicus에서 왔고 그리스어 mîmos '흉내 내는 사람, 배우'에서 나왔습니다.

senses.en: too numerous to be counted

examples.text: Earth hosts myriad animals.

senses.en: A countless number or multitude (of specified things)

examples.text: Earth hosts a myriad of animals.

origin.ko: 그리스어 myrias '1만'에서 왔습니다. 만 단위라서 셀 수 없이 많다는 뜻이 되었습니다.

senses.en: In spite of, despite.

examples.text: Notwithstanding repeated warnings, the company continued to dump waste into the river.

senses.en: Nevertheless, all the same.

examples.text: He, notwithstanding, persisted in his inquiries.

origin.ko: 중세 영어에서 not과 withstanding(맞서 버팀)을 합쳐 만든 말로, '~이 막지 못하더라도'라는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: The best or most favorable condition, or the greatest amount or degree possible under specific sets of comparable circumstances.

examples.text: Crop yields reach their optimum when rainfall and temperature stay within a narrow range.

senses.en: most desirable possible under a restriction expressed or implied

examples.text: an optimum return on capital

origin.ko: 라틴어 optimus '가장 좋은'의 중성형을 신라틴어로 쓴 말입니다.

senses.en: be persistent, refuse to stop

examples.text: The child persisted and kept asking questions

senses.en: To continue to exist.

examples.text: Throughout the period, toothy giants persisted in the oceans. Perhaps the most spectacular was the megalodon shark.

origin.ko: 라틴어 persistere '끝까지 서 있다'에서 왔습니다. 물러나지 않고 계속 버틴다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: the highest level or degree attainable; the highest stage of development

examples.text: Winning the Nobel Prize was the pinnacle of her scientific career.

senses.en: a lofty peak

examples.text: Climbers reached the rocky pinnacle just before sunrise.

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 pinnāculum '봉우리'에서 왔고, 라틴어 pinna와 이어집니다. 가장 높은 꼭대기를 뜻합니다.

senses.en: prove superior

examples.text: The champion prevailed, though it was a hard fight

senses.en: To be current, widespread, or predominant; to have currency or prevalence.

examples.text: In his day and age, such practices prevailed all over Europe.

senses.en: use persuasion successfully

examples.text: He prevailed upon her to visit his parents

origin.ko: 라틴어 praevaleō('더 힘이 세다')에서 왔습니다. 남보다 힘이 앞서 이긴다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: Related to procedure.

examples.text: The judge dismissed the case on procedural grounds: it wasn't the facts or the law, but just that they hadn't filed the correct forms.

origin.ko: procedure에 -al이 붙은 말입니다. 라틴어 prōcēdere('앞으로 나아가다')에서 '절차'의 뜻이 나왔습니다.

senses.en: To cause someone to become annoyed or angry.

examples.text: Don't provoke the dog; it may try to bite you.

senses.en: call forth (emotions, feelings, and responses)

examples.text: The film's final scene provoked an unexpected burst of laughter from the audience.

origin.ko: 라틴어 prōvocāre('불러내다')에서 왔습니다. 싸우자고 앞으로 불러내는 데서 '도발하다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: fighting with the fists

examples.text: Victorian crowds gathered by the thousands to watch bare-knuckle pugilism in country fields.

origin.ko: 라틴어 pugil('주먹싸움꾼')에 -ism이 붙은 말입니다. 주먹으로 싸우는 권투를 뜻합니다.

senses.en: Given to quirks or idiosyncrasies; strange in a somewhat silly, awkward manner, potentially cute.

examples.text: The film's quirky humor and odd characters made it a cult favorite.

senses.en: marked by a carefree unconventionality or disreputableness

examples.text: The painter's raffish charm and shabby velvet coat made him a favorite at every bohemian gathering.

origin.ko: raff('하층민')에 -ish가 붙은 말로, riffraff와 이어집니다. 격식에 매이지 않는 제멋대로의 태도를 뜻합니다.

senses.en: (often followed by ‘of’) a large number or amount or extent

examples.text: The new law was accompanied by a raft of amendments that confused even seasoned lawyers.

senses.en: Rife, or occurring widely, frequently or menacingly.

examples.text: There was rampant corruption in the city.

senses.en: unrestrained and violent

examples.text: rampant aggression

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 ramper('기어오르다')의 현재분사에서 왔습니다. 뒷발로 일어선 사나운 모습에서 '걷잡을 수 없는'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: praise enthusiastically

examples.text: She raved about that new restaurant

senses.en: To speak or write wildly or incoherently.

examples.text: The feverish patient raved through the night, calling out names no one in the room recognized.

senses.en: an extravagantly enthusiastic review

examples.text: he gave it a rave

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 raver('헛소리하다')에서 왔고 어원은 불확실합니다. 미친 듯 떠든다는 데서 열광적으로 칭찬한다는 뜻이 되었습니다.

senses.en: To obtain or receive as a reward, in a good or a bad sense.

examples.text: Companies that invested early in research are now reaping the rewards of their patience.

senses.en: gather, as of natural products

examples.text: Farmers gathered at dawn to reap the wheat before the autumn rains arrived.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 rēopan('베다')에서 왔습니다. 곡식을 베어 거두듯 결과를 거둔다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: have an effect for good or ill

examples.text: Her efforts will redound to the general good

senses.en: To contribute to the honour, shame etc. of a person or organisation.

examples.text: The scandal will redound to the discredit of everyone who tried to hide the facts.

origin.ko: 라틴어 redundāre('넘쳐 흐르다')에서 왔고 unda('물결')가 어원입니다. 파도가 되돌아오듯 결과가 돌아옵니다.

senses.en: recovering readily from adversity, depression, or the like

examples.text: Small businesses proved resilient during the downturn, adapting quickly to the sudden change in demand.

senses.en: elastic; rebounds readily

examples.text: Rubber is valued for being a resilient material that returns to its shape after stretching.

origin.ko: 라틴어 resilīre('뒤로 튀어 오르다')에서 왔습니다. 눌려도 도로 튀어 오르는 회복력입니다.

senses.en: concerned with or related to the past

examples.text: The study took a retrospective approach, examining medical records from the previous twenty years.

senses.en: an exhibition of a representative selection of an artist's life work

examples.text: The museum's retrospective traced the painter's evolution from early portraits to late abstractions.

origin.ko: 라틴어 retrōspicere('뒤돌아보다')에서 왔습니다. 지나온 과거를 되돌아본다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: causing intense interest, curiosity, or emotion

examples.text: The tabloid ran a sensational account of the scandal, heavy on rumor and light on fact.

senses.en: Exceptionally great.

examples.text: Young Dutch keeper Tim Krul saw his value rocket up with a sensational display.

origin.ko: sensation(감각)에 -al이 붙은 말입니다. 강한 감각과 감정을 자극해 세상을 놀라게 한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: A fake; an imitation that purports to be genuine.

examples.text: The time-share deal was a sham.

senses.en: Intended to deceive; false.

examples.text: It was only a sham wedding: they didn't care much for one another, but wanted their parents to stop hassling them.

senses.en: make believe with the intent to deceive

examples.text: He shammed a headache

origin.ko: 기원이 확실하지 않습니다. shame의 방언형일 것으로 추정됩니다.

senses.en: occurring or operating at the same time

examples.text: The simultaneous release of the film in forty countries broke the previous box-office record.

origin.ko: 라틴어 simul(함께, 동시에)에서 온 중세 라틴어 simultaneus에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: resembling or characteristic of a phantom

examples.text: The spectral chain-rattling and moans gave me the chills.

senses.en: of or relating to a spectrum

examples.text: spectral analysis

origin.ko: spectre(유령)에 -al이 붙은 말로, 라틴어 spectrum(보이는 형상)에서 나왔습니다. 눈에 보이는 환영 같다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: To make an inference based on inconclusive evidence; to surmise or conjecture.

examples.text: We can speculate that in many instances the sharks are not feeding on their victims, but only in a few cases can we guess what they are doing.

senses.en: reflect deeply on a subject

examples.text: philosophers have speculated on the question of God for thousands of years

senses.en: To make a risky trade in the hope of making a profit; to venture or gamble.

examples.text: Many small investors lost their savings by speculating in volatile currency markets.

origin.ko: 라틴어 speculor(망루에서 살피다)에서 왔습니다. 멀리서 내다보며 짐작한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: cause to be perplexed or confounded

examples.text: This problem stumped her

senses.en: travel through a district and make political speeches

examples.text: the candidate stumped the Northeast

senses.en: The remains of something that has been cut off; especially the remains of a tree, the remains of a limb.

examples.text: Children sat on the stump of the old oak and watched the workers clear the lot.

origin.ko: 중세 저지 독일어 stump(그루터기)와 같은 계열입니다. 그루터기에 걸려 막힌 듯 쩔쩔맨다는 이미지입니다.

senses.en: lower in rank or importance

examples.text: The several kinds […] and subordinate species of each are easily known.

senses.en: rank or order as less important or consider of less value

examples.text: Art is sometimes subordinated to Science in these schools

senses.en: an assistant subject to the authority or control of another

examples.text: A good manager listens carefully to every subordinate, however junior.

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 subōrdināre(아래 서열에 두다)에서 왔습니다. 서열이 아래인 하위의 뜻입니다.

senses.en: balance among the parts of something

examples.text: The architect prized the perfect symmetry of the building's two wings.

senses.en: (mathematics) an attribute of a shape or relation; exact reflection of form on opposite sides of a dividing line or plane

examples.text: A snowflake displays six-fold symmetry about its center.

origin.ko: 그리스어 symmetria에서 왔고 '함께 잰 것'을 뜻합니다. 부분들이 같은 척도로 맞는 균형입니다.

senses.en: the grammatical arrangement of words in sentences

examples.text: The poet's unusual syntax forces readers to pause and reconstruct each sentence's meaning.

origin.ko: 그리스어 syntaxis(함께 배열함)에서 왔습니다. 단어를 알맞게 늘어놓는 문장 구조입니다.

senses.en: so lacking in interest as to cause mental weariness

examples.text: The auditor spent weeks on the tedious task of reconciling thousands of nearly identical invoices by hand.

senses.en: using or containing too many words

examples.text: The report's tedious preamble buried its single useful recommendation under pages of needless qualification.

origin.ko: 라틴어 taedium(싫증, 지침)에서 온 taediōsus에서 왔습니다. 지치고 싫증 나는 지루함입니다.

senses.en: Moderated or balanced by other considerations.

examples.text: The council gave the plan a tempered endorsement, approving it while demanding stricter oversight of costs.

senses.en: made hard or flexible or resilient especially by heat treatment

examples.text: The vault door was fitted with tempered glass that could withstand repeated blows.

origin.ko: temper(누그러뜨리다)의 과거분사입니다. 다른 요소로 조절되어 완화되었다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: Uncertain; subject to future change.

examples.text: We have a tentative plan for the weekend, but nothing is confirmed yet.

senses.en: unsettled in mind or opinion

examples.text: The student offered a tentative answer, watching the professor's face for any sign of approval.

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 tentātīvus('시험해 보는')에서 왔습니다. 일단 해 보는 단계라서 '잠정적인'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: of or relating to or inhabiting the land as opposed to the sea or air

examples.text: Unlike its aquatic cousins, this terrestrial salamander spends nearly its whole life beneath fallen logs.

senses.en: concerned with the world or worldly matters

examples.text: The poet turned from celestial visions to the plain terrestrial concerns of rent and bread.

origin.ko: 라틴어 terra('땅')에서 온 terrestris에서 왔습니다. 땅에 속한다는 뜻에서 '육지의'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: overly sweet

examples.text: The film's treacly ending, full of tearful reunions and swelling violins, felt manipulative rather than moving.

senses.en: To proceed, to behave (in a certain manner).

examples.text: Negotiators must tread carefully when discussing the disputed border with both delegations in the room.

senses.en: To crush under the foot; to trample in contempt or hatred; to subdue; to repress.

examples.text: The regime sought to tread down every voice of dissent in the capital.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 tredan('밟다')에서 왔습니다. 땅을 밟으며 나아가는 모습이 '처신하다'로 번졌습니다.

senses.en: characterized by unrest or disorder or insubordination

examples.text: The mid-19th century was a turbulent time in American history.

senses.en: (of a liquid) agitated vigorously; in a state of turbulence

examples.text: Kayakers avoided the turbulent rapids below the dam after the heavy rains.

origin.ko: 라틴어 turbulentus에서 왔고 turba('소란, 군중')와 이어집니다. 어수선하게 휘몰아치는 모습입니다.

senses.en: the position of greatest importance or advancement; the leading position in any movement or field

examples.text: The laboratory has remained in the vanguard of research on renewable energy for two decades.

senses.en: The leading units at the front of an army or fleet.

examples.text: The army's vanguard crossed the river at dawn, well ahead of the main force.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 avant('앞')와 garde('경비')의 결합입니다. 맨 앞에서 지키는 부대가 '선봉'입니다.

senses.en: a difference between conflicting facts or claims or opinions

examples.text: The witness's account was at variance with the security footage, which raised doubts about her testimony.

senses.en: the second moment around the mean; the expected value of the square of the deviations of a random variable from its mean value

examples.text: A larger variance means the data points are spread more widely around the average value.

senses.en: an official dispensation to act contrary to a rule or regulation (typically a building regulation)

examples.text: a zoning variance

origin.ko: 라틴어 variantia에서 왔고 vary에 -ance를 붙인 형태입니다. 서로 달라서 '불일치'입니다.

senses.en: a large open vessel for holding or storing liquids

examples.text: a vat of liquid

origin.ko: 고대 영어 fæt('통, 그릇')의 방언형 vat에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: Sticky, slimy, or glutinous.

examples.text: The snail left a viscid trail across the stone path after the rain.

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 viscidus에서 왔고 viscum('새 잡는 끈끈이')과 이어집니다.

senses.en: put up with something or somebody unpleasant

examples.text: The editor could not abide careless prose and returned the manuscript with every page heavily marked.

senses.en: Used in a phrasal verb: abide by (“to accept and act in accordance with”).

examples.text: All member nations promised to abide by the ruling of the international tribunal.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 ābīdan(기다리다, 머물다)에서 왔습니다. 끝까지 버티며 기다리는 데서 '참다, 견디다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: follow through or carry out a plan without deviation

examples.text: Auditors must adhere strictly to the professional standards set by the regulatory body.

senses.en: come or be in close contact with; stick or hold together and resist separation

examples.text: The paint failed to adhere to the damp wall and peeled away within days.

senses.en: be a devoted follower or supporter

examples.text: Many members of the movement adhered to the doctrine long after its founder had died.

origin.ko: 라틴어 adhaerere(~에 달라붙다)에서 왔습니다. 딱 붙어 떨어지지 않는 데서 '고수하다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: a close connection marked by community of interests or similarity in nature or character

examples.text: Critics noted a striking affinity between the painter's early work and Japanese woodblock prints.

senses.en: A natural attraction or feeling of kinship to a person or thing.

examples.text: She felt a natural affinity for the desert and returned to it every spring.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 affinité에서 왔고 라틴어로 '경계를 맞댄'이라는 뜻입니다. 이웃처럼 가까운 관계가 '밀접한 관련'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: furnishing added support

examples.text: a right of way appurtenant to land or buildings

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 apurtenant에서 왔고 '속하다'라는 뜻의 appertain과 같은 뿌리입니다.

senses.en: To declare with assurance or plainly and strongly; to state positively.

examples.text: He would often assert that there was life on other planets.

senses.en: insist on having one's opinions and rights recognized

examples.text: Women should assert themselves more!

origin.ko: 라틴어 asserere(손을 얹어 자유인이라 선언하다)에서 왔습니다. 확신을 갖고 당당히 선언한다는 뜻이 되었습니다.

senses.en: the quality of being honest and straightforward in attitude and speech

examples.text: Readers admired the candidness of the memoir, which described the author's failures without excuses.

senses.en: a closed political meeting

examples.text: The party caucus met behind closed doors to settle on a candidate before the vote.

senses.en: meet to select a candidate or promote a policy

examples.text: Lawmakers from the region caucused to agree on a common position before the budget debate.

origin.ko: 기원은 불명입니다. 북미 원주민 알곤킨어에서 왔다는 설이 자주 거론됩니다.

senses.en: wearing or provided with clothing; sometimes used in combination

examples.text: Her downcast eyes were almost mesmerized by the huge tweed-clad knees which towered like monoliths beside her.

senses.en: having an outer covering especially of thin metal

examples.text: armor-clad

origin.ko: 중세 영어 clethen('옷을 입히다')의 과거분사에서 왔고, 천(cloth)과 같은 계통입니다.

senses.en: hide under a false appearance

examples.text: The regime cloaked its repression in the language of national security.

senses.en: anything that covers or conceals

examples.text: Night hid her movements with its cloak of darkness.

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 clocca('종')에서 왔습니다. 종 모양의 여행용 망토에서 왔고, 몸을 덮어 감추는 뜻이 되었습니다.

senses.en: To meditate, to ponder, to think deeply.

examples.text: He cogitated for weeks before deciding whether to leave academia for industry.

origin.ko: 라틴어 cōgitō('생각하다')에서 왔고 1570년에 처음 기록됩니다.

senses.en: take the first step or steps in carrying out an action

examples.text: The speeches commenced three days of workshops, seminars, and cultural activities.

origin.ko: 앵글로노르만어 comencer에서 왔고, 속라틴어 *cominitiāre(com- + initiō)가 뿌리입니다. initiate와 같은 계통입니다.

senses.en: an abstract part of something

examples.text: Hydrogen and oxygen are the constituents of water.

senses.en: a member of a constituency; a citizen who is represented in a government by officials for whom he or she votes

examples.text: The congresswoman answered letters from constituents worried about rising healthcare costs.

origin.ko: 라틴어 cōnstituēns에서 왔고, com-(함께)과 statuō(세우다)가 합쳐졌습니다. 함께 세워 이루는 부분입니다.

senses.en: corrupt morally or by intemperance or sensuality

examples.text: Moralists feared that cheap novels would deprave the young and undermine social order.

origin.ko: 라틴어 dēprāvāre(비틀다, 타락시키다)에서 왔고 pravus(비뚤어진)가 뿌리입니다.

senses.en: To order, command, control.

examples.text: Etiquette dictates that wedding invitations should be acknowledged in writing.

senses.en: a guiding principle

examples.text: the dictates of reason

origin.ko: 라틴어 dictō(되풀이해 말하다)에서 왔습니다. 말로 불러주는 데서 '명령하다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: To recognize as different or distinct.

examples.text: How do you differentiate a fake smile from a genuine one?

senses.en: To show or be the difference or distinction between things.

examples.text: What differentiates an alligator from a crocodile?

senses.en: become different during development

examples.text: cells differentiate

origin.ko: 라틴어 differentia(차이)에서 왔고 difference에서 파생한 말입니다.

senses.en: a loud harsh or strident noise

examples.text: The din of the construction site made conversation across the street nearly impossible.

senses.en: instill (into a person) by constant repetition

examples.text: he dinned the lessons into his students

origin.ko: 고대 영어 dyne(소음)에서 왔고 인도유럽어 어근 '소리 내다'로 거슬러 올라갑니다.

senses.en: afflicted with or marked by anxious uneasiness or trouble or grief

examples.text: She is distressed because she can't find her keys.

senses.en: facing or experiencing financial trouble or difficulty

examples.text: distressed companies need loans and technical advice

senses.en: To linger (on); to remain fixated.

examples.text: Stop dwelling on the past!

senses.en: be an inhabitant of or reside in

examples.text: The poor man dwells in a humble cottage near the hall where the lord of the domain resides.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 dwellan(헤매게 하다, 속이다)에서 왔습니다. 오래 머무르는 뜻으로 바뀌었고, 한 생각에 머물러 '곰곰이 되새기다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: avoiding waste

examples.text: The economical shopper compared prices at three stores before buying a single appliance.

senses.en: using the minimum of time or resources necessary for effectiveness

examples.text: a modern economical heating system

origin.ko: 그리스어 oikonomikós(가정 관리의)에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: A state of ongoing change.

examples.text: The schedule is in flux at the moment.

senses.en: a flow or discharge

examples.text: Researchers tracked the steady flux of migrants across the border over two decades.

origin.ko: 라틴어 fluxus(흐름)에서 고대 프랑스어를 거쳐 왔습니다. 계속 흘러 변한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: inspiring fear

examples.text: The team faced the formidable task of rebuilding the bridge before winter arrived.

senses.en: extremely impressive in strength or excellence

examples.text: a formidable opponent

origin.ko: 라틴어 formīdābilis(무시무시한)에서 왔고 formīdō(공포)가 바탕입니다. 두려워할 만한 상대라는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: a strong wind moving 45-90 knots; force 7 to 10 on Beaufort scale

examples.text: A gale tore shingles from the roofs and kept the ferries tied up in harbor.

senses.en: An outburst, especially of laughter.

examples.text: The comedian's closing joke drew a gale of laughter from the audience.

senses.en: exhibiting or restored to vigorous good health

examples.text: Though nearly ninety, the retired professor remained hale and walked to campus every morning.

senses.en: To drag or pull, especially forcibly.

examples.text: The protesters were haled before the magistrate to answer for the disturbance.

origin.ko: 고대영어 hāl '온전한, 건강한'에서 왔고 whole과 같은 뿌리입니다.

senses.en: To dominate or intimidate in a blustering way; to bully, to domineer.

examples.text: The coach was known to hector his players until they were too frightened to make mistakes.

origin.ko: 호메로스의 일리아드에 나오는 트로이 영웅 Hector에서 왔습니다. 영웅 행세하듯 큰소리치며 남을 윽박지른다는 뜻이 되었습니다.

senses.en: respectful deference

examples.text: The ceremony paid homage to the volunteers who rebuilt the town after the earthquake.

senses.en: An artistic work imitating another in a flattering style.

examples.text: The director's final scene is a loving homage to the silent comedies of the 1920s.

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 homināticum '봉신으로서의 봉사'에서 왔고 라틴어 homō(사람)가 뿌리입니다. 주군에게 바치는 충성이 '경의'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: A possible, or indirect, effect or result of a decision or action.

examples.text: Dumping waste in the river will have serious implications for the environment.

senses.en: a meaning that is not expressly stated but can be inferred

examples.text: The implication of her silence was clear: she disapproved of the plan but would not say so.

origin.ko: 라틴어 implicātiō '얽어 넣음'에서 왔습니다. 안에 접혀 들어 있는 간접적 결과를 뜻합니다.

senses.en: To harass with persistent requests.

examples.text: Reporters importuned the senator for a statement as he hurried toward the waiting car.

origin.ko: 라틴어 importūnus '항구가 없는'에서 왔습니다. 배를 댈 항구가 없는 듯 곤란하게 끈질기게 조릅니다.

senses.en: produce a literary work

examples.text: The poet retired to a cottage by the sea to indite a long elegy for her late mentor.

origin.ko: indict의 변형으로, 후기 라틴어 indictāre에서 왔습니다. 말한 것을 글로 받아 적는 데서 '쓰다, 짓다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: producing a sizeable profit

examples.text: Selling software subscriptions proved far more lucrative than the company's original hardware business.

origin.ko: 프랑스어를 거쳐 라틴어 lucrativus '이익이 되는'에서 왔고 lucrum(이익)에서 나왔습니다.

senses.en: move heavily or clumsily

examples.text: The heavy man lumbered across the room

senses.en: To load down with things, to fill, to encumber, to impose an unwanted burden on.

examples.text: I got lumbered with that boring woman all afternoon.

senses.en: the wood of trees cut and prepared for use as building material

examples.text: The builders ordered several tons of lumber for the new community center.

senses.en: The blundering use of an absurdly inappropriate word or expression in place of a similar-sounding one.
senses.ko: 비슷한 소리의 말로 잘못 쓰는 우스꽝스러운 실수

examples.text: The script employed malapropism to great effect.

origin.ko: 셰리든의 희곡 속 인물 Mrs. Malaprop의 이름에서 왔습니다. 이름은 프랑스어 mal à propos '부적절하게'에서 만든 것으로 보입니다.

senses.en: someone shirking their duty by feigning illness or incapacity

examples.text: The army doctor quickly exposed the recruit as a malingerer faking a back injury.

origin.ko: malinger(꾀병 부리다)에 '~하는 사람'을 뜻하는 -er이 붙었습니다.

senses.en: shackle that consists of a metal loop that can be locked around the wrist; usually used in pairs

examples.text: The guards removed the manacles from the prisoner's wrists before he entered the courtroom.

senses.en: confine or restrain with or as if with manacles or handcuffs

examples.text: Guards manacled the prisoner at the wrists before leading him down to the cells.

origin.ko: 라틴어 manicula '쟁기 손잡이, 수갑'에서 왔고 manus(손)에서 나왔습니다. 손을 묶는 쇠고랑입니다.

senses.en: chew (food); to bite and grind with the teeth

examples.text: The cow stood, quietly masticating its cud.

origin.ko: 라틴어 masticō '씹다'에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: a large indefinite quantity

examples.text: A multitude of factors contributed to the collapse of the regional economy.

senses.en: The mass of ordinary people; the masses, the populace.

examples.text: The orator addressed himself to the multitude gathered below the balcony.

origin.ko: 라틴어 multus '많은'에 상태를 나타내는 -tūdō가 붙은 multitūdō에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: reflect deeply on a subject

examples.text: She sat by the window and mused on how much the city had changed since her childhood.

senses.en: the source of an artist's inspiration

examples.text: Yoko Ono was John Lennon's wife, lover, and muse.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 muser에서 왔습니다. 멍하니 생각에 잠긴다는 뜻으로 '깊이 생각하다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: A form or state of connection.

examples.text: Scholars have long debated the nexus between economic inequality and political instability.

senses.en: A centre or focus of something.

examples.text: The old port city became a nexus of trade, rumor, and cultural exchange.

origin.ko: 라틴어 nectō '묶다, 잇다'에서 나온 nexus로, 묶인 상태, 즉 연결을 뜻합니다.

senses.en: outlying areas (as of a city or town)

examples.text: they lived on the outskirts of Houston

senses.en: A pattern, a way of doing something; especially a pattern of thought, a system of beliefs, a conceptual framework.

examples.text: Darwin's theory overturned the dominant paradigm of fixed species.

senses.en: a standard or typical example

examples.text: The Roman Republic became a paradigm of balanced government for later political thinkers.

origin.ko: 그리스어 parádeigma '본보기'에서 왔습니다. 옆에 놓고 견주도록 보여 주는 모범 틀이라는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: (rhetoric) the concluding section of an oration

examples.text: he summarized his main points in his peroration

origin.ko: 라틴어 perōrō '끝까지 말하다, 연설을 맺다'에서 왔습니다. 연설을 끝까지 말해 마무리하는 부분입니다.

senses.en: continuing forever or indefinitely

examples.text: Medieval alchemists dreamed of a perpetual source of energy and eternal youth.

senses.en: uninterrupted in time and indefinitely long continuing

examples.text: Residents complained of the perpetual noise from the highway outside their windows.

origin.ko: 라틴어 perpetuus '끊임없이 이어지는'에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: characterized by fantastic imagery and incongruous juxtapositions

examples.text: The film's phantasmagorical landscapes blend melting clocks with floating cities.

origin.ko: phantasmagoria(환등 쇼처럼 뒤섞인 환영)에 -ical이 붙은 말입니다.

senses.en: apparently reasonable and credible, and therefore convincing

examples.text: a plausible excuse

senses.en: given to or characterized by presenting specious arguments

examples.text: The plausible salesman argued so smoothly that few noticed the holes in his claims.

origin.ko: 라틴어 plausibilis '박수받을 만한'에서 왔고, plaudere는 '박수치다'입니다. 박수받을 만큼 그럴듯하다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: To beg, beseech, or implore, especially emotionally.

examples.text: He pleaded with me not to leave the house.

senses.en: To offer by way of excuse.

examples.text: Not wishing to attend the banquet, I pleaded illness.

senses.en: enter a plea, as in courts of law

examples.text: She pleaded not guilty

origin.ko: 옛 프랑스어 plaider '변론하다'에서 왔고, 라틴어 placeō '마음에 들다'와 이어집니다. 법정에서 호소하던 데서 간청하다가 되었습니다.

senses.en: a platform raised above the surrounding level to give prominence to the person on it

examples.text: The speaker stepped up to the podium and waited for the applause to fade.

origin.ko: 그리스어 pódion '받침, 작은 발'에서 왔고, poús는 '발'입니다. 사람을 발밑에서 받치는 단입니다.

senses.en: A person who practices a profession or art, especially law or medicine.

examples.text: Experienced practitioners of the craft often disagree about which technique is best for beginners.

origin.ko: 그리스어 prassō('행하다')에서 나온 practician에 -er가 붙은 말입니다. 실제로 일을 행하는 사람을 뜻합니다.

senses.en: intellectually productive

examples.text: a prolific writer

senses.en: bearing in abundance especially offspring

examples.text: flying foxes are extremely prolific

origin.ko: 라틴어 prōlificus에서 왔으며 prōlēs('자손')와 -ficus('만드는')가 합쳐졌습니다. 자손을 많이 낳듯 작품도 많이 냅니다.

senses.en: become putrid; decay with an offensive smell

examples.text: organic matter putrefies

origin.ko: 프랑스어 putréfier에서 왔고 라틴어 putrēs('썩은')와 -fy('~되게 하다')로 이루어졌습니다. 썩어서 악취가 난다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: isolation to prevent the spread of infectious disease

examples.text: Travelers arriving from the affected region were held in quarantine for two weeks.

senses.en: place into enforced isolation, as for medical reasons

examples.text: My dog was quarantined before he could live in England

origin.ko: 라틴어 quadrāgintā('40')에서 온 중세 라틴어 quarentena('40일')에서 왔습니다. 배를 40일 동안 격리하던 데서 나온 말입니다.

senses.en: Oppressed, dominated or plagued by.

examples.text: The region, ridden by corruption and debt, struggled to attract any foreign investment.

origin.ko: ride의 과거분사 형태입니다. '~에 올라타 짓눌린' 데서 시달리는 뜻이 나왔습니다.

senses.en: a personal or social separation (as between opposing factions)

examples.text: The disagreement over funding opened a deep rift between the two founders of the company.

senses.en: A chasm or fissure.

examples.text: The Grand Canyon is a rift in the Earth's surface, but is smaller than some of the undersea ones.

origin.ko: 북유럽어에서 온 말로 '찢어진 틈'을 뜻합니다. 땅의 균열이 사람 사이의 불화로 확장되었습니다.

senses.en: To repent of or regret (some past action or event); to wish that a past action or event had not taken place.

examples.text: I rued the day I crossed paths with her.

senses.en: sadness associated with some wrong done or some disappointment

examples.text: He accepted the verdict with quiet rue, wishing he had spoken up years earlier.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 hrēow(슬픔, 뉘우침)에서 왔습니다. 마음의 아픔이 지난 일을 후회하는 뜻이 되었습니다.

senses.en: To gradually drain (someone's energy or vitality).

examples.text: The relentless humidity sapped the hikers' energy long before they reached the summit.

senses.en: A naive person; a simpleton.

examples.text: Don't be a sap and believe every promise the salesman makes.

senses.en: a watery solution of sugars, salts, and minerals that circulates through the vascular system of a plant

examples.text: In early spring the maple's sap begins to rise, and farmers tap the trunks to collect it.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 sæp(수액)에서 왔습니다. 동사 sap은 프랑스어에서 온 별개의 말로, 땅굴을 파 무너뜨리듯 서서히 약화시킨다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: a genre of literature and performing arts, in which shortcomings are held up to ridicule, ideally with the intent of shaming others

examples.text: Swift's Gulliver's Travels is often read as satire aimed at the political follies of his age.

senses.en: A satirical work.

examples.text: a stinging satire of American politics.

origin.ko: 라틴어 lanx satura(가득 담은 접시)에서 왔습니다. 여러 소재를 뒤섞은 글이 풍자문학이 되었습니다.

senses.en: Shrewd, well-informed and perceptive.

examples.text: A savvy investor, she sold her shares months before the market began to decline.

senses.en: the cognitive condition of someone who understands

examples.text: Her political savvy helped the campaign navigate a series of unexpected crises.

origin.ko: 포르투갈어 sabe(안다)에서 온 크리올어를 거쳐 영어에 들어왔고, 라틴어 sapere에서 나왔습니다.

senses.en: Uncommon, rare; difficult to find; insufficient to meet a demand.

examples.text: By the end of the 20th century elephants had become scarce even in Africa.

origin.ko: 고대 북부 프랑스어 escars(인색한, 부족한)에서 왔고, 어원은 확실하지 않습니다. '뽑아내다'에서 왔다는 설이 있습니다.

senses.en: very irritable

examples.text: The splenetic critic dismissed the entire exhibition in a single bitter paragraph.

origin.ko: 라틴어 splen(비장)에서 왔습니다. 옛날에는 분노가 비장의 체액에서 생긴다고 믿었습니다.

senses.en: Following, next in order.

examples.text: Each succeeding generation inherited a slightly more fragile river ecosystem.

senses.en: concerned with or comprehending only what is apparent or obvious; not deep or penetrating emotionally or intellectually

examples.text: superficial similarities

senses.en: of, affecting, or being on or near the surface

examples.text: superficial burns

senses.en: of little substance or significance

examples.text: a few superficial editorial changes

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 superficiālis(표면의)에서 왔습니다. 겉 표면만 건드려 얕다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: humbly entreating

examples.text: a suppliant sinner seeking forgiveness

senses.en: one praying humbly for something

examples.text: I touch your beard as a suppliant, embrace your knees, imploring you to have pity on my wretchedness.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 suppliant(간청하는)에서 왔고 supplicant와 같은 계열입니다. 무릎을 꿇고 비는 모습입니다.

senses.en: characteristic of or devoted to the temporal world as opposed to the spiritual world

examples.text: Medieval popes claimed authority over temporal rulers as well as over matters of the soul.

senses.en: of or relating to or limited by time

examples.text: The study examined the temporal ordering of events rather than their spatial arrangement.

senses.en: not eternal

examples.text: The preacher reminded the congregation that wealth and fame are merely temporal comforts.

origin.ko: 라틴어 temporālis(시간의)에서 왔습니다. 영원과 대비되는 덧없는 현세의 뜻입니다.

senses.en: not moderated or controlled

examples.text: The young senator's untempered idealism clashed with the compromises that governing demands.

senses.en: not brought to a proper consistency or hardness

examples.text: untempered steel

senses.en: show off

examples.text: The company vaunted its record profits while quietly cutting hundreds of jobs.

origin.ko: 라틴어 vānus('헛된, 허풍 떠는')에서 온 고대 프랑스어 vanter에서 왔습니다. 속 빈 말로 뽐내는 것입니다.

senses.en: physically and mentally fatigued

examples.text: A weary traveller knocked at the door.

senses.en: lose interest or become bored with something or somebody

examples.text: The audience began to weary of the speaker's endless anecdotes.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 wēriġ('지친')에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: a policy of taking direct action to achieve a political or social goal

examples.text: Student activism on the campus grew sharply after the university announced steep tuition increases.

origin.ko: active에 -ism이 붙은 말입니다. 말보다 직접 행동한다는 입장을 가리킵니다.

senses.en: ask for or request earnestly

examples.text: The widow adjured the council to reopen the investigation into her husband's death.

senses.en: command solemnly

examples.text: The judge adjured the witnesses to tell the whole truth, reminding them of the oath they had taken.

origin.ko: 라틴어 adiurare(맹세시키다)에서 왔습니다. 맹세하듯 간곡히 청한다는 뜻이 되었습니다.

senses.en: serving to warn

examples.text: The article served as an admonitory tale about the dangers of unchecked financial speculation.

origin.ko: 라틴어 admonere(일깨우다)에서 나온 말입니다. 주의를 환기시키는 경고성을 뜻합니다.

senses.en: someone who acts as assistant

examples.text: A trusted aide drafted the senator's speech and briefed her before each interview.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 aide(도움, 조수)를 그대로 빌려온 말입니다.

senses.en: the highest point (of something)

examples.text: the apex of the building

origin.ko: 라틴어 apex(끝, 꼭대기)를 그대로 빌려온 말입니다.

senses.en: create and charge with a task or function

examples.text: The governor appointed a panel of experts to review the state's water policy.

senses.en: furnish

examples.text: a beautifully appointed house

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 apointier(정하다)에서 왔고 '요점으로 가져가다'가 원뜻입니다. 사안을 정해 사람을 지명하게 되었습니다.

senses.en: functioning in a supporting capacity

examples.text: the main library and its auxiliary branches

senses.en: Held in reserve for exceptional circumstances.

examples.text: The hospital switched to its auxiliary generators when the main grid failed.

origin.ko: 라틴어 auxiliarius(조력자)에서 왔고 auxilium(도움)에서 나왔습니다.

senses.en: be a signal for or a symptom of

examples.text: The sudden rise in unemployment betokens deeper problems in the region's economy.

senses.en: indicate, as with a sign or an omen

examples.text: Dark clouds on the horizon betokened a storm that sailors had learned to fear.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 betācnian('나타내다, 표시하다')에서 왔고, be-에 token(표지)이 붙은 말입니다.

senses.en: refer to for illustration or proof

examples.text: The author cites several studies to support her claim that sleep improves memory.

senses.en: commend

examples.text: he was cited for his outstanding achievements

senses.en: To summon officially or authoritatively to appear in court.

examples.text: The magistrate cited the landlord to appear before the court the following Monday.

origin.ko: 라틴어 citare('불러내다, 소환하다')에서 왔습니다. 증거를 법정에 불러내듯 '인용하다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: the body of voters who elect a representative for their area

examples.text: The senator spent the recess meeting with members of her constituency across the rural counties.

origin.ko: constituent(구성하는 사람)에 -ency가 붙은 말입니다. 대표를 함께 세우는 유권자 집단입니다.

senses.en: being determined by conditions or circumstances that follow

examples.text: arms sales contingent on the approval of Congress

senses.en: possible but not certain to occur

examples.text: The firm set aside funds for contingent expenses that might arise during construction.

senses.en: a gathering of persons representative of some larger group

examples.text: each nation sent a contingent of athletes to the Olympics

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 contingens('가능한, 우연한')에서 왔고, com-(함께)과 tangere(닿다)가 합쳐졌습니다. 조건에 맞닿아야 일어난다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: To commit (a task or responsibility) to someone, especially a subordinate.

examples.text: A good manager learns to delegate routine tasks so that she can focus on strategy.

senses.en: A person authorized to act as representative for another; a deputy.

examples.text: Each state sent a delegate to the convention to vote on the proposed treaty.

origin.ko: 라틴어 dēlēgāre(보내다, 맡기다)에서 왔습니다. 일을 맡겨 보내는 데서 '위임하다'입니다.

senses.en: expressive of low opinion

examples.text: derogatory comments

senses.en: To see, especially from afar; to discover (a distant or obscure object) by the eye; to espy; to discern or detect.

examples.text: From the crow's nest, the lookout could just descry a faint line of land on the horizon.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 descrier(외쳐 알리다)에서 왔다고 봅니다. decry와 같은 계열의 이중어입니다.

senses.en: To amuse oneself divertingly or playfully; in particular, to cavort or gambol.

examples.text: Children disported themselves in the shallow surf while their parents dozed on the sand.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 desporter(즐겁게 놀다)에서 왔습니다. 일에서 몸을 옮겨 놀이하는 이미지입니다.

senses.en: capacity or power to produce a desired effect

examples.text: concern about the safety and efficacy of the vaccine

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 efficācia에서 왔고 efficere(이루어내다)가 뿌리입니다.

senses.en: To adorn with prominent markings.

examples.text: The team's logo was emblazoned across the front of every jersey.

senses.en: To celebrate or extol as with deeds or merit.

examples.text: Poets sought to emblazon the heroes' deeds in verse for later generations.

origin.ko: en-에 blazon(방패 문장)이 붙었고, blazon은 고대 프랑스어 blason(방패)에서 왔습니다. 방패에 문장을 새기듯 화려하게 장식한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: lasting a long time

examples.text: The enduring appeal of the novel lies in its honest portrait of grief.

senses.en: Willing to co-operate or provide information; candid, frank, responsive.

examples.text: Once I explained why I needed to know, she was really forthcoming.

senses.en: available when required or as promised

examples.text: federal funds were not forthcoming

senses.en: of the relatively near future

examples.text: I shall vote in the forthcoming election.

origin.ko: forth(앞으로)와 coming(오는)이 합쳐졌습니다. 앞으로 나서서 협조하는 데서 '솔직한'이라는 뜻이 나왔습니다.

senses.en: Magnificent and impressive because of appearance, size, stateliness or dignity.

examples.text: an imposing building

origin.ko: impose에서 나온 말로, 라틴어 in-(위에)과 ponere(놓다)가 뿌리입니다. 보는 사람을 위에서 누르듯 압도하는 모습입니다.

senses.en: an accusation of wrongdoing

examples.text: the book is an indictment of modern philosophy

senses.en: a formal document written for a prosecuting attorney charging a person with some offense

examples.text: The grand jury returned an indictment against the mayor on three counts of bribery.

origin.ko: 중세영어 endytement '고발 행위'에서 왔고 라틴어 dicere(말하다)가 뿌리입니다. 잘못을 공식적으로 말해 고발하는 일입니다.

senses.en: arousing to action or rebellion

examples.text: Sam posted an inflammatory comment to the newsgroup.

senses.en: characterized or caused by inflammation

examples.text: Doctors prescribed a drug to reduce the inflammatory response in her damaged joints.

origin.ko: 라틴어 īnflammātōrius에서 왔습니다. 마음에 불꽃을 일으켜 사람들을 격앙시킨다는 이미지입니다.

senses.en: gradually intrusive without right or permission

examples.text: Many users objected to the app's invasive tracking of their location even when it was closed.

senses.en: marked by a tendency to spread especially into healthy tissue

examples.text: invasive cancer cells

origin.ko: 라틴어 invādō '안으로 들어가다, 침입하다'에서 왔습니다. 허락 없이 안으로 밀고 들어오는 느낌입니다.

senses.en: an extreme bellicose nationalist

examples.text: The jingoist columnist demanded military action at the first sign of diplomatic trouble.

senses.en: To release (someone) from slavery; to free.

examples.text: In his will, the planter chose to manumit every enslaved person on his estate.

origin.ko: 라틴어 manūmittere '손에서 내보내다'에서 왔습니다. 주인의 손에서 놓아 보낸다는 데서 '노예 해방'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: To move about in roving fashion looking for plunder; to loiter.

examples.text: Bands of deserters marauded through the countryside, stealing grain and livestock from frightened farmers.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 marauder에서 왔고 maraud '악당, 방랑자'에서 나왔습니다. 떠돌며 약탈하는 모습입니다.

senses.en: Abusive language.

examples.text: The whistleblower endured years of obloquy from former colleagues who accused him of betrayal.

senses.en: state of disgrace resulting from public abuse

examples.text: After the fraud was exposed, the executive died in obloquy, his name stripped from the building.

origin.ko: 라틴어 obloquor '맞서 말하다, 반박하다'에서 왔습니다. 남에게 맞서 퍼붓는 욕설과 비방입니다.

senses.en: the beginning or early stages

examples.text: the onset of pneumonia

senses.en: (military) an offensive against an enemy (using weapons)

examples.text: The sudden onset of the enemy cavalry scattered the unprepared defenders.

origin.ko: on과 set을 합친 말로, 원래 '덮쳐서 공격하다'라는 뜻이었다가 일의 시작을 가리키게 되었습니다.

senses.en: Clearly demonstrative.

examples.text: The teacher gave an ostensive definition by pointing directly at the object while naming it.

senses.en: represented or appearing as such; pretended

examples.text: His ostensive purpose was charity, his real goal popularity.

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 ostēnsīvus에서 왔고, ostendō '앞에 내밀어 보이다'가 원형입니다.

senses.en: beat rapidly

examples.text: His heart palpitated

senses.en: shake with fast, tremulous movements

examples.text: His nostrils palpitated

origin.ko: 라틴어 palpitō '떨다, 두근거리다'에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: Out of the ordinary; odd; strange; unusual.

examples.text: The sky had a peculiar appearance before the storm.

senses.en: Common or usual for a certain place or circumstance; specific or particular.

examples.text: Kangaroos are peculiar to Australia.

origin.ko: 라틴어 pecūliāris '자기 소유의'에서 왔고, pecus는 '가축'입니다. 자기만의 것이라 남과 다르고 독특하다는 뜻이 되었습니다.

senses.en: (of language) transparently clear; easily understandable

examples.text: The lawyer's perspicuous explanation made the complex statute easy for jurors to follow.

origin.ko: 라틴어 perspicuus '속이 환히 보이는'에서 왔습니다. 꿰뚫어 볼 수 있을 만큼 명료하다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: consider, ponder, or plan (an action) beforehand

examples.text: Prosecutors argued that the defendant had premeditated the crime for weeks.

origin.ko: 라틴어 praemeditārī('미리 곰곰이 생각하다')에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: (law) the institution of a sequence of steps by which legal judgments are invoked

examples.text: The company faces criminal proceedings over its handling of customer data.

senses.en: A published collection of papers presented at an academic conference, or representing the acts of a learned society.

examples.text: Her paper appeared in the proceedings of the annual linguistics conference.

origin.ko: proceed('앞으로 나아가다')에 -ing가 붙은 말입니다. 일을 한 단계씩 진행하는 법적 절차를 가리킵니다.

senses.en: make a prediction about; tell in advance

examples.text: Few analysts were willing to prognosticate about the outcome of such an unpredictable election.

senses.en: indicate, as with a sign or an omen

examples.text: The bluebells may prognosticate an early spring this year.

origin.ko: 그리스어 prognōsis('미리 앎')에서 나온 중세 라틴어 prognosticare에서 왔습니다. 앞일을 미리 아는 것이 예측입니다.

senses.en: Long-windedness, tiresome length, an excess of words.

examples.text: The prolixity of the contract made it nearly impossible for ordinary readers to understand.

origin.ko: 라틴어 prolixitas에서 왔으며 prolix('길게 뻗은')에 -ity가 붙었습니다. 말이 쓸데없이 길다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: under terms not final or fully worked out or agreed upon

examples.text: The provisional government promised elections once order had been restored.

origin.ko: provision에 -al이 붙은 말입니다. 라틴어 '미리 보고 마련함'에서 왔고, 임시로 마련한 것이라는 뜻으로 쓰입니다.

senses.en: imprudently incurring risk

examples.text: The CEO's rash decision to expand overseas without research nearly bankrupted the company.

senses.en: a series of unexpected and unpleasant occurrences

examples.text: a rash of bank robberies

senses.en: A fundamental principle or skill, especially in a field of learning.

examples.text: We'll be learning the rudiments of thermodynamics next week.

senses.en: A form that lacks full or complex development.

examples.text: I have the rudiments of an escape plan.

senses.en: the remains of a body part that was functional at an earlier stage of life

examples.text: The whale's pelvic bones are the rudiments of limbs its ancestors once used for walking.

origin.ko: 라틴어 rudimentum(첫 시도)에서 왔습니다. 아직 다듬어지지 않은 기초라는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: lacking in rigor or strictness

examples.text: Regulators criticized the bank for slack oversight that allowed the fraud to continue unnoticed for years.

senses.en: not tense or taut

examples.text: slack and wrinkled skin

senses.en: a noticeable deterioration in performance or quality

examples.text: Economists warned of slack in the labor market as hiring slowed for the third straight quarter.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 slæc(느슨한)에서 왔습니다. 팽팽하지 않고 풀어져 해이하다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: the existing state of affairs

examples.text: Conservative lawmakers resisted the reform because they preferred to preserve the status quo.

origin.ko: 라틴어 status quo(있는 그대로의 상태)에서 왔습니다. 현재 그 상태를 가리킵니다.

senses.en: the quality of being bland and gracious or ingratiating in manner

examples.text: The diplomat handled the tense negotiation with a suavity that disarmed even his harshest critics.

origin.ko: 라틴어 suāvitās(달콤함)에서 왔습니다. 부드럽고 상냥한 태도입니다.

senses.en: capable of being perceived; especially capable of being handled or touched or felt
senses.ko: 만져서 알 수 있는, 실체가 있는
