examples.text: The company could point to no tangible benefit from the expensive consulting project.

senses.en: capable of being treated as fact

examples.text: tangible evidence

senses.en: (of especially business assets) having physical substance and intrinsic monetary value

examples.text: tangible assets such as machinery

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 tangibilis에서 왔고 tangere(만지다)에서 나왔습니다. 만져서 알 수 있는 실체입니다.

senses.en: an extended area of land

examples.text: The developer bought a vast tract of farmland on the edge of the city.

senses.en: a brief treatise on a subject of interest; published in the form of a booklet

examples.text: The reformer distributed a political tract denouncing child labor in the textile mills.

origin.ko: 라틴어 tractus('끌어 늘임')에서 왔고 trahere('끌다')와 이어집니다. 길게 뻗은 공간이 '넓은 땅'입니다.

senses.en: of little substance or significance

examples.text: The committee wasted an hour on trivial objections while the central budget question went unanswered.

senses.en: Commonplace, ordinary.

examples.text: For the novelist, even the most trivial incident of daily life became material for reflection.

origin.ko: 라틴어 trivium('세 길이 만나는 곳')에서 왔습니다. 길거리에서 흔히 오가는 이야기라서 '사소한'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: To take upon oneself; to start, to embark on.

examples.text: They undertook the new venture, not sure where it would lead.

senses.en: To commit oneself (to an obligation, activity etc.).

examples.text: He undertook to exercise more in future.

origin.ko: 중세 영어 undertaken으로, under와 take의 결합입니다. 일을 자기 아래로 받아 든다는 뜻이 '떠맡다'입니다.

senses.en: any piece of work that is undertaken or attempted

examples.text: Building the transcontinental railway was an enormous undertaking that required a decade and thousands of workers.

senses.en: A promise or pledge; a guarantee.

examples.text: The firm gave a formal undertaking to repay all customers who had been overcharged.

origin.ko: undertake에 -ing를 붙인 말입니다. 떠맡은 일이 '사업, 과업'입니다.

senses.en: Not propitious; unfavourable, untimely.

examples.text: Launching a new product during a recession seemed an unpropitious moment, yet the firm proceeded.

senses.en: Effecting no purpose; pointless, futile.

examples.text: Rescuers made a vain attempt to reach the stranded climbers before the storm closed in.

senses.en: Overly proud of oneself, especially concerning appearance; having a high opinion of one's own accomplishments with slight reason.

examples.text: Every writer is a narcissist. This does not mean that he is vain; it only means that he is hopelessly self-absorbed.

origin.ko: 라틴어 vānus('텅 빈')에서 왔습니다. 속이 비어 '헛된'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: competent in many areas and able to turn with ease from one thing to another

examples.text: a versatile writer

senses.en: changeable or inconstant

examples.text: The critic complained of the versatile moods of a monarch whose favor shifted by the hour.

origin.ko: 라틴어 versātilis('쉽게 도는')에서 왔습니다. 이리저리 쉽게 돌려 쓸 수 있다는 뜻이 '다재다능한'입니다.

senses.en: lose clarity or turn aside especially from the main subject of attention or course of argument in writing, thinking, or speaking

examples.text: During the long lecture, my attention began to wander toward the clock on the wall.

senses.en: move about aimlessly or without any destination, often in search of food or employment

examples.text: The children wandered through the old market, stopping at every stall that caught their eye.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 wandrian('떠돌다')에서 왔고 '돌다, 바꾸다'는 뜻의 어근과 이어집니다. 길에서 벗어나 헤매는 것이 '딴 데로 빠지다'입니다.

senses.en: a written agreement between two states or sovereigns

examples.text: The two nations signed a peace accord ending nearly a decade of border disputes.

senses.en: harmony of people's opinions or actions or characters

examples.text: The committee members worked in rare accord, quickly settling the budget questions.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 acorder(마음을 맞추다)에서 왔습니다. 마음이 맞은 결과가 '협정'입니다.

senses.en: a supplementary component that improves capability

examples.text: The mansion's grand staircase and fountains were mere appurtenances to its real value, the land.

senses.en: equipment consisting of miscellaneous articles needed for a particular operation or sport etc.

examples.text: A couple of hair gloves, with a flesh-brush, may be added to the toilet appurtenances.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 apartenance에서 왔고 라틴어 appertinere(속하다)와 연결됩니다. 본체에 딸려 속한 것이 '부속물'입니다.

senses.en: the quality of innocent naivete

examples.text: The child's artlessness disarmed even the most skeptical members of the committee.

origin.ko: artless(꾸밈없는)에 -ness가 붙은 말로, 기교 없이 순수한 상태를 뜻합니다.

senses.en: attribute or credit to

examples.text: This poem is attributed to Browning.

senses.en: A characteristic or quality of a thing.

examples.text: His finest attribute is his kindness.

origin.ko: 라틴어 attribuere(~에게 할당하다)에서 왔습니다. 원인이나 공을 누군가에게 배정한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: To confuse or bewilder.

examples.text: The contradictory instructions bemused the new employees, who could not tell which rule applied.

origin.ko: be-와 muse(곰곰이 생각하다)가 합쳐진 말입니다. 생각에 빠져 멍해진다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: a cushion-like device that reduces shock due to an impact

examples.text: Savings served as a buffer against sudden expenses during the family's difficult year.

senses.en: protect from impact

examples.text: Generous unemployment benefits helped buffer workers from the worst effects of the recession.

origin.ko: 옛 동사 buff('치면 둔탁한 소리가 나다')에 -er가 붙은 말입니다. 충격을 둔탁하게 받아 주는 물건입니다.

senses.en: a loud resonant repeating noise

examples.text: The clangor of the factory bells echoed through the valley at dawn.

senses.en: make a loud resonant noise

examples.text: the alarm clangored throughout the building

senses.en: lessen the intensity of; temper; hold in restraint; hold or keep within limits

examples.text: The new regulations are meant to curb excessive speculation in the housing market.

senses.en: the act of restraining power or action or limiting excess

examples.text: Nothing acts as a stronger curb on reckless spending than a strict, publicly audited budget.

origin.ko: 라틴어 curvus(굽은)에서 프랑스어 courbe를 거쳐 왔습니다. 말을 굽은 재갈 사슬로 제어하는 데서 '억제하다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: An edict or law.

examples.text: The king issued a decree banning all public gatherings after the riots.

senses.en: decide with authority

examples.text: The King decreed that all firstborn males should be killed

origin.ko: 라틴어 dēcrētum(결정된 것)에서 고대 프랑스어를 거쳐 왔습니다.

senses.en: Loss of hope; utter hopelessness; complete despondency.

examples.text: He turned around in despair, aware that he was not going to survive.

senses.en: abandon hope; give up hope; lose heart

examples.text: Don't despair — help is on the way!

origin.ko: 라틴어 dēspērāre(희망을 잃다)에서 고대 프랑스어를 거쳐 왔습니다. 희망(esperer)이 없는 상태입니다.

senses.en: someone who takes spoils or plunder (as in war)

examples.text: The chronicler cursed the despoiler who had stripped the abbey of its gold and manuscripts.

origin.ko: despoil에 -er이 붙어 약탈하는 사람을 뜻합니다.

senses.en: showing lack of emotional involvement

examples.text: The surgeon spoke in a calm, detached tone, as though describing a problem in engineering.

senses.en: no longer connected or joined

examples.text: a detached part

senses.en: hold spellbound

examples.text: Her song enraptured the audience with vivid images of the Scandinavian landscapes.

senses.en: take into consideration, have in view

examples.text: He entertained the notion of moving to South America

senses.en: To amuse (someone); to engage the attention of agreeably.

examples.text: The motivational speaker not only instructed but also entertained the audience.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 entretenir(서로 붙들어 두다)에서 왔습니다. 마음속에 붙들어 두고 '품다, 고려하다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: draw from; make good use of

examples.text: The company hopes to exploit new markets in Southeast Asia as demand grows.

senses.en: To make unfair use of someone else's labor, person, or property to one's own advantage.

examples.text: The factory owners exploited immigrant workers by paying them far less than the legal minimum wage.

senses.en: a notable achievement

examples.text: The first trek to the summit of Mount Everest was a stunning exploit.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 esploit(성과, 이용)에서 왔고, 라틴어 explicāre(펼치다)와 이어집니다. 자원을 펼쳐 활용한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: The improper use of something for selfish purposes.

examples.text: The report documented the systematic exploitation of migrant laborers on the plantations.

senses.en: the act of making some area of land or water more profitable or productive or useful

examples.text: The exploitation of the region's mineral wealth transformed a sleepy village into a bustling mining town.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 exploitation에서 왔고, exploit에 -ation이 붙었습니다. 남을 이용해 이익을 뽑아내는 것입니다.

senses.en: lessen or to try to lessen the seriousness or extent of

examples.text: His lawyer argued that the defendant's youth and difficult upbringing should extenuate the offense.

origin.ko: 라틴어 extenuāre(얇게 만들다)에서 왔습니다. 죄의 무게를 얇게 줄여 경감한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: having an abundant supply of money or possessions of value

examples.text: a speculator flush with cash

senses.en: turn red, as if in embarrassment or shame

examples.text: She flushed with embarrassment when the teacher praised her in front of the whole class.

senses.en: of a surface exactly even with an adjoining one, forming the same plane

examples.text: a door flush with the wall

senses.en: a series of ordered groupings of people or things within a system

examples.text: The monastery maintained a strict hierarchy, from novices at the bottom to the abbot at the top.

origin.ko: 그리스어 hierarkhía '대사제의 통치'에서 왔습니다. hierós(신성한)와 árkhō(다스리다)가 합쳐져 성직의 위계가 '계층제'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: necessary (for someone) as a duty or responsibility; morally binding

examples.text: it is incumbent on them to pay their own debts

senses.en: currently holding an office

examples.text: the incumbent governor

senses.en: the official who holds an office

examples.text: The incumbent narrowly defeated her challenger after a bitter and expensive campaign.

origin.ko: 라틴어 incumbēns '기대고 누운'에서 왔고 incumbō(위에 얹히다)가 뿌리입니다. 어깨 위에 얹힌 책임이 '의무로 지워진'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: not appropriate in application; defective

examples.text: an infelicitous remark

senses.en: marked by or producing unhappiness

examples.text: infelicitous circumstances

origin.ko: felicitous(알맞은)에 부정 접두사가 붙은 말입니다. 라틴어 fēlix(행복한)가 뿌리입니다.

senses.en: A work or performance that imitates another work or performance with ridicule or irony.

examples.text: The cabaret's parody of the president's speech had the audience roaring with laughter.

senses.en: To make a parody of something.

examples.text: The comedy movie parodied the entire Western genre.

origin.ko: 그리스어 parōidía '곁에서 부르는 노래'에서 왔습니다. 원작 옆에서 흉내 내어 부르며 풍자하는 작품입니다.

senses.en: characterized by ease and quickness in perceiving

examples.text: A percipient observer, she noticed the subtle shift in the negotiators' tone.

origin.ko: 라틴어 percipiō '완전히 파악하다'에서 왔습니다. 재빨리 붙잡아 알아채는 통찰력입니다.

senses.en: A decided case which is cited or used as an example to justify a judgment in a subsequent case.

examples.text: The court cited an earlier ruling as precedent when it rejected the company's appeal.

senses.en: an example that is used to justify similar occurrences at a later time

examples.text: Granting one exception could set a dangerous precedent for every future request.

origin.ko: 라틴어 praecēdere('앞서 가다')의 현재분사에서 왔습니다. 앞서 있었던 사례가 곧 선례입니다.

senses.en: one who precedes you in time (as in holding a position or office)

examples.text: The new director reversed several policies introduced by her predecessor.

origin.ko: 라틴어 prae-('앞')와 dēcēdere('물러나다')에서 왔습니다. 먼저 물러난 자리의 사람이 전임자입니다.

senses.en: a statement that is assumed to be true and from which a conclusion can be drawn

examples.text: The argument collapses because its central premise rests on an unproven generalization.

senses.en: take something as preexisting and given

examples.text: The policy is premised on the belief that consumers will respond rationally to price changes.

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 premissa('앞에 놓인 명제')에서 왔습니다. 결론보다 앞서 내놓은 것이 전제입니다.

senses.en: a prediction made by extrapolating from past observations

examples.text: Official projections show the population doubling within the next fifty years.

senses.en: (psychiatry) a defense mechanism by which your own traits and emotions are attributed to someone else

examples.text: His constant accusations of dishonesty seemed less a judgment than a projection of his own guilt.

senses.en: any solid convex shape that juts out from something

examples.text: Climbers clung to small projections in the rock face.

origin.ko: 라틴어 prōiectiō('앞으로 던짐')에서 왔습니다. 현재를 앞으로 던져 미래를 내다본 추정치입니다.

senses.en: have or develop complicating consequences

examples.text: A small change in tax policy can ramify through the whole economy in unpredictable ways.

senses.en: To divide into branches or subdivisions.

examples.text: Beyond the delta, the river begins to ramify into dozens of narrow channels.

origin.ko: 라틴어 rāmus('가지')와 -ficō('만들다')에서 왔습니다. 가지가 갈라지듯 결과가 복잡하게 뻗습니다.

senses.en: returning to health after illness or debility

examples.text: The recovering patient was advised to rest for several weeks before returning to work.

senses.en: say (something) with great enthusiasm

examples.text: Critics rhapsodized about the young pianist's debut, calling it the most thrilling performance of the decade.

origin.ko: rhapsody에 동사 접미사 -ize가 붙었습니다. 서사시 낭송자처럼 열광적으로 말한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: having wisdom that comes with age and experience

examples.text: The senator offered sage advice to the newcomers, drawing on four decades of political experience.

senses.en: a mentor in spiritual and philosophical topics who is renowned for profound wisdom

examples.text: Villagers traveled for days to consult the sage, who was famed for his wisdom.

origin.ko: 라틴어 sapere(맛보다, 현명하다)에서 왔습니다. 맛을 분별하듯 사리를 분별하는 지혜입니다.

senses.en: Composure, self-possession or imperturbability especially when in a dangerous situation.

examples.text: He handled the stressful situation with great sangfroid.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 sang-froid에서 왔고 '차가운 피'를 뜻합니다. 피가 차분하다는 이미지에서 침착함이 되었습니다.

senses.en: avoiding waste

examples.text: The charity was anything but stinting in its praise of the volunteers who staffed the shelter.

senses.en: draw out a discussion or process in order to gain time

examples.text: The speaker temporized in order to delay the vote

senses.en: To discuss, to negotiate; to reach a compromise.

examples.text: Unwilling to temporize with the rebels, the governor demanded their immediate surrender.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 temporiser(때를 기다리다)에서 왔고 라틴어 tempus(시간)와 이어집니다. 시간을 벌려고 끌고 미룹니다.

senses.en: insignificantly small; a matter of form only (‘tokenish’ is informal)

examples.text: The council offered only a token apology, which did nothing to address residents' real complaints.

senses.en: Something serving as an expression of something else.

examples.text: According to the Bible, the rainbow is a token of God's covenant with Noah.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 tācn('표시, 상징')에서 왔습니다. 실질 없이 표시만 하는 것이 '명목상의'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: To malign a person or entity by making malicious and false or defamatory statements.

examples.text: Rivals traduced the physician in anonymous pamphlets, accusing him of crimes he had never committed.

origin.ko: 라틴어 trādūcō('끌고 건너다, 구경거리로 망신 주다')에서 왔습니다. 남을 끌어내 망신 주는 모습이 '중상하다'입니다.

senses.en: completely acceptable; not open to exception or reproach
senses.ko: 나무랄 데 없는, 흠잡을 수 없는

examples.text: The candidate's record was unexceptionable, offering opponents nothing to attack.

senses.en: Not forthcoming; laconic or uncooperative.

examples.text: The witness was unforthcoming, answering each question with a single word and offering no detail.

senses.en: unaccustomed or unusual

examples.text: The usually stern headmaster spoke with unwonted gentleness as he addressed the grieving students.

origin.ko: un-과 wonted('습관이 된')의 결합입니다. 습관이 아니라는 뜻이 '평소와 다른'입니다.

senses.en: an unexpected and inexplicable change in something (in a situation or a person's behavior, etc.)

examples.text: Farmers must plan around the vagaries of the weather, which can ruin a harvest overnight.

origin.ko: 라틴어 vagārī('떠돌다')에서 왔습니다. 정처 없이 떠돌듯 종잡을 수 없는 변화입니다.

senses.en: abnormally deficient in color as suggesting physical or emotional distress

examples.text: The patient looked wan and exhausted after the long night of fever.

senses.en: lacking vitality as from weariness or illness or unhappiness

examples.text: a wan smile

origin.ko: 고대 영어 wann('어두운, 칙칙한')에서 왔습니다. 안색이 어둡고 핏기 없는 모습이 '창백한'입니다.

senses.en: describe roughly or briefly or give the main points or summary of

examples.text: In her opening lecture, the professor adumbrated the arguments she would develop over the semester.

senses.en: To foreshadow vaguely.

examples.text: Early poems by the author adumbrate themes that would dominate her mature work.

origin.ko: 라틴어 adumbrare(그림자를 드리우다)에서 왔습니다. 그림자처럼 윤곽만 그린다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: the whole amount

examples.text: In the aggregate, the small donations exceeded what any single wealthy donor had given.

senses.en: formed of separate units gathered into a mass or whole

examples.text: The aggregate income of the three households barely covered the cost of the new school.

origin.ko: 라틴어 aggregare(무리로 모으다)에서 왔고 grex(양 떼)와 연결됩니다. 흩어진 것을 한 무리로 모은 것이 '총계'입니다.

senses.en: cause to feel sorrow

examples.text: The workers felt aggrieved by the sudden change in their contracts and filed a formal complaint.

senses.en: infringe on the rights of

examples.text: Any party aggrieved by the ruling may appeal to a higher court within thirty days.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 agrever(짐을 지우다)에서 왔고 라틴어 gravis(무거운)에서 나왔습니다. 무거운 짐을 얹듯 마음을 괴롭힙니다.

senses.en: Although, despite (it) being.

examples.text: The study offers a promising result, albeit one based on a very small sample.

origin.ko: 중세 영어 al be it (that), 즉 '비록 ~라 하더라도'를 줄여 붙인 말입니다.

senses.en: a person who has suddenly risen to a higher economic status but has not gained social acceptance of others in that class

examples.text: The old families snubbed the arriviste whose fortune had come from a single lucky merger.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 arriviste에서 왔고 arriver(도착하다)에서 나왔습니다. 막 도착해 올라선 사람을 빗댄 말입니다.

senses.en: personal independence

examples.text: Financial independence and micro retirement have come to represent the autonomy I've created for myself, which is a powerful feeling.

senses.en: immunity from arbitrary exercise of authority: political independence

examples.text: The province demanded greater autonomy from the central government.

origin.ko: 그리스어 autonomia(자기 법을 가짐)에서 왔습니다. 스스로 규칙을 정하는 독립을 뜻합니다.

senses.en: become inflated

examples.text: The city's budget deficit ballooned after the recession cut tax revenues sharply.

senses.en: large tough nonrigid bag filled with gas or heated air

examples.text: A hot-air balloon drifted slowly over the valley at sunrise.

origin.ko: 이탈리아어 pallone(큰 공)에서 왔습니다. 처음에는 큰 가죽 공으로 하던 놀이를 가리켰습니다.

senses.en: annoy persistently

examples.text: Reporters beleaguered the mayor with questions about the budget at every public appearance.

senses.en: surround so as to force to give up

examples.text: The army beleaguered the fortress for months, hoping hunger would force its defenders to yield.

origin.ko: 네덜란드어 belegeren(포위하다)에서 왔고 '진영을 에워싸다'가 원뜻입니다. 사방에서 끊임없이 괴롭힌다는 뜻이 되었습니다.

senses.en: adequate, but not outstanding or exceptional

examples.text: The orchestra gave a competent but uninspired performance of the familiar symphony.

senses.en: properly or sufficiently qualified or capable or efficient

examples.text: a competent typist

origin.ko: 라틴어 competens에서 왔고, competō('들어맞다, 감당할 수 있다')에서 갈라졌습니다.

senses.en: form or compose

examples.text: Women constitute a majority of the students enrolled in the program.

senses.en: set up or lay the groundwork for

examples.text: The assembly was constituted to draft a new charter for the republic.

origin.ko: 라틴어 cōnstituō('세우다, 확립하다')에서 왔고, con-(함께)과 statuō(세우다)가 합쳐졌습니다.

senses.en: the quality of being believable or trustworthy

examples.text: The newspaper lost much of its credibility after it published the fabricated interview.

origin.ko: credible에 -ity가 붙은 말로, 라틴어 crēdō(믿다)에서 나왔습니다.

senses.en: lower someone's spirits; make downhearted

examples.text: The team's third straight loss dejected the players and silenced the locker room.

origin.ko: 라틴어 dēicere(아래로 던지다)에서 왔습니다. 기분을 아래로 내던지니 '낙담시키다'입니다.

senses.en: bar from attention or consideration

examples.text: She dismissed the idea as ridiculous.

senses.en: terminate the employment of; discharge from an office or position

examples.text: The company dismissed me after less than a year.

senses.en: cease to consider; put out of judicial consideration

examples.text: The court dismissed the case.

origin.ko: 라틴어 dīmittō(보내 버리다)에서 왔습니다. 멀리 내보내는 이미지가 '묵살하다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: a person who professes beliefs and opinions that he or she does not hold in order to conceal his or her real feelings or motives

examples.text: The senator proved a skilled dissembler, smiling warmly at rivals he was quietly working to undermine.

origin.ko: dissemble에 -er이 붙어 본심을 숨기는 사람을 뜻합니다.

senses.en: hide (feelings) from other people

examples.text: He dissimulated his anger behind a polite smile throughout the tense negotiation.

origin.ko: 라틴어 dissimulō(숨기다, 가장하다)에서 왔고 dissimilis(닮지 않은)에서 나왔습니다.

senses.en: give qualities or abilities to

examples.text: The old tales endue their heroes with courage and almost limitless strength.

origin.ko: 라틴어 induere(옷을 입다, 걸치다)에서 왔습니다. 옷을 입히듯 자질을 부여한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: To settle comfortably.

examples.text: After lunch he ensconced himself in the armchair with a novel and a blanket.

origin.ko: en-에 sconce(작은 요새)가 붙었습니다. 요새 안에 안전하게 들어앉듯 편안히 자리 잡는다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: the condition of being honored (esteemed or respected or well regarded)

examples.text: We hold her in high esteem.

senses.en: regard highly; think much of

examples.text: Students esteem the teacher for her patience and her unfailing honesty.

origin.ko: 라틴어 aestimāre(값을 매기다)에서 프랑스어를 거쳐 왔습니다. 높은 가치를 매기는 데서 '존경'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: being or from or characteristic of another place or part of the world

examples.text: The market was filled with exotic fruits that most of the tourists had never tasted.

senses.en: strikingly strange or unusual

examples.text: Physicists have proposed exotic forms of matter that behave unlike anything seen in ordinary experiments.

origin.ko: 그리스어 exōtikós(바깥에서 온)에서 왔습니다. 바깥, 곧 외국에서 온 '이국적인' 것을 가리킵니다.

senses.en: perform without preparation

examples.text: he extemporized a speech at the wedding

origin.ko: 라틴어 ex tempore(즉석에서)에 -ize가 붙었습니다. 준비 없이 즉석에서 해 낸다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: To experience luck, fortune or treatment (of a certain kind).

examples.text: Did you fare well in the exam?

senses.en: Supplies for consumption or pleasure.

examples.text: The television channel tended to broadcast unremarkable downmarket fare.

senses.en: the sum charged for riding in a public conveyance

examples.text: The city raised the subway fare by fifty cents to cover rising maintenance costs.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 faran(여행하다, 가다)에서 왔습니다. 길을 가며 겪는 형편이 '지내다, 겪다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: To bear fruit; to generate useful products or ideas.

examples.text: Years of patient research finally fructified in a vaccine that saved millions of lives.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 fructefier에서 왔습니다. 열매(fruct)를 맺게 한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: The origin, start, or point at which something comes into being.

examples.text: Some point to the creation of Magna Carta as the genesis of English common law.

origin.ko: 그리스어 génesis '기원, 탄생'에서 라틴어를 거쳐 왔습니다. gen은 '태어나다, 낳다'를 뜻합니다.

senses.en: a small growth of trees without underbrush

examples.text: A grove of ancient olive trees shaded the small stone chapel.

origin.ko: 고대영어 grāf '작은 숲'에서 왔습니다. 게르만어 '가지, 덤불'이 뿌리입니다.

senses.en: praise vociferously

examples.text: The critics hailed the young pianist as a new Rubinstein

senses.en: To call out loudly in order to gain the attention of.
senses.ko: 큰 소리로 부르다, (택시 등을) 불러 세우다

examples.text: Hail a taxi.

senses.en: many objects thrown forcefully through the air

examples.text: A hail of criticism greeted the minister as she stepped up to the podium.

origin.ko: 고대 노르드어 heill '건강한'에서 온 인사말입니다. 건강을 빌며 맞이하는 데서 '환호하다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: having rugged physical strength; inured to fatigue or hardships

examples.text: Only the hardiest climbers attempted the final ascent in the freezing wind.

senses.en: able to survive under unfavorable weather conditions

examples.text: Hardy perennials such as lavender survive the harsh winters of the northern plains.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 hardi '대담한, 굳센'에서 왔고 프랑크어 hard(단단한)와 연결됩니다.

senses.en: make into a whole or make part of a whole

examples.text: She incorporated his suggestions into her proposal

senses.en: To form into a legal company.

examples.text: The company was incorporated in 1980.

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 incorporō '몸으로 만들다'에서 왔습니다. 하나의 몸(corpus) 안으로 넣어 통합한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: an event marking a unique or important historical change of course or one on which important developments depend

examples.text: The ruling was a landmark in the history of civil rights litigation.

senses.en: A recognizable natural or man-made feature used for navigation.

examples.text: Pilots flew at relatively low altitudes to identify ground landmarks, such as railroad tracks, rivers, highways, and distinctive towns.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 landmearc '경계'에서 왔고 land(땅)와 mark(표시)가 합쳐졌습니다. 땅의 경계표에서 '이정표'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: impose and collect

examples.text: to levy a tax

senses.en: a charge imposed and collected

examples.text: The government introduced a new levy on carbon-intensive industries to fund the transition.

senses.en: cause to assemble or enlist in military

examples.text: The king levied a fresh army from the northern provinces before the spring campaign.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 levee에서 왔고 라틴어 lēvāre '들어올리다'에서 나왔습니다. 세금을 걷어 올린다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: To erroneously attribute; to falsely ascribe; used especially of authorship.

examples.text: Many popular quotations are misattributed to Einstein, though he never said them.

origin.ko: mis-(잘못)와 attribute(~의 공으로 돌리다)가 합쳐졌습니다. 엉뚱한 사람에게 공을 돌린다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: most desirable possible under a restriction expressed or implied

examples.text: Engineers searched for the optimal design that would satisfy both the budget and safety limits.

origin.ko: 라틴어 optimus '가장 좋은'에 영어 -al이 붙은 말입니다.

senses.en: characterized by the attitude of a philosopher; meeting trouble with level-headed detachment

examples.text: She bore the desertion with philosophical indifference.

senses.en: of or relating to philosophy or philosophers

examples.text: philosophical writing

origin.ko: 그리스어 philosophía '지혜에 대한 사랑'에서 왔습니다. 철학자처럼 침착하게 받아들이는 태도를 뜻하게 되었습니다.

senses.en: contract one's lips into a rounded shape

examples.text: She pursed her lips and studied the contract with open suspicion.

senses.en: a sum of money offered as a prize

examples.text: The winner of the heavyweight bout took home a purse of two million dollars.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 purs('지갑')에서 왔고 라틴어 bursa('가죽 주머니')와 이어집니다. 주머니 입구를 오므리는 동작에서 '입술을 오므리다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: Good-natured banter, jest, or ridicule.

examples.text: Their friendly raillery over chess made the long train journey pass quickly.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 raillerie에서 빌려 온 말로 railler('놀리다')와 이어집니다. 악의 없는 놀림을 뜻합니다.

senses.en: cancel officially

examples.text: Parliament voted to repeal the outdated law that had restricted public gatherings for decades.

senses.en: the act of abrogating; an official or legal cancellation

examples.text: Lawmakers voted for the repeal of the unpopular tax after months of public pressure.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 rapeler('불러들이다, 철회하다')에서 왔고 라틴어 repellere와 이어집니다. 이미 내린 법을 거두어들입니다.

senses.en: express discontent

examples.text: Rather than repine over his lost fortune, he set about rebuilding his business from nothing.

origin.ko: re-에 pine('애타게 그리워하다')을 붙여 만든 것으로 보입니다. 마음이 상해 불평한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: a statement that limits or restricts some claim

examples.text: he recommended her without any reservations

senses.en: an unstated doubt that prevents you from accepting something wholeheartedly

examples.text: Several members voiced private reservations about the plan even as they voted in its favor.

senses.en: a district that is reserved for particular purpose

examples.text: The tribe's reservation covers a large stretch of arid land in the northern part of the state.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 reservation에서 왔고 reserve('따로 간직하다')에 -ation이 붙었습니다. 일부를 따로 남겨 두는 단서입니다.

senses.en: In a searching manner.

examples.text: He stared at me searchingly, trying to determine if I was lying.

senses.en: characteristic of or devoted to the temporal world as opposed to the spiritual world

examples.text: The university began as a religious seminary but gradually adopted a more secular curriculum.

senses.en: not concerned with or devoted to religion

examples.text: Most of the composer's output was secular, written for the court rather than the church.

senses.en: Continuing over a long period of time.

examples.text: The long-term growth in population and income accounts for most secular trends in economic phenomena.

origin.ko: 라틴어 saeculāris(한 시대의)에서 왔습니다. 영원한 세계에 대비해 지금 이 세상의 일을 가리킵니다.

senses.en: A prolonged military assault or a blockade of a city or fortress with the intent of conquering by force or attrition.

examples.text: They sued for peace after the long siege.

senses.en: A prolonged assault or attack.

examples.text: The mayor, under siege from reporters and angry residents, canceled all public appearances.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 siege(자리)에서 왔고, 라틴어 sēdēs(자리)와 이어집니다. 군대가 성 앞에 '눌러앉는' 이미지입니다.

senses.en: a union of interests or purposes or sympathies among members of a group

examples.text: Workers across the city struck in solidarity with the dismissed miners.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 solidarité에서 왔고 라틴어 solidus(단단한)와 이어집니다. 단단히 하나로 뭉친 연대입니다.

senses.en: severe and unremitting in making demands

examples.text: The remark earned me a stern rebuke.

senses.en: not to be placated or appeased or moved by entreaty

examples.text: The stern judge showed no mercy and refused every plea for leniency.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 styrne(엄격한)에서 왔습니다. 굳고 엄하다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: done or happening at the appropriate or proper time

examples.text: a timely warning

origin.ko: 고대 영어 tīmlīc에서 왔고 time에 -ly를 붙인 형태입니다. 때에 맞는다는 뜻 그대로 '시기적절한'입니다.

senses.en: An assembly including one or more judges to conduct judicial business; a court of law.

examples.text: The international tribunal heard testimony from survivors before issuing its judgment on the wartime atrocities.

origin.ko: 라틴어 tribūnal('재판관 단상')에서 왔고 tribus('부족')와 이어집니다. 재판하는 자리가 '법정'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: complete and absolute

examples.text: The experiment ended in utter failure, leaving the researchers with no usable data.

senses.en: express in speech

examples.text: Stunned by the verdict, she could not utter a single word in her own defense.

senses.en: put into circulation

examples.text: He was convicted of uttering counterfeit banknotes at several shops in the city.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 ūtera('바깥쪽의')에서 왔고 out의 비교급입니다. 끝까지 바깥으로 나갔다는 뜻이 '완전한'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: the quality of being facile in speech and writing

examples.text: His volubility at dinner parties often left others unable to get a word in.

origin.ko: 라틴어 volūbilitās에서 왔고 voluble에 -ity를 붙인 형태입니다. 말이 술술 굴러 나오는 것입니다.

senses.en: naughtily or annoyingly playful

examples.text: I attempted to hide my emotions, but an arch remark escaped my lips.

senses.en: Principal; primary.

examples.text: They were arch enemies.

origin.ko: 그리스어 접두사 arch-(으뜸)가 어원이며 흔한 짝인 'arch rogue(대악당)'를 거쳐 '짓궂은'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: leave suddenly and as if in a hurry

examples.text: The listeners bolted when he discussed his strange ideas

senses.en: eat hastily without proper chewing

examples.text: Don't bolt your food!

senses.en: secure or lock with a bolt

examples.text: Every night the innkeeper bolted the heavy oak door and checked the shutters.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 bolt('굵은 화살')에서 왔습니다. 화살이나 번개처럼 쏜살같이 튀어 나가는 이미지입니다.

senses.en: resist

examples.text: The small airline bucked the industry trend by cutting fares while its rivals raised them.

senses.en: to strive with determination

examples.text: John is bucking for a promotion

origin.ko: 중세 저지 독일어 bucken('구부리다')에서 왔고, 수컷 염소를 뜻하는 buck의 영향도 받았습니다.

senses.en: put an end to a state or an activity

examples.text: After a short while, it ceased to rain.

senses.en: have an end, in a temporal, spatial, or quantitative sense; either spatial or metaphorical

examples.text: The company's funding ceased abruptly once the grant expired at the end of the fiscal year.

origin.ko: 라틴어 cessō('그만두다')에서 왔고, cēdō(가다, 물러나다)에서 갈라졌습니다. 가던 길을 멈춘다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: act in accordance with someone's rules, commands, or wishes

examples.text: He complied with my instructions

origin.ko: 라틴어 complēre('가득 채우다, 이행하다')에서 왔습니다. 요구를 빈틈없이 채워 따른다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: slow to learn or understand; lacking intellectual acuity

examples.text: so dense he never understands anything I say to him

senses.en: Obscure or difficult to understand.

examples.text: The philosopher's dense prose rewards patient readers but baffles anyone looking for a quick summary.

senses.en: having component parts closely crowded together

examples.text: a dense population

origin.ko: 라틴어 dēnsus(빽빽한)에서 프랑스어를 거쳐 왔습니다. 빽빽해서 뚫고 들어가기 어려운 이미지가 '우둔한'으로 이어졌습니다.

senses.en: Cut off, or separated.

examples.text: divorced from reality

senses.en: of someone whose marriage has been legally dissolved

examples.text: Mark's parents are divorced.

senses.en: increase the level of

examples.text: This will enhance your enjoyment

origin.ko: 속라틴어 *inaltiāre(높이다)에서 왔습니다. alt(높은)를 향해 끌어올린다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: clearly revealed to the mind or the senses or judgment

examples.text: The full extent of her injuries did not become evident until they tried to move her.

origin.ko: 라틴어 ēvidēns(눈에 훤히 보이는)에서 왔습니다. 밖으로 드러나 보이니 '명백한'입니다.

senses.en: make easier

examples.text: New software was introduced to facilitate communication between the firm's offices in different countries.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 faciliter에서 왔고 라틴어 facilis(쉬운)가 바탕입니다. 일을 쉽게 만든다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: an undeveloped field of study; a topic inviting research and development

examples.text: Neuroscientists regard the study of consciousness as the last great frontier of biology.

senses.en: a wilderness at the edge of a settled area of a country

examples.text: Families heading west faced hardship on the American frontier in the nineteenth century.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 fronter(front 앞쪽)에서 왔습니다. 가장 앞에 맞닿은 경계라는 뜻에서 '최첨단, 미개척 분야'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: Doctrine, philosophy, body of beliefs or principles belonging to an individual or group.

examples.text: A dictatorship bans things, that do not conform to its ideology, to secure its reign.

origin.ko: 1796년 프랑스의 데스튀트 드 트라시가 만든 idéologie에서 왔습니다. 관념(idea)을 연구하는 학문이 '이념'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: a positive motivational influence

examples.text: Tax credits give homeowners a strong incentive to install solar panels on their roofs.

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 incentīvus '곡조를 시작하는'에서 왔습니다. 노래를 선창해 분위기를 띄우듯 행동을 북돋는 것입니다.

senses.en: Including (almost) everything within its scope.

examples.text: An inclusive study of the region's history must consider the voices of its minority communities.

senses.en: Including the extremes as well as the area between.

examples.text: numbers 1 to 10 inclusive

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 inclūsīvus에서 왔고 라틴어 inclūsus(안에 닫힌)가 뿌리입니다. 모든 것을 울타리 안에 넣는다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: be emphatic or resolute and refuse to budge

examples.text: The defendant insisted on his innocence.

senses.en: postulate positively and assertively

examples.text: The author insists that economic growth cannot continue without limits on resource consumption.

origin.ko: 라틴어 īnsistere '위에 서다, 버티다'에서 왔습니다. 자리를 딛고 물러서지 않는 모습입니다.

senses.en: supply the inspiration for

examples.text: The article about the artist inspired the exhibition of his recent work

senses.en: serve as the inciting cause of

examples.text: The mayor's evasive answers inspired little confidence among residents worried about the flooded streets.

senses.en: To draw in by the operation of breathing; to inhale.

examples.text: The patient was told to inspire deeply and hold the breath while the scan was taken.

origin.ko: 라틴어 īnspīrāre '숨을 불어넣다'에서 왔습니다. 안에 숨(영감)을 불어넣는다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: in like or similar manner

examples.text: Public transportation is virtually inaccessible in this country; likewise, its hospitals are also not very user-friendly.

senses.en: in addition

examples.text: Margaret enjoys playing tennis on Saturdays, Jeremy likewise.

origin.ko: 중세 영어 in like wise '같은 방식으로'가 줄어든 말입니다.

senses.en: To impose (oneself) on others; to cut in.

examples.text: He obtruded himself into the family's private discussion and offered unwanted advice.

senses.en: To become apparent in an unwelcome way, to be forcibly imposed; to jut in, to intrude (on or into).

examples.text: Unwelcome doubts kept obtruding on her mind as she rehearsed the speech.

origin.ko: 라틴어 obtrūdō '~쪽으로 밀어붙이다'에서 왔습니다. 남에게 자기를 억지로 들이미는 모습입니다.

senses.en: Anything that acts as counterbalance; a compensating equivalent.

examples.text: Today's victory was an offset to yesterday's defeat.

origin.ko: off와 set을 합친 말로, set off(상쇄하다)의 명사형입니다.

senses.en: The state of being precise or exact; especially, both exact and accurate.

examples.text: The surgeon worked with remarkable precision, leaving only a barely visible scar.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 precision에서 왔으며 precise('정확한')에서 나왔습니다. 군더더기를 잘라 내 정확해진다는 이미지입니다.

senses.en: An uncomplaining acceptance of something undesirable but unavoidable.

examples.text: She faced the diagnosis with quiet resignation, putting her affairs in order without complaint.

senses.en: the act of giving up (a claim or office or possession etc.)

examples.text: The minister's resignation followed weeks of mounting pressure over the budget scandal.

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 resignātiō에서 왔고 resign('내놓다')에 -ation이 붙었습니다. 바꿀 수 없는 일을 그대로 받아들이는 체념입니다.

senses.en: a clause that is appended to a legislative bill

examples.text: Lawmakers attached an unrelated rider to the spending bill, provoking objections from the opposition.

senses.en: An additional matter or question arising in corollary; a qualification.

examples.text: The committee approved the plan, adding a rider that funding be reviewed after one year.

origin.ko: ride에 -er이 붙은 말입니다. 법안 '위에 올라탄' 추가 조항이라는 비유로 쓰입니다.

senses.en: complete or extreme

examples.text: A flower was growing, in stark contrast, out of the sidewalk.

senses.en: severely simple

examples.text: a stark interior

senses.en: devoid of any qualifications or disguise or adornment

examples.text: The report gave a stark, unvarnished account of the factory's safety failures.

senses.en: providing no shelter or sustenance

examples.text: I picked my way forlornly through the stark, sharp rocks.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 stearc(뻣뻣한, 강한)에서 왔습니다. 꾸밈없이 뻣뻣하고 적나라해 극명하다는 뜻이 되었습니다.

senses.en: performed comprehensively and completely; not superficial or partial

examples.text: A thorough review of the archive turned up letters that no earlier historian had noticed.

senses.en: painstakingly careful and accurate

examples.text: our accountant is thorough

origin.ko: 고대 영어 þuruh에서 왔고 through와 같은 뿌리입니다. 끝까지 꿰뚫고 지나간다는 이미지에서 '철저한'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: Completely; entirely; to the fullest extent.

examples.text: Well, now we are utterly lost.

origin.ko: utter에 -ly를 붙인 부사입니다. '완전히'라는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: show consideration for; take into account

examples.text: The committee must weigh the benefits of the merger against its long-term risks.

senses.en: to be oppressive or burdensome

examples.text: The unanswered letters weighed heavily on her conscience for months.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 wegan('옮기다, 달다')에서 왔습니다. 저울에 달듯 따져 보는 것이 '고려하다'입니다.

senses.en: existing only in the mind; separated from embodiment

examples.text: Students often find justice easier to discuss as an abstract principle than to apply to real cases.

senses.en: An abridgement or summary of a longer publication.

examples.text: Reviewers read the abstract of each submitted paper before deciding which ones deserved a full evaluation.

origin.ko: 라틴어 abstrahere(끌어내다)에서 왔습니다. 구체적 사물에서 성질만 끌어낸 것이 '추상적인'입니다.

senses.en: call upon in supplication; entreat

examples.text: The defendant begged the judge for mercy, promising to repay every cent he had taken.

senses.en: dodge, avoid answering, or take for granted

examples.text: Calling the policy a success because it is popular begs the question of whether it works.

senses.en: A generally accepted principle; a rule.

examples.text: The trial must proceed according to the canons of law.

senses.en: A group of literary works that are generally accepted as representing a field.

examples.text: Scholars have argued for decades about which authors deserve a place in the literary canon.

origin.ko: 그리스어 kanōn('측량용 막대, 기준')에서 왔고, 갈대를 뜻하는 셈어에서 유래했습니다. 곧은 자가 '규범'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: agreement in the judgment or opinion reached by a group as a whole

examples.text: There is a growing scientific consensus that the underlying cause is environmental rather than genetic.

origin.ko: 라틴어 cōnsēnsus('일치, 합의')에서 왔고, cōnsentiō(함께 느끼다)에서 갈라졌습니다.

senses.en: give moral or emotional strength to

examples.text: Friends tried to console her after the failure of her business.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 consoler와 라틴어 cōnsōlor('위로하다')에서 왔고, solace(위안)와 같은 뿌리입니다.

senses.en: an unshakable belief in something without need for proof or evidence

examples.text: She spoke with such conviction that even skeptics in the audience began to nod.

senses.en: (criminal law) a final judgment of guilty in a criminal case and the punishment that is imposed

examples.text: the conviction came as no surprise

origin.ko: 라틴어 convictiō에서 왔고, convincō(설득하다, 유죄를 입증하다)에서 갈라졌습니다. 논쟁에서 완전히 이긴 확신입니다.

senses.en: subdue, restrain, or overcome by affecting with a feeling of awe; frighten (as with threats)

examples.text: Con artists are not cowed by the law.

origin.ko: 고대 노르드어 kúga(억압하다)에서 왔을 것으로 추정됩니다.

senses.en: a distinguishing difference between similar things or people

examples.text: There is a distinction to be made between resting and slacking.

senses.en: an honor awarded to someone in recognition of achievement or superiority

examples.text: She had the distinction of meeting the Queen.

origin.ko: 라틴어 distinctiō(구별)에서 왔고 distinguō(구분하다)의 명사형입니다.

senses.en: A safe place.

examples.text: Since its conception, the European Union has been a haven for those seeking refuge from war, persecution and poverty in other parts of the world.

senses.en: a sheltered port where ships can take on or discharge cargo

examples.text: The fishing fleet sought the haven of the bay as the storm closed in.

origin.ko: 고대영어 hæfen '항구'에서 왔습니다. 배가 안전하게 쉬는 항구가 '피난처'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: marked by meekness or modesty; not arrogant or prideful

examples.text: Despite her many awards, the scientist remained humble and credited her students for the discovery.

senses.en: To defeat or reduce the power, independence, or pride of.

examples.text: The unexpected defeat humbled the champions and forced them to rethink their strategy.

senses.en: low or inferior in station or quality

examples.text: The famous chef began his career in a humble kitchen behind a roadside diner.

origin.ko: 라틴어 humilis '낮은'에서 왔고 humus(땅)가 뿌리입니다. 땅에 가까이 낮추는 태도가 '겸손한'입니다.

senses.en: something that serves to indicate or suggest

examples.text: There's no indication that the fire was caused by criminals.

origin.ko: 라틴어 indicātiō에서 왔고 indicō(가리키다)가 뿌리입니다. 손가락으로 가리켜 보여 주는 것이 '징후'입니다.

senses.en: have in mind as a purpose

examples.text: He intends to go to university.

senses.en: design or destine

examples.text: The fund was intended to support young researchers, not to cover the institution's running costs.

origin.ko: 라틴어 intendere '~쪽으로 뻗다, 주의를 돌리다'에서 왔습니다. 마음을 한 방향으로 뻗는 것이 '의도하다'입니다.

senses.en: To provide an acceptable explanation for.

examples.text: How can you justify spending so much money on clothes?

senses.en: To be a good reason behind a normally-unacceptable action; to warrant.

examples.text: Nothing can justify your rude behaviour last night.

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 justificare '올바르게 만들다'에서 왔습니다. 옳다고 만들어 주니 '정당화하다'입니다.

senses.en: any admirable quality or attribute

examples.text: Reviewers disagreed about the merit of the novel, though all praised its ambition.

senses.en: be worthy or deserving

examples.text: Her performance merited wild applause.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 merite에서 왔고 라틴어 meritum '받을 만한 것'에서 나왔습니다. 보상받을 만한 가치입니다.

senses.en: Of, pertaining to, or consisting of money.

examples.text: Although of little monetary value, Rosie treasured her late grandfather's old hunting gear.

origin.ko: 로마의 유노 모네타 신전에 조폐소가 있었기에 monēta가 '주화'를 뜻하게 되었고, 여기서 '화폐의'가 나왔습니다.

senses.en: To long, to yearn so much that it causes suffering.

examples.text: Laura was pining for Bill all the time he was gone.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 pīnian '괴롭히다'에서 왔고, 고통(pīn)이 바탕입니다. 그리움으로 괴로워한다는 뜻이 되었습니다.

senses.en: the income or profit arising from such transactions as the sale of land or other property

examples.text: All proceeds from the auction will be donated to a children's hospital.

origin.ko: proceed('앞으로 나아가다')에서 나온 말입니다. 거래에서 앞으로 나오는 것, 곧 수익금입니다.

senses.en: strongly marked; easily noticeable

examples.text: a pronounced flavor of cinnamon

origin.ko: pronounce('선언하다')의 과거분사입니다. 분명하게 말해진 데서 '뚜렷한'이라는 뜻이 되었습니다.

senses.en: consistent with or based on or using reason

examples.text: rational behavior

senses.en: capable of being expressed as a quotient of integers
senses.ko: 유리수의, 정수의 비로 나타낼 수 있는

examples.text: The students showed that every repeating decimal is a rational number.

origin.ko: 라틴어 ratio('이성, 계산')의 형용사형 rationalis에서 왔습니다. 따져 헤아리는 힘이 이성입니다.

senses.en: having or appealing to those having worldly knowledge and refinement and savoir-faire

examples.text: a sophisticated audience

senses.en: ahead in development; complex or intricate

examples.text: The lab built a sophisticated imaging system capable of tracking individual cells in real time.

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 sophisticatus에서 왔고 그리스어 sophos(지혜로운)와 이어집니다. 처음에는 '세련되게 꾸민'이라는 뜻이었습니다.

senses.en: showing little if any change

examples.text: a static population

senses.en: angry criticism

examples.text: they will probably give you a lot of static about your editorial

origin.ko: 그리스어 statikos(멈추게 하는)에서 왔고 histēmi(세우다)와 이어집니다. 서 있어 변하지 않는다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: offer or present for acceptance

examples.text: The minister tendered his resignation after the audit revealed irregularities in his department.

senses.en: Sensitive or painful to the touch.

examples.text: Be careful: that area is tender.

senses.en: Fond, loving, gentle, or sweet.

examples.text: Suzanne was such a tender mother to her children.

origin.ko: 라틴어 tener('부드러운')에서 온 형용사에서 나온 동사입니다. 이 사전 정보만으로는 '제출하다' 의미로 이어진 과정이 분명하지 않습니다.

senses.en: something that may increase or decrease (like the tides of the sea)

examples.text: The tide of public opinion has turned.

senses.en: To carry over or through a problem or difficulty.

examples.text: A small emergency loan tided the bakery over until the holiday orders began arriving.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 tīd('때, 시간')에서 왔고 time과 친척입니다. 때에 맞춰 오가는 바닷물이 '흐름, 추세'로 비유되었습니다.

senses.en: Accustomed or used (to or with a thing), accustomed or apt (to do something).

examples.text: He is wont to complain loudly about his job.

senses.en: an established custom

examples.text: As was his wont, the professor began the seminar with a long, rambling anecdote.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 ġewunod('익숙해진')에서 왔고 ġewunian('거주하다, 익숙해지다')의 과거분사입니다. 몸에 밴 '버릇'입니다.

senses.en: capable of being read with comprehension

examples.text: The author makes complex economic theory accessible to readers with no background in the subject.

senses.en: Easy to get along with.

examples.text: Despite her fame, the professor remained accessible to students who wanted advice.

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 accessibilis에서 왔습니다. 다가갈 수 있다는 뜻에서 '이해하기 쉬운'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: make up a word or phrase

examples.text: The economist coined the term gig economy to describe short-term, freelance work arrangements.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 coigne('쐐기, 주화 찍는 틀')에서 왔고 라틴어 cuneus(쐐기)가 뿌리입니다. 틀로 찍어 새로 만든다는 뜻으로 이어졌습니다.

senses.en: make more intense, stronger, or more marked

examples.text: The delay in sending aid only compounded the suffering of the flood victims.

senses.en: a whole formed by a union of two or more elements or parts

examples.text: The final design was a compound of several earlier architectural styles.

origin.ko: 라틴어 componō('함께 놓다')에서 온 중세 프랑스어 componre에서 왔습니다. 요소를 겹쳐 쌓아 더 심하게 만든다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: expose or make liable to danger, suspicion, or disrepute

examples.text: The leak of classified files compromised the integrity of the entire investigation.

senses.en: an accommodation in which both sides make concessions

examples.text: After weeks of talks, the negotiators reached a compromise that neither side found ideal.

origin.ko: 라틴어 compromittere('함께 약속하다')에서 왔고, 원래는 중재 결정을 따르겠다는 상호 약속이었습니다. 약속에 얽매여 위태로워진다는 뜻으로 이어졌습니다.

senses.en: resistant to guidance or discipline

examples.text: The contrary child refused every suggestion simply because it came from an adult.

senses.en: very opposed in nature or character or purpose

examples.text: the facts point to a contrary conclusion

origin.ko: 라틴어 contrārius('반대의')에서 왔고 contrā(~에 맞서)가 뿌리입니다.

senses.en: To bring into being; give rise to.

examples.text: The discussion generated an uproar.

senses.en: produce (energy)

examples.text: The new wind farm will generate enough electricity to power forty thousand homes.

origin.ko: 라틴어 generō '낳다, 만들어내다'에서 왔고, genus(종류, 가문)와 같은 뿌리입니다.

senses.en: Of an activity, situation, words, etc.: the quality of having important or serious consequences; importance, seriousness.

examples.text: I hope you appreciate the gravity of the situation.

senses.en: a manner that is serious and solemn

examples.text: The judge read the verdict with a gravity that silenced the entire courtroom.

senses.en: (physics) the force of attraction between all masses in the universe; especially the attraction of the earth's mass for bodies near its surface

examples.text: The moon's weaker gravity allowed the astronauts to leap far higher than they could on Earth.

origin.ko: 라틴어 gravitās '무게, 엄숙함'에서 왔고 gravis(무거운)가 뿌리입니다. 무거움이 사안의 중대함으로 번졌습니다.

senses.en: set forth authoritatively as obligatory

examples.text: rules imposed by society

origin.ko: impose(부과하다)에서 왔고, 라틴어 in-(위에)과 ponere(놓다)가 합쳐진 말입니다. 위에 얹어 강제로 지운다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: the quality of being something that holds you back

examples.text: His habit of speaking without thinking became a serious liability during the campaign.

senses.en: the state of being legally obliged and responsible

examples.text: The company denied any liability for the damage caused by the faulty wiring.

senses.en: an obligation to pay money to another party

examples.text: The firm's liabilities exceeded its assets by several million dollars.

senses.en: In addition to what has been said.

examples.text: For three years there had been pestilence, and in the last of the three a famine; moreover, there was imminence of war.

origin.ko: 중세 영어에서 more(더)와 over(넘어서)를 붙여 만든 말로, '그 위에 더'라는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: Having honorable qualities; having moral eminence and freedom from anything petty, mean or dubious in conduct and character.

examples.text: He made a noble effort.

senses.en: impressive in size, manner, or appearance

examples.text: The noble facade of the library dominated the square.

senses.en: of or belonging to or constituting the hereditary aristocracy especially as derived from feudal times

examples.text: of noble birth

origin.ko: 라틴어 nōbilis는 '알려진, 유명한'이라는 뜻입니다. 이름이 널리 알려진 사람이 고귀한 사람이 되었습니다.

senses.en: A sentiment; an opinion.

examples.text: The notion that talent alone guarantees success has been challenged by recent research.

senses.en: an odd or fanciful or capricious idea

examples.text: She took a sudden notion to sell the house and sail around the world.

origin.ko: 라틴어 nōtiō '알게 됨, 개념'에서 왔고, nōscō는 '알다'입니다.

senses.en: wandering freely

examples.text: The professor's ranging mind moved easily from medieval law to modern astrophysics.

senses.en: A share or interest in a business or a given situation.

examples.text: The owners let the managers eventually earn a stake in the business.

senses.en: put at risk

examples.text: I will stake my good reputation for this

senses.en: A piece of wood or other material, usually long and slender, pointed at one end so as to be easily driven into the ground as a marker or a support or stay.

examples.text: We have surveyor's stakes at all four corners of this field, to mark exactly its borders.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 staca(말뚝)에서 왔습니다. 말뚝을 박아 내 몫을 표시하는 이미지로 지분이라는 뜻이 되었습니다.

senses.en: Having an enduring appeal; high-quality.

examples.text: The comedian delivered a vintage performance that reminded fans why they loved his early work.

senses.en: The year or place in which something is produced.

examples.text: The collector could date each bottle by its vintage and the vineyard on its label.

origin.ko: 라틴어 vindēmia('포도 수확')에서 왔고 vīnum('포도주')과 이어집니다. 특정 해 수확한 좋은 포도주에서 '고전적 가치'로 번졌습니다.

senses.en: appearing as such but not necessarily so

examples.text: the committee investigated some apparent discrepancies

senses.en: clearly revealed to the mind or the senses or judgment

examples.text: Her disappointment was apparent to everyone.

origin.ko: 라틴어 apparere(눈앞에 나타나다)에서 왔습니다. 눈에 보이는 대로라는 데서 '겉보기의'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: Empty, hypocritical talk.

examples.text: The speech was full of political cant about sacrifice from leaders who had never sacrificed anything.

senses.en: An argot, the jargon of a particular class or subgroup.

examples.text: He had the look of a prince, but the cant of a fishmonger.

senses.en: heel over

examples.text: The old fence began to cant toward the road after the heavy spring rains.

origin.ko: 라틴어 cantō('노래하다')에서 왔고 chant와 같은 어원입니다. 입에 발린 읊조림이라는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: give entirely to a specific person, activity, or cause

examples.text: She committed herself to the work of God

senses.en: To do (something bad); to perpetrate, as a crime, sin, or fault.

examples.text: to commit murder

senses.en: To give in trust; to put into charge or keeping; to entrust; to consign; used with to or formerly unto.

examples.text: The students were told to commit the formulas to memory before the exam.

origin.ko: 라틴어 committō('함께 두다, 맡기다')에서 왔고, com-(함께)과 mittō(보내다)가 합쳐졌습니다. 자신을 어떤 일에 내맡긴다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: unimaginative and conformist

examples.text: The film's conventional plot offered few surprises to seasoned viewers.

senses.en: following accepted customs and proprieties

examples.text: conventional wisdom

senses.en: make (someone) agree, understand, or realize the truth or validity of something

examples.text: He convinced me I had talent, and persuaded me to study music.

origin.ko: 라틴어 convincō('논박하다, 입증하다')에서 왔고, con-과 vincō(정복하다)가 합쳐졌습니다. 논리로 완전히 이겨 납득시킨다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: To fail to fulfill a financial obligation.

examples.text: to default on a loan

senses.en: A selection made in the absence of an alternative.

examples.text: With no other candidate willing to run, she won the chairmanship by default.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 defaute(결함, 부족)에서 왔고, 라틴어 fallo(속이다)와 이어집니다. 채무를 못 갚는 '불이행'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: formed or developed from something else; not original

examples.text: The French language is derived from Latin.

origin.ko: derive에 -ed가 붙은 말입니다.

senses.en: To disregard or regard as unimportant.

examples.text: Owing to his reputation, they discounted his comments.

senses.en: A reduction in price.

examples.text: For the summer sale, there was 40% discount in all the stores at the mall.

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 discomputō(차감하다)에서 왔습니다. 셈에서 덜어내는 데서 '대수롭지 않게 보다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: relating to or consisting of or derived from documents

examples.text: Historians found documentary evidence of the treaty in the national archives.

senses.en: A film, TV program, publication etc. which presents a social, political, scientific or historical subject in a factual or informative manner.

examples.text: Fifteen documentaries are in sharp-elbowed competition to be among the five Oscar nominees.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 documentaire에서 왔고 document에 -ary가 붙은 말입니다.

senses.en: of or being the essential or basic part

examples.text: The lecture covered elementary principles of logic before turning to proofs.

senses.en: easy and not involved or complicated

examples.text: an elementary problem in statistics

origin.ko: 라틴어 elementum(기본 요소)에 -ārius가 붙었습니다. 모든 것의 기초가 되는 요소라서 '기본적인'입니다.

senses.en: A whim.

examples.text: I had a fancy to learn to play the flute.

senses.en: The imagination.

examples.text: The poet distinguished fancy, which plays lightly with images, from the deeper power of true imagination.

senses.en: imagine; conceive of; see in one's mind

examples.text: She could hardly fancy a life without the sea after growing up in a fishing village.

senses.en: not plain; decorative or ornamented

examples.text: The hotel's fancy lobby, with its gilded mirrors and marble columns, impressed every visitor.

origin.ko: fantasy가 줄어든 말입니다. 그리스어 phantasía(눈에 보이게 함)에서 온 것으로, 마음속 환상이 변덕스러운 기분이 되었습니다.

senses.en: issue in a jet; come out in a jet; stream or spring forth

examples.text: flames were jetting out of the building

senses.en: of the blackest black; similar to the color of jet or coal

examples.text: Her jet hair stood out sharply against the pale winter landscape.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 jet '던지기'에서 왔고 라틴어 iacere '던지다'와 이어집니다. 내던지듯 뿜어져 나오는 것이 '분출'입니다.

senses.en: raise (someone) to knighthood

examples.text: The king knighted the young squire.

senses.en: A brave, chivalrous and honorable man devoted to a noble cause or love interest.

examples.text: The journalist became a knight of press freedom, defending reporters jailed abroad.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 cniht '소년, 하인, 기사'에서 왔습니다. 젊은 시종이 점차 기사를 뜻하게 되었습니다.

senses.en: In spite of what preceded; yet.

examples.text: The evidence was circumstantial; nevertheless, the jury found it persuasive enough to convict.

origin.ko: 중세 영어에서 never(결코) + the + less(덜)를 이어 붙인 말로, '그래도 덜하지 않게'라는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: a section of text; particularly a section of medium length

examples.text: The test asks students to read a short passage and summarize its central argument.

senses.en: The advance of time.

examples.text: The passage of decades has not erased the value of parental monitoring.

senses.en: the passing of a law by a legislative body

examples.text: The company was one of the prime movers in lobbying for the passage of the act.

origin.ko: 옛 프랑스어 passage에서 왔고, passer '지나가다'에서 나왔습니다. 글 속을 지나가는 한 구간이라는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: Without determination by or involvement of extraneous factors; by its very nature.

examples.text: Some people say that a hangover is caused by impurities in the drink, not by the alcohol per se.

origin.ko: 라틴어 per sē '그 자체로'를 그대로 쓰는 표현입니다.

senses.en: (used of opinions and actions) far beyond the norm

examples.text: Critics dismissed the senator's proposal as too radical for a cautious and divided legislature.

senses.en: arising from or going to the root or source

examples.text: a radical flaw in the plan

senses.en: markedly new or introducing radical change

examples.text: The architect's radical design abandoned every convention of the traditional civic building.

origin.ko: 라틴어 rādīcālis('뿌리의')에서 왔습니다. 뿌리부터 뒤엎는다는 뜻에서 '급진적인'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: a broad range of related objects or values or qualities or ideas or activities

examples.text: As Mr. Obama prepared to take the oath, his approval rating touched a remarkable 70 percent in some polling — a reflection of good will across the political spectrum.

senses.en: an ordered array of the components of an emission or wave

examples.text: The prism split the sunlight into its visible spectrum of colors.

origin.ko: 라틴어 spectrum(모습, 환영)에서 왔고 specere(보다)와 이어집니다. 눈에 보이는 빛의 띠가 넓은 범위라는 뜻으로 확장되었습니다.

senses.en: stop the flow of a liquid

examples.text: stem the tide

senses.en: grow out of, have roots in, originate in

examples.text: The increase in the national debt stems from the last war

senses.en: a slender or elongated structure that supports a plant or fungus or a plant part or plant organ

examples.text: the stem of an apple or a cherry

origin.ko: 동사 stem은 고대 노르드어 stemma(막다)에서 왔습니다. 흐름을 둑으로 막는다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: of considerable importance, size, or worth

examples.text: He inherited a substantial amount of money from his uncle.

senses.en: having substance or capable of being treated as fact; not imaginary

examples.text: the substantial world

senses.en: of good quality and condition; solidly built

examples.text: a substantial fence or wall

origin.ko: 라틴어 substantia(아래에 서 있는 것, 본질)에서 왔습니다. 실체가 탄탄해 상당하다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: the highest level or degree attainable; the highest stage of development

examples.text: Learning from others as from himself, he reached the summit of his development with his latest work.

senses.en: a meeting of heads of governments

examples.text: They met for an international summit on environmental issues.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 sommet(꼭대기)에서 왔고 라틴어 summum(맨 위)과 이어집니다. 가장 높은 지점입니다.

senses.en: (of undissolved particles in a fluid) supported or kept from sinking or falling by buoyancy and without apparent attachment

examples.text: dust particles suspended in the air

senses.en: Hung from above.

examples.text: A single bulb, suspended from the rafters, lit the cellar with a weak yellow glow.

senses.en: put forward, of a guess, in spite of possible refutation

examples.text: I would venture that the budget will be exceeded before the bridge is half finished.

senses.en: any venturesome undertaking especially one with an uncertain outcome

examples.text: The restaurant was a risky venture, and most of its investors expected to lose their money.

senses.en: put at risk

examples.text: Nothing ventured, nothing gained, she told herself as she invested her savings in the start-up.

origin.ko: adventure를 줄인 말입니다. 어떻게 될지 모르는 일에 나서는 것이 '감히 내놓다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: being actually such in almost every respect

examples.text: The angry peasants were a virtual army as they attacked the castle.

senses.en: Simulated in a computer and/or online.

examples.text: The virtual world of his computer game allowed character interaction.

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 virtuālis('힘이 있는')에서 왔고 virtūs('덕, 힘')와 이어집니다. 실제 힘을 지녔다는 뜻이 '사실상의'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: including all or everything

examples.text: a comprehensive history of the revolution

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 comprehēnsīvus에서 왔고 comprehendō(움켜쥐다)에서 갈라졌습니다. 모두 한 번에 움켜쥐는 포괄성입니다.

senses.en: consume all of one's attention or time

examples.text: The puzzle engaged her so completely that she forgot to eat lunch.

senses.en: carry out or participate in an activity; be involved in

examples.text: They engaged in a discussion

senses.en: engage or hire for work

examples.text: The firm engaged a consultant to review its accounting practices.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 engagier(맹세로 묶다)에서 왔고, gage는 '담보, 맹세'입니다. 약속에 묶여 몰두한다는 뜻이 되었습니다.

senses.en: a written record of events on a voyage (of a ship or plane)

examples.text: The captain's log recorded every change of course during the storm.

senses.en: enter into a log, as on ships and planes

examples.text: Technicians logged every temperature reading throughout the three-week experiment.

senses.en: the exponent required to produce a given number

examples.text: Taking the log of both sides turns the exponential equation into a linear one.

origin.ko: 중세 영어 logge '통나무'에서 왔습니다. 배의 속도를 재던 나무 부표(chip log)에서 항해 일지가 되었습니다.

senses.en: complain bitterly

examples.text: Residents railed against the council's decision to close the library without any public consultation.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 railler('조롱하다')에서 왔습니다. 소리 높여 비난하며 항의한다는 뜻이 되었습니다.

senses.en: conspicuously and outrageously bad or reprehensible

examples.text: The report condemned the minister's rank hypocrisy in lecturing others about thrift while living lavishly.

senses.en: very offensive in smell or taste

examples.text: a rank cigar

senses.en: very fertile; producing profuse growth

examples.text: rank earth

senses.en: relative status

examples.text: his salary was determined by his rank and seniority

senses.en: reflect deeply on a subject

examples.text: Before replying, she paused to reflect on what the committee's criticism really meant.

senses.en: give evidence of the quality of

examples.text: The mess in his dorm room reflects on the student

senses.en: to throw or bend back (from a surface)

examples.text: Sound is reflected well in this auditorium

origin.ko: 라틴어 reflectere('뒤로 구부리다')에서 왔습니다. 빛을 되꺾어 비추듯 생각을 되돌려 숙고한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: unlikely to occur

examples.text: Analysts said there was only a remote chance that the two rivals would agree to merge.

senses.en: Emotionally detached.

examples.text: After the divorce, he grew remote and rarely spoke to his colleagues at lunch.

origin.ko: 라틴어 remōtus('멀리 치워진')에서 왔고 removēre('치우다')의 과거분사입니다. 멀리 떨어져 가능성이 희박하다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: the ability to deal resourcefully with unusual problems

examples.text: a man of resource

senses.en: a source of aid or support that may be drawn upon when needed

examples.text: the local library is a valuable resource

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 resourdre('다시 솟아나다')에서 왔고 라틴어 resurgere와 이어집니다. 솟아나는 샘 같은 임기응변의 재주입니다.

senses.en: an ability that has been acquired by training

examples.text: With great skill, she navigated through the tricky passage.

origin.ko: 고대 노르드어 skil(구별, 분별력)에서 왔습니다. 잘 가려내는 능력이 기량이 되었습니다.

senses.en: In contrast; whilst on the contrary; although.

examples.text: He came first in the race, whereas his brother came last.

origin.ko: where와 as의 결합입니다.

senses.en: have an effect upon

examples.text: Scientists are studying how rising temperatures affect the migration patterns of coastal birds.

senses.en: the conscious subjective aspect of feeling or emotion

examples.text: The patient's flat affect worried the therapist, who saw no change in his expression throughout the session.

origin.ko: 라틴어 afficere(~에 작용하다)에서 왔습니다. 무언가에 힘을 가해 변화를 일으키는 것이 '영향을 미치다'입니다.

senses.en: speaking or behaving in an artificial way to make an impression

examples.text: The poet's affected manner of speaking made his sincere ideas hard to take seriously.

senses.en: acted upon; influenced

examples.text: Farmers in the affected region will receive aid after the prolonged drought.

origin.ko: affect(~인 체하다)에 -ed가 붙은 말입니다. 일부러 꾸며낸 태도를 뜻합니다.

senses.en: be the cause or source of

examples.text: The hilltop affords a sweeping view of the harbor and the distant islands.

senses.en: have the financial means to do something or buy something

examples.text: Few families in the region could afford the tuition without taking on heavy debt.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 forthian(앞으로 나아가게 하다, 이루다)에서 왔습니다. 해낼 수 있다는 뜻이 '제공하다'로 이어졌습니다.

senses.en: a short pithy instructive saying

examples.text: The old editor's favorite apothegm was that a sentence should earn its place or lose it.

origin.ko: 그리스어 apophthegma(또렷이 내뱉은 말)에서 왔습니다. 짧고 힘 있게 말한 금언입니다.

senses.en: attractiveness that interests or pleases or stimulates

examples.text: It's blowing a gale and this holiday destination loses all its appeal in an instant in weather like this.

senses.en: request earnestly (something from somebody); ask for aid or protection

examples.text: The minister appealed to citizens to conserve water during the drought.

senses.en: take a court case to a higher court for review

examples.text: He was found guilty but appealed immediately

origin.ko: 라틴어 appellare(~를 부르다)에서 왔습니다. 호소해 부르는 데서 사람을 끄는 '매력'으로 뜻이 넓어졌습니다.

senses.en: ideas or actions intended to deal with a problem or situation

examples.text: his approach to every problem is to draw up a list of pros and cons

senses.en: begin to deal with

examples.text: approach a task

senses.en: come near or verge on, resemble, come nearer in quality, or character

examples.text: His playing approaches that of Horowitz

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 appropiare(가까이 가다)에서 왔고 prope(가까이)에서 나왔습니다. 다가가는 방식이 '접근법'입니다.

senses.en: expressing or manifesting praise or approval

examples.text: The coach gave an approbatory nod as the rookie completed the drill flawlessly.

origin.ko: 라틴어 approbare(좋다고 인정하다)에서 나온 말입니다. 찬성과 칭찬을 나타냅니다.

senses.en: a complex mental state involving beliefs and feelings and values and dispositions to act in certain ways

examples.text: he had the attitude that work was fun

origin.ko: 프랑스어 attitude에서 왔고 이탈리아어 attitudine(적성, 자세)을 거쳤습니다. 몸의 자세에서 마음가짐으로 뜻이 넓어졌습니다.

senses.en: bark with prolonged noises, of dogs

examples.text: The hounds began to bay as soon as they caught the fox's scent.

senses.en: an indentation of a shoreline larger than a cove but smaller than a gulf

examples.text: This hotel has a great view across the bay.

senses.en: according with custom or propriety

examples.text: The senator's becoming restraint during the debate won praise even from his political opponents.

senses.en: displaying or setting off to best advantage

examples.text: She chose a becoming shade of green that brought out the color of her eyes.

senses.en: edit by omitting or modifying parts considered indelicate

examples.text: The bowdlerized version of the novel, while free of vulgarity, was also free of flavor.

origin.ko: 의사 Thomas Bowdler가 1818년 점잖지 못한 부분을 뺀 셰익스피어 가정판을 낸 데서 나온 말입니다.

senses.en: a series of actions advancing a principle or tending toward a particular end

examples.text: Health groups launched a campaign to persuade teenagers to give up smoking.

senses.en: exert oneself continuously, vigorously, or obtrusively to gain an end or engage in a crusade for a certain cause or person; be an advocate for

examples.text: She campaigned for better social security.

origin.ko: 이탈리아어 campagna('들판, 군사 작전')에서 왔고 라틴어 campus(들판)에서 갈라졌습니다. 들판에서 벌이는 작전이 '운동'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: a deliberative or legislative or administrative or judicial assembly

examples.text: The resolution, which speedily passed the Senate, was unable to gain a majority in the lower chamber.

senses.en: a natural or artificial enclosed space

examples.text: A canal lock chamber; a furnace chamber; a test chamber

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 chambre에서 왔고, 라틴어 camera를 거쳐 그리스어 kamara('둥근 천장의 방')까지 거슬러 갑니다.

senses.en: To promote, advocate, or act as a champion for (a cause, etc.).

examples.text: The senator championed the bill for years before it finally won enough votes to pass.

senses.en: someone who fights for a cause

examples.text: Emmeline Pankhurst was a champion of women's suffrage.

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 campio('결투 전사')에서 왔고, 라틴어 campus(들판)에서 갈라졌습니다. 싸움터에서 대신 싸우던 전사입니다.

senses.en: hold back, as of a danger or an enemy; check the expansion or influence of

examples.text: Check the growth of communism in South East Asia

senses.en: the act of restraining power or action or limiting excess

examples.text: checks and balances

senses.en: examine so as to determine accuracy, quality, or condition

examples.text: check your facts

origin.ko: 페르시아어 shāh('왕')가 아랍어와 프랑스어를 거쳐 체스의 '장군!'이 되었고, 그것을 막는다는 뜻에서 '저지하다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: a person's financial situation (good or bad)

examples.text: The family lived in reduced circumstances after the factory closed and the father lost his job.

senses.en: your overall circumstances or condition in life (including everything that happens to you)

examples.text: Whatever one's circumstances, the novel argues, a person can still choose how to respond to misfortune.

senses.en: To make a minimal effort; to continue to do something in a routine way, without initiative or effort.

examples.text: After winning the early rounds, the team coasted through the rest of the season without much effort.

senses.en: move effortlessly; by force of gravity

examples.text: The cyclist stopped pedaling and coasted down the long hill toward the village.

origin.ko: 라틴어 costa('갈비뼈, 옆구리')에서 왔고, 고대 프랑스어에서 '옆, 해안'이라는 뜻이 되었습니다. 동사는 해안을 따라 가다에서 파생됩니다.

senses.en: A body or group of people, officially tasked with carrying out a particular function.

examples.text: the European Commission

senses.en: A fee charged by an agent or broker for carrying out a transaction.

examples.text: a reseller's commission

senses.en: To place an order for (often a piece of art).

examples.text: The museum commissioned a mural from a local artist to mark its centennial.

origin.ko: 라틴어 commissiō('함께 보냄, 위임')에서 왔고, committō에 -tiō가 붙었습니다. 어떤 일을 맡겨 보낸 사람들의 모임이 '위원회'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: an abstract or general idea inferred or derived from specific instances

examples.text: The concept of justice has been debated by philosophers for more than two thousand years.

origin.ko: 라틴어 conceptus('생각, 잉태')에서 왔고 concipiō(받아들이다)에서 갈라졌습니다. 머릿속에 붙잡아 품은 생각입니다.

senses.en: be relevant to

examples.text: The new policy concerns only those employees hired after the merger.

senses.en: an anxious feeling

examples.text: Doctors expressed concern about the rapid spread of the infection in rural areas.

origin.ko: 라틴어 concernō('함께 체로 치다, 섞다')에서 왔고 con-과 cernō(가려내다)가 합쳐졌습니다.

senses.en: manner of acting or controlling yourself

examples.text: The committee praised the soldiers for their exemplary conduct under extreme pressure.

senses.en: direct the course of; manage or control

examples.text: The team conducted a rigorous survey of more than two thousand households.

senses.en: transmit or serve as the medium for transmission

examples.text: Copper conducts electricity far more efficiently than most other common metals.

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 conductus('호위, 인도')에서 왔고, condūcō(함께 이끌다)에서 갈라졌습니다. 이끌린 대로 하는 행동이 '품행'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: think about carefully; weigh

examples.text: The board will consider several proposals before choosing a new director.

senses.en: show consideration for; take into account

examples.text: The judge considered the defendant's youth when deciding on a sentence.

origin.ko: 중세 프랑스어 considerer와 라틴어 considerare를 거쳐 중세 영어에 들어온 말입니다.

senses.en: steadfast in purpose or devotion or affection

examples.text: He remained a constant friend through every hardship in her long career.

senses.en: unvarying in nature

examples.text: maintained a constant temperature

origin.ko: 라틴어 constans에서 왔고 cōnstāre('굳건히 서다')에서 갈라졌습니다. 흔들리지 않고 선다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: become smaller or draw together

examples.text: Metal contracts as it cools, which is why bridges include expansion gaps.

senses.en: be stricken by an illness, fall victim to an illness

examples.text: Several of the sailors contracted malaria during the long voyage.

senses.en: a binding agreement between two or more persons that is enforceable by law

examples.text: Both parties signed the contract, which specified penalties for late delivery.

origin.ko: 라틴어 contrahere('함께 끌어당기다')에서 왔습니다. 동사는 원래 '오그라들다'였고, 계약 뜻은 나중에 생겼습니다.

senses.en: A practice or procedure widely observed in a group, especially to facilitate social interaction; a custom.

examples.text: The convention of driving on the right is reinforced by law.

senses.en: a large formal assembly

examples.text: Delegates from every state gathered at the party's national convention to choose a nominee.

origin.ko: 라틴어 conventiō('모임, 합의')에서 왔고, conveniō(함께 모이다)에서 갈라졌습니다. 모여서 합의한 것이 '관습'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: seek someone's favor

examples.text: The candidate spent the summer courting wealthy donors in several cities.

senses.en: an assembly (including one or more judges) to conduct judicial business

examples.text: The appeals court overturned the earlier ruling on procedural grounds.

origin.ko: 라틴어 cohors(울타리 친 뜰)에서 고대 프랑스어를 거쳐 왔습니다. 궁정에서 군주의 환심을 사려 한 데서 '구애하다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: A group of people working together on a task.

examples.text: A road crew worked through the night to repair the bridge before the morning commute.

senses.en: A close group of friends.

examples.text: I’d look out for that whole crew down at Jack’s.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 creue(증원군)에서 왔고 라틴어 crescere(자라다)와 이어집니다. 불어난 인원이 '일단의 사람들'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: something in an artistic work designed to achieve a particular effect

examples.text: Foreshadowing is a common literary device that hints at events yet to unfold in the story.

senses.en: any clever maneuver

examples.text: he would stoop to any device to win a point

senses.en: an instrumentality invented for a particular purpose

examples.text: a device intended to conserve water

origin.ko: 라틴어 dīvidō(나누다)의 과거분사에서 고대 프랑스어 devis로 이어졌습니다. 계획하고 배치한 것이 '장치, 기법'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: record in detail

examples.text: The parents documented every step of their child's development

senses.en: support or supply with references

examples.text: Can you document your claims?

origin.ko: 라틴어 documentum(가르침, 증거)에서 왔습니다. 가르치고 증명하는 것이 '문서'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: go after with the intent to catch

examples.text: Allegations of corruption dogged the senator throughout his final term in office.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 docga에서 왔지만 기원이 분명하지 않습니다.

senses.en: the efficient use of resources

examples.text: The poet's economy of language made every line carry more meaning than its length suggested.

senses.en: the system of production and distribution and consumption

examples.text: The national economy contracted sharply as export demand collapsed.

origin.ko: 그리스어 oikonomía '집안 살림 관리'에서 왔습니다. 집안 살림을 아껴 꾸리는 데서 '절약'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: cause to grow thin or weak

examples.text: Months of famine emaciated the villagers until many could barely walk.

origin.ko: 라틴어 ēmaciāre(바싹 마르게 하다)에서 왔습니다. macer는 '마른'이라는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: Having a legal or moral right or claim to something.

examples.text: If you were injured at work you may be entitled to compensation.

senses.en: Convinced of one's own righteousness (self-righteousness) or the justifiability of one's actions or status, especially wrongly so; demanding and pretentious.

examples.text: Critics described the heirs as entitled, expecting privileges they had never earned.

senses.en: establish the validity of something, as by an example, explanation or experiment

examples.text: to establish a fact

senses.en: set up or found

examples.text: The council voted to establish a fund for victims of the flood.

origin.ko: 라틴어 stabilīre(굳히다)에서 고대 프랑스어를 거쳐 왔습니다. stabilis(튼튼한)처럼 굳게 세워 입증한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: the quality of being meager

examples.text: The exiguity of the villagers' food supplies became obvious as the harsh winter dragged on.

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 exiguitās에서 중세 프랑스어를 거쳐 왔습니다. 아주 적고 보잘것없는 상태를 뜻합니다.

senses.en: One who or that which explicates.

examples.text: As an explicator of medieval poetry, she made difficult verse accessible to generations of students.

senses.en: the act of expressing earnest opposition or protest

examples.text: Despite his father's expostulation, the young man refused to abandon his plan to sail alone.

origin.ko: 라틴어 expostulāre(강하게 요구하다)에서 왔습니다. 잘못을 따져 간곡히 항의하는 것입니다.

senses.en: Of a strong and cruel nature; eager and unsparing; grim; fierce; ruthless; savage.

examples.text: The tyrant's fell designs were halted only when his own generals turned against him.

senses.en: cause to fall by or as if by delivering a blow

examples.text: Loggers felled hundreds of ancient oaks before the council finally banned the practice.

senses.en: involving financial matters

examples.text: For financial reasons, we're not going to be able to continue to fund this program.

origin.ko: 중세 프랑스어 finance(채무를 끝내는 지불)에서 왔습니다. 돈을 치르고 결제를 마무리하는 일에서 '재정'이 되었습니다.
