senses.en: deliberate and intentional triggering (of trouble or discord)

examples.text: Officials blamed the fomentation of ethnic hatred on a handful of radio broadcasters.

senses.en: application of warm wet coverings to a part of the body to relieve pain and inflammation

examples.text: The nurse recommended a warm fomentation to ease the swelling around the sprained ankle.

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 fōmentātiō(찜질)에서 왔습니다. 따뜻하게 덥혀 키운다는 데서 '조장, 선동'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: being in accord with established forms and conventions and requirements (as e.g. of formal dress)

examples.text: The embassy issued a formal protest after the ambassador was publicly insulted.

senses.en: Relating to the form or structure of something.

examples.text: Formal linguistics ignores the vocabulary of languages and focuses solely on their grammar.

origin.ko: 라틴어 fōrmālis(형식의)에서 고대 프랑스어를 거쳐 왔습니다. 정해진 형식을 갖춘다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: be willing to concede

examples.text: I grant you that the plan is ambitious, but it remains financially unrealistic.

senses.en: To give (permission or wish).

examples.text: He was granted permission to attend the meeting.

senses.en: The thing or property granted; a gift; a boon.

examples.text: I got a grant from the government to study archeology in Egypt.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 granter '허락하다, 보증하다'에서 왔고, 라틴어 credere(믿다)와 연결됩니다. 상대의 말을 믿고 인정해 주는 데서 '인정하다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: annoy continually or chronically

examples.text: He is known to harry his staff when he is overworked

senses.en: make a pillaging or destructive raid on (a place), as in wartimes

examples.text: Raiders harried the coastal villages each summer, burning crops and seizing livestock.

origin.ko: 고대영어 hergian '약탈하다'에서 왔고, 게르만어 harjaz(군대)가 뿌리입니다. 군대가 쳐들어와 시달리게 하는 이미지입니다.

senses.en: a disposition not to be liberal (generous) with money

examples.text: The patron's illiberality with funds left the young orchestra unable to afford new instruments.

senses.en: The condition of being illiberal

examples.text: Critics decried the illiberality of a law that silenced dissenting newspapers.

origin.ko: illiberal에 -ity가 붙은 말입니다. 후하지(liberal) 못한 상태가 '인색함'입니다.

senses.en: an item of information that is typical of a class or group

examples.text: The company's collapse is a striking instance of what can happen when oversight is neglected.

senses.en: clarify by giving an example of

examples.text: The professor instanced several famine years to show how policy failures magnify natural disasters.

origin.ko: 라틴어 īnstantia '가까이 있음, 끈질김'에서 왔습니다. 곁에 서 있는 구체적인 '사례'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: set up or lay the groundwork for

examples.text: The new administration moved quickly to institute reforms in the way public contracts are awarded.

senses.en: an association organized to promote art or science or education

examples.text: I work in a medical research institute.

origin.ko: 라틴어 īnstituō '세우다, 설치하다'에서 왔습니다. 어떤 것 위에 기틀을 세운다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: highly complex or intricate and occasionally devious

examples.text: He related an involved story about every ancestor since 1895.

senses.en: connected by participation or association or use

examples.text: Several senior officials were found to have been involved in the scheme from its earliest stages.

origin.ko: involve에 -ed가 붙은 말입니다. 안으로 돌돌 말려 얽힌 모습에서 '복잡한'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: an important question that is in dispute and must be settled

examples.text: politicians never discuss the real issues

senses.en: prepare and issue for public distribution or sale

examples.text: The central bank issued a statement reassuring investors about the stability of the currency.

senses.en: come out of

examples.text: Water issued from the hole in the wall

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 issue '출구'에서 왔고 라틴어 exeō '나가다'와 이어집니다. 법정에서 쟁점으로 나온다는 뜻으로 퍼졌습니다.

senses.en: strive and make an effort to reach a goal

examples.text: For years the team labored to turn a modest prototype into a commercially viable product.

senses.en: productive work (especially physical work done for wages)

examples.text: his labor did not require a great deal of skill

origin.ko: 라틴어 labor '노동, 수고'에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: A group or association of cooperating members.

examples.text: the League of Nations

senses.en: A class or type of people or things that are evenly matched or on the same level.

examples.text: Forget about dating him; he's out of your league.

origin.ko: 이탈리아어 lega를 거쳐 라틴어 ligō '묶다'에서 왔습니다. 서로 묶여 맺은 '동맹'입니다.

senses.en: talk frankly with; lay it on the line

examples.text: I have to level with you

senses.en: aim at

examples.text: level criticism or charges at somebody

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 livel에서 왔고 라틴어 libella '수준기, 저울'에서 나왔습니다. 평평한 수평에서 '솔직하게 말하다'로 번졌습니다.

senses.en: To devise a plot or secret plan; to conspire.

examples.text: Had she already managed to machinate a cushy job for her husband?

origin.ko: 라틴어 machinor '꾀하다'에서 왔고 māchina(장치, 계략)에서 나왔습니다.

senses.en: To declare or affirm (a clause) to be true; to assert.

examples.text: The defendant maintained his innocence throughout the lengthy trial.

senses.en: cause to continue in a certain state, position, or activity

examples.text: maintain contact

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 maintenir에서 왔고 라틴어 manū tenēre '손으로 붙들다'와 이어집니다. 손에 쥐고 놓지 않으니 '주장하다'입니다.

senses.en: the property resulting from being or relating to the greater in number of two parts; the main part

examples.text: The majority of his customers prefer it.

senses.en: Legal adulthood, age of majority.

examples.text: The heir would not control the estate until he reached his majority at twenty-one.

origin.ko: 프랑스어와 중세 라틴어를 거쳐 라틴어 maior '더 큰'에서 왔습니다. 수가 더 큰 쪽이라는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: how something is done or how it happens

examples.text: Each culture develops its own mode of expressing grief at funerals.

senses.en: The most frequently occurring value in a distribution.

examples.text: In the exam scores, the mode was 72, higher than the median of 70.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어를 거쳐 라틴어 modus '척도, 박자'에서 왔습니다. 재는 방식이 '방식'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: Weight or importance.

examples.text: The committee postponed matters of little moment and focused on the budget crisis.

senses.en: a particular point in time

examples.text: the moment he arrived the party began

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어를 거쳐 라틴어 mōmentum에서 왔습니다. momentum, movement와 같은 뿌리입니다.

senses.en: deprive of by deceit

examples.text: The con artist mulcted elderly investors out of their retirement savings.

senses.en: impose a fine on

examples.text: The court mulcted the company a substantial sum for violating environmental regulations.

origin.ko: 라틴어 mulcta '벌금'에서 왔습니다. 벌금을 물려 돈을 빼앗는 데서 속여서 빼앗다가 되었습니다.

senses.en: remaining after all deductions

examples.text: net profit

senses.en: A trap.

examples.text: A man that flattereth his neighbor spreadeth a net for his feet.

origin.ko: '공제 후의'라는 뜻은 라틴어 nitidus '깨끗한'에서 왔습니다. 깔끔하게 덜어내고 남은 금액이라는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: To bewilder or perplex (someone); to confound, to flummox.

examples.text: The student's unexpected question nonplussed the professor, who had no ready answer.

origin.ko: 라틴어 nōn plūs '더 이상 없다'에서 왔습니다. 더는 나아갈 수 없는 막막한 상태라는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: To rebuke or scold strongly.

examples.text: The coach objurgated his players after the team squandered a ten-point lead.

origin.ko: 라틴어 obiūrgō '꾸짖다'에서 왔습니다. 상대에게 맞서 호되게 나무란다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: An asset or useful addition.

examples.text: He is a real plus to the team.

senses.en: involving advantage or good

examples.text: a plus (or positive) factor

origin.ko: 라틴어 plūs '더'에서 왔습니다. 더해진 이점이라는 뜻이 되었습니다.

senses.en: a plan of action adopted by an individual or social group

examples.text: The university adopted a strict policy against late submissions after repeated complaints from faculty.

senses.en: Wise, advantageous, or politic conduct; prudence, formerly also with connotations of craftiness.

examples.text: Honesty is not merely a virtue but, in the long run, the best policy for any institution.

origin.ko: 그리스어 politēs('시민')에서 나온 politeia('시민권, 국가 통치')가 라틴어와 프랑스어를 거쳐 '정책'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: pleasantly (even unrealistically) optimistic

examples.text: Analysts dismissed the forecast as Pollyannaish given the mounting evidence of an economic slowdown.

senses.en: a customary way of operation or behavior

examples.text: It is standard practice in the industry to disclose potential conflicts of interest before publication.

senses.en: Actual operation or experiment, in contrast to theory.

examples.text: That may work in theory, but will it work in practice?

senses.en: systematic training by multiple repetitions

examples.text: Mastery of a difficult instrument demands years of disciplined daily practice.

origin.ko: 그리스어 prassō('행하다')에서 나온 praktikos가 라틴어와 프랑스어를 거쳐 들어왔습니다. 행하는 방식이 '관행'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: First in importance, degree, or rank.

examples.text: Our prime concern here is to keep the community safe.

senses.en: the period of greatest prosperity or productivity

examples.text: The sculptor produced her finest work in the prime of her career.

senses.en: fill with priming liquid

examples.text: prime a car engine

origin.ko: 라틴어 prīmus('첫째의')에서 왔습니다. 맨 앞에 있어 가장 중요하다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: extend out or project in space

examples.text: A narrow balcony projected over the street from the second floor.

senses.en: To make plans for; to forecast.

examples.text: The CEO is projecting the completion of the acquisition by April 2007.

senses.en: To assume qualities or mindsets in others based on one's own personality.

examples.text: Anxious people often project their own fears onto those around them.

origin.ko: 라틴어 prōicere('앞으로 던지다')에서 왔습니다. 앞으로 내던져 튀어나오는 모습입니다.

senses.en: An attribute or abstract quality which is characteristic of a class of objects.

examples.text: Matter can have many properties, including color, mass and density.

senses.en: something owned; any tangible or intangible possession that is owned by someone

examples.text: The law protects private property from seizure without fair compensation.

origin.ko: 라틴어 proprius('자기 고유의')에서 나온 proprietās가 어원입니다. 고유한 성질, 그리고 자기 소유라는 뜻이 되었습니다.

senses.en: an area in which something acts or operates or has power or control:

examples.text: The committee's investigation was limited in range, leaving several important questions unanswered.

senses.en: a variety of different things or activities

examples.text: he answered a range of questions

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 rengier('줄 세우다')에서 왔고 renc('줄')는 프랑크어 hring('고리')에서 나왔습니다. 줄 세운 영역이 '범위'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: Breaking out again or reemerging after temporary abatement or suppression.

examples.text: Officials feared a recrudescent wave of violence once the troops withdrew from the region.

origin.ko: 라틴어 recrūdēscō('다시 날것이 되다')에서 왔습니다. 가라앉았던 상처가 다시 생생해져 도집니다.

senses.en: A strong will; the state of being resolute.

examples.text: The explorers faced the blizzard with a resolution that astonished even their own guides.

senses.en: finding a solution to a problem

examples.text: Both sides welcomed the swift resolution of the dispute over water rights.

senses.en: a formal expression by a meeting; agreed to by a vote

examples.text: The assembly passed a resolution condemning the use of chemical weapons.

origin.ko: 라틴어 resolūtiō('풀어냄')에서 왔습니다. 갈등을 풀고 마음을 굳히는 결의입니다.

senses.en: in the order given

examples.text: the brothers were called Felix and Max, respectively

senses.en: one who reviles

examples.text: The reviler of the new policy flooded the comment section with insults rather than arguments.

origin.ko: revile(욕하다)에 행위자 접미사 -er이 붙어 '욕하는 사람'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: an angry dispute

examples.text: The two neighbors had a bitter row over the boundary fence that lasted for months.

senses.en: an arrangement of objects or people side by side in a line

examples.text: a row of chairs

origin.ko: 기원이 분명하지 않습니다. 말다툼의 row는 소란을 뜻하는 별개의 말로 보입니다.

senses.en: To climb to the top of.

examples.text: Hilary and Norgay were the first known to have scaled Everest.

senses.en: relative magnitude

examples.text: The sheer scale of the disaster overwhelmed local relief agencies within days.

senses.en: pattern, make, regulate, set, measure, or estimate according to some rate or standard

examples.text: The firm plans to scale its production in line with projected demand.

origin.ko: 라틴어 scāla(사다리, 계단)에서 왔습니다. 사다리를 오르듯 정상에 오른다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: A plot or secret, devious plan.

examples.text: Her brain is continually fermenting new schemes.

senses.en: an elaborate and systematic plan of action

examples.text: The council unveiled an ambitious scheme to revitalize the city's abandoned waterfront.

senses.en: form intrigues (for) in an underhand manner

examples.text: The courtiers schemed endlessly to win the king's favor and undermine their rivals.

origin.ko: 그리스어 skhēma(모양, 형태)에서 왔습니다. 짜 놓은 계획의 틀이 음모라는 뜻으로 이어졌습니다.

senses.en: social or financial or professional status or reputation

examples.text: a member in good standing

senses.en: Remaining in force or status; ongoing.

examples.text: standing committee

origin.ko: stand(서다)에 -ing이 붙은 말입니다. 사회에서 서 있는 위치가 지위와 평판이 되었습니다.

senses.en: move or jump suddenly, as if in surprise or alarm

examples.text: She startled when I walked into the room

senses.en: bring into being

examples.text: Who started this company?

origin.ko: 고대 영어 styrtan(뛰어오르다)에서 왔습니다. 깜짝 놀라 펄쩍 뛴다는 뜻이 남아 있습니다.

senses.en: repeated too often; overfamiliar through overuse

examples.text: The film relies on stock characters and a predictable plot that audiences have seen many times before.

senses.en: a supply of something available for future use

examples.text: Lay in a stock of wood for the winter season.

senses.en: the hereditary derivation of an individual

examples.text: The family was of sturdy farming stock that had worked the same valley for centuries.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 stocc(나무 줄기)에서 왔습니다. 늘 쓰는 기본 재고가 되어 진부한 뜻으로도 쓰입니다.

senses.en: without evasion or compromise

examples.text: What's more, he actually tries to answer a straight question with a straight answer.

senses.en: successive (without a break)

examples.text: sick for five straight days

senses.en: characterized by honesty and fairness

examples.text: straight dealing

origin.ko: 중세 영어 streight는 strecchen(펴다)의 과거분사입니다. 쭉 펴져 곧다는 데서 솔직하다는 뜻이 나왔습니다.

senses.en: imagine to be the case or true or probable

examples.text: I suspect he is a fugitive

senses.en: regard as untrustworthy; regard with suspicion; have no faith or confidence in

examples.text: I suspect her true motives

senses.en: Viewed with suspicion; suspected.

examples.text: What I can do or offer is suspect.

origin.ko: 라틴어 suspicere(아래에서 올려다보다)에서 왔습니다. 의심스러운 눈으로 올려 본다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: hold back to a later time

examples.text: The committee voted to table the proposal until its next meeting.

senses.en: a set of data arranged in rows and columns

examples.text: The report includes a table comparing enrollment figures across the past decade.

origin.ko: 라틴어 tabula(널빤지, 판)에서 왔습니다. 안건을 탁자 위에 올려 둔다는 데서 보류한다는 뜻이 나왔습니다.

senses.en: powerfully persuasive

examples.text: The senator's most telling argument was a simple comparison of costs before and after the reform.

senses.en: Revealing information; bearing significance.

examples.text: a telling smile

origin.ko: tell(말하다)에 -ing이 붙은 말입니다. 말이 먹혀드는 효과적인 힘을 가리킵니다.

senses.en: an area of knowledge or interest

examples.text: Quantum computing remains uncharted territory for most economists, who are only beginning to study its likely effects on markets.

senses.en: A geographic area under control of a single governing entity such as state or municipality; an area whose borders are determined by the scope of political power rather than solely by natural features such as rivers and ridges.

examples.text: Troops were forbidden to cross into neighboring territory without the express approval of the government.

origin.ko: 라틴어 territōrium('땅의 구역')에서 왔습니다. 땅의 영역이 지식·관심의 '분야'로 확장되었습니다.

senses.en: a tentative insight into the natural world; a concept that is not yet verified but that if true would explain certain facts or phenomena

examples.text: The detective's theory that the butler was innocent rested on a single overlooked footprint.

senses.en: The underlying principles or methods of a given technical skill, art etc., as opposed to its practice.

examples.text: Lopukhov wrote a number of books and articles on ballet theory, as well as his memoirs.

origin.ko: 그리스어 theōrós('구경꾼')에서 나온 theōría('관찰, 숙고')를 라틴어와 프랑스어를 거쳐 받았습니다. 보고 헤아린 생각이 '이론, 가설'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: a journey or route all the way around a particular place or area

examples.text: On our last holiday to Spain we took a tour of the wine-growing regions.

senses.en: a period of time spent in military service

examples.text: After completing his second tour overseas, the sergeant retired and opened a small hardware store.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 tour('돌기')에서 왔습니다. 한 바퀴 빙 도는 여정이 '순회 여행'입니다.

senses.en: applicable to or common to all members of a group or set

examples.text: The film earned universal acclaim, with critics of every persuasion praising its direction.

senses.en: of worldwide scope or applicability

examples.text: Hunger is a universal concern that crosses every national and cultural boundary.

origin.ko: 라틴어 ūniversālis에서 왔고 universe('하나로 돌아가는 전체')에 -al을 붙인 형태입니다. 전체에 두루 적용되는 것이 '보편적인'입니다.

senses.en: appearing to be true or real

examples.text: a verisimilar tale

origin.ko: 라틴어 vērī similis('진실과 비슷한')에서 왔습니다. 진짜 같아 '그럴듯한'입니다.

senses.en: By way of; passing through.

examples.text: You can enter the building via the western gate.

senses.en: By (means of); using.

examples.text: I'll send you the information via e-mail.

origin.ko: 라틴어 via('길')의 탈격 viā('길을 따라')에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: inadequate in amount or degree

examples.text: The committee found the proposal wanting in both detail and ambition.

senses.en: nonexistent

examples.text: Basic courtesy was sadly wanting in the way the staff treated the customers.

origin.ko: want('모자라다')에 -ing를 붙인 말입니다. 모자란 상태가 '부족한'입니다.
